dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-mudon.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Physics at Higher and Standard Level. Each profile names the level and the option topic they have taught, because option content varies by school and a request should reach someone who has worked the right one.

intro.heading: Physics grades move on technique, not on more content
paragraphs: A Diploma physics student stuck at a 4 usually knows the physics. What they have not learned is the form of answer the papers reward. A calculation is produced and the assumption behind it is never stated. A graph is drawn and the gradient is never converted into the quantity the question asked for. An extended response names the right phenomenon and never builds the causal chain that collects the marks. None of that is fixed by rereading a textbook.

Mudon sharpens the problem for a different reason. The community sits off Al Qudra Road in Dubailand with no secondary school inside its own boundary, so Diploma students travel to Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches, GEMS International School Al Khail, Nord Anglia in Al Barsha South or Fairgreen International in The Sustainable City. The evening is short, and a short evening spent on content review duplicates the school day rather than adding to it.

Physics also carries an uncomfortable dependency: it is examined in English and marked on reasoning, but it is failed most often on mathematics. Rearrangement, standard form, logarithms, gradients and uncertainties appear throughout the papers, and a student weak in any of them loses physics marks that look like physics gaps. Diagnosing that correctly is often the whole value of a first session.

There is a second reason local search is a poor filter here. Physics is one of the subjects where school departments in this belt differ most in the option they teach and in the practical programme they run, so a tutor's usefulness depends on matching the school rather than the postcode. A tutor fifteen minutes away who has taught a different option is less use than one on a screen who has taught the same one, and the family cannot tell the difference from a directory listing.

The internal component adds a second axis. The scientific investigation carries roughly a fifth of the subject grade, is marked against published criteria, and depends on the school's own equipment and practical scheme. Online tutoring cannot run the experiment and does not claim to. What it does is prepare the design, interrogate the variable control, examine the uncertainty treatment and give criterion feedback on the student's own write-up.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so a session can sit at 4.15pm for a student home early or after 8pm where both parents commute. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and nothing here should be read as an offer to arrive at a Mudon door. The trade is a physical presence for a tutor who has actually taught Higher Level physics. What follows is organised by component rather than by topic, because that is how the marks are distributed and how a plan should be built.

sections.heading: What each physics component actually examines
paragraphs: Diploma physics is examined across several papers plus an internal investigation, and each rewards something different. Multiple choice rewards speed, precision and elimination. Short and extended response rewards constructed reasoning. The experimental and option paper rewards data handling, uncertainty treatment and familiarity with the specific option the school teaches.

The internal investigation is the component students most often underestimate. It carries roughly a fifth of the subject grade, which makes it comparable to a whole paper, and it is marked on design and analysis and evaluation rather than on whether the experiment worked. A technically modest investigation, well designed and honestly evaluated, outscores an ambitious one written up loosely.

Exact weightings come from the current subject guide, which the school's physics department can confirm. They should not be taken from a tutoring page, because guides change between cycles and a stale figure is worse than no figure. What is stable is the relative shape: the response paper carries the largest external share, and the investigation carries a meaningful internal one.

The practical use of knowing this is prioritisation. A student losing most of their marks in extended response should not be spending their tutoring hour on multiple-choice drills, however much better that feels.

One further point about the option paper. Because schools choose the option, a published revision guide bought online may cover content the student will never be examined on, and that discovery is usually made late. Checking the option against the school's own scheme of work before buying any resource saves both money and revision time, and it takes one question at a parents' evening.

sections.heading: The topics where Higher Level grades separate
paragraphs: Across marked Higher Level scripts the losses concentrate in a few predictable places. Fields is the first: gravitational and electric fields treated as separate memorised cases rather than as one idea with different constants, so a question phrased unfamiliarly defeats a student who could answer the standard version.

Electromagnetic induction is the second. Students can state the law and cannot apply it to a situation where the geometry changes, because they learned a result rather than the reasoning that produces it. The repair is working several physically different situations until the method rather than the answer becomes the thing remembered.

Thermal physics and the gas laws form a third cluster, where the failures are usually mathematical: unit conversion, absolute temperature, and proportional reasoning under time pressure. Quantum and nuclear content is a fourth, and here the losses are often about precision of language, since the mark schemes are specific about terms in a way that general understanding does not satisfy.

Mechanics is the outlier. Most students handle it adequately because it is taught first and revisited often, but when it does fail the cause is nearly always vector treatment, and that is a mathematics problem wearing a physics costume.

The useful consequence is that the topic order of a tutoring plan should not follow the textbook. Fields and induction taught properly early, with the reasoning rather than the results committed to memory, prevents most of the losses described above. Mechanics revisited only if a script shows vector errors. Quantum and nuclear handled late, with the emphasis on precise terminology rather than on additional content.

sections.heading: Extended response: the marks almost nobody collects
paragraphs: Extended response is where the largest single block of recoverable marks sits in Diploma physics, and most students have never been taught how to write one. They treat it as a long short-answer and produce a correct calculation with no surrounding argument, which collects the method marks and leaves the rest.

What a mark scheme rewards is explicit. The physics is named rather than implied. The assumption is stated: that air resistance is negligible, that the collision is elastic, that the field is uniform over the region considered. Each step follows from the last in a sequence a reader can follow. The final answer carries units and a sensible number of significant figures. And where the question asks for a comment, there is one.

The drill is to write the structure before the physics. Three or four extended responses a week, each planned in two lines before any working, each marked by the student against the published scheme. Within a month most students stop losing those marks, which is a faster return than any content revision available to them.

The second habit worth installing is reading the mark allocation. A six-mark question wants six creditable statements, not one long paragraph, and a student who counts before writing finishes the paper.

There is one more habit worth installing, and it is about handwriting and layout rather than physics. Markers award credit for statements they can find. An answer written as a single dense block, with the working interleaved and no line breaks, loses marks that the same content laid out in steps would collect. Students resist this until they mark a classmate's script and cannot follow it either.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, read as criteria
paragraphs: The investigation is assessed against published criteria, not against whether the data came out well. That single fact changes how a student should approach it. A measurement that produces a messy relationship, honestly analysed and evaluated with its limitations named, can score higher than a clean result reported without reflection.

Design is where the ceiling is set. A research question with one clear independent variable, a controlled set of others, and a measurable dependent variable can score across every criterion. A vague question cannot be rescued, however carefully the experiment is run, because the criteria ask about the quality of the investigation rather than the effort behind it.

Analysis is where most of the mathematical marks live. Uncertainties have to be propagated rather than mentioned, graphs chosen so the relationship is visible, gradients converted to the physical quantity they represent, and anomalies addressed rather than deleted. Students who have never been taught uncertainty propagation lose these marks silently.

Evaluation is the criterion most often treated as a conclusion. It asks for specific, physics-based limitations and realistic improvements, not a note that more trials would have helped. A tutor can explain each descriptor and mark the student's own draft against it, which is permitted. Drafting, rewriting or supplying data is not, and the investigation is authenticated by the teacher.

Timing matters here as much as technique. Criteria reward process, and process has to exist before it can be written up. A student who runs the experiment first and reads the criteria afterwards has already lost design marks that cannot be recovered. Reading the descriptors before the practical, and keeping a dated log while it happens, costs nothing and changes the ceiling.

sections.heading: The mathematics hiding inside physics
paragraphs: A large share of physics failures are mathematics failures, and treating them as physics wastes a term. The pattern is consistent: a student understands the concept, cannot execute the manipulation under time, and concludes they are bad at physics. The diagnosis is visible in a marked script, because the errors cluster around the algebra rather than around the ideas.

Rearrangement is the most common. A formula with the unknown in the denominator, or inside a square root, or on both sides, defeats students who can state the relationship perfectly. The repair is twenty minutes a week of pure manipulation practice with physics formulas, separated from any physics reasoning so that only one skill is being tested at a time.

Standard form and unit prefixes are second. Converting nanometres, kilojoules and microamps reliably under pressure is a skill, and students who do it slowly lose marks to time rather than to error. Logarithms arrive in the nuclear and quantum content and in graph linearisation, and a student who cannot manipulate them cannot access those questions at all.

Gradients are the highest-value item on the list. Physics asks constantly for a gradient to be converted into a physical quantity, in both the papers and the investigation, and students who treat a gradient as a number rather than as a quantity with units lose marks in several places at once.

The diagnostic trick is simple enough for a parent to apply. Take a question the student got wrong, remove the physics and ask them to do the algebra alone. If the algebra fails in isolation, the problem is mathematical and should be treated as such. If it succeeds, the problem is in the physics reasoning or in the answer construction, and the hour belongs somewhere else entirely.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level in physics
paragraphs: Parents often ask whether Standard Level is the safer choice, and the answer depends on what the student needs rather than on difficulty alone. Higher Level covers additional content, examines an extra paper, and is usually required for engineering and physical-science applications. Standard Level covers the core and examines fewer papers.

The part families underestimate is that the question styles are the same. Standard Level is not an easier style of examination; it is a narrower syllabus examined in the same way, which means the technique demands are identical. A student who struggles with extended response will struggle with it at either level, and dropping to Standard does not solve a technique problem.

Where dropping to Standard Level genuinely helps is content load, particularly for a student carrying three Higher Level sciences or combining Higher Level physics with Higher Level mathematics and chemistry. That combination is heavy, and a student doing all three badly is worse placed than one doing two well.

The decision belongs with the school, and the useful time to make it is early rather than during the second year. The question to ask is what university routes the student is realistically considering, checked against each institution's own published entry profile rather than against general advice.

One practical note on timing. A level change is easier early in Year 12 than late, and in some schools it becomes impossible once the second year begins because the teaching groups diverge. If the question is live, ask the school for its own deadline in writing rather than assuming flexibility exists, and ask what evidence they would want to see either way.

sections.heading: The laboratory question, answered honestly
paragraphs: An online physics tutor cannot run an experiment with a student, and any page suggesting otherwise is overselling. The practical work belongs to the school: its equipment, its safety procedures, its scheme of work. What a Mudon family should expect from online tutoring is work on everything that surrounds the practical, which is where the assessed marks actually sit.

Before the laboratory, a session can interrogate the research question, test whether the proposed method will produce a measurable relationship, identify the variables that need controlling and anticipate where the largest uncertainty will come from. Students who do this arrive with a plan rather than with an idea, and the difference shows in the design criterion.

After the laboratory, a session can examine the raw data, check whether the chosen graph makes the relationship visible, work through uncertainty propagation on the student's own numbers, and read the draft against each criterion. This is the part of the investigation most students rush, and it carries more marks than the measuring did.

The school's equipment also constrains what is sensible to attempt. A research question requiring apparatus the department does not hold is a dead end regardless of how good the idea is, which is why naming the school at the start of a tutoring arrangement matters more than it appears to.

A short note on data. Where a student has measured something and the relationship is unclear, the instinct is to repeat the experiment. Often the better move is to examine whether the graph chosen hides the relationship, since linearising the data can reveal a pattern that a direct plot conceals. That is analysis work, it happens on a screen, and it rescues more investigations than another afternoon of measuring does.

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs, and what to ask before paying
paragraphs: Physics requests land in the specialist end of this market, because the subject is harder to cover credibly than most. Named IB and IGCSE specialists publish roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table giving AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 500 to 650, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Below that, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52, which can suit routine question practice but rarely suits Higher Level technique work. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the price.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. For context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. These are market figures with their sources named rather than IB Gram prices.

The questions that matter before paying are narrow. Which level have you taught and for how many cohorts. Which option topic. How do you teach uncertainty propagation. What will you do with an investigation draft, and what will you refuse to do. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023.

faqs.question: Why does my son understand physics and still score 4s?
faqs.answer: Almost always answer construction rather than knowledge. The pattern in marked Higher Level scripts is consistent: a calculation is correct and the assumption behind it is never stated, a graph is drawn and the gradient is never converted into the quantity asked for, and an extended response names the right phenomenon without building the causal chain. None of that improves with rereading. It improves by planning the structure before writing, marking his own work against the published scheme, and counting the mark allocation before answering.

faqs.question: Which physics topics should a Higher Level student attack first?
faqs.answer: Fields and electromagnetic induction, in most cases. Across marked scripts those two carry the heaviest losses, because students learn results rather than the reasoning that produces them and then fail when the geometry or the phrasing changes. Thermal physics and the gas laws form a second cluster where the failures are usually mathematical rather than conceptual. Mechanics is generally adequate, and when it does fail the cause is vector treatment. A marked paper will confirm which of these applies before any time is spent.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with the physics investigation without a laboratory?
faqs.answer: With everything except the measuring, which is where the marks are. Before the practical, a session can interrogate the research question, test whether the method will produce a measurable relationship, identify the variables needing control and anticipate the largest uncertainty. After it, a session can examine the raw data, check the graph choice, work uncertainty propagation on the student's own numbers and read the draft against each criterion. The experiment itself belongs to the school and its equipment, and no page should claim otherwise.

faqs.question: How much does the physics investigation count towards the grade?
faqs.answer: Roughly a fifth of the subject grade, with the precise figure set by the current subject guide, which the school's physics department can confirm. That makes it comparable to a whole paper. What surprises students is that it is marked on design, analysis and evaluation rather than on whether the experiment produced a clean result: a messy relationship, honestly analysed with its limitations named in physics terms, can outscore a tidy result reported without reflection.

faqs.question: Is poor maths the real reason a student fails Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: Very often, and misdiagnosing it wastes a term. The signature in a marked script is errors clustering around algebra rather than around concepts: rearrangement with the unknown in a denominator or under a root, slow or wrong standard-form conversion, logarithms that block access to a question entirely, and gradients treated as bare numbers rather than as quantities with units. The repair is twenty minutes a week of pure manipulation practice using physics formulas, deliberately separated from physics reasoning so only one skill is tested at a time.

faqs.question: Should a struggling student drop from Higher to Standard Level physics?
faqs.answer: Only for the right reason. Standard Level covers the core without the Higher Level extensions and examines fewer papers, but the question styles are identical, so a technique problem travels with the student. Dropping genuinely helps where the issue is content load, particularly for someone carrying three Higher Level sciences or combining Higher Level physics with Higher Level mathematics and chemistry. The decision belongs with the school, and it should be checked against the published entry profiles of the universities actually being considered.

faqs.question: Does the option topic my child's school teaches really matter?
faqs.answer: Enough that revising the wrong one is a wasted term. Schools choose which option to teach, so two Diploma physics students in Dubai can sit the same core content and entirely different option questions. Paper 3 preparation has to match the school's choice. Name the school and the option when you enquire, and the tutor sets questions from the right one. It also tells us what the practical scheme and the available equipment look like, which shapes what an investigation can realistically attempt.

faqs.question: What does an extended-response drill actually look like?
faqs.answer: Three or four questions a week, each planned in two lines before any physics is written, each marked by the student against the published scheme. The plan names the physics to be used and the assumption to be stated. The marking is the part that teaches, because it shows exactly which statements earned credit. A second habit goes with it: count the mark allocation before writing, since a six-mark question wants six creditable statements rather than one long paragraph. Most students stop losing those marks within a month.

faqs.question: How do we prepare for Diploma physics over the summer before Year 12?
faqs.answer: Six to eight sessions on the things the first term assumes and does not teach. Rearrangement at speed, standard form and prefixes, basic logarithm manipulation, vector components, and the habit of justifying rather than stating. Students arriving at a Diploma physics class in Arabian Ranches or Al Khail come from several different schools and boards, so the class contains very differently prepared students, and the gap shows within weeks. The summer block is the cheapest useful window in the course and almost nobody uses it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both physics and maths for a Mudon Year 13?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and the overlap is genuine: calculus, vectors and graph interpretation appear in mechanics and fields, so one subject can be taught through the other rather than competing with it. At Higher Level in both simultaneously the combination is less common and the honest answer is sometimes two tutors. Ask which papers the tutor has marked in each subject rather than whether they can cover both. Scheduling is identical either way, because no travel has to be arranged between slots.

faqs.question: Is a physics Extended Essay a good idea?
faqs.answer: It can be excellent and it is unforgiving. The research question has to be answerable with equipment the school actually holds, in a measurement a student can take reliably, and within the word limit. Most weak physics Extended Essays are not badly written; they ask a question that could not be answered with the available apparatus. One or two sessions interrogating the question before any work begins is worth more than ten later. The essay itself must be entirely the student's own work, authenticated by the supervisor.

faqs.question: What does a Higher Level physics tutor cost in this market?
faqs.answer: Physics sits in the specialist end. Named IB and IGCSE specialists publish roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table at AED 200 to 450 or more, while premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. These are published market figures rather than IB Gram prices, and a free trial lesson comes before any payment.

faqs.question: How quickly can a physics tutor start for a Mudon student?
faqs.answer: Standard Level physics is usually covered within a few days of you naming the level, option and school. Higher Level with a common option is similar. Narrower requests take longer: a less-taught option, Higher Level physics paired with Further Mathematics, or investigation coaching close to a school deadline can need a week or more. Where coverage is genuinely thin you are told with a timescale or offered an alternative, rather than matched to a generalist. The trial lesson is free and happens before any payment.

faqs.question: Will a tutor explain uncertainty propagation properly?
faqs.answer: It should be one of the first things covered, because it is assessed in two places and taught thoroughly in few. Uncertainties have to be propagated through calculations rather than mentioned in a sentence, and the method differs for sums, products and powers. Students who have never been shown it lose marks in the data paper and in the investigation's analysis criterion simultaneously. The practical approach is to work through propagation on the student's own measured data, so the method is learned on numbers they recognise rather than on a textbook example.

Send the level, the option the school teaches, the school itself and one marked response paper, and a free trial lesson over live video is arranged before any payment is taken. The session should end with something specific named, whether that is unstated assumptions in extended response or rearrangement failing under time. Lessons are delivered online on Gulf Standard Time; the experiment stays with the school, and home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only.

intro.heading: Why physics is the hardest subject to staff in eastern Dubai
paragraphs: There is a pattern in enquiries from this catchment that is worth saying out loud. Mathematics, chemistry and biology reach a trial lesson within a few days. Physics at Standard Level is similar. Physics at Higher Level is noticeably thinner, and it takes four to seven days to match properly rather than two. That matters because Higher Level physics is also one of the most commonly required subjects for engineering admission, so the families who need it most are the ones facing the longest wait.

The scarcity is not about Dubai. Physics graduates who teach well are in short supply in most markets, and the ones who end up tutoring privately in a neighbourhood tend to be the ones whose subject spread is broad. Around Muhaisnah, where the school catchment is dominated by Indian and British curricula, a tutor advertising IB physics is frequently someone who teaches CBSE physics and will attempt the Diploma. The content overlaps; the assessment does not.

That assessment gap is the whole point of this page. The current Diploma physics guide organises content into five themes rather than the older numbered topics, examines across two papers with the first split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, and carries a single scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade and marked against four criteria of six marks each. A tutor working from the previous structure will teach competent physics and prepare your child for a paper that no longer exists in that form.

So the verification question for physics is blunt and specific: name the five themes, tell me the paper structure at my child's level with the weightings, and tell me what the investigation is marked out of and against which criteria. A Diploma physics specialist answers all three in under two minutes. Nobody else does, and no amount of enthusiasm substitutes.

On delivery, stated plainly rather than buried: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India, and the published Dubai market rate for in-home visits is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included if that is the route you want. For a Muhaisnah family we match a Diploma physics specialist, who may be based outside the UAE, and teach one-to-one over live video at a Gulf Standard Time slot, with a free trial lesson before anything is charged. Widening the geography is the only lever that actually solves a supply problem.

One more thing before the detail. The largest share of lost marks in Diploma physics is not content. It is graph interpretation, uncertainty handling and definition precision, and all three are recoverable in weeks rather than terms. So the first useful conversation is about a marked script rather than about a syllabus plan, because a student who reports struggling with fields is often losing most of their marks somewhere else entirely, and buying more fields teaching would not have found that out.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-muhaisnah.programmesIntro: Physics requests from this catchment arrive from three stages, and the useful work differs completely between them.

programmes.name: Diploma physics
programmes.description: Two years covering five themes, with additional higher-level content in each, examined across two written papers plus a scientific investigation worth 20%. Paper 1 contains a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section; Paper 2 is extended response. Higher Level sits longer papers covering the additional material rather than a separate third paper.
programmes.countryNote: The majority of our physics enquiries from eastern Dubai are Higher Level students in the first year who have hit fields or the particulate nature of matter and want the foundations rebuilt. That is the right instinct and the right time, because second-year physics assumes the first year is secure.

programmes.name: Middle Years sciences
programmes.description: Integrated sciences assessed against four criteria, each marked out of 8. Criterion B asks students to inquire and design, criterion C to process and evaluate, which is where the investigative skills the Diploma later assesses begin. There is no terminal examination unless the school uses eAssessment.
programmes.countryNote: Students in Mirdif and Festival City continuum schools arrive in Diploma physics having done criterion-marked investigations for years, which is an advantage they usually do not know they have. The gap is quantitative: by-hand algebra and uncertainty arithmetic, which the Middle Years Programme does not push.

programmes.name: IGCSE physics as the route in
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1, tiered, with practical skills assessed either by a practical test or by an alternative-to-practical written paper. The content overlaps with the first Diploma theme substantially, but the mathematical demand and the expectation of explanation are both lower.
programmes.countryNote: A student entering Diploma physics from a Core or Foundation IGCSE tier faces the steepest first term of any science in this catchment, because the algebra required is immediate. The honest fix is foundational work on rearrangement, proportionality and graph skills before the term starts.

programmes.name: A Level physics, for comparison
programmes.description: The alternative route many eastern Dubai schools offer instead of the Diploma. More depth in fewer subjects, with practical skills assessed differently depending on the board. Universities state offers in either currency, and neither route is universally preferred.
programmes.countryNote: Families occasionally ask us whether moving from Diploma physics to A Level physics would be easier. It is a different shape rather than an easier one, and switching mid-course loses the investigation work already done, so it is a conversation for the school's head of sixth form rather than for a tutor.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-muhaisnah.subjectsIntro: Diploma physics breaks into identifiable areas and difficulty concentrates predictably. These are the ones Muhaisnah enquiries name.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, and at Higher Level rotational and relativistic extensions. The foundational theme, and the one where a student's by-hand algebra either holds or does not. Marks go on sign conventions and on free-body diagrams drawn incompletely.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws and the behaviour of particles. Students handle the equations and lose marks explaining why a quantity changes at constant volume, which is a conceptual answer rather than a calculation.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Oscillations, wave properties, superposition, and at Higher Level more demanding treatment of interference and simple harmonic motion. Phase relationships are where understanding most often turns out to be superficial.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields and their analogies, with induction and circuits. The theme that most commonly breaks first-year Higher Level students in this catchment, because the analogies between field types are load-bearing and rarely taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactivity, nuclear binding, and quantum behaviour with Higher Level extensions. Content-heavy and often taught late in the second year, which means it is the theme students revise least and lose most on.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and uncertainty bars on graphs. Examined on paper in the data-analysis section and assessed in the investigation. The most reliably recoverable marks in the whole course.

subjects.name: Graph interpretation
subjects.description: Gradient and area meaning, linearisation, and reading a relationship from a plot. The commonest single loss in physics: a student calculates a gradient correctly and cannot say what quantity it represents, which is the mark the question wanted.

subjects.name: Definitions and command terms
subjects.description: State, define, outline, explain, discuss and compare each demand a different answer. Physics definitions are precise and partially memorised; a near-miss definition loses the mark entirely, which students find unfair until it is explained.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: A single piece of independent research worth 20% of the grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria. Research design decides most of the available marks before any data exists, which is why the topic conversation matters more than the write-up.

subjects.name: Experimental technique on paper
subjects.description: Reading instruments, choosing ranges, identifying systematic versus random error, and suggesting improvements. All assessed in writing, which means it is teachable on a shared screen rather than requiring a bench.

subjects.name: Mathematical fluency for physics
subjects.description: Rearrangement, proportional reasoning, logarithms, trigonometry and small-angle approximations. A student weak here will appear to be weak at physics, and the diagnosis matters because the remedies are completely different.

subjects.name: Higher Level extension material
subjects.description: The additional content within each theme rather than a separate unit, examined in the same papers. Students who revise the shared content thoroughly and the extension material lightly are capped, and this is a planning error rather than a capability one.

sections.heading: The five themes, and why the structure matters when choosing a tutor
paragraphs: The current Diploma physics guide organises content into five themes with additional higher-level material inside each, rather than the older arrangement of numbered core topics plus separate additional higher-level topics and an option. That reorganisation changes how a course is sequenced, how revision should be structured, and which paper a given piece of content appears in. A tutor who learned the previous structure and has not revisited it will teach correct physics in the wrong order for the wrong paper.

The themes are: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Each carries higher-level extension content examined in the same papers as the shared material rather than separately. That last detail is the one that catches students out, because revising the shared content thoroughly and the extension material lightly produces a capped grade with no warning.

The table sets out the themes with what each contains, where students in this catchment typically struggle, and the mathematical tool each demands. Read the last column carefully: physics difficulty in the first year is very often a mathematics problem wearing a physics costume, and the remedies are completely different. A student who cannot rearrange confidently will look weak at fields and will not be helped by more fields teaching.

Confirm the detail against the current subject guide for your child's cohort, which the school's IB coordinator can supply, because guides are reissued and content moves. What will not change is the verification instruction: ask a prospective physics tutor to name the themes without looking. It takes fifteen seconds and it filters more effectively than any qualification summary.

sections.heading: What your child actually sits: papers, durations and weightings
paragraphs: Ask any prospective tutor to recite this before you book. The current model examines physics across two written papers plus the internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 is split: a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, together carrying 36% of the grade. Paper 2 is extended response and carries 44%. The investigation carries the remaining 20%.

The difference between the levels is duration and content depth rather than an extra paper. At Standard Level the papers run an hour and a half each; at Higher Level Paper 1 runs two hours and Paper 2 two and a half, covering the extension material in the same components. There is no separate third paper in physics, which distinguishes it from Higher Level mathematics and is a point tutors from a mathematics background sometimes get wrong.

The planning consequence is that the data-analysis section deserves disproportionate attention. It sits inside Paper 1, it rewards uncertainty handling, graph interpretation and experimental reasoning, and those skills are independent of how confident a student feels about fields or quantum behaviour. A student weak on content can still score well there, which makes it the most reliable place to recover marks in the final term.

The second planning consequence concerns the investigation. Twenty per cent of the grade is submitted before any examination and is entirely within the student's control for the months it is in progress. Families who treat it as a report to be written at the end have already forfeited most of the research-design marks. Confirm weightings and durations against the current subject guide, because they are revised when a guide is reissued.

sections.heading: Where physics marks actually go, in order of size
paragraphs: Marked scripts from this catchment show the same four losses repeatedly, and the largest is not content. It is graph interpretation: a student calculates a gradient correctly and then cannot state what physical quantity it represents, or reads an intercept without saying what it means. The question asked for meaning and received arithmetic. This is a comprehension and vocabulary issue as much as a physics one, and it responds to practice within weeks.

The second is uncertainty. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a multiplication or a power, and uncertainty bars drawn and used on a graph. It is examined in the data-analysis section and assessed again in the investigation, which means the same skill earns marks twice. Students treat it as an annoying appendix to real physics and lose a predictable number of marks every time.

The third is definition precision. Physics definitions are exact and partly memorised, and a near-miss loses the mark entirely. Students find that unfair until somebody explains that the definition is the content being assessed, not a preamble to it. Command terms compound this: state, define, outline, explain, discuss and compare each demand a different length and structure of answer, and a student writing an explanation where a definition was requested is doing more work for fewer marks.

The fourth is the one families most often assume is first: genuine content gaps. These are real, they cluster in fields and in the late-taught nuclear and quantum material, and they take longer to fix than the other three combined. Which is exactly why a diagnostic on marked work matters before buying hours. If three-quarters of the lost marks are graphs, uncertainty and definitions, a bounded technique block will move the grade faster than a term of content teaching.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks and a hard boundary
paragraphs: The investigation is 20% of the final grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Most of what decides the mark happens before the student collects a single reading, because research design and the quality of what can be analysed are determined by the question chosen and the variables identified. A good investigation with a poor question is not possible.

The failure pattern is consistent. A student picks a topic that interests them, discovers it has no cleanly measurable independent variable, collects data anyway, and produces an analysis with nothing to analyse. By the time a tutor sees the draft, the research-design marks are gone and so are most of the analysis marks. One session on question viability at the start is worth more than five sessions on the write-up at the end.

What a tutor may do here is firmly bounded and we state it on every page. Explain what each criterion asks for. Interrogate the research question, the independent and dependent variables, the control of conditions and the proposed range of readings. Read the student's own draft and say which descriptor is not yet met. Check that uncertainties have been handled and propagated properly. What a tutor may not do is write, restructure or complete any part of the submission, supply data, or perform the analysis.

The test is simple. After a useful session the student holds three specific problems to fix and the document contains nothing the tutor produced. Providers who will write an investigation exist in this market, and one of them publishes a price for completed internal assessments. Using such a service triggers IB malpractice procedures against the student, not the seller, which is why we say this plainly rather than in small print.

sections.heading: Practical work when the lesson is on a screen
paragraphs: This is the honest objection to online physics tutoring and it deserves a precise answer. Hands-on apparatus time is the school's job and the school has the equipment: the oscilloscopes, the light gates, the power supplies. No online tutor replaces that and we would not claim to. What the Diploma assesses in writing, however, is substantial, and most of it is better taught on a shared screen than at a bench.

Consider what the data-analysis section actually asks for. Reading a scale and recording to an appropriate precision. Choosing a sensible range and interval. Identifying whether an error is systematic or random. Tabulating with consistent significant figures and correct units in headers. Plotting with a sensible scale, drawing a line of best fit, extracting a gradient, interpreting it physically. Suggesting a specific improvement rather than a generic one. Every item on that list is a paper skill.

Several are taught considerably better remotely. Plotting is the clearest case: a tutor annotating the student's actual graph live, pointing at the scale choice that lost a mark, does more in five minutes than a comment written in an exercise book that goes home. Linearisation, where a student has to decide what to plot against what in order to get a straight line, is pure reasoning on a shared document.

What a Muhaisnah family needs to provide is modest and it matters. A way for the tutor to see written work as it is produced: a tablet with a stylus is ideal, a phone propped over a page works, and a shared spreadsheet is excellent for data handling. Where the school runs a practical examination rather than a written alternative, the focus shifts to recording conventions and to rehearsing method sequences so the student is not reading a procedure for the first time under pressure.

sections.heading: Two minutes that identify a Diploma physics specialist
paragraphs: Three requests, in this order, on any tutor including ours. First: name the five themes of the current physics guide. A specialist does this in fifteen seconds. Somebody working from the previous structure will describe numbered core topics and an option, which tells you immediately that their preparation material is out of date, and out-of-date material in physics means teaching towards a paper that no longer exists in that form.

Second: describe the papers at my child's level, with weightings. The expected answer names Paper 1 with its multiple-choice and data-analysis sections at 36%, Paper 2 at 44%, and the investigation at 20%, with the durations differing by level and no separate third paper. A tutor who mentions a third paper has confused physics with mathematics.

Third, and the strongest filter: what is the investigation marked out of, and against which criteria? The answer is 24 marks across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. This is the question most generalists fail, because it is the part of the course furthest from subject content and closest to assessment literacy, and it is also the single component where a specialist adds the most value.

If you want a fourth, hand them your child's marked script and ask them to find three marks lost for a reason that is not about understanding physics. A specialist finds them in two minutes: an unstated gradient meaning, an uncertainty not propagated, a definition that was nearly right. That request cannot be prepared for, and the quality of the answer will be obvious to you even if you have never studied the subject.

sections.heading: Higher Level physics, university routes and what the market charges
paragraphs: Higher Level physics is required or strongly expected for engineering across most destinations and for several physical science programmes, which is why the demand for it in this catchment outstrips supply. It also pairs with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches in those requirements, so a student aiming at engineering typically needs both at Higher Level and has correspondingly little slack in their week. Check the specific requirement on the university's own admissions page: requirements are stated by subject and level, and no tutoring page should be relied on for them.

For medicine the picture varies by country and institution, and chemistry and biology are more commonly the required pair, with physics useful rather than mandatory. We will not generalise further than that, because the requirement is institutional and a wrong generalisation on a page like this could shape a subject choice badly.

On what support costs: across the published Dubai figures, qualified subject tutors working online sit roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with one agency publishing IB from AED 200. Specialists across IB, IGCSE and A Level run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with one UK agency publishing AED 270 and a premium examiner-branded provider publishing AED 650. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Higher Level physics tends to sit at the specialist end simply because fewer people can teach it.

Our own figure is agreed at the consultation once the level and cadence are known, and we sit in the qualified-specialist band rather than the budget one. The trial lesson is free and nothing is charged before it. Where the marked work says a bounded data-analysis and technique block will move the grade faster than a term of content teaching, we will quote the block, which is the smaller sale and usually the better purchase.

sections.heading: Starting physics support from Muhaisnah
paragraphs: Send the level, the most recent marked script and the school's weekly timetable. The marked script is the important one: it tells a physics specialist within two minutes whether the losses are graphs, uncertainty, definitions or genuine content, and those four need entirely different work. A description of the problem in words usually points at the wrong one, because students report content difficulty when the marks say technique.

Expect a slightly longer wait than for mathematics. Standard Level physics typically reaches a trial inside a week; Higher Level takes four to seven days and sometimes longer, and the specialist may be based outside the UAE teaching at a Gulf Standard Time slot. We will say that rather than offering you a chemistry teacher who is willing to try, because the difference will surface in the second year when fields and quantum behaviour arrive.

At the trial, run the three requests from the previous section. Then agree one narrow capability for session six: propagating a percentage uncertainty through a power without prompting, stating the physical meaning of a gradient every time, or giving the exact definition of a named quantity. All three are visible in a marked script, so the review is evidence rather than impression.

And if your child is in the first year, consider spending the first block on uncertainty, graphs and the investigation question rather than on the current theme. Those three transfer across the whole two years, they are the most reliably recoverable marks on the course, and they are entirely within the student's control. Families who start with the theme they are currently failing almost always come back for the other three later, having paid twice.

faqs.question: Why is it harder to find an IB physics tutor than a maths tutor here?
faqs.answer: Because the supply genuinely is thinner, particularly at Higher Level. Physics graduates who teach well are scarce in most markets, and around Muhaisnah the school catchment is dominated by Indian and British curricula, so the local tutoring supply is strong on CBSE and IGCSE physics and weak on the Diploma. Expect four to seven days to match Higher Level properly, sometimes longer, and expect the specialist to be based outside the UAE teaching at a Gulf Standard Time slot. We would rather state the wait than offer a chemistry teacher willing to attempt it.

faqs.question: What are the five themes in the current IB physics course?
faqs.answer: Space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Each carries additional higher-level content examined in the same papers rather than separately, which is the detail that catches students out: revising the shared content thoroughly and the extension material lightly produces a capped grade with no warning. Ask any prospective tutor to name the themes without looking. Somebody describing numbered core topics and an option is working from superseded material. Confirm the current structure against your child's subject guide.

faqs.question: How is IB physics examined at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Across two written papers plus the scientific investigation, with no separate third paper, which distinguishes it from Higher Level mathematics. Paper 1 contains a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section and carries 36%. Paper 2 is extended response and carries 44%. The investigation carries 20%. At Higher Level Paper 1 runs two hours and Paper 2 two and a half, covering the extension content in the same components. Confirm durations and weightings against the current subject guide for your child's cohort, because they are revised when a guide is reissued.

faqs.question: My child can do the calculations but still loses marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly graph meaning, uncertainty and definitions. The largest single loss in physics is calculating a gradient correctly and failing to state what physical quantity it represents, because the question asked for meaning and received arithmetic. The second is uncertainty: absolute, fractional and percentage, propagated through calculations and shown on graphs. The third is definition precision, where a near-miss scores nothing rather than partial credit. All three are visible on a marked script and all three respond within weeks, which is faster than any content work.

faqs.question: What is the physics investigation marked out of?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four marks across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and it carries 20% of the subject grade. Most of the outcome is decided before any readings are taken, because research design and the quality of what can be analysed depend on the question and the variables chosen. A good investigation built on a poor question is not possible, which is why one session on question viability at the start outperforms five sessions on the write-up at the end.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the physics investigation without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is specific. A tutor may explain what each of the four criteria asks for, interrogate the research question, the variables and the control of conditions, check that uncertainties have been propagated properly, and read the student's own draft to say which descriptor is not yet met. A tutor may not write, restructure or complete any part of it, supply data, or perform the analysis. After a useful session the student holds three problems to fix and the document contains nothing the tutor produced.

faqs.question: How are physics practicals covered if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Apparatus time belongs to the school, which has the equipment, and no online tutor replaces it. What the Diploma assesses in writing is substantial and much of it is taught better on a screen: recording to appropriate precision, choosing ranges, distinguishing systematic from random error, tabulating with consistent significant figures, plotting, linearising and extracting a gradient with its physical meaning. A tutor annotating your child's actual graph live does more in five minutes than a comment in an exercise book that goes home a week later.

faqs.question: Which physics theme causes the most trouble in the first year?
faqs.answer: Fields, consistently, in enquiries from this catchment. The analogies between gravitational, electric and magnetic fields are load-bearing and are rarely taught explicitly, so students learn three apparently unrelated sets of equations and lose the reasoning that connects them. Inverse-square relationships and algebraic confidence are both assumed. A secondary trouble spot is nuclear and quantum physics, not because it is harder but because it is usually taught late in the second year and therefore revised least and lost most.

faqs.question: Is my child's physics difficulty actually a maths problem?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and the distinction decides what to buy. Rearrangement, proportional reasoning, logarithms, trigonometry and small-angle approximations all underpin Diploma physics, and a student weak in those will look weak at physics while more physics teaching has little effect. A specialist can separate the two from a marked script in minutes: if the physics reasoning is sound and the algebra collapses, the remedy is mathematical fluency. Students entering from a Core or Foundation IGCSE tier face the sharpest version of this in their first term.

faqs.question: Do we need Higher Level physics for engineering?
faqs.answer: It is required or strongly expected for engineering across most destinations, usually alongside Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, which means a student aiming that way carries two demanding Higher Level subjects and little slack. Requirements are stated by subject and level on each university's own admissions page, and that is where to check rather than on any tutoring page including this one. For medicine the picture varies by country and institution and chemistry and biology are more commonly the required pair, with physics useful rather than mandatory.

faqs.question: What does Diploma physics support cost in eastern Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with one agency publishing IB from AED 200, and specialists across IB, IGCSE and A Level at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with one UK agency publishing AED 270 and a premium examiner-branded provider at AED 650. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Higher Level physics sits toward the specialist end because fewer people can teach it, not because the hour is different.

faqs.question: Should we start physics support in the first or second year?
faqs.answer: The first year, and the money goes much further there. Diploma physics is cumulative: second-year content assumes the first year is secure, and a gap left in fields in the first term is still costing marks in the final paper. The best first-year purchase is not more coverage of the current theme but uncertainty handling, graph interpretation and the investigation question, because all three transfer across both years and all three are the most recoverable marks on the course. Second-year work is triage by comparison.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting physics tutoring six weeks before the exams?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only for a specific kind of work. Six weeks is enough to drill the data-analysis section, uncertainty propagation, gradient-meaning questions and definition precision, which together account for a substantial share of lost marks and are independent of content confidence. Six weeks is not enough to rebuild fields or quantum physics from scratch, and a provider telling you otherwise is selling hope. Send the marked script and we will say which of the two situations your child is in before taking a booking.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor teach physics and maths for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: It is the one pairing where a single specialist genuinely works, because both reward stated method, careful algebra and interpretation of graphs. It still requires somebody who teaches both courses habitually rather than one who will attempt the second. Test it directly: ask them to recite the assessment structure for each separately. A tutor who mentions a third paper in physics has confused it with Higher Level mathematics, which tells you the physics preparation is thin and will show when fields arrive.

intro.heading: Physics marks move on a timetable, not on effort
paragraphs: There are two distinct physics problems and they arrive at different points in the Diploma calendar. The first is the internal assessment, a single piece of independent investigative work carrying twenty per cent of the grade, which appears in the spring of DP1 or the autumn of DP2 depending on the school and is almost always underestimated. The second is the examination papers, where capable students lose marks not on physics but on uncertainties, graph handling, command terms and the arithmetic that physics wraps around itself.

Each problem has a window. The internal assessment is decided at the point the research question is chosen, because a question that cannot generate a sufficient range of data, or whose relationship is linear and therefore trivial to analyse, caps the available marks before a single measurement is taken. Fixing that takes an hour in the week the question is being chosen. Fixing it after the data has been collected takes a repeat of the whole investigation, which schools rarely permit and students rarely have time for.

The examination problem has a longer window and a harder floor. Content that was never understood in DP1 can still be rebuilt in the autumn of DP2. By February the honest work is technique: uncertainty propagation, linearising a relationship to test it, reading command terms properly, and the discipline of carrying units and significant figures through a multi-step calculation. Those are worth a great deal and they are not the same as learning more physics.

Nad Al Hamar is a residential district on the eastern side of Dubai, between the Ras Al Khor sanctuary and the Dubai-Al Ain Road, whose children travel out to schools in Festival City, Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Academic City. There is no Diploma school in the district and almost no chance of a resident Higher Level physics specialist. Searching by distance returns a list of generalists; the subject needs somebody who has marked a data-analysis section against the published criteria.

Teaching is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, at a fixed weekly hour. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, because home tutoring is a service we run in India only. For physics specifically the online format has a concrete advantage beyond availability: graphing software, uncertainty calculations and a student's own data set sit on a shared screen where both people can work on them, which a kitchen table cannot reproduce. What follows is the assessment taken apart component by component, the four internal assessment criteria with their mark allocations, the DP2 countdown stretch by stretch, uncertainty handling in full, the mathematics physics assumes, and what physics help actually costs in this market with every figure attributed to whoever published it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-nad-al-hamar.subjectsIntro: Physics divides into content areas and into skills that cut across all of them. These are what a physics tutor should be able to take apart by name.

subjects.name: Mechanics and kinematics
subjects.description: Motion, forces, momentum and energy. Usually the strongest area for Dubai students because it is the most familiar from IGCSE, and the place where a student's confidence is set for the rest of the course. Marks go to sign conventions and to treating momentum problems as energy problems.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, the gas laws and the kinetic model. Short, heavily examined and routinely under-revised. Errors cluster around unit conversion and around assuming a process is isothermal when the question has not said so.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, superposition, standing waves, diffraction and interference, with additional Higher Level material. Phase relationships are the persistent difficulty, and students who can reproduce the formulae frequently cannot say what is happening physically.

subjects.name: Electricity and magnetism
subjects.description: Circuits, fields, electromagnetic induction and at Higher Level more demanding field work. The area most often named by parents as the problem, and usually it is a circuit-reasoning problem rather than a formula problem: students cannot say what happens when a component changes.

subjects.name: Fields and gravitation
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric field strength, potential, orbital motion and escape conditions. Mathematically the most demanding part of the Higher Level course, and the clearest case of physics marks being lost to algebra rather than to physics.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, the photoelectric effect and at Higher Level more detail. Heavy on definitions that must be stated precisely, which makes command-term discipline worth more here than almost anywhere else in the course.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error treatment
subjects.levels: All levels, examined and internally assessed
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through sums and products, uncertainty bars on graphs and the uncertainty in a gradient. Not a topic the course lists prominently and the single most recoverable source of lost marks in the subject.

subjects.name: Graph handling and linearisation
subjects.description: Rearranging a relationship so that a straight-line graph can test it, then extracting a physical quantity from the gradient or intercept. Appears in the data-analysis section and in the internal assessment, and is a mathematics skill that physics teaching often assumes rather than teaches.

subjects.name: The internal assessment
subjects.description: One independent investigation, marked against four criteria of six marks each, carrying twenty per cent of the final grade. Research design and data analysis carry most of the risk, and the mark ceiling is effectively set by the research question.

sections.heading: What the physics assessment is actually made of
paragraphs: Physics at both levels is assessed through written papers plus one internally assessed investigation. The investigation carries twenty per cent of the grade and is marked by the school against four criteria before being moderated. The written papers include a multiple-choice section, a data-analysis section and an extended-response paper, with additional material examined at Higher Level. Exact weightings are set in the current subject guide, which is revised, so confirm them with your teacher rather than with a tutoring page.

What matters more than the weightings is that these components fail students in different ways. The multiple-choice section punishes shaky definitions and sign conventions, because there is nowhere to show reasoning and partial credit does not exist. The data-analysis section punishes students who have never processed their own uncertainty-bearing data, which is a surprising number given that they have all done practical work. The extended-response paper punishes command-term blindness and poor algebra more than it punishes gaps in physics.

The investigation fails earlier than any of them, at the research question. A question whose independent variable cannot be varied across a useful range, or whose relationship is a simple proportionality that needs no real analysis, puts a ceiling on the data analysis criterion and therefore on the total. Students choose questions for interest and availability of equipment, which are reasonable criteria and not the ones the marking rewards.

The practical reading for a parent is that physics support should be bought for a named component rather than for the subject. A student losing marks on the data-analysis section and a student losing marks on extended response need different sessions, and a tutor should be able to say which from a marked paper in a few minutes.

sections.heading: The four internal assessment criteria, with their marks
paragraphs: The physics internal assessment is marked against four criteria, each worth six marks, giving twenty-four before any scaling. Naming them matters because students work on the wrong one. Research design covers the question, the methodology and the control of variables. Data analysis covers the processing, the treatment of uncertainty and the graphing. Conclusion covers the interpretation of the result against accepted physics. Evaluation covers the critique of the method and realistic improvements.

Research design is where the mark ceiling is set. A question must be focused and must permit genuine variation of an independent variable across a range wide enough for a relationship to emerge above the noise. Students lose marks for vague questions, for ignoring variables that obviously need controlling, and for methodologies that cannot actually produce the data the question demands. All of that is fixable in one session held before the laboratory work, and effectively unfixable afterwards.

Data analysis is where the most marks are routinely lost by students who did everything else well. It requires uncertainties carried through the processing rather than quoted at the end, uncertainty bars on the graph, a gradient with its own uncertainty, and enough processing to test the relationship rather than merely display the data. A student who plots raw data with no uncertainty bars has given away a large share of six marks regardless of how good the experiment was.

Conclusion and evaluation are shorter and more tractable. Conclusion needs the result compared against accepted physics with reference to a source, and a statement about whether the uncertainty permits that comparison to be meaningful. Evaluation needs specific weaknesses with specific improvements, not a list of generic limitations. A tutor can teach both directly, because they are forms of writing about evidence rather than physics content.

sections.heading: The DP2 physics countdown, stretch by stretch
paragraphs: Counting backwards from the May session, physics has a clear shape. The last six to eight weeks are for timed papers and error correction, with uncertainty and graph technique drilled because those are the most recoverable marks at that point. New content learned in this stretch rarely reaches a paper, and a provider selling content recovery in April is selling something they cannot deliver.

The stretch from the mock window to the spring break is for acting on the mock. The marked script tells you which of four things is happening: content not known, content known but misapplied, arithmetic and uncertainty errors, or command terms misread. Those four need different sessions, and a parent who reads the grade rather than the script will buy the wrong one. This is also the stretch in which the internal assessment must be finished if it is not already.

The autumn term of DP2 is the last content window. Fields, electromagnetic induction and the quantitative Higher Level material are the usual candidates, and they can genuinely be rebuilt here. It is also when the internal assessment deadline typically lands, which is why this term is overloaded and why doing the design work in DP1 matters so much. Two things competing for the same eight weeks is how capable students lose marks in both.

DP1 is where the leverage is and where almost nobody buys help. The research question gets chosen in the spring. The habits that determine whether a student carries uncertainties properly get set in the first term. The algebra that physics assumes can be repaired cheaply before it becomes a physics problem. An hour a week in DP1 is worth several hours a week in DP2, and it costs the same per hour.

sections.heading: Uncertainties: the physics that is really arithmetic
paragraphs: Uncertainty handling is the most recoverable source of lost marks in IB physics and the least systematically taught. The content is small. Absolute uncertainty is the raw spread on a measurement. Fractional and percentage uncertainty is that spread relative to the value. Uncertainties add in absolute terms when quantities are added or subtracted, and add in fractional terms when quantities are multiplied or divided. A power multiplies the fractional uncertainty by the exponent. That is nearly the whole of it.

Where students fail is in carrying it through. A student computes a value from three measurements, quotes it to five significant figures, and then appends an uncertainty invented at the end. Another plots a graph with no uncertainty bars and extracts a gradient with no uncertainty, which removes any basis for saying whether the result agrees with accepted physics. Both are mechanical failures and both are fixed by drilling rather than by explanation, which is why frequency beats depth in these sessions.

The second half of the same skill is linearisation. A relationship that is not linear can be rearranged so that a straight-line graph tests it, and the physical quantity then comes from the gradient or the intercept. Period against length is not linear; period squared against length is. Students who have only ever plotted what the worksheet told them to plot cannot do this with an unfamiliar relationship, and the data-analysis section asks exactly that.

Significant figures and units are the third part and are worth a surprising number of marks across a paper. The rule is to work to full precision throughout and round once, at the end, to a number of figures justified by the least precise measurement. Units must be carried, including through rearrangement, because a dimensionally wrong answer is marked as wrong even when the arithmetic was right. A thirty-second check at the end of each question, practised until automatic, is the whole remedy.

sections.heading: Practical work, and how physics tutoring handles it online
paragraphs: A fair question from parents: if physics is a practical subject, how does a video session help. The answer separates the parts of practical work that need apparatus from the parts that do not. Taking the measurements needs apparatus and happens at school, under supervision, as it must. Everything surrounding it, designing the method, deciding the range and the number of repeats, processing the data, propagating uncertainties, plotting, linearising, extracting a gradient and writing the evaluation, is desk work.

Desk work is where almost all the marks live, and it is where a shared screen beats a kitchen table. The student's own spreadsheet, their own graph and their own uncertainty calculations are open in front of both people, and the tutor can annotate them in place. Graphing software can be driven jointly. A gradient uncertainty can be worked through twice. None of that requires anybody to be in the room, and the written record survives the session in a way a conversation over a notebook does not.

For the examination's data-analysis section the practical dimension is entirely absent anyway: the student is handed somebody else's data and asked to process it. That is a desk skill being assessed as a desk skill, and it is the single most trainable part of the physics papers. Students who have only processed data from their own tidy experiments find unfamiliar data unsettling, and the remedy is volume of unfamiliar data sets.

Where a video session genuinely cannot help is apparatus familiarity, and that gap should be named rather than glossed. A student who has not handled the equipment will write a method that cannot be executed. The fix is the school's laboratory, not a tutor, and a good tutor will tell a student to go and try the method before writing it up rather than pretend the design can be perfected from a desk.

sections.heading: The mathematics inside physics, and the course pairing that matters
paragraphs: A sizeable share of what parents report as a physics problem is a mathematics problem wearing a physics label. Rearranging a formula with the unknown in a denominator. Handling indices and standard form under time pressure. Working with logarithms when a relationship is exponential. Resolving vectors. Using small-angle approximations. Differentiating or recognising a rate of change in a kinematics context. Each of these is examined inside physics questions and taught, if at all, in mathematics lessons.

The practical consequence is that a physics tutor who cannot teach the mathematics will plateau. A student who understands electromagnetic induction conceptually and cannot rearrange the resulting expression will score as though they understood nothing. Conversely a student with secure algebra often finds Higher Level physics tractable even when the concepts are unfamiliar, because the questions reward correct manipulation of a stated relationship.

This feeds the course-pairing question families ask in Year 11. Physics at Higher Level alongside Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is possible and is harder than it looks, because the algebraic fluency that physics assumes is exactly what Applications and Interpretation trims. Physics at Higher Level alongside Analysis and Approaches is the natural pairing and the one most engineering and physical-science degrees expect in some combination. Check the specific requirements on the specific university course page rather than relying on a general rule.

For a student already in the awkward pairing, the remedy is narrow and achievable: a block of sessions on rearrangement, indices, logarithms and vector resolution, taught for physics rather than for mathematics. Six to eight hours removes most of the handicap, and it is a far cheaper intervention than a term of general physics support that keeps running into the same wall.

sections.heading: What physics help costs, priced by what you are fixing
paragraphs: Price the problem rather than the subject. A research question screening session is one or two hours and sits at the top of the value table because it protects a share of twenty per cent of the grade. An uncertainty and linearisation block is four to six hours and recovers marks across every paper. A content rebuild in fields and induction is eight to twelve weeks. A final technique block is six to eight weeks. Those are four different purchases and families tend to buy the last one only.

The market figures, each published by the provider named and read in October 2026: a qualified subject tutor online is quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. Matching tier of tutor to task is where the saving is. Uncertainty drilling and timed-paper marking do not require a specialist at the top of the range. Research question screening and Higher Level field work do. Buying the premium tier for everything is the commonest overspend in this market, and no agency will point it out.
