sections.heading: The honesty line on an investigation, and what we refuse
paragraphs: The physics internal assessment is the student's own work and the school attests to it. That makes the boundary on help a matter of the candidate's exposure rather than ours. A malpractice finding falls on the student and can cost them the diploma, and at least one site ranking for these searches sells completed internal assessments outright. We do not, at any price, and we say so to the student in the first session rather than leaving it implied.

What a physics tutor may do is substantial. Teach the content the investigation requires. Explain what each of the four criteria rewards and how the six marks are distributed within it. Discuss whether a proposed research question can generate usable data, which is advice about feasibility rather than about content. Demonstrate a complete worked analysis on an entirely different data set so the student can see what good processing looks like. Read the student's own draft and ask questions: why this range, what justifies that number of repeats, where does this uncertainty come from, does the conclusion follow from the gradient.

What a tutor may not do is choose the question, design the method for the student, process the student's data, write or rewrite any section, or edit the draft into shape. The difference between the two lists is whether the intellectual work is the student's. A useful test: if the student cannot explain every line of their own write-up to their teacher without hesitation, the help went too far, and that is a problem for them rather than for us.

We also do not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. They belong to the IB, the official sites publish what is public, and your child's school has proper access to the assessment material. A tutor working from that material inside a session is ordinary practice. A site hosting a download library of it is distributing someone else's property.

faqs.question: How is the IB physics internal assessment marked, and what is it worth?
faqs.answer: Against four criteria, each worth six marks, giving twenty-four before scaling, and it carries twenty per cent of the physics grade. The criteria are research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design sets the ceiling, because a question whose independent variable cannot be varied across a useful range limits what the analysis can show. Data analysis is where most marks are lost by students who did the experiment well, usually through plotting raw data with no uncertainty bars and extracting a gradient with no uncertainty attached.

faqs.question: Our physics research question is already chosen and the data collected. What can still be done?
faqs.answer: The analysis, the conclusion and the evaluation, which between them carry eighteen of the twenty-four marks, so a great deal. Uncertainties can be propagated properly, the data can be linearised so the relationship is tested rather than displayed, a gradient can be given its own uncertainty, the result can be compared against accepted physics with a cited source, and the evaluation can be made specific rather than generic. What cannot be fixed is a question that could never generate usable data, which is why screening belongs before collection.

faqs.question: Why is our child strong in physics lessons and weaker in physics exams?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three things, and a marked script tells you which. Uncertainty handling, where the physics is right and the treatment of error is absent or invented at the end. Command terms, where explain, deduce, outline and justify are all answered as though they said describe. Or algebra, where the concept is understood and the rearrangement under time pressure is not. All three are technique rather than content, all three are recoverable in weeks, and none of them is addressed by covering more syllabus.

faqs.question: What exactly does uncertainty propagation require us to do?
faqs.answer: Add absolute uncertainties when quantities are added or subtracted, add fractional uncertainties when they are multiplied or divided, and multiply the fractional uncertainty by the exponent when a quantity is raised to a power. Then carry that through the whole calculation rather than appending something at the end, put uncertainty bars on the graph, and give the gradient its own uncertainty. That last step is what makes a comparison with accepted physics meaningful, and most students omit it.

faqs.question: Can physics really be tutored without apparatus in the room?
faqs.answer: The measurements need apparatus and belong at school under supervision. Everything else is desk work: method design, deciding range and repeats, processing, uncertainty propagation, plotting, linearising, extracting a gradient and writing the evaluation. That is where almost all the marks are, and a shared screen with your child's own spreadsheet and graph open on it is better for that work than a kitchen table. The data-analysis section of the examination hands students somebody else's data, which is pure desk skill.

faqs.question: When in DP1 should we start thinking about the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: By the spring, and earlier if your school's internal deadline is early, which in the Festival City cluster it tends to be. The research question is the single decision that caps the mark, and screening it takes an hour. Ask the physics teacher when the question has to be agreed, then plan a session for the fortnight before that date. Students who leave it until the DP2 autumn are choosing a question in the same term as the write-up deadline, with everything else in six subjects happening at once.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics possible alongside Maths Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Possible and harder than it looks. Physics at Higher Level assumes sustained algebraic fluency, logarithmic handling and vector work, and Applications and Interpretation trims exactly that material in favour of statistics and modelling. A student in that pairing is not disadvantaged conceptually but is handicapped mechanically. Six to eight hours on rearrangement, indices, logarithms and vector resolution, taught for physics rather than for mathematics, removes most of the handicap and is far cheaper than a term of general physics support.

faqs.question: Which physics topics most often need rebuilding in the DP2 autumn?
faqs.answer: Fields and gravitation, and electromagnetic induction, at Higher Level. Both are mathematically demanding and both arrive at a point in DP1 when students are still adjusting to the course, so they are frequently half-learned. Thermal physics is a smaller but common one, usually under-revised because it is short. The autumn of DP2 is the last stretch in which any of these can genuinely be rebuilt rather than merely revised, and a provider offering content recovery in April is overpromising.

faqs.question: What does a physics specialist cost in Dubai close to the exams?
faqs.answer: Expect the upper part of the market bands. Qualified subject tutors online are quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named tutors at AED 500 to 650 and more, with BartyED at AED 650. Bestimate's monthly estimate for an examination-year specialist on a weekly hour is AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026; we quote after a free trial.

faqs.answer: The Dubai Festival City cluster, including Deira International School and Universal American School Dubai, and the Mirdif belt, including Uptown International School, with other eastern-suburb schools taking students to IGCSE before a Diploma or A Level split. Whether a school runs physics at Higher Level in a given year can depend on cohort size, so it is worth asking the coordinator rather than assuming. Schools are named here as local context only, with no affiliation or endorsement implied.

faqs.question: Our child came from MYP integrated science rather than IGCSE physics. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It changes what the first term needs. A student from MYP integrated science usually has better investigative instincts, because criteria B and C in MYP sciences rehearse exactly the design and processing the Diploma investigation asks for. What they often lack is the quantitative security that a separate IGCSE physics course builds: formula rearrangement, unit handling and the volume of numerical practice. A student from IGCSE physics has the reverse profile. Both are fixable in the DP1 autumn and cheaply.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week make sense in DP2?
faqs.answer: One during term time if the problem is a single content area or a technique gap, rising to two in the final eight to ten weeks when timed papers and their review both need hours. Beyond two the limiting factor becomes the student's own practice time, and a Diploma candidate carrying six subjects, Theory of Knowledge and an Extended Essay has less spare capacity than an hourly plan assumes. Start at one, measure the error categories, and add only if the measurement says to.

faqs.question: Will you help write up the investigation if we are short of time?
faqs.answer: No, and the refusal is in your child's interest rather than ours. We will teach the content, explain how the six marks sit within each criterion, advise on whether a question is feasible, demonstrate a full worked analysis on a completely different data set, and read your child's own draft and ask questions about range, repeats, uncertainty and whether the conclusion follows from the gradient. We will not choose the question, process the data, write a section or edit the draft. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: What should a first physics session produce for us?
faqs.answer: A named component, a named skill and a named habit. Not weak on electricity, but cannot reason about what happens to the current when one resistor changes; not careless, but appends an uncertainty at the end instead of propagating it. The tutor should also say what they would deliberately leave alone, because a plan to fix everything is a plan built on no diagnosis. What it should not produce is a predicted grade or a promised improvement, and a provider offering one is selling rather than teaching.

intro.heading: Is it physics, or is it the combination?
paragraphs: Most families who go looking for an IB physics tutor in Nad Al Sheba are reacting to a specific event: a DP1 report, a failed topic test, or a mock grade two bands below the predicted one. The instinct is to treat physics as the problem and buy physics hours. Often that is right. Just as often the problem is comparative — physics is the subject that broke first under a load three Higher Level subjects were always going to create, and fixing it in isolation moves the breakage somewhere else.

So this page is written as a comparison. Physics against chemistry, as the second HL science a student might have chosen instead. Physics against the maths course underneath it, which is more often the real constraint than the physics itself. The investigation against the two other internal assessments competing for the same weeks. And the Nad Al Sheba school cluster against the one next door, which turns out to matter far less than any of the above.

The district context is worth having. Repton School Dubai, Kings' School Nad Al Sheba and GEMS Modern Academy sit inside Nad Al Sheba; Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai are in Sobha Hartland; Swiss International Scientific School Dubai is at Al Jaddaf. Dubai held 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across seventeen licensed curricula, with the IB accounting for around 7% of enrolment. Physics Higher Level cohorts in individual schools are small, which has a direct consequence for tutoring: the pool of local specialists is small for the same reason.

That is the structural argument for online delivery in this subject specifically. A Nad Al Sheba family looking for somebody who teaches IB Physics at Higher Level, knows the current five-theme syllabus rather than the previous options-based one, and has marked investigations against the four criteria, is looking for a narrow specialism. Within a twenty-minute drive that person may not exist. Within the timezone they do.

IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For physics there is also a practical gain: on a shared screen a graph can be plotted live, a gradient taken from it, and the official mark scheme read beside the student's own working, all without anything being passed across a table.

One practical instruction before the detail, because it shortens everything that follows. Bring a marked script rather than a report card to the first conversation: a topic test, a mock paper, a returned data-analysis question, anything with annotations still on it. A grade tells you how large the problem is. A script tells you whether the lost marks were theme content the student never met, command terms misread under time pressure, or algebra that failed halfway through a rearrangement. Those three diagnoses lead to three different purchases, and buying the wrong one is the most common way a term of physics tutoring in this corridor gets spent without the grade moving at all.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences
programmes.description: MYP sciences are marked on four criteria out of 8 each, including scientific inquiry and reflecting on the impacts of science. Students who score well on knowledge and poorly on inquiry are the ones who later struggle with the Diploma investigation, because the investigation is an inquiry task rather than a knowledge task. Identifying that pattern in Year 10 is far cheaper than discovering it in DP2.

Students arriving in DP1 from IGCSE physics have met most of the mechanics and electricity content and almost none of the quantum and nuclear material, and they have been trained to write more detail than an IB mark scheme rewards. dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.subjectsIntro: Physics is one subject with five themes and two levels, and the tutoring decision is made at theme level. Below are the themes and the components Nad Al Sheba students bring, described by where the marks actually go in each.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.levels: HL and SL, HL extension included
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, with circular motion and at Higher Level relativistic ideas. The strand where IGCSE students feel most at home and therefore the one they revise most and gain least from. Marks go in unstated assumptions and in using an average velocity where an instantaneous one was required.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.levels: HL and SL, HL extension included
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, internal energy and at Higher Level entropy and engine cycles. Sign conventions in the first law cost two marks at a time, reliably, and students who can state the law often cannot apply it to a compression. Graph work on pressure-volume cycles rewards reading the axes before the question.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.levels: HL and SL, HL extension included
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave properties, superposition, standing waves and Doppler effects, with Higher Level extensions on diffraction and resolution. The single most common loss is confusing path difference with phase difference, and the second is sketching a standing wave without marking nodes.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.levels: HL and SL, HL extension included
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, circuits, electromagnetic induction and at Higher Level field potential and capacitance. Circuit questions reward redrawing the circuit before calculating. Induction questions reward stating which flux is changing, which is the step most students skip straight past.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.levels: HL and SL, HL extension included
subjects.description: Radioactivity, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect, matter waves and at Higher Level quantum tunnelling and nuclear binding. The theme IGCSE students have met least, which makes it the most common genuine content gap in a DP2 diagnostic and the one worth front-loading.

subjects.name: Paper 1A: Multiple choice
subjects.description: Thirty to forty questions depending on level, no marks for method, and therefore the paper where guessing strategy and pace matter as much as knowledge. Students lose marks by spending four minutes on one question and then rushing six. Timed practice on sections of ten is the drill.

subjects.name: Paper 1B: Data analysis
subjects.description: Experimental data, graphs, uncertainties and evaluation of a method. Highly predictable in structure and under-practised, which makes it the best return on tutoring time in the whole subject. Uncertainty propagation and gradient-with-error work are mechanical once taught properly.

subjects.name: Paper 2: Extended response
subjects.description: Structured longer questions across the themes, where command terms decide the mark. An answer that explains when the question said state scores the state marks only. Students who write a paragraph for a two-mark question run out of time on the last page, which is where the heaviest questions sit.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An individual experimental or data-based investigation marked on four criteria over 24 marks with a 3,000-word limit. Research design and evaluation are the criteria most often scored low, and both reward specificity about variables and limitations rather than more data.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error analysis
subjects.levels: Both levels, examined in Paper 1B and the investigation
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and uncertainty bars with best and worst-fit gradients. Taught once in most schools and assessed repeatedly, which is why it appears as a gap in the majority of physics diagnostics in this corridor.

subjects.name: Mathematical requirements for physics
subjects.description: Logarithms, trigonometry, vector resolution and at Higher Level calculus-shaped reasoning. A student on Applications and Interpretation Standard Level taking Physics Higher Level is carrying a genuine gap here, and it is more often the real cause of poor physics marks than the physics content is.

subjects.name: Practical skills and the lab programme

sections.heading: Physics against chemistry: which Higher Level science is harder here?
paragraphs: This is the comparison a DP1 student in Nad Al Sheba is usually making privately before a parent makes it out loud. Both sciences carry a 20% investigation, both examine Higher Level extension content alongside the core, and both punish command-term carelessness. They are hard in different places, and knowing where helps a family decide whether to get support or to consider a change while a change is still possible.

Physics is more mathematical and more front-loaded on reasoning. A student who can resolve vectors, handle logarithms and rearrange fluently will find the content tractable even when it is unfamiliar. A student whose maths is shaky will struggle in physics regardless of how well they understand the ideas, because the marks sit in the execution. That is why the maths course underneath is so often the real diagnosis.

Chemistry is more memory-dense and more sensitive to precision in language. Organic mechanisms, equilibrium sign conventions and definitions that must be stated exactly carry marks that physics awards for reasoning instead. A student with a strong verbal memory and weak algebra will usually find chemistry the kinder of the two; the reverse student will find physics so.

The practical conclusion for a Nad Al Sheba family mid-DP1 is narrow. If the physics marks are poor and the maths marks are also poor, the physics tutoring should start with the mathematical requirements, not with theme content. If the physics marks are poor and the maths is strong, the diagnosis is usually command terms and Paper 1B technique, which is a short fix. Switching subject is the right answer rarely, and only in the first weeks when the investigation has not begun.

sections.heading: The papers, the weightings and the themes behind them
paragraphs: Parents are rarely shown how a physics grade is assembled, and it is worth seeing. Paper 1 carries 36% and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section. Paper 2 carries 44% in structured extended response. The scientific investigation carries 20% at both levels. Standard Level runs 150 teaching hours and Higher Level 240, which is the honest measure of the step between them.

The current syllabus is organised around five themes rather than the older core-plus-options structure, and Higher Level extension content sits inside those themes rather than in a separate paper. That has a direct teaching consequence that some tutors have not caught up with: a Higher Level student cannot cover the core first and add the extension later, because the extension questions appear alongside the core ones on the same paper and often inside the same question.

Each paper punishes something specific. Paper 1A punishes poor pacing, since there are no method marks and four minutes spent on one question is paid for by six rushed ones. Paper 1B punishes never having practised uncertainty propagation, which is mechanical and under-taught. Paper 2 punishes command-term carelessness and over-writing, because the heaviest questions sit at the end and a student who wrote paragraphs earlier arrives there with no time.

Reading the table below alongside a marked mock script is the most useful twenty minutes a parent can spend. It tells you which of three very different problems you have: content missing from a theme, technique missing on a paper, or time management across the whole sitting. Those need different purchases, and buying the wrong one is how a term gets spent without a grade moving.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria, 24 marks, 3,000 words
paragraphs: A fifth of the physics grade is a piece of written scientific work, and it is the most controllable fifth in the course because it can be planned in daylight. It is marked on four criteria over 24 marks with a 3,000-word limit, and a piece that runs to 4,200 words has not impressed anybody — the excess simply goes unread.

The criteria reward specificity above all. Research design wants the variables named, the control justified and the method capable of actually answering the question asked. Data analysis wants uncertainties carried through rather than mentioned. The conclusion wants a comparison with accepted physics, stated numerically where possible. Evaluation wants limitations identified and their effect on the result reasoned, not a list of ways the experiment could have been better.

The two criteria most often scored low in this corridor are research design and evaluation, and both are failures of specificity rather than of effort. A student who writes 'the temperature was kept constant' without saying how, or 'human error may have affected the results' without saying which measurement and in which direction, has written sentences that score nothing. Translating the criteria wording into a checklist takes twenty minutes and is worth more than another week of data collection.

The honesty boundary is firm and worth stating to the student directly. A tutor may discuss whether a research question is feasible and whether the method can answer it, explain what each criterion asks for, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not design the experiment, produce or clean the data, write any part of the text, or edit the piece to completion. The declaration on the submitted work is the student's, and one page ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright.

sections.heading: The maths course underneath the physics
paragraphs: This is the diagnosis that saves Nad Al Sheba families the most money, and almost nobody checks it first. IB Physics assumes a level of mathematical fluency that the Diploma maths courses deliver unevenly. A student taking Physics Higher Level alongside Applications and Interpretation Standard Level is carrying a real gap, and that gap looks exactly like weakness in physics.

The specific demands are identifiable. Vector resolution for forces and fields. Logarithms for radioactive decay and intensity. Fluent rearrangement for every multi-step calculation. Trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles for wave and circular motion questions. Gradient and area interpretation on every graph. None of those are physics content, and all of them cost physics marks when they are shaky.

The test is cheap. Take a physics question the student got wrong and ask them to do only the algebra, with the physics already set up for them. If they can, the problem is the physics. If they cannot, the problem is the maths, and physics tutoring that ignores that will deliver three months of frustration at specialist rates. In this corridor the second case is more common than parents expect, particularly among students who chose Applications and Interpretation for its reputation as the lighter course.

What follows from that is a different purchase. Sometimes the right answer is four sessions on the mathematical requirements for physics, delivered inside the physics context so the student sees the point, and then a return to theme content. Sometimes it is a parallel maths session for a term. Occasionally it is a conversation with the school about the maths course, which is only possible very early in DP1. All three are better than more physics hours.

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs in an examined year
paragraphs: Start with the figure that actually lands on a card in DP2, because that is the one families in this corridor plan around. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more per month, mid-band support at AED 600 to 1,200, and budget support at AED 240 to 600, all for a weekly one-hour session. Packages published elsewhere in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Translate that into hourly bands and the market reads as follows, all figures read in October 2026 and all belonging to whoever published them. Budget online or undergraduate tutoring runs AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. An IB specialist runs AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 500 including travel. The premium end reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

Physics Higher Level is one of the subjects where the band genuinely matters rather than signalling. Marking a Paper 1B uncertainty question correctly, or judging whether an investigation's research design will clear criterion one, is narrow work. An able undergraduate can revise kinematics with a Standard Level student perfectly well and cannot do either of those things, and pretending the bands are interchangeable would be dishonest in both directions.

The shape of the spend matters more than the rate. The highest-value windows are the term in which the investigation is drafted and the six weeks before papers, and they want different sessions. A family spending a flat monthly figure across two years will have overspent in DP1 term two and run out of room in DP2 term four. Ask any provider for the session length behind the quoted rate, whether VAT is included, and what happens if you stop after one lesson.

sections.heading: Practical work, when the tutoring is online
paragraphs: This is the honest question about online science tutoring and it deserves a straight answer rather than a reassurance. A tutor on video cannot run a practical. The school's laboratory programme, the equipment, the collaborative sciences project and the supervised data collection are the school's job, and nothing about an outside tutor replaces them.

What an online session can do is everything around the practical, which is where the assessed marks actually sit. The investigation is assessed on the write-up, not on laboratory technique: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Paper 1B assesses experimental reasoning on data the student has never collected. So the examined skills are analytical and written, and they are taught at a desk in either format.

In several respects a shared screen is better than a bench for this work. A graph can be plotted live with uncertainty bars, best and worst-fit lines drawn and compared, and a gradient taken while both people watch. A spreadsheet can be built together so the student sees how propagation works rather than being told. The official mark scheme sits open beside the student's own working. None of that is available with one exercise book between two people.

Where a parent should push back on any provider, in any format, is a claim to supply practical results or to produce data for an investigation. That is not tutoring and it is an academic-honesty breach. IB Gram does not host, reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables either; those are the board's copyright and are referenced and linked at ibo.org rather than copied.

sections.heading: The investigation against the two others in the same term
paragraphs: A Higher Level physics student in Nad Al Sheba is not writing one internal assessment. They are writing three, plus a 4,000-word Extended Essay and a 1,600-word Theory of Knowledge essay, and in most schools those land in a cluster across DP2 term four. The failure almost never looks like inability. It looks like a physics investigation written in four days because the maths exploration and a history investigation took the other three weeks.

That makes sequencing a tutoring job as much as a teaching one. The physics investigation benefits from being started early for a specific reason: it depends on data collection, which depends on laboratory access, which depends on the school's timetable. An exploration can be written at a desk the week before it is due. An investigation whose data turns out to be unusable cannot be rescued in a weekend.

The practical approach is to put all five deadlines on one page in September of DP2 and work backwards from the earliest. Decide which piece is being done first and protect its weeks. Decide which piece is going to be done to a competent rather than an excellent standard, because with five components and six subjects something will be, and choosing deliberately beats discovering it in April.

The comparison across subjects is worth naming too. Physics, chemistry and biology investigations share the same four criteria and 24 marks; the maths exploration uses five criteria over 20 marks; history uses three sections over 25. A student who understands that the science investigations are graded on specificity about variables, and the exploration on personal engagement and reflection, can target each rather than writing all five in the same register.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor driving to the villa
paragraphs: For physics the comparison has one feature it does not have in essay subjects: almost all the work is diagrams, graphs and working. That changes which format loses less. Two people reading the same line of working, on the same screen, with the mark scheme beside it, is closer to a laboratory notebook review than to a conversation.

What a travelling tutor gives is presence. A parent can see the session, a student cannot drift to another tab, and drift gets noticed faster in a room. For a DP1 student with attention problems that is a real benefit and this page is not going to argue otherwise. It is also what the market charges roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour extra for, which across a two-year Diploma in a single subject runs to several thousand dirhams.

What online gives is reach, and in physics reach is the decisive factor. A Higher Level physics specialist who knows the current five-theme syllabus and has marked investigations against the four criteria is a narrow profile. Physics Higher Level cohorts in individual Nad Al Sheba schools are small, which means the supply of people who teach it all week is small locally and ample across the timezone.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. sections.heading: Why Nad Al Sheba and Meydan get the same answer
paragraphs: Having made several comparisons on this page, it is worth being explicit about the one that turns out not to matter. A physics student in Nad Al Sheba and a physics student in Meydan, Sobha Hartland or Mohammed Bin Rashid City need the same thing, and it is not available at different quality levels in different postcodes.

The reason is supply. Physics Higher Level is taught to small cohorts in each school, so the number of people within driving distance of any one Dubai community who teach it every week is small everywhere. A family in a well-served district is not better served for this subject than a family three kilometres away; both are drawing from a thin local pool, and both have the whole timezone available if they stop insisting on a car.

What does differ across the four communities is the clock. Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland have schools inside their boundaries and can take a 15:30 session. Meydan runs 16:00 to 16:30 depending on the school. Mohammed Bin Rashid City loses time inside District One's road network before reaching Al Khail. Al Quoz families consistently start latest. Online delivery removes all four differences, because nothing has to travel.

So the recommendation is the same regardless of which of the four you live in: identify whether the problem is the physics, the maths underneath it or the investigation; buy the format that matches that diagnosis; and insist on a tutor matched to the level and the current syllabus rather than to the drive. The free trial lesson exists so that judgement is made by you, before anything is paid, and if the specialist you need is not free this term you get a date rather than a generalist.

faqs.question: Is the IB physics tutoring delivered in Nad Al Sheba itself or online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. For physics the format matters less than the match, because Higher Level cohorts in individual Dubai schools are small and so is the pool of people within driving distance who teach the subject every week. A shared screen also suits the work: a graph with uncertainty bars can be plotted live and a gradient taken while both people watch.

faqs.question: Should my child be doing physics or chemistry at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: They are hard in different places. Physics rewards mathematical execution — vector resolution, logarithms, fluent rearrangement — and punishes a shaky grasp of those regardless of conceptual understanding. Chemistry is more memory-dense and more sensitive to exact language in definitions and sign conventions. Both carry a 20% investigation marked on four criteria over 24 marks, so switching brings no relief on workload. A switch is only sensible in the first weeks of DP1, with evidence rather than relief as the motive.

faqs.question: How is the IB physics grade split between the papers?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section. Paper 2 carries 44% in structured extended response. The scientific investigation carries 20% at both Standard and Higher Level. Standard Level courses run 150 teaching hours and Higher Level 240, which is the real measure of the step between them. A fifth of the grade is therefore settled before any exam, which makes the investigation the most controllable part of the course.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on physics questions they say they understood?
faqs.answer: Three usual causes, and they need different fixes. Command terms: an answer that explains when the paper said state earns the state marks only. Unstated assumptions: a correct calculation that never says which simplification was made. And the mathematics: a student who understands the physics but cannot rearrange fluently loses the execution marks. Take one wrong question and ask them to do only the algebra with the physics already set up. If they cannot, the diagnosis is maths rather than physics.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria on the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth 6 marks for a total of 24, with a 3,000-word limit on the write-up. Research design wants variables named and controls justified rather than asserted. Data analysis wants uncertainties propagated, not merely mentioned. The conclusion wants a numerical comparison against accepted physics. Evaluation wants limitations identified with their direction and effect reasoned, which is why generic references to human error score nothing at all.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the investigation without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Within a clear line, yes. A tutor may discuss whether a research question is feasible, whether the method can actually answer it, and what each criterion asks for, and may give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the experiment, produce or clean data, write any part of the text or edit it to completion. The declaration on the submitted work is the student's. A page ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments, which is a malpractice trigger for the student.

faqs.question: Does the maths course my child chose affect their physics grade?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect. Physics assumes vector resolution, logarithms, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles and fluent rearrangement. Analysis and Approaches builds all of those, and its non-calculator paper reinforces the rearrangement fluency specifically. Applications and Interpretation covers some of them less securely, so a student taking Physics Higher Level alongside Applications and Interpretation Standard Level is carrying a real gap that looks like weakness in physics. It is worth testing for before buying physics hours.

faqs.question: How can online tutoring help with practical work?
faqs.answer: It cannot run the practical, and no honest provider should claim to. The school's laboratory programme, equipment and supervised data collection are the school's job. What a tutor can do is everything the investigation is actually assessed on: research design, variable control, uncertainty treatment, the conclusion's numerical comparison and the evaluation's reasoning. Paper 1B likewise assesses experimental reasoning about data the student never collected. Those are written and analytical skills, taught at a desk in either format.

faqs.question: What is Paper 1B and why is it the easiest part to improve?
faqs.answer: It is the data-analysis section of Paper 1: experimental data, graphs, uncertainties and evaluation of a method. It is highly predictable in structure and under-practised in most schools, which is an unusual combination. Uncertainty propagation, best and worst-fit gradients and error bars are mechanical once taught properly, so three or four focused sessions move the score in a way that three or four sessions of theme revision rarely do. It is the best return per hour available in IB physics.

faqs.question: Which physics theme do students most often arrive missing?
faqs.answer: Nuclear and quantum physics. Students coming from IGCSE physics have met mechanics and electricity in some depth and this material hardly at all, so it shows up as a genuine content gap in most DP2 diagnostics rather than as a technique issue. The practical consequence is that it should be front-loaded rather than left to the end of a revision plan, which is where it usually sits because syllabus order puts it last.

faqs.question: How do we manage three internal assessments landing in the same term?
faqs.answer: Put all five deadlines on one page in September of DP2 — three internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay — and work backwards from the earliest. Start the physics investigation first, because it depends on laboratory access and on data that might turn out unusable, which cannot be rescued in a weekend. Then decide deliberately which component will be done to a competent rather than an excellent standard, since with six subjects something will be.

faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026: budget online tutoring AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; a qualified subject tutor online AED 150 to 300, Unitors listing IB from AED 200; an IB specialist AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase publishing AED 270; in-home visits AED 180 to 500 including travel; and a premium end reaching AED 650 at BartyED. Monthly, Bestimate puts specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more.

faqs.question: Is it worth hiring a specialist rather than a general science tutor?
faqs.answer: For Standard Level theme revision, a strong general science tutor can be perfectly adequate and costs less. For Higher Level, Paper 1B uncertainty work and investigation feedback, it is genuinely different work: judging whether a research design will clear criterion one, or marking uncertainty propagation correctly, is narrow experience. The bands in this market broadly reflect that. Ask any tutor to talk through where marks go on Paper 1B and you will know within ten minutes which you are speaking to.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take physics and maths for the same student?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level, often, and it can be the efficient choice because the maths gap and the physics gap get fixed in the same hour. At Higher Level in both, it is a narrow request: genuine depth in Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 and in Higher Level physics papers rarely sits in one person, and a tutor who stretches to cover both is a generalist with two labels. We will say which case applies rather than filling the slot.

faqs.question: Where can we find the real IB exam dates for physics?
faqs.answer: From your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. UAE schools sit the May session, and that is as specific as this page gets, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Dates circulate on secondary sites and get republished without verification, and a family planning travel around one of those is acting on an unchecked number. One email to the coordinator settles it.

faqs.question: Do you supply past papers, mark schemes or data for the investigation?
faqs.answer: No to all three, for different reasons. Papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are the board's copyright, some of it unreleased, so we reference and link ibo.org rather than hosting or distributing them; your school holds licensed access. Data for an investigation is an academic-honesty matter rather than a copyright one: the student collects and processes their own, and any provider offering to supply results is offering something that puts the student at risk.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-oud-metha.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Diploma Physics at Higher and Standard Level for students at the Diploma schools reachable from Oud Metha, Al Jaddaf and Bur Dubai. Sessions concentrate on the theory, the mathematical handling and the investigation process, with the practical work left where it belongs - in the school laboratory.

intro.heading: The physics that only happens at school, and the hour that handles the rest
paragraphs: Diploma Physics is the subject where the school and a private tutor have the clearest division of labour, and where families most often blur it. The laboratory is the school's. The equipment, the double period, the supervision and the data your child collects with their own hands all live inside the timetable, and nothing bought outside it substitutes for that. What a tutor outside school can do is everything else: the theory, the mathematical handling, the structure of a long-answer response, and the process of turning a practical idea into an investigation that satisfies the criteria.

That division matters more in this belt than elsewhere because of where the Diploma schools sit. The schools on the Oud Metha Road mostly run to sixteen, so a local Physics student has usually moved campus - to Al Jaddaf, across the creek toward Festival City, or out to Nad Al Sheba. Their day is longer than their younger siblings' and their journey home is longer too. By the time they are back in Karama or Al Mankhool, the practical work is behind them and what remains is the hardest part of the subject to do alone.

The second feature of a Physics week is the double period. Science timetables cluster, so most Diploma Physics students have one or two days where science dominates and other days where it barely appears. Those heavy days are the worst possible evenings for a Physics session: the student is saturated. The light days are the best, because the subject gets refreshed in a week where it would otherwise go quiet for four days. Almost nobody books on this basis, because the family does not have the timetable in front of them when they choose a slot.

Then there is the mathematics, which is the real reason most Diploma Physics students stall. Physics Higher Level assumes algebraic rearrangement, graph interpretation, proportional reasoning and - depending on the topic - a comfort with trigonometry and with small-angle thinking that a student on Applications and Interpretation Standard Level has not necessarily been taught. The physics is not the problem. The student can describe the mechanism and then cannot execute it, and a term of physics teaching will not fix a mathematics gap.

Finally, Dubai's own timetable constraint. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA calculating instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. Those periods are inside the day, competing with six Diploma subjects, a laboratory requirement, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. The week is tighter than the subject list suggests, and a Physics plan that assumes open evenings is planning for a week that does not exist.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-oud-metha.programmesIntro: Physics appears in four forms across the schools reachable from Oud Metha, and each form assesses it differently. What a tutor should be doing changes with the form, not just with the student.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Taken at Higher or Standard Level as one of the six Diploma subjects, with written papers plus an internally assessed scientific investigation of the student's own design. Higher Level carries additional content and an additional paper, and the step from Standard to Higher is one of the largest in the Diploma science group. The investigation is written at home over weeks against published criteria.
programmes.countryNote: The nearest Diploma provision to Oud Metha sits in Al Jaddaf, across the creek toward Festival City, and out toward Nad Al Sheba, so a Physics student from this belt is usually commuting. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools, creating 16,846 places in total, which is gradually shortening those journeys for families here.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Science is taught as an integrated subject group and assessed against four criteria on a 1-8 scale rather than by terminal papers. Criterion B inquiring and designing and Criterion C processing and evaluating are the direct ancestors of the Diploma investigation, which makes MYP the cheapest place to learn investigation skills properly.
programmes.countryNote: Where a student continues from MYP into Diploma Physics at the same school in Al Jaddaf, the investigation skills usually transfer well and the content step is the harder part. Where a student arrives into Diploma Physics from an IGCSE background instead, the opposite is true: the content feels familiar and the investigation is unfamiliar territory.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics
programmes.description: The route most students in the Oud Metha school belt take before sixteen, tiered Core and Extended, with practical skills examined either through a practical paper or through the alternative-to-practical paper depending on the centre. Electricity and electromagnetism are the topics where UAE candidates most reliably lose structured-question marks.
programmes.countryNote: A student entering Diploma Physics from 0625 Core rather than Extended has a real content gap, and it shows in the October of Diploma year one rather than earlier. Closing it in the summer before Year 12 costs a short block; discovering it in the first set of Diploma assessments costs a term.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics
programmes.description: The other pre-sixteen route sat in Dubai, with its own paper structure and question style. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January.
programmes.countryNote: Because schools in this belt split entries between Cambridge and Pearson, two Diploma Physics students sitting beside each other in Year 12 can have arrived with meaningfully different preparation. A tutor's first job is to establish which one, rather than assuming a common starting point from a grade.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-oud-metha.subjectsIntro: Physics support is not one thing. These are the specific pieces a Diploma Physics student in this belt actually needs help with, and the mathematics courses that sit underneath them.

subjects.name: Diploma Physics
subjects.description: The full content set plus the additional Higher Level material and an extra paper. Students who cope with the mechanics and then meet fields, induction and quantum topics often find the difficulty is cumulative rather than local: each new topic assumes fluency with the mathematical handling of the last.

subjects.name: Diploma Physics
subjects.description: A reduced content set, but the same demand for precise definition and for explanation rather than description. Standard Level students lose most marks on long-answer questions by stating what happens without identifying the mechanism, which is a writing habit as much as a physics one.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An internally assessed piece of the student's own experimental work and writing, marked against published criteria. The design and the evaluation of uncertainty carry the marks that students most often miss. A tutor may coach the process and question reasoning; a tutor may not write any part of it.

subjects.name: Mechanics and energy
subjects.description: The foundation topic and the one students feel most confident about, which is why gaps here go undetected. Problems usually come from inconsistent handling of vectors and from treating energy conservation as a formula rather than as a constraint on the whole situation.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Where marks disappear in volume. Students can recite the relationships and still cannot reason about what happens to the rest of a circuit when one component changes. Circuit reasoning is trainable with targeted question practice and does not improve by re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Fields, induction and electromagnetism
subjects.description: The topic that separates a comfortable Higher Level student from a struggling one, because it demands holding a geometric picture and an algebraic relationship at the same time. Sessions here benefit from drawing before calculating, every time.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Conceptually accessible and mathematically unforgiving. Phase, path difference and superposition questions punish approximate reasoning, and students who are strong elsewhere often find this is where their long-answer marks drop without warning.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The mathematics route that most comfortably supports Physics Higher Level, because the algebraic fluency and calculus are taught directly. Students taking Physics HL with AA SL rather than HL are usually fine, provided the algebra is secure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A combination that needs watching. Applications and Interpretation Standard Level does not teach everything Physics Higher Level assumes, so a short bridging block on rearrangement, proportionality, graphs and trigonometry is often the highest-value physics purchase available.

subjects.name: Pre-Diploma physics bridging
subjects.description: A short block before Diploma year one starts, closing the gap between 0625 or 4PH1 and what Diploma Physics assumes. It needs no term-time slot and prevents the October problem that sends most families searching in the first place.

sections.heading: Draw the line between the school's laboratory and a tutor's hour
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake in Diploma Physics tuition is paying someone to do what the school already does well. The laboratory, the equipment, the supervised practical sessions and the teacher who knows this cohort's coursework deadlines are all inside the school day, free at the point of use, and irreplaceable. A tutor who spends the hour describing experiments the student has already performed is selling a duplicate.

What falls outside the school day is a specific and substantial list. Theory that was taught once in a crowded double period and never revisited. The mathematical handling that physics assumes and that the mathematics course may not have reached yet. The structure of a long-answer response, which is where Diploma Physics marks are won and lost and which is almost never taught explicitly because it is not content. And the investigation process: choosing a research question that can actually be investigated, understanding what the criteria reward, and being questioned hard on reasoning.

A useful test before booking: ask what the student did in their last two physics lessons, and what they did with it afterwards. If the answer is that they performed an experiment and then nothing, the hour belongs to turning the data into understanding. If the answer is that they sat through theory they did not follow, the hour belongs to that theory. If the answer is that they followed everything and still cannot answer the questions, the hour belongs to question technique and probably to mathematics.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, as a weekly load
paragraphs: The step from Standard to Higher Level Physics is one of the largest in the Diploma science group, and it is not simply more topics. Higher Level content is cumulative in a way that Standard Level content is not: fields, induction and the later topics each assume fluency with the mathematical handling of the earlier ones, so a student who got through mechanics on intuition rather than on method hits a wall in the second year rather than the first.

That cumulative structure changes what a weekly hour is for. For a Standard Level student, a weekly hour tracking the school's current topic works well all the way through. For a Higher Level student, the hour needs a second job: keeping the earlier mathematical handling alive so that the later topics have something to stand on. In practice that means a portion of most sessions spent on the algebra and graph work of an earlier topic, which students resist because it feels like going backwards.

The level decision also interacts with the mathematics route. Physics Higher Level alongside Mathematics Applications and Interpretation Standard Level is a combination that works, but only if someone explicitly teaches the mathematical handling that the physics assumes and the mathematics course does not cover. Families who do not realise this buy physics tuition for a mathematics problem, and the grade does not move.

sections.heading: The mathematics inside the physics, named topic by topic
paragraphs: A large share of the Diploma Physics students who need help do not have a physics problem. They can describe the mechanism, name the relationship and explain what is happening, and then cannot execute. The failure is in the mathematical handling, and because the subject on the timetable is physics, that is what the family buys tuition in. Six weeks later the understanding is better and the marks are the same.

The diagnostic is quick. Give the student a physics problem they have described correctly and watch where the pencil stops. If it stops at rearranging a relationship to make a different quantity the subject, the gap is algebraic. If it stops at reading a gradient or an area from a graph, the gap is graphical. If it stops at resolving a vector into components, the gap is trigonometric. None of those is physics, and none of them is fixed by physics teaching.

The awkward part is that the mathematics course may not have covered it yet, or may not cover it at all. A student taking Physics Higher Level with Mathematics Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is in exactly this position: the physics assumes handling the mathematics course does not teach, and nobody owns the gap. It is nobody's fault and it is entirely fixable, usually in a short narrow block rather than a term.

sections.heading: The investigation, timed from the school's deadline backwards
paragraphs: The internally assessed scientific investigation is the part of the Physics grade written at home, over weeks, against published criteria - and the part most exposed to both procrastination and bad help. Its deadline is set by your child's school, not by the IB, and it is almost always earlier than students expect. Asking for that date at the start of the year is the single most useful administrative act available to a parent.

Working backwards from it produces a sane plan. Before the deadline sits the writing. Before the writing sits the data collection, which has to fit the school's laboratory access rather than the student's convenience. Before the data sits the method, before the method sits the research question, and before the research question sits a period of reading and thinking that students compress to a weekend and should not. A research question chosen late is a research question that cannot be changed when it turns out not to be investigable.

What the marks actually reward is worth being specific about. The design of the investigation and the evaluation of uncertainty carry marks that students routinely leave on the table, because both require explaining choices rather than reporting results. A student who collected good data and wrote up what happened, without justifying the method or engaging honestly with its limitations, has written a competent lab report and a weak investigation.

The boundary for a tutor is clean. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, test whether a research question can be investigated with available apparatus, teach uncertainty analysis as a method, read the student's own draft and question reasoning that does not hold. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or complete any part of it. IB Gram tutors do not produce assessed work, and we do not supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables - those are published and owned by the IB and your school holds the current versions.
