sections.heading: Reading the week: double periods, clinics and the slot that survives
paragraphs: Science timetables cluster, and that clustering is the most useful scheduling information a Physics family has. A student with a double period of Physics on two days of the week has two days where the subject is saturated and three where it is absent. The saturated days are poor evenings for a session because the student has had enough; the absent days are good ones because the subject gets refreshed in a gap where it would otherwise go quiet.

Overlay two more things. The school's own after-hours commitments - revision clinics, Creativity Activity Service, Extended Essay supervision meetings, fixtures - fall on specific weekdays and will quietly claim any slot booked on top of them. And the commute: a Physics student travelling back from Festival City or Nad Al Sheba at peak is not starting a demanding session at half past four, whatever the plan says.

The practical approach is to get the term calendar at the start of term, write out the five weekdays with the science periods and the school commitments marked, and look for the intersection: a day with no double science, no school commitment, and a manageable journey home. In this belt there is usually one such day, occasionally two. That is where the hour goes, and it goes there for the whole term rather than moving around.

Ramadan needs deciding in advance as well. School hours shorten, the day changes shape and useful working energy moves to after Iftar. Agreeing beforehand that the Physics hour shifts to a post-Iftar slot for that period and returns afterwards preserves continuity through a month that otherwise costs four sessions and the momentum with them.

sections.heading: What the hour costs here, and why the laboratory changes the sum
paragraphs: Rates in this market are published across an unusually wide band, and the figures below belong to the providers that published them rather than to IB Gram. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For qualified online tuition, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026, gives AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level provision sits at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end.

Physics changes how to read those numbers, because the expensive part of the subject is already paid for. The laboratory, the equipment and the supervised practical time sit inside school fees, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. The marginal purchase a family is making is theory, mathematics and investigation process - a narrower product than it feels like, and one that should often be bought in shorter blocks.

Monthly figures compare more cleanly than hourly ones. One Dubai provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, roughly AED 100 an hour. In-home monthly packages are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, roughly AED 200 to 225 for the same eight hours. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Diploma Physics sessions for Oud Metha students run one-to-one over live video. For this subject specifically the format has a practical advantage beyond rate: diagrams, graphs and worked algebra sit on a shared screen where both people can annotate them, which is more legible than a notebook turned sideways on a kitchen table.

sections.heading: Regulators, the mandatory block and what a parent can verify
paragraphs: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, inspecting on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and publishing the reports. For a Physics family that report is directly useful: if it names science attainment or teaching as a strength at your child's school, the laboratory side of the subject is in good hands and your money belongs on theory, mathematics and the investigation. If it flags science as an area for improvement, the balance shifts.

The rest of the country divides differently. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain; the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah; Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates it there; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project.

The mandatory block applies to every Dubai private school whatever its licensed curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year or April 2026 where the year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are required for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited.

On tutors: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Tutoring without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published so no amount is quoted. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by any of these bodies and has no UAE office.

process.title: Tell us the level, the maths route and the school
process.description: Physics Higher or Standard Level, the mathematics course and level taken alongside it, and the school. That combination predicts most of what a Physics student will struggle with, and the mathematics route in particular changes the plan more than the physics level does.

process.title: Send the science timetable, not just the report
process.description: Which weekdays carry double periods and which do not, plus the school's term calendar. The session belongs on a light science day with no school commitment, and that day is identifiable in ten minutes from documents the school already publishes.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a worked problem
process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video at no charge, built around a problem the student has already attempted. Watching where the pencil stops tells a tutor whether the gap is physics, mathematics or long-answer writing, which is three different plans.

process.title: A written split, then a plan sized to it
process.description: After the trial you get the gap named explicitly: theory not absorbed, mathematical handling missing, long-answer structure untrained, or investigation process. Narrow blocks are often the right answer, particularly where the real gap is mathematical rather than physical.

process.title: Review against school assessments and the investigation deadline
process.description: Progress is judged against the school's own marks and against whether the investigation is on schedule, not against how the sessions feel. If neither is moving, the plan changes or the tutor does, and we will say so rather than sell another term.

whyPoints.title: We do not sell what the school already provides
whyPoints.description: The laboratory, the equipment and the supervised practical work belong inside the school day and cannot be bought outside it. The hour is pointed at theory, mathematical handling, long-answer structure and investigation process, which is a narrower product and usually a shorter plan.

whyPoints.title: The mathematics gap diagnosed, not ignored
whyPoints.description: Many Diploma Physics students who need help have an algebra, graph or trigonometry problem wearing a physics badge. Physics Higher Level alongside Applications and Interpretation Standard Level is the classic case. We name it and fix it in a narrow block rather than selling physics hours.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the science timetable
whyPoints.description: A session on a double-period day meets a saturated student; a session on a light day refreshes a subject that would otherwise go quiet for four days. We pick the weekday from the school's own timetable and term calendar rather than from a tutor's diary.

whyPoints.title: Investigation help that stays legitimate
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain the criteria, test whether a research question is investigable with the apparatus available, teach uncertainty analysis, and question the student's own draft. They do not write, draft or complete any part of it, and we supply no board papers or mark schemes.

whyPoints.title: Shared screen suits this subject
whyPoints.description: Diagrams, graphs and worked algebra sit on a surface both people can annotate, which is more legible than a notebook turned sideways. For a subject where drawing before calculating is the core discipline, that is a practical gain rather than a compromise.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed, no claims we cannot show
whyPoints.description: The dirham bands here belong to the providers that published them, with the month read. No regulator approval, no UAE office, no grade guarantees, no IB dates we have not been able to verify, and no statistic without a source.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with IB Physics when the practical work happens at school?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the practical work is not the part that needs buying. The laboratory, the apparatus and the supervised experiments sit inside the school day and nothing replaces them. What falls outside is the theory that went past too fast in a double period, the mathematical handling physics assumes, the structure of a long-answer response, and the process of turning an experiment into an investigation that satisfies the criteria. That list is substantial, and all of it works over a shared screen. A tutor describing experiments the student has already performed is selling a duplicate.

faqs.question: My child can explain the physics and still loses marks. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Usually the mathematics, wearing a physics badge. Give them a problem they have described correctly and watch where the pencil stops. Stopping at rearranging a relationship is an algebra gap; stopping at reading a gradient or an area off a graph is a graphical one; stopping at splitting a vector into components is trigonometry. None of those is fixed by physics teaching, which is why a term of physics tuition can improve understanding without moving the grade. A short narrow block on the specific skill usually does more than six physics hours.

faqs.question: Is Physics Higher Level manageable with Maths Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: It is, but only if somebody explicitly teaches the mathematical handling that the physics assumes and that course does not cover. Rearrangement with squared terms, resolving components, gradients and areas as physical quantities, proportional reasoning and exponential behaviour all turn up in Higher Level Physics topics. Nobody owns that gap by default: the physics teacher assumes the maths course covers it and the maths course has a different syllabus. Identify it before Year 12 if you can, and close it in a short block rather than discovering it in October.

faqs.question: Which day of the week should a Physics session go on?
faqs.answer: A day without a double science period, with no school commitment, and a manageable journey home. Science timetables cluster, so most students have two saturated days and three where the subject is absent - and the absent days are the valuable ones, because the hour refreshes a subject that would otherwise go quiet for four days. Get the term calendar and the science timetable at the start of term, mark the five weekdays, and look for the intersection. In this belt there is usually one clear day, sometimes two.

faqs.question: When should work on the scientific investigation actually start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than it does, and the first step is administrative: ask the school for the internal deadline at the start of the year rather than in the term it falls. Then work backwards - writing before the deadline, data collection before the writing and constrained by laboratory access, method before data, research question before method, and reading and thinking before that. Students compress the last part into a weekend, which is how they end up with a question that turns out not to be investigable and no time left to change it.

faqs.question: Which part of the investigation do students lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: The design and the evaluation of uncertainty, rather than the experiment itself. Both require explaining and justifying choices instead of reporting results, which is a different kind of writing from anything else in the subject. A student who collected good data and wrote up what happened, without defending the method or engaging honestly with its limitations, has produced a competent laboratory report and a weak investigation. That distinction is teachable in a few sessions, and it is worth more than extra content work.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with the investigation draft?
faqs.answer: Explain what each criterion rewards. Test whether a research question can actually be investigated with the apparatus the school has. Teach uncertainty and error analysis as a method the student then applies. Read the student's own draft and ask hard questions about reasoning that does not hold. Point out where a section fails to address the criterion it is meant to. What a tutor may not do is write, draft, rewrite or complete any part of it. IB Gram tutors do not produce assessed work, and the consequences of the alternative fall on the student.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from IGCSE Physics to Diploma Physics?
faqs.answer: Larger from Core than from Extended, and larger in mathematical demand than in content. A student arriving from 0625 Extended or 4PH1 with secure algebra usually copes; a student arriving from a Core tier has a genuine content gap that shows up in the October of Diploma year one rather than earlier. The cheapest fix is a short bridging block in the summer before Year 12, which needs no term-time slot at all. Discovering the gap in the first set of Diploma assessments instead costs a term of catching up.

faqs.question: Which Physics topics should a Higher Level student expect to need help with?
faqs.answer: Fields, induction and electromagnetism, more than anything else, because they demand holding a geometric picture and an algebraic relationship simultaneously. Waves, phase and path difference come next: conceptually accessible and mathematically unforgiving. Circuits catch out students who can recite relationships but cannot reason about what happens elsewhere when one component changes. Mechanics is rarely named as a problem and is often where the undetected gap sits, because early confidence there hides handling weaknesses that later topics expose.

faqs.question: Does my child's school inspection report tell us anything useful here?
faqs.answer: More than usual for a science subject. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the reports free. If science teaching or attainment is named as a strength at your child's school, the laboratory and teaching side is in good hands and your money belongs on theory, mathematical handling and the investigation. If science is flagged as an area for improvement, the balance shifts and a weekly theory hour is doing more structural work than it would otherwise.

faqs.question: How do we plan backwards from the IB exams if we do not know the dates?
faqs.answer: Plan from the school-set milestones, which are the ones that actually govern the work. The investigation internal deadline, the mock window and the end-of-year-one audit of what year two assumes are all set by your child's school and are available from the term calendar. On the IB's own dates we will not guess: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and we do not publish one. Take yours from your school's IB coordinator.

faqs.question: What does Diploma Physics tutoring cost around Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; AED 150 to 300 for qualified online tuition, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; AED 200 to 450 or more for specialist IB provision, with TutorChase publishing AED 270; AED 180 to 500 for in-home including travel; and AED 650 at the premium end from BartyED. All read October 2026, all the providers' figures rather than ours. Monthly, one provider publishes AED 799 for eight online sessions.

faqs.question: Is an in-home Physics tutor worth the premium in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: The drives here are short, so the premium is not mileage - it is the small number of people who can teach Diploma Physics well and will commit to arriving at a specific Karama or Al Mankhool address at a fixed hour. Published in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; sessions run one-to-one over live video. For this subject the shared annotated screen is also genuinely better for diagrams and graphs than a notebook at the table edge.

faqs.question: How do we keep the Physics hour running through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Decide before it starts rather than improvising. School hours shorten, the shape of the day changes and productive energy moves to after Iftar, so a slot that works in November will not survive unchanged. Agree in advance that the session shifts to a post-Iftar time for that period and returns afterwards. Families who plan this keep continuity through a month that otherwise costs four sessions and the momentum with them. Online delivery makes the shift simple; a fixed in-home arrival window is the hardest commitment in the week to move.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory UAE subjects affect how much physics teaching my child gets?
faqs.answer: They press on the timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Those periods sit inside the day alongside six Diploma subjects, a laboratory requirement, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, so the week is tighter than a subject list suggests.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level Physics specialist is available when we need one?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than putting a general science tutor in the slot and charging for the hour. Diploma Physics at Higher Level is a narrower specialism than Mathematics or Chemistry and the pool is smaller, so the honest options are to wait for the right tutor, to start with a related specialist on a clearly stated interim basis, or not to book. Because delivery is online rather than by someone driving across Dubai, the pool is every Higher Level Physics specialist available rather than the few who will travel to Oud Metha at five o'clock.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-oud-metha.closingHeading: Separate the laboratory from the hour, then book the hour
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-oud-metha.closingBody: Before buying anything, work out which part of Diploma Physics you are actually short of. The laboratory, the apparatus and the supervised practical work are the school's and are already paid for. What is usually missing is theory that went past too quickly, the mathematical handling the subject assumes, the structure of a long-answer response, and a credible plan for the investigation. Bring a problem your child has already attempted to a free trial lesson, let the tutor watch where the pencil stops, and let that decide whether the next block is physics, mathematics or process work. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: What a Palm Jumeirah family is actually buying when they pay for Physics help
paragraphs: Palm Jumeirah has no secondary school on it. Children living on the fronds, along the Shoreline, in the Golden Mile or at the tip travel off the island every morning through a single trunk-road junction, most of them to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim or the Jumeirah beach strip. That geography matters to a Physics fee in a way nobody writes about: a tutor who drives to a frond villa is paid for the drive as well as the teaching, and the drive is not negotiable because there is one road on and off.

The market does not help a parent work this out. Of the pages ranking for Dubai IB tutoring searches, three publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars - a currency no Dubai family pays school fees in. One ranking agency's own list of frequently asked questions poses the price question and then declines to answer it. So the first thing this page does is publish the bands, in AED, with the name of whoever published each figure and the month it was read. Those are market rates, not IB Gram's rates. What IB Gram offers before any money is discussed is a trial lesson.

The second thing worth doing is matching money to the mark scheme. Diploma Physics under the current guide is assessed through two written papers and one scientific investigation, and the investigation carries a fifth of the final grade on its own. A family that buys twenty hours of topic revision and none of it on the investigation has spent well and aimed badly. A family that buys four hours in the design week of the investigation, before the data exists, has usually bought the single most valuable block of the two years.

Where money goes wrong is predictable. It goes wrong on hours bought in the eight weeks before the May session, when the content gap is too wide to close and the only available gain is exam technique. It goes wrong on a cheap tutor who can do the physics but cannot read an IB mark scheme, so the student keeps writing descriptions where the command term asked for an explanation. It goes wrong on examiner-badged premium rates for topics a competent specialist fixes at half the price. And it goes wrong on in-home visits where a third of the fee is travel on the Palm's one access road.

This page is written to be used before the first payment. It gives the AED bands and their sources, the component weightings so the hours can be aimed, a comparison of online, in-home and group delivery with the island's travel reality priced in, and an honest account of what a tutor may and may not touch on an investigation that has to be the student's own work. IB Gram delivers all of it as one-to-one online tuition. Home visits are an India-only service and are not sold anywhere in the UAE.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.programmesIntro: Palm Jumeirah children sit in three different IB programmes depending on their age, and the Physics question looks different in each. The notes below are specific to families commuting off this island rather than to IB programmes in general.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma, taken with three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard. Physics sits in Group 4 and can be taken at either level. Under the current guide the course is organised into themes covering motion, the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour, fields, and nuclear and quantum physics, and is assessed by two written papers plus one scientific investigation. The investigation is internally marked against published criteria and externally moderated.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's Diploma cohort is small relative to the British-curriculum majority, which is why a Physics specialist is scarce near any one neighbourhood. A Palm Jumeirah student is usually one of a handful taking Physics at Higher Level in their year group, and the school's physics teaching load is spread across IGCSE and Diploma classes. Paid hours here are most often bought because the school cannot timetable extra one-to-one support, not because the teaching is poor.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of broad study across eight subject groups, with Sciences assessed on four criteria rather than by percentage. MYP Sciences marks knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A student can be strong on content and still score poorly because the design and evaluation criteria were never taught explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools Palm Jumeirah families use run MYP to year 5 and then Diploma, while others switch to IGCSE at 14. That fork decides what Physics looks like at 16. An MYP student who has never written a hypothesis with a controlled variable arrives in Diploma Physics with a gap that shows up in the investigation rather than in the papers, and it is cheaper to close at 14 than at 17.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary education organised around transdisciplinary themes, finishing with an exhibition in the final year. Science appears as inquiry rather than as a named subject, so a child can leave PYP confident at asking questions and unpractised at the arithmetic that later Physics depends on.
programmes.countryNote: Palm Jumeirah's own provision is early years and nursery; primary-age children already commute. For PYP families the useful Physics-adjacent investment is not Physics at all but number fluency and measurement, because the Diploma Physics students who struggle most are usually struggling with rearranging an equation rather than with the physics in it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely the only subject a Diploma student needs help with, and the combinations are predictable. These are the subjects most often requested alongside it by families on the Palm and the Jumeirah strip.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two written papers and one scientific investigation. Marks are lost most often on uncertainty treatment in the data-analysis section, on derivations that skip a line of algebra, and on explanation questions answered as descriptions. Higher Level questions assume complete Standard Level fluency rather than extra memory.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most Physics students take, and the one engineering admissions usually expect. Calculus and algebraic manipulation here are the same skills Physics Paper 2 needs, which is why weak maths shows up as a physics mark. The exploration is assessed separately and often collides with the Physics investigation deadline.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-heavy and modelling-led, with a graphical-calculator expectation throughout. Taking Physics HL with Applications SL is workable but leaves gaps in algebraic fluency that have to be filled deliberately, and some engineering courses state a preference for Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The other Group 4 subject Palm Jumeirah families most often pair with Physics. Shares the investigation structure and the data-handling demands, so one tutor can sometimes cover both internal assessments even where the content teaching needs two specialists.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Taken alongside Physics by students aiming at medicine or biomedical engineering. The assessment shape matches Physics, but the mark scheme rewards precise terminology far more, which catches out students who write fluently and imprecisely.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Frequently chosen with Physics HL. The solution development work is a separate internal assessment with its own deadline, and it tends to land in the same term as the Physics investigation. Planning the two together is a scheduling job, not a teaching one.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Offered by fewer Dubai schools and much less tutored, so availability near any single neighbourhood is thin. Shares a design-cycle logic with MYP Design, and students coming from MYP Design usually find the transition manageable.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: A Group 4 alternative that satisfies the science requirement without Physics-level mathematics. Chosen by students who want a science but not a quantitative one, and it still carries an internal investigation with the same evidence standards.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Can count as either a Group 3 or a Group 4 subject, which makes it useful for timetable problems. Assessment rewards systems thinking and data interpretation, and students strong at Physics data analysis often score well here with little extra teaching.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Compulsory, with an exhibition and an essay. Physics students often have the sharpest material available for it and the least patience with it. Support here is structural - argument shape, counterclaim, and evidence selection - rather than content teaching.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.regionsIntro: Students on this page come from the island itself and from the coastal communities either side of it. Session timing differs by a surprising amount between them, because the constraint is the trunk road rather than the distance.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah fronds
regions.note: Gated single-lane spines off the trunk road, with villa gates at the far end. A visitor arriving at 4:30pm faces the junction queue and then the frond itself. Online sessions remove both and let a 4:00pm start actually begin at 4:00pm.

regions.name: Shoreline and Golden Mile
regions.note: Apartment blocks along the eastern trunk, with visitor parking and building access to negotiate. Families here often have two children on different school runs, so a fixed evening slot is worth more than a flexible afternoon one.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The nearest off-island school cluster and the first stop for most Palm commuters. Secondary days here typically end mid-afternoon, which sets the earliest realistic session time for a student who still has to cross back onto the island.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: A dense school belt along the beach road with heavy drop-off and pick-up traffic. Students travelling back to the Palm from here arrive later than the distance suggests, so sessions scheduled before 5:00pm regularly start late.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: Low-rise villa districts running along Beach Road with several schools inside them. A number of Palm families keep younger children in Jumeirah schools and move them off-island for secondary, so the two commutes run in opposite directions.

regions.note: Where much of the IB and American provision sits. The furthest regular Palm commute, and the one most likely to make a 4:00pm in-home visit impossible for a tutor based near the school.

sections.heading: What an hour of Diploma Physics support actually buys from the Palm
paragraphs: An hour of one-to-one Diploma Physics teaching in Dubai is sold anywhere between roughly AED 45 and AED 650, and the spread is not mostly about quality. It is about tier, format and travel. At the bottom sit online tutors working from published worked examples. In the middle sit qualified subject teachers. At the top sit tutors marketing scarcity. Travel is the hidden variable: an in-home rate in Dubai includes the drive, and from a frond villa on Palm Jumeirah the drive crosses a single access junction twice.

The honest way to think about the fee is to ask what the hour is aimed at. Diploma Physics is assessed by two written papers and one scientific investigation, and those three things fail for different reasons. Paper 1B fails on uncertainty and graph reading. Paper 2 fails on command terms and on derivations with a missing line. The investigation fails at the design stage, weeks before anyone writes anything, usually because the research question cannot generate enough data to analyse. An hour spent on the wrong one of those is not a cheap hour. It is a wasted one.

This is where a Palm Jumeirah family has an advantage they rarely use. Because the island has no secondary school, the local tutor pool was never the relevant pool - every option already involves a commute. Once the commute is accepted as unavoidable, removing it entirely by teaching over live video costs nothing in convenience and widens the choice from whoever happens to live within a drive to every Diploma Physics specialist available. The question stops being who is nearby and becomes who teaches this syllabus.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one Physics tuition to Palm Jumeirah over live video. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because a family comparing an in-home quote against an online one needs to know which they are buying before they compare the numbers.

sections.heading: The AED bands the Dubai market publishes, and who publishes them
paragraphs: Below are the hourly bands currently published by providers serving Dubai, read in October 2026, with the source of each band named in the table. These are market figures and not IB Gram's prices. They are reproduced because a parent cannot judge a quote without knowing the distribution it sits in, and almost nobody in this market publishes one.

Two patterns are worth reading out of the table. The first is that the in-home band starts higher than the online band and ends higher, and the gap is travel. The second is that the specialist band and the premium band overlap heavily, which means a large part of what separates an AED 270 hour from an AED 650 hour is positioning rather than teaching. Where the premium band genuinely buys something is in narrow subject availability, and Physics at Higher Level is narrower than most.

Monthly packaging changes the arithmetic again. Online monthly packages have been published at AED 799 for eight sessions, and in-home monthly packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Read per hour, the in-home package is not dramatically dearer; read per contact hour of actual teaching with travel stripped out, it is. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

Whatever band a family lands in, the figure to ask for is the one that includes everything. Ask whether the rate is per hour or per lesson, whether a 90-minute session bills as 1.5 hours, what a late cancellation costs, whether written feedback between sessions is included, and whether the price changes closer to an exam series. Those five answers move the real cost more than the headline rate does.

sections.heading: Aiming the money: Physics components and what each one is worth
paragraphs: A Diploma Physics grade is built from two written papers and one scientific investigation. Paper 1 is split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section and carries 36% of the grade between them. Paper 2 carries 44%. The scientific investigation carries 20% and is marked inside the school against published criteria before external moderation. Those proportions should decide where paid hours go, and in most families they do not.

The cheapest marks on the page are in Paper 1B, the data-analysis section. Uncertainty propagation, gradient work, linearising a relationship and reading a graph nobody has seen before are all teachable in a small number of hours, and most students have never been taught them explicitly because class time goes on content. A student who can handle uncertainty confidently picks up marks across both papers and in the investigation at the same time, which makes it the highest-return block of hours available.

The dearest marks are in late content recovery. If a student reaches February of the final year without secure work on fields or on nuclear and quantum physics, buying that content back costs many hours and competes with revision for five other subjects. This is the single most common way Physics money is wasted in Dubai: hours bought at the point of panic, at the highest rates of the year, on the problem that was least amenable to a quick fix.

Weightings and component structures change between guides, so the table below should be checked against the subject guide your child's school is actually teaching. Ask the Diploma coordinator which guide and first-examination year applies. A tutor who cannot tell you which guide they are teaching to is not the tutor to buy twenty hours from.

sections.heading: Four spending patterns that waste Physics money on this island
paragraphs: The first is buying hours too late. A block started eight weeks before a written series can sharpen technique and cannot rebuild a year of content. Families who start in the first Diploma year pay less in total and buy more, because the same money goes on learning rather than on triage. If a student is already inside the final two months, the honest advice is to narrow the aim hard - two topics and exam technique - rather than to buy more hours.

The second is paying for travel without noticing. On Palm Jumeirah the in-home premium is not a rounding error. A tutor coming to a frond villa crosses the trunk-road junction, drives the frond spine, clears a gate, and does it all again afterwards. That time is inside the quoted rate, so a family paying AED 350 for a 60-minute in-home session is buying roughly the teaching an online session delivers for substantially less. Some families want a person in the room and are happy to pay for it; the point is to know the trade being made.

The third is buying the wrong specialism. Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics look adjacent on a school report and are not interchangeable to teach. A general science tutor can keep a Standard Level student afloat and will struggle with Higher Level fields or with a derivation that needs calculus. Conversely, a brilliant Physics tutor cannot fix a mathematics problem that is really about rearranging equations. Diagnosing which subject is failing before buying a term of the wrong one is the cheapest decision available.

The fourth is buying support on work that must be the student's own. Internal assessment help has a hard boundary: a tutor may teach the method, discuss the research question, ask whether the data supports the conclusion, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not supply text, data or analysis that then gets submitted. Anyone selling a finished investigation is selling the student a malpractice finding, and the hours are worse than wasted.

The monorail runs along the trunk and serves the hotel strip rather than the residential fronds, so it does not help a school run or a tutor visit. For a parent weighing delivery options, that layout is the whole argument: the island is pleasant to live on and expensive to drive to on a weekday afternoon.

The travel column is the part no competitor page quantifies, and on this island it is the part that decides what an hour is worth.

Read across the rows and a pattern appears. Online delivery converts the whole fee into teaching and draws on every available Diploma Physics specialist rather than on the small number who live within a comfortable drive of the island. In-home delivery buys physical presence and pays for the junction. Group delivery buys a lower per-student rate and gives up the thing one-to-one is for, which is stopping on the exact place where this student's reasoning breaks.

None of this makes in-home tutoring wrong. For a nine-year-old who needs an adult in the room, presence matters more than specialism. For a Higher Level Physics student eight months from a written series, the opposite is true, and the Palm's geography makes the trade unusually clear. sections.heading: Budgeting two Diploma years instead of one panic term
paragraphs: Most Physics money in Dubai is spent in the last six months of a two-year course, at the highest rates of the year, on the hardest problem to fix. Spreading the same budget across both years changes what it buys. In the first Diploma year the money goes on building uncertainty and graph fluency, on getting command terms right while there is time for habits to form, and on the investigation design before the data exists. In the second year it goes on consolidation and timed practice.

A workable shape looks like this. Term one of the first year: a short diagnostic block and then fortnightly sessions. Term two: a concentrated run on the data-analysis skills that feed every component. Term three, when the investigation is set: a few hours before the design is fixed, then feedback on the student's own draft. Second year: weekly sessions through the content-heavy terms, then timed-paper work with technique review. That sequence rarely costs more in total than a panicked final-term intensive and consistently buys more.

There is also a school-fee context worth knowing. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For a family already paying Dubai school fees, that freeze is the one piece of budget stability in the year, and it is the natural moment to decide what tutoring is worth over two years rather than reactively each term.

Finally, decide what you will not buy. Do not buy a package before a diagnostic session. Do not buy an exam-season intensive for a subject the student has not been attending properly, because attendance is the problem and hours will not fix it. Do not buy hours for a sibling simply because one child benefited. And do not buy anything on the promise of a particular grade - no tutor can promise a score, and anyone who does has told you something important about the rest of their claims.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: what a Physics tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: A fifth of the Diploma Physics grade comes from one investigation the student designs, carries out and reports. It is also where paid support is most often sold dishonestly, because a parent under deadline pressure is an easy customer. The boundary is not vague. Everything submitted must be the student's own, and the school signs a declaration to that effect.

Inside the boundary, a tutor can do a great deal. They can teach the physics the investigation depends on. They can press on whether a research question is answerable with the equipment available, which is the single most common design failure. They can explain what the published criteria reward, show worked examples of uncertainty treatment, and ask the questions an examiner would ask of a conclusion. They can read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning does not hold. All of that is teaching, and all of it is allowed.

Outside the boundary is anything that puts the tutor's words, numbers or analysis into the submitted file. A tutor supplying data, rewriting sections, or handing over a template that becomes the report has crossed from teaching into malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student. One operator in this market openly sells finished internal assessments. That is an academic-integrity breach and an expulsion risk, not a shortcut, and no amount of urgency makes it worth considering.

The practical advice for a Palm Jumeirah family is to buy hours early and ask for process coaching, not rescue. Two or three sessions in the week the research question is being chosen are worth more than ten in the week before submission, cost less, and leave no ambiguity about whose work was submitted. Ask any prospective tutor directly what they will and will not do with internal assessment work. The answer is a reliable test of everything else.

sections.heading: Starting from Palm Jumeirah, and what the first session costs
paragraphs: The first step is a conversation about what is actually wrong, which is free. Useful things to have to hand: the current school report with the Physics grade and any predicted grade, which subject guide the school is teaching to, whether the student is at Higher or Standard Level, the date of the next school assessment, and a recent marked paper if one exists. A marked paper is worth more than a report, because it shows where marks were lost rather than how many.

The second step is a trial lesson at no cost. It exists to answer one question: can this tutor teach this student this syllabus. Watch for whether the tutor asks the student to explain their reasoning rather than explaining it to them, whether they name the component being worked on, and whether they can say which guide they are teaching to. Those three signals predict the next twenty hours better than any rate card does.

The third step is honest about availability. Diploma Physics at Higher Level is a narrow specialism and UAE-based availability for a specific weekday slot is not guaranteed. Where no UAE-based specialist is free at the time a family needs, the alternative offered is a specialist from the wider network teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and that is stated before anything is booked rather than discovered afterwards. Nobody else in this market discloses a coverage limit; this page does.

The fourth step is the schedule itself. Sessions are timed around the school day and the trunk-road reality, which usually means a start after 5:00pm for a secondary student travelling back from Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim, and a different pattern during Ramadan, when a post-Iftar slot often works better than an afternoon one. Lessons are delivered live online, one to one. IB Gram does not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE, and no UAE office or centre exists - the service is the teaching, delivered over video.

faqs.question: What does an hour of IB Physics support cost for a Palm Jumeirah family?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for premium named tutors. Qualified online subject tutors are advertised from around AED 150 to 300, IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the rate. Those are market figures from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED, not IB Gram's prices. What IB Gram offers before any fee conversation is a trial lesson at no cost, so the teaching can be judged first.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put two children in the same Physics session?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes. Small-group rates in Dubai are published at roughly AED 60 to 120 per student, against AED 150 or more for one-to-one. Whether it is cheaper per mark depends on the two students. Siblings taking the same level, at the same point in the course, with similar gaps, can share a session usefully. Siblings a year apart, or one at Higher and one at Standard Level, cannot: the session drifts to the middle and neither gets the diagnosis that one-to-one is for. A diagnostic session each is the cheaper experiment before committing.

faqs.question: How many Physics hours does an HL student usually need in the final year?
faqs.answer: There is no reliable average, and anyone quoting one is guessing. What is predictable is the shape. A Higher Level student with secure content usually needs weekly sessions through the content-heavy terms, a concentrated block on data analysis and uncertainty, two or three hours around the investigation design, and timed-paper technique work in the final term. A student with real content gaps needs more hours and should start sooner, because the same money buys learning in the first year and triage in the last. Start with a diagnostic session and plan the term from what it finds.

faqs.question: Does a higher hourly rate mean a better Physics tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. The specialist band and the premium band overlap heavily in published Dubai rates, so a substantial part of the gap between an AED 270 hour and an AED 650 hour is positioning rather than teaching. What a higher rate does buy, sometimes, is scarcity: Higher Level Physics is a narrow specialism and genuine availability is limited. The useful tests are not price. Can the tutor name which subject guide they teach to, which component they are working on, and what they will not do with internal assessment work? A trial lesson answers all three.

faqs.question: Which part of IB Physics is worth paying for first?
faqs.answer: The data-analysis section of Paper 1. Uncertainty propagation, gradient work, linearising a relationship and interpreting an unfamiliar graph are all teachable in a handful of hours, and most students have never had them taught explicitly because class time goes on content. The skills then pay off twice more, in Paper 2 and in the scientific investigation, which carries 20% of the grade. After that, command-term work on Paper 2 explanations. Late content recovery is the most expensive block available and should be the last thing bought, not the first.

faqs.question: Do Physics tutoring rates rise as the May session gets closer?
faqs.answer: Effective cost does, even where the headline rate does not move. Availability tightens in the months before a written series, the slots left are the inconvenient ones, and the work left to do is the kind that responds least to hours. Some providers also package exam-season intensives at a premium. The practical consequence for a Palm Jumeirah family is that the same budget buys more in the first Diploma year than in the last term. Ask any provider directly whether their rate changes by season, and get the answer before booking a block.

faqs.question: What does the scientific investigation cost in tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Far less than families expect, if the hours are bought early. Two or three sessions in the week the research question is being chosen typically do more than ten in the week before submission, because the common failure is a design that cannot generate analysable data. Later support is limited to what is legitimate: explaining the published criteria, teaching the physics involved, and giving feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. Nothing in the submitted file may come from the tutor. Buying early is both cheaper and the only version that leaves no ambiguity.

faqs.question: Is group Physics revision worth the saving over one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For broad revision across a syllabus, a group at AED 60 to 120 per student is reasonable value. For diagnosis, it is not, because a group cannot stop on the specific place where one student's reasoning about fields or uncertainty breaks down. Most families get the best result from a mixture: group or self-directed work for coverage, one-to-one hours aimed at the two or three error patterns a marked paper reveals. If only one can be afforded, buy the diagnosis, because revising the wrong thing thoroughly is the most expensive outcome available.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a single diagnostic Physics session rather than a block?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a student stuck in the middle bands it is usually the right first purchase. One session spent on recent marked work, read against the published criteria, normally identifies one or two habits doing most of the damage - a missing line in derivations, uncertainty ignored, explanation questions answered as descriptions. Knowing that is worth more than a term bought on a guess. It also means the honest answer is available: sometimes the problem is mathematics rather than physics, or attendance rather than either, and no amount of Physics tutoring fixes those.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if a Palm Jumeirah session is cancelled late?
faqs.answer: Ask this before booking anything, with any provider. Cancellation terms move the real cost of tutoring more than the headline rate does, and they vary widely: some providers bill in full inside 24 hours, some rebook once, some charge nothing. For a family on the island, the related question is what happens when a school event or a traffic problem makes a start time impossible. Online sessions are easier to shift than in-home visits for the obvious reason that nobody has already driven across the trunk-road junction to get there.

faqs.question: Does an hourly tutoring rate in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: That depends on the provider, and it should be asked directly rather than assumed. The UAE VAT treatment of education services is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority, and a tutoring page is not the place to state it as settled fact. What a parent can reasonably insist on is clarity about the specific quote in front of them: whether the figure shown is the final amount payable, whether any tax is added at invoice, and whether the provider holds a tax registration number. Any provider unwilling to answer that in writing has answered a different question.

faqs.question: Why does a Physics specialist cost more than a general science tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the supply is much smaller and the work is different. A general science tutor can keep a Standard Level student moving and will usually struggle with Higher Level fields, with nuclear and quantum content, or with a derivation requiring calculus fluency. A specialist also knows the assessment: which command terms demand what, how the investigation criteria are applied, where the data-analysis section allocates marks. In published Dubai bands that difference shows as roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified general tutor against AED 200 to 450 and above for a subject specialist.

faqs.question: Is Physics tutoring in the first Diploma year money well spent?
faqs.answer: It is the best-value window in the course. In the first year the money goes on building habits while there is time for them to form: uncertainty fluency, command-term discipline, and a sound investigation design before any data exists. In the final term the same money buys triage on the problem least able to be fixed quickly. Families who start early generally spend less in total and get more for it. The counter-argument is that a student may not need help in the first year, which is exactly what a single diagnostic session will tell you.

faqs.question: Does my child need laboratory equipment at home for online Physics?
faqs.answer: No. The practical work for the scientific investigation is done at school, with the school's equipment, under the school's supervision, and that is where it belongs. What an online Physics session needs is modest: a stable connection, a device with a decent camera, a headset, a graphical calculator where the school specifies one, and some way to show working - a tablet with a stylus, or a phone positioned over paper. The single biggest improvement most families can make is the headset, because physics explanation depends on hearing the reasoning clearly.

faqs.question: How do we check a Dubai Physics tutor may legally charge for lessons?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Ask a prospective tutor whether they hold the permit, and check the official MoHRE service page for how it is issued.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to raise a Physics 4 to a 6?
faqs.answer: Spend first on finding out why the 4 is a 4. In most cases a marked paper shows two or three repeating habits rather than broad ignorance: explanation questions answered as descriptions, uncertainty omitted, derivations with a skipped step, or arithmetic collapsing under time pressure. Those are cheap to fix and worth whole grade boundaries. Then buy hours on the data-analysis section and on investigation process, since both pay off across components. No tutor can promise a particular grade, and a provider who offers one has told you how seriously to read their other claims.

intro.heading: Four reasons a physics mark falls, and only one of them is physics
paragraphs: When a Pearl Jumeira family looks at a disappointing physics report, the natural conclusion is that the student does not understand physics. Sometimes that is right. More often, in this cluster, the mark is being lost in one of three other places, and knowing which one changes what the sessions should contain and how many of them are needed.

The first is mathematics. Diploma Physics assumes a student can rearrange a formula before substituting into it, handle standard form without hesitation, resolve a vector with trigonometry, read a gradient and an area from a graph, and at Higher Level use some calculus. A student taking Mathematics Applications and Interpretation meets less of that incidentally than one taking Analysis and Approaches, and the result is a physics mark that reflects algebraic fluency rather than physical understanding. This is diagnosable in one session with a marked script: the question is whether the error is in the physics or in the algebra the physics demanded.

The second is uncertainty and data handling. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, how each propagates through a calculation, how to place uncertainty bars, how to draw maximum and minimum gradient lines, and how many significant figures a processed result may honestly carry. All of that is assessed, both in the data-based questions and in the scientific investigation, and it is routinely the thing a crowded school timetable has least room for. It is also, fortunately, a small and bounded body of technique.

The third is command terms. State, outline, describe, explain, determine, deduce, show that, compare, discuss, suggest and justify make different demands and carry different mark allocations. A student who treats explain and describe as synonyms will write a careful description and receive two marks of four. This is not a physics weakness and it does not improve with revision; it improves with being shown the mark scheme.

Only the fourth reason is content, and when it is content it is usually concentrated rather than general: one theme, often fields, rather than the whole course. That distinction matters because the four causes need different purchases. Technique work is a short bounded block of four to six sessions. Uncertainty work is roughly two. Command terms are one session plus repetition against a mark scheme. Only a genuine content gap needs a standing weekly booking across a term, and buying one for a technique problem is how a family funds a year of teaching for something a month would have fixed. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which matters practically here: a processed data table and an annotated graph produced in a session are kept, and the uncertainty method shown in November is available in April rather than remembered.

For island families the useful move is to spend the summer before Year 12 on mathematical technique rather than on physics content, because the content will be taught and the technique will be assumed.

programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 or Pearson Edexcel 4PH1. Both leave a student confident substituting into a formula and much less practised at rearranging before substituting, which is precisely what Diploma Paper 2 requires from the first term onwards.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates arrive having sat a practical component worth 20 per cent, as Paper 5 or Paper 6, so they have met experimental design and simple uncertainty ideas. Pearson candidates, assessed on those skills inside the written papers, often meet formal uncertainty propagation for the first time in the Diploma, which is a known and bounded gap.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-pearl-jumeira.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of Diploma Physics that generate the most sessions for Pearl Jumeira families, separated into technique and content so the diagnosis stays honest.

subjects.name: Rearranging and substituting
subjects.description: Technique rather than physics. Rearranging symbolically before putting numbers in is faster, less error-prone and what the mark scheme expects to see as working. Students who substitute first and rearrange numerically lose method marks and time.

subjects.name: Standard form and unit prefixes
subjects.description: Nano, micro, milli, kilo, mega and giga appear constantly, and a prefix error produces an answer wrong by three orders of magnitude with correct physics behind it. Pure technique, fixable in one session and then maintained by habit.

subjects.name: Uncertainty propagation
subjects.description: Absolute uncertainties add for sums and differences; percentage uncertainties add for products and quotients and multiply by the index for powers. Assessed in data questions and in the investigation, and the single most under-taught body of technique in the course.

subjects.name: Graph linearisation and gradients
subjects.description: Turning a non-linear relationship into a straight line and extracting a physical quantity from the gradient or intercept. The most transferable skill in the course and the one most often absent when a student arrives for a first session.

subjects.name: Theme A: space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, extended at Higher Level into rigid body mechanics and relativity. Sign convention in momentum problems is the reliable loss, and it is a convention rather than a concept.

subjects.name: Theme B: the particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws, current and circuits. Students are comfortable with the numbers and lose marks on the explanation questions that ask why rather than how much, which is a command-term problem in disguise.

subjects.name: Theme C: wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave phenomena, standing waves and the Doppler effect, with interference and diffraction extended at Higher Level. Graph interpretation dominates, which makes shared-screen annotation unusually useful here.

subjects.name: Theme D: fields
subjects.levels: SL and HL, heaviest extension at HL
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric fields, motion within a field, and induction. The theme where Higher Level diverges most, and where questions fail on the combination of steps rather than on any individual one.

subjects.name: Theme E: nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Decay, binding energy, fission and fusion, with the photoelectric effect and quantum ideas extended at Higher Level. Taught late, which means it arrives alongside mocks and needs to be placed on the calendar rather than discovered.

subjects.name: Command terms and mark allocation
subjects.description: Writing four distinct points for a four-mark explain question, and recognising that determine, deduce and show that each demand different working. Not physics, not revision, and among the fastest sources of recovered marks available.

sections.heading: Separating a physics problem from a mathematics problem
paragraphs: This is the first thing a session should establish and it takes one marked script. The question is narrow: at the point where the mark was lost, was the student wrong about the physics, or wrong about the algebra the physics required? Those two findings lead to completely different plans, and conflating them is how families fund a year of physics tutoring for a student whose physics was never the issue.

The diagnostic signs are reasonably clear once you look for them. A student who writes the correct equation, identifies the correct quantities, and then produces an answer wrong by a factor of a thousand has a prefix or standard-form problem. A student who substitutes numbers before rearranging, and then gets lost in the arithmetic, has a technique problem. A student who resolves a vector in the wrong direction has a trigonometry problem. A student who cannot extract a quantity from a gradient has a graph-skills problem. None of those is physics, and all of them look like physics on a report.

The mathematics course the student is taking is a strong predictor. Analysis and Approaches covers algebraic manipulation, calculus and trigonometric technique in a way that happens to serve physics well. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, data and technology, which serves other things well and leaves the physics-facing technique to be taught deliberately. A Pearl Jumeira student taking Physics Higher Level with Applications and Interpretation is not in the wrong place, but they are in a place where four to six sessions of explicit technique work pays for itself several times over.

The reverse diagnosis matters too, and it is the one that saves money. A student whose algebra is secure, whose uncertainty work is sound, and who is still losing marks on fields questions has a genuine content problem, and that needs physics teaching rather than technique work. Being able to say which of the two applies is the whole purpose of buying a diagnostic hour before a standing booking.
bullets: Answer wrong by a factor of a thousand: a prefix or standard-form problem
Lost in the arithmetic after substituting first: a rearranging problem
Vector resolved in the wrong direction: a trigonometry problem
Secure technique and still losing fields marks: a genuine content problem

sections.heading: Uncertainty work: small, assessed, and almost never taught fully
paragraphs: Uncertainty is the clearest example of a high-value, low-volume body of technique in the whole Diploma science programme. The rules take perhaps two sessions to teach properly. They are assessed in the data-based questions and again in the scientific investigation, which is 20 per cent of the grade. And in a crowded school year they are usually covered once, early, and then assumed.

The table sets out what a student actually needs to be able to do. Note how little there is: a handful of rules and two graphical techniques. What makes it valuable is that it recurs in every theme, so a student who is fluent here collects marks across the whole paper rather than in one topic.

The two graphical techniques deserve particular attention because they are where the marks concentrate. Placing uncertainty bars correctly, then drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines through them to estimate the uncertainty in a gradient, is a procedure with a defined output, and students who have practised it three times do it reliably. Students who have seen it once draw a single line of best fit and write a gradient with no uncertainty attached, which caps the mark regardless of how good the rest of the analysis is.

Significant figures are the quiet companion to all of this. A processed result cannot honestly carry more precision than the raw data it came from, and an answer quoted to six figures from measurements taken to two is a statement about the student rather than about the physics. Mark schemes notice. This is a one-minute correction made repeatedly rather than a concept to be grasped, which is exactly the kind of thing a weekly session is good at and a single long session is not.

table.caption: THE UNCERTAINTY TECHNIQUE A DIPLOMA PHYSICS STUDENT NEEDS
rows: Stated to one significant figure, matching the measurement precision
Multiply the percentage uncertainty by the index
Plotted from the absolute uncertainty in each quantity
Drawn through the bars to bound the gradient
No more precision than the raw data supports

sections.heading: Command terms: the same knowledge, two different marks
paragraphs: Two students can know identical physics and receive different marks because one of them read the command term and the other did not. This is the cheapest body of marks in the entire course to recover, and it is almost never the reason a family thinks they are hiring a tutor.

The underlying problem is that command terms look like ordinary English and are not. In ordinary English, describe and explain are nearly interchangeable. In a Diploma physics paper, describe asks for what happens and explain asks for why, with reference to a physical principle, and a careful description earns part marks on an explain question. Determine implies that a value must be found from given information rather than recalled. Deduce requires a conclusion with reasoning attached. Show that requires the student to arrive at a stated result and to display the route, which means an answer with no working earns nothing even when it is correct.

Mark allocation is the second half of the same skill. A four-mark question wants four distinct creditable points, which in practice means four separate statements rather than one long paragraph that contains four ideas in a tangle. Students who write beautifully often lose here, because the examiner has to find the points and the mark scheme awards them individually. Writing to the marks available is a discipline, and it is learned by writing to a mark scheme several times rather than by being told about it once.

The table maps the terms onto their demands. It is worth more to a family than it looks, because it converts a vague instruction to read the question carefully into a specific checklist the student can apply under exam conditions.

table.caption: WHAT EACH PHYSICS COMMAND TERM ACTUALLY DEMANDS
rows: A short answer with no working or justification
Writing a paragraph where one line was wanted
An account of what happens, without reasons
Adding reasons and omitting the sequence
Reasons referenced to a physical principle
A value found from the information given
Quoting a recalled figure instead of deriving it
A conclusion with the reasoning shown
Giving the conclusion with no reasoning
Arriving at a stated result with visible working
Writing the stated result with no route
Similarities and differences, both sides addressed
A plausible proposal consistent with the physics
Treating it as a recall question

sections.heading: Practical skills when the teaching happens online
paragraphs: The reasonable question a Pearl Jumeira parent asks about online physics is what happens to the practical side. The honest answer begins by separating two things that get conflated: handling apparatus, and the analytical skills the examination assesses.

Handling apparatus happens at school, which is where the equipment is, where the technician is, and where the investigation data is collected. Nothing a tutor does replaces that, and nobody should claim otherwise. What the papers assess, however, is largely not apparatus handling. The data-based questions give a student a table or a graph and ask them to process it, linearise it, extract a quantity, attach an uncertainty and comment on the conclusion. The investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and three of those four are desk work.

Those analytical skills are taught better on a shared screen than on paper, for a practical reason rather than a promotional one. A data set can be processed live, with the student doing the work and the tutor marking it as it appears. Uncertainty bars can be added and then moved. Maximum and minimum gradient lines can be drawn, compared, and redrawn. And the whole thing is kept, which means the method is available when the student meets a similar question in April instead of existing only in the memory of a session six months earlier.

There is one area where school and tutor genuinely overlap, and it is worth using deliberately. A student who has collected data at school can bring it to a session and process it properly rather than hurriedly. That is the best use of the format available in this subject: the measurement is the school's job, the analysis is the session's job, and the marks are mostly in the second.

sections.heading: Fitting physics into the island afternoon
paragraphs: Session timing is not an administrative detail in this subject. Physics is where tiredness shows first, because a tired student can still read and still recognise a question type while making the arithmetic slips that send a tutor after the wrong problem entirely.

The shape of the afternoon here is fixed. Senior school days in the Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim cluster end between about 2:45pm and 3:30pm. Pearl Jumeira is reached by a single causeway, so the drive home means crossing Al Wasl Road or Jumeirah Beach Road and then joining one queue onto the island, which takes thirty to forty-five minutes at that hour. Activity programmes run from roughly 4pm to 6pm. The two windows that survive a full year are an early one from about 4:45pm on activity-free days and a dependable one from 6:45pm after food.

For Standard Level one hour in either window is normally the whole requirement. For Higher Level the second year usually needs two hours on separate days, because the fields theme carries the heaviest extension, the investigation reaches its deadline, and the mocks arrive, all in the same term. Two separate hours allow a question to be set, attempted alone and then marked, which a single longer session cannot do because nothing has been attempted in between.

The slots have to be claimed in September. Activity programmes, fixtures and the school's own revision sessions fill the calendar progressively, and by January the available windows in this cluster have usually narrowed to after 7pm. Deciding in September costs nothing and secures the better slot for two years, which is the cheapest advantage available in this subject.
