sections.heading: Physics Higher Level as a pathway decision
paragraphs: A substantial number of Pearl Jumeira students take Physics Higher Level because a degree pathway appears to require it, and it is worth being precise about that rather than vague, because the decision carries two years of workload.

Engineering and physics degrees commonly expect physics and mathematics at Higher Level, and competitive courses in those areas frequently specify Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level alongside. Medicine and dentistry pathways generally centre on chemistry and biology rather than physics, so a student taking Physics Higher Level primarily for a medical application may be carrying a heavy subject for no admissions benefit. Architecture, computer science and some economics routes vary considerably between universities. None of that can be settled on a tutoring page; it is settled on the admissions pages of the specific universities a student might apply to, and those should be read before the subject combination is confirmed.

What a tutor can usefully contribute is the honest workload picture. Physics Higher Level is 240 teaching hours, carries the heaviest extension in the fields theme, and demands mathematical technique that depends on which maths course the student is taking. Paired with Chemistry Higher Level and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, it produces a week with very little slack in it, which in a cluster where school ends at 3:30pm and activities run to six is a real constraint rather than a theoretical one.

The useful conversation to have in the spring of Year 11 is therefore about combinations rather than about individual subjects. A student who takes Physics at Standard Level and performs strongly may be in a better position, for the courses they actually want, than one who takes it at Higher Level and performs adequately. That is a judgement to make with the admissions requirements in front of you rather than on an assumption about what looks stronger.
bullets: Engineering and physics routes commonly expect Higher Level physics and maths
Medicine and dentistry pathways generally centre on chemistry and biology
Check the specific universities' own admissions pages before confirming subjects
A strong Standard Level grade can serve a student better than an adequate Higher Level one

sections.heading: Using past papers across two years without wasting them
paragraphs: Past papers are the most valuable resource in the course and the most commonly squandered, because they get used too early, too fast and without marking. A deliberate programme across the two years makes a finite supply last and extracts more from each one.

In the first year, whole papers are mostly premature, since much of the content has not been taught. What works instead is single questions, chosen by topic, worked immediately after that topic is covered in class. This builds the habit of writing to the mark scheme while the material is fresh and consumes almost no papers. A tutor's job in this period is to mark those questions properly and to name the loss type each time, so the student starts recognising their own patterns.

In the second year the unit becomes the section and then the paper. Data-based questions make an excellent weekly diet because they drill uncertainty and graph work simultaneously. Extended-response questions should be written to the mark allocation and marked against the published scheme, with the student counting their own creditable points before the tutor does. Higher Level students need deliberate practice at long structured questions, where the value is in carrying on after an early error rather than in any individual topic.

In the final weeks the papers should be sat whole, under time, unaided, and then marked. That is also when the paid hours should reduce rather than increase. A session in this period is most useful for marking what the student has done alone, because accuracy and pace set through their own repetition rather than through further teaching. One further point on materials: past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade boundary tables belong to the IB and are referenced and linked rather than redistributed, and a tutor arriving with a folder of copied material has told you something about their standards before teaching anything.

sections.heading: What physics support costs, and the limits on investigation help
paragraphs: Two practical matters belong together at the end, because both are things a family should know before committing. The market rates first. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350. Online qualified subject tutors are published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IB rates from AED 200 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. Premium examiner-branded providers reach AED 500 to AED 650, with BartyED at AED 650. Those figures belong to the providers named and were read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price list.

On a single-causeway island a large part of any in-home premium is covering the approach rather than the teaching, and that is worth seeing clearly. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the rate carries no travel and the second weekly hour in the heavy term costs an hour rather than an hour plus two drives.

Now the limits. The scientific investigation is 20 per cent of the Physics grade, marked against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, within a 3,000-word limit. What a tutor may legitimately do is explain what each criterion rewards, teach the physics involved, show how uncertainty propagates through the particular calculation, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. What a tutor may not do is write, draft, redraft or supply any part of it, or hand over a research question for adoption.

That boundary is stated here rather than buried because at least one operator ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. Submitting purchased work is a malpractice risk that attaches to the student rather than to the seller, and the consequence sits on a transcript rather than on an invoice. No grade or improvement is guaranteed here either, because nobody can honestly stand behind such a promise.

faqs.question: My child understands physics but keeps losing marks. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three things that are not physics. Mathematical technique: substituting before rearranging, prefix and standard-form errors, or resolving a vector wrongly. Uncertainty handling: no uncertainty attached to a gradient, or significant figures that the raw data does not support. Command terms: writing a description where an explanation was asked for. All three look like physics on a report and none responds to physics revision. A single session on a marked script will say which one is operating.

faqs.question: Does taking Applications and Interpretation make Diploma Physics harder?
faqs.answer: It leaves more of the physics-facing technique to be taught deliberately. Diploma Physics assumes rearranging before substituting, confident standard form, trigonometry for resolving vectors, gradient and area work, and some calculus at Higher Level. Analysis and Approaches covers much of that incidentally; Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, data and technology instead. The gap is specific and bounded rather than a general disadvantage, and four to six sessions of explicit technique work usually closes it.

faqs.question: What uncertainty rules does a Diploma physics student actually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most students expect. Absolute uncertainties add for sums and differences. Percentage uncertainties add for products and quotients. For a power, the percentage uncertainty multiplies by the index. Uncertainty bars are plotted from the absolute uncertainties, and maximum and minimum gradient lines drawn through them bound the gradient. A processed result carries no more precision than the raw data supports. That is close to the whole body of technique, and it is assessed across every theme.

faqs.question: Why does a gradient without an uncertainty cap the mark?
faqs.answer: Because the data analysis criterion and the data-based questions both expect uncertainty to be carried through to the result. A single line of best fit with a gradient quoted and no uncertainty attached is an incomplete analysis however accurate the gradient is. Drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines through the uncertainty bars is a defined procedure with a defined output, and students who have practised it three times do it reliably. Students who saw it once generally do not do it at all.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describe and explain in a physics paper?
faqs.answer: Describe asks for what happens, as a sequence, without reasons. Explain asks for why, with reference to a physical principle. A student who gives a careful description on an explain question will earn part of the marks and feel the mark scheme was unfair. The same applies to determine, which requires a value derived from given information, and deduce, which requires a conclusion with reasoning shown. Show that requires visible working, so a correct answer with no route earns nothing.

faqs.question: How should a four-mark physics question be answered?
faqs.answer: With four distinct creditable statements rather than one paragraph containing four ideas. Mark schemes award points individually, and an examiner has to be able to find each one. Students who write fluently often lose marks here, because the ideas are present but tangled. Writing to the mark allocation is a discipline learned by writing several answers against a published scheme and counting the creditable points before the tutor does, not by being told to read the question carefully.

faqs.question: How does practical physics work if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The apparatus work stays at school, where the equipment and the technician are and where investigation data is collected. What the examination mostly assesses is the analysis: processing a data set, linearising it, extracting a quantity from a gradient, attaching an uncertainty and judging the conclusion. Three of the four investigation criteria are desk work. Those skills are taught better on a shared screen than on paper, because the processing happens live and the completed working is kept for later.

faqs.question: Can my child bring school data to a session to work through?
faqs.answer: That is the best use of the format available in this subject. The measurement is the school's job and the analysis is the session's job, and the marks are mostly in the second. A student who has collected data at school can process it properly rather than hurriedly: place uncertainty bars, linearise the relationship, bound the gradient, and write a conclusion that the data actually supports. The work remains entirely theirs, and the session is spent on technique rather than on explanation.

faqs.question: What time should a physics session run for a student on Pearl Jumeira?
faqs.answer: Around 4:45pm on an activity-free day, or from 6:45pm after food. School in this cluster ends between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, and the Al Wasl Road crossing plus the causeway queue takes thirty to forty-five minutes. Physics is where tiredness shows first: a tired student still recognises question types while making arithmetic slips, which sends the tutor after the wrong problem. Nothing useful happens after about 8:30pm on a school night in this subject.

faqs.question: Why would Higher Level physics need two sessions a week in the second year?
faqs.answer: Because three demanding things arrive in the same term: the fields theme with the heaviest Higher Level extension, the investigation deadline, and the mock window. Two separate hours on different days create a gap in which work can be attempted unaided, which is what gives the second session something real to mark. A single two-hour block cannot do that, since nothing has been attempted between its halves. Planning for it in September secures a better slot than scrambling in January.

faqs.question: Is Physics Higher Level necessary for medicine?
faqs.answer: Generally not, and this is worth checking rather than assuming. Medicine and dentistry pathways typically centre on chemistry and biology, so a student carrying Physics at Higher Level mainly for a medical application may be taking a heavy subject for no admissions benefit. Engineering and physics degrees are the routes that commonly expect it, frequently alongside Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Read the specific universities' own admissions pages before the subject combination is confirmed, rather than relying on any tutoring site.

faqs.question: When should past papers start being used in Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: Single questions from the first year, whole papers in the second. In year one much of the content has not been taught, so a whole paper mostly demonstrates what the student cannot yet do. Single questions worked immediately after a topic is covered in class build mark-scheme habits while the material is fresh and consume almost no papers. In year two the unit becomes the section and then the paper, with data-based questions as a useful weekly diet.

faqs.question: What does legitimate investigation support look like week by week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the legitimate version is substantial. A tutor explains what research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation each reward, teaches the physics the student has chosen to investigate, shows how uncertainty propagates through that particular calculation, and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. What a tutor does not do is write, draft, redraft or supply any part of it, or hand over a research question. Submitting purchased work is a malpractice risk carried by the student alone.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor onto Pearl Jumeira?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. intro.heading: Three comparisons sit underneath one question about physics
paragraphs: A physics enquiry from this corridor usually carries three unspoken comparisons. The first is between systems: a Diploma student's parents watching a neighbour take three A Levels and wondering whether six subjects plus a core is the harder bargain. The second is between levels, Higher against Standard, usually framed as difficulty when the real variable is load. The third is between combinations, because physics is rarely chosen alone and what it is paired with decides what it opens.

Those comparisons matter because physics is a gateway subject. Engineering and the physical sciences expect it, often at Higher Level and usually alongside a particular mathematics route, and a combination assembled without checking can close doors quietly. The checking belongs with each university's own published entry profile rather than with general advice, and it should happen in Year 11 rather than in Year 13.

Remraam shapes the practical side. It is a low-rise apartment community in Dubailand, built as the Al Thamam and Al Ramth clusters with its own park and retail, reached from Al Qudra Road and Emirates Road. South View School sits close by and takes students through Year 11, so Diploma students have generally moved outward to Dubai Hills, Al Barsha South or The Sustainable City, which means a longer afternoon and a shorter evening than their IGCSE years allowed.

It also shapes supply. The tutors advertising along this corridor are based around Dubai Investment Park, Dubai Sports City and Motor City, and most of them work across several sciences at IGCSE level with Diploma physics as an extension. Higher Level physics is one of the thinnest specialisms in any tutoring market, which is the practical argument for choosing by level and option rather than by distance.

There is a fourth comparison that nobody frames as one, and it costs real money: the option topic. Schools choose which option to teach in physics, so two Diploma students in Dubai can sit the same core and entirely different option questions. A revision guide bought online, a group class assembled from several schools, or a tutor who was never told the option can all end up preparing material the student will never be examined on. One message to the department settles it, and almost nobody sends it.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, so a session can sit early or after eight depending on the household. The experiment stays with the school and its laboratory, which this page states rather than skirts. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and nothing here should be read as an offer to arrive at a Remraam address. Each of the four comparisons gets its own section below, with a table where the detail justifies one.

sections.heading: IGCSE physics into Diploma physics, mapped
paragraphs: The step from IGCSE physics into either Diploma level is larger than the grade at sixteen suggests, and it is larger in specific ways that can be prepared for. Content is the smallest part of it. The three real changes are mathematical demand, the expectation of justification rather than statement, and the arrival of a substantial internally assessed investigation with published criteria.

The mathematical change is the one that catches students from this corridor, who generally sat IGCSE locally and then moved schools. IGCSE physics rewards recall and single-step calculation. Diploma physics assumes rearrangement is automatic, uses standard form constantly, introduces logarithms in the nuclear and quantum material, and asks repeatedly for a gradient to be converted into a physical quantity with units. A student who was comfortable at IGCSE and slow at algebra will feel competent for a term and then stop coping.

The justification change is cultural. An IGCSE answer often earns full marks for stating what happens. A Diploma extended response wants the physics named, the assumption stated and the steps connected, and students carry the IGCSE habit forward for months without anyone identifying it as the problem. It reads as a content gap and is not.

The investigation is new in kind. Nothing at IGCSE prepares a student for being marked on design and evaluation against descriptors rather than on whether an experiment produced a tidy result, and the earlier they read those descriptors, the better the first attempt goes.

sections.heading: Diploma physics against A Level physics
paragraphs: Both qualifications are accepted by universities worldwide and the choice is about the student rather than about status. The structural difference is that the Diploma asks for six subjects plus a core while A Levels ask for three or four studied further, and physics sits inside those two shapes quite differently.

In the Diploma, physics is one of six commitments and carries an internal investigation alongside its papers, so a student is managing breadth, a coursework deadline in every subject, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge simultaneously. In A Levels, physics is one of three or four, usually with a smaller internal element, and the student has more hours per subject and far fewer parallel deadlines.

The consequence is temperamental rather than academic. A student who manages competing deadlines well and dislikes narrowing at sixteen is better served by the Diploma. A student who works deeply on fewer things and struggles to juggle is often better served by A Levels, and choosing the Diploma for its reputation while being the second kind of student is a predictable way to underperform.

On depth, A Level physics typically goes further in individual topics while Diploma physics covers more ground and distributes the mathematical demand. Neither is a disadvantage at university entry, but it does change what preparation looks like: A Level students need depth drilling, Diploma students need breadth retention and a plan for the internal component.

One practical note for families comparing locally. Several schools within reach of this corridor run A Levels after Year 11 while others run the Diploma, so the choice is often made at the same time as a school choice rather than separately. That bundling obscures the question, and it is worth separating the two decisions explicitly before either is made.

sections.heading: Subject combinations compared for engineering and the sciences
paragraphs: Physics is almost never the decisive subject on its own. What decides an engineering or physical-science application is the combination, and the combination is assembled in Year 11 by students who have not yet looked at an entry profile. That sequence is backwards and it is easy to fix.

The combination most competitive engineering courses expect is physics and mathematics at Higher Level, with Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation as the mathematics route. Substituting Applications is where students most often discover a problem after offers are published, because some institutions specify the route and not merely the level. Equally, Physics at Standard Level will not satisfy most engineering requirements however strong the grade.

For chemical engineering and materials, chemistry joins the pair. For architecture the picture is more permissive and Applications is often acceptable. For biomedical routes, biology enters and the physics requirement is sometimes relaxed. None of these generalisations should be relied on, because requirements differ by country and institution and change between cycles.

The useful action is narrow and free. List the five or six universities genuinely under consideration, read each one's published entry profile for the specific course, and write down what it says about level and route. Do that with the school's careers office before subject choices are confirmed, and the combination becomes a decision rather than an accident.

Load is the other half of the combination question. A student who assembles the most demanding possible set to keep every door open can end up performing moderately across all of it, which closes more doors than a slightly narrower set performed well. That trade is worth making consciously in Year 11, with the school, rather than discovering it in the autumn of the final year.

sections.heading: Higher against Standard Level: a load question
paragraphs: The level question is usually asked as difficulty and is better answered as load. Higher Level physics covers additional content and examines an extra paper, and it is the level most engineering and physical-science applications expect. Standard Level covers the core across fewer papers. Those are facts about quantity and about doors, not about whether the examination is gentler.

The part families misjudge is that the question styles are identical. Standard Level is not an easier form of assessment on narrower content; it is the same form of assessment on narrower content. A student losing marks to unstated assumptions in extended response will lose them at either level, which means dropping a level does not solve a technique problem and should not be sold as if it does.

Where dropping genuinely helps is total load. A student carrying three Higher Level sciences, or Higher Level physics alongside Higher Level mathematics and chemistry, is carrying three content loads and three internal investigations on overlapping deadlines. That combination defeats capable students, and doing two of them well is a better outcome than doing three adequately.

Timing matters as much as the decision. A level change is practical early in Year 12 and in some schools becomes impossible once the second year begins because teaching groups diverge. If the question is live, ask the department for its own deadline in writing and for the evidence it would want to see either way.

There is one more consideration that is rarely raised. Dropping a level mid-course changes the teaching group and sometimes the teacher, and for a student who was coping socially rather than academically that disruption has its own cost. It is still often the right decision, and it is better made deliberately with the department than as a reaction to one bad report.

sections.heading: What the school's option choice changes
paragraphs: Schools choose which option topic to teach in physics, which means two Diploma physics students in Dubai can sit the same core content and entirely different option questions. Families rarely know this, and it quietly wastes revision time and money every year in this city.

The practical consequences are three. A revision guide bought online may cover an option the student will never be examined on. A group revision class assembled from several schools cannot teach the option at all, because the room contains more than one. And a tutor who has not been told the option will prepare the wrong material, which is a mistake nobody notices until a mock.

The fix costs one question at a parents' evening or one message to the department: which option are you teaching, and which paper does it appear in. Write the answer down and give it to anyone who sets work for the student. It is the single most useful administrative fact a Diploma physics family can hold.

The school also determines the practical programme, which constrains the investigation. A research question requiring apparatus the department does not own is a dead end regardless of its quality, and asking for the practical calendar early is the cheapest planning available in the subject. Both facts are reasons a tutoring enquiry should name the school as well as the level.

A related point concerns moving school mid-Diploma, which happens in this city. Two schools may teach different options, so a transferring student can arrive having studied content they will not be examined on and missing content they will. That is one of the few situations where a short, targeted block of tutoring is genuinely unavoidable, and it should be arranged before the move rather than after it.

sections.heading: Why Higher Level physics help is thin along this corridor
paragraphs: Higher Level physics is one of the thinnest specialisms in any tutoring market, and the reason is arithmetic rather than neglect. A tutor who teaches only Higher Level physics needs a large catchment of Diploma students to fill a week, and the Diploma is 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum. Within Dubailand, where most schools run IGCSE and A Levels, the local pool is thinner still.

So the people advertising along this corridor, based around Dubai Investment Park, Dubai Sports City and Motor City, sensibly cover several sciences at IGCSE level and take Diploma physics as an extension. That is a reasonable business and a poor match for a student at a 4 in Physics Higher Level who needs somebody who knows what Paper 3 rewards and which option their school teaches.

Removing the distance filter changes the pool completely. Selecting by level and option means selecting from people who have taught the level repeatedly, wherever they happen to live, and the lesson arrives over video either way. For Standard Level the difference is smaller, because the content is narrower and more widely covered. For Higher Level it is the difference between a tutor who explains and a tutor who keeps pace.

The honest corollary is that coverage still has limits. Higher Level physics with a less common option, or physics paired with Further Mathematics, is thin everywhere, and where that applies a family should be told with a timescale rather than matched with a generalist and left to discover it.

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs across these comparisons
paragraphs: The comparisons on this page imply different purchases, and two of them are small. A choice and combination session in Year 11 is one or two hours. A summer bridging block is six to eight sessions. Term-time technique and investigation support is a weekly hour. Only the final-stretch work in Year 13 is a sustained twice-weekly commitment.

Physics sits at the specialist end of the published bands because credible Higher Level coverage is scarce. Named IB and IGCSE specialists publish roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table giving AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 500 to 650, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Below that, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52, which suits routine question practice rather than Higher Level technique. Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. sections.heading: Permits, laboratories and coursework limits
paragraphs: Three boundaries apply and all three are worth stating plainly. The first is the laboratory: an online tutor cannot run an experiment, and the practical belongs to the school, its equipment and its safety procedures. What a session does is interrogate the research question before the practical and examine the data, graph choice, uncertainty propagation and evaluation afterwards, which is where most of the criterion marks sit.

The second is coursework. The investigation is assessed and must be the student's own, authenticated by the teacher. A tutor may teach the physics, explain what each criterion rewards, say that a method will not produce usable data, and mark a draft the student wrote against the published descriptors. A tutor may not draft, rewrite, edit to completion, supply text or provide data the student did not collect, and the temptation to do the last of those is real when an experiment fails near a deadline.

The third is permits. An individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws with no published fine schedule.

A business with premises needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit instead, renewed annually. IB Gram has no UAE premises, holds no such permit, and does not use a regulator's name to describe its tutors. Board material stays with its publishers and is linked rather than circulated.

faqs.question: Is Diploma physics harder than A Level physics?
faqs.answer: Different rather than harder. A Level physics typically goes deeper in individual topics; Diploma physics covers more ground, distributes its mathematical demand across the course, and sits inside six subjects plus a core with an internal investigation in every subject. The practical difference is temperamental: a student who manages competing deadlines well and dislikes narrowing at sixteen suits the Diploma, while one who works deeply on fewer things and juggles poorly often does better with A Levels. Both are accepted by universities worldwide.

faqs.question: What actually changes between IGCSE physics and Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: Three things, and content is the smallest. Mathematical demand rises sharply: rearrangement is assumed automatic, standard form is constant, logarithms arrive, and gradients must be converted into quantities with units. The answer expectation shifts from stating what happens to naming the physics and the assumption and connecting the steps. And a marked investigation appears, assessed on design and evaluation rather than on a tidy result. All three are preparable in a summer block and otherwise look like weakness in the first mock.

faqs.question: Does an engineering application really need Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Many competitive courses specify it rather than accepting either maths route, and that is the detail students discover after offers are published. The pairing usually expected is physics and mathematics at Higher Level with Analysis as the route. Applications and Interpretation is more often acceptable for architecture and some applied programmes. None of this should be relied on generally, because requirements differ by country and institution and change between cycles. List the universities genuinely under consideration and read each one's published course page.

faqs.question: Will Physics at Standard Level be enough for a science degree?
faqs.answer: For most engineering and physical-science courses, no, however strong the grade, because the level itself is frequently stated as a minimum. Standard Level physics works well as a third science for economics, business and some architecture routes. The way to settle it is to read the entry profile for the specific course at each institution rather than to rely on general advice, and to do that in Year 11 while the choice is still open rather than in Year 13 when it is not.

faqs.question: Should our son drop Physics HL to reduce his workload?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and for the right reason. The question styles are identical at both levels, so a technique problem such as unstated assumptions in extended response travels with him and dropping will not fix it. Where dropping genuinely helps is total load, particularly for a student carrying three Higher Level sciences or Higher Level physics with Higher Level mathematics and chemistry, which is three content loads and three internal investigations on overlapping deadlines. Ask the department for its own deadline, because the change becomes impractical once the second year starts.

faqs.question: Why does the option topic matter so much for physics?
faqs.answer: Because schools choose it, so two Diploma physics students in Dubai can sit the same core and completely different option questions. Three things follow: a revision guide bought online may cover an option your child will never be examined on, a group class assembled from several schools cannot teach any single option, and a tutor who was not told will prepare the wrong material. One message to the department settles it, and the answer should be given to anybody who sets work for the student.

faqs.question: How should the summer before Diploma physics be used?
faqs.answer: On the things the first term assumes and does not teach. Rearrangement at speed, standard form and prefix conversion, basic logarithm manipulation, vector components, and the habit of justifying rather than stating. Six to eight sessions is realistic with no competing homework. Students from this corridor generally sat IGCSE locally at South View School and then moved, so they arrive in a class containing students from several boards with very different preparation, and the gap shows within weeks rather than months.

faqs.question: Is it true that weak maths is behind most physics failure?
faqs.answer: Very often, and misreading it wastes a term. The signature in a marked script is errors clustering around algebra rather than around concepts: rearrangement failing when the unknown sits in a denominator or under a root, slow standard-form conversion, logarithms blocking access to a question entirely, and gradients treated as bare numbers. The test a parent can apply is to strip the physics from a failed question and ask for the algebra alone. If that fails in isolation, the hour belongs to manipulation practice.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: With everything except the measuring, which carries the fewest marks. Before the practical, a session can interrogate the research question, test whether the method will produce a measurable relationship, name the variables needing control and anticipate the dominant uncertainty. Afterwards it can examine the raw data, check whether a different graph reveals a relationship a direct plot hides, work propagation on the student's own numbers and read the draft against each criterion. The experiment belongs to the school and its equipment.

faqs.question: Why is Higher Level physics tutoring so hard to find near Remraam?
faqs.answer: Arithmetic rather than neglect. A tutor teaching only Higher Level physics needs a large Diploma catchment to fill a week, and IB programmes accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25 against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum. Within Dubailand, where most schools run IGCSE and A Levels, the local pool is thinner still, so advertisers here sensibly cover several sciences at IGCSE level. Selecting by level and option rather than distance replaces that geographic pool with a subject pool.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take physics and maths for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and the overlap is genuine: calculus, vectors and graph interpretation all reappear in mechanics and fields, so one subject reinforces the other rather than competing with it. At Higher Level in both simultaneously the combination is less common and the honest answer is sometimes two tutors. The question to ask is which papers the tutor has marked in each subject rather than whether they can teach both. Scheduling is identical either way, because no travel has to be arranged between slots.

faqs.question: What does a physics specialist cost compared with a general science tutor?
faqs.answer: Physics sits at the specialist end because credible Higher Level coverage is scarce. Named IB and IGCSE specialists publish roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table at AED 200 to 450 or more, while premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. These are published market figures rather than IB Gram prices, and a free trial comes before payment.

faqs.question: Is a physics Extended Essay worth attempting?
faqs.answer: It can be excellent and it is unforgiving for practical reasons. The research question has to be answerable with apparatus the school actually holds, through a measurement a student can take reliably, within the word limit. Most weak physics Extended Essays are competently written and ask something the available equipment could never answer. One or two sessions interrogating the question before any work begins is worth more than ten afterwards, and the essay itself must be entirely the student's own, authenticated by the supervisor.

faqs.question: How long before results should a combination conversation happen?
faqs.answer: A full year before applications, which in practice means during Year 11. The combination is assembled then, by students who have not yet read an entry profile, and it quietly decides what the application can aim at. The exercise is free: list the five or six universities genuinely under consideration, read what each publishes for the specific course, and note what it says about level and maths route. Do it with the school's careers office, and the combination becomes a decision instead of an accident.

intro.heading: Physics is where a generalist tutor cannot hide
paragraphs: Serena sits off Al Qudra Road at the outer edge of the Dubailand belt, among clusters including Bella Casa and Casa Viva, with Mudon, Villanova and Remraam nearby. Families here asking whether anyone nearby knows the physics syllabus are asking the right question in the wrong form. The useful question is whether a given tutor knows this course, at this level, under the current guide — and that has nothing to do with distance.

Physics is the subject where the gap between a competent graduate and a physics teacher shows fastest. A mathematician can solve the problems and will not know that the examiner wants a derivation where the student wrote a description. An engineer will handle the content and may never have taught uncertainty propagation, which is examined and almost never taught. Both will teach a student who then loses the same marks they were losing before.

There is a second trap specific to this subject: the mathematical demand. Physics at Diploma level assumes fluent algebraic rearrangement, confident standard form, comfort with gradients and, in places, small-angle approximations and logarithmic scales. A student paired with Mathematics Applications and Interpretation often looks careless in physics when they are carrying arithmetic overload, and a tutor who does not separate the two diagnoses the wrong problem.

IB Gram matches on the named level and on the component the marked papers point at, and teaches live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. No tutor travels to a UAE address — home visits are a service we run only in India — and there is no IB Gram office or centre in the country. For physics specifically the online format gives up little: the subject is worked on a page and a graph, and simulations let a student change a parameter and watch the consequence, which is the fastest route into field and circuit reasoning.

What follows is the detail you need to interrogate any physics tutor. The questions that identify real course knowledge. What the Higher Level content actually adds, theme by theme. Uncertainties, properly explained. The command terms that decide marks. The experimental programme and what it requires. The mathematical demand by topic. And where availability and price genuinely sit in this market.

One standing note: we publish no IB exam or results dates, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and a date a family plans around must be checkable. UAE schools sit the May session. Specification versions are also revised, so confirm paper durations, weightings and practical hours for your child's cohort with the school rather than treating any page as final, this one included. What does not change between guides is the structure of the problem: five themes with unequal Higher Level extensions, an examined data-analysis skill nobody teaches, command terms that decide marks before the physics is read, and an investigation whose ceiling is set by its research question.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-serena.subjectsIntro: This page is about physics, so these are the themes and components, each with the specific skill it examines and the error that costs marks.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum and energy, with rotational and relativistic extensions at Higher Level. Familiar enough to breed false confidence: students solve standard questions and then fail to justify which relationship applies and why, which is what the harder questions ask.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws and current electricity. Circuits are the largest reliable loss in UAE cohorts, because students know the rules and cannot reason about what happens elsewhere in the circuit when one component changes.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Wave models, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect, with further interference work at Higher Level. The commonest loss is description without cause: stating that a pattern appears without identifying the path difference or phase relationship producing it.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields including induction, and the heaviest Higher Level extensions. Sign conventions in potential energy problems and field-line reasoning are where Higher Level marks disappear in volume, usually because the theme was reached late.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Atomic structure, decay, fission, fusion and quantum phenomena at Higher Level. Conceptually unfamiliar and computationally tidy, which makes it the most reliable late-stage gain for a student who postponed it.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error analysis
subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and uncertainty in a gradient. Threaded through the data-analysis component and the investigation, examined consistently, and the single most under-taught skill in the course.

subjects.name: Data analysis and graphing
subjects.description: Plotting, linearising a relationship, reading a gradient and drawing a supported conclusion from unseen data. Students who have never plotted error bars by hand or found a gradient uncertainty lose these marks regardless of how well they know the themes.

subjects.name: Extended response technique
subjects.description: Multi-part questions that build, carrying the largest share of the grade. Marks go missing to description where derivation was required, to abandoned part-answers, and to units dropped in the final line after correct physics throughout.

subjects.name: The Scientific Investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation of up to 3,000 words worth 20 per cent, marked on four criteria of six marks each. Research design sets the ceiling: a question with no measurable, controllable relationship cannot score on the later criteria however carefully it is written up.

subjects.name: The experimental programme
subjects.description: A required number of practical hours across the course, including a collaborative sciences project, delivered and supervised by the school. Confirm the hours and arrangements with your child's teacher, since they are a school-managed requirement rather than something a tutor provides.

subjects.name: Mathematical technique in physics
subjects.description: Rearranging before substituting, standard form, gradients, small-angle approximations and reading logarithmic scales. For students taking Mathematics Applications and Interpretation this strand usually needs explicit support rather than assumption.

subjects.name: Command terms
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, deduce, derive, discuss and justify each carry a distinct expectation and mark ceiling. A student answering 'explain' with a description has lost the marks before the physics is read, and the fix is one session with a marked paper.

sections.heading: Four questions that identify a physics teacher
paragraphs: These work on a neighbour's recommendation, an agency and on us, and they take two minutes. They are deliberately not about years of experience, because experience in a superseded version of the course can mislead a student confidently.

First: what does Higher Level add, and where? The answer is content inside all five themes rather than a sixth theme, with the heaviest extensions in fields and in Theme A, and longer papers. A tutor who says Higher Level is 'the same with harder questions' has not taught it. Second: how do you handle uncertainties? A physics teacher will talk about absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation and the uncertainty in a gradient. A generalist will say they cover errors.

Third: what is the difference between 'describe', 'explain' and 'derive' in a mark scheme? The answer should be immediate and specific, because it is the single largest source of lost marks in the subject. Fourth: what do you do with the student's experimental data in investigation support? The correct answer is nothing: they look at it, question it and comment on the processing, and the student produces and processes it.

A fifth question is worth asking if the student takes Applications and Interpretation for mathematics: how will you handle the mathematical demand? A physics teacher who has taught that combination will name the specific pressure points — rearrangement speed, standard form, logarithmic scales — and plan explicit work on them. One who has not will treat careless arithmetic as inattention and keep teaching physics.

sections.heading: Higher Level versus Standard Level, theme by theme
paragraphs: The most common misconception among parents is that Higher Level is the same course with harder examinations. It is not: there is additional content, it is distributed unevenly across the themes, and the papers are longer. Knowing where the extra material sits changes when it should be taught.

The extensions are heaviest in Theme A and Theme D. In Theme A the additional work pushes into rotational dynamics and relativistic ideas; in Theme D it deepens field reasoning and induction. Theme E adds quantum material that is conceptually unfamiliar. Themes B and C extend less dramatically. The practical consequence is that a Higher Level student who treats all five themes as equal workloads will under-prepare the two that carry the most new material.

The timing problem follows from that. Fields is both the hardest theme and one of the latest to be taught in many schemes of work, which means the heaviest Higher Level extension arrives in DP2 at the same time as the Scientific Investigation deadline. That collision is predictable and therefore avoidable: front-loading field reasoning in DP1, even informally, removes the worst of it.

Confirm the exact arrangement for your child's cohort with the school, since specification versions are revised. What does not change is the shape of the problem: unequal extensions, a late-arriving hard theme, and an internal assessment deadline in the same window. The question to put to a school, early in DP1, is simply when fields is scheduled - and if the answer is the second half of DP2, that is worth knowing a year in advance rather than discovering it alongside the investigation.

sections.heading: Uncertainties: the skill nobody teaches
paragraphs: If a Serena family buys only three physics sessions, this is what they should buy. Uncertainty handling is examined in the data-analysis component and throughout the Scientific Investigation, it appears in extended response, and almost no student has been taught it properly. The marks are available to anyone who learns it, which is unusual in a subject this competitive.

What it actually involves is finite and learnable. Absolute uncertainty on a single reading, and why it is half the smallest division only sometimes. Percentage uncertainty, and when to convert between the two. Propagation: adding absolute uncertainties when quantities are added or subtracted, adding percentage uncertainties when they are multiplied or divided, and multiplying the percentage by the power when a quantity is raised. Quoting an uncertainty to one significant figure and matching the precision of the value to it.

Then the graphical work, which is where investigation marks live. Plotting error bars by hand. Drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines and using them to estimate the uncertainty in a gradient. Understanding that a linearised plot exists so that a gradient can be interpreted physically, not because graphs must be straight. Students who have done this once on paper handle it; students who have only seen it in a slide do not.

The reason this is under-taught is not negligence. It is slow to teach, it looks like arithmetic rather than physics, and it rarely features in a textbook chapter that a class is working through. That is exactly why it is efficient to buy from outside: three sessions on it typically shows up in a mock more clearly than three sessions on any single theme.

sections.heading: Command terms, and the marks they decide
paragraphs: Physics mark schemes are written against command terms, and students read them as synonyms. That misreading is the largest single category of lost marks we see in marked papers from Dubai cohorts, and it is correctable in a single session.

'State' wants a fact with no justification, so time spent explaining is wasted. 'Describe' wants what happens without the why. 'Explain' wants the mechanism or reason, and a description earns nothing. 'Deduce' wants a conclusion reached from given information. 'Derive' wants the algebra from a starting relationship to the required result, and quoting the result is worth nothing at all. 'Discuss' wants both sides or a balanced consideration. 'Justify' wants a reason attached to a choice.

The diagnostic exercise is simple and worth doing at home before any tutoring is bought. Take the student's last marked paper, go through every question where marks were lost, and mark each loss as content, arithmetic, or command term. In most mid-grade papers from this belt the command-term column is larger than families expect, and it is the cheapest of the three to fix.

This is also why strict marking matters more in physics than almost anywhere else. A tutor who ticks answers that are physically correct but do not do what the command term asked is confirming the habit that is costing the marks. Work should be marked the way an examiner marks it — command term, units, significant figures, derivation shown — rather than assessed for whether the student understood.

sections.heading: The experimental programme and the investigation
paragraphs: Physics carries a required practical element delivered by the school, including an individual Scientific Investigation and a collaborative project element. Confirm the exact hours and arrangements with your child's teacher, because they are school-managed and vary in how they are scheduled, but the principle is fixed: the apparatus work happens in the school laboratory, under the school's supervision.

That boundary is worth stating plainly because it is often fudged in advertising. No online tutor can substitute for handling apparatus, and for the Scientific Investigation the student's own experimental work is a requirement rather than a preference. Anyone implying that a screen replaces the laboratory is overselling, and a family should treat that as a warning about everything else they claim.

What is genuinely teachable away from the bench is most of where the marks are. Research design: whether the question has a variable the student can change, a quantity they can measure with the school's equipment, and the other variables controllable. Data analysis: processing with correct uncertainties, plotting something interpretable, extracting a gradient and its uncertainty. Conclusion: a result the measurements support rather than the one the textbook predicts. Evaluation: specific prioritised weaknesses with realistic improvements, not generic remarks about human error.

The boundary on help is the same as elsewhere in the Diploma and firmer than many families expect. A tutor may explain criteria, test a research question, question reasoning and comment on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the investigation, produce or process the data, write or rewrite text, or supply a previous student's report. Those are passing off another person's work as the student's own, which risks the Diploma rather than one grade.

sections.heading: The mathematical demand, topic by topic
paragraphs: Physics failures are frequently mathematics failures wearing a physics costume, and separating the two is the most useful diagnostic move available in the first session. A student who can explain the physics verbally and cannot execute the algebra needs different help from one who cannot explain it.

The demands are specific rather than general. Kinematics needs confident rearrangement and quadratic solution. Circuits need ratio reasoning and simultaneous thinking about series and parallel combinations. Fields need inverse-square manipulation and careful sign handling. Waves need trigonometric relationships and, in places, small-angle approximation. Nuclear decay needs logarithms and exponential reasoning. Data analysis needs gradients, linearisation and percentage work.

That is why the mathematics course a student takes alongside physics matters. Analysis and Approaches builds the rearrangement fluency and calculus habits physics assumes. Applications and Interpretation builds statistical and modelling strength instead, which is valuable and different. A Higher Level physics student on Applications and Interpretation is not in the wrong place, but the mathematical strand needs explicit support from the first term rather than discovery in a mock.

The table below maps the demand so a family can see which gaps to test for. In practice the test is quick: give the student a rearrangement exercise with no physics in it and see what happens. If the algebra is slow, the physics sessions should start there, because every subsequent topic will be carried on top of it. Two or three sessions of rearrangement and standard-form work, with no physics attached, is an unglamorous purchase that changes the return on everything bought afterwards.

sections.heading: Tools, graphs and simulations: what helps and what does not
paragraphs: Physics has more usable technology than any other Diploma subject, and most of it is free. Used well it accelerates exactly the reasoning students find hardest; used badly it replaces thinking with watching.

What helps: a graphing tool in which the student plots their own data and manipulates the axes, because linearising a relationship becomes concrete rather than abstract. A spreadsheet in which they build the uncertainty columns themselves, which teaches propagation faster than any explanation. And interactive simulations of fields and circuits, where changing one parameter and predicting the consequence before releasing it is genuinely the fastest route into the reasoning the harder questions demand.

What does not help: watching a simulation run while a tutor narrates it. The learning is in the prediction, not the animation. The same applies to video explanations of worked examples, which feel productive and produce recognition rather than capability. A student who has watched someone derive a result can usually follow it and cannot reproduce it, which is a distinction that shows up immediately in a timed paper.

The practical point for an online arrangement is that these tools work better on a shared screen than they do in a dining room. Both people can manipulate the graph, both keep the annotated file, and the spreadsheet the student built in week three is still there in week ten. What the room needs is paper and pencil, because the useful physics thinking still happens by hand before it is shown to the camera.

Keep paper and pencil in the room; the thinking still happens by hand

sections.heading: Availability and cost for physics in this belt
paragraphs: Physics sits in the specialist band of the Dubai market and in the tight half on availability, which is the opposite of what families assume when they see how many tutors advertise science.

On price, published figures: an IB specialist teaching online is AED 200 to 450 or more an hour, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table at AED 200 to 450+. A qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 can serve Standard Level content competently. Budget online tuition at AED 33 to 65 — Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 — buys supervision, which in physics is worth less than in most subjects because what a struggling student needs is their reasoning interrogated.

In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, per Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with Serena at the upper end because the round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes. For physics the premium buys presence and little else: the subject's working surface transfers well to a shared screen, and the simulation and graphing work is better there. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE in any case, since that is an India-only service.

On availability, we would rather state it than let a family discover it: Higher Level physics is among the tightest categories we staff, particularly in the weeks before mocks when every Diploma family in Dubai wants the same thing. Where we cannot cover a request in your window, you get the slots that exist, an honest estimate, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. A general science tutor is not placed into a Higher Level fields request.

process.title: Send the level and two marked papers
process.description: Higher or Standard Level, the school and year group, and photographs of two marked papers. The papers say more in five minutes than a conversation does in thirty, because students cannot see their own command-term and uncertainty errors from the inside.

process.title: Matched to the level, with the maths demand checked
process.description: Tutors are matched to Higher or Standard Level rather than to science generally, and we ask which mathematics course the student takes. A Higher Level physics student on Applications and Interpretation usually needs explicit mathematical technique work, and saying so early prevents a term of misdiagnosis.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: A real lesson with the person who would continue, no card required. It separates the three causes — content, mathematics, command-term misreading — and ends with a session count. If the pace or style does not suit your child, say so and we match again.

process.title: Uncertainties and data analysis scheduled, not assumed
process.description: The plan gives explicit time to uncertainty propagation and graph work, because they are examined and almost never taught deliberately. At Higher Level, field reasoning is front-loaded where the school's scheme of work allows, to avoid the DP2 collision with the investigation deadline.

process.title: Marked strictly, reviewed each term
process.description: Work is marked the way an examiner marks it: command term, units, significant figures, derivation shown. Each term the plan is reviewed against marked evidence, and when a component stops needing weekly support we say so rather than letting the slot run.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the level, with the extensions named
whyPoints.description: Higher Level adds content inside all five themes rather than a sixth theme, weighted towards fields and Theme A. A tutor who can say where the extra material sits teaches it in the right order; one who treats Higher Level as harder questions does not.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainties taught properly
whyPoints.description: Propagation rules, error bars drawn by hand and gradient uncertainty from maximum and minimum lines. It is examined in the data-analysis component and throughout the investigation, and it is the most under-taught skill in the course, which makes it the best three sessions a physics family can buy.

whyPoints.title: Command terms fixed with a marked paper
whyPoints.description: Describe, explain, deduce, derive, discuss and justify each demand something specific, and misreading them is the largest category of lost marks we see. One session with the student's own marked paper usually ends a habit that has been costing marks for a year.

whyPoints.title: The mathematics separated from the physics
whyPoints.description: Students who can explain the physics and cannot execute the algebra need different help from those who cannot explain it. We test the rearrangement speed directly rather than treating careless arithmetic as inattention, particularly for students taking Applications and Interpretation.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the laboratory and about coverage
whyPoints.description: Apparatus work and the practical hours stay with the school, and we say so. Higher Level physics is among the tightest things we staff, so we offer real slots or tell families to look elsewhere. No UAE office, no regulator approval, and no IB date published, because ibo.org blocks verification.

faqs.question: What should I ask a physics tutor before hiring them for a Serena student?
faqs.answer: Four things. What does Higher Level add and where — the answer is content inside all five themes, weighted towards fields, not a sixth theme. How do you handle uncertainties, including the uncertainty in a gradient. What separates 'describe', 'explain' and 'derive' in a mark scheme. And what will you do with my child's experimental data for the investigation, where the only correct answer is nothing: look at it, question it, comment on the processing. A physics teacher answers all four immediately; a capable generalist does not.

faqs.question: What exactly does Higher Level physics add over Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Additional content inside all five themes rather than a separate sixth theme, plus longer papers. The extensions are unevenly distributed: heaviest in Theme A, which pushes into rotational and relativistic work, and in Theme D fields, which gains substantial depth in field reasoning and induction. Theme E adds quantum material. Themes B and C extend less. The practical consequence is that a Higher Level student treating all five themes as equal workloads under-prepares the two carrying the most new material.

faqs.question: Why do so many IB physics students lose marks on uncertainties?
faqs.answer: Because it is examined and almost never taught deliberately. It is slow to teach, looks like arithmetic rather than physics, and rarely sits in a textbook chapter a class works through. The content is finite: absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation rules, uncertainty quoted to one significant figure with the value's precision matched, error bars drawn by hand, and gradient uncertainty from maximum and minimum lines. Three sessions on it typically shows up in a mock more clearly than three sessions on any single theme.

faqs.question: Which physics command term costs students the most marks?
faqs.answer: 'Explain', because students answer it with a description. 'Describe' wants what happens; 'explain' wants the mechanism or reason, and a description earns nothing. 'Derive' is the other expensive one: it wants the algebra from a stated relationship to the required result, and quoting the result scores nothing at all. The diagnostic exercise costs nothing: take the last marked paper and label each lost mark as content, arithmetic or command term. In most mid-grade papers the command-term column is larger than families expect.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics manageable with Maths Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Yes, with explicit support for the mathematical strand from the first term rather than discovery in a mock. Physics assumes fluent rearrangement, confident standard form, comfort with gradients and, in places, logarithms and small-angle approximations — a profile Analysis and Approaches builds directly. Students in the Applications combination often look careless in physics when they are carrying arithmetic overload. The quick test is to give them a rearrangement exercise with no physics in it and watch the speed.

faqs.question: Which physics theme should be front-loaded?
faqs.answer: Fields, Theme D. It is the hardest theme for most students, it carries the heaviest Higher Level extension, and in many schemes of work it is taught late — which means it collides with the Scientific Investigation deadline in DP2. Front-loading field reasoning in DP1, even informally through simulation work and sign-convention practice, removes the worst of that collision. Circuits in Theme B deserve early attention too, because they are the largest reliable loss in UAE cohorts and respond to question-led teaching.

faqs.question: How does the practical side work if physics tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: The apparatus work and the required practical hours stay with the school, including the individual Scientific Investigation and the collaborative project element — confirm the exact arrangements with your child's teacher, since schools schedule them differently. Online teaching covers research design, processing with correct uncertainties, graphing, conclusions and evaluation, which is where most of the assessed marks sit. Nobody should claim a screen replaces handling equipment, and a provider who does is telling you something about their other claims too.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with my child's investigation data?
faqs.answer: Look at it, question how it was processed, and comment on whether the conclusion follows from it. Nothing more. A tutor may explain each of the four criteria and their six-mark allocations, test whether the research question has a measurable and controllable relationship, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the investigation, produce or process the data, write or rewrite text, or supply a previous student's report. Those risk the Diploma rather than one grade.

faqs.question: Do simulations actually help with physics, or are they a gimmick?
faqs.answer: They help when the student predicts before releasing. Changing one parameter in a field or circuit simulation and committing to a prediction first is the fastest route into the reasoning the harder questions demand. Watching a simulation run while someone narrates it is close to worthless, as is watching a video of a worked derivation: both produce recognition rather than capability, and the difference shows up immediately in a timed paper. The learning is in the prediction and in doing the plotting yourself.

faqs.question: Is physics harder to teach over video than in person?
faqs.answer: Marginally easier, in practice. The subject's working surface is a page of algebra and a graph, both of which transfer to a shared screen that both people can annotate and that saves the file. Live graphing lets a student linearise their own data and see the consequence, and simulations are better on a shared screen than on a phone at a dining table. What the room needs is paper and pencil, because the useful thinking still happens by hand before it is shown to the camera.

faqs.question: Will an IB physics tutor come to our house in Serena?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video, there is no IB Gram office or centre in the country, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. Independent in-home physics tutors do work in this belt at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Serena at the upper end because the round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes. The premium buys presence rather than better teaching of fields or uncertainty propagation.

faqs.question: What does IB physics tutoring cost around Serena?
faqs.answer: Physics sits in the specialist band, which published Dubai figures put at AED 200 to 450 or more an hour: TutorChase at AED 270, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 200 to 450+. A qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 is adequate for Standard Level content. Budget supervision at AED 33 to 65 buys less in physics than elsewhere, because what a struggling student needs is their reasoning interrogated. Our rate is quoted after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: When should a Serena family book Higher Level physics sessions?
faqs.answer: Three to four weeks, and earlier in the run-up to mocks. Higher Level physics is among the tightest categories any provider staffs, partly because the pool of people who have taught it through a cycle is small and partly because demand concentrates in the same few weeks across the whole city. Where we cannot cover a request in the window you want, you will get the slots that genuinely exist, an honest estimate of when the preferred window may open, or a recommendation to look elsewhere.

faqs.question: Can you confirm the May exam dates for physics?
faqs.answer: No, and we would be cautious about any page that does. ibo.org returns errors to automated fetching, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and an unverified date is worse than none when a family books travel around it. UAE schools sit the May session. For the window, the investigation upload deadline and your school's own internal dates, ask the IB coordinator — and note that the school's internal deadlines fall weeks earlier and are the ones that actually constrain the plan.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-serena.closingHeading: Ask the four questions, send the papers
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-serena.closingBody: Physics is the subject where the questions you ask a prospective tutor matter most. What does Higher Level add and where. How are uncertainties handled. What separates describe, explain and derive. And what will you do with my child's data — where the right answer is nothing. Send us the level, the mathematics course your child takes alongside, and two marked papers, and you will get straight answers plus a free first lesson with the tutor who would continue. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online; the laboratory stays at school.

You meet one in a free trial before any money moves.

intro.heading: What you are actually buying when you pay for Physics help
paragraphs: Start with the number, because that is what you came for. Private tuition in Dubai is quoted anywhere from AED 45 an hour to AED 650 an hour, and IB Diploma Physics sits in the upper half of that range for a reason that has nothing to do with marketing. Physics is one of the few DP subjects where a tutor has to hold three separate competences at once: the mathematics of the topic, the physical reasoning the examiner is testing, and the command-term discipline that decides whether a correct idea scores. A tutor who has only the first of those is cheap and often useless. A tutor who has all three is not cheap, and the honest version of this page is that you should expect to pay for the third one.

Sobha Hartland is a small, dense, recently built community on the Dubai Creek side of Ras Al Khor, with two substantial international schools inside the masterplan itself and a short drive to several more along Al Khail Road and into Meydan. That geography changes the economics of tutoring more than most parents realise. A neighbourhood with two schools has a shallow local pool of Physics specialists. The subject is already thin on the ground: a school with one DP Physics teacher has no spare capacity for paid support, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi staff plus the conduct code attached to the MoHRE private tuition permit both point the same way on tutoring your own school's students. So the local market for Sobha Hartland Physics is small, which pushes travel-inclusive rates up, and the tutors who do travel are chosen for proximity rather than for knowing Topic D inside out.

That is the whole argument for delivering this subject online, and it is an argument about money rather than convenience. When a family in Sobha Hartland hires on a map radius, they are paying a premium between roughly AED 180 and AED 500 an hour, per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and the published in-home ranges, for a tutor selected from however many qualified Physics teachers happen to live within a twenty-minute drive. When the same family hires online, the travel component disappears from the invoice and the selection pool becomes every Physics specialist available in a Gulf Standard Time evening slot. You pay for teaching rather than for a car.

There is a second cost that never appears on an invoice and is usually larger. A Diploma Physics student who spends a term being re-taught content they already understand loses that term. The Internal Assessment is 20% of the grade at both levels and has a hard internal deadline set by the school, not by the IB. A tutor who starts the IA conversation in the final weeks is charging full rate for damage limitation. Sequencing is where the real money is made or lost, and it is the one thing an hourly rate tells you nothing about.

So the structure of this page is a price list first, then the syllabus the price is supposed to cover, then the three expenditures we think Sobha Hartland families should stop making. Every AED figure is the market's, attributed to whoever published it, with the date. IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages; a free trial lesson and a consultation are how you find out what a specific tutor and a specific schedule cost.
