dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.programmesIntro: Sobha Hartland students reach Diploma Physics by two different routes, and a third group is still two or three years away from it. The programme notes below describe what each stage actually demands of a Physics student in this part of Dubai, rather than restating the IB's own brochure copy.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Two years, taken at Standard Level over roughly 150 teaching hours or Higher Level over roughly 240. The assessed structure is Paper 1 (multiple choice plus data analysis), Paper 2 (extended response) and Paper 3, plus the scientific investigation worth 20%. The HL course adds depth across every theme rather than bolting on separate options, which is why a student who copes at SL can still be surprised by HL Paper 2. Command terms carry the marks: explain, deduce, determine and outline each want a different shape of answer.
programmes.countryNote: Both schools inside the Sobha Hartland masterplan run Diploma Physics, and families here also travel to DP Physics at schools in Al Jaddaf, Nad Al Sheba and Al Garhoud. In Dubai, KHDA inspects these schools annually and publishes a report; the subject-level detail in it is thinner than most parents expect, so a school's overall band is a weak proxy for its Physics department.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Five years of integrated sciences assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. MYP marks are criterion levels out of 8, not percentages, which is the single most common source of confusion in this age group. For a future Physics student the criterion that matters most is processing and evaluating, because it is the direct ancestor of the DP scientific investigation and the place where weak uncertainty handling first shows up.
programmes.countryNote: Sobha Hartland's MYP cohort sits alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirement, which applies in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed curriculum. That is real timetable pressure on a Year 10 student, and it is why science support for this age group in this neighbourhood usually has to fit a single weekday evening rather than spreading across the week.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the DP entry route
programmes.description: Cambridge Physics 0625 or Pearson Edexcel 4PH1, sat at 16, is how most Sobha Hartland students arrive at Diploma Physics. The Extended tier of 0625 covers the algebraic treatment that DP assumes; the Core tier does not. A student entering DP Physics HL from Core has a genuine gap in kinematics algebra and electrical circuit analysis, and it is better closed in the summer before DP1 than discovered in October.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June and November series. The February-March series is an India-only offering and does not apply to a student in Dubai. For MoE equivalency on the British track, a student needs five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count of five.

programmes.name: Pre-Diploma bridging in Physics
programmes.description: A short, defined block of work rather than an open-ended commitment: vector resolution, rearranging multi-variable equations, graph gradients with units, and the difference between a random and a systematic error. Six to ten sessions covers it for most students. This is the cheapest useful money in the whole Physics pathway because it prevents the slow, expensive version of the same remediation spread across DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Sobha Hartland families are often mid-relocation in that summer window, which is exactly when an online block works and a home visit does not. Sessions continue from a rented apartment in Business Bay, a hotel in Downtown, or a grandparent's house abroad, because nothing in the arrangement depends on a car reaching a specific villa.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.subjectsIntro: Physics is the page, but almost no Sobha Hartland family buys one subject in isolation. The Diploma is six subjects and three core components sat together, and the realistic question is which combination to support. These are the subjects most often paired with Physics by students in this part of Dubai.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject of this page. Marks are lost in three predictable places: unit and significant-figure discipline in Paper 1 data questions, command-term mismatch in Paper 2 extended response, and uncertainty propagation in the investigation. All three are teachable in a fixed number of sessions rather than being a matter of aptitude.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The default pairing with Physics HL, and for good reason. Calculus fluency in AA HL feeds directly into the modelling and rate-of-change reasoning that Physics HL assumes. A student taking Physics HL with Maths AI SL is not doomed, but needs the algebraic manipulation covered explicitly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The second science for most Sobha Hartland students aiming at engineering or medicine. Energetics and the mole concept carry arithmetic habits that transfer to Physics; organic mechanisms do not. The two IAs land in overlapping windows, which is a scheduling problem worth planning around in DP1.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by students whose university route does not demand AA. The statistical content is genuinely useful for the Physics investigation, particularly in choosing a sensible treatment of repeated measurements, but the algebra ceiling is lower and needs supplementing for Physics HL.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Common as the third science or as a Physics alternative for medicine applicants. The shared skill with Physics is the scientific investigation: the same criteria, the same uncertainty expectations, and the same habit of writing a conclusion that ignores the error bars just computed.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A rising pairing with Physics in Dubai, driven by engineering and data-science ambitions. The internal assessment is a solution to a client's problem, a very different animal from a Physics investigation, and students taking both frequently misjudge the time the CS product consumes.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Offered by fewer Dubai schools but a natural fit for Physics students. The design cycle shares its testing-and-iteration logic with experimental physics; the trap is a project whose engineering is sound but whose data collection would not satisfy a Physics examiner.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Not a science, but it is where Physics students most often lose aggregate points. The Paper 1 guided analysis rewards a structural argument rather than content recall, which is an unfamiliar mode for a student whose other subjects reward precision of fact.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The TOK essay and exhibition are assessed and contribute to the bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. Physics students often have good raw material here and present it badly, treating a knowledge question as a science question with a right answer.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent investigation supervised by a school teacher. The failure mode is a research question too broad to answer with available equipment. Narrowing it early is worth more than any amount of later writing support, and the supervision relationship belongs to the school, not to a tutor.

sections.heading: What an IB Physics tutor in Sobha Hartland costs, by tier
paragraphs: Market rates for Physics tuition reaching Sobha Hartland fall into five recognisable bands, and the gap between the cheapest and the most expensive is a factor of roughly fourteen. At the bottom, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52; those rates buy a university student or a generalist, which can be the right answer for Year 8 science and is rarely the right answer for Diploma Physics HL. In the middle, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which is the band where a genuine subject specialist starts to be plausible. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named or examiner-led hour.

In-home delivery occupies its own band because the travel is priced in. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. For a Sobha Hartland family the arithmetic is unusually visible: the masterplan is compact and well connected, so a tutor coming from Downtown or Business Bay is a short drive, but one coming from Dubai Marina or Al Barsha is paying for Al Khail Road twice in an evening and that is in the quote whether or not it is itemised.

Monthly packages are where the comparison gets honest, because they expose how many hours a family is actually buying. Published examples include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Read those figures against each other and the in-home premium is roughly double for half the contact hours.

None of these are IB Gram's prices. They are what the market publishes, cited so you can check them, and they exist on this page because three of the six best-ranking competitor pages for this query publish no price at all. sections.heading: The Physics assessment you are paying someone to know
paragraphs: A rate is only meaningful against a syllabus, so here is what a Diploma Physics tutor has to cover. The assessment is three papers plus the scientific investigation. The investigation is 20% of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level, which surprises parents who assume coursework matters less at HL. The papers carry the remaining 80%, split so that Paper 1 combines multiple-choice questions with a data-analysis section, Paper 2 is extended response, and Paper 3 tests experimental technique and the analysis of unfamiliar material.

The themes run across both levels with HL going deeper rather than wider: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. The HL additions are not a separable module a student can leave until last. They are extensions inside each theme, which is why a student comfortable with SL mechanics can still be caught by HL questions on the same topic that ask for a more complete treatment.

Where a tutor earns the upper band is in command terms. State, outline, describe, explain, deduce, determine, show that and comment each specify a different answer shape and a different mark allocation. A student who writes a correct physical explanation in response to determine has lost marks for a reason they will never diagnose alone, because the physics was right. This is the single most teachable thing in the subject and the thing a generalist tutor at the budget rate almost never addresses.

The second place the money shows is data. Significant figures, units, uncertainty propagation and the honest reading of a gradient are examinable in every paper and are the backbone of the investigation. They are also where a cheap hour and an expensive hour differ most visibly, because teaching them requires the tutor to have marked work against the criteria rather than merely to know the answer.

sections.heading: Online or a car: the comparison Sobha Hartland families should actually run
paragraphs: Parents in this neighbourhood search for a home tutor because that is the familiar phrase, and the question behind it is reasonable: will somebody competent sit with my child regularly. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tutors do not travel to addresses in Sobha Hartland or anywhere else in the Emirates; home visiting is a service we run in India only. Everything here is one-to-one over live video, in a Gulf Standard Time slot.

We say that early rather than late because the comparison is one we are willing to have on cost. An in-home Physics hour in Dubai carries a travel premium of roughly AED 30 to AED 150 against the equivalent online hour, depending on which published range you take. For that premium the family gets physical presence and loses tutor selection, because the pool shrinks to qualified DP Physics teachers willing to drive to Ras Al Khor on a weekday evening. For a subject with as few specialists as Physics, that is a steep trade.

There is a scheduling cost too. A tutor with a 6pm booking in Al Barsha and a 8pm booking in Sobha Hartland has to protect the gap, so the slot a family is offered is the slot the route allows. Online, the slot is the slot the student wants, and a cancelled lesson can be moved to the next evening rather than to the next week. Over a two-year Diploma that difference compounds into a meaningful number of recovered sessions.

The case against online is worth stating fairly. A younger child who needs a physical presence to stay on task is better served in a room. A practical skill that requires handling apparatus cannot be fully taught through a screen, though the analysis of that practical work can. For a sixteen to nineteen year old working on Physics papers and a data-heavy investigation, the screen is not the constraint most parents fear it is.

sections.heading: Where Sobha Hartland families waste money on Physics
paragraphs: Three expenditures come up repeatedly in first conversations with families here, and all three are avoidable. The first is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. A parent sees a 4 in Physics on a report, books ten sessions, and the tutor spends the first four working out what is wrong. That is four hours at AED 200 to AED 450 spent on information a single diagnostic session would have produced. The sequence should be diagnose, then decide how much to buy, and sometimes the honest answer is less than the parent expected.

The second is paying a premium rate for content delivery. The most expensive tutors are worth their rate for component technique, command-term discipline and investigation criteria. They are not worth it for re-teaching Topic A kinematics that the school already covered and the student partly understood. Content gaps can be closed with mid-band support or, often, with the school's own resources and a structured week. Reserve the top band for the diagnosed gap and the spend drops without the support getting worse.

The third is the group class bought as a substitute for one-to-one. A class of four students at a reduced per-student rate is good value when all four have the same gap, which is almost never true in Diploma Physics. One student cannot resolve vectors, one cannot structure a Paper 2 answer, one has an unanswerable research question, and the hour goes to whoever speaks first. The per-hour saving is real and the per-outcome cost is higher.

A fourth, smaller one: buying tuition in the final fortnight. At that point no new content can be learned securely and the useful work is paper technique and triage. It is worth doing, it is worth doing with a specialist, and it is worth being honest that it is a different product from two years of teaching. Any provider implying otherwise is selling you urgency.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: A fifth of the Physics grade sits in a piece of work that must be the student's own, which makes the academic-honesty boundary a practical matter rather than a legal footnote. A tutor may teach the physics, explain the assessment criteria, challenge whether a research question can be answered with the apparatus the school actually has, teach uncertainty propagation, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write any part of it, may not edit it to completion, may not supply data, and may not suggest a conclusion the student has not reached from their own results.

This matters in this SERP because the boundary is openly crossed. One site found in the research for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is an academic-honesty breach that triggers IB malpractice procedures against the student, not the seller. The student risks the whole Diploma for one component. We say this plainly on every Physics page because a parent comparing providers should be able to see which side of the line each one sits on.

What the honest version looks like in a session: the tutor asks what the independent variable is and how many values of it the student can realistically collect, which usually kills the first research question. Then the dependent variable and how it will be measured, which exposes the uncertainty problem. Then the controlled variables, which exposes whether the experiment means anything. By the time those three questions are answered the student has a plan they can defend, and they wrote it.

The supervision relationship stays with the school. Your child's supervising teacher signs the authenticity declaration and knows the school's internal deadline, which is usually months before any IB date. A tutor who does not ask for that deadline in the first session is not planning the work properly.
bullets: A tutor teaches criteria, technique and physics; the student writes every word

sections.heading: Exam sessions counted backwards from a Sobha Hartland desk
paragraphs: Nobody ranking for this query publishes a calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what a parent needs to decide when to spend. The useful version runs backwards from the papers rather than forwards from today. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. Before the papers sit mock examinations, before those sits the school's internal investigation deadline, and before that sits the data collection that nobody schedules.

IB session and results dates are not restated here with specific dates, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and a date a parent acts on must be checkable. Confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator, who holds the school's own version of the schedule including the internal deadlines that matter more to your planning than the IB's do. For IGCSE students in the same household, Cambridge runs June and November series and Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November; the Pearson November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which gives you a realistic sense of the gap between paper and result.

Counted backwards, the spending decisions fall in a clear order. A bridging block belongs in the summer before DP1. Weekly support belongs in DP1 if the diagnosis says content. Investigation support belongs around the school's internal deadline, wherever the school puts it. Component technique belongs in the two terms before the papers. Anything bought outside that order is bought at the wrong time regardless of the rate.

The one date to find out this week is your school's internal deadline for the scientific investigation. It is set locally, it varies by several weeks between the schools serving Sobha Hartland, and it is the hinge the whole DP Physics timeline turns on.

sections.heading: KHDA, the schools around Sobha Hartland, and what a rating does not tell you
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A Sobha Hartland family deals with KHDA, but the distinction matters if you relocate within the UAE mid-Diploma.

KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak and publishes the report. What the report will not tell you is whether the Physics department is any good. Inspection judgements aggregate across phases and subject groups, so a school rated Outstanding may still have a single DP Physics teacher covering both levels with no spare capacity, and a school rated Good may have an unusually strong science team. Parents treat the band as a proxy for subject quality more often than it deserves.

Scale is worth knowing too. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum schools at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and International Baccalaureate at 7%, per Dubai Media Office figures. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. For Physics specifically, that 7% IB share explains why DP Physics tutors are scarcer than IGCSE ones.

One thing KHDA requires that affects a Physics student's week directly: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises no mandatory lesson run shorter than 25 minutes. That time comes out of the same week as Physics revision, which is why realistic scheduling beats ambitious scheduling.

sections.heading: Permits, legality and what a Sobha Hartland parent can verify
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated, and a parent can check this themselves rather than taking a provider's word. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and u.ae states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone quoting you a permit fee is either mistaken or inventing a cost. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page for it is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. u.ae also states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source and does not appear on this page.

There is a separate and often confused category. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That is a different thing from an individual tutor's MoHRE permit, and marketing copy in this market routinely conflates the two. IB Gram holds neither and does not claim to.

One more boundary worth knowing before you ask a school teacher privately. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE permit also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK directly if it affects your decision.

You take a free trial lesson with no payment. If the match is wrong, you say so and we propose someone else; if it is right, you decide how many sessions to buy, and we will tell you if we think that number is too high.

The part most providers leave out is availability. Diploma Physics HL is a narrow specialism and there are evenings when nobody who genuinely covers it is free in a Gulf Standard Time slot. When that happens we say so and give you a date, rather than filling the hour with a generalist at the same rate. For a family in Sobha Hartland that is occasionally an inconvenient answer and it is the honest one: a general science tutor taking a DP Physics HL session is a worse outcome than waiting a week.

Where tutors are based is a fair question and the answer is public. Our Physics specialists work across the UAE and India, and sessions are scheduled in your time zone. Nobody travels to a UAE address. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the Emirates, and anyone implying otherwise about any provider is worth checking. The conversion path on this page is a UAE-appropriate enquiry form and a free trial, not an overseas phone number.

On data: a lead form here collects a child's name, year group, school and the subject that needs help, because a match cannot be made without them. It is used to propose a tutor and nothing else, and it can be deleted on request. Our privacy notice is linked from every page, consistent with UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Physics tutor in Sobha Hartland cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates for Diploma Physics reaching Sobha Hartland run from about AED 150 to AED 650 an hour. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase AED 270, and BartyED AED 650 for premium examiner-led support; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts specialist tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 or more. In-home delivery sits at AED 180 to AED 500 because travel is priced in. Those are published market figures as read in October 2026, not IB Gram's rates. Ours come out of a consultation after a free trial lesson, because the honest number depends on the level, the component and the weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Is paying AED 650 an hour for Physics ever worth it in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, for a narrow purpose. A top-band hour is worth its price for a diagnosed technique gap at Higher Level: command-term discipline in Paper 2, uncertainty propagation, or an investigation whose research question will not survive contact with the apparatus. It is poor value for re-teaching content the school already covered, which mid-band support at AED 150 to AED 300 handles equally well. The expensive mistake is not the rate; it is buying ten premium hours before anyone has diagnosed what is wrong. One diagnostic session first usually reduces the total spend.

faqs.question: Is Sobha Hartland tuition delivered at our address or over video?
faqs.answer: Over video. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; nobody travels to addresses in Sobha Hartland, Mohammed Bin Rashid City or elsewhere in the Emirates. Home visiting is a service we run in India only. All UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We are direct about it because the trade is worth seeing clearly: you lose a physical presence in the room and you gain the pick of every available Diploma Physics specialist rather than whoever can drive to Ras Al Khor on a weekday evening, and the travel premium leaves the invoice.

faqs.question: What does the Physics Internal Assessment count for, and can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: The scientific investigation is 20% of the final Physics grade at both Standard and Higher Level. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria, interrogate whether the research question is answerable with the apparatus your school has, teach uncertainty and error analysis, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor cannot write it, cannot edit it to completion, and cannot supply data. Your child's school supervisor signs the authenticity declaration. The school's internal deadline governs the timeline and usually falls months before any IB date, so find it out early.

faqs.question: My child is at a Sobha Hartland school and dropped from a 6 to a 4 in Physics. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With a diagnosis, not with hours. A drop of two grades is usually one of three things: a content gap opening in a specific theme, a command-term problem where the physics is right and the answer shape is wrong, or workload collapse where Physics is losing the week to five other subjects. Those need different responses and cost different amounts. A single diagnostic session reviewing the marked papers identifies which one it is, and it sometimes ends with a recommendation to buy fewer sessions than you expected.

faqs.question: Why is Diploma Physics tuition harder to find in Sobha Hartland than IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Numbers. International Baccalaureate students were 7% of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25, against 37% for UK curriculum schools, so the pool of teachers who have actually taught Diploma Physics is a fraction of the pool who have taught IGCSE science. Sobha Hartland compounds it: a compact community with two schools inside the masterplan has a shallow local supply of any specialism. Hiring on a map radius makes the shortage worse, because proximity becomes the selection criterion. Online delivery is how the pool widens back out to every available specialist.

faqs.question: Is a group Physics class cheaper than one-to-one for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, often more expensive per outcome. A group of two to four costs less per student, and it works when every student in the room has the same gap. In Diploma Physics they rarely do: one student cannot resolve vectors, another cannot structure a Paper 2 answer, a third has an unworkable investigation question. The hour goes to whoever speaks first and the others pay for listening. Groups are reasonable for broad content revision. For component technique, one-to-one is the cheaper purchase even at a higher rate.

faqs.question: Does my Physics tutor need a UAE permit, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone quoting a permit fee is mistaken. You can ask a tutor directly whether they hold it. Note that a tutoring operation with premises in Dubai needs a separate KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a different thing entirely and is the distinction most marketing copy blurs.

faqs.question: How many Physics sessions a week should a DP1 student in Sobha Hartland have?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases. A weekly 60 or 90-minute session across DP1 gives enough contact to track the school's scheme of work and enough gap for the student to do the independent practice that actually moves a grade. Two sessions a week usually means the student has no time left to work alone, which is where learning happens in this subject. The exception is a diagnosed content gap with a deadline, where a short burst of two a week for a few weeks closes it faster, then drops back to one.

faqs.question: When do Physics exam sessions fall, and when should we start spending?
faqs.answer: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. We do not restate specific IB dates because ibo.org blocks automated verification, so confirm them with your school's Diploma coordinator, who also holds the internal deadlines that matter more to your planning. Counted backwards, the spending order is: a bridging block the summer before DP1, weekly support through DP1 if the diagnosis says content, investigation support around the school's internal deadline, then component technique in the two terms before the papers. Buying outside that order wastes money regardless of the hourly rate.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Physics HL and SL for tutoring purposes?
faqs.answer: Higher Level runs roughly 240 teaching hours against about 150 at Standard Level, and the extra depth sits inside each theme rather than in a separate module. That is why a student comfortable with SL mechanics can still be caught by an HL question on the same topic demanding a fuller treatment. The investigation is 20% at both levels and the paper structure is the same, so SL support concentrates on secure coverage and answer shape, while HL support spends more time on the extended reasoning that Paper 2 rewards.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics and Maths for a Sobha Hartland student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and for a Physics HL with Maths Analysis and Approaches combination it can be efficient, because the calculus and algebraic manipulation overlap substantially. It is worth checking that the tutor genuinely teaches both at Diploma level rather than teaching one and coping with the other. Where it works less well is Physics HL with Maths Applications and Interpretation, because the two subjects pull in different directions and a single tutor tends to default to whichever they know better. Two specialists are sometimes the cheaper answer.

faqs.question: Does online Physics tuition work when the subject needs practical apparatus?
faqs.answer: The practical work itself happens in your child's school laboratory, where the apparatus and the supervising teacher are. What online tuition handles is everything around it: whether the research question can be answered with the equipment available, how many values of the independent variable are realistic, how to treat repeated measurements, how uncertainties propagate through a calculation, and whether the conclusion is consistent with the error bars. Those are the parts the assessment criteria reward and the parts students most often get wrong, and none of them require the tutor to be in the room.

faqs.question: What does KHDA's school rating tell us about a school's Physics department?
faqs.answer: Less than most parents assume. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes a report, but the judgements aggregate across phases and subject groups. A school rated Outstanding may run Diploma Physics with one teacher covering both levels and no spare capacity; a school rated Good may have an unusually strong science team. Read the report for what it says about secondary science specifically, ask the school how many teachers cover DP Physics, and treat the headline band as context rather than as a subject verdict.

faqs.question: What happens if no Diploma Physics specialist is available in our slot?
faqs.answer: You get a date rather than a substitute. Diploma Physics, particularly Higher Level, is a narrow specialism and there are evenings when nobody who genuinely covers it is free in a Gulf Standard Time window. When that happens we say so and tell you when it changes. The alternative, which this market does quietly and often, is to fill the hour with a general science tutor at the specialist rate. For a DP Physics HL student that is worse than waiting a week, so we do not do it.

faqs.question: Are there cheaper options before we pay for a Physics tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Two, and both are underused. The first is your school's own support sessions, which are usually free to enrolled students and run by the department that sets the assessments. Ask what is available for senior science before paying anyone. The second is structured independent practice using the school's own past-paper access, with a clear weekly plan. If a diagnostic session concludes that the problem is workload rather than content, those two cost nothing and work better than paid hours. We will tell you if that is what we see.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.closingHeading: Price it properly, then buy only what the diagnosis justifies
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.closingBody: The market will quote a Sobha Hartland family anything from AED 150 to AED 650 an hour for Diploma Physics, and the rate is a poor guide to what you get. What matters is whether the tutor can name the component losing the marks, whether the investigation is being handled in the term it was set, and whether anybody has told you the sessions you do not need. Start with a free trial lesson and a diagnosis. Decide the session count afterwards, with the market bands on this page in front of you and the source of every figure checkable. Lessons are one-to-one, live online, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: What Barsha Heights families actually spend on physics, and on what
paragraphs: Diploma physics is one of the most tutored subjects in Dubai and one of the most expensively mistutored. The rates are public enough to check: published Dubai figures read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialists across the International Baccalaureate, IGCSE and A Level at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and BartyED publishing AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors.

Multiply any of those by a weekly session across two Diploma years and the number stops being a rate and becomes a commitment. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session put mid-market support at AED 600 to 1,200 a month and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. That is a decision worth making deliberately rather than drifting into, and the purpose of this page is to let a Barsha Heights family make it with the actual structure of the subject in front of them.

Where does the money go wrong? Almost always in one of five ways, and none of them involves a dishonest tutor. Content teaching bought when the problem was exam technique. Five subjects tutored eight weeks before an assessment when two were affordable. A flat retainer running through a quiet term with nothing due. A premium rate paid for routine weekly consolidation that a mid-market hour would have covered. And the Scientific Investigation, worth a fifth of the grade and produced under near-perfect conditions, left unsupported while hours go into papers.

The last of those is the most expensive and the least obvious. A fifth of the final grade, produced over months, with feedback available from a teacher and no time pressure, marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each. Every mark lost there was available in ideal conditions and was given away. Families routinely spend heavily on Paper 2 technique and nothing on the investigation, which is the wrong way round if you are buying marks rather than reassurance.

On what we provide and what we do not: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the question, the working, the graph and the student's own draft shared on screen. For Barsha Heights, which has no large school campus of its own and whose students are bussed outward daily, removing a fourth journey from the week is worth something in itself. What the format mainly buys, though, is a physics specialist rather than the nearest available science teacher.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-tecom.programmesIntro: Physics sits inside a sequence and the spending decision differs sharply by where a student is in it. Here is each stage and what it is worth paying for.

programmes.name: Diploma Physics, Year One
programmes.description: The cheapest hours on the whole course, because mistakes are free and there is runway. Mechanics, waves and the start of fields, plus the mathematical fluency the subject assumes: rearranging, significant figures, unit handling and reading a gradient. A weekly mid-market hour in DP1 does more than a specialist hour in the final term, and costs roughly half as much.
programmes.countryNote: Barsha Heights students arrive into DP1 from campuses across Al Barsha, Al Barsha South and Al Sufouh on two different pre-16 routes, and the gaps differ. An IGCSE route usually leaves conceptual electricity thin; a Middle Years route usually leaves timed answering thin. Both are cheaper to fix in DP1 than later.

programmes.name: Diploma Physics, Year Two
programmes.description: Remaining content, the Scientific Investigation deadline, and then execution. Spending in this year should be concentrated rather than continuous: a block around the investigation, then a block on papers once teaching is complete. A retainer running evenly through DP2 pays for hours in months where nothing is due and runs out of money in the months where it matters.
programmes.countryNote: Internal school deadlines for the investigation arrive well before anything the International Baccalaureate sets and are the ones that bind a term. Your Diploma coordinator publishes them, and a tutoring plan built on them beats one built on a general assumption about when the year gets busy.

programmes.name: The Scientific Investigation
programmes.description: Marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Worth a fifth of the final grade, produced over months with teacher feedback available. The symmetry of the criteria is the thing families underestimate, because it means evaluation is worth exactly as much as data analysis and cannot be a closing paragraph.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest marks available anywhere in Diploma physics and the most commonly unsupported. Four to six sessions spread across the investigation, spent on the research question and then on the evaluation, is the highest return per dirham on the whole course.

programmes.name: What Physics Is Being Bought For
programmes.description: Higher Level physics is a common requirement for engineering, physics and some computing programmes, and the grade rather than the experience is what the application uses. That is worth stating because it disciplines the spending: money spent on genuine grade movement is an investment, and money spent on reassurance is not, and the two feel identical at the point of purchase.
programmes.countryNote: Admissions requirements are set by each institution. Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah and Zayed University each publish their own, as do overseas universities, and the published programme page is the authority rather than any claim made by a tutoring provider.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-tecom.subjectsIntro: Diploma physics divides into content areas that cost very different amounts to repair. These are the ones Barsha Heights students most often need, with where the marks and the money go.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, energy and circular motion, with relativity added at Higher Level. Usually the most secure area because students met much of it before 16. Paying specialist rates to revise it is the clearest example of wasted spend, and a mid-market hour or self-study with past papers covers it.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws and the kinetic model, with thermodynamics extended at Higher Level. Marks are lost on explanations that describe a process rather than accounting for it in terms of particle behaviour, which is a command-term problem rather than a content gap and therefore cheap to fix.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Wave characteristics, superposition, standing waves, the Doppler effect and diffraction. The mathematics is more demanding than students expect and the diagrams carry marks of their own. A genuine content area where a specialist hour earns its rate, particularly at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, circuits, electromagnetic induction and, at Higher Level, considerably more field theory. The single most expensive area of the course to repair and the one where an under-powered pre-16 electricity foundation shows. Worth paying properly for and worth starting in DP1.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear energy, the photoelectric effect and, at Higher Level, quantum and nuclear structure extensions. Taught late in most schools, which means it is routinely under-practised when papers arrive. Short, concentrated work here is good value precisely because the whole cohort is thin on it.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error analysis
subjects.levels: SL and HL, heavily in the investigation
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, and error bars with a line of worst fit. Examined in Paper 1B and central to data analysis in the investigation. Compact enough to teach in two or three sessions and worth a disproportionate number of marks, which makes it exceptional value.

subjects.name: Graph interpretation
subjects.description: What a gradient and an area under a line physically represent, linearising a relationship to test it, and reading a value with its uncertainty. Students produce a number where the question asked for a physical meaning. One of the cheapest and most transferable skills on the course to buy.

subjects.name: Mathematical fluency for physics
subjects.description: Rearranging before substituting, significant figures, standard form, unit consistency and trigonometry in resolving vectors. Not physics content but the cause of a large share of physics marks lost. Weeks rather than sessions to build properly, which is why it belongs in DP1 and is poor value to attempt late.

subjects.name: Paper 1A multiple choice
subjects.description: Short multiple-choice questions where the distractors are built from the specific misconceptions the syllabus expects. Highly coachable from past papers at low cost, because the same misconceptions recur, and a student who learns to spot the trap pattern gains quickly without new content.

subjects.name: Paper 1B data-based questions
subjects.description: Experimental and data-analysis questions sitting inside Paper 1, drawing on uncertainty, graphing and method evaluation. It overlaps heavily with the Scientific Investigation skills, which means hours spent here are bought twice over, and that overlap is the single best value in the subject.

subjects.name: Paper 2 extended response
subjects.description: Short-answer and extended questions carrying the largest share of the grade at both levels. Marks are lost to command terms and to unexplained working rather than to missing knowledge. Technique work here is cheap relative to its effect and should usually precede any further content teaching.

subjects.name: Higher Level extension content
subjects.description: Additional material within each theme rather than a separate unit, with extra depth in fields, thermodynamics and quantum physics. The extension content is where Higher Level grades are decided, so a Higher Level student paying for help with Standard Level material is paying for the wrong half of their course.

sections.heading: What an IB physics tutor in TECOM costs, band by band
paragraphs: Here is the market, with every figure credited to the provider that published it and read in October 2026. None of it is IB Gram's price list. Reading the table from the bottom up is more useful than from the top down, because the question is not what the best tutor costs but what the least expensive option that solves your actual problem costs.

The budget band, roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, is published by EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For Diploma physics this band is genuinely limited. It can supervise, keep a student company and check that work has been attempted, and for a DP1 student whose problem is discipline rather than understanding that may be enough. It cannot diagnose a Higher Level fields gap or coach a Scientific Investigation to the criteria.

The qualified band, AED 150 to 300, is where most of the useful spending sits, with Unitors publishing International Baccalaureate from AED 200. A weekly hour here through DP1 is the single best-value purchase in the subject. Above it, the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate reaching past 450, is worth paying for the Higher Level extension content and the final execution window, and is poor value for routine weekly consolidation.

At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650. A rate like that can be defensible for narrow, late grade-ceiling work on Higher Level material; it is almost never defensible for a term of general support. And the in-home column, AED 180 to 350 from Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, is buying travel rather than physics. In Barsha Heights, where a tutor arrives with a variable twenty minutes attached, that is a particularly poor exchange for a subject where specification match is the scarce thing.

sections.heading: The five ways physics tutoring money gets wasted
paragraphs: None of these involves a dishonest tutor. They are all mismatches between what was bought and what the student needed, and they recur often enough to be predictable. A family that recognises its own pattern in this list can usually spend less and get more, which is a strange thing for a tutoring page to argue and is also true.

The first and largest is buying content when the problem was technique. A student who understands fields perfectly and loses marks for unexplained working, missing units or answering a describe question when the paper asked for an explanation does not need more physics. They need four sessions on execution, which is cheaper than four on content and produces a bigger movement. The way to tell is a marked script: if lost marks are concentrated in method and command terms rather than in whole unanswered questions, the problem is technique.

The second is breadth under deadline pressure. Eight weeks before an assessment, a family worried about several subjects buys tutoring in all of them and halves the hours available for each. A student tutored in five subjects eight weeks out is being tutored in none of them. Two subjects, chosen by which marks sit nearest a boundary, is the only version of that purchase that moves anything.

The third is the flat retainer through a quiet term. The fourth is paying a specialist or premium rate for routine consolidation that a mid-market hour covers, which can double the annual cost for no additional effect. And the fifth, the most expensive, is leaving the Scientific Investigation unsupported while hours go into papers. A fifth of the grade, produced in ideal conditions, marked out of 24 across four equal criteria, and routinely the one thing nobody buys help with.

sections.heading: Where the marks are, so you can see where the money should go
paragraphs: A spending decision needs the weightings in front of it. Diploma physics is assessed through Paper 1, which carries 36% and divides into Paper 1A multiple choice and Paper 1B data-based questions, through Paper 2 at 44%, which carries the short-answer and extended-response load, and through the Scientific Investigation at 20%. That structure applies at both Standard and Higher Level, with Higher Level adding extension content within each theme rather than a separate paper.

Read those proportions against where tutoring hours usually go and the mismatch is obvious. Paper 2 is the largest component and usually gets attention. Paper 1B, the data-based section, overlaps almost completely with the skills the investigation assesses, which means hours spent on uncertainty propagation, error bars and method evaluation are bought twice over. That overlap is the single best value in the subject and it is rarely exploited deliberately.

Paper 1A rewards a different kind of work again. Multiple-choice distractors are built from the specific misconceptions the syllabus anticipates, and the same traps recur across series. A student who learns the pattern gains marks without learning new physics, which makes it cheap. It also requires nothing more than past papers and somebody to explain why each wrong option was attractive, so a mid-market hour covers it perfectly well.

As ever, treat these as the published structure to be confirmed rather than figures to act on blindly. Subject guides are revised and your school's Diploma coordinator holds the version that applies to your child's cohort. No International Baccalaureate examination or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated access and no date in this project has been confirmed from source.

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation: the cheapest marks in the course
paragraphs: Marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A fifth of the final grade. Produced over months rather than in an examination hall, with teacher feedback available and no clock running. There is no other component in Diploma physics where the conditions are this favourable, and there is no other component families so reliably leave unsupported.

The symmetry of the criteria is the fact that changes behaviour once a family knows it. Evaluation is worth exactly as much as data analysis. Most first drafts we see contain several pages of data processing and four sentences of evaluation, which gives away a quarter of the available marks in the last paragraph. Research design is worth the same again, and it is determined before any data exist, by whether the research question is measurable, controllable and answerable with the apparatus available.

That ordering tells you when to buy the sessions. Two before data collection, on the research question and the method, because a question that cannot be controlled caps research design and then undermines everything downstream. Two in the middle, on uncertainty propagation, graphing and the line of worst fit, which also prepares Paper 1B. Two at the end, on evaluation, which is the thinnest part of nearly every draft. Six sessions, timed to the school's own internal deadlines rather than spread evenly.

The boundary on what a tutor may do here is firm and worth stating before anybody books. A tutor may explain the criteria, question whether a research question is measurable, check whether uncertainty has been handled correctly, ask why a conclusion follows from the data, and mark the student's own draft against the published criteria. A tutor may not design the investigation, process the data, write any section, or revise prose until the words are no longer the student's. The student and the school declare the work authentic, and a breach is a malpractice finding against your child.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, and whether it costs more to support
paragraphs: Higher Level physics adds extension content within each theme rather than a separate paper, with additional depth in fields, thermodynamics and quantum physics. The component weightings stay the same. That structure has a direct consequence for spending that families rarely see: a Higher Level student paying for help with Standard Level material is paying for the wrong half of their course, because the grade is decided in the extension content.

The practical sequence is therefore to establish security in the shared material first, cheaply, and only then buy specialist help for the extension depth. A student who is shaky on circuits should not be paying specialist rates for Higher Level field theory, because the field theory will not hold on a weak foundation and the hours will be spent re-teaching circuits at a premium rate. That is one of the most common and most expensive mismatches in the subject.

There is a related decision some families face in DP1, which is whether to continue at Higher Level at all. That should be made on evidence rather than ambition. A timed section of a Higher Level paper, marked, tells you plainly where a student sits. So does the same student's performance on the mathematical fluency the course assumes, because Higher Level physics is less forgiving of hesitant algebra than Standard Level is. A tutor's useful contribution here is the diagnostic, not the opinion.

Where a student does continue, the honest spending shape is a cheap weekly hour in DP1 building fluency and the shared content, then a defined specialist block in DP2 on the extension material, plus the investigation sessions. That costs materially less than a specialist retainer across two years and targets the money at the content that actually separates grades. We will recommend it in those terms, including when it means a smaller booking.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context for a Dubai family
paragraphs: Tutoring is not the only education cost in a Dubai household, and the context changes how a figure feels. One useful anchor: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. For a family already committed to private school fees, a frozen year is the moment a tutoring decision becomes easier rather than harder.

The scale of the market around you is worth knowing too. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37% of enrolment, Indian 26%, US 14% and the International Baccalaureate 7%. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, with enrolment having risen 6% during 2025-26.

Against that backdrop, here is the honest arithmetic of the tutoring options as a Barsha Heights family would actually encounter them, built from the published bands rather than from our own prices. A weekly mid-market hour across a Diploma year, a concentrated investigation block, a technique block before an assessment, and a specialist extension block. Seeing them side by side usually changes which combination a family chooses, because the cheapest combination that solves the real problem is rarely the one that gets bought by default.

One honest caution about the whole table. We do not know your child's diagnosis, so these are costs rather than recommendations, and we decline to quote an hour count before a diagnostic for the same reason. An estimate produced before anybody has seen a marked script or a draft investigation is a sales number dressed as a plan, and you should treat it as one wherever you encounter it, including from us.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, copyright and what we will not sell
paragraphs: This belongs on a page about money because some of what is sold in this market should not be bought at any price. Research for this project found a provider selling completed Internal Assessments outright at a published figure. That is not tutoring. It is an academic-integrity breach that triggers malpractice proceedings against the student rather than the seller, and a family buying it is paying for a risk to their child's qualification.

The legitimate boundary is clear enough to apply yourself. A tutor may teach content, explain assessment criteria, model how a question type is answered, question whether a research question is measurable, mark the student's own work and give feedback on it, and coach planning and revision. A useful test is whether your child's own school teacher could do the same thing openly. If they could, a tutor can too.

A tutor may not design an investigation, process its data, write any section of it, dictate answers for transcription, or edit text until the words are no longer the student's. Nor may anybody legitimately distribute International Baccalaureate subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary documents as downloads, because those are the IB's copyright. We reference them, link to the official source and work from them inside a session, and your child's school can reach the official material directly.

On status: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, and claims none of those relationships. We do not operate an office, centre or branch in the UAE. Any provider using a phrase like approved by a regulator should be asked to produce the permit or centre number, because those instruments are specific and checkable.

sections.heading: Booking, and the number we will not give you
paragraphs: Send the level, the component causing the problem, and a marked script or a draft investigation if you have one. The marked script is the document that determines the whole spending decision, because it shows whether lost marks sat in content, method, technique or timing, and those four cost very different amounts to fix. A description of the problem rarely distinguishes them and the script does it in two minutes.

The number we will not give you before that is an hour count. Any figure quoted before somebody has seen the evidence is invented, however confidently it is delivered, and it is usually invented upward. After the free trial you receive a written note: the component, where the marks went, what the cheapest effective intervention is, and a realistic session estimate for the window you have. If that estimate is four sessions rather than a term, the note will say four.

Scheduling follows Barsha Heights reality. Children here return on multi-stop bus routes between a quarter past five and six, so the workable slots are 17:30 and 18:00, and those are the most demanded tutoring hours in the Dubai year with demand peaking in the second term. Securing one in term one costs nothing extra and is worth real money. Investigation work often moves to weekend mornings, which suits sustained writing better than a weekday evening after a commute.

Two limits before you commit. Higher Level physics specialists for a specific weekend hour are among the thinner combinations we staff, and we will give you a date rather than take a booking and hope. And if no UAE-based tutor is free for your combination, we will say whether a tutor based elsewhere can cover your hour in Gulf Standard Time, and you may decline. IB Gram runs no home visits in Dubai; every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video.

process.description: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation each carry six of the 24 marks, and evaluation is the thinnest part of nearly every draft we read. Sessions are placed two before data collection, two during analysis and two on evaluation rather than spread evenly, because that is where the unclaimed marks sit.

process.title: Review on marks, then stop
process.description: Every fourth session includes a timed section measured against earlier attempts at the same question types. If the marks have moved and the component is secure, we say so and the block ends rather than renewing by default. A tutoring arrangement that never recommends its own conclusion is selling reassurance.

faqs.question: How much does an IB physics tutor cost in TECOM?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing International Baccalaureate from AED 200, and specialists across IB, IGCSE and A Level at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED publishing AED 650 at the premium end. Budget online options run AED 45 to 150. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors. None of those is IB Gram's price; we start with a free trial and a consultation.

faqs.question: Where do families most often waste money on physics tutoring?
faqs.answer: Five places, none of which involves a dishonest tutor. Buying content teaching when a marked script shows the problem was technique. Tutoring five subjects eight weeks before an assessment instead of two. Running a flat retainer through a term with nothing due. Paying a specialist or premium rate for routine consolidation a mid-market hour would cover. And leaving the Scientific Investigation unsupported while every hour goes into papers, which gives away a fifth of the grade under near-perfect conditions. The marked script usually identifies which pattern applies.

faqs.question: Is a premium rate ever worth paying for physics?
faqs.answer: Narrowly, yes. A rate at the top of the published range can be defensible for short, late work on Higher Level extension content where a student is already secure in the shared material and the grade sits on the extra depth in fields, thermodynamics or quantum physics. It is almost never defensible for a term of general support or routine theme revision, where a qualified tutor at AED 150 to 300 does the same job. The distinction is whether the work is genuinely specialist or simply being delivered by a specialist.

faqs.question: What is the Scientific Investigation worth and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent of the final physics grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is produced over months with teacher feedback available and no clock running, which makes it the most controllable mark on the whole course. Every mark lost there was available in ideal conditions and was given away. It is also the component families most reliably leave unsupported, which is why it is the cheapest place in the subject to buy marks.

faqs.question: Which part of the investigation is usually weakest?
faqs.answer: Evaluation, by a wide margin. It carries six of the 24 marks, exactly as much as data analysis, and most first drafts contain several pages of processing and four sentences of evaluation. Research design is the other recurring weakness, and it is decided before any data exist, by whether the research question is measurable, controllable and answerable with the apparatus available. That is why the sensible pattern is two sessions before data collection, two during analysis and two on evaluation rather than six spread evenly.

faqs.question: How are the physics papers weighted?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% and divides into Paper 1A, multiple choice, and Paper 1B, data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2 carries 44% with short-answer and extended-response questions. The Scientific Investigation carries 20%. That structure applies at both Standard and Higher Level, with Higher Level adding extension content within each theme rather than a separate paper. Confirm the figures against the current subject guide through your school's Diploma coordinator, because the International Baccalaureate revises its guides periodically.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 1B unusually good value to prepare?
faqs.answer: Because the skills it tests overlap almost completely with the Scientific Investigation. Uncertainty propagation, error bars, lines of worst fit, reading a value with its uncertainty, and evaluating a method all appear in both. Hours spent on them are therefore bought twice over, counting towards a component inside the 36% paper and towards a component worth 20% of the grade on its own. That overlap is the single best value available in Diploma physics and it is rarely exploited deliberately.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level physics add, and should we pay more for it?
faqs.answer: It adds extension content within each theme rather than a separate paper, with additional depth in fields, thermodynamics and quantum physics, while the component weightings stay the same. Pay for a specialist on the extension content and not on the shared material. The common and expensive mismatch is a student who is shaky on circuits paying specialist rates for Higher Level field theory: the field theory will not hold on a weak foundation, and the premium hours get spent re-teaching the basics.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time to buy physics tutoring?
faqs.answer: The first Diploma year, by a clear margin. Content taught properly then does not need re-teaching later, mathematical fluency has time to become a reflex, and a mid-market hour at AED 150 to 300 covers the work that would otherwise need a specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more in the final term. Families who buy the cheap hour early rarely need the expensive version late. The most expensive moment to start is eight weeks before an assessment, when the options narrow to technique alone.

faqs.question: Can a physics tutor help with the investigation without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Within firm limits. A tutor may explain the criteria, question whether a research question is measurable and controllable, check whether uncertainty has been handled correctly, ask why a conclusion follows from the data, and mark the student's own draft against the published criteria. A tutor may not design the investigation, process the data, write any section, or revise prose until the words are no longer the student's. The student and the school declare the work authentic, and a breach is a malpractice finding against your child rather than the tutor.

faqs.question: Is in-home tutoring worth the premium for physics?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the reason is specific to this subject. The published in-home band of AED 180 to 350 from Bestimate, or AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, is buying travel rather than physics, and in Barsha Heights a tutor driving in at half past five arrives with a variable twenty minutes attached. What is scarce in Diploma physics is a person who has taught Higher Level fields to examination, and the local pool is small. Presence in the room is a real good; it is just not the scarce one here.

faqs.question: Why will you not tell me how many sessions my child needs?
faqs.answer: Because any number given before somebody has seen a marked script or a draft investigation is invented, and usually invented upward. Lost marks in content, method, technique and timing cost very different amounts to repair, and only the evidence distinguishes them. After the free diagnostic you get a written estimate alongside the cheapest effective intervention, and if that estimate is four sessions rather than a term, the note will say four. Treat any provider who quotes before diagnosing as giving you a sales figure.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school fee freeze change the tutoring decision?
faqs.answer: It makes it easier for a family already committed to private fees. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. A frozen fee year is a reasonable moment to fund a concentrated block, such as investigation support, that would otherwise be postponed. It does not change what is worth buying, only when it is affordable.

faqs.question: What time do physics sessions run for Barsha Heights families?
faqs.answer: Usually 17:30 or 18:00, because Barsha Heights contains no large school campus and children return on multi-stop bus routes between a quarter past five and six rather than at a bell. Those evening hours are the most demanded tutoring slots in the Dubai year, with demand peaking in the second term, so arranging one in term one secures it at no extra cost. Investigation work often moves to weekend mornings, which suits sustained writing better. During Ramadan, sessions shift to post-Iftar slots for families who want them there.

faqs.question: Can you give me the IB physics exam dates?
faqs.answer: No, and we will not estimate them. The International Baccalaureate's own website returns an error to automated requests, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from source, and an unverified date that a family plans around is worse than none at all. The May session is the one UAE schools sit. Your Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative dates and, more usefully, the internal deadlines for the Scientific Investigation, which arrive well before anything the IB sets and are what actually shapes the spending plan.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-tecom.closingHeading: Buy the diagnosis before you buy the hours
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-tecom.closingBody: Almost all of the money wasted on physics tutoring in Dubai is wasted at the point of purchase rather than during the teaching, because the wrong thing was bought with the best intentions. A marked script tells you whether the problem is content, method, technique or timing, and those four cost very different amounts to repair. A draft investigation tells you whether a fifth of the grade is being handled or quietly given away. Send us the level, the component and whichever of those documents you have, and the free trial lesson will produce a written note naming the cheapest effective intervention and a realistic session count. If that count is four rather than a term, the note will say four. Lessons are one-to-one online, in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-greens.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Physics at Diploma level and nothing adjacent to it. Each one has taken a cohort through Paper 1B data questions and the scientific investigation, and each works to a Gulf Standard Time timetable built around when a Greens bus route actually drops.

intro.heading: The real constraint in The Greens is the clock, not the subject
paragraphs: Parents in The Greens rarely start by asking whether their child needs help with Physics. They already know. What they ask is when a lesson could possibly happen. The Greens sits inside Al Thanyah Third, a low-rise grid of apartment blocks wrapped around Emirates Golf Club, with one artery in from Sheikh Zayed Road and another from Al Khail. Secondary school buses reach the community in a band that runs from about 15:30 to 16:30, depending on which school and which loop. By the time a fifteen-year-old has eaten, the afternoon is half gone.

That single fact decides more about tutoring outcomes here than any claim a provider can make about teaching quality. A session scheduled at 16:00 because it suited the tutor will be missed, moved or sat through in a daze roughly every third week. A session scheduled at 16:45, after the Dubai British School loop has cleared Al Thanyah, holds. The difference between those two bookings is the difference between twenty-eight lessons in a school year and eighteen.

Physics punishes gaps more than most Diploma subjects, which is why the timing matters this much. The 2023 course is cumulative: the kinematics and energy work in Theme A underpins the circular motion and gravitation in Theme D, and the wave treatment in Theme C reappears inside the quantum material in Theme E. A student who misses three consecutive weeks in February does not simply lose three weeks of content. They lose the scaffolding for the HL extension topics that arrive in the second year, and they discover it in a mock paper.

The other half of the problem is supply. The Greens has a dense population of international families and a thin population of people who have actually taught Diploma Physics. Chemistry and Maths tutors are findable within a short drive. A Physics specialist who can explain why a gradient of a velocity-time graph carries an uncertainty, and who knows that Paper 3 was retired with the 2023 guide, is a much rarer animal in any one neighbourhood. Searching by distance narrows the pool to whoever is nearby; searching by syllabus does not.

So IB Gram does the opposite of a proximity search. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and the tutor is chosen for the course your child is sitting rather than for the postcode they live in. Nobody drives anywhere. The afternoon window that exists after the bus is the window the lesson uses, and the specialist is the right specialist whether they are in Dubai, Mumbai or Manchester.

What follows is specific to this community: the schools The Greens feeds, the finish times those schools run, the realistic session windows that survive them, the assessment structure your child is being measured against, and the places Physics marks quietly leak away.
