dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-greens.programmesIntro: Physics sits at the end of a long run-up. A Greens student arriving in DP1 has usually come through MYP Sciences at Emirates International School Meadows or Dubai International Academy, or through IGCSE Physics at Dubai British School or Dubai College. Each route leaves a different gap.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: The two-year course assessed on the 2023 guide. Five themes — Space, time and motion; The particulate nature of matter; Wave behaviour; Fields; Nuclear and quantum physics — plus a compulsory scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. HL students take the same themes with additional depth and sit longer papers. Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-and-experimental section; Paper 2 is short answer and extended response.
programmes.countryNote: Among the schools a Greens family realistically chooses between, Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills, Emirates International School Meadows and GEMS Wellington International School all run Diploma Physics. Cohort sizes at HL are small, often a single teaching group, which means a student who falls behind in Theme D has nobody sitting next to them in the same position to compare notes with.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The feeder course for most IB Physics students. MYP Sciences is marked against four criteria — knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science — each scored out of eight. It builds experimental design and data handling early, but it carries very little of the algebraic manipulation that Diploma Physics assumes from week one.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy both run the MYP through to Year 11, so a large share of Greens students enter DP1 from criterion-based marking rather than from an examination. The jump that catches them is not the content. It is being asked to rearrange an equation under time pressure without a criterion rubric explaining what good looks like.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route that pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. A CP student may take Physics SL as one of their Diploma courses, which means the same papers and the same scientific investigation but a different surrounding workload and a different set of deadlines competing for the same afternoon.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is offered by only a handful of Dubai schools, so a Greens family on this route is usually travelling further for school than their neighbours. That longer journey compresses the available afternoon further, and it is the main reason CP Physics students here tend to book the Friday short-day slot.

programmes.name: The IGCSE Physics run-up
programmes.description: Not an IB programme, but the course most British-curriculum Greens students arrive from. Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 both build strong recall and formula handling. Neither asks a student to propagate an uncertainty through a calculation, and neither requires the extended written reasoning that Paper 2 rewards at Diploma level.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai British School Emirates Hills, Dubai College and Kings' School Al Barsha all feed Greens households, and all run IGCSE before splitting towards A Level or the Diploma. A student moving from a grade 8 or A* in 0625 into Physics HL often meets their first real difficulty around uncertainties, which no IGCSE paper examined.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-greens.subjectsIntro: A Physics tutor is useful in proportion to how precisely they can name what is going wrong. The units below are the teachable blocks of the 2023 course as a tutor plans them, rather than a chapter list, and each carries its own characteristic failure.

subjects.name: Theme A — Space, time and motion
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extension
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, work, energy and momentum, then circular motion and, at HL, rotational dynamics and special relativity. The theme that everything later depends on. Students who cannot resolve a force on an incline reliably in DP1 will struggle with fields in DP2, because the geometry is the same problem in a different costume.

subjects.name: Theme B — The particulate nature of matter
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extension
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, the kinetic model, and at HL the thermodynamic treatment with entropy. Marks here are usually lost to units and to confusing temperature with internal energy. The arithmetic is gentle, which makes students careless with it.

subjects.name: Theme C — Wave behaviour
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extension
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave characteristics, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect, with diffraction and resolution added at HL. The theme most often taught well and examined badly: students can define a node and still not interpret an unfamiliar interference sketch in Paper 1B.

subjects.name: Theme D — Fields
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extension
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields treated as one idea, plus electric circuits and electromagnetic induction. This is where most Diploma Physics students in Dubai first ask for help. Field lines, potential and potential energy get blurred together, and the sign conventions are unforgiving.

subjects.name: Theme E — Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extension
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear binding energy, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and, at HL, the quantum and nuclear structure extension. Arrives late in DP2 when revision has already begun, so it is routinely the least secure theme in a mock paper.

subjects.name: Paper 1A technique
subjects.description: Multiple choice across all five themes with no partial credit. Scoring here is a trainable skill distinct from physics knowledge: elimination, order-of-magnitude checks and recognising distractors built from a common algebraic slip. Many students lose more in Paper 1A than in any single theme.

subjects.name: Paper 1B data and experimental skills
subjects.description: Unseen apparatus, unseen data, graphs to draw and gradients to interpret with uncertainties attached. Nothing in the MYP or in IGCSE prepares a student for this. It is the single highest-return thing to drill with a tutor, because the skills transfer directly into the scientific investigation.

subjects.name: Paper 2 extended response
subjects.description: Short answers building into multi-part questions that cross themes. Command terms decide the mark: explain, deduce, outline and determine each demand a different shape of answer. Students who write everything they know for every verb run out of time in the final third of the paper.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: One student-designed investigation, around ten hours of class time, a 3,000-word ceiling, marked on four criteria for a total of 24. Twenty per cent of the final grade, decided months before the examinations and almost entirely recoverable with structured feedback on the student's own drafts.

subjects.name: Mathematics for Physics
subjects.description: Logarithms for decay, small-angle approximations, vector resolution, unit algebra and rearranging before substituting. Physics HL students taking Maths AI rather than AA meet this gap most sharply. A Physics tutor who ignores the maths will keep re-teaching the same topic.

sections.heading: What time can an IB Physics session actually start in The Greens?
paragraphs: For most Greens households the honest answer is 16:30 at the earliest, and 16:45 if the school sits in Al Sufouh or Al Barsha. Dubai secondary timetables generally finish between 14:45 and 15:15, buses load for ten to fifteen minutes, and the run back into Al Thanyah Third takes between fifteen and forty minutes depending on the loop and the day. Add a meal and the first workable hour begins in the middle of the afternoon.

The variation inside that band is larger than parents expect. Regent International School sits inside The Greens itself, so its students are home before many buses have left their yards. Emirates International School Meadows runs a short loop and is usually the earliest bus back. Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School are further west along Al Sufouh Road, and their loops arrive last. A single booking time cannot serve all of them, which is why a provider that offers fixed class times rather than fixed slots loses Greens students at the same rate every term.

The table below gives indicative windows for the schools this community feeds. Treat them as a starting point for a conversation rather than as published timetables: finish times differ by year group, co-curricular commitments move the bell, and bus routes are redrawn at the start of each academic year. The only number that matters is the one on your own route, and the reliable way to find it is to watch the drop time for two weeks before fixing a slot.

One more piece of arithmetic is worth doing before booking. A ninety-minute session starting at 16:45 ends at 18:15, which leaves a Diploma student their own evening for homework and sleep. A ninety-minute session starting at 18:00 ends at 19:30, by which point a DP2 student who was up at six has very little left. Later is not safer. The window immediately after the bus, before the day closes down, is the one that produces work.

sections.heading: The IB Physics course your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: Physics was rewritten for first teaching in 2023, and the version many tutors still describe no longer exists. The old options — astrophysics, imaging, relativity as an option block — are gone. Paper 3 is gone. In their place sit five themes taught to both levels, with the Higher Level course adding depth rather than separate option material, and a single internal assessment called the scientific investigation.

The assessment weighting is worth memorising because it changes where effort should go. Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and is split into a multiple-choice section and a data-and-experimental section sat inside the same time allowance. Paper 2 carries 44% and is where the long reasoning lives. The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20% and is finished long before the examination session. A student who treats the investigation as a side task has handed away a fifth of the grade before the first paper is opened.

The practical difference between SL and HL is not a different syllabus. It is 240 taught hours against 150, additional depth inside each theme, and considerably longer papers. Paper 2 runs for an hour and a half at SL and two and a half hours at HL. That extra hour is not generosity; it is more extended-response marks, and stamina in the final forty minutes is a genuine differentiator in HL results.

This matters when you are choosing a tutor. Ask them which theme contains gravitational potential, or whether Paper 1B is sat separately. A tutor working from the pre-2023 course will answer the first question with an option number and the second with a yes. Neither answer is compatible with the course your child is actually taking, and the gap will not show up until a mock paper.

sections.heading: Where Physics marks leak away, theme by theme
paragraphs: Physics marks are rarely lost to not knowing the physics. They are lost to a small set of repeated technical failures, and each one is diagnosable from a single marked script. A tutor who cannot name which of them your child is doing is guessing, and a term of guessing costs more than the lessons did.

In Theme A the recurring loss is vector resolution under pressure. A student who can resolve a force on an incline when asked to resolve a force on an incline will often fail to recognise the same geometry inside a question about a banked curve or a pendulum. The fix is not more kinematics. It is twenty questions in which the geometry is hidden, until the recognition becomes automatic.

Theme D produces the largest single bleed in most Dubai cohorts. Gravitational potential, gravitational potential energy and field strength are three different quantities with three different units, and students who learn them as three similar formulae will mix them in any question that does not label which is wanted. Electric circuits add a second failure: internal resistance is taught once, appears in Paper 2 regularly, and is forgotten by almost everyone who has not been made to derive it.

Across every theme the quietest loss is command terms in Paper 2. State, outline, explain, deduce, determine and discuss ask for different amounts of writing and different kinds of reasoning. A student who writes a paragraph for every state and a sentence for every explain will be marked down twice: once for the missing reasoning and once for the time they no longer have. Marking a student's own script against the command terms, line by line, moves more marks in a fortnight than a month of new content.

Theme B: temperature confused with internal energy, and unit slips

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: a fifth of the grade, settled before the exams
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is the part of IB Physics most open to improvement and most often left until it is too late. It is one investigation of the student's own design, around ten hours of class time, with a 3,000-word ceiling and four marking criteria worth six marks each. Twenty-four marks in total, scaled to a fifth of the final grade, and unlike the examinations it can be revised, reconsidered and rebuilt before submission.

Dubai cohorts lose marks here in a predictable pattern, and most of it is visible in the research question. A question like 'how does temperature affect resistance' cannot be answered within ten hours because it does not specify a material, a range or a method of measurement. Criterion A asks for a design another student could repeat, and a broad question makes that impossible. Narrowing the question is usually the single highest-value hour a tutor spends on an investigation.

Criterion B is where physics students with good laboratory habits still lose marks. Uncertainties get recorded neatly in the raw data table and then vanish. They do not appear as error bars, they are not propagated into the gradient, and the final value arrives without a range attached. A moderator reading that sees a student who has collected data rather than analysed it. Criterion D compounds the problem: an evaluation that says 'human error' names nothing and therefore earns little.

The boundary a tutor works inside here is firm and worth stating plainly. The investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach uncertainty propagation, may explain what each criterion rewards, may read a draft and say which criterion is unmet, and may ask the questions that make a student see their own gap. A tutor may not supply text, may not author a section, and may not hand over a method. IB academic-honesty rules make that distinction an expulsion risk for the student, not a stylistic preference.

sections.heading: Friday short days, Ramadan and the Dubai revision calendar
paragraphs: The UAE working and school week runs Monday to Friday with a short Friday, and that single structural fact is underused by every family who schedules tutoring as though it were a five-full-day week. Friday afternoon is the only genuine daytime block during term. A two-hour Friday session can hold a full timed Paper 2 and its marking, which no weekday hour between the bus and bedtime can.

Ramadan reorganises the day again. School hours shorten, energy drops through the afternoon, and the productive hours move either very early or to after Iftar. Families in The Greens who try to hold a 16:45 slot through Ramadan generally lose half of it. Moving the session to a post-Iftar evening window for those weeks, and agreeing that in advance rather than cancelling week by week, keeps the thread intact. A tutor who cannot shift timezone-wise for a month is the wrong tutor for a UAE family.

Counting backwards from the examination session is the part almost nobody does. Dubai schools sitting the May session run internal deadlines for the investigation and for the extended essay through the autumn and winter of DP2, with mocks in between. By the time the May papers arrive, the internal 20% has been locked for months. The work that moves a Physics grade therefore has to happen a long way before the revision period that parents instinctively plan for.

A note on dates. IB session and results dates are published by the IB itself and by your school's IB coordinator, and they change. This page deliberately publishes none of them. Cambridge and Pearson publish their own International GCSE timetables, which matter if a younger sibling is in Year 11, and those should be read from the board's live timetable page rather than from any tutoring site, including this one.

sections.heading: Practical skills when the lesson is on a screen
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online Physics teaching is practical work, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. Your child's practical scheme of work belongs to their school. The laboratory is at school, the apparatus is at school, and the ten hours of investigation time are timetabled at school. No tutor, online or otherwise, replaces that, and any provider implying they can is describing something that is not theirs to offer.

What a tutor can do is the part schools have least time for: the analysis. Paper 1B does not test whether a student can clamp a boss head. It tests whether they can read unfamiliar apparatus from a diagram, identify what was controlled, decide which quantity to plot against which to get a straight line, draw error bars that mean something, and extract a gradient with an uncertainty attached. Every one of those is a screen activity. Shared datasets, a spreadsheet both people can see, and a graph built live are better teaching tools for this than a bench would be.

Screen sharing also makes a specific kind of feedback possible that is awkward in person. A tutor can open the student's own graph, zoom into the line of best fit, and show exactly where the chosen scale has thrown away two significant figures. They can replay a recorded explanation of uncertainty propagation three times before the next session. Both of those are routine online and clumsy across a kitchen table.

The honest limit is this: a student who has not been attending their school practicals will have a gap that tutoring narrows rather than closes. The first conversation with a tutor should establish how much laboratory time has actually happened, because the plan for a student with a full practical folder and a student with three loose sheets is not the same plan.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on assessed work
paragraphs: This section exists because the search results your child's friends are using include sites selling finished internal assessments. Those sites are not an edgy shortcut. Under IB academic-honesty rules, submitting work that is not your own is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the website. A Diploma can be withheld. It is worth saying out loud to a sixteen-year-old under deadline pressure, because they will meet the offer.

The permitted boundary is wide and genuinely useful. A tutor may teach the underlying physics, explain what each marking criterion rewards, model the analysis on a different dataset, read a student's draft and name the criterion that is unmet, question a conclusion until the student sees the hole in it, and teach the mathematics of uncertainty until it is automatic. All of that improves marks and all of it is legitimate, because the thinking stays with the student.

The forbidden side is narrow and absolute. A tutor does not supply sentences for submission, does not author a method, does not hand over a dataset, and does not edit a draft into something the student could not have produced. The same line applies to the extended essay and to theory of knowledge. If a provider's offer is that something arrives finished, the offer is malpractice regardless of how it is described.

There is a practical test a parent can apply. Ask the tutor what they would do if your child sent a half-written investigation at ten at night with a deadline the next morning. The right answer is a list of questions sent back and an honest statement that the remaining work is the student's to do. Any answer that involves the tutor producing content is the wrong answer, and hearing it early saves a great deal of trouble later.
bullets: Permitted: teaching, criterion explanation, draft feedback, questioning, modelling on other data
Not permitted: supplying text, authoring sections, handing over methods or datasets

sections.heading: KHDA reports, and what they tell you about a physics department
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which inspects them annually and publishes the outcome on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Dubai's private sector held 227 schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for seven per cent of enrolment against thirty-seven per cent on the UK curriculum. That mix is why a Greens apartment block contains students on three different science courses.

An inspection report is more useful to a parent than its headline band. The reports break attainment and progress down by subject and by phase, which means a school rated Very Good overall can carry a science department whose secondary progress is only Good. If you are trying to work out whether your child's difficulty with Theme D is personal or structural, that breakdown answers the question better than a parents' group chat does.

KHDA also sets requirements that shape the timetable your tutoring has to fit inside. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, with instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. For an IB student those lessons occupy periods that are not available for Physics, which is part of why the Diploma feels compressed in Dubai schools specifically.

A word on what a regulator relationship is and is not. KHDA inspects and licenses schools, and it issues educational services permits to training institutes that operate premises in Dubai. IB Gram holds no such permit, claims no regulatory approval, and operates no centre in the UAE. Any tutoring provider describing itself as approved by KHDA, by ADEK, by the Ministry of Education or by the IB should be asked to show the permit number, because the claim is specific and checkable.

process.title: Send the timetable, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that helps is the one that includes the school, the year group, the bus drop time and whether the student is SL or HL. Those four facts decide which tutors can be offered at all, because a slot nobody can attend is not a match however good the teaching is.

process.title: A short diagnostic on Paper 1B
process.description: Before any teaching, the student works through a small set of unseen data questions while the tutor watches. This is the fastest way to see whether the problem is content, mathematics, uncertainty handling or examination technique, and it takes about half an hour rather than three lessons of discovery.

process.title: A trial lesson in the slot you actually want
process.description: The trial runs at the real time on the real day, not at a convenient demonstration hour. If 16:45 on a Tuesday is the slot, that is when the trial happens, because a trial at eleven on a Saturday tells you nothing about whether a tired Diploma student will engage after a bus ride.

process.title: A written plan against the five themes
process.description: After the trial you receive a plan naming which themes will be covered in which order, how the school's own scheme has been accounted for, and where the scientific investigation sits in the calendar. A plan you can read is a plan you can hold a tutor to.

process.title: Fortnightly review, and a swap if the fit is wrong
process.description: Every two weeks there is a short note on what moved and what did not. Personality mismatches happen and are nobody's failure. Asking for a different tutor costs nothing and should happen at week three rather than at week twelve, when a term has already gone.

whyPoints.title: The tutor is chosen for the syllabus, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Searching for a Physics specialist within driving distance of Al Thanyah Third produces a short list. Searching the whole pool for someone who has taken cohorts through the 2023 guide produces a better one. Online delivery is what makes the second search possible at all.

whyPoints.title: Sessions are built around the bus, not the calendar
whyPoints.description: Slots are placed after the actual drop time for your actual route, with Friday short days and Ramadan handled in advance. Attendance is the variable that most affects results, and attendance is a scheduling problem before it is a motivation problem.

faqs.question: What time can an IB Physics lesson start if my child takes a school bus home to The Greens?
faqs.answer: For most routes, 16:30 is the earliest workable start and 16:45 is safer. Dubai secondary timetables finish between roughly 14:45 and 15:15, buses load for ten to fifteen minutes, and the run into Al Thanyah Third takes fifteen to forty minutes. Students at Regent International School, which sits inside The Greens, can start earlier because they need no bus. Students at Dubai College or GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh usually need 17:00. The reliable method is to watch your own drop time for two weeks and then fix a slot ten minutes after the latest arrival you saw.

faqs.question: Has IB Physics Paper 3 really been removed from the course?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Physics guide for first teaching in 2023 restructured the course into five themes taught at both levels and removed the separate option paper entirely. Assessment is now Paper 1, split into a multiple-choice section and a data-and-experimental section, carrying 36% of the grade; Paper 2 carrying 44%; and the scientific investigation carrying 20%. A tutor who talks about option topics or about preparing for Paper 3 is working from the previous course. Ask any prospective Physics tutor this question directly, because the answer tells you within a sentence whether they have taught the current syllabus.

faqs.question: My son is at Dubai International Academy and finds Theme D fields impossible. Is that usual?
faqs.answer: It is the most common sticking point in Diploma Physics, and it is usually a naming problem rather than a conceptual one. Field strength, potential and potential energy are three distinct quantities with three sets of units, and students who learn them as three similar equations cannot tell which a question wants. Electric circuits add internal resistance, which is taught once and then assumed. The fix is narrow and quick: separate the three quantities explicitly, derive rather than memorise, and work through unlabelled questions until recognition is automatic. Most students need three or four focused sessions, not a term.

faqs.question: How many hours of IB Physics tutoring does a Greens student typically need before mocks?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the diagnosis, which is why an honest answer starts with a diagnostic rather than a package. A DP1 student drifting in one theme often needs six to eight sessions. A DP2 student whose mock revealed losses across Themes C, D and E, plus weak Paper 1A technique, is looking at two sessions a week through a six to eight week block. A student whose real problem is the mathematics underneath Physics may need a longer run. Any provider quoting a fixed hour count before seeing a marked script is guessing at your expense.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Physics scientific investigation without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the permitted work is substantial. A tutor can teach uncertainty propagation, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, model an analysis on an unrelated dataset, read a draft and name which criterion is unmet, and question a conclusion until the student sees the gap themselves. What a tutor must never do is supply sentences for submission, author a section, or hand over a method or dataset. The thinking and the words stay with the student. That line is what keeps the diploma safe, and it is worth asking any tutor to state it before you book.

faqs.question: Does my child need laboratory equipment at home for online IB Physics lessons?
faqs.answer: No. The practical scheme of work and the ten hours of investigation time belong to your child's school, where the apparatus is. Tutoring covers the part schools have least time for, which is analysis: reading unfamiliar apparatus from a diagram, deciding what to plot to get a straight line, drawing meaningful error bars, and extracting a gradient with an uncertainty attached. All of that is better done on a shared screen with a live spreadsheet than at a bench. The first session should establish how much laboratory time has actually happened, because that changes the plan.

faqs.question: How are uncertainties and error bars examined in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: They appear in two places and they carry real weight in both. Paper 1B presents unseen data and asks a student to process it, which routinely means propagating an uncertainty into a gradient and stating a final value with a range. Criterion B of the scientific investigation marks the same skill on the student's own data, and this is where most marks are lost: uncertainties get tabulated once and then disappear, with no error bars on the graph and no range on the result. Neither Cambridge nor Pearson IGCSE examines this, so it is genuinely new in DP1.

faqs.question: Is Physics HL worth taking if my child wants to study engineering at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Physics HL is the conventional route and most engineering faculties treat it as the expected preparation, usually alongside Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. What matters more than the general answer is the specific entry page of the specific programme, because requirements vary between institutions and between engineering disciplines, and they are revised. Read the university's own admissions page and, if the student needs certificate equivalency, the Ministry of Education's own guidance. No tutoring provider should tell you what a university requires, and tutoring is not a requirement for any admissions process.

faqs.question: Do The Greens and The Views share the same tutoring slots?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, and that is worth knowing before you book. The two communities sit either side of Emirates Golf Club on the same Al Thanyah Third approach, frequently on the same school bus loops, and they feed the same set of schools. Demand for the 16:30 and 17:30 Physics windows therefore peaks across both at once, and those are the first slots to disappear each September. Families who fix a slot in the first fortnight of term get the window they want; families who wait until after the first assessment generally take what is left.

faqs.question: What happens to our Physics sessions during Ramadan in The Greens?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten, afternoon energy drops, and a 16:45 slot that worked in January stops working. The approach that holds is to agree the Ramadan arrangement before the month begins rather than cancelling week by week: either an early slot before school pressure builds or a post-Iftar evening session. Both are normal for UAE families and both are workable online, since no travel is involved. A tutor who cannot move within the day for a month is the wrong tutor for a household in Dubai, and this is a fair question to ask at the trial.

faqs.question: Should my child take Physics HL alongside Mathematics Applications and Interpretation rather than Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: It is possible and some students do it successfully, but it creates a workload a tutor has to plan around. Physics HL leans on algebraic manipulation, logarithms for decay, small-angle approximations and vector resolution, and Analysis and Approaches builds those explicitly while Applications and Interpretation takes a different route. A student pairing Physics HL with Applications usually needs part of their Physics time spent on the mathematics itself. That is manageable when it is planned for and expensive when it is discovered in DP2. Discuss the combination with the school's IB coordinator before the choice is locked.

faqs.question: What do Physics tutors charge per hour around The Greens and Dubai Marina?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai, taken from providers' own pages and from independent cost surveys, run roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget or university-student online tutoring, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to AED 450 or more for an IB or A Level specialist. Those are market figures attributed to their sources, not an IB Gram price list. Our own rates are discussed in the consultation against the number of sessions actually needed.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Physics tutor to our apartment in The Greens?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tutoring is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, and there are no home visits in Dubai. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation: it means the Physics specialist matched to your child is chosen from the whole pool rather than from whoever can reach Al Thanyah Third before six. For a subject with as few genuine Diploma specialists as Physics, the trade of travel for expertise is the one that moves grades.

faqs.question: My daughter is resitting Physics in a later session. Can a tutor pick that up mid-course?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a resit is one of the clearer tutoring briefs because the evidence already exists. The starting point is the component breakdown from the previous session: a student who lost marks mainly in Paper 1A needs technique work, one who lost them in Paper 2 needs command-term and extended-response work, and one whose internal mark was weak has a different problem again. The internal assessment mark usually carries forward, so confirm with your school's IB coordinator what has to be resubmitted before planning any sessions around it.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection report actually tell me about a school's science teaching?
faqs.answer: More than the headline band does. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes outcomes on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, but the reports break attainment and progress down by subject and by phase. A school rated Very Good overall can hold a secondary science department whose progress is only Good, and that detail is published. If you are trying to judge whether a difficulty with Theme D is your child's or the department's, the subject-level breakdown in the report answers it better than any parent group chat.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-greens.closingHeading: Fix the slot first, then the physics
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-greens.closingBody: The useful next step for a Greens family is small. Note the actual bus drop time for your route, note whether your child is SL or HL, and find the most recent marked Physics script in the bag. With those three things a tutor can tell you within one conversation whether the problem is content, mathematics, uncertainty handling or examination technique, and which of the five themes is costing the most. The trial lesson then runs at the real time on the real day, so you can see whether a tired Diploma student engages after a bus ride. intro.heading: What a Lakes parent is really asking when they search for a Physics tutor
paragraphs: The search phrase is about distance, but the worry underneath it is not. A parent in The Lakes typing 'IB physics tutor near me' is asking something narrower and harder: is there anybody reachable who actually knows this syllabus? Not science in general. Not physics as it was taught twenty years ago in another country. The specific IB Physics course their child is sitting, with its five themes, its two papers, its data-analysis section and its 24-mark scientific investigation. That is a fair question and it deserves a straight answer rather than a map pin.

The straight answer is that proximity and subject depth pull in opposite directions in this part of Dubai. The Lakes sits inside Emirates Living, a villa community with Emirates International School Meadows, Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Regent International School within a few minutes, and the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh schools fifteen minutes further on. There is no shortage of people in that radius who can help a child with secondary science. There is a genuine shortage of people who have taught Physics at Higher Level, marked against the current guide, and can tell you from memory what Theme D contains and what the HL extension to it adds. Searching by distance filters for the first group and ignores the second.

IB Gram resolves that by dropping the distance filter altogether. Every lesson for a UAE family is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. What that buys a Lakes household is a specialist rather than a neighbour: a tutor whose teaching history is in IB Physics specifically, who is not chosen because they happen to live on the right side of Sheikh Zayed Road, and who is not charging an hour of Dubai traffic back to you as part of the rate.

The rest of this page is written to answer the question properly. It sets out what the current Physics guide contains theme by theme, where the marks sit in each component, what the four internal-assessment criteria reward and what a tutor may legitimately do with an investigation that must remain the student's own work. It publishes what the Dubai market charges in AED, with the source of each figure, because three of the six strongest pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all. It covers the maths a Physics HL student is quietly assumed to have, the permit a private tutor in the UAE is required to hold, and what happens on the days when no Higher Level specialist has a free slot.

sections.heading: Who you will actually find teaching Physics within reach of The Lakes
paragraphs: Start with the honest version. Within a twenty-minute drive of The Lakes there are five or six strong schools, a handful of tuition centres and a large informal market of private tutors advertising on community groups. Most of the people in that market are competent. Very few of them are IB Physics specialists, and fewer still have taught Higher Level in the last two years. That is not a slur on anybody. It is arithmetic: Physics is the least-taken of the three main IB sciences at most schools, Higher Level is the smaller half of that, and a neighbourhood of a few thousand villas simply does not contain many people who have done it.

The practical consequence is that a distance-first search gives you the wrong shortlist. You will get science graduates, engineers, retired teachers from other systems and university students, all nearby and all cheaper than a specialist. Some of them will be genuinely useful to a child who has missed a fortnight of Theme A and needs the basics rebuilt. None of them will reliably spot that your child's Paper 2 answers are losing marks because they describe when the command term asks them to explain, or that their investigation has an uncontrolled variable that will cost criterion A marks no matter how neat the write-up is.

The table below is the shortcut. It lists the categories of tutor a Lakes parent realistically encounters, what each one tends to be good at, where the gap usually shows, and one question you can ask in the first five minutes that reveals which category you are talking to. The questions are deliberately specific. A person who knows the current guide answers them without pausing; a person who learned physics elsewhere and is improvising will give you a general answer about problem-solving.

sections.heading: What the current IB Physics guide actually contains, theme by theme
paragraphs: IB Physics is organised into five themes labelled A to E rather than the older core-plus-options structure. Theme A is space, time and motion. Theme B is the particulate nature of matter. Theme C is wave behaviour. Theme D is fields. Theme E is nuclear and quantum physics. Standard Level runs to 110 taught hours and Higher Level to 180, and the extra seventy hours are not a separate module at the end. They sit inside the themes, which is why a student who moves from SL to HL mid-course finds the earlier material has grown rather than been added to.

Knowing the theme letters matters more than it sounds. School schemes of work, revision guides and tutor conversations all use them, and a parent who can say 'she is fine until Theme D' has described the problem precisely enough for a specialist to quote a plan. It also works as a credential test. Anyone who has taught the current course can tell you what sits in Theme D without looking it up; anyone working from the previous structure will reach for topic numbers instead.

The pattern of difficulty is consistent across Dubai cohorts. Theme A feels familiar to anyone with a decent IGCSE, which breeds false confidence. Theme B punishes students who learned gas laws as formulae. Theme C is where graphical reasoning starts to matter. Theme D is where most students genuinely stall, because gravitational, electric and magnetic fields are taught as one idea with three faces and a student who learned them as three separate chapters cannot transfer between them. Theme E then arrives late in DP2, when revision for everything else has already started.

sections.heading: Paper by paper: where the marks are and how they leave the room
paragraphs: The assessment is three components and the weightings are identical at both levels, which surprises most parents. Paper 1 carries 36% and splits in two: Paper 1A is multiple choice and Paper 1B is a set of data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2 carries 44% and mixes short-answer with extended-response items. The scientific investigation carries 20%. Standard Level students sit shorter papers; Higher Level students sit two hours on Paper 1 and two and a half on Paper 2, so stamina becomes a real variable rather than a figure of speech.

Paper 1B is the component most often neglected and the one most responsive to tutoring. It asks students to work with somebody else's experiment: read a method, identify the controlled variable, interpret a graph, comment on uncertainty, suggest an improvement. Those are the skills of the investigation, examined under time pressure on unfamiliar apparatus. A student who has done a good investigation and never practised 1B will still lose marks, because the paper rewards speed of recognition rather than care.

Paper 2 loses marks for a different reason. The command terms do precise work. Describe, explain, deduce, discuss and justify each ask for a different structure, and an extended-response answer that gives a good physical account without matching the command term collects partial credit at best. In practice a Lakes student who is capable of a 6 and scoring a 4 is usually losing those two grades in the extended responses, not in the content. That is a diagnosable, fixable problem, and it is the single most common reason a family in Emirates Living books Physics support in the first place.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion, and what a tutor may touch
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the grade is decided before any exam, by a single piece of coursework marked out of 24 against four criteria, each worth six marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The report runs to a 3,000-word maximum. Those are the numbers that nobody ranking for these searches publishes, and they are the numbers that decide whether your child's investigation is on track in November of DP2 or already capped.

The failure mode is almost always criterion A. A student picks a question they find interesting rather than one they can control, measures something with an uncontrolled variable sitting in the middle of it, and then writes a careful report about compromised data. No amount of polish in the conclusion recovers those marks, because the criteria are not independent: a weak design limits what the analysis can show, and a limited analysis caps the conclusion. The investigation is won in the first fortnight and lost in the first fortnight.

The honesty boundary here is firm and worth stating plainly, because at least one site ranking in this search sells completed internal assessments outright. A tutor may teach the underlying physics, explain what each criterion rewards, ask the questions that expose a flawed design, teach uncertainty treatment and graph construction properly, and read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sections, produce the analysis or draft the report. Under IB academic-honesty rules the work has to be the candidate's own, and a breach is a malpractice matter for the student, not an inconvenience for the tutor. No tutor at IB Gram will write an internal assessment for a child.

sections.heading: What Physics tuition costs around Emirates Living, cheapest band first
paragraphs: Work up from the bottom and the price structure explains itself. The cheapest online tutoring advertised to Dubai families starts around AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and from roughly AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. Those rates buy a university student or an early-career tutor, usually a generalist. For a child who has missed two weeks of Theme A and needs the mechanics rebuilt, that can be perfectly adequate. For a Higher Level student losing marks on extended responses, it is not, and the reason is simply that the person at that price point has not marked against the criteria.

The next step up is where most Lakes families land. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate survey puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutoring at AED 200 to 450 and above. The jump from the budget band to this one is not a jump in enthusiasm; it is the step from somebody who knows physics to somebody who knows this examination. Premium named and examiner-led tutors sit higher again, with BartyED publishing AED 650 an hour. Every figure in this paragraph is a published competitor or survey rate as of the October 2026 research, not an IB Gram price.

In-home visiting rates are a separate band and the gap is instructive. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in the Dubai market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Compare those two monthly figures and the travel premium becomes visible: roughly double the monthly cost for half the number of contacts. For a Physics student the economics are worse than that, because contact frequency is what fixes paper technique. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, so these figures are published as market context for the comparison rather than as an alternative we offer.

sections.heading: Maths is the quiet gate in Physics at Higher Level
paragraphs: Physics HL assumes mathematics the student has often not been taught yet. The Diploma does not synchronise the two courses, so a Physics class reaches kinematics with calculus in it before the Maths class has finished differentiation, and reaches fields before vectors are secure. Students read that mismatch as being bad at physics. They are usually behind in maths and converting it into a physics diagnosis, which sends the family looking for the wrong tutor.

The route choice matters too. Analysis and Approaches carries the calculus and algebraic fluency that Physics HL leans on hardest. Applications and Interpretation goes further into statistics and modelling and lighter on calculus, which is survivable alongside Physics SL and uncomfortable alongside Physics HL. The right time to think about this is in the subject-choice weeks of DP1, not in February of DP2, and it is also worth checking the published entry requirements of the specific university courses your child has in mind, since engineering routes differ on this point.

In practice a diagnostic session answers the question quickly. Give a Physics HL student a Theme A problem that needs differentiation and a Theme D problem that needs vector resolution and you can see within twenty minutes whether the obstacle is physical or mathematical. If it is mathematical, the efficient fix is a short block of targeted maths rather than a term of physics tuition, which is cheaper and faster. The table below maps the main pressure points.

sections.heading: Practical and data skills when the lesson happens on a screen
paragraphs: The fair objection to online Physics tuition is apparatus. A tutor on a screen cannot hand a student a trolley and a light gate. That objection is real, and it is worth answering rather than brushing aside, because practical work is examined in this course through Paper 1B and through the investigation.

What the examination actually tests, though, is the thinking around apparatus rather than the handling of it. Paper 1B gives the student somebody else's method and somebody else's readings and asks them to find the weakness, process the data and judge the conclusion. Not one mark in that paper depends on having touched the equipment. The investigation does require real measurement, but the measurement happens in the school laboratory under a teacher's supervision, which is where the IB requires it to happen. The parts a tutor can affect are the design before the data and the analysis after it, and both are done better on a shared screen than across a kitchen table, because a spreadsheet, a graph and a mark scheme can all be visible at once.

There is a practical advantage as well. A screen session can be recorded for the student's own revision, graphs can be built live and saved, and a tutor can mark a scanned Paper 2 answer in real time with the official criteria open alongside it. A Lakes family that has tried both usually notices the difference in the week before a mock, when the useful thing is a shared document rather than a shared room.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question almost nobody in the search results answers, and it has a clear answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are, in the ministry's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting you a specific amount is guessing.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Those are checkable facts on a government website, and a parent is entitled to ask a tutor whether they hold the permit.

One further constraint is worth knowing because it shapes who may teach your child. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than read from the policy document itself, so treat it as a strong indication to verify rather than a quotation. The general principle still holds in Dubai: 'your child's own class teacher, privately' is not a product anybody should be selling you.

sections.heading: Starting from The Lakes, including what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The first step is a conversation rather than a form, and the most useful thing you can bring to it is specificity. 'Physics is going badly' takes a diagnostic session to decode. 'Higher Level, strong on Theme A, lost in Theme D, last Paper 2 came back at 4 with the extended responses blank' lets a specialist quote a plan in ten minutes. If you have a recent mock paper, the school's scheme of work, or the predicted grade, say so. If your child has an investigation already underway, say which stage it is at, because that changes the urgency entirely.

Then there is a free trial lesson, one per student and with no card details needed to book it, with the tutor who would actually teach the course. Not a sales call, not a different person. A Physics trial should include a real problem at the real level, and you should expect to hear the tutor name the theme and the command term rather than talk about confidence and motivation. If the chemistry is wrong, say so and ask for a different match; that costs nothing and it is a far better outcome than three paid sessions of politeness.

The honest part: Higher Level Physics specialists are the scarcest category on the platform, and there are weeks when no suitable tutor has a free slot in the evening band a Lakes family needs. When that happens you will be told, with a date, rather than matched to whoever is available. If the slot you need cannot be covered by a UAE-based tutor, the alternative offered is a UAE-timed slot with an IB Physics specialist elsewhere, which is the same delivery format at the same hour in Gulf Standard Time. Waiting a fortnight for the right person beats starting on Thursday with the wrong one, particularly in a subject where the wrong teaching has to be unlearned before the right teaching can begin.

process.title: Say which theme, not just which subject
process.description: Tell us the level, the theme letter where the trouble starts, the last paper mark and whether the investigation is underway. Four pieces of information turn a general enquiry into a specific brief, and they let us check availability against the exact Physics profile your child needs rather than against the word 'science'.

process.title: A trial with the tutor who would teach
process.description: One free trial lesson per student, no card details required to book, taught by the person who would take the course if you continue. Expect a real problem at the real level, and expect the tutor to name the theme and the command term they are working on. A trial that is all rapport and no physics has told you something useful.

process.title: A diagnostic against the real criteria
process.description: Before a plan is written, the tutor marks a piece of your child's actual work against the official assessment criteria, and shows you where the marks went. Most Lakes students who book Physics support are losing grades to command terms or to uncertainty treatment rather than to missing content, and that distinction changes the whole plan.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a written note each time
process.description: A standing slot in Gulf Standard Time, sixty or ninety minutes, with a short written note after each session naming what was covered, what was set and what still needs work. The note is for you as much as for the student, because it is how you tell progress from attendance.

process.title: Reassess at each reporting point
process.description: School reports, mocks and internal deadlines are the natural review points. At each one the plan is checked against the mark, the level of entry and the state of the investigation, and the session frequency is adjusted. Dropping from weekly to fortnightly once a theme is secure is a normal outcome, not a lost customer.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus, not by distance
whyPoints.description: The constraint that makes a local Physics search frustrating is removed rather than worked around. A Lakes family is matched to a tutor who has taught the current Physics guide at the level their child sits, and that pool is national rather than a twenty-minute radius of Emirates Living.

One site competing for this search sells completed internal assessments. That is a malpractice risk carried by the student, and it is not something IB Gram will do.

whyPoints.description: The same tutor each week, a written note after every session, and a reassessment at each school reporting point. Continuity is what lets a backlog be cleared in sequence instead of rediscovered, and the note is the evidence a parent needs to judge whether the money is working.

faqs.question: Is there really an IB Physics tutor near me in The Lakes?
faqs.answer: Within a twenty-minute drive of The Lakes there are plenty of science tutors and very few IB Physics specialists, particularly at Higher Level. Physics is the smallest of the three main IB sciences at most Dubai schools, and Higher Level is the smaller half of that, so the local pool is thin by arithmetic rather than by accident. IB Gram answers the question by removing distance from it: your child is matched to an IB Physics specialist and taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The tutor may live elsewhere; the lesson still starts at 7pm Dubai time.

faqs.question: Which IB Physics themes do students around Emirates Living struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Theme D, fields, by a wide margin. Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields are one idea presented three ways, and a student who memorised them as three separate chapters cannot move between them under exam pressure. Theme B comes second, usually because gas behaviour was learned as a set of formulae rather than as a particle model. Theme A is deceptive: it looks like IGCSE mechanics, so students coast through it and then meet calculus-based kinematics unprepared. Theme E suffers from timing more than difficulty, since it often arrives in DP2 when revision for everything else has already begun.

faqs.question: How is Paper 1B different from the data questions in Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Paper 1B is a dedicated set of data-based and experimental questions sitting inside the 36% that Paper 1 carries. It hands the student an unfamiliar method and someone else's readings and asks them to identify the controlled variable, process the data, comment on uncertainty and suggest a specific improvement. Paper 2's data items are embedded in wider short-answer and extended-response questions and are usually closer to the taught content. In practice 1B rewards speed of recognition on apparatus a student has never seen, which is why it needs separate practice rather than general revision.

faqs.question: My child is at a Meadows school doing Physics HL and is lost in fields. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Usually, and faster than parents expect, because the problem is normally structural rather than cumulative. Students who stall in Theme D have almost always learned gravitational, electric and magnetic fields as three unrelated topics. Teaching the shared structure, inverse-square behaviour, field lines, potential and the force on a test object, lets them reuse one piece of reasoning in three contexts. A specialist will also check the vector mathematics underneath, since resolution of components is often the real obstacle. Six to eight focused sessions is a typical plan, with Paper 2 extended responses practised throughout rather than saved for the end.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Physics scientific investigation without writing any of it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the only acceptable arrangement. A tutor may teach the physics involved, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, interrogate a research question until the student finds the uncontrolled variable themselves, teach uncertainty treatment and graphing on practice data, and read a draft the student has written to say where it falls short. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sections or produce the analysis. Under IB academic-honesty rules the investigation has to be the candidate's own work, and a breach is a malpractice matter for the student. No IB Gram tutor will write an internal assessment.

faqs.question: What does Physics tuition cost for a family in Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai, as published in October 2026, run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online generalists, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist. TutorChase quotes around AED 270; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey puts specialist tutoring at AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home visiting rates sit at AED 180 to 500 because travel is billed through the hourly rate. Those are other providers' published figures, not IB Gram prices. Ask about our rates on the consultation call.

faqs.question: Does my child need Maths AA to cope with Physics at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Not formally, but Analysis and Approaches carries the calculus and algebraic fluency that Physics HL leans on hardest. Applications and Interpretation goes deeper into statistics and lighter into calculus, which works alongside Physics SL and gets uncomfortable alongside Physics HL, particularly in Theme A kinematics and Theme D fields. The time to weigh this is during DP1 subject choices, and it is worth reading the published entry requirements of the specific university courses your child has in mind, since engineering routes differ. A single diagnostic session will usually show whether the obstacle is physical or mathematical.

faqs.question: How are practical skills taught if the Physics lesson is on a screen?
faqs.answer: The examined practical skills are mostly skills of reasoning about apparatus rather than handling it. Paper 1B gives the student someone else's method and readings to evaluate, and no mark in it depends on having touched the equipment. The scientific investigation does require real measurement, and that happens in the school laboratory under a teacher's supervision, which is where the IB expects it. What a tutor affects is the design before the data and the analysis afterwards. Both are done better on a shared screen, where a spreadsheet, a graph and the criteria can all be visible together.

faqs.question: What time can a Physics session realistically start on a Lakes school night?
faqs.answer: Most Emirates Living schools finish between 2:30pm and 3:30pm, and once activities and the drive home are accounted for, a workable weekday start is 5pm at the earliest. Families with a parent commuting back from Business Bay or DIFC tend to prefer 7pm or 8pm, and an online slot makes that straightforward because there is no travel at either end. Ninety-minute Physics sessions work better than sixty-minute ones, since a full extended-response question and its mark scheme rarely fit inside an hour. Weekend mornings are the other popular band, especially in the run-up to mocks.

faqs.question: Does a Physics tutor teaching my child in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you read as unverified.

faqs.question: How long is the IB Physics scientific investigation allowed to be?
faqs.answer: The report runs to a maximum of 3,000 words and is marked out of 24. Length is rarely the binding constraint, though. Students who exceed it have usually written a literature review in front of their method, and students well under it have usually skipped the evaluation. The useful target is proportion rather than total: enough design detail that a reader could repeat the experiment, enough analysis that the uncertainty treatment is visible, and a conclusion short enough to be judged against the data. Confirm the current limit with your child's school coordinator before submission.

faqs.question: What do the four Physics investigation criteria actually reward?
faqs.answer: Research design, six marks, rewards a focused question with properly controlled variables and a workable method. Data analysis, six marks, rewards correct processing, honest uncertainty treatment and appropriate graphs. Conclusion, six marks, rewards a conclusion the data actually supports, set against accepted physics. Evaluation, six marks, rewards limitations that are specific and improvements that are realistic. The criteria are not independent: a weak design caps the analysis, and a limited analysis caps the conclusion. That is why investigations are won or lost in the first fortnight rather than in the write-up.

faqs.question: Will the tutor follow my child's school scheme of work or the IB guide?
faqs.answer: Both, in that order of priority. The school's sequence decides what is useful this week, because a student revising Theme C while the class is being assessed on Theme B gets no immediate benefit. The IB guide decides what has to be covered by the end, and it is the reference point for depth at each level. In practice a tutor asks for the scheme of work in the first session, maps it against the guide, and flags anything the school is covering lightly that the examination weights heavily. The investigation timeline comes from the school, since internal deadlines are set there.

faqs.question: What happens if no Physics HL specialist is free when I get in touch?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date, rather than matched to whoever happens to be available. Higher Level Physics is the thinnest specialism in the set, and the evening slots Lakes families want are the most contested. If no UAE-based tutor covers the slot, the alternative offered is a UAE-timed session with an IB Physics specialist based elsewhere, delivered in the same format at the same Gulf Standard Time hour. Waiting a fortnight for the right match is usually the better outcome, because incorrect teaching in Physics has to be unlearned before correct teaching can take hold.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-lakes.closingHeading: Ask one specific question and you will know within minutes
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-lakes.closingBody: If you remember one thing from this page, make it the test rather than the sales pitch. Ask any prospective Physics tutor which theme contains fields and what Higher Level adds to it, then ask them to name the four investigation criteria and their marks. Someone teaching the current guide will answer both without hesitating. Someone improvising will talk about confidence and problem-solving. That question works whether you call us, a Dubai agency or a neighbour's recommendation, and it is a fairer filter than distance. When you are ready, a free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the course is the next step, and it costs nothing but the hour.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-meadows.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma physics at Higher and Standard Level and state which themes and which components they most often work on. Availability is listed by slot, because in this neighbourhood the time a session can start is usually the binding constraint rather than the subject.

intro.heading: Count the hours before you buy any of them
paragraphs: Parents in The Meadows generally arrive at physics tutoring with a grade problem and discover a timetable problem. The sequence is familiar: a 4 appears on a Year 12 report in a subject the student chose and wanted, a tutor is sought, and the first three attempts at a weekly slot collapse because nobody worked out what time the child is actually home, awake and capable of concentrating. Two months pass. The grade has not moved and nothing has been taught, because the arrangement never survived contact with the week.

So this page starts with arithmetic rather than pedagogy. A Diploma physics course at Higher Level is commonly timetabled at four to six periods a week, which after registration, settling and the practical programme leaves rather less genuine teaching time than the number suggests. The course expects independent work on top of that: question practice, consolidation of five themes, and a scientific investigation worth twenty per cent of the final grade that is largely produced outside lesson time. The gap between what is timetabled and what the course needs is the space tutoring occupies, and it is worth measuring before paying for it.

Then there is the geography, which in this neighbourhood is unusually specific. Emirates Living is a gated villa community with no schools inside most of it and no tuition centres at all. The campuses its buses serve sit mainly along the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh corridor, with the IB schools split between Emirates Hills and the Barsha side. Day ends cluster between 2:45pm and 3:20pm. The internal bus loop through Meadows 1 to 9 adds twenty to fifty minutes depending on where in the loop your gate sits, so the honest earliest session time varies by street rather than by community.

Those two facts together explain why the online format is not a compromise here. A physics specialist at Higher Level is a scarce commodity in any city, and a family in Meadows 7 who insists the tutor drives to them has narrowed the pool to whoever is willing to spend ninety minutes in traffic for a sixty-minute lesson, then pay for the privilege in the rate. IB Gram does not operate that way: we do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE, because in-home visiting is a service our India operation runs. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time.

What follows is the detail. A week-by-week map of the windows that actually exist in a Meadows household, the hours budget for Diploma physics set against what schools timetable, the campuses this area feeds and what each one's day end does to a session, the component structure of the current physics course and where the marks sit, the scheduling of the scientific investigation across Year 12, the term-level arithmetic of driving to a tutor instead, and the boundary on what help an investigation written at home may receive.
