dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-meadows.programmesIntro: Physics appears under three different names along the route through a Dubai international school, and the support each one needs is genuinely different. These are the stages behind the enquiries that reach us from Emirates Living.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Integrated or discipline-based sciences assessed against four criteria rather than percentages, with physics content distributed through the years rather than taught as a separate subject in most schools. Criterion scores look reassuring and conceal the specific weakness that matters later: fluency in rearranging equations and in reading quantitative information off a graph.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills both run MYP. For a family here the practical point is that a strong MYP science profile does not predict Diploma physics performance, because the Diploma asks for sustained mathematical work that MYP criteria do not specifically test. The gap becomes visible in the second term of Year 12.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Five themes from space, time and motion through the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour, fields and nuclear and quantum physics, assessed by two written papers plus an internally assessed scientific investigation worth twenty per cent. Higher Level sits longer papers with additional content in each theme; the component weightings are the same at both levels.
programmes.countryNote: The IB carried 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25 and three further IB schools join the emirate's 2026-27 intake. Higher Level physics is the thinnest specialist supply in this subject anywhere in the market, which is the practical reason a family in The Meadows should not also be filtering tutors by drive time.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE Physics
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 with its separate practical or alternative-to-practical paper, or Pearson 4PH1 which assesses practical skills inside the written papers. The usual feeder into Diploma physics for students in British-curriculum schools, and the point at which electricity and electromagnetism either become secure or stay permanently shaky.
programmes.countryNote: Because most schools around Emirates Living run IGCSE rather than MYP, the majority of Diploma physics students locally arrive from 0625 or 4PH1. A strong IGCSE physics grade earned on scaffolded questions is a weaker predictor of Diploma success than parents expect, and the diagnostic signal is how the student handles an unfamiliar context.

programmes.name: A Level Physics
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 physics route in the British-curriculum schools nearby, with no internally assessed investigation carrying a fifth of the grade and a heavier emphasis on practical endorsement. Students choosing between it and Diploma physics are choosing between depth in three subjects and breadth across six with a substantial independent research component.
programmes.countryNote: Families in this neighbourhood often hold the decision open into the spring of Year 11, and physics is frequently the subject that settles it. The useful input is diagnostic: a student who finds independent extended work difficult will find the Diploma investigation harder than the content, and that is worth knowing in March rather than in the following January.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-meadows.subjectsIntro: Physics is set out first by theme, because the current guide organises the course that way and a tutor who cannot name the themes has not read it. The subjects after it are the ones that share a week with physics in a Diploma timetable.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, energy and, at Higher Level, rotational and relativistic extensions. The first theme taught and the one whose weaknesses propagate furthest: a student who cannot resolve vectors confidently here will struggle in fields and in circular motion later in the course.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, current electricity and, at Higher Level, additional thermodynamic work. Circuit questions are where many students first lose marks in quantity, usually because potential difference and current are being reasoned about qualitatively rather than calculated.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave phenomena, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect, with extensions at Higher Level. The theme that most rewards careful diagram work: a correctly drawn wave with labelled amplitude and wavelength earns marks that a correct verbal description does not.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential, and electromagnetic induction. The theme Higher Level students most often name as the hardest, because the mathematics is unforgiving and the three field types invite confusion between formulae that look superficially similar.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear structure and energy, fission and fusion, and quantum phenomena with Higher Level extensions. Taught late in most schemes of work, which means it is frequently the least secure theme going into the final papers simply because it has had the fewest weeks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The natural partner subject, and the one where sharing a tutor can genuinely save hours in a crowded week. Rearrangement, graph interpretation, logarithms and calculus all appear in physics questions, and a student weak in one subject is usually losing marks in both for the same reason.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A workable combination with physics, with a caveat worth stating early: the calculus and algebraic manipulation available in Analysis and Approaches support Higher Level physics more directly. Students pairing Applications and Interpretation with Physics Higher Level often need a short algebra block to keep pace.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the scientific investigation structure and the data-analysis skills, so a tutor who understands one investigation understands the other. The content overlap is narrow, mostly energetics and atomic structure, so the saving from a shared tutor is real for the internal assessment and limited for the papers.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pairs well with physics for students who think procedurally, and the internally assessed solution has a similar independent-project rhythm to the physics investigation. Both components slip for the same reason, which is that neither is timetabled, so a student taking both needs the week planned deliberately.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Shares mechanics and materials content with physics and a substantial internally assessed project. Students taking both are carrying two significant independent components alongside the Extended Essay, which is an hours problem rather than a difficulty problem and is best planned in Year 12.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay in physics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay supervised by the school. Physics is a demanding choice because a question that can actually be investigated with available equipment is hard to frame. A tutor's contribution is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts, never research or writing.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by exhibition and essay, and the natural sciences are one of the areas of knowledge students write about. Support means explaining how the assessment instrument works and responding to the student's own argument, never supplying the argument or the examples.

sections.heading: The physics week from the bell to the screen
paragraphs: Start with the window that actually exists. Campuses serving Emirates Living finish between roughly 2:45pm and 3:20pm. The bus loop through Meadows 1 to 9 adds twenty to fifty minutes depending on where your gate sits in the sequence, so a student in Meadows 2 might be home by 3:40pm while a student in Meadows 8 walks in after 4:10pm. Add eating and the recovery a fifteen-year-old needs after a full day, and the earliest honest start for quantitative work is somewhere between 4:30pm and 6pm, by street rather than by community.

The rest of the week constrains it further. Most Diploma students in these schools carry at least two co-curricular commitments, often sport with fixed training evenings. Homework across six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge consumes the rest. Friday is a short school day across the UAE and the family rhythm around it is different, which makes Friday afternoons either the best slot in the week or the worst depending on the household. Saturday mornings are the most productive hour available to most students and the first to be booked.

The practical rule is to book the slot against arrival time rather than finish time, and to confirm it against two weeks of reality rather than one good week in September. Arrangements in this community fail most often in October, when the first fixture clash or the first late bus reveals that the slot was always twenty minutes too early. The table below sets out the windows as they actually behave across a Meadows week, with what each one is genuinely good for, because a tired 4:30pm hour and a rested Saturday ninety minutes are not interchangeable units of tutoring.

sections.heading: Counting the Diploma physics hours: timetabled against needed
paragraphs: Schools timetable Diploma physics generously by secondary-school standards and thinly by the standards of what the course contains. Higher Level is commonly scheduled at four to six periods a week, Standard Level at three to four, and a meaningful share of that time goes to the practical programme, which is required and valuable and is not content delivery. Subtract registration, settling and the inevitable interruptions of a school calendar and the genuine teaching time is noticeably less than the period count implies.

Against that, count what the course asks for. Five themes across two years, each with Higher Level extensions. Two written papers carrying eighty per cent of the grade between them, examined through unfamiliar contexts that reward practice rather than recall. A scientific investigation worth the other twenty per cent, produced over months and largely outside lessons. Question practice sufficient to build the pattern recognition the papers test. And, in a Dubai school, mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies lessons occupying timetable hours that have to come from somewhere.

The deficit this produces is where tutoring sits, and naming it changes what you buy. If the gap is content coverage, a weekly hour through Year 12 is the right purchase and the cheapest one. If the gap is practice volume, the answer is a structured set of problems with marked feedback rather than more teaching. If the gap is the investigation, the answer is three to five scheduled clinics at the right points in the drafting period, not a term of weekly sessions. sections.heading: Which campuses this neighbourhood feeds, and what each day end means
paragraphs: A Meadows address does not map to one school. The buses out of Emirates Living serve the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh corridor, the two IB campuses on the Emirates Hills side, and increasingly the newer schools in Al Barsha South and Motor City. Which one your child attends determines the day end, the route length and therefore the earliest session that is honestly available, which is why a tutoring plan built without naming the school tends to fall apart in the first month.

It also determines something more consequential for physics specifically: whether Higher Level is offered in your child's cohort at all. Diploma physics at Higher Level requires enough students to make a set viable, and in smaller cohorts it occasionally does not run, or runs in a block that collides with another subject the student wanted. Families discover this at options time and have limited room to move. Where a student has ended up at Standard Level by timetable rather than by choice, tutoring is sometimes being asked to do a job that a subject change would have done better.

sections.heading: Where the physics grade actually sits, component by component
paragraphs: The current Diploma physics course is assessed by two written papers and one internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent of the grade and combines multiple-choice questions with data-based questions; Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent through short-answer and extended-response questions; the investigation carries the remaining twenty per cent. Higher Level sits longer papers with additional content in each theme, but the weightings are the same at both levels, which surprises parents who assume Higher Level shifts the balance.

That distribution has a direct planning consequence. Paper 2 is the single largest component in the course, it is where extended reasoning and command-term discipline are tested, and it is the component least improved by content revision alone. The investigation is the second largest at twenty per cent, it is settled before the examinations are sat, and it is the only component where a student can bank marks calmly over months rather than produce them in a hall. A plan that spends its hours on content coverage and leaves both of those to look after themselves is misallocated.

Where marks leak is predictable by theme. Vector resolution in theme A propagates errors into fields and circular motion. Circuit reasoning in theme B fails when potential difference is argued about instead of calculated. Theme C rewards labelled diagrams over verbal description. Theme D, fields, is the one Higher Level students name most often as impossible, because three field types share superficially similar formulae and the mathematics is unforgiving. Theme E is usually the least secure simply because it is taught last. None of that is a mystery to a tutor who has taught the course, which is why asking about it in a trial lesson is informative.

sections.heading: Fitting the scientific investigation into a Year 12 week
paragraphs: A fifth of the physics grade is produced at home, over months, with a handful of supervised checkpoints, while the student is also carrying five other subjects, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Stated like that, the reason investigations slip is obvious: the work has no timetabled hour, so it competes with everything that does. Families in The Meadows discover this in the week before the school's internal deadline, which is the most expensive week in which to discover it.

The fix is calendar work rather than teaching. Put the school's internal deadline on a calendar, then place four milestones backwards from it: a research question agreed, data collected, analysis complete, full draft written. Each milestone needs a dated slot in the week, and a Saturday morning is usually the only place one genuinely exists. A tutoring clinic placed at each milestone is worth more than a weekly session running alongside, because the failure here is not a lack of understanding; it is a lack of scheduled time.

The criteria matter to that scheduling because they tell you where the hours should go. Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation each carry six marks, making twenty-four in total. Students typically overspend on data collection and underspend on evaluation, which is where the marks are easiest to earn with careful writing. Knowing the allocation before starting changes how the months are spent, and it is the single most useful thing a tutor can hand a Year 12 student in the autumn term.

sections.heading: What driving to a tutor actually costs over a term
paragraphs: The cost conversation in Dubai right now has a useful anchor: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are, for once, a fixed quantity, which makes it a reasonable year to look hard at the variable spending around them, and tutoring is the largest piece of that for most Diploma families in this neighbourhood.

Market rates in Dubai, read in October 2026, put budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table at AED 200 to 450 and upwards for specialist exam-year support. In-home visits including travel run AED 180 to 500, on Bestimate's AED 180 to 350 band plus independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, and BartyED is published at AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages in circulation include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Every one of those figures belongs to the named provider; none is an IB Gram price, and we publish a free trial lesson and a consultation instead of a rate card.

The figure nobody puts on a page is the travel. A round trip from Meadows 6 to a tutor or centre in Al Barsha at half past four, allowing for the afternoon peak in both directions, commonly runs to ninety minutes. Over a thirty-week term at one session a week that is forty-five hours of a parent's year and forty-five hours of a student's, spent sitting still. The table below prices that honestly alongside the rates, because the comparison between online and in-home in this community is not really about the hourly figure. It is about what else those forty-five hours could have been.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE lessons, and the study hours they occupy
paragraphs: A physics hours budget in a Dubai private school is incomplete without the subjects every school must teach regardless of its licensed curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The arithmetic is specific. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects.

For a Diploma physics student this is why the independent-study budget is smaller than a six-subject timetable suggests, and it is a reason to plan the investigation and the Extended Essay deliberately rather than hoping they fit. Where support in these subjects is needed, it has to work inside the school's own material: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That rules out a parallel course and makes the school, rather than a tutor, the right first conversation.

sections.heading: An investigation written at home, and the line that protects the qualification
paragraphs: Because the scientific investigation is produced at a kitchen table rather than in a classroom, the question of what help is permitted arrives in practice rather than in theory. The boundary is worth writing down before any session is booked, and it is a genuine point of difference in this market, where completed coursework is openly sold to UAE families by at least one site in the same search results.

What a tutor may legitimately do: explain each criterion and its mark allocation in plain language, discuss whether a proposed research question is viable with the equipment available, teach the physics and the uncertainty treatment the student needs, show what a strong evaluation looks like in general terms, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. What a tutor may not do: choose the research question, process the data that appears in the report, supply the evaluation, or rewrite the work to completion. The student does the investigation and writes every submitted word.

The reason to be strict about this is not squeamishness. IB academic-honesty rules make submitted work that is not the student's own a malpractice matter, and the consequence falls on the student's qualification rather than on the tutoring fee. The school supervisor also authenticates the work, so an investigation that does not match the student's demonstrated ability is a risk at the point of submission. Ask any prospective tutor where their line sits. A tutor who cannot describe one in concrete terms is a risk to your child, whatever the rate.

sections.heading: Starting physics support from The Meadows, timetable first
paragraphs: The first thing we ask is not about physics. It is which school, which sub-community, and what time your child actually walks through the door, because that determines whether any arrangement will survive October. Then the level, the themes covered so far, whether the investigation has a research question yet, and the most recent marked work you hold. A free 45-minute trial follows, one-to-one over live video with the tutor who would teach the term rather than a consultant, and no card details are required to book it.

The recommendation will sometimes be to buy less. If the gap is practice volume, the right purchase is a set of marked problems rather than a weekly teaching hour. If the investigation has no research question in November, that is the thing to spend on and the content can wait. If the student is at Standard Level because of a timetable block and wanted Higher Level, that is a conversation with the school before it is a tutoring question. Saying so is what makes the advice worth anything on the occasions when it is to spend more.

The limits, stated in advance. Higher Level physics is the thinnest specialist supply in this subject anywhere, and Saturday morning slots in this neighbourhood are gone by mid-January; where no UAE-based tutor covers the level and slot you need, the match may be an experienced Diploma physics specialist teaching from outside the UAE on the same live video format and the same Gulf Standard Time schedule, and we say so before you book. No tutor will promise a grade. No tutor will produce any part of the investigation. No tutor will come to a villa in Emirates Living, because in-home visiting is not a service we sell in the UAE. No IB session dates appear on this page, because the IB's own site could not be verified for this project: confirm them with your school's coordinator. And nothing here claims approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership with the IB, KHDA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, because IB Gram holds none of those and runs no UAE office.

The scheme of work is usually available on request.

process.description: Forty-five minutes, one-to-one over live video, with the tutor who would teach the term. Ask them where students lose marks in fields, how they teach uncertainty treatment, and what the investigation criteria are worth. Each needs a dated slot, and a Saturday morning is usually the only place one genuinely exists in a Diploma week. Clinics placed at the milestones beat a weekly session running alongside.

If a named theme has not moved in four weeks, change the method or the tutor. Agreeing that trigger before the first invoice keeps the conversation administrative.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma physics session start on a Meadows weekday?
faqs.answer: It depends which sub-community you are in, because the afternoon bus loop runs through nine of them in sequence. Schools serving Emirates Living finish between roughly 2:45pm and 3:20pm, and the loop adds twenty to fifty minutes, so a student in Meadows 2 may be home by 3:40pm while one in Meadows 8 arrives after 4:10pm. Allowing for eating and recovery, the honest earliest start is 4:30pm for the early stops and 6pm for the late ones. Booking against the school bell rather than actual arrival is why most weekly arrangements here fail in October.

faqs.question: How many physics periods a week does a Higher Level student actually get?
faqs.answer: Commonly four to six, with Standard Level at three to four, and a meaningful share of that going to the required practical programme rather than content delivery. Subtract registration, settling and the interruptions of a school calendar and the genuine teaching time is less than the period count suggests. Against that the course asks for five themes with Higher Level extensions, two papers worth eighty per cent between them, substantial marked question practice, and an investigation worth twenty per cent produced outside lessons. The deficit is where tutoring belongs, and naming which part of it you are buying matters more than the rate.

faqs.question: Which schools near The Meadows actually run Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: The IB campuses within reach of this neighbourhood include Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills on the Emirates Hills side, with GEMS World Academy Dubai, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and Dubai International Academy Al Barsha across the Barsha corridor. Whether Higher Level physics runs in a given cohort depends on set sizes, and in smaller cohorts it occasionally does not, or collides in the block structure with another chosen subject. Ask the school directly at options time. Schools are named here as local context only; IB Gram has no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: What are Paper 1 and Paper 2 worth in Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent of the grade and combines multiple-choice with data-based questions. Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent through short-answer and extended-response questions, which makes it the single largest component in the course. The scientific investigation carries the remaining twenty per cent. Higher Level sits longer papers with additional content in each theme, but the weightings are identical at both levels, which often surprises parents. The planning consequence is that extended reasoning and command-term discipline, which Paper 2 tests, deserve more of the tutoring budget than content coverage usually gets.

faqs.question: How is the physics scientific investigation marked?
faqs.answer: Against four criteria, each carrying six marks for a total of twenty-four, which converts to twenty per cent of the final grade at both levels. Research design rewards a focused research question with a justified methodology. Data analysis rewards correct processing, proper treatment of uncertainties and appropriate graphs. Conclusion rewards a conclusion genuinely justified by the data. Evaluation rewards meaningful discussion of limitations and realistic improvements, and it is both the most underspent criterion and the easiest to earn marks on with careful writing. Knowing the allocation before drafting changes how the months get spent.

faqs.question: When in Year 12 should the investigation be started?
faqs.answer: Earlier than it usually is, and the useful discipline is calendar work rather than teaching. Put the school's internal deadline on a calendar and place four milestones backwards from it: research question agreed, data collected, analysis complete, full draft written. Each milestone needs a dated slot, and in a Diploma week a Saturday morning is often the only place one genuinely exists. The failure here is almost never a lack of understanding; it is that the work has no timetabled hour and therefore competes with everything that does.

faqs.question: How much of our week does driving to a physics tutor cost?
faqs.answer: A round trip from Meadows 6 to a tutor or centre in Al Barsha at half past four, allowing for the afternoon peak in both directions, commonly runs to ninety minutes. At one session a week across a thirty-week term that is thirty to forty-five hours for the parent driving and the same for the student sitting in the car. That figure rarely appears in a rate comparison, and in this community it is the largest single difference between an online arrangement and a local one. The teaching in the hour is the same either way.

faqs.question: What should my child do with a returned physics paper?
faqs.answer: Mark it themselves against the published scheme, line by line, before discussing it with anyone. The purpose is to count the marks they earned the thinking for and failed to claim, which in physics usually means unstated assumptions, missing units, no reference to a named law, or a conclusion that does not answer the command term. That number changes behaviour faster than any instruction. The paid role in this is setting the work, verifying the marking and keeping an error log by theme, not sitting with the student while they read it.

faqs.question: Which physics theme causes the most trouble for Year 12 students?
faqs.answer: Theme D, fields, is the one Higher Level students name most often, because gravitational, electric and magnetic fields share superficially similar formulae and the mathematics is unforgiving. Theme A causes quieter damage earlier: a student who cannot resolve vectors confidently carries that weakness into circular motion and fields months later. Theme E is frequently the least secure simply because it is taught last and gets the fewest weeks. A tutor who can describe this pattern without being prompted has taught the course; one who cannot is teaching physics in general.

faqs.question: Can physics and maths share one tutor to save time in the week?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in a crowded Diploma week the saving is in hours as much as in dirhams. Rearrangement, graph interpretation, logarithms and calculus all appear in physics questions, and a student weak in both subjects is frequently losing marks for the same underlying reason. The caveat is the investigation: it has its own criteria and needs somebody who has supervised one, so check that the shared tutor covers that component too. Pairing physics with a non-quantitative subject under one tutor rarely works and is not a saving worth making.

faqs.question: Are Saturday morning sessions better than weekday evenings here?
faqs.answer: For quantitative work, usually yes, and that is why the 9am Saturday slots in this community are gone by the second week of January. A rested student working for ninety minutes without homework, co-curriculars or a bus competing for the time produces considerably more than a tired one at 4:30pm. Weekday evenings still matter for consolidation, marking review and setting practice. The practical advice for a Meadows family is to secure the weekend slot in the autumn term and use weekday evenings as the flexible part of the arrangement.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect study time?
faqs.answer: They occupy timetable hours that have to come from somewhere, which is why the independent-study budget in a Dubai school is smaller than a six-subject timetable implies. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA calculates the instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, advising at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are required in several of them. Plan the investigation and Extended Essay around this rather than discovering the squeeze in February.

faqs.question: What does Diploma physics support cost around The Meadows?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 ran roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200; AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists, with TutorChase at AED 270; and AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits including travel, with BartyED published at AED 650 at the premium end. None is an IB Gram price. Worth noting as context: KHDA confirmed no private school fee increase in Dubai for 2026-27.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting physics tutoring in the final weeks before the session?
faqs.answer: It can be, provided the work changes shape. In the last six to eight weeks, new content teaching is poor value and timed-paper work with proper marking is not: most of the remaining gain sits in command-term discipline, unit and assumption discipline, and pace. Set a fixed stop date and leave the final week to the student. What it cannot do is substitute for a missing investigation, which carries twenty per cent and is settled before the papers. If that component is incomplete, it is the first call on whatever time remains.

faqs.question: What happens to our sessions during school mock examinations?
faqs.answer: They should change purpose rather than stop. During mock weeks, new content is wasted and paper technique is not, so the hour is better spent on timed sections, mark-scheme reading and the specific themes the mocks will cover. Pausing rather than cancelling keeps the slot, which matters because in this community a surrendered Saturday morning is not recoverable in January. Agree at the start of the year that mock weeks switch to technique and that study-leave weeks may need a different timetable; both are easier to arrange in September than in February.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the investigation when the school already supervises it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the two roles are different. The school supervisor runs the required checkpoints and authenticates the work; a tutor adds explanation of the criteria, discussion of whether a research question is viable, teaching of the physics and the uncertainty treatment, and feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor must not choose the research question, process the data that appears in the report, supply the evaluation or edit the work to completion. Submitted work that is not the student's own is a malpractice matter, and the consequence falls on the qualification rather than the fee.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-meadows.closingHeading: Fix the slot first, then fix the physics
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-meadows.closingBody: Work out what time your child genuinely reaches home in your part of The Meadows, check where the investigation stands, and find out which themes the school has actually taught. Then tell us all three, along with the level, and take the free 45-minute trial with the tutor who would teach the term. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. If the honest answer is a set of marked problems, a Saturday clinic on the investigation or a conversation with the school about a timetable block, you will hear that before you hear a rate.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-springs.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are Physics-first: people who teach the current Diploma Physics guide, mark against its four internal-assessment criteria, and can say which theme a dropped mark came from. Each one works online with students across Emirates Living.

intro.heading: The cost of IB Physics help in The Springs, before anyone quotes you a number
paragraphs: Ask five providers what an IB Physics tutor in The Springs costs and you will get five answers spread across a factor of ten. Budget online platforms advertise from the low double figures in AED per hour. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one work at AED 180 to 350 and subject specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. One UK agency publishes AED 270 for its UAE work. A named-examiner service in Dubai publishes AED 650. None of those figures is a lie, and none of them tells you what your child's Physics problem will cost to fix.

The reason is that Physics does not fail in one place. A Springs student can be fluent in kinematics and unable to read a gradient off a log plot. Another can handle every calculation in Theme A and lose eleven marks across Paper 2 because nobody ever showed them what the command term 'deduce' requires that 'state' does not. A third has a scientific investigation due in eleven weeks with no measurable variable chosen yet. Those are three different jobs, needing three different numbers of hours, and a rate card cannot separate them.

So this page is built the other way around. It starts from the assessment, because the assessment decides where hours are worth buying. It then puts real AED bands next to the three jobs a Physics tutor is usually hired for, names the three ways families around Emirates Living spend money without moving a grade, and finishes with what happens when a household decides to start. Every figure carries the source it came from and the date it was published.

The delivery model is worth stating before the prices, because it changes the arithmetic. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Springs townhouse or to any other UAE address; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. Physics support for families here is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run. That removes the travel component that in-home Dubai rates carry, and it widens the pool from whoever is free in Emirates Living to whoever actually teaches Diploma Physics well.

The Springs sits inside the densest private-school market in the country. KHDA counted 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai in 2024-25, with 17 different curricula licensed and the International Baccalaureate holding seven per cent of that enrolment. Seven per cent of a market that size is a lot of Diploma students and a small, over-subscribed group of people who teach Physics at Higher Level. That scarcity, not the cost of an hour, is what makes Physics the subject families struggle to resource locally.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-springs.programmesIntro: Physics sits in a programme, and the programme decides what a tutor is actually being asked to do. These are the four stages a Springs family passes through, with what each one costs in support hours rather than in fees.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences in the MYP is marked against four criteria lettered A to D, each scored one to eight, with no external paper until the optional eAssessment at the end of MYP 5. Physics content appears inside integrated science units rather than as a separate subject, so a student can arrive in DP1 having never written a full physics derivation.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows runs the IB continuum on the doorstep of The Springs, which means a sizeable group of local children meet criterion-based science marking years before they meet a Physics paper. Support at this stage is cheap in hours and disproportionately useful, because it is where measurement, uncertainty and graph work are either learned or quietly skipped.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: The current Physics guide organises content into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Assessment is Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the internal assessment at 20%, with Higher Level sitting longer papers over additional higher-level-only content.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where Springs families start searching. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Emirates International School Meadows both run the Diploma, and the common pattern is a student who chose Physics HL on the strength of an MYP science grade and met the fields and quantum material without the mathematics to carry it. Confirm which guide version your child is entered for with their DP coordinator.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE Physics
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools around Emirates Living run Cambridge Physics 0625 or the Pearson Edexcel equivalent, tiered into Core and Extended at Cambridge with a practical or alternative-to-practical component. It is the qualification that decides whether Physics HL is a realistic Diploma choice two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Regent International School and Dubai British School Emirates Hills take a large share of Springs children through IGCSE. A grade 6 at Extended level is the usual signal that Physics SL will be comfortable and Physics HL will need deliberate mathematical support from the first week of DP1 rather than from the first mock.

programmes.name: A Level Physics as the alternative route
programmes.description: Several campuses in the second ring around The Springs offer A Level rather than the Diploma. A Level Physics goes deeper into fewer topics and carries no equivalent of the Diploma's internal assessment weighting, which changes both the revision shape and the amount of supervision a student needs outside lessons.
programmes.countryNote: Worth naming on a cost page because the two routes need different numbers of hours. A Level Physics support tends to cluster into pre-exam blocks; Diploma Physics support spreads across two years because the investigation, the themes and the mathematics all mature at different speeds.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: Physics is the page, but almost no Springs household buys one subject. These are the courses most often added to a Physics booking, with the specific thing each one tends to need.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, two written papers and a 3,000-word scientific investigation. Marks are lost most reliably in uncertainty propagation, in field-line reasoning, and in extended-response questions where the answer is right and the reasoning is not shown.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual companion booking for a Physics HL student. Calculus fluency, not algebraic neatness, is what decides whether a Physics derivation is readable. Students who take Applications and Interpretations alongside Physics HL need the gap closed early.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the same assessment shape as Physics, including the 20% investigation, so one tutor can often coach both internal assessments through the same criteria. Energetics and equilibrium are where the overlap with Physics thinking is strongest.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by students who want the statistics and modelling route. It is a legitimate pairing with Physics SL. Paired with Physics HL it leaves a measurable calculus gap that shows up in Theme D.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The third science in most Springs timetables. Its investigation is judged on the same four criteria as Physics, which means a student juggling two science investigations has one skill to learn, not two.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Frequently added by Physics students aiming at engineering. The internal assessment is a developed product with documentation, so the supervision load lands in a different term from the Physics investigation.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Overlaps with Physics in mechanics and materials. Its coursework is substantial and runs long, so families pairing it with Physics HL should plan the calendar before booking hours.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A popular choice for strong Physics students and a difficult one, because a measurable, repeatable experiment is harder to design than a reading-based question. Supervision is feedback on the student's own drafts, never drafting.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The core element Physics students most often underestimate. It asks for argument rather than calculation, and a 1,600-word limit punishes the habit of writing everything known about a topic.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. It sits outside the IB grade but inside the weekly timetable, and it competes for exactly the hours a Physics student wants for revision.

sections.heading: What an IB Physics tutor costs around The Springs, in AED and with sources
paragraphs: Dubai market rates for Physics tuition run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 for a named-examiner service. The useful part of that range for a Diploma Physics student is narrower. Published 2026 rate tables for Dubai put qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 once travel is priced in, and IB or A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. One UK-based agency publishes AED 270 for its UAE tutoring. A Dubai premium service publishes AED 650 for examiner-led work.

Those bands behave differently at the two ends. Below about AED 150 an hour you are usually buying a university student who knows the physics and has never seen an IB mark scheme. That is adequate for homework rescue and poor value for Paper 2 technique, because the thing being bought is content the student can already read in a textbook. Above about AED 450 the premium is being charged for examiner adjacency rather than for teaching hours, and examiner status cannot legitimately be sold as access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

The middle band is where Diploma Physics work actually sits, and the honest answer to 'how much will this cost' is a number of hours multiplied by a rate, not a rate alone. A student who needs Paper 2 technique for a May series typically needs twelve to twenty sessions. A student rebuilding Theme D from scratch needs more. A student who needs the investigation steered to a defensible research question needs four to six. Multiply before you compare providers.

IB Gram does not publish an hourly price list on these pages, because the rate depends on the tutor matched and the subject level. What we publish is the market context above, the free trial lesson that precedes any payment, and the consultation where the hours are estimated out loud. Any figure on this page is a market rate from a named published source, not a quotation from us.

sections.heading: The three places Physics money disappears in Emirates Living
paragraphs: The first leak is buying content when the problem is technique. A Springs parent sees a 4 in a Physics mock and books twenty hours of teaching through the themes. The student already knew most of it; the marks were lost because 'explain' answers were written as 'describe' answers, because uncertainties were quoted to four significant figures, and because the final two questions on Paper 2 were never reached. Twenty hours of re-teaching produces a student who knows the course slightly better and scores the same. The diagnostic that would have found this costs one session.

The second leak is group classes bought at a per-head rate that looks efficient. Small-group science in Dubai is advertised widely and it works for structured content delivery. It does not work for a student whose problem is specific, because a group moves at the median and Physics failures are rarely median. A household paying a reduced group rate for sixteen weeks often pays more in total than one that bought eight properly targeted individual sessions, and the grade movement is smaller.

The third leak is starting late and paying the panic premium. Rates in this market do firm up as a series approaches, and availability for Higher Level Physics thins first. A family that books in October has a choice of specialists at the standard band. A family that books in late February is choosing from whoever is left, often at the top of the range, and buying hours that have to carry both content repair and paper technique at once. The calendar section below counts this backwards so the decision can be made early.

There is a fourth pattern worth naming because it is not a leak at all. Families who buy fewer hours than they expected to, after a diagnostic, frequently get better results than families who buy a large block up front. The reason is dull: targeted work on three known weaknesses moves more marks than general improvement across a course a student mostly knows.

sections.heading: Where the Physics grade actually sits: papers, weightings and hours
paragraphs: Spending decisions get easier once the assessment is on the table. In the current Diploma Physics guide, Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade, Paper 2 carries 44%, and the internal assessment carries 20%, at both Standard and Higher Level. Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 is short and extended response. Higher Level sits longer papers covering the additional higher-level content inside each of the five themes. Confirm the version and the timings for your child's cohort with their Diploma coordinator before planning around them.

Read that weighting as a budget. Paper 2 is the single largest block of marks on the course, and it is the component most responsive to tutoring, because extended response is a trainable skill with a vocabulary. The internal assessment is a fifth of the grade, is completed months before the examinations, and is the component where a student has the most control. Paper 1 rewards breadth and speed and is the hardest to move quickly with extra hours.

The practical consequence for a Springs household is a spending order rather than a spending total. Secure the investigation first, because it is worth 20% and it has a deadline that does not move. Then put the bulk of weekly hours into Paper 2 technique across the themes the student is weakest in. Treat Paper 1 as something maintained with timed practice rather than taught. A plan built in that order tends to need fewer total hours than one built by walking through the syllabus from Theme A.

The investigation deserves its own note, since it is where the 20% is won or lost quietly. It is a single report with a 3,000-word ceiling, judged against four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Students lose marks in research design more than anywhere else, usually by choosing a question with no genuinely controllable independent variable. That is a one-session conversation in September and an unfixable problem in March.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: school fees, the fee freeze and a two-year Physics plan
paragraphs: Tutoring is a line in a household education budget that already has a much larger line in it. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a Springs family, that freeze is the reason a tutoring decision this year is a decision about new money rather than about absorbing a fee increase.

Put a Physics plan against that. A weekly 90-minute session at the mid band of the market runs into a monthly figure in the hundreds of dirhams; published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions in Dubai sit at AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The two-year shape matters more than the monthly number. DP1 Physics support is cheap and preventive: fortnightly sessions, an early investigation conversation, and a mathematics check. DP2 support is expensive and corrective: weekly sessions, a paper-technique block, and whatever the investigation did not get done. Families who spend modestly in DP1 generally spend less in total, because the expensive work is the work that has to be done against a deadline.

Dubai's school sector is also still growing, which affects availability rather than price. Seven new private schools open for the 2026-27 intake, four British-curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places; six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. More Diploma cohorts mean more demand for the same small group of Higher Level Physics teachers, and that pressure is felt as waiting time, not as a higher advertised rate.

sections.heading: Online or in-home for Physics in The Springs, judged on value rather than preference
paragraphs: The in-home question is the one most Springs parents actually arrive with, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is real, it is widely available, and published rate tables put it at AED 180 to 350 an hour with home tutors advertised up to AED 500. The premium over online work is not a quality premium. It is the cost of the tutor's travel, the vehicle, and the dead time on either side of the lesson, which in practice is charged back inside the hourly rate.

The second cost is invisible and larger. Choosing in-home restricts you to Physics teachers who can reach Emirates Living inside an acceptable drive. In a subject with as thin a specialist pool as Higher Level Physics, that filter removes most of the candidates before quality enters the conversation. A Springs family optimising for a tutor who can park outside is optimising for geography, and geography does not teach fields and quantum physics.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in our India operation. Physics work for Springs households is one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for diagrams, graph work and marked scripts. For a subject built on annotated diagrams and worked algebra, a shared screen is closer to how a Physics teacher actually works at a whiteboard than a notebook on a kitchen table is.

There is one genuine advantage to a physical presence, and it is worth naming: a younger student who will not sit still is easier to manage in the same room. For a fourteen-year-old on 0625 that can matter. For a seventeen-year-old on Physics HL preparing for a May series, the deciding variable is whether the person on the other side of the session has taught the course and marked to its criteria.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the series your child is entered for
paragraphs: Physics spending is time-sensitive in a way most subjects are not, because the investigation has an internal deadline months before the papers. Working backwards from the examination series is the single most useful planning exercise a Springs family can do, and it is the thing no competitor page in this market does at all.

We do not publish IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so every date we could print would be second-hand, and a second-hand date on an examinations page is a liability rather than a service. UAE schools sit the May series as the main session, with November available; the exact windows, the internal upload deadlines and the results dates come from your child's Diploma coordinator, who works to the current official calendar.

Cambridge and Pearson publish their dates openly, and they illustrate how far ahead the real deadlines sit. In the UAE, Cambridge examines International GCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and in a November series only, and it allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, so two students in neighbouring Dubai schools can be working to different timetable versions for the same paper. Entries for a June sitting close in the spring, well ahead of the papers, and forecast grades go in before them; the exact day is confirmed on the centre's statement of entry rather than estimated on a page like this one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November series; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached them on 22 January 2026.

The operational point for a Physics family is that the entry deadline sits roughly three months before the first paper, and the tutoring decision that matters sits before that again. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. Ask your school which zone it sits in before you plan a revision calendar around a published timetable.

sections.heading: What a Physics tutor may and may not do with an investigation
paragraphs: Spending money on internal assessment support raises a question parents are right to ask, because the answer separates teaching from malpractice. A Physics tutor may explain what each of the four criteria rewards, ask why a variable was chosen, point out that an uncertainty has been quoted without justification, question whether a conclusion is supported by the data, and read a draft the student wrote and say where the reasoning stops. That is supervision, and it is what the 20% component is meant to receive.

A tutor may not choose the research question, design the method, process the data, write any part of the report, or edit a draft into a different piece of work. IB Gram does not provide any of those things and will not take a booking that asks for them. The work has to be the student's own, and a report that is not is an academic-honesty matter for the student with consequences far larger than a Physics grade.

This has a practical cost consequence for a Springs household. Supervision is cheaper than it looks, because it is a small number of well-timed conversations rather than a long block of hours. Four to six sessions spread across the drafting window usually covers the research question, the method review, a first look at the analysis and a final read of the student's own draft. Families who ask for more hours than that are usually asking, without meaning to, for someone else to do the work.

The same boundary applies to a Physics Extended Essay, to Theory of Knowledge and to any school coursework. Official past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are not ours to distribute; they belong to the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and the correct route to them is through the school or the board's own site. We reference them and point to them; we do not hand them over.

sections.heading: Permits, ethics and the questions that protect your money
paragraphs: A cost page is incomplete without the legal position, because the cheapest tutor in Emirates Living may be the one who should not be teaching your child. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and it covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services.

Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor without one has no financial excuse. Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted at you by anyone. Asking whether a tutor holds a current permit is a reasonable question and a cheap piece of due diligence.

There is a second rule that catches a common Springs arrangement. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy before relying on it, but the direction is clear: your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to hire privately, however convenient the arrangement looks.

One further distinction matters in Dubai specifically. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE permit. A tutoring operation with premises and staff needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a six-month maximum to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram operates no premises in the UAE, holds no regulator permit of that kind, and does not describe itself as having one.

sections.heading: Starting Physics support from The Springs, and what we will tell you honestly
paragraphs: The order is deliberately boring. You tell us the school, the stage, the level and what the last assessment said. We find a Physics specialist who has taught that course, and you take a free trial lesson before any money is discussed. After the trial, the tutor gives an estimate of hours and a short list of what those hours will work on. If the estimate is smaller than you expected, that is the normal outcome of a diagnostic and not a sales tactic in reverse.

The free trial has one condition worth stating on the same screen: it is one lesson, before a booking, and it is intended to test the match rather than to deliver a course. No card is taken to arrange it. If the match is wrong, say so and we will try a different tutor; if it is wrong again, the honest answer may be that we are not the right provider for that subject at that level.

That last possibility is real and worth putting in writing on a cost page. Higher Level Physics specialists are a small group, and there are weeks in the year when none is free at the hour a Springs family needs. When that happens we say so rather than matching a generalist at a specialist rate. The alternative we offer is a tutor based outside the UAE working on Gulf Standard Time, named as such, with the rate stated before the trial. What we will not do is take the booking and hope.

Lead forms on this page collect a parent's name, contact details, the child's year group, school and subject, for the single purpose of matching a tutor and arranging the trial. Nothing about a child's grades, photograph or school record is required to make an enquiry, and the data can be deleted on request. Our privacy notice is linked from every page and explains what is held and for how long, in line with UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection.

process.title: Tell us the stage, not the symptom
process.description: School, year, programme, level and the last marked assessment. A Springs enquiry that says 'Physics HL at Emirates International School Meadows, 4 in the November mock, investigation not started' can be matched in a single pass. One that says 'needs help with physics' takes three.

process.title: Diagnostic before hours
process.description: The first working session is a marked piece of the student's own Physics work, read against the criteria or the mark scheme. It produces a written list of three things to fix. Everything you spend after that point is aimed at that list rather than at the syllabus in order.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: One lesson, no card, no obligation. It exists to test whether the student will talk to this particular person about physics for ninety minutes a week. A tutor who is technically excellent and whom your child will not question is a poor match and an expensive one.

process.title: An hours estimate you can argue with
process.description: After the trial the tutor says how many sessions the list needs and over what period. You are entitled to push back, to buy half of it, or to start and review in four weeks. An estimate that cannot be questioned is not an estimate.

process.title: Review against the list, then stop
process.description: Every four to six weeks the three items are checked off or rewritten. When the list is empty the sessions should end rather than renew by default. Tuition that continues because it is in the calendar is the most common way a Dubai household overspends on a subject.

whyPoints.title: The rates on this page are sourced, not implied
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here comes from a published 2026 Dubai rate table or a provider's own published price, and is presented as the market rather than as our quotation. Three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: Physics specialists rather than general science tutors
whyPoints.description: A tutor matched for Physics HL has taught the current Diploma Physics guide and marked investigations against its four criteria. A general science tutor can explain the content and cannot usually say why a Paper 2 answer scored four out of seven.

whyPoints.title: The pool is not limited to Emirates Living
whyPoints.description: Because sessions run over live video, a Springs student can work with the right Physics teacher rather than the nearest one. In a subject this thinly staffed in Dubai, that difference is larger than any rate difference on this page.

whyPoints.title: The assessment boundary is stated before you ask
whyPoints.description: Teaching, review and feedback on the student's own investigation; never drafting, designing or producing it. Two providers ranking in this market sell completed internal assessments. That is an expulsion risk for the student, and we will not take the booking.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around an Emirates Living week
whyPoints.description: Sessions sit in Gulf Standard Time after the school-bus return, move for Ramadan timings, and pause for study leave if that is what the week needs. No travel is priced into the hour because nobody is driving anywhere.

whyPoints.title: We say when nobody is available
whyPoints.description: If no Higher Level Physics specialist is free at the hour you need, you are told that, with the alternative and its rate named before any trial. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: What should I expect to pay per hour for IB Physics help in The Springs?
faqs.answer: Published 2026 Dubai rate tables put qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB or A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home one-to-one sits higher, at AED 180 to 350, because travel is priced inside the hour. Those are market figures from published sources, not our quotation. What actually decides your total is the number of hours, and that is set by whether the problem is content, paper technique or an unstarted investigation. Take the free trial and ask the tutor for an hours estimate before you compare rates with anyone.

faqs.question: Is Physics more expensive to tutor than other Diploma subjects in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not by rate, but often by availability. The published AED bands are the same across subjects at the same level. What differs is the size of the specialist pool. Higher Level Physics teachers are a small group in Dubai, and in a market where the International Baccalaureate accounts for seven per cent of a 387,441-student private sector, that scarcity shows up as waiting time and as a thinner choice in February than in October. Families who book Physics support early pay the standard band; families who book late choose from whoever is still free, usually at the top of it.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Physics HL student in Emirates Living usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which component is failing, which is why an estimate without a diagnostic is guesswork. As rough shapes: a scientific investigation steered from a blank page takes four to six sessions across the drafting window. A Paper 2 technique rebuild before a May series takes twelve to twenty. Repairing a whole theme from the ground up takes longer than either. A student who is broadly fine and wants maintenance needs fortnightly contact, not weekly. Ask for the three things being fixed in writing, then count hours against that list rather than against the course.

faqs.question: Why does the investigation matter so much to the money I spend?
faqs.answer: Because it is twenty per cent of the Physics grade, it is finished long before the papers, and it is the component a student controls most. It is one report with a 3,000-word ceiling, judged against four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design is where marks go missing, usually through a research question with no genuinely controllable independent variable. Fixing that in September costs one conversation. Discovering it in March costs a block of hours and still cannot recover the marks, because the data has already been collected.

faqs.question: Can a cheaper tutor at AED 100 an hour do the job for my child?
faqs.answer: For some jobs, yes. Below roughly AED 150 an hour the Dubai market is mostly university students who know the physics and have not marked to an IB criterion. That is genuinely useful for unblocking homework, for MYP science catch-up, or for drilling Paper 1 speed. It is poor value for Paper 2 extended response, where the skill being bought is knowing what a command term demands, and for investigation supervision, where the skill is reading a draft against published criteria. Match the band to the job rather than to the budget, and the total often comes out lower.

faqs.question: Do you teach Physics at our townhouse in Springs 4?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. Physics sessions for Springs households are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for diagrams, graph work and marked scripts. For a subject that lives on annotated diagrams and worked algebra, a shared screen is closer to how a Physics teacher works at a board than a notebook on a dining table is. It also means the tutor is chosen for Physics rather than for proximity to Emirates Living.

faqs.question: Why are in-home Physics rates in Dubai higher if the teaching is the same?
faqs.answer: Because the rate carries the drive. Published Dubai tables put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with some home tutors advertised to AED 500, and the premium over online rates is travel, vehicle and dead time either side of the lesson. There is a second cost that never appears on an invoice: choosing in-home filters the candidate list down to Physics teachers who can reach Emirates Living inside a tolerable drive. In a subject with this small a specialist pool, that filter removes most of the people you actually wanted to consider.

faqs.question: My child scores well in class tests and badly on Paper 2. What is that worth fixing?
faqs.answer: A great deal, because Paper 2 is forty-four per cent of the grade and it is the most trainable component on the course. The pattern you are describing is almost always technique rather than knowledge: answers written to 'describe' when the question says 'explain', reasoning left in the student's head, working not shown, and the last two questions unreached because earlier ones were over-answered. That is a small number of targeted sessions with marked timed practice, not a re-teach of five themes. Insist on a marked diagnostic first so the hours go where the marks are.

faqs.question: Are small-group Physics classes in Dubai better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes. Per mark, usually not. A group moves at its median student, and Physics failures are rarely median: one student cannot propagate uncertainties, another cannot read a field diagram, a third writes extended response as bullet points. A sixteen-week group course at a reduced per-head rate frequently costs a household more in total than eight well-aimed individual sessions, and moves less. Groups do work for structured content coverage where several students genuinely share the same gap. Ask what the group is covering week by week before assuming the saving is real.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma should we start paying for Physics support?
faqs.answer: Earlier and lighter beats later and heavier. DP1 support is preventive and cheap: fortnightly sessions, a mathematics check against the calculus the course assumes, and an early conversation about the investigation's research question. DP2 support is corrective and dear: weekly sessions, a paper-technique block, and whatever the investigation did not get finished. Households that spend modestly through DP1 generally spend less across the two years, because the expensive work is the work that has to be done against a fixed deadline with no room left to move.

faqs.question: Does school fee pressure in Dubai change what tutoring is worth this year?
faqs.answer: It changes the framing. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate do not rise for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a Springs household, that means a tutoring decision this year is about new spending rather than about absorbing a fee increase, which is a cleaner decision to make. It is also a reason to use the school's own after-hours support first: it is already paid for inside fees and is the single most underused resource in this market.

faqs.question: Will you put the Physics exam dates on this page so I can plan?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is worth knowing. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any session or results date we printed would be second-hand, and a second-hand date on an examinations page is a liability rather than a service. UAE schools sit the May series as the main session, with November available. The authoritative calendar for your child, including internal upload deadlines, comes from the school's Diploma coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson publish theirs openly, which is why the dates quoted on this page are theirs rather than the IB's.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Physics Extended Essay without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that should be stated before you book. A tutor can explain what the assessment criteria reward, press on whether a research question is answerable with a measurable experiment, question the method, read drafts the student has written and say where the reasoning fails. A tutor cannot choose the question, design the experiment, process the data or write any part of the essay. We do not offer those things and will not take a booking that asks for them, because the consequence lands on the student and it is far larger than one subject grade.

faqs.question: How do I check that a Physics tutor is allowed to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask for the permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Because it costs nothing, a tutor without one has no financial excuse. Operating without it brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount quoted at you with scepticism. Ask separately which school a teaching tutor works at.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level Physics specialist is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: You are told that plainly, which is not what this market usually does. Higher Level Physics is a thin pool in Dubai and there are weeks, particularly from January, when nobody is free at a Springs family's preferred hour. In that case we name the options: wait for a slot, take a different time, or work with a specialist based outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time, identified as such with the rate stated before the free trial. What we will not do is match a general science tutor at a specialist rate and let you discover the difference in a mock.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-springs.closingHeading: Start with a number of hours, not a rate card
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-springs.closingBody: The useful question for a Springs household is not what a Physics hour costs in Dubai. It is how many hours this particular student needs, aimed at which three weaknesses, and finishing on which date. Tell us the school, the level and what the last marked paper said, and we will match a Physics specialist who has taught that course. The trial lesson is free and takes no card. After it you get an estimate of hours you are welcome to argue with, a short written list of what those hours are for, and a date when the plan should end rather than quietly renew.
