dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-sustainabl.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB physics at Higher and Standard Level to students in The Sustainable City and the wider Dubailand belt. Each is listed by the level they teach to examination, because the Higher Level extensions in fields and quantum physics are where a general science tutor stops being useful.

intro.heading: Two different problems both look like a physics problem
paragraphs: When a Diploma physics grade stalls, there are usually two candidate explanations and they need different tutors. Either the student does not have the physics — the mechanism, the model, the conditions under which an equation applies — or the student has the physics and loses marks in the mathematics wrapped around it: rearranging before substituting, powers of ten, uncertainty, gradients from a graph that is not quite linear. Those are both fixable, and treating one as the other wastes a term.

The distinction is diagnosable in about two sessions, from a marked paper and a few questions attempted in front of a tutor. Students whose physics marks improve sharply after what looks like mathematics tutoring never had a physics problem; they had an arithmetic one that surfaced under time pressure. Conversely, a student fluent in the algebra who cannot say why a field is conservative has a physics problem that more practice questions will not touch.

The current Diploma physics course is organised into five themes, running from space, time and motion, through the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour and fields, to nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level extends several of them substantially. Assessment is two written papers, one of which includes a data-based section, plus the scientific investigation, which is 20% of the final grade at both levels. Syllabus structures are revised, so confirm the current arrangement with your child's subject teacher rather than taking it from any website.

That 20% changes the timing of everything. The investigation is designed, carried out and written by the student, to a school deadline that sits months before the examinations. A family that engages a physics tutor in the second term of the second Diploma year is too late to affect a fifth of the grade. In The Sustainable City, where most Diploma students attend the IB continuum school inside the community and share one subject teacher, that deadline tends to arrive for the whole cohort at once.

Delivery is online, stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at an address in this community. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard for working, diagrams and graph sketches, and screen-shared past-paper questions. Household visits exist in our India operation only. For physics the loss is minimal, because what a tutor needs to see is the line of working where the student stopped being sure. The format also removes the two car journeys either side of a visit, which is why a session can run while a student is still able to concentrate on an uncertainty calculation, and why the tutor can be chosen for the level they teach rather than for the distance they are prepared to drive down Al Qudra Road at five in the afternoon.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-sustainabl.programmesIntro: Physics is taught here across three stages, and the preparation that makes Higher Level viable happens before the Diploma begins. These are the stages and what each one actually demands.

programmes.name: Middle Years sciences
programmes.description: Assessed on four criteria covering knowledge and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The inquiry and processing criteria are where the skills the Diploma investigation examines at 20% are first built, and they are the criteria capable students most often neglect in favour of content recall.
programmes.countryNote: In a continuum school such as the one inside The Sustainable City, MYP science grades inform the Diploma level decision. A student aiming at Higher Level physics needs the processing and evaluating criterion marks rather than only the knowledge one, because that criterion is the direct ancestor of the investigation's data-analysis assessment.

programmes.name: Physics at Standard Level
programmes.description: Covers all five themes at core depth, with two written papers and the scientific investigation at 20%. Most Standard Level students who underperform do so on explanation questions rather than calculations: they describe what happens accurately and never name the mechanism that makes it happen, which is what the command term explain requires.
programmes.countryNote: Standard Level physics is a common choice for Dubai students heading towards medicine, architecture or economics who want a quantitative science without the Higher Level load. It is still a demanding course, and the data-based section of the written paper assumes graph and uncertainty skills many students have not practised deliberately.

programmes.name: Physics at Higher Level
programmes.description: Extends several themes substantially, with fields and nuclear and quantum physics carrying the heaviest additional load. The mathematical demand rises sharply, which is why Higher Level physics and Higher Level Analysis and Approaches are so often taken together and why students taking Higher Level physics with Standard Level mathematics feel the strain by the second term.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families usually choose Higher Level physics with engineering, physical sciences or medicine in view. Published university requirements differ and are revised, so read the admissions pages of the specific institutions on the shortlist rather than relying on general advice, and check whether a minimum grade rather than just the subject is specified.

programmes.name: IGCSE or MYP science into Diploma physics
programmes.description: The step into Diploma physics is steep in two specific places: the mathematics becomes continuous rather than arithmetical, and explanations must name mechanisms rather than describe outcomes. A student who scored well at IGCSE by memorising standard answers finds the first term of the Diploma genuinely difficult, and that is usually a method problem rather than a capability one.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving between communities in this belt frequently change schools and boards at once, so a student may arrive in the first Diploma year from a different science sequence with two or three unmet topics. A short bridging block in the first term is far cheaper than remediation in the examination year.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-sustainabl.subjectsIntro: What follows is the content map by theme, with the specific thing that costs marks in each. An enquiry that names a theme and a question type gets a better first session than one describing general difficulty.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, and at Higher Level more demanding treatment including rotational and relativistic ideas depending on the current syllabus. Marks are lost on sign conventions in momentum questions and on energy arguments that omit the system boundary being considered.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, and the kinetic model. The recurring failure is mixing temperature and internal energy in explanations, and using the ideal gas relationship without checking which quantities are being held constant in the situation described.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Oscillations, wave models, superposition, standing waves and, at Higher Level, further treatment of interference and diffraction. Students lose marks drawing diagrams that are approximately right: a standing wave with the wrong number of nodes earns nothing even when the explanation is correct.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, circuits, and electromagnetic induction, with substantial Higher Level extension. Circuit questions are where Standard Level students most often go wrong, usually by treating a potential divider as a series of independent components.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactivity, nuclear reactions, and quantum ideas including the photoelectric effect, with Higher Level going considerably further. Explanation questions here reward precise language about photons and energy levels, and lose marks for descriptions that could equally apply to a wave model.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade, designed and written by the student and marked against published criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The most common cause of a weak mark is a research question too broad to be answered by the data the student can realistically collect.

subjects.name: Data analysis and the data-based paper section
subjects.description: Graph work, gradients, intercepts, uncertainty bars and judging whether a relationship is linear. This section rewards students who have practised reading data they have not seen before, and it is the part of the paper most often left unrehearsed because it cannot be revised by rereading notes.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error treatment
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and significant figures that reflect the precision of the measurement. It is examined throughout rather than as a topic, which is exactly why students never revise it and why it costs marks in every paper.

subjects.name: The mathematics inside physics
subjects.description: Rearranging before substituting, powers of ten, logarithms where the syllabus requires them, trigonometry in resolving vectors, and gradients from curved graphs. A substantial share of lost physics marks are mathematical, which is a diagnosable distinction rather than a guess.

subjects.name: Chemistry and mathematics alongside physics
subjects.description: Students taking physics usually take at least one of these too, and the overlap is real: energetics calculations and uncertainty treatment transfer directly. Sequencing tutoring across two sciences in the same term is usually a mistake, and the reason is set out later on this page.

sections.heading: The five themes and where each one loses marks
paragraphs: Physics is a subject where the examiner's requirements are unusually explicit, and the losses cluster in predictable places within each theme. Most of them are not about missing knowledge. They are about explanations that stop one step short of the mechanism, diagrams drawn approximately, and equations applied outside the conditions under which they hold. A tutor who can name those per theme is doing something a general science tutor cannot.

The pattern worth understanding is the explanation question. A six-mark explanation in physics is marked for a chain of reasoning, and a student who writes an accurate description of the phenomenon earns the description marks only. Naming the mechanism — the force, the field, the energy transfer, the photon interaction — is what earns the remaining marks. Students find this frustrating because their answer is not wrong; it is incomplete in a way that feels arbitrary until they see a mark scheme broken down line by line against what they actually wrote.

The second pattern is conditional equation use. Physics equations hold under stated conditions: constant acceleration, ideal gas behaviour, negligible resistance, small-angle approximation. A student who applies one outside its conditions produces a confident wrong answer and often loses the marks for the reasoning as well. The table below sets this out theme by theme, so a parent can check whether sessions are addressing the actual failure or simply covering content again. If several weeks pass without any of these appearing in a session note, that is a fair question to put to the tutor.

sections.heading: Uncertainty: examined everywhere, revised nowhere
paragraphs: Uncertainty treatment is assessed throughout Diploma physics — in the data-based paper section, in the investigation, and inside ordinary calculation questions where significant figures must reflect the precision of the measurement. It is also the topic students revise least, because it is not a theme and never appears as a heading in a revision guide. The result is a steady, invisible leak of marks across every paper a student sits, and because it is spread thinly it rarely shows up as a topic anyone decides to address.

The specific failures are consistent. Absolute and percentage uncertainty are confused. Uncertainties are not propagated through multi-step calculations, so a final answer carries a precision the measurements cannot support. Significant figures are copied from a calculator display. In graph work, uncertainty bars are drawn but never used to assess whether a proposed relationship is actually supported, which is usually the question being asked.

The fix is mechanical and fast, which is what makes it good value. Three or four sessions on uncertainty, worked on the student's own investigation data rather than on textbook examples, usually eliminates the leak. It also improves the investigation mark directly, because data analysis and evaluation are two of the assessed areas. This is the clearest example in the subject of a small, specific intervention producing marks across several components at once. It is also work a parent can verify is happening, because an uncertainty session leaves visible traces in the student's own processed data rather than in a general sense of having revised.

sections.heading: The mathematics that quietly costs physics marks
paragraphs: A notable share of lost physics marks are not physics losses at all. The commonest profile we see in this community is a student who understands the mechanism, selects the right equation, and then loses the mark rearranging it, mishandling a power of ten, or resolving a vector with the wrong trigonometric ratio. Under timed conditions those slips multiply, and the student concludes they are bad at physics when they are in fact slow at algebra.

This matters for how a family spends money. A student in this situation does not need more physics teaching; they need three or four weeks of dense manipulation practice in physics contexts. That is cheaper, faster and more measurable than a term of content review. It is also why we ask for a marked paper before the first session: the distinction between a physics gap and a mathematics gap is visible in the working, and it is not visible in a conversation.

Higher Level students taking Standard Level mathematics are the group most at risk. The Higher Level physics extensions in fields and quantum physics assume comfort with manipulation that Standard Level mathematics does not drill to the same depth. That combination is workable, and it is the single most common reason a capable Higher Level physics student stalls in the second term. Identifying it early turns it into a scheduling decision rather than a crisis, and it is one of the first things a diagnostic session is designed to establish.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation is a fifth of the grade
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of a Diploma physics grade comes from the student's own investigation, marked against published criteria covering research design, data collection and processing, analysis and conclusion, and evaluation. It is submitted to a school deadline months before the examinations. That single fact should reorder a family's thinking about when physics tutoring is worth buying, and it almost never does, because nobody tells parents until the deadline is close.

The dominant cause of a weak mark is scope. A research question that cannot be answered by the data a school laboratory and a sixteen-year-old can realistically produce generates thin analysis, however good the physics behind it. Testing feasibility is therefore the highest-value session in the whole engagement, and it happens before any data is collected. Students who get this stage right frequently need very little help afterwards.

The boundary on what a tutor may do is strict and we state it rather than leaving it vague. A tutor may teach the underlying physics, explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a method is reproducible, press on whether a conclusion follows from the data, teach uncertainty treatment on the student's own measurements, and comment on writing the student produced. A tutor may not design the investigation, collect or supply data, write or rewrite any part of the report, or provide a model to adapt. Operations in this market sell completed internal assessments; that is academic misconduct and the student carries the consequence.

sections.heading: Higher Level or Standard Level physics, and the mathematics pairing
paragraphs: The level decision in physics is unusually consequential because of its interaction with mathematics. Higher Level physics extends several themes substantially, with fields and nuclear and quantum physics carrying most of the additional load, and the mathematical demand rises with them. A student taking Higher Level physics alongside Higher Level Analysis and Approaches has the tools the course assumes. A student pairing it with Standard Level mathematics is doing something harder than the syllabus documents suggest.

That is not an argument against the pairing, which many students manage well. It is an argument for noticing it in the first term rather than the fourth. The signal is specific: a student who understands the lesson and cannot complete the problem set at speed is hitting a mathematical ceiling, not a physics one. Three or four weeks of manipulation work at that point usually resolves it, while the same situation discovered a year later is a much larger repair.

On university requirements, the honest position is that it varies. Engineering and physical science degrees commonly expect Higher Level physics, sometimes with a minimum grade; medicine varies substantially by country; and many quantitative economics or computer science routes care more about the mathematics. Published requirements change, so read the admissions pages of the specific institutions on the shortlist early enough to act, rather than relying on general guidance including ours. Whether Higher Level physics can be timetabled alongside Higher Level mathematics at your child's school is also worth asking early, because in smaller cohorts it occasionally cannot.

sections.heading: What physics tutoring costs, and the three-science trap
paragraphs: Published Dubai market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider advertising AED 650. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65, and in-home visits AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included. Those figures belong to the companies and rate guides that published them, read in October 2026.

The trap in a science-heavy Diploma is arithmetic rather than pedagogical. A student taking three sciences has three investigations and three sets of papers, and a family that engages a tutor per subject arrives at three hours a week plus mathematics. At the mid-market online rate, that is a monthly figure well above what most households intend to spend, and more importantly it is more between-session work than a Diploma student carrying six subjects and the core can complete. The result is three half-used engagements.

The better structure is sequencing. Identify which subject's investigation deadline falls first and which subject's marks are furthest from target, address those, and rotate. One subject at a time, properly used, outperforms three subjects partially used, and it costs a third as much in any given month. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, which makes the arithmetic of restraint fairly clear.

sections.heading: What a tutor may not do, and what the regulators actually govern
paragraphs: The academic honesty line in physics is the same as elsewhere and worth repeating because the investigation makes it tempting. A tutor teaches, explains criteria, questions method and reasoning, and comments on the student's own writing. A tutor does not design investigations, supply data, write or redraft reports, or provide specimens to adapt. One operation in this market sells completed internal assessments at AED 3,750; buying one is misconduct under IB rules and the candidate carries the consequence, not the seller.

On materials, IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the IB's copyright. We reference and cite them and work from what the school legitimately holds, with questions shown on screen during sessions. A service advertising an unlimited paper bank invites a fair question about provenance. We also do not describe tutors as IB examiners unless current examiner status can be evidenced, a claim made frequently in this market and rarely supported.

On regulators, the position is narrow. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education covers Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram holds no permit, approval or partnership from any of them, nor from the IB, and has no UAE office. An individual tutoring privately in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: When a physics session should actually happen
paragraphs: Physics punishes fatigue more than most subjects, because a tired student makes manipulation errors and uncertainty slips that teach the wrong lesson when they are reviewed. Session timing is therefore a real variable. A student at school inside The Sustainable City can start at 3.30pm and still think clearly; one travelling back from Motor City or Al Barsha is not realistically available until 5.30pm, and the value of an hour drops noticeably after seven in the evening.

The UAE week pushes certain work to the weekend. Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday leaves Saturday and Sunday as the only full days, which is why investigation work and whole-paper practice usually belong there: both need an uninterrupted block rather than a squeezed hour. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and the useful window moves after Iftar, where a physics session is frequently more productive than any afternoon slot in that month.

Our side is straightforward. Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time, move after Iftar through Ramadan with the same tutor, and can pause during a school's own examination fortnight where adding sessions produces fatigue rather than marks. We do not rotate students between tutors to fill a diary. In physics the tutor's accumulated knowledge of whether a given student's errors are mathematical or conceptual is most of the value, and rebuilding it with somebody new takes several weeks. That is why we would rather hold one protected slot across a whole term than fill a diary with sessions that keep being moved.

process.title: Send the level and a marked paper
process.description: Higher or Standard Level, which mathematics course your child takes alongside it, and a photograph of recently marked work. That combination usually tells us whether the problem is physics or the mathematics inside it, which decides which tutor we approach first.

The answer changes the priority order completely, because the investigation is 20% of the grade and its deadline is set by the school rather than by the examination timetable, usually months earlier than families expect.

process.description: You receive a plan that names syllabus themes and assessed components rather than describing general improvement, with the between-session work and the date everything counts back from. Named themes mean you can check whether sessions are doing what the plan said.

process.description: Each note records whether the session's errors were conceptual, mathematical, uncertainty-related or technique. Over a month the pattern either thins or it does not, and if it does not we change the method or the tutor rather than quietly adding hours.

whyPoints.description: A large share of lost physics marks are mathematical, and the two problems need different work. We diagnose which from a marked paper before the first session, because treating an algebra problem as a physics problem wastes a term and a considerable amount of money.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainty taught as a subject in its own right
whyPoints.description: It is examined in every paper and in the investigation and revised by almost nobody, which makes three or four focused sessions on it the best value available in the course. The gain shows up in both the written papers and the internal mark.

whyPoints.title: The investigation treated as 20%
whyPoints.description: Because that is what it is worth, at both levels, to a school deadline months before the examinations. We start with whether the research question can be answered by data a student can realistically collect, which is what decides most of the mark.

whyPoints.description: A student taking three sciences cannot absorb three tutored hours a week alongside six subjects and the core. We will say which subject to address first and rotate, because three partially used engagements cost three times as much and achieve less.

whyPoints.description: IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE. Lessons are one-to-one over live video with a shared whiteboard, which for physics costs almost nothing and buys a tutor chosen for the level they teach rather than the distance they can drive.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's problem is physics or maths?
faqs.answer: From a marked paper rather than a conversation, because the distinction is visible in the working. If the mechanism is identified and the right equation selected but the mark is lost in rearranging, a power of ten, or a trigonometric ratio, the problem is mathematical and three to four weeks of manipulation practice in physics contexts usually fixes it. If the student cannot say why an effect happens, the problem is conceptual and needs theme teaching. Treating one as the other costs a term, which is why we ask for marked work before the first session.

faqs.question: How is the Diploma physics syllabus organised now, and what is examined?
faqs.answer: The current syllabus is organised into space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics, with Higher Level extending several of them substantially, most heavily in fields and in nuclear and quantum work. Assessment is two written papers, one including a data-based section, plus the scientific investigation at 20% of the grade. The IB does revise courses, so confirm the current structure and paper arrangements with your child's subject teacher rather than relying on any website.

faqs.question: Why does uncertainty cost so many marks?
faqs.answer: Because it is examined everywhere and revised nowhere. Uncertainty appears in the data-based paper section, inside ordinary calculation questions through significant figures, and twice over in the investigation's data analysis and evaluation. It is not a theme, so it never appears as a heading in a revision guide and students skip it. The failures are consistent: absolute and percentage uncertainty confused, uncertainty not propagated through multi-step calculations, and uncertainty bars drawn on a graph but never used to judge whether a relationship is supported.

faqs.question: How much of the physics grade is the internal investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent at both Higher and Standard Level. It is designed, carried out and written by the student and marked against published criteria covering research design, data collection and processing, analysis and conclusion, and evaluation. Critically, it is submitted to a school deadline that sits months before the examinations, so a family engaging a tutor in the final terms has already lost the chance to influence a fifth of the grade. If you are deciding when physics tutoring is worth buying, that weighting argues for the first Diploma year.

faqs.question: My son takes Higher Level physics with Standard Level maths. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is workable and it is harder than the syllabus documents suggest. The Higher Level extensions in fields and in nuclear and quantum physics assume manipulation fluency that Standard Level mathematics does not drill to the same depth. The signal to watch for is a student who follows the lesson perfectly and then completes the problem set slowly: that is a mathematical ceiling, not a physics one. Noticed in the first term it is three or four weeks of work; noticed in the fourth it is a much larger repair.

faqs.question: Why do explanation questions score so badly even when the answer is right?
faqs.answer: Because a physics explanation is marked for a chain of reasoning and most students stop one step short of the mechanism. An accurate description of what happens earns the description marks; naming the force, the field, the energy transfer or the photon interaction is what earns the remaining marks. Students find this arbitrary until they see their own answer against a broken-down mark scheme, at which point it usually clicks. It is one of the fastest improvements available, because the physics is already understood.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with a laboratory-based investigation?
faqs.answer: With everything except the laboratory work itself, which belongs to the school. A tutor can test whether the research question is answerable with data your child can realistically collect, teach the uncertainty and processing treatment using the student's own measurements, explain what each assessed criterion rewards, question whether a conclusion follows, and comment on writing the student produced. A tutor must not design the investigation, supply data, or write any part of the report. In practice the feasibility conversation before any data is collected is where most of the value sits.

faqs.question: Should we tutor physics and chemistry at the same time?
faqs.answer: Usually not in the same term. A student taking three sciences has three investigations and three sets of papers, and three tutored hours a week on top of six subjects and the core means the between-session work is the first thing dropped. The better structure is sequencing: address the subject whose investigation deadline falls first or whose marks are furthest from target, then rotate. One subject properly used beats three partially used, and it costs a third as much in any given month.

faqs.question: What should we budget for physics tutoring for one Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Published figures put qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IB from AED 200, and IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included. Bestimate's monthly estimate for one weekly hour is AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not our prices; we quote after a free trial for the actual level.

faqs.question: Is the data-based section of the paper worth practising separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the section most often left unrehearsed, because it cannot be revised by rereading notes. It asks a student to read data they have not seen before, judge whether a relationship is linear, extract a gradient and intercept with their physical meaning, and use uncertainty bars to decide whether a proposed relationship is supported. The only preparation that works is repeated practice on unfamiliar data sets, which is why every session in a technique block here includes one.

faqs.question: My daughter came from IGCSE physics with a grade 8 and is now struggling. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the method changed, not because the capability did. IGCSE physics rewards well-learned standard answers; Diploma physics requires explanations that name mechanisms and mathematics that is continuous rather than arithmetical. A student who scored highly by memorising responses finds the first Diploma term genuinely hard, and reads that as a loss of ability. It is a method problem and it resolves within a term with explanation drills and manipulation practice. Recognising it early prevents a confidence problem turning into a subject-choice regret.

faqs.question: Do you provide IB physics past papers or data booklets?
faqs.answer: No. IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, data booklets and grade-boundary tables are the IB's copyright. We reference them, cite the official source, and work from material your child's school legitimately holds, with questions shown on screen during sessions. A service advertising an unlimited paper bank raises a fair question about provenance, and occasionally about whether material has been released at all. The school's own holdings are also what your child will be marked against.

faqs.question: Are your physics tutors IB examiners?
faqs.answer: We do not make that claim, because current examiner status is rarely verifiable and it is widely asserted in this market without support. What we will tell you about any tutor is which level they teach, how long they have taught it to examination, and what they have taught recently. Examiner status is also sometimes used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content, which it does not confer. If a provider leans on the examiner label, asking how the status is evidenced is a reasonable question.

faqs.question: How long does it take for physics marks to move?
faqs.answer: For a mathematical cause, three to four weeks, because manipulation improves with repetition and shows up directly in the next marked paper. For uncertainty, often faster, since two or three focused sessions eliminate a leak that was costing marks on every paper. Conceptual gaps take one to three weeks per theme. Investigation work is judged against criteria rather than marks until the school assesses it. Session notes record which error class appeared, so the trend is in the record rather than in impressions.

faqs.question: Can sessions be held at a weekend instead of after school?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some work a weekend is better. Investigation sessions and whole-paper practice need an uninterrupted block rather than a squeezed hour, so Saturday or Sunday suits them, particularly for households commuting out of this community where nobody is realistically free before 5.30pm on a school day. Weekday sessions are better for short, frequent fluency work. Naming the problem first makes the choice obvious, and the slot stays held in Gulf Standard Time either way.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-sustainabl.closingHeading: Level, mathematics course, and where the investigation stands
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-sustainabl.closingBody: Three facts get the first session right: Higher or Standard Level, which mathematics course your child takes alongside it, and whether the scientific investigation is unstarted, drafted or submitted. Add a photograph of recently marked work and the diagnosis is usually complete before anyone speaks. Next is a free trial lesson on an unfamiliar question in the weakest theme, with the tutor who would continue, then a written plan naming themes and components. Lessons run one-to-one over live video into The Sustainable City in Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE. If the loss turns out to be mathematical, we will say so.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-valley.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB physics at Higher and Standard Level to students living in The Valley and along the Al Ain road. Each is listed by the level they teach to examination, and each plan is built backwards from the school's own deadlines rather than from the examination timetable alone.

intro.heading: A fifth of the grade is settled before anyone sits a paper
paragraphs: The most useful thing a parent can know about Diploma physics is that the scientific investigation is 20% of the final grade at both Higher and Standard Level, and that it is submitted to a school deadline months before the examinations. That single fact reorders everything about when physics tutoring is worth buying. A family who engages a tutor in the second term of the second Diploma year is too late to influence a fifth of the result, however good the tutor is.

So this page is organised around time. It sets out what each stage of the two Diploma years requires: when a research question has to be scoped, when the data has to actually exist, when the draft is due, where the mock block sits, and what the final eight weeks can and cannot deliver. It also covers the level decision, which has its own deadline, and the mathematics pairing that decides whether a Higher Level physics student will cope with the problem sets.

The Valley adds a practical constraint. This is a newer community on the road to Al Ain with no school inside its own boundary at the time of writing, so students here travel outward in two directions and attend several different schools. Those schools teach the five syllabus themes in different orders and set their own investigation deadlines, which means neighbours are frequently at different points in the same course and a family has to work from its own school's calendar.

The course itself is organised into five themes, running from space, time and motion, through the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour and fields, to nuclear and quantum physics, with Higher Level extending several of them substantially. Assessment is two written papers, one including a data-based section, plus the internal investigation. Syllabus structures are revised, so confirm the current arrangement with your child's subject teacher rather than taking it from any website, including this one.

Delivery is stated plainly rather than implied: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard for working, diagrams and graph sketches, and past-paper questions on screen. Household visits exist in our India operation only. For physics the format loses very little, because what a tutor needs to see is the line of working where the student stopped being sure. The format also removes the two car journeys either side of a visit, which in a household where the school run has already taken an hour from the day is the difference between a session a student can use and one they merely attend.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-valley.programmesIntro: Four stages, each with a different job and a different deadline. The commonest expensive error in physics is buying the final-term version of the work when the investigation stage was the one that mattered.

programmes.name: Middle Years sciences
programmes.description: Four assessed criteria covering knowledge and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The design and processing criteria are the direct ancestors of the Diploma investigation, and they are the ones capable students neglect in favour of content recall, which later costs them in the 20% component.
programmes.countryNote: Valley students reach the Middle Years at several different schools, so the timing of criterion-marked tasks differs between neighbours. A student aiming at Higher Level physics should be watching the processing and evaluating criterion marks rather than the knowledge one, because that is where the skills the Diploma assesses at 20% are first built.

programmes.name: The first Diploma year
programmes.description: Content begins across the themes and, critically, the investigation is scoped and often carried out. This is the year in which everything is still available: content, the investigation, and the level decision itself. It is also the year most families do not engage a tutor, which is why so many physics problems arrive at the point when they are hardest to solve.
programmes.countryNote: Schools in the two travel directions from The Valley set their investigation deadlines at different points in the year, and some front-load data collection into the first year while others do not. Ask your own school for the investigation timeline in the first term, because by the second term the scoping decision has usually already been made.

programmes.name: The second Diploma year
programmes.description: Remaining content, the investigation submission, the mock block, then study leave and the examinations. In this year almost all available improvement is in the written papers: explanation technique, uncertainty treatment, the data-based section and pacing. The investigation, once submitted, is banked and outside what any tutor can affect.
programmes.countryNote: For Valley students the commute makes the second year harder to schedule than the first. One protected weekday evening plus a weekend block is the structure that survives, and the weekend block is where the data-based paper section and whole-paper rehearsal belong because both need uninterrupted time.

programmes.name: Into Diploma physics from IGCSE or MYP
programmes.description: Two things change at once: the mathematics becomes continuous rather than arithmetical, and explanations must name mechanisms instead of describing outcomes. A student who scored highly at IGCSE by learning standard answers finds the first Diploma term genuinely hard, which is a method problem rather than a loss of ability and resolves within a term once named.
programmes.countryNote: Because families move into The Valley from across Dubai and from abroad, a student may begin the first Diploma year from a different science sequence entirely, with two or three unmet topics. A short diagnostic in the first term is far cheaper than remediation in the examination year, and it also establishes whether the mathematics pairing will hold.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-valley.subjectsIntro: The content map by theme, with the specific place marks go in each. An enquiry naming a theme and a question type produces a far better first session than one describing general difficulty with physics.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, with Higher Level extending the treatment. Marks go missing on sign conventions in momentum questions and on energy arguments that never state which system is being considered, so the examiner cannot follow the reasoning.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws and the kinetic model. The recurring failure is conflating temperature and internal energy in explanations, and using the ideal gas relationship without checking which quantities the question holds constant.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Oscillations, wave models, superposition and standing waves, with further interference and diffraction work at Higher Level. Diagrams that are approximately right earn nothing: a standing wave with the wrong number of nodes loses the mark even alongside a correct explanation.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, circuits and electromagnetic induction, with substantial Higher Level extension. Circuit questions cost Standard Level students the most, usually because a potential divider is treated as a series of independent components.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactivity, nuclear reactions and quantum ideas including the photoelectric effect, extended considerably at Higher Level. Explanation questions reward precise language about photons and energy levels and lose marks for descriptions that would suit a wave model equally well.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade, designed and written by the student against published criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The usual cause of a weak mark is a research question too broad to be answered by the data a student can realistically collect.

subjects.name: The data-based paper section
subjects.description: Graph work, gradients and intercepts with their physical meaning, uncertainty bars, and judging whether a proposed relationship is supported. It cannot be revised by rereading notes, which is exactly why it is the part of the paper most often left unrehearsed.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error treatment
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and significant figures that reflect measurement precision. It is examined throughout rather than as a topic, which is why students never revise it and why it leaks marks on every paper.

subjects.name: The mathematics inside physics
subjects.description: Rearranging before substituting, powers of ten, trigonometry in resolving vectors, logarithms where required, and gradients from curved graphs. A notable share of lost physics marks are mathematical, which is diagnosable from marked work rather than a matter of opinion.

subjects.name: Mathematics and chemistry alongside physics
subjects.description: Most physics students take at least one of these, and the overlap in uncertainty treatment and data handling is direct. Tutoring two sciences in the same term is usually a mistake in a commuting household, because the between-session work for both will not be completed.

sections.heading: The two Diploma years for physics, in order
paragraphs: Physics has a distinctive shape among Diploma subjects because one component carries 20% and is finished long before the rest. Everything else follows from that. The first year is where the investigation is scoped and usually carried out, where the level decision is still open, and where content coverage begins across the themes. The second year is remaining content, the submission, the mock block, then papers. Those are different years requiring different work, and conflating them is how money gets spent badly.

The deadline sequence is set by the school rather than by the IB, which matters practically in this community. Schools in the two travel directions from The Valley set their investigation timelines at different points, some front-loading data collection into the first year and others leaving it later. A family here cannot infer the schedule from a neighbour; it has to ask its own school, ideally in the first term when the information is still actionable.

The table below is the order of events with what should already be done at each point. It is deliberately written in stages rather than months, because dates differ by school and the IB revises its own arrangements. What does not change is the logic: scope before collecting, collect before analysing, analyse before writing, and finish writing before the mock block rather than during it. Families who follow that order rarely need an emergency engagement later, and the ones who do not usually arrive asking for help with a component that has already closed.

sections.heading: The investigation, stage by stage, and what a tutor may do at each
paragraphs: Because this component is a fifth of the grade and the commonest source of avoidable loss, it is worth setting out properly. It is marked against published criteria covering research design, data collection and processing, analysis and conclusion, and evaluation. The dominant cause of a weak mark is scope: a question that cannot be answered by the data a school laboratory and a sixteen-year-old can realistically produce will generate thin analysis however sound the underlying physics.

That makes the earliest stage the most valuable. Testing a research question before any data is collected costs one or two sessions and determines most of the eventual mark, because every later criterion depends on having usable data. Students who get this stage right frequently need very little help afterwards. Students who get it wrong spend the following months processing data that cannot support a conclusion, and no amount of writing rescues that.

The boundary on tutoring is strict and we state it at each stage rather than in general. A tutor may teach the underlying physics, explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a method is reproducible, press on whether a conclusion follows from the results, teach uncertainty treatment using the student's own measurements, and comment on writing the student produced. A tutor may not design the investigation, collect or supply data, write or rewrite any part of the report, or provide a model to adapt. The table sets that boundary out stage by stage, so a parent can see exactly what legitimate help looks like at each point.

sections.heading: The level decision, and when it actually closes
paragraphs: Higher Level physics extends several themes substantially, with fields and nuclear and quantum physics carrying most of the additional load, and the mathematical demand rises with them. A student taking Higher Level physics with Higher Level Analysis and Approaches has the tools the course assumes. A student pairing it with Standard Level mathematics is attempting something harder than the syllabus documents suggest, and it is workable but should be noticed in the first term rather than the fourth.

The practical point is that this is a calendar decision as much as an academic one. Schools set their own deadlines for changing a registered level, and once the second year begins a change usually means resetting the investigation as well as the accumulated content. The signal to watch for is specific: a student who follows the lesson perfectly and then completes the problem set slowly is hitting a mathematical ceiling, not a physics one, and three or four weeks of manipulation work usually resolves it.

For families still choosing, the other decision in this community is whether to take Diploma physics at all rather than A Level Physics at one of the schools in the other travel direction. Published university requirements differ and are revised, so read the admissions pages of the specific institutions on the shortlist, and check whether a minimum grade rather than just the subject is specified. Ask the school when its level-change deadline falls, because that is the date the decision actually has to respect.

sections.heading: The final eight weeks, and what they can change
paragraphs: By the last stretch the investigation is submitted and banked, so the realistic gains are entirely in the written papers. That is not a small thing: uncertainty treatment, the data-based section, explanation technique and pacing are all improvable quickly and all tend to be under-practised, because none of them can be revised by rereading notes. A student who adds those to existing content knowledge picks up marks across every question rather than in one topic.

The highest-yield order is specific. Uncertainty first, because it leaks marks on every paper and three or four focused sessions usually stop the leak. Then the data-based section, practised on unfamiliar data every week, because the skill is reading data the student has not seen. Then explanation questions against the command term, since the difference between describing an effect and naming its mechanism is the difference between half and full marks on a large share of the paper. Pacing last, with whole papers.

What eight weeks cannot do is cover a third of a syllabus never met, and a tutor implying otherwise is selling. The honest conversation happens before the booking rather than in week six. In a commuting community the other honest point is capacity: a student with a long school run and three Higher Levels cannot absorb two tutored hours a week plus the between-session work, so one weekend block used properly beats two weekday hours half-used. The order in the table below is the one that pays, and it is deliberately not the order most families would choose instinctively.

sections.heading: Theme order, school moves and the jagged profile
paragraphs: In a community where families arrive from across Dubai and from abroad, and where children attend several different schools, the order in which physics themes are taught matters more than it would elsewhere. One school covers fields in the first year and nuclear physics in the second; another does the reverse. A student moving between them is not behind; they arrive with a jagged profile, strong in most themes and missing one or two entirely.

The remedy for a jagged profile is completely different from the remedy for being behind, and families often buy the wrong one. Being behind needs a sustained programme; a jagged profile needs one or two themes taught and the rest left alone, which is a fraction of the work. The diagnosis is straightforward: work through a mixed past paper and record which questions the student cannot start, as distinct from the ones they start and then slip in.

There is a second effect worth knowing about. A student who changes school mid-Diploma may also arrive with an investigation at a different stage from their new cohort, because schools time it differently. That is the single most urgent thing to establish after a move, ahead of any content work, because the component carries 20% and the new school's deadline may be considerably closer than the old school's would have been. Asking that question in the first week after a move costs nothing and occasionally saves a fifth of a grade.

sections.heading: What physics support costs at each stage
paragraphs: Price the stages against what is actually at stake, which in Diploma physics is the fifth of the grade sitting inside the scientific investigation. Published Dubai figures put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IB from AED 200: two scoping sessions at that band is a sum most households in The Valley would spend on a single school trip, and it is spent protecting 20% of the final grade. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, a real band for drilling definitions and a poor one for a research question nobody has approved yet. Above it sit the IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider advertising AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, and from a community this far out along the Dubai-Al Ain Road the travel is a long way from nothing. Bestimate's monthly estimate for one weekly hour is AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, which is the figure to set against a school submission deadline rather than against an examination date.

For physics the stage matters more than the rate. Two sessions scoping an investigation in the first year protect a fifth of the grade for a fraction of a term's cost, which is the best-value purchase available in the subject and the one families most often skip. A theme-teaching term costs a full monthly figure and closes content gaps. An eight-week paper block in the second year costs a similar amount and buys technique rather than content.

The arithmetic to avoid is three sciences at once. A student taking physics, chemistry and biology has three investigations and three sets of papers, and three tutored hours a week at the mid-market rate is a monthly figure most households did not intend and more between-session work than a Diploma student with a long commute can complete. Sequencing by deadline order works better and costs a third as much in any given month. All figures were read in October 2026.

sections.heading: Honesty, materials and the claims we do not make
paragraphs: The academic honesty line in physics matters because the investigation involves data and data can be fabricated. A tutor may teach, explain criteria, question method and reasoning, teach uncertainty treatment on the student's own measurements, and comment on the student's own writing. A tutor may not design investigations, supply or adjust data, write or redraft reports, or provide specimens to adapt. One operation in this market sells completed internal assessments at AED 3,750; buying one is misconduct under IB rules and the candidate carries the consequence.

On materials, IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, data booklets and grade-boundary tables are the IB's copyright. We reference and cite them and work from what the school legitimately holds, with questions shown on screen during sessions. A service advertising an unlimited paper bank invites a fair question about provenance. We also do not describe tutors as IB examiners unless current examiner status can be evidenced, a claim made frequently in this market and rarely supported.

On regulators, the position is narrow and deliberate. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with ADEK in Abu Dhabi, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram holds no permit, approval or partnership from any of them or from the IB, and no UAE office. An individual tutoring privately in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: Scheduling physics around a long school run
paragraphs: Physics punishes fatigue more than most subjects, because a tired student makes uncertainty and manipulation errors they would not otherwise make, and then those errors are reviewed as if they were real. With no school inside this community, a secondary student is realistically home around a quarter past five, and the value of an hour falls noticeably after seven in the evening. Session timing is therefore a planning variable rather than an administrative detail.

The work splits by its timing needs. Explanation practice and theme teaching work in a weekday hour. Uncertainty work, the data-based section, investigation writing and whole papers all need uninterrupted attention, which in this community genuinely exists only at the weekend. A student doing one weekday evening slot and one weekend block is running a better programme than one attempting two tired weekday hours and completing the work for neither.

The UAE calendar shapes the rest. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, leaving Saturday and Sunday as the only full days. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the useful window moves after Iftar, where a physics session is frequently better than any afternoon slot in that month. Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time, move after Iftar with the same tutor retained, and can pause during a school's own examination fortnight rather than adding sessions that produce fatigue. We also keep the same tutor across a term rather than rotating students to fill a diary, because knowing whether a particular student's errors are mathematical or conceptual takes weeks to rebuild with somebody new.

process.description: You receive a plan naming themes and components, the between-session work, and the date it counts back from, with theme teaching on a weekday and papers or investigation work at the weekend. Named components mean the plan can be checked.

whyPoints.title: The physics and the maths separated first
whyPoints.description: A large share of lost physics marks are mathematical, and the two problems need different work. We diagnose which from marked work before the first session, because treating an algebra problem as a physics problem wastes a term.

faqs.question: How much of the physics grade is settled before the examinations?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, through the scientific investigation, at both Higher and Standard Level. It is designed, carried out and written by the student and marked against published criteria covering research design, data collection and processing, analysis and conclusion, and evaluation. Critically it is submitted to a school deadline months before the papers, so a family engaging a tutor in the second Diploma year has already lost the chance to influence a fifth of the result. That weighting is the main argument for starting in the first year.

faqs.question: When should the investigation research question be decided?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most students do it, and the first useful session is about scope rather than content. A question that cannot be answered by the data a school laboratory and a sixteen-year-old can realistically produce will generate thin analysis however sound the physics behind it, and every later criterion depends on having usable data. Testing feasibility costs one or two sessions and determines most of the eventual mark. Students who get this stage right frequently need very little help afterwards.

faqs.question: Our school sets the investigation deadline differently from our neighbours'. Why?
faqs.answer: Because schools time it themselves, and in The Valley children attend several different schools in two travel directions. Some front-load data collection into the first Diploma year while others leave it considerably later. That means a neighbour's timeline carries no information about your own child's, and it is worth asking your school for the investigation schedule in the first term rather than discovering it when a draft is suddenly due. After a school move it is the first thing to establish.

faqs.question: My daughter understands the lessons but takes ages over the problem sets. What is that?
faqs.answer: Almost always a mathematical ceiling rather than a physics one, and it is the signal to watch for in Higher Level physics taken with Standard Level mathematics. The Higher Level extensions in fields and in nuclear and quantum physics assume manipulation fluency that Standard Level mathematics does not drill to the same depth. Three or four weeks of manipulation work in physics contexts usually resolves it. Noticed in the first term it is a short block; noticed in the fourth it is a much larger repair.

faqs.question: What should the last eight weeks before the papers contain?
faqs.answer: Uncertainty first, because it leaks marks on every paper and three or four sessions usually stop the leak. Then the data-based section, practised on unfamiliar data every week, because the skill is reading data the student has not seen. Then explanation questions against the command term, since naming a mechanism rather than describing an effect is the difference between half and full marks on a large share of the paper. Pacing last, with whole papers under timing.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with a laboratory investigation?
faqs.answer: With everything except the laboratory work, which belongs to the school. A tutor can test whether the research question is answerable with data your child can realistically collect, teach uncertainty recording before collection begins, teach processing and graph work on the student's own measurements, explain what each criterion rewards, and question whether a conclusion follows. A tutor must not design the investigation, supply or adjust data, or write any part of the report. The feasibility conversation before collection is where most of the value sits.

faqs.question: We changed school mid-Diploma and some physics themes are missing. How bad is that?
faqs.answer: Usually less bad than it looks, because it is a jagged profile rather than a deficit. Schools teach the five themes in different orders, so a student moving between them typically has one or two themes entirely unmet and the rest intact. The diagnosis is to work through a mixed past paper and record which questions the student cannot start at all, as distinct from those they start and then slip in. One or two themes taught is a fraction of the work a full catch-up programme would be.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting physics tutoring in the second Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Yes for the papers and no for the investigation, and the honest version of that distinction should be stated before any booking. In the second year the achievable gains are uncertainty treatment, the data-based section, explanation technique and pacing, all of which are real and all of which are usually under-practised. What is gone is any influence over the 20% component once it is submitted. A tutor promising to change that is selling, and families deserve to hear the limit first.

faqs.question: Should we tutor physics and chemistry in the same term?
faqs.answer: Usually not in a household with a long school run. A student taking three sciences has three investigations and three sets of papers, and three tutored hours a week plus the between-session work for each is more than the week holds once the commute is counted. The better structure is sequencing by deadline: address whichever subject's investigation falls first or whose marks are furthest from target, then rotate. One subject properly used beats three partially used at a third of the monthly cost.

faqs.question: Why does uncertainty cost so many marks when nobody teaches it as a topic?
faqs.answer: That is exactly why. Uncertainty is assessed throughout — in the data-based paper section, inside ordinary calculations through significant figures, and twice over in the investigation's processing and evaluation criteria — but it is not a theme, so it never appears as a heading in a revision guide and students skip it. The failures are consistent: absolute and percentage uncertainty confused, no propagation through multi-step calculations, and uncertainty bars drawn on a graph but never used to judge whether a relationship is supported.

faqs.question: How should a physics week be structured around the commute?
faqs.answer: Theme teaching and explanation practice work in a weekday evening hour after the school run. Uncertainty work, the data-based section, investigation writing and whole papers all need uninterrupted attention, which in a community with no school inside it genuinely exists only at the weekend. One weekday slot plus one weekend block is the pattern that lasts a full term here, and it produces more than two tired weekday hours with the between-session work left undone for both.

faqs.question: What does physics tutoring cost at each stage?
faqs.answer: Published rates put qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IB from AED 200 and specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 or more. Two sessions scoping the investigation is a fraction of a term's cost and protects a fifth of the grade. A theme-teaching term or an eight-week paper block each run to roughly a monthly figure of AED 600 to AED 1,200 on Bestimate's mid-market estimate. Those figures were read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Do you work from our school's data booklet and past papers?
faqs.answer: We work from what your child's school legitimately holds, with questions shown on screen during sessions, and we reference the official sources rather than distributing anything. IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, data booklets and grade-boundary tables are the IB's copyright. A service advertising an unlimited paper bank raises a fair question about provenance and occasionally about unreleased material. The school's own holdings are also what your child will be marked against, which makes them the better source in practice.

faqs.question: How will we know whether the physics sessions are working?
faqs.answer: Each session note records which error class appeared — conceptual, mathematical, uncertainty-related or technique — rather than listing topics covered. For uncertainty and technique causes the change usually appears in the next marked paper, within three or four weeks. Conceptual gaps take one to three weeks per theme. Investigation work is judged against criteria rather than marks until the school assesses it, so progress there shows as a tighter research question and a draft that survives criterion review.

faqs.question: Will a physics tutor come to our house in The Valley?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in this community. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard for working, diagrams and graph sketches, and questions on screen. Home tutoring is a service we operate in India only. For physics the format loses very little, because what a tutor needs to see is the line of working where the student stopped being sure, and that is visible either way.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-valley.closingBody: That single answer — unstarted, question chosen, data collected or submitted — decides what the first month of physics sessions should contain, because a fifth of the grade is attached to a school deadline rather than to the examination timetable. Add the level, the mathematics course taken alongside it, this term's theme and a photograph of marked work, and the diagnosis is largely complete. Next is a free trial lesson on an unfamiliar question in the weakest theme, with the tutor who would continue, then a written plan split between a weekday slot and a weekend block. Lessons run one-to-one over live video into The Valley, with no UAE home visits.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-views.tutorsIntro: Physics is the subject Views families most often come to late, usually after a disappointing mock. Tutors are matched by level and by the component losing marks, because the student who cannot handle uncertainties and the student who cannot write an explanation need different sessions.

intro.heading: The question is not who is nearby. It is who teaches the current course.
paragraphs: A parent in The Views searching for a physics tutor is usually two weeks past a report that said something like working below potential. The instinct is to find someone local and start quickly. The better first question is narrower: does this person teach the IB physics syllabus as it stands now, or the one they learned on? The course was substantially rebuilt for first teaching in 2023, with first examinations in 2025. The optional topics that used to end the course are gone. Paper 1 has been split into a multiple-choice section and a separate data-analysis section. Content is organised into five themes rather than the old topic numbering.

That matters practically rather than academically. A tutor working from pre-2025 material will spend sessions on an option your child is not studying, will prepare for a Paper 1 that no longer exists in that form, and will teach the internal assessment as though it were the old two-part model rather than the single scientific investigation marked out of twenty-four. Everything they say about physics will be true. Very little of it will be aimed at the examination your child is sitting.

The second thing worth saying plainly is that there is no reason the right person lives near Emirates Golf Club. IB physics at Higher Level is a narrow specialism. Roughly seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment sits on an IB programme at all, and of those students a minority take physics, and of those a smaller group take it at Higher Level. Filtering that pool by who can drive to a Views tower by 17:30 leaves whoever remains, which is not a method. So IB Gram matches on the subject, the level and the failing component, and the lesson arrives over live video, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. Nobody travels to a UAE address; in-home visiting is a service we run in India only.

For physics specifically, the screen is an advantage rather than a concession. Half of what a physics tutor does is drawing: a free-body diagram built up one force at a time, a field pattern sketched and corrected, a graph with a tangent drawn at the right point and the gradient read off properly. On a shared whiteboard all of that is visible, reversible and saved for the following week. A spreadsheet of experimental data can be manipulated live while the student watches the uncertainty propagate. Across a dining table, both people are drawing on the same sheet of paper upside down.

The rest of this page is written so you can test any physics tutor, ours or anyone else's. It sets out the five themes and what Higher Level adds to each. It gives the assessment model with the weightings and the durations. It names the six specific ways physics marks are lost, which is more useful than a topic list. It explains the data-based question and uncertainty arithmetic, the four criteria of the scientific investigation with their mark allocations, and the mathematics problem that sits underneath more physics failures than anything else.

It publishes no examination date. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing of that kind in this project has been verified at source, and your school's IB coordinator is the only authority worth using. It publishes no grade guarantee and claims no approval from the IB, KHDA or the Ministry of Education, because IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and holds none. Syllabus details change; confirm anything decisive against the current subject guide through the school.
