dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-views.programmesIntro: Physics appears at three points in a Views student's path, and each one is a different teaching job. The level matters more here than in almost any other Diploma subject, because Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra hours.

programmes.name: Physics, Higher Level
programmes.description: All five themes taken to the additional Higher Level depth, with the scientific investigation at 20% of the grade. Paper 1 carries 36% and is split between a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section; Paper 2 carries 44% and is extended response. Higher Level content extends each theme rather than sitting alongside it, which is why a mid-course change of level is harder in physics than in most subjects.
programmes.countryNote: The level most Views students taking physics are on, since they tend to be heading for engineering, medicine or the physical sciences. It is also the level where tutoring demand peaks in the first term of DP2, when the extended-response paper starts to separate students who understand physics from students who can write about it.

programmes.name: Physics, Standard Level
programmes.description: The same five themes at reduced depth, with the same assessment structure and the same 20% scientific investigation. Paper 1 and Paper 2 are shorter. The content is less extended but the skill demands are identical: uncertainties, graph interpretation and explanation writing are assessed in the same way.
programmes.countryNote: Frequently chosen by Views students who want a physical science without six Higher Level commitments, and the usual landing place for students who begin at Higher Level and move down during DP1. Moving in November is routine; moving in April is not, because the investigation is already under way.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, the feeder
programmes.description: Integrated or separate sciences assessed against four criteria rather than percentage marks. Students arrive in the Diploma strong on investigation design and weak on quantitative work, because criterion-based assessment rewards process and the Diploma papers reward precise calculation and precise explanation under timing.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma physics transition is a recurring request from the Emirates Living schools running the continuum. The gap is almost entirely numerical: rearranging equations, handling units and significant figures, and reading a graph quantitatively rather than describing its shape.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 before the Diploma. Both cover similar ground at a level that assumes formulas are given and used rather than derived. Neither prepares a student for the explanation demands of Diploma Paper 2, where a correct equation earns nothing without the reasoning around it.
programmes.countryNote: An Extended grade 7 in IGCSE physics is a respectable result and an unreliable predictor of Higher Level success. The variable that matters more is mathematics: a student entering Higher Level physics without comfortable algebra will struggle regardless of their physics grade, and that is the single most common pattern we see from this community.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-views.subjectsIntro: Physics rarely arrives alone on a request from The Views. These are the subjects and components most often tutored alongside it, with the specific demand each one makes.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, two papers and a scientific investigation. Marks are lost in uncertainty arithmetic, in graph work where the gradient has to answer the question asked, and above all in extended-response explanation where a student states what happens instead of why.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route that supports Higher Level physics properly. Algebraic rearrangement, calculus and function handling appear constantly inside physics questions, and a student fluent here has capacity left for the physics itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A frequent and under-discussed problem when paired with Higher Level physics at Standard Level. The modelling route does not drill algebraic manipulation to the same depth, and the shortfall shows up as apparent physics weakness in DP1.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the 2023 assessment model and the same single scientific investigation, so a student doing both has two investigations to manage in the same window. Energetics and equilibrium carry the lost marks on the chemistry side.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Also on the 2023 model. Taken by medicine candidates alongside physics and chemistry, which makes DP1 the busiest internal-assessment year any Diploma student will have and a scheduling problem as much as a teaching one.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Common pairing with Higher Level physics. The theory paper rewards precise vocabulary about data and complexity, which is the same writing discipline physics Paper 2 rewards and is often worth tutoring once for both.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Overlaps physics in materials, forces and energy, and shares the investigation-style internal assessment. Students who enjoy physics practically and struggle with its algebra often do well here, which is worth knowing at option-choice time.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Physics is the natural science students most often use as an example and most often handle badly, because they treat experimental results as certainty rather than examining how physical knowledge is justified and revised.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in physics
subjects.description: Chosen by a steady trickle of Higher Level students. The difficulty is the research question: an experimental essay needs a measurable relationship and equipment the school actually has, and most failed physics essays failed at that first decision.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: One investigation, twenty-four marks, four criteria. Students lose most on evaluation, because they list limitations instead of weighing which one actually mattered to the conclusion they reached.

sections.heading: Five themes, and what Higher Level adds to each
paragraphs: The current syllabus organises physics into five themes rather than the numbered topic list older material uses, and the optional topics that used to sit at the end of the course have been removed. For a parent the practical value of knowing this is that it gives you a way to check whether a tutor is current within about thirty seconds of conversation.

The themes run from motion and mechanics, through the particulate nature of matter and thermal physics, into wave behaviour, then fields including gravitational, electric and magnetic effects, and finally nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level does not bolt on a separate module. It extends each theme, which is why moving between levels mid-course is harder in physics than in subjects where the Higher Level content is separable. A student who drops to Standard Level in February has been studying extended material all year and has to re-sort what is and is not assessed.

Where Views students lose marks is reasonably predictable by theme. Fields is the hardest for most, because it is abstract and because the mathematics is unforgiving. Wave behaviour catches students who can recite the equations and cannot handle a phase or path-difference argument. Nuclear and quantum physics is usually taught last and revised least, which makes it a reliable source of recoverable marks late in DP2. Mechanics feels easy and is where careless loss happens, particularly in questions involving two linked bodies.

One caution, stated once and meant. Subject guides are revised, and a tutoring page is not the authority on the current specification. If a syllabus detail matters to a decision you are making, confirm it through the school's IB coordinator or the current subject guide rather than relying on this page or any other.

sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2: the assessment model with the weightings
paragraphs: Very few families can say how their child's physics grade is composed, and the composition is what tells you what kind of help is worth buying. A student losing marks in multiple choice and a student losing marks in extended response need almost opposite interventions.

Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and is in two parts. The first is multiple choice, which rewards fast, secure recall and punishes a student who tries to derive everything from first principles under time pressure. The second is a data-analysis section built on experimental results, which rewards graph work, uncertainty handling and the ability to say what a gradient physically represents. Those are two different skills inside one paper, and a student can be strong at one and weak at the other while the overall mark hides it.

Paper 2 carries 44% and is extended response. This is where the grade is usually decided and where the most marks are quietly thrown away. The paper rewards structured explanation: naming the physical principle, applying it to the specific situation in the question, and reaching a conclusion that answers what was asked. A correct equation with no reasoning around it scores a fraction of the available marks. The command terms are published and they are not decorative: explain, outline, discuss and justify ask for genuinely different answers, and students who treat them as synonyms lose marks in every question.

The scientific investigation makes up the remaining 20%, written during DP1 and marked out of twenty-four. The arithmetic to hold on to is that Paper 2 and the investigation together are nearly two thirds of the grade, and both are about writing physics rather than doing calculations. Most tutoring in this subject is bought for calculations.

sections.heading: Uncertainties: the arithmetic nobody is taught properly
paragraphs: If there is a single technical topic that costs IB physics students more marks than any other, it is uncertainty handling, and it is almost never the reason a family seeks a tutor. It appears in the data-analysis section of Paper 1, it appears throughout the scientific investigation, and it appears in Paper 2 wherever a question asks a student to comment on the reliability of a result.

The problems are consistent. Students confuse absolute and percentage uncertainty and mix them inside one calculation. They add percentage uncertainties when a quantity is multiplied, which is right, and then do the same when it is raised to a power, which is not. They quote a result to six significant figures with an uncertainty in the first decimal place, which tells an examiner immediately that the arithmetic was done without thought. They draw error bars and then fit a line that ignores them, or draw a line of best fit and never consider the maximum and minimum gradients the bars allow.

None of that is conceptually difficult, and that is exactly why it goes untaught. Schools cover it in a lesson early in DP1 and then assume it, because there is a syllabus to finish and uncertainties are not a theme. By the time the investigation is being written, a student is applying rules they half-remember to their own data, and the marks for analysis and conclusion are lost on arithmetic rather than physics.

It is also the single clearest case for an online session over a tutor at a dining table. Uncertainty work is spreadsheet work: a column of raw measurements, a column of means, a column of absolute uncertainties, a propagated result. On a shared screen a tutor can change one input and let the student watch the propagated uncertainty move, which is the moment the rules stop being arbitrary. Across a table, with one calculator between two people, it is a lecture.

sections.heading: Writing physics: why a correct equation earns almost nothing
paragraphs: The hardest thing to explain to a capable physics student is that knowing the answer is not the task. Paper 2 carries 44% of the grade and it is a writing paper. The marks are allocated to steps in an argument, and a student who writes the final relationship without the argument has produced a result the examiner cannot award.

A typical example runs like this. A question asks a student to explain why the current through a component changes when something else in the circuit is altered. The student writes the correct final statement about the current and stops. The mark scheme wanted the resistance change named, the effect on the total circuit resistance stated, the consequence for the total current derived, and only then the conclusion about the component. Four marks were available and one was earned, and the student genuinely understood the physics throughout.

The second pattern is command-term blindness. Outline, describe, explain, discuss, justify, suggest and evaluate ask for different things, and the mark allocation tells you how much. A two-mark explain question wants two linked steps. A four-mark discuss question wants a position and a counter-consideration. Students who write the same shape of answer regardless of the instruction lose a steady percentage across every paper, and because the loss is spread thinly it never appears as a topic weakness on any report.

This is the most coachable part of the subject and the least commonly bought. It needs a student to write answers under timing and have them marked immediately against the real allocation, with the tutor pointing at where the second and third marks were sitting unclaimed. Six to ten sessions of that in DP2 moves a grade more reliably than another pass through fields, and it is why the physics bookings from this community cluster on weekend mornings where there is time to write.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria, twenty-four marks
paragraphs: The internal assessment in physics is a single scientific investigation worth 20% of the grade, written during DP1 and marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each. Almost no family has seen that allocation, and seeing it changes how a student spends their time, because the two criteria students treat as an afterthought carry half the marks.

Research design comes first and decides the rest. A question that does not yield a measurable relationship cannot produce a good analysis however well the student works, and most weak investigations were lost at this point. The commonest failure in this community is an ambitious question requiring equipment the school does not have, closely followed by a question so safe that there is nothing to analyse. Data analysis is the second criterion, and it is where the uncertainty arithmetic discussed above either holds up or does not.

Conclusion and evaluation carry the other twelve marks and are where capable students throw them away. A conclusion must be stated in terms of the research question, with reference to the data and to accepted physics, and qualified by the uncertainty. Students instead write that the hypothesis was supported. Evaluation must weigh which limitation actually mattered to the result obtained, and propose a realistic improvement. Students instead list every imperfection they can think of, which earns almost nothing because no judgement has been exercised.

What a tutor may do here is bounded and worth stating. The criteria can be taught, because they are published. A research question can be narrowed and pressure-tested in conversation. A technique can be demonstrated on entirely different data so the method transfers without the content being handed over. A draft the student has written can be read and told which criterion is underserved and why. What a tutor must not do is write any part of it, rewrite a passage, or supply data or a conclusion. The school's supervisor runs the process and signs it off, and that is where it belongs.

sections.heading: The mathematics problem underneath most physics failures
paragraphs: A pattern worth naming, because it accounts for a large share of the physics enquiries from The Views and is almost always diagnosed as a physics problem. A student takes Higher Level physics alongside Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level. They are capable. They work. Physics goes wrong anyway, and nobody can say why.

The reason is that Higher Level physics assumes algebraic fluency rather than algebraic competence. Questions require rearranging a relationship with three or four variables, substituting one expression into another, handling indices and powers of ten without thinking, and occasionally differentiating. The Applications and Interpretation route is a perfectly good mathematics course and it does not drill those manipulations to the same depth, because its own assessment does not need them. A student who has to stop and think about rearranging has no working memory left for the physics in the question.

The diagnosis is easy to run at home. Give the student a physics question they got wrong and ask them to talk through it. If they can state the physical principle correctly and then stall on the algebra, the problem is mathematical. If they cannot state the principle, it is physics. In this community the first is more common than the second, and the two require different tutors or at least different sessions.

The practical remedy depends on timing. In DP1 the honest answer is sometimes to fix the mathematics instead of the physics for six weeks, which feels counterintuitive and works. In DP2 there is less room, so the work becomes drilling the specific manipulations physics questions actually require rather than mathematics in general. At option-choice time the useful advice is simpler: a student intending Higher Level physics is usually better served by Analysis and Approaches, even at Standard Level, than by the modelling route.

sections.heading: Ten minutes of questions that identify a current physics specialist
paragraphs: You do not need physics to test a physics tutor. You need questions whose answers are specific to the current course, because those are the ones a confident generalist cannot produce. Ask them in the free first lesson, of us or of anybody else, and listen for precision rather than reassurance.

The most useful single question is what happened to the options. A tutor teaching the current course will say immediately that the optional topics were removed in the 2023 guide and may add that it changed how the final term is spent. A tutor working from older material will either describe an option as though your child is studying it or become vague. The second most useful is how Paper 1 is structured, because the split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section is recent and specific.

Then the internal assessment. Ask how it is marked. The answer you want names four criteria at six marks each, twenty-four in total, and ideally mentions that conclusion and evaluation carry half of them. An answer describing two separate pieces of work, or a general coursework grade, tells you the person is recalling an older model. And ask what they would want to see before the second session: your child's marked script or investigation draft is the right answer, their own diagnostic test is a weaker one.

A tutor who offers to confirm something against the current subject guide is being honest, and that is a better signal than a fluent wrong answer. Guides do change. What should concern you is an hour of reassurance containing no component names, no weightings and no mention of command terms.

sections.heading: What a Higher Level physics specialist costs, from the top down
paragraphs: Physics is one of the subjects where the premium end of the Dubai market genuinely exists for a reason, so it is worth reading the rates from the top rather than the bottom. Scarcity is real here: Higher Level physics with strong uncertainty and extended-response teaching is a narrow specialism, and a narrow specialism is priced accordingly.

At the top of the published market, BartyED is quoted at AED 650 an hour for premium examiner-led tutoring. Below that, named IB and IGCSE specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 or more at the specialist end. In-home one-to-one visits sit across the middle at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel, with Bestimate's usual band AED 180 to AED 350. Qualified online subject tutoring begins around AED 150, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The bottom of the market is online supervision from university students, advertised from roughly AED 33 to AED 52 by Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 by EdFlik.

For Higher Level physics the bottom band is rarely the right purchase, and that is an unusual thing for a tutoring page to say. Supervision can keep a student at a desk through a problem set. It cannot diagnose whether a mock script lost marks to uncertainty arithmetic, to command-term blindness or to the mathematics underneath. For Standard Level content consolidation it is a reasonable choice. For a DP2 student who needs Paper 2 explanation work, paying AED 60 an hour for eight months is a more expensive mistake than paying AED 250 for ten sessions.

Every figure here is that provider's own published rate as read in October 2026. sections.heading: Starting from The Views, and the limits stated first
paragraphs: Four things get this moving: the school, the level, the component where marks are going, and the evenings that are genuinely free. If you do not know the component, that is normal and the free lesson establishes it. Bring a marked mock script or the investigation draft; real marked work tells a tutor in ten minutes what a conversation cannot tell them in an hour, because it shows whether the marks went to recall, to uncertainty arithmetic, to explanation or to the mathematics underneath.

The free first lesson is one per family, about thirty minutes, with no charge and no card details taken. A good one ends with the tutor naming the pattern and outlining the first four sessions, including whether part of the work is actually mathematical. A session that ends with a general offer to go through the syllabus is a weaker sign, and it has cost you nothing to find that out.

Then the arrangement is deliberately ordinary. Same tutor, same evening, a short written note after each session. The notes matter in physics more than in most subjects, because the gains are specific and cumulative: uncertainty rules secured in week two should not still be a problem in week eight, and the notes are how you see that. If the match is wrong, say so after the second lesson and we will change the tutor rather than defend it.

The limits, stated before you book. Nobody travels to a UAE address; home visiting is an India-only service. No examination date appears on this page, because the IB's site cannot be checked automatically and the school's IB coordinator is the only source worth using. We do not reproduce or supply IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, because they belong to the IB; we reference them. No grade is guaranteed. No part of an investigation is written for your child. And when no Higher Level physics specialist is free in your slot, you get the realistic date instead of a general science tutor.

faqs.question: Did the IB physics course really change, and does it affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantially, and it affects tutoring more than most families realise. The current guide was for first teaching in 2023 with first examinations in 2025. The optional topics were removed, content was reorganised into five themes, and Paper 1 was split into a multiple-choice section and a separate data-analysis section. A tutor working from older material will prepare your child for an examination structure that no longer exists and may spend sessions on an option they are not studying. Ask the question directly before booking.

faqs.question: How is the physics internal assessment marked now?
faqs.answer: It is a single scientific investigation worth 20% of the grade, marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The important consequence is that conclusion and evaluation together carry half the marks, and they are the parts students write last and fastest. A conclusion must reference the data, the research question and accepted physics; an evaluation must weigh which limitation actually mattered rather than listing everything that was imperfect.

faqs.question: Which physics topic causes the most trouble for Dubai students?
faqs.answer: Fields is the hardest conceptually, because it is abstract and the mathematics is unforgiving, and sign conventions plus the distinction between field and potential account for a lot of lost marks. But the biggest single source of loss is not a theme at all: it is uncertainty arithmetic, which appears in the data-analysis section, throughout the investigation, and in any question about reliability. Students mix absolute and percentage uncertainty, mishandle powers, and quote results to more significant figures than the uncertainty allows.

faqs.question: My child understands physics but writes poor answers. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: It is the most fixable thing in the subject, and it is worth a lot. Paper 2 carries 44% of the grade and awards marks to steps in an argument rather than to the final statement. A student who writes the correct conclusion without naming the principle, applying it and deriving the consequence earns one mark out of four on physics they genuinely understood. Six to ten sessions of writing answers under timing, marked immediately against the real allocation, moves a grade more reliably than another pass through content.

faqs.question: Could my child's physics problem actually be a maths problem?
faqs.answer: Very often, and it is the pattern we see most from this community. Higher Level physics assumes algebraic fluency, not competence: rearranging relationships with several variables, substituting expressions, handling powers of ten without pausing. A student on Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level may be perfectly able and simply not drilled in those manipulations. Test it at home: ask them to talk through a question they got wrong. If they state the principle correctly and stall on the algebra, the problem is mathematical.

faqs.question: How much extra work is Higher Level physics for a student in The Views?
faqs.answer: It is harder in a specific way. The five themes are the same, but Higher Level extends each one rather than adding a separable module, so the extra depth is distributed through the whole course. That is also why moving down a level mid-year is messier in physics than in some subjects: a student who switches in February has been studying extended material all year and has to work out what is still assessed. Moving in November is routine; moving in April is not, because the investigation is already running.

faqs.question: What is the data-analysis section of Paper 1 actually testing?
faqs.answer: Experimental reasoning rather than recall. It presents results from an investigation and asks a student to process them, graph them, handle their uncertainties and say what a gradient physically represents. Students who are strong in multiple choice are regularly weak here, because the skills have nothing in common. It is also the part of the paper that rewards practice on real datasets most directly, which is work done far better on a shared spreadsheet than on paper across a table.

faqs.question: How should we choose a physics investigation topic?
faqs.answer: Start from what can be measured with equipment the school actually has, and work backwards to a question. The commonest failure in this community is an ambitious question needing apparatus nobody owns, and the second commonest is a question so safe that there is nothing to analyse. A good research question yields a relationship between two variables with a range wide enough to graph. The school's supervisor approves the topic and owns the process; a tutor can pressure-test the question in conversation before it is submitted.

faqs.question: How much of the scientific investigation is a tutor allowed to touch?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that is easy to describe. A tutor can teach the four published criteria and their mark allocation, help narrow a research question, demonstrate a processing technique on completely different data, and read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is underserved. A tutor cannot write or rewrite any part of it, or supply data or a conclusion. The test a school applies is whether the work is recognisably your child's, in their own voice, with their own errors in it.

faqs.question: We are three months from the exams. Is physics tutoring still worth it?
faqs.answer: It depends on the diagnosis. The investigation is already submitted, so that twenty per cent is settled. Content gaps in fields cannot be rebuilt in three months and anyone promising otherwise is selling. What can be moved in that window is technique: command-term discipline on Paper 2, uncertainty rules for the data-analysis section, timing across whole papers, and the nuclear and quantum theme, which is usually taught last and revised least and therefore holds recoverable marks. Bring the mock script.

faqs.question: What should we budget for Higher Level physics support in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Most Higher Level arrangements land in the specialist band. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai monthly estimates put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for one weekly hour, with mid-market at AED 600 to AED 1,200. Hourly, named specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium examiner-led tutoring at AED 650 by BartyED. Those are other providers' published October 2026 figures, not ours; we publish no fixed price list.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest online tutoring ever right for physics?
faqs.answer: For Standard Level content consolidation, sometimes. Online supervision from university students is advertised in Dubai from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, and for keeping a student moving through a problem set it does the job. For Higher Level it is usually the wrong purchase, because the task is diagnostic rather than supervisory: working out whether a mock script lost marks to uncertainties, to command terms or to the mathematics underneath needs somebody who knows the mark allocation. Eight months of the wrong band costs more than ten sessions of the right one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both physics and maths for the same student?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and in this subject it is often the better arrangement. A specialist in Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level commonly teaches physics as well, and where a physics problem is really an algebra problem one tutor holding both threads is more efficient than two. Where each subject has an independent problem, two specialists in two shorter sessions usually beats one person covering both, because depth in the failing component matters more than the convenience of a single booking.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give the physics exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified at source. The IB's own website returns an error to automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed, and secondary sites occasionally disagree with each other. UAE schools sit the May session, and that much is safe to state. For the dates your child is working to, including internal investigation checkpoints and registration deadlines, the school's IB coordinator holds the authoritative version and it should be taken over anything published here.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level physics tutor is free on our evening?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a realistic date. Higher Level physics in the 17:00 to 18:00 window is one of the tightest combinations in Dubai, because the specialism is narrow and every Emirates Living family wants the same hour. The alternative to saying so is placing a general science tutor in a Higher Level slot, which costs a term before anybody admits the mismatch. Usually the fix is an adjacent evening or a weekend morning; occasionally it is a short wait, and that decision is yours.

Each teaches the course at a named level and has worked with the scientific investigation, and they will tell you honestly when a level or subject choice looks wrong.

intro.heading: Before the teaching, three comparisons
paragraphs: A lot of physics tutoring in Dubai is bought to solve a problem that is actually a choice. A student struggling with Higher Level physics may be in the wrong level. A student who dislikes physics and keeps it because it sounds serious may be carrying a subject nothing they want to study requires. And in this part of Dubailand, where provision is predominantly British curriculum, some families are weighing the Diploma against A Level and assuming the two treat physics similarly, which they do not.

So this page makes three comparisons before it discusses teaching. Higher against Standard Level physics, on the dimensions that actually differ rather than on difficulty in the abstract. IB Physics against A Level Physics for a UAE student, including what universities expect and how the two are structured. And physics against chemistry and biology, for a family deciding which science to keep when something has to go. A tutor who will not have those conversations is selling hours rather than advice.

Tilal Al Ghaf is a reasonable place to raise the A Level comparison, because it is a live question here. The community has a British-curriculum school inside its boundary and DAMAC Hills and Dubai Sports City have their own provision next door, while IB Diploma schools sit further out towards Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills Estate. Families in this belt frequently have genuine access to both routes, which means the choice is real rather than theoretical and deserves to be made on information.

The practical advantage of the community is the clock. Because the school run is short and pupils are often home before four, an early weekday session is realistic. Physics benefits from that more than most subjects, because the thing a physics student most needs is sustained concentration for explanation writing, and explanation writing at seven in the evening after a full day produces answers that describe rather than reason.

One component deserves early mention because it is the same whichever level a student takes. The scientific investigation carries 20% of the physics grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria. Its mark is largely determined at the design stage, before any data exists, by whether the chosen variable produces a change the school's apparatus can actually measure. That makes it the earliest real deadline in the subject and the place a tutor can most legitimately help.

IB Gram delivers physics tuition to Tilal Al Ghaf as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Practical work happens in your child's school laboratory and no tutor substitutes for that in any format, which this page addresses directly rather than glossing over.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.subjectsIntro: These are the physics topics Tilal Al Ghaf families ask about, with the level at which each becomes demanding. The Higher Level column is the honest answer to whether the extension is manageable.

subjects.name: Mechanics and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum and energy. Accessible at both levels and the place where the explanation habit is formed: students who reason from the resultant force score, while those who describe the velocity graph do not. Momentum questions reward stating conservation before calculating.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The reliable weak point in every cohort because circuit reasoning holds current, potential difference and resistance together rather than recalling one formula. Internal resistance at Higher Level is where capable students separate from very capable ones.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.levels: HL and SL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields and the analogies between them. The Higher Level treatment of potential and potential energy is the single most common reason a strong student requests help, because the sign conventions are unforgiving and the concepts abstract.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Wave behaviour, superposition, standing waves and simple harmonic motion. Phase relationships carry the marks, and the fix is sketching displacement against time before attempting a verbal answer. Diffraction questions want the condition named, not the pattern described.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Internal energy, specific heat capacity, latent heat and the ideal gas treatment. Marks are lost by conflating heat and temperature in written answers, which is a vocabulary problem with a mark consequence rather than a conceptual gap.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Decay, binding energy, mass defect and the photoelectric effect. Binding-energy calculations compound errors across several steps, so one early rounding decision survives to the final answer. The photoelectric effect rewards a precise statement of the threshold condition.

subjects.name: Energy production
subjects.description: Sources, efficiency and the physics of generation and transfer. Often under-revised because it feels descriptive, and a reliable source of accessible marks for a student who learns the efficiency arguments properly rather than in general terms.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error analysis
subjects.levels: HL and SL, examined and assessed internally
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations and error bars on graphs. Examined in the papers and central to the investigation, so time spent here is paid for twice. Almost always under-taught in both systems.

subjects.name: Graph work and data analysis
subjects.description: Linearising relationships, gradients with physical meaning, intercepts and best-fit judgement. Students plot competently and then fail to state what the gradient physically represents, which is where the marks sit, and it transfers directly into the investigation.

subjects.name: Explanation and command terms
subjects.levels: HL and SL, across every topic
subjects.description: 'State', 'describe', 'explain', 'deduce' and 'discuss' carry different mark expectations. Teaching a student to answer the verb recovers marks in every topic simultaneously, which makes it the highest-yield single intervention available in the subject.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: HL and SL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The decisive factor is whether the chosen variable produces a change the school's apparatus can measure precisely enough to show the effect.

subjects.name: Mathematical technique for physics
subjects.description: Rearranging, indices, standard form, trigonometry for resolving vectors and, at Higher Level, the beginnings of calculus reasoning. A physics problem is frequently a mathematics problem in disguise, which is why a diagnostic must test the algebra separately.

sections.heading: Higher against Standard Level physics, compared properly
paragraphs: The usual framing is that Higher Level is harder, which is true and not useful. What a family needs is the shape of the difference, because it determines whether a struggling student should be moved and how many tutoring hours the level realistically demands.

The key structural fact is that Higher Level physics extends the treatment of most topics rather than adding a separate block at the end. Fields, nuclear physics, waves and electricity all go deeper rather than appearing only at Higher Level. That has a direct consequence families should know before choosing: you cannot prepare for Higher Level by learning the Standard Level course and bolting the extension on afterwards, because the extension is woven through. A Higher Level student who is behind therefore needs roughly half again the total hours that the same gap would need at Standard Level.

The second difference is mathematical. Higher Level physics assumes confident rearranging, indices, standard form, vector resolution and the beginnings of calculus reasoning, and it assumes them at speed. A student taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level alongside Higher Level physics is carrying a mismatch that shows up in physics marks rather than in mathematics marks, and it is one of the commonest hidden causes of physics underperformance in Dubai schools.

The third is the investigation, which is the same task at both levels and judged against the same four criteria. That is worth knowing, because it means the 20% component is equally reachable for a Standard Level student. A student who moves from Higher to Standard Level does not lose access to any part of the assessment; they lose content depth and one layer of mathematical demand. For a student whose degree route does not require Higher Level physics, that trade is often straightforwardly correct.

sections.heading: IB Physics or A Level Physics, for a student in this belt
paragraphs: This comparison is live in Tilal Al Ghaf in a way it is not everywhere, because local provision is predominantly British curriculum while IB Diploma schools sit a short drive away. Dubai's 2024-25 figures put the UK curriculum at 37% of private enrolment and the International Baccalaureate at 7%, so a family here is choosing between a well-supplied local option and a less common one that requires a longer journey.

The honest comparison is about shape rather than quality. A Level Physics is narrower and deeper: three or four subjects total, no compulsory core components, and physics content explored further than the Diploma goes. Practical work is assessed through a separate practical endorsement rather than a single marked investigation, which means laboratory skills are examined across many activities instead of one piece of coursework. The written papers reward depth within physics.

IB Physics sits inside a six-subject programme with the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS alongside it. The physics goes less far than A Level in places and the student carries a broader load, including a second language and the core components. The single marked investigation carries 20% of the physics grade, which concentrates risk and reward into one piece of work in a way the practical endorsement does not.

Which suits a student depends on two things that have nothing to do with physics. Whether they are better served by breadth with compulsory writing components or by depth with fewer subjects. And what the universities they are considering actually ask for, which is published by each institution and varies by course and year, so it should be read on the course pages rather than inferred. Both qualifications are widely recognised; the mistake is choosing on reputation rather than on fit and published requirements.

sections.heading: Physics, chemistry or biology: which science to keep
paragraphs: Diploma students sometimes have to drop a science, change a level, or decide which of three to take at Higher Level, and the decision is frequently made on which teacher they like. It is worth making on two better criteria: what the intended degree requires, and which assessment profile the student actually suits.

On requirements, the pattern is reasonably stable and should still be verified on each university's own course pages, because it varies by institution and by year. Engineering and physics routes commonly expect Higher Level physics with Analysis and Approaches. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary routes commonly expect Higher Level chemistry, often with biology. Life sciences generally expect biology, frequently with chemistry. A student keeping physics for a medical route and dropping chemistry has usually made the wrong trade.

On assessment profile, the three sciences reward different things despite sharing the same investigation structure. Physics rewards reasoning from principles and punishes description; it is the least content-heavy and the most conceptually demanding of the three. Chemistry is sequential and quantitative, so it punishes a weak foundation more than the others and rewards disciplined calculation. Biology is content-heavy and rewards precise terminology and command-term discipline, with the lowest mathematical demand of the three.

A student who reasons well and dislikes memorising belongs in physics. A student who is organised and precise with numbers belongs in chemistry. A student with a strong memory and good written discipline belongs in biology. None of that outranks the degree requirement, but where the requirement leaves a choice, matching the profile is a better basis than preference for a teacher, and it is the conversation a tutor should be willing to have even when it means a smaller booking.

sections.heading: The investigation, and how physics differs from the other sciences
paragraphs: All three Diploma sciences use the same investigation structure: an individual scientific investigation marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each carrying six marks, scaled to 20% of the subject grade. Confirm the current criteria with your child's teacher, since the IB revises its guides. What differs is where each subject's investigation tends to fail, and physics has its own characteristic trap.

In physics the trap is measurability against uncertainty. A student chooses a relationship that is genuinely interesting and then finds the effect is smaller than the uncertainty of the instrument available — a temperature change inside the resolution of a school thermometer, a time interval too short to measure by hand, a mass difference below the balance's precision. The data then shows noise rather than a relationship, and no amount of careful writing recovers it. That is why the design conversation, held before any apparatus is booked, is the single most valuable hour a physics tutor spends.

The second physics-specific issue is that uncertainty propagation is both examined in the written papers and central to the investigation, so it is paid for twice. Most students arrive never having been taught it systematically, because it tends to be covered alongside practicals rather than as a topic in its own right. Two or three sessions on absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, and error bars with a stated effect on the conclusion will earn marks in both places.

The criteria students neglect are conclusion and evaluation, which together carry twelve of the twenty-four marks and are the cheapest to improve because they reward thinking rather than apparatus. A conclusion must answer the stated research question and be justified by the data, and an evaluation must identify specific methodological weaknesses and propose realistic improvements rather than mentioning human error. Both can be improved after the data exists, which makes them the right target for a student who is already late.

sections.heading: Two kinds of struggling physics student
paragraphs: Physics underperformance in Dubai has two standard profiles and they look identical on a school report. Telling them apart is the first thing a diagnostic should do, because they need opposite responses and treating the wrong one wastes a term.

The first profile calculates confidently and explains poorly. These students handle numerical questions and lose marks on extended response, which carries the larger share of the grade. The cause is usually conceptual rather than linguistic: they can use an equation without understanding the relationship it expresses, so when a question asks why rather than how much they have nothing to reason from. Teaching command terms helps immediately, but the underlying repair is conceptual and takes a term.

The second profile reasons well and calculates badly. These students write good qualitative answers and lose marks whenever a question requires rearranging, unit handling or multi-step arithmetic. The cause is mathematical rather than physical, and no amount of physics teaching fixes it, because the physics was never the problem. These students need a short mathematics block, which is both cheaper and faster than the physics tutoring they were about to buy.

The diagnostic that separates them is simple and almost never done: work calculation questions and explanation questions separately and record the two scores apart rather than producing a single mark. A school report cannot do this, because it reports one grade. A marked mock can, if someone bothers to split it. Doing that in the first session is why our diagnostic looks different from a normal first lesson, and it regularly changes what the family buys.

sections.heading: Practical physics when the tutor is on a screen
paragraphs: A straight answer rather than reassurance. Practical work in IB Physics happens at school. Your child's school has the apparatus, runs the laboratory sessions and supervises the investigation. No tutor in any delivery format runs experiments for a student, and an in-home tutor arriving at a Tilal Al Ghaf villa with a trolley and a light gate is not what in-home tutoring looks like either.

What a tutor genuinely contributes divides into three things, all of which work on a shared screen. Design: whether the proposed variable can be measured well enough, what must be controlled, how many values are needed and over what range, and whether a trial should be run before committing. Uncertainty and data treatment: propagating uncertainty, plotting with error bars, deciding what a gradient means physically. And the writing: reading the student's own draft and saying what is not working and why.

On the middle one, a screen is actually better than a dining table. Both parties see the same spreadsheet, the same graph and the same error bars, and a change made to a cell is visible to both immediately. Anyone who has tried to discuss a data set over someone's shoulder on paper will recognise why.

Where a screen genuinely loses something is apparatus intuition: what a reading looks like when it has drifted, how a light gate actually behaves, why a trial failed. The school provides that and we will not pretend to substitute for it. What a tutor can do is send a student into a laboratory session with a plan, which matters more than it sounds given how many students arrive at a practical with none and spend the session following instructions.

sections.heading: What physics tutoring costs, and which block to buy
paragraphs: Price the investigation block rather than the hour, because that is the unit physics divides into. Six sessions at Tutopiya's advertised AED 33 to AED 52 an hour is AED 198 to AED 312; at EdFlik's AED 45 to AED 65 it is AED 270 to AED 390; at Unitors' published AED 200 for IB, or AED 150 for IGCSE, it is AED 1,200; at TutorChase's AED 270 it is AED 1,620; at BartyED's AED 650 it is AED 3,900. Every one of those rates was read in October 2026 from the provider's own published figures. Bestimate's Dubai table frames the same market twice over, putting in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, then converting one weekly hour into monthly estimates of AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Measured against a component worth a fifth of the grade, the gap between those block prices is the decision a family in this community is really making.

In physics the best value is rarely open-ended weekly tutoring, because the subject divides cleanly into blocks with different returns. A decision session on level or subject choice is one hour and can save a family two years of the wrong course. An investigation coaching block of six to eight sessions addresses a fifth of the grade at the point the mark is still determinable. A command-term block of four to six sessions recovers marks in every topic simultaneously. A mathematics block of four to six sessions fixes the physics problem that was never a physics problem.

Content teaching is the least efficient per hour, not because it fails but because it addresses one topic at a time and there are many. That makes it the right purchase when the diagnostic says content is genuinely thin, and the wrong default when nobody has checked. A family buying weekly physics support without a split diagnostic between calculation and explanation is buying attention rather than a plan.

IB Gram publishes no hourly rate on this page, because the right figure depends on level, stage and which block the evidence calls for. The market band lets you judge any quote including ours, and the first lesson is free. In it, ask the tutor to name the four investigation criteria with their marks and to explain the difference between a 'describe' and an 'explain' question. A genuine physics specialist answers both immediately.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and the limits we work to
paragraphs: The investigation is individual assessed work and there are providers in this region selling completed internal assessments at published prices. Submitting one is academic misconduct and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. Because families in Dubai encounter such providers through the same search results as legitimate ones, the boundary belongs on the page, and we state it to the student rather than only to the parent.

A tutor may teach any physics the investigation requires, test whether a design is measurable, explain each criterion and its descriptors, teach uncertainty treatment, and read the student's own draft and say what is not working. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply the data, choose the research question outright, or edit a draft into something the student did not produce. Where a draft needs changing, the tutor names the problem and the student rewrites. That is slower and it is the only version that is both lawful and effective, because conclusion and evaluation reward thinking the student actually did.

A physics-specific version of the same boundary applies to paper. Any provider offering a Tilal Al Ghaf family a shared folder of IB physics papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables is distributing material that belongs to the IB, and reproducing or distributing it is copyright infringement whoever assembled the folder. Our tutors work from legitimately obtained material and from the student's own data, and the more useful transfer is teaching a sixteen-year-old to read the four investigation criteria unaided, since the descriptors are the document the mark is actually awarded against. The companion claim to refuse is the examiner badge: we do not describe tutors as IB examiners where current status cannot be evidenced, and examiner experience gives no access to marking, to boundaries, or to unseen paper content in any case.

On regulation: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Those operating without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so distrust quoted amounts, and ask any tutor to show the permit rather than describe it. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from the IB, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education.

faqs.question: Should my child move from Higher to Standard Level physics?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and two things decide it. First, whether any university course they are considering requires Higher Level physics, which is published on each institution's own course pages and varies by course and year. Second, whether the mathematics is there: Higher Level assumes confident rearranging, vectors and early calculus reasoning at speed. A student moving down loses content depth and one layer of mathematical demand, and loses no part of the assessment, because the investigation is the same task judged against the same four criteria at both levels.

faqs.question: How does IB Physics compare with A Level Physics for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: In shape rather than quality. A Level is narrower and deeper: three or four subjects, no compulsory core components, physics explored further, and practical skills assessed through a separate endorsement across many activities. IB Physics sits inside a six-subject programme with the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, and concentrates practical assessment into one marked investigation worth 20% of the grade. Both are widely recognised; read the published requirements of the specific universities rather than choosing on reputation.

faqs.question: Which science should my child keep if one has to go?
faqs.answer: Start with what the intended degree requires, verified on each university's own course pages. Engineering and physics routes commonly expect Higher Level physics; medicine, dentistry and pharmacy commonly expect Higher Level chemistry. Where the requirement leaves a choice, match the assessment profile: physics rewards reasoning from principles and has the highest mathematical demand, chemistry is sequential and quantitative, and biology is content-heavy with the lowest mathematical demand and the greatest reward for precise terminology.

faqs.question: Will a physics tutor visit our home in Tilal Al Ghaf?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Practical physics happens in your child's school laboratory in either case, so no tutor in any format substitutes for that. What a screen does better than a dining table is shared data work: both parties see the same spreadsheet, graph and error bars, and a change to a cell is immediately visible to both.

faqs.question: Why does my child calculate well and still score badly in physics?
faqs.answer: Because extended-response questions carry the larger share of the grade and they are marked on reasoning rather than on calculation. A student who can use an equation without understanding the relationship it expresses has nothing to reason from when a question asks why rather than how much. Teaching command terms helps immediately; the underlying conceptual repair takes a term. The opposite profile also exists — reasons well, calculates badly — and those two students need opposite help despite identical reports.

faqs.question: How is the physics investigation marked and where does it fail?
faqs.answer: Out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each — research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation — scaled to 20% of the grade. Confirm the current allocations with your child's teacher. The physics-specific failure is measurability: a student chooses a relationship where the effect is smaller than the uncertainty of the available instrument, so the data shows noise rather than a relationship. That is decided before any apparatus is booked, which is why the design conversation is the most valuable hour on this component.

faqs.question: Is uncertainty work worth paying a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is among the best value in the subject because it is paid for twice. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, and error bars with a stated effect on the conclusion all appear in the data section of the written papers and are central to the investigation. Two or three sessions covers it. Most students arrive never having been taught it systematically, because it tends to be covered alongside practicals rather than as a topic in its own right.

faqs.question: Does the maths course my child takes affect their physics marks?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and it is one of the commonest hidden causes of physics underperformance in Dubai schools. Higher Level physics assumes confident rearranging, indices, standard form, vector resolution and early calculus reasoning, at speed. A student taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level alongside Higher Level physics is carrying a mismatch that shows up in physics marks rather than mathematics marks, and it responds to a short mathematics block rather than to more physics teaching.

faqs.question: How many hours does Higher Level physics need compared with Standard?
faqs.answer: Roughly half again, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of difficulty. Higher Level extends the treatment of most topics rather than adding a separate block at the end, so the extension is woven through the whole syllabus and cannot be learned afterwards. A Higher Level student who is behind needs the same hours the Standard Level gap would need plus about fifty per cent, and the sooner that is recognised the cheaper it is to supply.

faqs.question: Which rate band should we expect for Higher Level physics?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget and student tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for qualified subject tutors online, and AED 200 to AED 450 or above for IB specialists, with in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel. Monthly at one weekly session that is roughly AED 240 to AED 600, AED 600 to AED 1,200, or AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. Those are published market numbers, not our prices, and the first lesson is free.

faqs.question: Which physics block gives the best return?
faqs.answer: A one-hour decision session first if level or subject choice is genuinely in question, because it can save two years of the wrong course. Then a split diagnostic to establish which struggling profile your child fits. After that: investigation coaching for six to eight sessions if the component is still determinable, a command-term block of four to six if calculation is sound and marks are low, or a mathematics block of four to six if the physics was never the problem. Content teaching is the least efficient per hour and the most common default.

faqs.question: Can my child reach a good investigation mark if they have already collected the data?
faqs.answer: Partly, and it is worth knowing which part. Research design and data analysis are largely fixed once the data exists, but conclusion and evaluation together carry twelve of the twenty-four marks and can still be improved, because they reward thinking rather than apparatus. A conclusion must answer the stated research question and be justified by the data; an evaluation must identify specific methodological weaknesses and propose realistic improvements rather than mentioning human error. That is the right target for a student who is already late.

faqs.question: Why is an early session better for physics specifically?
faqs.answer: Because explanation writing is concentration work rather than repetition. A student who reasons well at four-thirty frequently describes rather than explains at seven, after a school day and other homework, and a session spent producing weak answers teaches weak habits. Tilal Al Ghaf has a school inside the community and neighbouring communities have their own provision, so pupils are often home before four and the early slot is genuinely available here in a way it is not across most of this belt.

A tutor cannot choose the research question outright, supply the data or write any part of the document, because conclusion and evaluation together carry twelve of the twenty-four marks and reward thinking the student actually did. Where a draft is not working, the tutor names the problem and the student rewrites it.

Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of quoted amounts. Ask to see the document rather than accepting an assurance, and ask the same of any agency placing a tutor with your family.

intro.heading: When does physics actually fit into a Town Square week?
paragraphs: Physics is the subject where the hour matters most and gets chosen least carefully. A tired student can read a biology chapter and retain something useful. A tired student cannot follow a derivation, cannot carry units through four steps of a calculation without losing one, and cannot hold a free-body diagram in mind while resolving forces in an unfamiliar direction. Those are the actual demands of a Diploma physics session, and they do not survive a bad hour.

Town Square makes the timing problem concrete. It is a Nshama community off Al Qudra Road, and the schools offering Diploma physics are not nearby — students here travel to Motor City, Dubai Sports City, or further into Al Barsha and Silicon Oasis. A school day ending at half three becomes a 4:45pm arrival home once the afternoon traffic on the Al Qudra approach is counted, and from an inner-city school it is nearer five.

A visiting tutor compounds it. They leave another part of Dubai in the same traffic, so the realistic start is half six, the session ends at eight, and the student has been working for thirteen hours by the time somebody asks them to propagate an uncertainty. That arrangement is not failing on teaching quality. It is failing on the clock, and from this community the clock is what is in short supply.

IB Gram removes travel from both sides. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we make no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. So a Year 12 student can start at 4:45pm, fifteen minutes after walking through the door, and a Year 13 student can take an 8pm ninety-minute block once the house is quiet, which for a full data-analysis question plus marking is the right shape.

The second thing worth establishing early is when in the course help is worth most, because for physics the answer is weighted heavily towards the first year. Everything in the course assumes algebraic fluency that the course itself does not teach. The investigation is worth 20% of the grade and is finished long before exam revision begins. And the Higher Level practical paper tests a skill built over months rather than crammed in a term.

The IB accounts for around 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools, spread across the whole emirate, with only the final two years sitting the Diploma. Physics at Higher Level is a narrow specialism inside that, so the chance that a qualified HL physics teacher lives near Town Square with a free weekday evening is low. Matching online makes the question irrelevant, which is the point.

programmes.description: Written papers plus the investigation at 20% of the grade. Breadth rather than depth, which makes coverage the risk: a topic taught in a hurried fortnight can stay unlearned until a mock finds it. Definitions and the correct use of units are examined relentlessly throughout the course.
programmes.countryNote: SL physics is a common Town Square choice for students heading into economics, architecture or life sciences, and is often paired with Applications and Interpretation maths. That pairing works provided the algebra underneath is taught explicitly, because the physics course expects rearrangement AI does not emphasise.

programmes.name: Physics Higher Level
programmes.description: Additional content depth plus a third written paper testing experimental technique and data analysis directly. The investigation remains 20%. HL rewards students who can sustain a multi-step argument with units and uncertainties carried correctly through every stage, and penalises formula lookup.
programmes.countryNote: The level most engineering and physical-science applications require, and the level at which local specialist supply around Town Square most often reaches zero. Families here frequently need exactly the tutor the neighbourhood cannot provide, which is the whole case for matching online rather than by distance.

programmes.name: IGCSE or MYP into Diploma physics
programmes.description: An underestimated step. IGCSE physics rewards recall and single-step calculation; Diploma physics expects derivation, multi-step reasoning and uncertainty treatment. A strong IGCSE grade offers no protection, and the slip usually becomes visible by November of Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: The summer before Year 12 is the only period when a Town Square week has genuinely spare hours in it, which makes it the best-value point to do the bridging work: algebraic rearrangement, logarithms, graph interpretation and uncertainty basics, before two years of content gets built on top.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-town-square.subjectsIntro: The physics topics and components Town Square students need work on, with the specific place marks go in each. Availability varies by level and term and is confirmed at the trial lesson.

subjects.name: Mechanics and kinematics
subjects.description: Projectiles, momentum, energy and circular motion. Students usually know the equations and lose marks on sign conventions, on resolving forces in an unfamiliar direction, and on choosing a force argument where an energy argument would have been shorter and safer.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The most commonly named weak topic and often genuinely weak. Internal resistance, potential dividers and real components under load. Students apply Ohm's law competently and cannot reason about what happens to a circuit when one component changes.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Superposition, standing waves, diffraction and simple harmonic motion. Phase relationships are the recurring difficulty, and a correctly labelled wave diagram answers several marks of question on its own, which students rarely exploit.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat and the kinetic model. Marks sit in precise definition and in whether a student can explain a temperature change at the level of particles rather than restating the equation they used to calculate it.

subjects.name: Fields: gravitational, electric and magnetic
subjects.description: Field strength versus potential is the distinction students most often blur, and Higher Level questions exploit it directly. Sketching a field pattern correctly and reasoning about work done moving a charge or mass through it recurs across papers.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Binding energy, decay, the photoelectric effect and energy levels. Arithmetic with very large and very small numbers in standard form costs marks independently of whether the physics is understood, which is worth diagnosing as a separate fault.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error propagation
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, how each propagates through addition, multiplication and powers, and what that implies about the precision an answer may claim. Examined across every component and taught in a rush almost everywhere.

subjects.name: Graph work and linearisation
subjects.description: Choosing what to plot so a relationship becomes a straight line, then reading physics from the gradient and intercept. A technique rather than a topic, which is why it responds quickly to one-to-one work and why it is worth isolating.

subjects.name: The practical and data-analysis paper
subjects.description: Reading instruments to sensible precision, identifying a flawed method, selecting controlled variables, judging whether data supports a conclusion. A different skill from the content papers, reached late in most schools, and worth preparing for separately.

subjects.name: The Physics investigation
subjects.levels: HL and SL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation against published criteria. Most marks are lost before any data exists: no measurable variable, too few repeats to say anything about reliability, or a range too narrow for a relationship to show above the noise.

subjects.name: The maths underneath physics
subjects.description: Algebraic rearrangement, indices, logarithms for exponential relationships, trigonometry for resolving vectors, and gradient reasoning. Students taking Applications and Interpretation maths alongside physics usually need this layer taught explicitly.

sections.heading: Four windows in a Town Square week, and what physics each supports
paragraphs: Scheduling ends more physics arrangements than teaching does. A family agrees a time in September, then an investigation deadline lands in November, a mock arrives in January, and by February the sessions have stopped without anyone deciding to stop them. Physics suffers more than other subjects when that happens, because each session builds directly on the last and the thread does not pick up where it was dropped.

There are four candidate windows out here. Straight off the school run, 4:30pm to 5:30pm, which only exists if nobody is travelling to you. After dinner from seven, which competes with the student's own best independent working hour. Late, from eight, which Year 13 students use well and younger students cannot. And weekend mornings, which are the most reliable and the least used.

For physics the match between task and window is unusually clear. New teaching — a derivation, uncertainty propagation taught properly for the first time, an unfamiliar technique — needs the alert window and should go early in the day. Past-paper practice with marking needs ninety minutes, which rules out the sixty-minute after-dinner slot. Investigation work needs a long uninterrupted block, which in practice means a weekend. And consolidation of material already understood tolerates a later hour.

Choose with your child present, because they know which hour they can concentrate in better than either of us does. Then protect it, and plan the Ramadan change deliberately rather than discovering it: shortened school days, evenings reorganised around Iftar, and a shift to a late-morning, early-afternoon or post-Iftar slot, with content moving towards consolidation rather than new technique for that month.

sections.heading: The Diploma physics year, term by term
paragraphs: Knowing when help is worth most matters as much as knowing what kind. For physics the value is front-loaded, and the reasons are structural rather than motivational.

End of Year 11 and the summer that follows: the bridging window, and the cheapest point in the whole course. IGCSE physics rewards recall and single-step calculation; Diploma physics expects derivation, multi-step reasoning and uncertainty treatment, and the algebra underneath — rearrangement, indices, logarithms, gradient reasoning — is assumed rather than taught. A short block here changes how every later session lands.

First and second terms of Year 12: new content, and the point at which uncertainty technique should be taught properly rather than absorbed incidentally. Third term of Year 12 into first term of Year 13: the investigation, where most of the 20% is decided in the fortnight the research question and method are chosen rather than in the write-up. First term of Year 13 also brings mocks.

Second term of Year 13: paper technique only, including dedicated work on the Higher Level practical paper, which most schools reach late because practice naturally concentrates on the papers both levels sit. Then the May session. One honesty note: the IB's own site blocks automated retrieval, so no IB exam or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org. We name the May session and publish no specific date — get those from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and usable: Cambridge runs June and November series with February/March offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

sections.heading: The maths underneath decides the physics grade
paragraphs: This is the hidden prerequisite and it explains a large share of the physics struggles we diagnose from this corridor. IB physics assumes algebraic comfort the course never teaches: rearranging an equation with the unknown in the denominator, working with indices and standard form at speed, taking logarithms when a relationship is exponential, resolving vectors with trigonometry, and reasoning fluently about gradients and intercepts.

Where it bites hardest is the combination of Physics Higher Level with Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation. AI is a good course and emphasises modelling, statistics and technology rather than algebraic manipulation, so a student can be doing well in maths and still lack the exact fluency the physics paper demands. That pairing is common in Dubai schools, it is not a mistake, and it needs the algebra taught alongside rather than assumed.

The diagnostic consequence is that we look underneath whatever the student names. A student who says fields are the problem often cannot rearrange the expression confidently enough to see what a question is asking. A student who says the practical paper is impossible often cannot take logarithms of both sides to find a power relationship. Teaching more fields content to the first, or more experimental theory to the second, misses the layer where the marks are actually going.

In practice this means a short algebraic block early is among the best investments a Year 12 physics family can make, and it is faster than it sounds — six to ten focused sessions on rearrangement, indices, logarithms and gradient reasoning. Done in the summer before Year 12 it is cheap and unhurried. Done in February of Year 13 it is a rescue competing with everything else in the week.
bullets: Physics assumes rearrangement, indices, logarithms and gradient reasoning
