sections.heading: The investigation is decided in a fortnight, not a term
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the physics grade comes from an individual investigation, and by the time most students ask for help the marks that mattered have already been settled — in the fortnight when the research question was chosen and the method planned, not in the writing.

The design faults recur with remarkable consistency. A research question with no genuinely measurable independent variable, so nothing can be varied systematically. A range too narrow for a relationship to show above the noise. Two readings per point, or none, so nothing honest can be said about reliability. A controlled variable that was named but not actually controlled, discovered at the evaluation stage when the only option left is to confess it. A measurement method whose uncertainty is larger than the effect being measured.

None of those can be fixed by a better conclusion, which is why a tutor who reads the criteria with the student in week one is worth several who read a draft in week ten. The permitted work is substantial: explaining what each criterion rewards and what it is worth, testing whether a proposed question can be investigated with the available equipment, checking the planned range and repeats will produce analysable data, and giving criterion-level feedback on a draft the student has written.

The line is authorship and it is firm. A tutor may not write any part of the investigation, supply data or calculations, provide a model to adapt, or edit a draft to a finish. The student signs an authorship declaration and the supervisor signs alongside, and the IB withdraws awards for malpractice. This search result contains operators selling completed Internal Assessments — one advertises them at AED 3,750 — which risks the whole Diploma rather than one component. We also host no IB past papers, mark schemes or subject guides as downloads; they belong to the IB and we link the official source.
bullets: Most marks are decided in the planning fortnight, not the write-up
Measurable variable, adequate range, enough repeats, genuinely controlled variables
Permitted: criteria explained, method tested, feedback on the student's own draft
Not permitted: writing, supplying data, model investigations, editing to a finish

sections.heading: The Higher Level practical paper as its own body of work
paragraphs: Higher Level candidates sit a third written paper that Standard Level does not, and it tests experimental technique and data analysis as a skill in its own right rather than as a layer over the content. Treating it as revision is the commonest planning error in HL physics.

What it actually asks for is a specific set of habits. Reading an instrument to a precision the instrument justifies. Spotting that a described method cannot answer the question it was set. Identifying which variable needed controlling and was not. Building a results table with correct headings and units. Choosing what to plot so a relationship linearises, drawing maximum and minimum lines through error bars to get an uncertainty on a gradient, and saying what the gradient means physically. Judging whether a conclusion is supported by the data presented.

Schools teach all of it, inside a practical timetable that is always under pressure, and they usually reach the paper late. A student who missed a few weeks of that teaching rarely recovers the technique from a textbook, because none of it is really content. It is a set of procedures that need to be performed, corrected and performed again — which is exactly what one-to-one work with marked past data-analysis questions provides.

The useful shape is one real data-analysis question a week, marked properly rather than discussed, with the error pattern deciding what gets taught next. Ninety minutes is the right length, which is why the 8pm Year 13 window suits this work specifically. It also transfers directly into the investigation's processing and evaluation marks, so the same preparation earns credit twice.

sections.heading: What physics tutoring costs in this market
paragraphs: Take the in-home line first, because in Town Square it is the number most families price before anything else: AED 180-500 an hour including travel, read from provider pages in October 2026 along with everything else here. Online, a qualified subject tutor runs AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. The specialist tier of IB, IGCSE and A Level runs AED 200-450 and above, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate puts the band at AED 200-450 plus, while BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Budget online advertises from AED 33-65, with Tutopiya at AED 33-52 and EdFlik at AED 45-65. Convert that to a term: two hours a week across a twelve-week Diploma term is twenty-four contact hours, which is AED 792 at Tutopiya's floor and AED 15,600 at BartyED's published rate. That span, not a single hourly figure, is what a Town Square parent is choosing inside.

There is a timing dimension to cost that is specific to this community. An in-home arrangement from Town Square costs more per hour and buys a worse hour, because the drive pushes the start past six and physics tolerates a late hour less well than any other subject. So the premium is paying for a journey that degrades the product it is attached to. For a younger child needing physical presence the trade can still be worth making; for a Diploma physics student it rarely is.

The advertised packages are where the Town Square premium turns into arithmetic. Eight online sessions run around AED 799 a month. Four in-home two-hour visits run AED 1,599-1,799 a month. That is eight contact hours either way, so the in-home route costs roughly double for the same quantity of teaching, and the hours it buys start later in the evening. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour sit underneath both routes: AED 240-600 at the budget band, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work.

None of the figures above is our price. Each belongs to the provider publishing it, and IB Gram carries no rate card on these pages at all, because a number typed into a landing page cannot know the three things that actually set it: the level the student is sitting, the specific gap the marked work exposes, and how many weeks are left to close it. The in-home premium described above is one we are not competing on either way, since we do not drive to Town Square. What we do instead is make the first lesson free, run the diagnostic inside it, and quote only once there is evidence to quote against.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and keeping the thread
paragraphs: A physics plan that ignores the UAE academic year will break, and physics breaks worse than other subjects because the material is cumulative in a direct way: this week's uncertainty work is next week's investigation analysis, and a three-week gap does not resume where it stopped.

Ramadan is the biggest change. School days shorten, the evening reorganises around Iftar, and a student comfortable at six o'clock is not. Town Square families typically shift to a late-morning or early-afternoon slot, move to post-Iftar, or pause part of the month and resume with a heavier block afterwards. All three work; keeping the usual weekday evening does not. Content should also move towards consolidation rather than new technique for that period, which is a better use of a shorter attention span anyway.

Prayer times matter all year and move through the calendar, so we build slots around them from the start rather than waiting for a family to raise it. The same applies to the long summer and the travel weekends that are normal here — sessions continue while a family is away, because the tutor's location is already part of the arrangement rather than an obstacle to it, and only the time of day needs adjusting.

What we work to avoid is the drift of cancel, reschedule, cancel, until nobody says out loud that the arrangement has ended. The small commitment we ask for is a deliberate reset: tell us the new pattern and we move the fixed slot, rather than letting a run of missed weeks make the decision by default.

sections.heading: What we will not claim about a physics result
paragraphs: No grade guarantee. Not a specific number, not a points improvement, not a particular paper score. The variables — prior algebra, weeks remaining, whether the investigation was designed well, whether the student has ever been taught to write every step down — are not all under a tutor's control, and an offer that ignores that is a sales device.

No statistics without a sample size, a date and a method, which means none published. No average physics score achieved by students we have taught, no percentage improved, no satisfaction figure, no self-generated star rating. Competitors publish such numbers routinely, sometimes in two conflicting versions on the same page, and almost never state how any was produced.

No regulator or awarding-body claim, and no examiner descriptions. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, has no office or centre anywhere in the UAE, and does not describe tutors as IB examiners because current examiner status is not something we can evidence. Examiner status also confers no access to marking, boundaries or paper content, whatever anybody implies.

And we will decline a session time rather than take it. If a family proposes half seven for a Year 12 physics slot after a long run from Al Barsha, we will say that the hour is too late for the subject and propose a weekend block instead. That costs us bookings occasionally and it is the honest position: physics taught to a tired student is a cost rather than an investment.

faqs.question: What time can a physics session start after the Town Square school run?
faqs.answer: For a short run — South View in Remraam, or Fairgreen in The Sustainable City — around 4:15pm to 4:30pm. From GEMS Metropole in Motor City or the Dubai Sports City cluster in peak traffic, 4:45pm. From an inner-city school in Al Barsha or Silicon Oasis, closer to five, and many of those families choose an 8pm slot instead. These times exist only because nobody is driving to you; a visiting tutor leaving another part of Dubai in the same traffic realistically starts at half six.

faqs.question: Why does the session time matter so much for physics specifically?
faqs.answer: Because of what a physics session actually demands. Following a derivation, carrying units through four steps without losing one, holding a free-body diagram in mind while resolving forces in an unfamiliar direction — none of that survives a tired hour, in a way that reading a chapter and retaining something does. Physics is the most attention-expensive subject on a Diploma timetable, so booking whichever slot happens to be free is a worse decision here than in any other subject.

faqs.question: Which window suits a Year 13 physics student in Town Square?
faqs.answer: Usually 8pm to 9:30pm, ninety minutes rather than sixty, because a full data-analysis question plus proper marking does not fit in an hour and the marking is the part that teaches. It is also the right slot for dedicated Higher Level practical paper work. The 4:45pm window suits Year 12 and MYP students better, while attention is fresh enough for new technique. The 7pm slot looks convenient and consumes the student's own most productive independent hour.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma is physics tutoring worth most?
faqs.answer: The summer before Year 12 and the first term of Year 12. The summer is the only period when a Town Square week has genuinely spare hours, and it is the right time for bridging work: algebraic rearrangement, logarithms, graph reading and uncertainty basics, all of which the course assumes and does not teach. The first term of Year 12 is when uncertainty technique should be taught properly rather than absorbed incidentally. By the spring of Year 13 only paper technique remains movable.

faqs.question: Why is my child struggling with IB physics after a good IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Because the step is real and a strong IGCSE result offers no protection against it. IGCSE physics rewards recall and single-step calculation; Diploma physics expects derivation, multi-step reasoning, uncertainty treatment and graph linearisation. The slip usually becomes visible around November of Year 12, and it is the curriculum rather than a decline in ability. The effective intervention is a short block on the algebra and uncertainty layer, done early, before two years of content is built on top of it.

faqs.question: How should a Town Square HL student prepare for the third physics paper?
faqs.answer: It is the third written paper only HL candidates sit, and it tests experimental technique and data analysis directly: reading instruments to a justified precision, spotting that a method cannot answer its question, identifying uncontrolled variables, building correct results tables, linearising to read physics from a gradient, and judging whether a conclusion is supported. Schools reach it late inside a crowded practical timetable. One real past data-analysis question a week, marked properly rather than discussed, is the shape that works.

faqs.question: When should investigation coaching start for a Town Square physics student?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, at both Higher and Standard Level, and most of those marks are decided before any data exists. The recurring faults are a research question whose independent variable cannot be varied systematically, a range too narrow for a relationship to show above the noise, two readings per point so nothing honest can be said about reliability, and apparatus whose uncertainty exceeds the effect. None of those is rescuable by a better conclusion, which is why week-one criterion reading beats week-ten draft reading.

faqs.question: Does taking AI maths alongside Physics HL cause a problem?
faqs.answer: It creates a specific gap worth planning for rather than a problem. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and technology rather than algebraic manipulation, so a student can be doing well in maths and still lack the rearrangement, index and logarithm fluency the physics paper assumes. The pairing is common in Dubai schools and workable, provided the algebra is taught explicitly alongside. Six to ten focused sessions on rearrangement, indices, logarithms and gradient reasoning changes how every later physics session lands.

faqs.question: Is there an HL physics specialist living near Town Square?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The IB is around 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils spread across the whole emirate, only the final two years sit the Diploma, and Physics at Higher Level is a narrow specialism inside that. The pool who have taught it to final grade is small citywide, and most are serving school staff whose permit code of conduct bars tutoring students enrolled at their own school. Town Square is also a newer community where residential build-out outran tutoring supply. Online matching removes distance from the problem.

faqs.question: Can we have an in-home physics tutor in Town Square instead?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram delivers physics tuition to Town Square one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. Beyond that, in-home is particularly poor value for Diploma physics from this community: published rates are AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and the drive pushes the start past six, so you pay more per hour for a worse hour in the subject that tolerates a late slot least well.

faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures read in October 2026: qualified online subject tutors AED 150-300 an hour with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, IB specialists AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate giving AED 200-450 plus, budget online from AED 33-65 with Tutopiya and EdFlik, in-home visits AED 180-500 including travel, and BartyED at AED 650 premium. faqs.question: How do physics sessions change during Ramadan in Town Square?
faqs.answer: They move, and planning the move beats improvising it. School days shorten and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so the usual slot stops working. Families here typically switch to a late-morning or early-afternoon session, move to post-Iftar, or pause part of the month and resume with a heavier block. Content should also shift towards consolidation rather than new technique, which suits a shorter attention span better anyway. Tell us the pattern and we reset the fixed slot deliberately rather than losing the thread.

faqs.question: Will you turn down a session time if it does not suit the subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we do. If a family proposes half seven for a Year 12 physics slot after a long run from Al Barsha, we will say the hour is too late for the subject and offer a weekend block instead rather than taking the booking. Physics taught to a tired student is a cost rather than an investment, and the arrangement tends to end in February with nobody quite deciding to end it. Saying so occasionally loses us bookings, which is why it is worth stating.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover physics and maths for a Town Square student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in this pairing specifically there is a real argument for it: the algebraic and graphical demands overlap heavily, so one specialist teaches the rearrangement layer once rather than twice and stops a student treating the two as unrelated subjects. It also lets one person weigh a physics investigation deadline against a maths mock instead of two tutors each optimising for their own subject. What we will not do is stretch a tutor across courses they do not genuinely teach to save a second match.

faqs.question: When are IB physics exams for students in Town Square?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no specific IB date, and the reason matters: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, and we will not put an unverified date in front of a family who will plan around it. Get exact dates from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. For IGCSE siblings, Cambridge runs June and November series — February/March is India-only — and Pearson runs May/June and November.

intro.heading: Umm Al Sheif, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa: one question, one answer
paragraphs: Umm Al Sheif is a small residential pocket in Dubai. It runs inland from Jumeirah Beach Road towards Al Wasl Road, bordered by Umm Suqeim to the west, Al Safa to the east and Al Manara across the Sheikh Zayed Road side. A family in Umm Al Sheif, a family three streets over in Umm Suqeim 2, and a family behind Safa Park are all within a ten-minute drive of each other, send their children to an overlapping set of schools, and search for Physics help using whichever area name appears on their tenancy contract.

That matters because the local-tutor model treats those three addresses as three different markets. A freelance Physics tutor who lives in Al Barsha quotes one travel surcharge to Umm Al Sheif and another to Al Safa. A tuition centre on Al Wasl Road draws from the streets that can reach it before the 5pm traffic. The pool of people who can physically reach your gate at a fixed hour on a Tuesday is small, and it gets smaller the more specific your requirement becomes. Higher Level Physics with a weak grasp of fields is a specific requirement.

Online delivery removes the variable entirely. The answer to "who can teach my child Paper 2 Higher Level Physics" stops depending on which side of Al Hadiqa Street you live on. The question becomes which tutor knows the 2023 themes well enough to spot that your child is not bad at circuits but is mishandling internal resistance, and that is a question about the tutor, not about geography. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Umm Al Sheif are delivered one-to-one over live video, and the comparison table further down this page sets out what that trades away and what it buys back.

The Physics-specific part of the argument is sharper than the general one. Diploma Physics is not a subject where a generalist maths tutor can improvise. The 2023 subject guide reorganised the course into five themes, folded the old options away, and rebuilt assessment around Paper 1A multiple choice, Paper 1B data and practical questions, and Paper 2 short and extended response. A tutor who last taught the pre-2023 course will set your child practice that no longer matches the paper. That is a syllabus problem, and no amount of proximity fixes it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.programmesIntro: Physics sits at the end of a ten-year run through the IB continuum. A student in Umm Al Sheif who struggles with Diploma Physics in Year 12 usually has a gap that opened earlier, in MYP Sciences or in the mathematics that Physics assumes. These are the three programmes and what each one needs from a tutor.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics at Standard Level runs 150 teaching hours and Higher Level 240. Both sit the same two papers with different durations and different depth: Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44%, the Scientific Investigation at 20%. The five themes are space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level adds extension content inside each theme rather than a separate options block.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Sheif families reach Diploma Physics through a handful of schools in the Jumeirah and Al Sufouh corridor, including Jumeirah Baccalaureate School in Al Safa, Emirates International School on the Jumeirah side of Sheikh Zayed Road, and the larger IB schools a short drive inland. All are KHDA-inspected. Each sets its own internal investigation deadlines, which is why lesson sequencing has to be built around the school's calendar rather than a generic one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Each criterion is marked out of 8 against descriptors, not out of a percentage. Students arriving into Diploma Physics from MYP have usually met the investigation skills but not the algebra density, because MYP Science rarely pushes rearrangement, indices and trigonometric resolution as hard as Physics does.
programmes.countryNote: In this part of Dubai a child may do MYP at one school and then move for the Diploma, so the handover is rarely clean. The gap that shows up in Umm Al Sheif cohorts most often is vector resolution: a student who can describe an experiment well cannot split a 240 N force on a 23-degree slope. That is a two-session fix in Year 11 and a recurring loss of marks if it reaches Year 12 untouched.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme has no external examination. Learning runs through transdisciplinary units of inquiry, and reporting is against learner-profile attributes and conceptual understanding rather than subject marks. For a family whose older child is doing Diploma Physics, the relevant PYP point is numeracy fluency: the arithmetic and measurement habits laid down here are the ones Physics later leans on without teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Several Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim primaries run PYP, and parents in Umm Al Sheif often have one child in PYP and another in MYP or the Diploma at the same time. Where that happens we keep the siblings on separate tutors, because the teaching skills do not transfer: an inquiry-based primary specialist and a Higher Level Physics specialist are different people, and pretending otherwise short-changes one of the two.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: The Diploma core sits outside the six subjects and still shapes a Physics student's year. A Physics Extended Essay has to pose a researchable question with measurable variables, which is a harder brief than most students expect, and the three Theory of Knowledge assessment points compete for the same weeks as the Physics investigation. Core deadlines are what usually causes a strong Physics student's term to collapse.
programmes.countryNote: The practical consequence for an Umm Al Sheif household is calendar management. School core deadlines in Dubai tend to cluster in the second term, so Physics revision has to be front-loaded into the first. A tutor who does not ask what the school's Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge dates are will schedule Physics work into a fortnight the student has already lost.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.subjectsIntro: Physics is the page, but students in Umm Al Sheif rarely take it alone, and the combination changes the tutoring plan. A Higher Level Physics student taking Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches needs different support from one taking Applications and Interpretation, because the calculus arrives at different times.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, two papers and one investigation. Marks are lost in Paper 1B's data questions, where uncertainty handling and significant figures are assessed directly, and in Paper 2's extended response, where students describe a physical situation instead of explaining it. Higher Level extension content sits inside the themes, so a student cannot skip a topic and hope it was optional.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The natural partner to Higher Level Physics. Differentiation and integration arrive here before Physics needs them for fields and for rates of change, so a student behind in Analysis and Approaches is behind twice. Proof and algebraic fluency are the two areas Umm Al Sheif students most often ask for help with alongside Physics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistically weighted and technology-heavy, which suits a student heading towards economics or design but leaves gaps that Physics then exposes. Students on this route need targeted work on algebraic rearrangement and on graph gradients with units, because Physics assumes both and Applications and Interpretation does not drill them.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Taken with Physics by most students aiming at engineering or medicine. The investigation criteria are shared across the sciences, so a student doing both can prepare one set of research-design skills and apply it twice. The energetics and kinetics topics also overlap conceptually with Physics thermodynamics, which makes joint revision efficient.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Often the third science for a medicine applicant. The volume of terminology is the challenge rather than the mathematics, and the command terms behave differently: an "explain" in Biology wants a mechanism, in Physics it wants a causal chain with a principle named. Students who confuse the two lose marks in both subjects.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paired with Physics by students who like modelling. The internal assessment is a developed solution rather than an experiment, so a student taking both has two very different coursework projects running at once. Sequencing those two deadlines is a scheduling job before it is a teaching job.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Shares the mechanics and materials content with Physics and assesses it through a design cycle instead of a paper. Students who take both can reuse Physics calculations inside Design Technology coursework, provided the work remains their own and is referenced where it draws on taught material.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: A frequent alternative where a student wants a science without Physics mathematics. The biomechanics section still uses force, moment and energy, so students who dropped Physics sometimes find it again here. Short targeted sessions on the mechanics subset are usually all that is needed.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A common sixth subject for Umm Al Sheif students who are strong in Physics but want a social science. The diagram discipline is the transferable skill: labelled axes, stated units and an explained shift, which is exactly what Physics graph questions want and what students lose marks for skipping.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Relevant to a Physics student because the extended-response marks in Paper 2 reward structured written argument. Students who write well in English A and badly in Physics are usually not writing badly; they are answering a different question from the one asked. sections.heading: What a search for an IB Physics tutor in Umm Al Sheif is really asking
paragraphs: The phrase is a proximity search, and the need behind it is almost never proximity. A parent types an area name because that is how search works, not because distance is the requirement. The requirement is a person who knows the 2023 Physics subject guide, can diagnose which of the five themes is actually failing, and is available at a time that survives the school run.

Umm Al Sheif is a compact residential area and it has no Diploma school of its own. Every Physics student living here commutes, most of them to the Jumeirah, Al Safa, Al Sufouh or Al Barsha schools. That means the student's syllabus, teacher, internal deadlines and mock timetable all belong to a school somewhere else. A tutor's usefulness depends on knowing those, and none of them are visible from the street the tutor lives on.

So the honest reading of the search is this: the parent wants a Physics specialist, reliably, soon, at a predictable hour. Umm Al Sheif is how they described where they are. IB Gram answers the search with online one-to-one lessons, matched on subject and level, and the rest of this page shows the working rather than asking anyone to take it on trust.

The comparison that follows is deliberate. If the answer for Umm Al Sheif is the same as the answer for Umm Suqeim and Al Safa, that is worth demonstrating with the detail rather than asserting, because a parent who has already been quoted a travel surcharge by a local tutor is entitled to see why the surcharge buys nothing a Physics student needs.

sections.heading: The Physics assessment structure, component by component
paragraphs: Diploma Physics is assessed through two written papers and one internal investigation at both Standard and Higher Level. Paper 1 carries 36% and splits into two parts sat together: Paper 1A is multiple choice, Paper 1B is data-based and practical-technique questions. Paper 2 carries 44% and runs short-response into extended-response questions. The Scientific Investigation carries the remaining 20%.

The split inside Paper 1 is the part parents most often do not know, and it changes how revision should be organised. Paper 1A rewards speed and precision on a wide spread of content. Paper 1B rewards a narrow set of skills done properly: reading a graph, propagating an uncertainty, recognising a systematic error, quoting a result to a defensible number of significant figures. Those are trainable in a handful of sessions and they are worth marks on every single sitting.

Higher Level is not a different course with extra papers. The 2023 structure puts Higher Level extension content inside the same five themes, which means a Higher Level student who ignores a theme loses access to both core and extension marks on that material. The practical consequence is that theme-by-theme coverage has to be complete before any paper-technique work can pay off.

Teaching hours differ: 150 at Standard Level, 240 at Higher. That ratio is the single most useful planning number a parent has, because it tells you roughly how much additional depth a Higher Level student is expected to have absorbed in the same two years, and therefore how much more support the subject tends to need.

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The investigation is worth a fifth of the grade and it is marked out of 24, across four criteria of 6 marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. No competitor page in this market names a single one of those criteria, which is remarkable given that it is a fifth of the subject and the one component a student has months to improve.

Most lost marks are lost in research design, and they are lost early. A research question that cannot be answered by the data the student is able to collect cannot recover later, no matter how clean the graphs are. The fix is unglamorous: narrow the question until the independent variable has a range the student can actually produce and the dependent variable has a measurable response across it.

Data analysis is where the uncertainty work shows up for marks a second time, after Paper 1B. Error bars that appear without justification, gradients quoted without units, and a line of best fit drawn through a curve are the three most common losses. Evaluation is where strong students under-score: they list limitations instead of ranking them by effect on the conclusion, which is what the descriptor asks for.

What a tutor does here is bounded, and the boundary is worth stating plainly on a public page. A tutor teaches the technique, questions the design, and gives feedback against the descriptors. The student plans, performs, processes and writes their own investigation. Any arrangement where someone else produces the text is academic malpractice under IB rules and puts the student's entire diploma at risk, and we will not take that work.

sections.heading: Where Umm Al Sheif Physics students actually lose marks
paragraphs: Diagnosis beats coverage. A student who scores 4 in Physics is rarely weak across all five themes; they are usually strong in two, functional in two and missing something structural in one. Finding the structural gap is worth more than a full revision cycle, and it takes a tutor one or two sessions of watching the student work rather than talking at them.

In this cluster the recurring structural gaps are predictable. Vector resolution comes first: a student who cannot split a force on an inclined plane will lose marks in space, time and motion, and again in fields. Internal resistance comes second: students treat a cell as an ideal source and then cannot explain why terminal voltage drops. Phase relationships in simple harmonic motion come third, because the mathematics is sine and cosine but the physics is about what is happening at the extremes.

A fourth pattern is linguistic rather than physical. The command terms carry precise mark expectations: state wants an answer with no working, explain wants a causal chain, determine wants a calculation shown, deduce wants a conclusion drawn from given information. Students who answer the wrong command term write perfectly correct physics and score nothing for it. This is the single fastest-paying thing to fix in the eight weeks before a session.

The fifth pattern is graph literacy. Physics graph questions want axes labelled with quantity and unit, a gradient interpreted physically rather than numerically, and an intercept explained. Students lose these marks in Paper 1B, in Paper 2 and inside the investigation, which means one block of teaching repairs three components at once.

paragraphs: Start with the monthly number, because that is the one a household budget actually feels. A single weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor at market rates lands somewhere around AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month, on Bestimate's published mid-tier monthly estimate for weekly one-hour sessions. Specialist examination-year support in the same source's estimate runs AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and upwards. Two sessions a week roughly doubles it.

Converted to hourly bands, the Dubai market sorts into five tiers. Budget online tuition, often delivered by university students, sits at AED 45 to AED 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to AED 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500 to AED 650, with BartyED at AED 650. Those are the market's figures, published by those providers, not ours.

The interesting band is in-home one-to-one, quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel, with Bestimate at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors reaching AED 500. The premium over online qualified tuition is real and it is substantial. What it buys is a person in the room. What it does not buy is subject depth, because the pool you can draw from is limited to whoever can reach Umm Al Sheif at your preferred hour.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on this page, and that is deliberate rather than evasive: the figures above are the market's, cited to who published them, and quoting our own number next to them would turn a reference table into an advertisement. A free trial lesson and a consultation establish what your child's Physics gap actually is first, which is the only sensible basis for a quote. Monthly packages in this market have been advertised around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is a useful sense of the spread.

sections.heading: Online lessons against a tutor driving to Umm Al Sheif
paragraphs: This is the comparison the page exists for, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales argument. In-home tutoring has genuine advantages: a young child concentrates better with an adult physically present, a reluctant teenager finds it harder to disengage, and nothing has to be set up. For a Year 4 student who needs supervision as much as teaching, in-home is often the better product.

Diploma Physics is a different case. The binding constraint is subject depth, and subject depth is exactly what a travel radius destroys. Requiring a tutor to be within a twenty-minute drive of Umm Al Sheif at 4.30pm on a Tuesday reduces the candidate pool to a handful of people, and the probability that one of them is a Higher Level Physics specialist who understands the four investigation criteria is not high. Online, the radius constraint disappears and the only filter left is competence.

The practical differences are smaller than people expect. Working is shared on a digital whiteboard, which has the useful side effect of being saved and re-readable, something a page of handwriting in an exercise book is not. Diagrams are drawn live. Past papers are annotated on screen where both parties can see them. Experimental technique is taught through the student's own data, which is what the investigation requires anyway. A document camera handles anything that needs to be shown on paper.

To be explicit, because the market is full of ambiguity on this point: IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for an Umm Al Sheif family is one-to-one over live video, and the trial lesson exists so that you can test whether that format works for your child before committing to anything.

sections.heading: The examination calendar counted backwards
paragraphs: Almost nobody in this market writes about sessions, deadlines or results dates, which is strange, because the calendar is what determines whether tutoring arrives in time to be useful. The principle is simple: work backwards from the sitting, not forwards from today. Everything a Physics student has to do has a latest-useful date, and most of those dates are months before the paper.

For Diploma Physics, UAE schools sit the May session as the main examination series, with November available as the alternative sitting. IB session and results dates are set and published by the IB, and this page deliberately does not state them: the authoritative source is ibo.org and your child's IB coordinator, and a date restated second-hand is a date that can be wrong. Ask the coordinator for the school's own internal deadline schedule, which is the one that actually governs the student's term.

For the IGCSE qualifications that feed into the Diploma, the dates are published and can be stated. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series that Cambridge also operates is offered to India only, so it is not a route available from Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, because it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after reading the wrong one.

Backward-looking dates are worth keeping because they make the pattern checkable. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That January gap is the reason a November resit is a slow route: the result arrives most of a term later. Always open the live official timetable rather than trusting any restated date, including the ones above.

sections.heading: KHDA, inspection bands and the mandatory UAE subjects
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. For an Umm Al Sheif family, KHDA is the one that matters, and its inspection reports are public.

Scale is worth knowing. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with UK programmes at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Seven new private schools were announced for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places.

An inspection band is useful context and a poor proxy for a single student's Physics outcome. A school rated Outstanding can still have a Higher Level Physics set in which several students are losing marks on uncertainty handling, and a school in a lower band can have an exceptional Physics department. Read the subject-level commentary in the report rather than the headline band if you want something that bears on your decision.

One thing a parent in Umm Al Sheif should know regardless of curriculum: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum they are licensed for, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These subjects sit alongside Diploma Physics in the student's week and compete for the same hours.

sections.heading: Permits, academic honesty and what a Physics tutor may not do
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here; figures circulating online could not be verified against an official source. A separate point worth knowing: Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules have been reported as barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct along the same lines. Marketing a child's own classroom teacher as a private tutor is not a route we will arrange.

The academic-honesty boundary in Physics is specific and it is where this market is at its worst. One page found in this SERP sells completed Internal Assessments. That is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, who can lose the diploma. A tutor may teach experimental design, explain uncertainty propagation, question whether a conclusion follows from the data, and give feedback against the published criteria. A tutor may not produce the report, rewrite it into final form, or supply data the student did not collect.

Two related limits apply to materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter. And IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Anyone advertising tutors as having been given approval by KHDA is telling you something about themselves rather than about the regulator.

process.title: Tell us the theme, not just the subject
process.description: The useful first message is specific: Higher Level Physics, Year 12, struggling with fields, investigation due in six weeks, school in Al Safa. That tells us which specialist to look for. "Needs Physics help" tells us nothing a matching system can act on, and it is the main reason a first match goes wrong.

process.title: A free trial lesson, used as a diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a working session, not a sales call. The tutor sets the student a short sequence of problems and watches where the reasoning breaks. You get a written note naming the specific gap. If the gap is vector resolution rather than fields, the plan changes, and it is better to find that out before paying for anything.

process.title: Match against the school's calendar
process.description: We ask for the school's internal investigation deadline, mock window and reporting dates, then build the lesson sequence backwards from those. A plan that ignores the school's dates will schedule content revision into the fortnight the student has already committed to coursework, which wastes both the time and the money.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a written record
process.description: Each lesson ends with a short note: what was covered, what the student got wrong and why, what to practise before next week. The shared whiteboard file is saved. Parents can read the note without sitting in the lesson, which is usually what they actually want rather than a monthly report.

process.title: Change the tutor if the match is wrong
process.description: Subject competence and teaching fit are different things, and a tutor who suits one student may not suit the next. If the fit is wrong after two or three sessions, say so and we move the student. No case is made for persevering with a match that is not working; that costs the student weeks it cannot get back.

whyPoints.title: The 2023 subject guide, not the previous one
whyPoints.description: Physics was restructured for first examinations in 2025: five themes, Higher Level extension content embedded, Paper 1 split into 1A and 1B. A tutor working from the old options-based course will set practice that no longer matches the paper. Our Physics tutors work from the current guide and the current command terms.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before coverage
whyPoints.description: A student scoring 4 usually has one structural gap, not five weak themes. We spend the first sessions finding it by watching the student work, because repairing vector resolution or uncertainty handling moves more marks than a second pass through content the student already knows.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on coursework
whyPoints.description: The investigation is the student's own work, and we say so to the student in the first session. We teach technique and give feedback against the four criteria. We do not produce the report. In a market where one page openly sells completed investigations, that boundary is worth stating rather than assuming.

whyPoints.title: No tutor pool limited by a drive from Umm Al Sheif
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run over live video, the person teaching your child is chosen for knowing Higher Level Physics rather than for living near Al Hadiqa Street. That is the whole substantive difference between this page's answer and a local-tutor listing, and it is a larger difference than it sounds.

whyPoints.title: Figures that carry their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names who published it. Every regulatory statement names the authority. We publish no invented satisfaction percentage, no self-awarded star rating and no tutor headcount, because a number without a source is worth nothing to a parent trying to compare providers.

whyPoints.title: Sessions built around the school's dates
whyPoints.description: Umm Al Sheif students attend schools across Jumeirah, Al Safa, Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, each with its own internal deadlines. We ask for those dates before planning, so revision lands in weeks the student has available rather than in the fortnight the coursework deadline already owns.

faqs.question: Can I get a Physics tutor who comes to our villa in Umm Al Sheif?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We do not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for an Umm Al Sheif family is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason is not convenience but tutor quality: requiring someone to be within a short drive of your gate at a fixed weekday hour shrinks the pool to whoever lives nearby and is free, and the chance that person is a Higher Level Physics specialist is low. Online, you choose on subject depth instead. The market does offer in-home visits at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, so the option exists elsewhere if physical presence is the priority.

faqs.question: Does it matter that we live in Umm Al Sheif rather than Al Safa or Umm Suqeim?
faqs.answer: For the academic side, no. Those three neighbourhoods feed an overlapping set of schools, their Diploma Physics students sit the same papers against the same subject guide, and the internal deadlines come from the school rather than the street. What differs between them is travel time, which only matters if a tutor has to drive. Al Safa does have a higher concentration of IB Diploma students because of the schools sited there, which thins the local pool for Higher Level science help faster than in Umm Al Sheif. That is an argument for choosing a tutor on competence rather than on distance, which is what online delivery lets you do.

faqs.question: How is Paper 1 split, and why does that change how we revise?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% of the Physics grade and is sat in two parts. Paper 1A is multiple choice across all five themes. Paper 1B is data-based and practical-technique questions. They fail differently. Paper 1A punishes slow working and guessing by elimination. Paper 1B punishes weak uncertainty handling, careless significant figures and the inability to tell a random error from a systematic one. Revising them as one block hides which of the two is losing the marks. We practise them separately, timed, and look at the error patterns rather than the score, because 1B skills are trainable in a handful of sessions and pay out on every sitting.

faqs.question: What exactly are the four criteria the Scientific Investigation is marked against?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth 6 marks, for 24 in total, and the component is 20% of the Physics grade at both levels. Research design wants a focused question with justified methodology and controlled variables. Data analysis wants correct processing, uncertainties and sensible graphing. Conclusion wants a result justified by the data and set against accepted theory. Evaluation wants strengths and weaknesses weighted by their actual effect on the conclusion, not a list. Most marks go missing in research design, because a question too broad for the available apparatus cannot be rescued later however well the rest is written.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Physics investigation without crossing an honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear enough to state. A tutor may teach experimental design, explain uncertainty propagation, challenge whether a conclusion follows from the data, and give feedback against the published descriptors. A tutor may not produce the report, rewrite it into its final form, or supply data the student did not collect. The student plans, performs, processes and writes the investigation. We say this to the student in the first session. One page competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright; under IB rules that is malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student, who can lose the diploma over it.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Physics tutor cost around Jumeirah and Umm Al Sheif?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not ours. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors in Dubai are published between AED 200 and AED 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate quoting AED 200 to AED 450 upwards. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Budget online tuition sits at AED 45 to AED 150. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 600 to AED 1,200 for weekly mid-tier sessions and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 upwards for specialist examination-year support. We quote after a free trial establishes what the gap actually is.

faqs.question: My child is at Higher Level and scoring 4. Is that fixable before the session?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the first job is finding out why rather than revising harder. A student at 4 is rarely weak across all five themes; the typical pattern is strength in two, adequacy in two and a structural gap in one. In this cluster the recurring gaps are vector resolution, internal resistance treated as ideal, and simple harmonic motion described rather than reasoned. A second pattern is command-term misreading, where correct physics scores nothing because the student described when the question said explain. Both are repairable in weeks rather than terms. The honest answer depends on how many weeks remain, which is why the trial lesson is diagnostic.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Physics genuinely much harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: The teaching-hour ratio gives you the scale: 240 hours at Higher Level against 150 at Standard. Both sit Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the investigation at 20%, and both cover the same five themes. The difference is depth, and in the 2023 structure the Higher Level extension content sits inside those themes rather than in a separate options block. That has a practical consequence: a Higher Level student who skips a theme loses the core marks on it as well as the extension marks, so partial coverage is more costly than it used to be. Complete theme coverage has to come before any paper-technique work.

faqs.question: Which schools do Umm Al Sheif Physics students usually attend?
faqs.answer: Umm Al Sheif has no Diploma school of its own, so every student here commutes. The coastal cluster includes Jumeirah Baccalaureate School in Al Safa, Emirates International School on the Jumeirah side of Sheikh Zayed Road, Horizon English School, Jumeirah College, Kings' School Dubai and Raffles World Academy. Inland within a short drive sit Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School, Dubai American Academy, Kings' School Al Barsha and Nord Anglia International School Dubai. All are inspected by KHDA. We name them to describe the local school landscape; IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them.

faqs.question: When do UAE students actually sit the examinations my child is working towards?
faqs.answer: For the IB Diploma, UAE schools sit the May session as the main series, with November as the alternative sitting. We deliberately do not publish IB session or results dates here, because the authoritative source is the IB and your child's IB coordinator, and a second-hand date can be wrong in a way a parent acts on. For the IGCSE qualifications that feed in, Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge assigns every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used.

faqs.question: Is the Physics tutor teaching my child legally permitted to tutor in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold the permit.

faqs.question: Does online teaching work for a practical subject like Physics?
faqs.answer: For the assessed parts, yes, and in one respect better. Written working is shared on a digital whiteboard which is saved and re-readable, unlike a page in an exercise book. Past papers are annotated on screen. Diagrams are drawn live. Experimental technique is taught through the student's own data, which is what the investigation requires in any case, because the student must collect it themselves. What online cannot replace is the school laboratory, and it is not meant to: the apparatus work belongs at school with the teacher supervising. A document camera covers anything that has to be shown on paper.

faqs.question: How does the school's own timetable affect when tutoring should start?
faqs.answer: It governs everything, and most plans fail by ignoring it. Each Dubai school sets its own internal investigation deadline, mock window and Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge dates. In this cluster the core deadlines tend to cluster in the second term, which means Physics content revision has to be front-loaded into the first or it collides with a fortnight the student has already lost. We ask for those dates before building a lesson sequence. A tutor who does not ask will schedule revision into weeks that are already committed, and the family pays for sessions the student cannot absorb.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education really compulsory alongside the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, in every Dubai private school whatever international curriculum it is licensed for. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory, and KHDA required its arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Physics student the practical effect is on the weekly timetable: these lessons compete for the same hours as revision.

faqs.question: What should I send when asking for a Physics tutor, to get the right match first time?
faqs.answer: Five things, and it takes two minutes. The level, Higher or Standard. The year group and the school, so we know whose internal deadlines apply. The specific theme or topic where marks are being lost, if you know it, or the most recent report if you do not. The dates that are fixed, such as an investigation deadline or a mock window. And two or three time slots that survive the school run. A message with those five lines gets a specialist match. A message saying "needs Physics help" gets a guess, and a guess is the main cause of a wrong first match.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Physics and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches together?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking for rather than assuming. The two subjects overlap where Physics needs calculus for fields and rates of change, and a student behind in Analysis and Approaches is effectively behind in Physics as well. A tutor comfortable in both can repair the algebra inside the Physics lesson, which saves a session a week. Where the mathematics gap is large, two specialists work better than one generalist, because Higher Level Analysis and Approaches has proof and sequence content that a Physics teacher has no particular reason to have taught. Tell us the combination and we will say which applies.

intro.heading: Why "physics tutor near me" is the wrong search in Umm Suqeim
paragraphs: Umm Suqeim is a residential strip between Jumeirah 3 and Al Sufouh, two to three kilometres deep from Jumeirah Beach Road down to Al Wasl and Sheikh Zayed Road. It is villas, low-rise compounds and a handful of schools. What it is not is a dense pool of Higher Level physics teachers. A family here who types "IB physics tutor near me" is hoping geography and expertise happen to overlap. In a subject this narrow, they rarely do.

The number of people within a fifteen-minute drive of Umm Suqeim 2 who can teach the current IB Physics course to Higher Level is small. The course was rewritten for first examination in 2025: the old core-plus-options structure went, and five themes replaced it. A tutor who last taught physics from the 2014 guide will still recognise most of the content, but not the shape of the papers, not the single scientific investigation that replaced the old practical scheme, and not the way tools and inquiry skills are now examined inside the themes rather than beside them. Content knowledge is the easy part. Knowing which 2025-onwards command term triggers which structure of answer is the part that moves a grade.

So the honest reframing is this. Stop asking who is nearby and start asking who can answer four questions: what is the weighting split between Paper 1 and Paper 2, what does Paper 1B actually contain, how many marks is the investigation out of and across how many criteria, and what distinguishes an HL-only extension from core theme content. A tutor who answers those four without hesitating has taught the course. A tutor who answers them vaguely has read about it.

Once that is the question, distance stops mattering and starts costing. Market rates for an in-home visit in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, and part of that spread is travel. Bestimate's "Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026" rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with specialist IB and IGCSE tutors at AED 200 to 450 and above. The premium is not buying better physics. It is buying a car journey, which on Jumeirah Beach Road between four and seven in the evening is not a short one.

IB Gram's answer is to drop the radius entirely. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, so an Umm Suqeim student is matched to a physics specialist on the strength of the subject and level rather than the postcode. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. What that trade buys is specific: a tutor who has taken students through Theme D fields at Higher Level, instead of whoever is free and lives near Kite Beach.

The rest of this page is the detail a parent in this neighbourhood actually needs: the assessment structure with its real weightings, the topics where marks leak, what the market charges and who publishes those rates, the four investigation criteria with their mark allocations, the academic-honesty line a tutor must not cross, and what happens in the weeks before a May session.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.programmesIntro: Physics does not begin in DP1. An Umm Suqeim student arriving in Diploma physics has usually come through MYP sciences at an IB continuum school or through IGCSE Physics at a British-curriculum one, and the gap each route leaves is different.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Two years, five themes, and an assessment model that is three-quarters written papers. Standard Level and Higher Level share the five themes; Higher Level adds extension content inside each one rather than bolting on separate options. Paper 1 carries 36 per cent of the grade, Paper 2 carries 44 per cent, and the scientific investigation carries the remaining 20 per cent. Students sit Paper 1 in two sections: 1A is multiple choice, 1B is data and laboratory-based questions drawn across the themes.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma is the minority route by enrolment. Of the emirate's 387,441 private-school students in 2024-25, the International Baccalaureate accounted for seven per cent against 37 per cent on UK curricula. That ratio is why an Umm Suqeim family often finds plenty of tutors for IGCSE Physics 0625 and very few for DP Physics at Higher Level, and why matching by subject rather than by neighbourhood matters here more than it would in a mostly-IB market.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: MYP sciences are assessed against four criteria rather than examined on content, which makes the jump into Diploma physics a change of genre as well as difficulty. An MYP 5 student is used to being marked on inquiry design and on reflecting on the impacts of science. A DP1 student is marked on whether the number is right, the unit is right and the uncertainty is propagated correctly. Bridging work closes that gap before it shows up in a DP1 report.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Umm Suqeim and the wider Jumeirah coast run the full IB continuum, so a student can reach DP physics having never sat an externally marked science paper. Families here often ask for six to eight sessions over a summer specifically to practise timed written physics, because that is the single skill the MYP does not test and the Diploma tests hardest.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the pre-DP route
programmes.description: The commoner feeder in this part of Dubai. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 both leave a student with solid mechanics and electricity and almost no experience of uncertainty arithmetic, log-linearised graphs or the extended written response that DP Paper 2 asks for. The content overlap is reassuring and slightly misleading: a student who found 0625 comfortable can still open DP1 and find Theme A unfamiliar in style.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai by enrolment, so most Umm Suqeim students entering DP physics arrive from 0625 or 4PH1 rather than from MYP. The useful diagnostic in the first week of DP1 is not a content test. It is one past-paper data question with raw readings, because that exposes in ten minutes whether the student has ever been taught to treat uncertainty as part of the answer.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.subjectsIntro: IB Physics is now organised into five themes plus the tools and inquiry strand that runs through all of them. Below is what each theme actually assesses and where Umm Suqeim students most often lose ground, at both levels.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, and at Higher Level rigid-body rotation and relativity. The content feels familiar after IGCSE, which is the trap: questions now expect a stated model, a justified assumption and consistent significant figures. Most early DP1 marks are lost to unjustified assumptions rather than to arithmetic.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, the kinetic model, and at Higher Level entropy and the second law. Students handle the equations and then lose marks explaining why a process is irreversible. Written explanation carries real weight in Paper 2, and this theme is where vague answers cost most.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave characteristics, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect, with phase and interference extended at Higher Level. Diagrams are assessed here as answers, not decoration: an unlabelled wavefront sketch earns nothing, while a labelled one with path difference marked can carry most of the marks.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential, circuits and electromagnetic induction. The Higher Level extension on field potential and orbital motion is the single topic Umm Suqeim students most often ask for help with, usually because the mathematics of potential energy in a radial field was skipped at IGCSE entirely.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Structure of the atom, radioactive decay, nuclear binding energy, fission and fusion, and at Higher Level the photoelectric effect, matter waves and the standard model. It is often taught last and revised least, which makes it unusually profitable in a six-week programme before a May session.

subjects.name: Tools and inquiry: experimental technique
subjects.description: Measurement, instrument resolution, systematic against random error, and the choice of independent and dependent variables. The current guide examines these inside the themes and inside Paper 1B rather than treating them as a separate unit, so a student cannot leave them to the week before the investigation is due.

subjects.name: Tools and inquiry: data and uncertainty
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through products and powers, uncertainty bars, maximum and minimum gradients. This is the highest-yield block of teaching available in DP physics and the one most commonly missing from a student's toolkit on arrival from IGCSE.

subjects.name: Tools and inquiry: mathematics for physics
subjects.description: Rearrangement, exponentials and logarithms, small-angle approximations, vector resolution and the linearisation of a non-linear relationship. A student taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation alongside Higher Level physics usually needs explicit work on logarithmic plotting, because the maths course meets it later than physics needs it.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL · 20% of the grade
subjects.description: One open investigation of up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each. Research design and evaluation are where marks cluster and where they are lost. A tutor's role is to question the research design, review the student's own analysis and give feedback, never to write the report.

subjects.name: Higher Level extension content
subjects.description: The additional material sits inside the five themes rather than in separate options, so Higher Level students cannot revise an HL section in isolation. Each theme has to be revisited at its deeper level, which is why an HL repair programme is typically ten to twelve sessions rather than four.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB Physics tutor in Umm Suqeim actually turns up
paragraphs: A search for an IB Physics tutor in Umm Suqeim returns three kinds of result, and only one of them is a physics specialist. The first is a general tutoring agency listing every subject from Year 1 phonics to A Level further maths. The second is an independent tutor advertising on a community group, usually strong in mathematics and willing to take physics. The third is an international platform with no UAE presence that will route your enquiry to a tutor in another time zone and quote in dollars.

None of those is dishonest, but none of them answers the question you asked. What a DP2 student losing marks in Theme D needs is somebody who has taught field potential at Higher Level under the current guide and has marked the data questions in Paper 1B. That is a narrow qualification, and the probability that such a person lives within a 15-minute drive of Umm Suqeim 2 and happens to be free at 5pm on a Tuesday is low. It is not a comment on Umm Suqeim. The same arithmetic applies in Mirdif, Arabian Ranches and Khalifa City.

The useful move is to separate two things parents merge. Proximity solves logistics. Specialism solves physics. For a subject taken by a minority of a minority — Higher Level physics inside a programme that is seven per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment — insisting on both at once usually means quietly giving up the second. IB Gram solves logistics with scheduling instead of with driving: one-to-one lessons over live video in Gulf Standard Time, so the specialist requirement never has to be traded away.

That is the whole argument of this page, and everything below it is the evidence: what the course actually examines, where marks leak, what the market charges for each format, and what a tutor is and is not permitted to do with a scientific investigation.

sections.heading: The IB Physics course your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: The Physics guide first examined in 2025 replaced the old core, additional-higher-level and options structure with five themes, A to E, taken by Standard and Higher Level students alike. Higher Level content is embedded inside each theme as extension material rather than parcelled into separate sections. That single structural change explains most of the confusion when a family hires a tutor who last taught the previous guide: the content is largely recognisable, the architecture is not.

Assessment is three components. Paper 1 runs in two sections — 1A is multiple choice, 1B is data-based and laboratory-focused questions drawn across the themes — and together they carry 36 per cent of the final grade. Paper 2 is structured and extended response, worth 44 per cent. The scientific investigation, marked internally against published criteria and moderated by the IB, carries the remaining 20 per cent. Paper 1B is the component most often neglected, because it looks like a short section and in fact examines the experimental and uncertainty skills a student has either been taught or has not.

Durations differ by level and are the first thing worth checking on your child's own school assessment schedule, since mocks are usually timed to match. The weightings below are the published figures for the current guide; the per-paper content descriptions are what a tutor should be able to recite without looking.

One practical consequence of the 36-44-20 split: a student who treats the investigation as an inconvenient coursework task is discarding a fifth of the grade that is, uniquely, not time-pressured. It is the one component where unhurried, well-supervised work converts directly into marks, and the one where a tutor's feedback has the clearest effect inside the academic-honesty rules.

sections.heading: Where IB Physics marks actually leak, topic by topic
paragraphs: Marks in DP physics are rarely lost where a student thinks they are lost. A report that says "needs to work on Theme D" is almost never accurate at that resolution. The loss is usually one repeatable habit expressed across several topics: a missing unit, an unstated assumption, a graph gradient read without uncertainty, an explanation that describes instead of explaining. Fixing the habit fixes several topics at once, which is why a diagnostic first session is worth more than four sessions of content revision.

The pattern in this corridor is consistent enough to be useful. Students arriving in DP1 from IGCSE Physics 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 are strong on circuits and mechanics and almost untrained on uncertainty. Students arriving from MYP sciences are confident designing an investigation and unpractised at timed written answers. Students at Higher Level who were comfortable through DP1 commonly come unstuck in the field-potential extension in Theme D, where the mathematics is heavier than anything the first year required.

The table below maps the symptom a parent can see — usually in a mock script — to what is actually missing underneath it. The repair estimates are honest ranges for one-to-one work, not promises: a student who has never propagated an uncertainty needs two sessions to learn the arithmetic and several weeks of applying it to make it automatic.

One warning about diagnosing from a percentage. A mock mark of 54 per cent tells you almost nothing about which of these rows applies, and a tutor who plans a programme from the percentage rather than from the script is guessing. Ask for the marked paper. Everything useful is in the examiner's crossings-out, not in the total.
