sections.heading: Eight questions that tell you whether a tutor knows this syllabus
paragraphs: Credentials are a weak filter in this market. A physics degree, twenty years in a classroom and a reference from a neighbour are all compatible with never having taught the current IB guide. What separates a specialist from a competent generalist is a set of specifics that cannot be bluffed in a trial lesson, and a parent does not need to understand physics to ask for them. You only need to notice whether the answer is immediate and precise or general and warm.

Ask them during a free trial lesson, which is exactly what a trial is for. A tutor who has taught the course answers all eight in under two minutes. A tutor who answers three well and waves at the rest may still be a good mathematics tutor, and that is worth knowing before DP2 rather than during it.

The last two questions matter most and are asked least. Academic honesty on the investigation is the point where a well-meaning tutor can cause a student real damage, and a tutor who is hazy about where the line sits is a risk regardless of how well they teach Theme A. A clear answer sounds like this: the student designs it, the student collects the data, the student writes it, and the tutor asks questions and gives feedback on what the student has produced.

Note too what is not on the list. Nothing here asks about examiner status. Examiner experience can be genuinely useful, but it is also the most-claimed and least-verifiable credential in this market, and it implies nothing about access to papers, mark schemes or boundaries. Judge the teaching, not the badge.
bullets: What is the weighting split between Paper 1, Paper 2 and the investigation?
What does Paper 1B contain that Paper 1A does not?
Name the five themes and tell me which carries the heaviest HL extension.
How many marks is the investigation and across how many criteria?
Show me how you would propagate an uncertainty through a square.
What does "deduce" require that "state" does not?
Where is the line between reviewing my child's investigation and writing it?
If my child takes Maths AI rather than AA, what do you teach differently?

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs around Umm Suqeim, and what you can verify yourself
paragraphs: Start with what is checkable rather than with what is advertised. Any parent in Umm Suqeim can establish the local rate for Diploma physics in an afternoon: ask three providers for a written per-hour figure, ask whether it is per hour or per session, ask whether it includes travel, and ask whether the quoted price includes VAT. Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for UAE queries publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in dollars, so the number you are given on the phone is often the only number that exists.

The published market figures, read in October 2026, sort into five bands. Budget online tuition with a university-student tutor runs about AED 45 to 150 an hour, with agency rate cards starting as low as AED 33 to 65. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with IGCSE entry points near AED 150 and IB near AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180 to 500 once travel is inside the figure. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with one UK-based agency publishing AED 270. Named or examiner-tier tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and beyond. Bestimate's "Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026" table is the most useful single source because it separates in-home from online rather than averaging them.

Monthly, that converts to figures a household budget can actually use. Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 a month for weekly hour-long budget tuition, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Published packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Compare those two per teaching minute rather than per month and the travel premium becomes visible immediately.

None of these are IB Gram's prices. They are the market, dated October 2026, and they are published here because the market mostly refuses to. For what a specific match costs, the honest route is the free trial lesson and a quoted figure in writing before anything is booked.

sections.heading: Online against in-home physics tutoring from an Umm Suqeim address
paragraphs: The comparison that matters is not online against in-home in the abstract. It is what a paid hour contains in each format, from this specific address, at the time of day a DP student is actually free. Umm Suqeim sits on Jumeirah Beach Road with Al Wasl behind it, and between four and seven in the evening both are slow. A tutor driving from Business Bay or Al Barsha to Umm Suqeim 2 is spending 25 to 40 minutes each way, and that time is inside the rate whether it is itemised or not.

For physics specifically, the format also changes what is teachable. Screen-sharing a past-paper script and annotating it live is better than looking over a shoulder at a printed page. Graphing software, uncertainty calculations and a shared document of worked solutions all behave better on a screen than on a kitchen table. The one genuine advantage of a physical presence — handling apparatus — is largely irrelevant, because the school provides the laboratory and the investigation is conducted there, not at home.

The table sets out both formats honestly, including where in-home wins. For a younger student who will not sit still without an adult in the room, presence has real value, and for a household with poor connectivity it is the safer option. For a DP2 student who needs Theme D at Higher Level, the pool of people who can teach it is the constraint, and no amount of presence substitutes for it.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service is offered only in India. sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks across four criteria
paragraphs: The investigation is the most mishandled component in DP physics and the easiest to improve legitimately. Under the current guide it is a single open investigation of up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 against four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is worth 20 per cent of the final grade, which is more than most students behave as though it is worth, and it is the only component where a student can take their time.

Marks cluster in two places. Research design carries six marks that are decided before any data exists, which is why the single highest-value conversation about an investigation happens at the planning stage and not at the draft stage. Evaluation carries another six and is the criterion students treat as a conclusion paragraph: a real evaluation identifies specific weaknesses in the method, explains their effect on the result, and proposes realistic improvements rather than listing "more trials" and "better equipment".

What goes wrong is usually structural rather than scientific. A research question too broad to control, a dependent variable that cannot be measured with the resolution available, five data points where eleven were needed, raw data with no uncertainty attached, a conclusion stated more confidently than the data supports. All five are visible to a tutor in twenty minutes at the planning stage, and all five are nearly unfixable three days before submission.

The table below sets out the four criteria, their mark allocations and what examiners actually reward, alongside the failure this corridor's students repeat most. Treat the word limit as a real constraint too: 3,000 words is generous for a well-focused investigation and punishing for a broad one, because the broad one spends its allowance on description.

sections.heading: What a physics tutor may and may not do with that investigation
paragraphs: This boundary is worth being blunt about, because the UAE search results for IB coursework include providers who cross it. One operator in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller, and it can end a Diploma. No part of a legitimate tutoring service touches that.

What a tutor may do is substantial. They may discuss the physics behind a candidate research question and point out that it cannot be controlled. They may teach uncertainty propagation using the student's own readings. They may mark a student-written draft against the four published criteria and explain which band it currently sits in and why. They may ask the questions that make a weak evaluation into a specific one. They may teach the formatting conventions for tables and graphs. All of that is teaching, and all of it is permitted.

What a tutor must never do is produce the work. A tutor never writes the investigation, never drafts a section for the student to adapt, never supplies data, never edits a report into its final form, and never hands over a worked exemplar to be reshaped. The distinction a student should be able to state out loud is simple: every sentence and every number in the submitted report was produced by the student, and the tutor's contribution was questions and feedback on what the student produced.

Ask any prospective tutor where that line sits before the first session. A hesitant answer is a reason to keep looking, however strong the physics. The same principle governs the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay: supervision, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts, nothing beyond.

sections.heading: A May session counted backwards from an Umm Suqeim school calendar
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May session, and the work that decides a physics grade is distributed across the preceding eighteen months rather than concentrated in April. The most useful planning document a family can build is a backwards calendar from the exam window, with the school's own internal deadlines on it, because those deadlines — not the IB's — are the dates that bite first.

One caution before any dates are written down. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date on this site is treated as confirmed. Every specific date in your child's year must come from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly. What is reliable, and what the table below gives, is the sequence and the relative timing: which task has to be finished before which, and how many weeks of lead time each needs. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the picture is firmer, because both publish their timetables openly: Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 series runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January, and Cambridge runs June and November series in this region.

The practical lesson from the sequence is that physics revision cannot wait for the investigation to be finished. The investigation's final deadline usually lands in the middle of DP2, exactly when Theme D and Theme E are still being taught. A student who leaves the investigation to the last fortnight loses that fortnight from content teaching, and it is the fortnight that was supposed to cover the material that is examined least well.

Build the calendar in DP1, not DP2. Put the school's internal investigation deadline on it, the mock window, the point at which Theme E is scheduled to be taught, and the weeks you intend to keep clear for timed past papers. Then work out where tutoring fits around it rather than on top of it.

sections.heading: If no Higher Level physics specialist is free this term
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider in this market implies infinite availability, and none has it. Higher Level physics is one of the genuinely scarce matches: the pool of people who can teach Theme D extension content well is small, and it is at its smallest in the two months before a May session, when every DP2 student in the Gulf wants the same slots. A provider who promises an immediate match for HL physics in March is either very lucky or not telling you the whole truth.

What IB Gram does instead is disclose the position. If a Higher Level physics specialist is not available for the hours an Umm Suqeim family needs, you are told that, and you are offered the real alternatives: a different time slot with the right tutor, a Standard Level specialist who can cover the shared theme content while HL extension work waits, a short diagnostic block now with the full programme starting when the specialist frees up, or a referral elsewhere. Nobody is matched with a generalist and a hope.

The reason to care about this as a parent is sequencing. Eight weeks with the right tutor beats sixteen weeks with the wrong one, and the damage from a mismatched physics tutor is not neutral — it is weeks of practising the wrong answer structure, which then has to be unlearned. If a provider cannot tell you which specific tutor your child will work with, at which level, and when, the match has not been made yet.

faqs.question: Is there an IB Physics tutor near me in Umm Suqeim?
faqs.answer: Probably not in the sense you mean. Umm Suqeim is residential, and the number of people living within a short drive who can teach Higher Level physics under the current IB guide is small. The Diploma accounts for about seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment against 37 per cent on UK curricula, so local supply follows IGCSE demand. IB Gram's answer is to stop searching by radius: your child is matched to a physics specialist anywhere, taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Nobody travels to a UAE address, and nothing about the specialism has to be compromised to make the timing work.

faqs.question: What does an IB Physics tutor cost per hour in Dubai in 2026?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 sit in bands. Budget online tuition with a student tutor runs about AED 45 to 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor online is roughly AED 150 to 300, with IB entry points near AED 200. An in-home visit is AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the hour. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, and named or examiner-tier tutors reach AED 500 to 650. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table separates in-home from online rather than averaging them, which makes it the most useful single source. None of these are IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: How do I check that a physics tutor knows the current IB Physics guide?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions in the trial lesson. What is the weighting split between Paper 1, Paper 2 and the investigation? What does Paper 1B contain that 1A does not? Name the five themes. How many marks is the investigation and across how many criteria? A tutor who has taught the course answers all four in under a minute: 36, 44 and 20 per cent; data and experimental questions; themes A to E; 24 marks across four criteria of six. Vague answers do not mean a weak teacher, but they do mean a teacher who has not taught this version of the course, which is a different thing from knowing physics.

faqs.question: Can online lessons teach the practical side of IB Physics?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the practical side that is assessed is mostly analytical rather than manual. Paper 1B examines measurement, resolution, error type, variable choice and uncertainty handling, all of which teach better on a shared screen than over a shoulder. The investigation's apparatus work happens in the school laboratory under the school's supervision, not at home, so a tutor would not be present for it in either format. What a tutor does with the practical component is interrogate the research design before data collection and review the student's own analysis afterwards, and both of those are screen-based tasks.

faqs.question: What share of the final IB Physics grade is already banked before the papers?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, under the guide first examined in 2025. It is one open investigation of up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The other 80 per cent is written papers, with Paper 1 at 36 per cent and Paper 2 at 44 per cent. The investigation is the only component without time pressure, which makes it the one where careful work converts most directly into marks. Confirm your child's internal submission deadline with their school, since that date usually falls a term before anything the IB publishes.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Physics scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: With the work, yes. With producing it, never. A tutor may question whether the research question can be controlled with school apparatus, teach uncertainty propagation on the student's own readings, mark a student-written draft against the four published criteria, and push a vague evaluation into a specific one. A tutor does not write any part of the report, draft a section to be adapted, supply data or edit the work to completion. One provider in this market sells finished Internal Assessments; buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student. Ask any tutor where that line sits before the first session.

faqs.question: My child is strong at maths but keeps losing physics marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because physics marks are awarded for reasoning that maths does not require. A correct numerical answer with no stated model, no justified assumption, no unit or no uncertainty will lose marks that the arithmetic earned. The command terms are the other half: "deduce" and "determine" demand working that "state" does not, and a strong mathematician often answers too briefly. Both are repairable in two or three sessions because they are habits rather than knowledge gaps. The diagnosis needs the marked script, though, not the percentage — the examiner's annotations show exactly which of the two is happening.

faqs.question: Is IB Physics HL much harder than SL for a student in Umm Suqeim?
faqs.answer: Harder in a structural way. Under the current guide the Higher Level content sits inside the five themes as extension material rather than in separate sections, so an HL student cannot revise "the HL part" in isolation; every theme has to be revisited at its deeper level. Paper 2 is also longer at HL. The practical consequence for tutoring is that an HL repair programme typically runs ten to twelve sessions where an SL one runs four to six. The heaviest extension in our experience of this corridor is Theme D, where potential in a radial field asks for more mathematics than DP1 required.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week does a DP2 student need?
faqs.answer: Most families in this area start with one 60 or 90-minute session a week and add a second only in the term before the May session. One weekly slot is enough to keep pace with a school scheme of work and to correct recurring errors while they are still small. Two becomes useful when there is both untaught content to cover and timed past papers to mark, which is the usual position after mocks. More than two is rarely productive: the limiting factor at that point is the student's own practice time between sessions, not the number of hours bought.

faqs.question: Which schools near Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah offer IB Physics?
faqs.answer: The corridor runs both IB continuum and British-curriculum schools. Raffles World Academy in Umm Suqeim 3, Emirates International School in Jumeirah and Jumeirah Baccalaureate School in Al Safa are IB programme schools in or near the neighbourhood, while Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh, and Dubai International Academy in Emirates Hills, sit on the daily commute from here. Always confirm current programme offerings and inspection ratings on KHDA's own site, since both change. Schools are named here as neighbourhood context; IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them.

faqs.question: Can physics sessions fit around an Umm Suqeim school run and Beach Road traffic?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where online scheduling earns its place. School days around Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh generally end between 2.30pm and 3.30pm, so a student is home well before four. The two slots that work most reliably here are 4.30pm, before the evening builds, and 7pm, after it. An online slot is unaffected by Jumeirah Beach Road at 5.30pm, where a booked in-home visit absorbs 25 to 40 minutes of driving each way and the family carries that time in the rate whether or not it is itemised.

faqs.question: Does a physics tutor working with an Umm Suqeim family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by MoHRE. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you. The official route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service at mohre.gov.ae.

faqs.question: What happens if no IB Physics HL specialist is free this term?
faqs.answer: You are told, before anything is booked. Higher Level physics is one of the scarcer matches, and availability is tightest in the two months before a May session. The alternatives offered are concrete: a different time slot with the right specialist, a Standard Level tutor to cover shared theme content while extension work waits, a short diagnostic block now with the full programme starting later, or a referral elsewhere. What does not happen is a generalist presented as a specialist, because eight weeks with the right tutor beats sixteen weeks of practising the wrong answer structure and then unlearning it.

faqs.question: Does my child need physics tutoring to meet UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a documentation process run by the Ministry of Education, and tutoring is not part of it. On the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. No IB points threshold should be quoted to you unless it has been read on moe.gov.ae itself. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency; verify the current requirement with the Ministry directly.

faqs.question: Can physics lessons move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth planning before the month starts rather than during it. Dubai private schools shorten the day during Ramadan, so afternoons open up while evenings compress around Iftar. Most families here either move to a late-morning or early-afternoon slot while school hours are reduced, or shift to a post-Iftar session around 8.30pm or 9pm. Online delivery makes either switch administratively trivial, since there is no travel to re-time. Agree the Ramadan schedule two or three weeks ahead, because the post-Iftar slots fill quickly across the Gulf.

intro.heading: Physics is the subject that cannot be taught at the end of a long drive
paragraphs: Villanova sits off Al Qudra Road in the Dubailand belt, and its Diploma students are scattered across schools from Fairgreen International in The Sustainable City to the Al Barsha cluster forty minutes away in the wrong direction at 15:30. Every tutoring decision in this community begins with that geography, and physics is the subject where it bites hardest.

The reason is specific rather than sentimental. Physics at Diploma level is built on derivation and multi-step reasoning: you set up a situation, apply a relationship, carry units through three or four steps, and check whether the answer is physically sensible. That is working-memory intensive in a way that revising a biology definition is not. A student who walks in at 17:05 after fifty minutes on Al Khail Road can revise flashcards. They cannot derive.

So the practical question for a Villanova family is not only who teaches physics well, but when physics can be taught at all. The answer depends on which school cluster your child travels to, and this page sets that out properly: the arrival times, the slot that follows, and — the part nobody writes about — which kind of physics work belongs in an early slot and which survives a late one.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses. Home visits are a service we offer only in India, and Villanova students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For physics that is close to an advantage. The lesson happens on a shared surface where graphs can be plotted live, error bars drawn and redrawn, and simulations run — and both the tutor and the student keep the annotated record afterwards.

The substance of the page is the syllabus. The five themes and what each demands. The paper structure and weightings, including the multiple-choice and data-analysis split in Paper 1. The Scientific Investigation with its four criteria and twenty-four marks, which no competitor page in this market publishes. Where marks actually go missing, theme by theme. And how practical work is handled when the teaching happens on a screen and the laboratory stays at school.

One standing caution: we publish no IB exam or results date anywhere on this site, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and a date a parent plans around has to be checkable. UAE schools sit the May session; get the window and your school's internal Scientific Investigation deadlines from your child's IB coordinator and cite them rather than us. What is worth knowing in advance is the shape of the DP2 collision: in most Dubai schools the physics investigation deadline arrives in the same few weeks as two or three others, and the Higher Level extensions in fields arrive at the same time, which is the single most predictable pressure point in the course.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-villanova.subjectsIntro: This page is about physics, so these are its themes and components, with what each assesses and where Villanova students lose marks.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, energy and, at Higher Level, rotational and relativistic extensions. The most familiar material and the place students build false confidence: they can solve standard projectile questions and fail the moment a question asks them to justify which relationship applies and why.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws, current electricity and circuits. Circuits are the reliable weak point across UAE cohorts: students can recite the rules and cannot reason about what happens to the rest of a circuit when one component changes, which is precisely what questions ask.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Wave models, superposition, standing waves, the Doppler effect and, at Higher Level, further interference work. The commonest loss is describing rather than explaining — stating that a pattern appears without identifying the path difference or phase relationship that produces it.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, including induction. The hardest theme for most students and the one most often rushed in DP2. Field-line reasoning and the sign conventions in potential energy problems are where Higher Level marks go missing in volume.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Structure of the atom, radioactive decay, fission and fusion, and quantum phenomena at Higher Level. Conceptually unfamiliar but computationally tidy, which makes it a reliable late-stage gain for a student who has left it until revision.

subjects.name: Paper 1A: Multiple choice
subjects.description: Thirty multiple-choice questions with no partial credit, which means timing and elimination technique are worth real marks. Students lose here by working every question fully rather than recognising which can be settled by a units check or an order-of-magnitude estimate.

subjects.name: Paper 1B: Data analysis
subjects.description: A data-based question on unseen material: plotting, gradients, uncertainties and drawing a conclusion the data supports. Anyone who has not plotted error bars by hand and worked out a gradient uncertainty loses marks here regardless of how well they know the themes.

subjects.name: Paper 2: Extended response
subjects.description: The largest single component, carrying structured questions that build across parts. Marks are lost to answers that describe where derivation was asked for, to unit omissions, and to candidates who abandon a part-answered question instead of stating the relationship they would use.

subjects.name: The Scientific Investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation of up to 3,000 words, worth 20 per cent, marked on four criteria of six marks each. Research design decides the ceiling: a question with no measurable, variable relationship cannot score well however carefully the data is processed. Support is feedback on the student's own work only.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error analysis
subjects.description: Threaded through every paper and the investigation. Absolute and percentage uncertainties, propagation through calculations, and uncertainty in a gradient. It is the single most under-taught examinable skill in the course and one of the cheapest to fix properly.

subjects.name: Mathematical technique in physics
subjects.description: Rearranging before substituting, handling standard form, small-angle approximations, and reading a logarithmic scale. Students paired with Mathematics Applications and Interpretation most often need this strand supported explicitly rather than assumed.

subjects.name: Command terms
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, deduce, derive and justify each carry a different expectation and a different mark ceiling. A student who answers 'explain' with a description has lost the marks before the physics is examined, and this is correctable in a single session with a marked paper.

sections.heading: What time physics can realistically start in this community
paragraphs: Begin with the clock, because in physics the slot determines what the session can achieve. The table below maps the school clusters Villanova children travel to onto arrival times, and then does the part nobody else does: it says which kind of physics work belongs in the slot that follows.

The principle is simple. Derivation and new abstract content need working memory, so they belong in the earliest slot a family can get. Marking a paper, going through uncertainties, plotting and interpreting a data set, and discussing an investigation's research design all tolerate tiredness far better, because the student is responding to something in front of them rather than holding four steps in their head.

This has a practical consequence that surprises parents. For a student on the Al Barsha run, whose realistic start is 18:00, the right answer is often not to fight for an impossible 16:30 slot but to put the derivation-heavy theme work on a weekend morning and use the weekday evening for marking and data analysis. That is a better plan than a 17:00 session that happens two weeks in three and is spent recovering from the drive.

The reverse is also true. A student at a near Dubailand school arriving at 15:50 has the most valuable physics slot available in this belt, and it is frequently wasted on homework supervision. If your child arrives early and the session is spent checking completed questions, you are using the best hour of the week for the least demanding task.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what each actually demands
paragraphs: Physics at Diploma level is organised into five themes studied at both levels, with Higher Level going further within each. Knowing which theme is costing marks is the whole diagnostic job, and it is answerable from two marked papers rather than from a conversation.

The distribution of difficulty is consistent across the Dubai cohorts we see. Theme A feels familiar and breeds false confidence. Theme B contains circuits, which is where the largest reliable loss sits. Theme C punishes description. Theme D, fields, is the hardest and the most often rushed. Theme E is conceptually strange and computationally tidy, which makes it the best late-stage gain available.

What the table adds is the kind of thinking each theme asks for, because that is what decides how it should be taught. A theme that rewards reasoning about change — circuits, fields — is taught by asking what happens next and why, not by working more examples. A theme that rewards precision of language — waves — is taught by marking answers against command terms. Treating all five the same way is the commonest flaw in general science tutoring, and it is the clearest signal that a tutor has taught the subject rather than read about it.

Higher Level students should note that the additional content is not evenly spread. The extensions in Theme A and Theme D carry the most weight and the most unfamiliar mathematics, and they arrive in DP2 when the Scientific Investigation is also due. That collision is predictable, which means it is plannable.

sections.heading: Paper structure, weightings and what each component tests
paragraphs: Physics is assessed by two written papers plus the Scientific Investigation, and the internal split inside Paper 1 is the part families most often do not know. Paper 1 contains a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, which are two different skills examined in one sitting.

The weightings matter for planning. Across both levels the two papers carry the large majority of the grade — roughly 36 per cent for Paper 1 and 44 per cent for Paper 2 — with the Scientific Investigation at 20 per cent. Higher Level sits longer papers covering the additional content. Specification versions do get revised, so confirm the exact durations and weightings for your child's cohort with the school rather than treating any page, including this one, as final.

The planning consequence is that Paper 2 is where the grade mostly lives, and Paper 2 is the extended-response paper. Students who revise by doing multiple-choice questions are practising the smaller component because it feels more productive: thirty questions answered feels like progress, whereas one extended question properly reviewed feels slow. The slow one is the one that pays.

Paper 1B deserves its own time. It is a data-analysis question on unseen material, and it rewards a skill — plotting, gradients, uncertainty in a gradient, drawing a supported conclusion — that is almost never practised deliberately. Three sessions on it is usually worth more than three sessions of theme revision for a mid-grade student.

table.caption: PHYSICS ASSESSMENT COMPONENTS — CONFIRM DURATIONS WITH YOUR SCHOOL

Never having drawn error bars by hand
One question marked properly beats ten skimmed
Independent experimental work, up to 3,000 words
A research question with no measurable relationship
Research design checked before weeks are spent

sections.heading: Where physics marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Physics loses marks in a small number of recognisable ways, and almost none of them are 'did not know the topic'. This is why a first session should look at marked papers rather than ask a student what they find hard.

The largest category is command-term failure. A question says 'explain' and the student describes. It says 'derive' and the student states the final relationship. It says 'justify' and the student asserts. The physics in their head may be correct and the marks are gone before it is examined. One session with a marked paper and the command-term list fixes a pattern that has been costing marks for a year.

The second is units and uncertainties. Dropping a unit, mixing standard-form prefixes, rounding mid-calculation, or quoting an uncertainty to three significant figures. These look like carelessness and are actually untaught habits — most students have never been shown how an uncertainty propagates through a multiplication, so they guess consistently.

The third is abandoning a part-answered question. In extended response, a student who cannot complete a calculation often writes nothing, when stating the relationship they would use and the quantity they would find earns marks. That is pure exam behaviour, learnable in two sessions, and it is worth more to a mid-grade student than another theme. The fourth, specific to circuits and fields, is reasoning about change: the student knows the rules and cannot say what happens to the rest of the system when one element alters, which is exactly what the harder questions ask.
bullets: Command terms: explain, derive and justify answered as description
Units, prefixes, mid-calculation rounding, and uncertainty propagation
Abandoning part-answered extended questions instead of stating the method
Circuits and fields: knowing the rules without reasoning about change

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation: four criteria, twenty-four marks
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation is 20 per cent of the physics grade, runs to a maximum of 3,000 words, and is marked against four criteria of six marks each. It is also the component where informed students gain most, because the criteria are public and almost nobody reads them before choosing a question.

Research design is where the ceiling is set. A question must have a measurable relationship between a variable the student can change and a quantity they can measure, with the other relevant variables controllable in the school's laboratory. Questions that fail this test cannot score well on the later criteria however carefully the work is done, because there is nothing to analyse. Testing a research question properly takes twenty minutes and saves weeks.

Data analysis and conclusion are where most of the recoverable marks sit. Processing with correct uncertainties, a graph that is actually interpretable, a gradient with its uncertainty, and a conclusion that is justified by the data rather than by what the textbook says should happen. Evaluation is the criterion most often written the night before, and it asks for specific, prioritised weaknesses with realistic improvements rather than a list of generic apologies about human error.

The boundary is firm and worth stating. A tutor may explain the criteria, test whether a research question is viable, question the reasoning, and give honest feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not design the investigation for them, produce or process the data, write or rewrite text, or supply a previous student's report as a model. Those are passing off another person's work as the student's own, which is misconduct under IB rules and risks the Diploma rather than one grade.

sections.heading: Practical physics when the teaching is online
paragraphs: The fair question from any physics parent: how does an online tutor handle a subject with a laboratory in it? The honest answer splits the work in two, and being clear about the split is more useful than a reassuring generality.

The hands-on part stays at school, because that is where the apparatus, the technician and the safety framework are. Nobody should claim otherwise. Your child measures, builds the circuit, times the oscillation and records the readings in the school laboratory under their teacher's supervision — and for the Scientific Investigation that is a requirement, not a preference.

What online teaching does well is everything that surrounds the measurement, which is also where most of the assessed marks are. Designing the investigation and testing whether the variables work. Processing data with correct uncertainties. Plotting a graph and arguing about whether the line is justified. Reading a gradient and its uncertainty. Writing a conclusion the data supports and an evaluation that prioritises real weaknesses. All of that is screen work, and a shared screen with live graphing is better for it than a notebook on a dining table.

There is also a teaching gain that is specific to physics. Simulations let a student change a parameter and watch the consequence, which is the fastest route into field and circuit reasoning — exactly the themes where marks are lost. Being explicit about the limits: IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, home visits are India-only, and no online session can substitute for handling apparatus. Independent in-home tutors in this belt charge roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel if presence in the room is the requirement.
bullets: Apparatus work stays at school, under the school's supervision — including for the investigation
Design, uncertainties, graphing, conclusion and evaluation are screen work
Simulations accelerate field and circuit reasoning, the two biggest loss areas
No UAE home visits; in-home tutors in this belt run AED 180-500 including travel

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs around Villanova
paragraphs: Physics sits in the specialist band of this market, which is to say the upper half. Published Dubai rates for IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more per hour: TutorChase publishes AED 270, Unitors publishes IB from AED 200, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table shows AED 200 to 450+. A qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 can serve Standard Level competently; Higher Level fields and Paper 2 reasoning genuinely want the specialist band.

Below that, at AED 33 to 65 — Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 — you are buying supervision. In physics that is worth less than in most subjects, because the thing a weak student needs is somebody to interrogate their reasoning, and supervision does not do that. Paying AED 50 an hour for physics help that cannot explain why a circuit behaves differently when a resistor changes is cheap and ineffective.

In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, per Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with Villanova at the top of the range because the drive is long. The premium buys presence. For physics specifically it buys little else, because the subject's teaching surface is a page of working and a graph, both of which transfer to a shared screen with the useful addition that the annotated file is kept.

Where physics money is best spent, in order: three sessions on Paper 1B data analysis and uncertainty handling, which almost nobody practises deliberately; one session on command terms with a marked paper; and a short block on whichever of fields or circuits is failing. Where it is worst spent: a weekly session that re-teaches Theme A to a student who is already fine at Theme A, which is comfortable and changes nothing.
bullets: Specialist band for Higher Level physics: AED 200-450+ (TutorChase 270; Bestimate 200-450+)
Qualified subject tutor, AED 150-300, is adequate for Standard Level content

sections.heading: From MYP Sciences to Diploma Physics
paragraphs: A recurring October enquiry from this belt: a student who did well in MYP Sciences and is struggling in DP1 Physics. It is a predictable transition rather than a surprise, and it has three distinct causes worth separating.

The first is assessment type. MYP is criterion-marked with design and processing tasks carrying real weight and no timed terminal paper deciding the grade. Diploma physics puts the large majority of the grade into two timed papers. A student who has never worked a timed extended-response physics paper meets one at sixteen, and the first difficulty is pace and structure rather than content.

The second is mathematical load. Diploma physics assumes fluent rearrangement, confident standard form, and comfort reading a gradient off a graph. MYP Sciences does not guarantee any of that, and the gap appears as careless errors that look like inattention and are actually arithmetic overload. Students paired with Mathematics Applications and Interpretation need this strand supported explicitly.

The third is the demand for justification. MYP rewards a well-organised investigation; the Diploma rewards saying why a relationship applies. Students arrive able to do physics and not yet able to argue physics, and the papers mark the argument. A bridging block of ten to fifteen hours over the summer between MYP 5 and DP1, or in the first half-term, addresses all three far more cheaply than remediation in DP2 when the Scientific Investigation is also due. The order that works is mathematical technique first, then timed-paper structure, then justification practice on questions the student has already answered once.
bullets: MYP has no timed terminal paper; the Diploma puts most of the grade in timed papers
Diploma physics assumes algebraic fluency MYP Sciences does not guarantee
The new demand is justification, not more content
A 10-15 hour bridge beats DP2 remediation during the investigation period

process.title: Send the level, the school and the arrival time
process.description: Four facts make the first exchange useful: Higher or Standard Level, the school, the year group, and what time your child actually gets home. The last one is not small talk — for physics it decides which slots are worth offering and what each one should contain.

process.title: Matched to the level, with two marked papers
process.description: Tutors are matched to Higher or Standard Level rather than to science generally, and we ask for two marked papers before the first session. Those papers say more in five minutes than a conversation does in thirty, because students cannot see their own command-term and uncertainty errors.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: A genuine lesson with the person who would continue, no card required. It produces a diagnosis: which theme, which component, and whether the losses are content, reasoning or command-term misreading. If the fit is wrong in style or pace, say so and we match again.

process.title: A plan by component, slot and deadline
process.description: You get the component to attack first, the topics in order, the session count and the dates it is set against — your school's internal investigation deadline and mock week. The plan also names which work belongs in your child's actual slot, which is the part that makes it survive a Villanova afternoon.

process.title: Marked strictly, reviewed each term
process.description: Work is marked the way the examiner marks it: units, uncertainties, command terms and reasoning treated seriously rather than ticked as broadly right. Each term the plan is reviewed against the marked evidence, and when a component stops needing weekly support we will say so.

whyPoints.title: Session content matched to the slot
whyPoints.description: Derivation and new abstract content go in the earliest slot a family can get; marking, uncertainties and data analysis go later. For a community whose students arrive home anywhere between 15:40 and 16:45, planning content by slot is the difference between a session that teaches and one that recovers from a drive.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1B treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: The data-analysis component rewards plotting, gradients, uncertainty propagation and supported conclusions, and almost no student practises it deliberately. Three sessions there typically move more marks for a mid-grade student than three sessions of theme revision.

whyPoints.title: Investigation criteria read before the question is chosen
whyPoints.description: Research design sets the ceiling: a question without a measurable, controllable relationship cannot score on the later criteria. Testing viability takes twenty minutes and saves weeks, and it is the single highest-value conversation in the course.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the laboratory
whyPoints.description: Apparatus work stays at school, where the equipment and supervision are, and we say so rather than implying a screen can replace it. What online teaching does better is everything around the measurement, which is also where most of the assessed marks sit.

whyPoints.title: Sources, not assertions
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here names who published it, every regulatory statement names u.ae, KHDA or MoHRE, and we publish no IB exam or results date at all because ibo.org blocks automated verification. Ask your IB coordinator for dates and cite them rather than us.

faqs.question: What time should a physics session start for a Villanova student?
faqs.answer: As early as the school run allows, because physics is derivation-heavy and working-memory intensive. Students at the near Dubailand schools arrive around 15:50 and can start at 16:30, which is the best physics slot in this belt. Those travelling back from the Al Barsha IB schools arrive closer to 16:30 and realistically start at 18:00. If the only available slot is late, change what goes in it: paper marking, uncertainties and data analysis survive tiredness; a first encounter with electromagnetic induction does not.

faqs.question: Which physics theme causes the most trouble in Dubai cohorts?
faqs.answer: Theme D, fields, followed closely by the circuits content in Theme B. Fields is conceptually demanding, carries the heaviest Higher Level extensions, and is often reached late in DP2 when the Scientific Investigation is also due. Circuits fails for a different reason: students learn the rules and cannot reason about what happens to the rest of the circuit when one component changes, which is precisely what the harder questions ask. Both respond well to simulation work and to being front-loaded rather than left.

faqs.question: How is IB Physics assessed, and where does the grade actually live?
faqs.answer: Two written papers plus the Scientific Investigation. Paper 1 combines a multiple-choice section with a data-analysis section and carries roughly 36 per cent; Paper 2 is extended response and carries roughly 44 per cent; the investigation is 20 per cent. Higher Level sits longer papers with additional content. Confirm exact durations and weightings for your child's cohort with the school, since specification versions are revised. The planning point is that Paper 2 holds the largest share, and extended-response practice is what most students do least of.

faqs.question: What is Paper 1B and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: It is the data-analysis part of Paper 1, set on unseen material: plotting, reading a gradient, handling uncertainties and drawing a conclusion the data supports. It matters because it examines a skill almost nobody practises deliberately — most revision is content revision — so marks are available to anyone who does. A student who has never drawn error bars by hand or worked out the uncertainty in a gradient loses marks here regardless of how well they know the five themes. Three focused sessions usually show up.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria on the IB physics investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Against four criteria of six marks each, twenty-four in total, worth 20 per cent of the grade, within a 3,000-word maximum. Research design covers a focused question with measurable, controllable variables. Data analysis covers processing, uncertainties and interpretable graphs. Conclusion asks for a result the data actually supports. Evaluation asks for specific prioritised weaknesses with realistic improvements, not generic remarks about human error. Research design sets the ceiling, which is why the question must be tested before weeks are spent on it.

faqs.question: Where is the line on tutor help with a Villanova student's physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor may explain each criterion, test whether a research question has a measurable relationship in it, question the reasoning, and give honest feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the investigation, produce or process the data, write or rewrite text, or supply a previous student's report as a model. Those cross into passing off another person's work as the student's own, which is misconduct under IB rules and risks the Diploma rather than one grade.

faqs.question: How do practicals work if physics lessons happen online?
faqs.answer: The apparatus work stays at school, where the equipment, the technician and the safety framework are — and for the Scientific Investigation that is required rather than preferred. What online teaching covers is everything around the measurement: designing the investigation, processing data with correct uncertainties, plotting and arguing about graphs, reading gradients, and writing conclusions and evaluations. That is where most of the assessed marks sit. Simulations also let a student change a parameter and watch the consequence, which is the fastest route into field and circuit reasoning.

faqs.question: Will a physics tutor come to our villa in Villanova?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach UAE students one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India, so no tutor will arrive at a Dubailand address. Independent in-home physics tutors do work in this belt at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Villanova at the top of that range because the drive is long. For physics the online format gives up little: the lesson is a page of working and a graph, both of which transfer well to a shared screen that both people can annotate and keep.

faqs.question: What does an IB physics tutor cost in the Dubailand belt?
faqs.answer: Physics sits in the specialist band, which published Dubai figures put at AED 200 to 450 or more an hour: TutorChase at AED 270, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, and Bestimate's 2026 table at AED 200 to 450+. A qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 is adequate for Standard Level content. Budget supervision at AED 33 to 65 buys less in physics than elsewhere, because what a struggling student needs is somebody interrogating their reasoning. Our own rate is quoted after the free trial.

faqs.question: Does Physics HL work with Maths Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: It can, but the pairing needs support rather than assumption. Physics at Higher Level assumes fluent algebraic rearrangement, confident standard form, and comfort with gradients and logarithmic scales — a profile that Analysis and Approaches builds directly and Applications and Interpretation builds less of. Students in that combination often look careless in physics when they are actually carrying arithmetic overload. Where we see this pairing, we usually recommend a short explicit block on mathematical technique in physics rather than more theme revision.

faqs.question: My child did well in MYP Sciences and is struggling in DP1 Physics. Why?
faqs.answer: Three things change at once. Assessment type: MYP is criterion-marked with no timed terminal paper, while the Diploma puts most of the grade in timed papers. Mathematical load: Diploma physics assumes fluency MYP Sciences does not guarantee. And the demand for justification: MYP rewards a well-organised investigation, the Diploma rewards explaining why a relationship applies. A bridging block of ten to fifteen hours over the summer or in the first half-term addresses all three, far more cheaply than remediation in DP2.

faqs.question: Is six weeks before the May session long enough to improve physics?
faqs.answer: Enough to convert knowledge into marks, which is where most students are losing them, but not enough to build the themes from nothing. The efficient use of that window is timed extended-response questions marked strictly, with every lost mark categorised as content, reasoning or command-term misreading, and the command-term and uncertainty habits attacked first because they close fastest. Theme E is also a reasonable late target, being conceptually unfamiliar but computationally tidy. The investigation, by then, has been submitted.

faqs.question: Which schools near Villanova offer IB Diploma Physics?
faqs.answer: Full IB continuum provision around Dubailand is limited, so most Villanova Diploma students travel towards Al Barsha, where schools including GEMS World Academy Dubai, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha and Nord Anglia International School Dubai sit. Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City is the nearest IB option for many families in this belt. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new International Baccalaureate schools. Schools are named as context only; no affiliation with any of them is implied or held, and subject availability should be confirmed with the school.

faqs.question: Do physics tutors teaching Dubai students need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years according to u.ae. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applying through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service. Operating without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, treat any amount quoted at you as unverified.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-villanova.closingHeading: Tell us when the bus arrives
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-villanova.closingBody: For physics more than any other subject, the useful first message from a Villanova family contains the time your child gets home. With that, the level, and two marked papers, a specialist can tell you which theme and which component are costing the grade, how many sessions that needs, and what should go in the slot you actually have. The first lesson is free and taught by the tutor who would continue. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time; the laboratory stays at school and nobody drives to Dubailand.

dubai/ib-predicted-grades-improvement.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work with DP1 and DP2 students in the months when assessed evidence is still accumulating. Each teaches to published criteria, marks written work, and reports what the evidence shows rather than what a family hopes it shows.

intro.heading: Who actually decides a predicted grade
paragraphs: A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by a subject teacher and submitted by the school's Diploma coordinator. It exists because university applications happen long before any real IB result does. The prediction is the school's property, not the student's and certainly not a tutor's, and it is formed from the evidence the department holds: mock papers, in-class assessments, Internal Assessment drafts, and the teacher's read of trajectory across two years.

That makes the honest version of this page narrower than most pages on this topic. Nobody outside the school can move a prediction directly. What can change is the quality and recency of the evidence in the folder when the judgement is made. A student who produces a strong, criteria-marked piece of work three weeks after a weak mock has genuinely altered the information available, and most Dubai schools will take recent evidence seriously because it is the most current data they have.

Dubai-specific timing sharpens the point. Diploma mocks at most Dubai schools run between late November and early February, and predictions follow within weeks of them. UK applications through UCAS sit earlier in that cycle than many families expect, and United States applications run on their own calendar with early deadlines in the autumn of DP2. The practical consequence is that the window in which fresh evidence still matters is often six to ten weeks long, and it closes quietly.

The second Dubai factor is class size. Diploma subject groups in Dubai schools can be very small; a Physics HL set of nine is ordinary. Students in such a group often read their position in the class as their grade, which is a category error in a criterion-referenced system. Part of what a tutor does here is convert a mark into a criteria-referenced estimate, so a family can see whether a 5 in the class is a 5 against the grade descriptors or something different.

There is a further asymmetry worth naming. A prediction that is too low costs a student the chance to apply where they might have succeeded, and a prediction that is too high costs them at confirmation. Neither error is correctable after the event, which is why a family is better served by accurate evidence than by advocacy. Teachers in Dubai schools are generally willing to look at recent assessed work; what they will not do is revise a judgement on the basis of a parent's confidence in their child. The currency is marked paper, and there is usually still time to produce some.

All of our UAE work runs one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For this particular job the online format matters because the work is evidence-specific and short: a family in Nad Al Sheba needing six weeks of criteria-level Economics marking should be matched on the subject, not on who can reach Nad Al Sheba on a Tuesday.

dubai/ib-predicted-grades-improvement.programmesIntro: Prediction pressure is a Diploma phenomenon, but the groundwork sits earlier. Here is what each stage contributes to the judgement a coordinator eventually makes.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Year 2
programmes.description: The prediction year. Mocks are sat, Internal Assessments are finalised, and predicted grades are submitted for university applications. The evidence window is short and the work has to be targeted at whatever the department will next assess rather than at the syllabus as a whole.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP2 students frequently apply across three systems at once: UK universities, United States colleges, and institutions inside the UAE. Each wants the prediction at a different moment, which means a Dubai family can face an effective deadline in October and another in January for the same set of grades. Knowing which applies first changes where the hours go.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Year 1
programmes.description: Where predictions are quietly built. End-of-year DP1 examinations and early Internal Assessment work form the baseline a teacher carries into DP2. A student who ends DP1 at a 4 in a Higher Level subject starts the application year from that reading of their trajectory.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest point to change a Dubai student's predicted grades is the DP1 summer, and almost nobody buys support then. Six weeks of work between DP1 and DP2 moves the baseline before the application calendar begins, when there is no deadline pressure and specialist availability across the emirate is at its loosest.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Year 5
programmes.description: The stage at which Higher and Standard Level choices are made. Those choices shape what is predictable: three Higher Levels chosen against the grain of a student's MYP profile will show up as a strained prediction eighteen months later rather than as a problem at the time.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP to Year 11 rather than IGCSE, so students arrive in DP1 without ever having sat a timed external-style paper. Dubai MYP5 cohorts therefore tend to lose their first DP1 marks to exam technique, and that early reading of ability can follow a student into the prediction if nobody corrects it.

programmes.name: The core: TOK, Extended Essay, CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry up to three additional points through a published matrix, and both are predicted alongside subjects. CAS is a completion requirement rather than a graded one, but an incomplete CAS record blocks the Diploma whatever the subject grades say.
programmes.countryNote: Core points are the most under-managed part of a Dubai application. A student predicted 38 subject points with an estimated core contribution they never asked about is applying with a number they have not checked. Asking the coordinator what core points are being predicted, and on what basis, is a five-minute conversation worth having in DP2.

dubai/ib-predicted-grades-improvement.subjectsIntro: Different subjects respond at different speeds to new work. The list below names what a teacher can actually reassess in a few weeks, subject by subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Responds quickly, because teachers set frequent timed assessments. A student who fixes method presentation and non-calculator technique can show measurable change on the next in-class paper within three weeks, which is unusually fast evidence.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Also fast-moving, with the gains usually in statistical interpretation and modelling language rather than calculation. The IA is a second lever here, since the exploration is assessed against published criteria the student can be taught to read.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Slower to move on paper marks because the content load is heavy, but the IA is a genuine opportunity. A well-designed investigation with clear data treatment can shift a teacher's overall read, and the criteria reward process the student controls.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Moves fastest through command-term work, because most lost marks are shape rather than content. A student who learns what 'explain', 'outline' and 'suggest' each require can show a different quality of answer in the next assessment without learning new material.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Responds to data-booklet discipline and to unit and significant-figure accuracy, both teachable in weeks. Topic gaps in fields and induction take longer and usually cannot be closed before a prediction is submitted.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Among the fastest subjects to show improvement, because diagram accuracy and evaluation structure are both learnable quickly. A student who starts reaching a judgement supported by a correctly labelled diagram moves whole mark bands.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis is where a visible change can be produced in a few weeks, since the skill is identifiable and practisable. The HL essay and oral components sit on fixed internal deadlines that constrain when new evidence can appear.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study technique improves quickly once a student stops reciting tools and starts applying them to the stimulus. Teachers tend to set case-based assessments frequently, so the evidence cycle is short.

subjects.name: Psychology

sections.heading: The evidence a Dubai coordinator is actually looking at
paragraphs: Predictions are not guesses, and they are not formulas either. A subject teacher assembles what they have: timed assessments across two years, the mock paper, Internal Assessment drafts and their mark against criteria, and classroom evidence of how the student handles unfamiliar questions. Different departments weight those differently, and in Dubai schools with small Diploma sets the teacher's direct knowledge of the student carries real weight.

What follows from that is a short list of things a family can usefully do. Find out what evidence exists, when the next piece will be produced, and which criteria it will be marked against. Those three questions are answerable in one email to a subject teacher, and the answers determine whether any outside support can reach the folder before it closes.

The table below sets out the usual evidence types and how much room each leaves for change. Read the right-hand column carefully: some evidence is already fixed and cannot be revisited, and effort aimed at it is wasted. A mock sat in December cannot be re-sat. An Internal Assessment still in draft, by contrast, is live, and so is every assessment the department has yet to set.

One warning about this market. Any provider implying it can influence a prediction, negotiate with a school, or deliver a specific predicted grade is describing something it cannot do and should be read as a signal about everything else on its page. Predictions belong to schools. Evidence belongs to students. The honest offer is help producing better evidence, in the weeks when better evidence is still possible.

sections.heading: The application calendar, and when the window closes
paragraphs: Three different calendars run over a Dubai DP2 student at once, and they do not agree. United States applications open in the summer before DP2 and carry early deadlines in the autumn, at which point the prediction used is often based on DP1 evidence alone. UK applications through UCAS fall later in the autumn and winter, close enough to the mock window that a December mock can matter enormously. UAE institutions and many others run later still, sometimes into the spring.

The result is that the question 'when is it too late' has a different answer for each family, and the answer depends on which application matters most. A student applying to United States colleges with early deadlines has a prediction window that effectively closed during the previous summer. A student applying only within the UAE may have months of live evidence-building ahead.

Our first question to any family on this page is therefore which system has the earliest binding deadline for them. Everything about the plan follows from the answer, including whether the plan should exist at all. Where the window has genuinely closed, the right advice is to stop spending on prediction work and redirect everything towards the May session itself, because the final result is what will eventually matter at confirmation.

There is one further step after predictions that families forget: a conditional offer is confirmed against actual results, not predicted ones. A prediction that was generous does the student no favours at that point. This is a real argument for honest evidence-building rather than prediction-chasing, and it is the argument we make to families whose instinct is to push for a number the work does not yet support.

sections.heading: What a predicted grade will and will not do for an offer
paragraphs: Predicted grades get an application read and an offer made. They do not get a place confirmed. That distinction decides how much a family should be prepared to spend chasing a number, and it is routinely blurred by providers who market prediction improvement as an end in itself.

A conditional offer states the grades the student must actually achieve. If the predicted total was 40 and the offer is set at 38, the student must reach 38 in the real session. A prediction higher than the student's trajectory therefore buys an offer that may not survive results day, and the summer that follows is harder than the winter that would have been. Dubai families with experience of the cycle, usually through an older child, tend to understand this better than first-time applicants.

The useful consequence is that evidence-building and exam preparation are the same work seen from two angles. Producing a genuinely stronger piece of assessed work in January both improves the information in front of the teacher and improves the student's position in May. Work aimed only at impressing a department, without changing underlying capability, does neither.

The table below sets out what each part of an application actually responds to, which is the clearest way we have found to show families where effort pays. Note that the core points row is the most neglected: three points moved for comparatively little work, on components almost nobody targets deliberately. It is also the row where a Dubai student has the most direct control, since the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay are written to criteria the student can read in an afternoon.

sections.heading: What this work costs in Dubai, and what changes the number
paragraphs: Prediction-window work is usually short and intense, which makes hourly rates more relevant than monthly packages. The figures here are other providers' published rates in the Dubai market, read in October 2026. They are the market, not our price list, and we publish them because most pages ranking for Dubai IB queries publish no figure at all and two of the ones that do quote in US dollars.

Three variables move the number. The first is level: Higher Level work in a science or in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches sits at the top of every provider's band. The second is urgency, and this is the one families on this page feel most. A request made in the autumn, before the UCAS rush, meets looser availability than the same request made in January, when every Dubai school's mock has just been returned at once. The third is narrowness: criteria-level marking of a specific component is a scarcer skill than general subject teaching, and it is priced accordingly.

Against those market figures, the honest cost comparison for this specific job is time rather than money. Three sessions aimed at the department's next assessment, taken in October, are worth more than ten taken in February, because the earlier ones can still reach the evidence folder. Families who come to us in the DP1 summer spend less and get more, every time.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on these pages. The right number depends on subject, level and how many weeks remain, and the free trial lesson exists so the match can be judged before money is discussed. No condition attaches to the trial beyond booking a time.

sections.heading: Why this work is delivered online in the UAE
paragraphs: Evidence-building is subject-specific and deadline-bound, which makes the tutor's exact expertise the only variable that matters. A generalist can revise with a student. Only a subject specialist can look at an Economics Paper 1 response and say that the evaluation reached a conclusion without using the diagram, which is the sentence that changes the next assessment.

In-home tutoring in Dubai is a substantial market, with published rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour and monthly in-home packages quoted around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. A portion of that is travel. The larger constraint is reach: a family is selecting from the specialists prepared to drive to their community within the hours a DP2 student is free, which in a narrow combination may be nobody at all.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Every UAE session is one-to-one over live video, consistent with every other country page on this site. For this job the format has a specific advantage: marked work is annotated on a shared screen and saved, so when a family needs to show a department a sequence of improving criteria-marked work, the sequence exists as documents rather than as a recollection.

Where in-home genuinely helps is with younger students who need someone in the room. A DP2 student six weeks from a UCAS deadline is not that student. The deciding factor for them is whether the person on the other end of the call knows what the criteria say, and online delivery is what makes that person reachable from anywhere in Dubai.

sections.heading: The honesty boundary, and why it protects the application
paragraphs: Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay must be the student's own work under IB rules. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the criteria, question the reasoning and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write it, rewrite it, or edit it into shape. That line is not a formality during prediction season, because an IA draft is exactly the evidence a teacher is weighing.

There is a market reason to say this plainly. At least one provider ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at around AED 3,750. A student who submits one risks a malpractice finding, which can cost the entire Diploma rather than one subject grade. Any improvement to a prediction bought that way is worth nothing against that risk, and the risk sits with the student, not the seller.

The practical version of the boundary is recognisable. A good session is interrogative: what is your research question asking, why this method, what does your data show that your conclusion does not. A bad one is dictation. Parents can audit it by asking the student to explain their own argument without notes a week later. If they cannot, the work was not theirs and the evidence in the folder is false evidence.

The same principle applies to the documents. We reference IB, Cambridge and Pearson material and link to the publishers rather than redistributing syllabus documents, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Your child's subject teacher and Diploma coordinator are the correct source for the school's own criteria sheets and internal deadlines.
