sections.heading: KHDA, the Dubai calendar and the weeks that are already full
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Its annual inspection reports are public and often comment at department level, which is directly useful when reading a subject's assessment practice. Dubai's private sector is large and growing: 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with seven new schools added for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 places.

KHDA also fixes part of the week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Those lessons do not pause for application season, so evidence-building hours have to come from what remains.

The academic year adds two more constraints that break prediction-season plans. The winter break usually sits inside or immediately beside the mock window, which decides whether December is a fortnight of lost momentum or concentrated work. Ramadan brings shortened school days; sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar slot, which many students prefer because evening concentration during Ramadan is often better than late-afternoon concentration.

On tutors and regulation: private tuition in the UAE operates under the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligible categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents and university students. Those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published. Abu Dhabi's ADEK rules also bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, which is a sound principle to apply anywhere. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry endorsement and claims none.

sections.heading: Starting in the window that is actually open
paragraphs: Send three things: the subject and level, the most recent assessed mark with what it was marked against, and the earliest application deadline that binds your child. The third is the one families leave out and the one that decides whether the plan is worth making. We will say plainly if the window has closed and the better use of the money is May preparation.

The second thing to find out, before any session, is what the department will assess next and when. That is a one-email question to the subject teacher, and the answer sets the target. Work aimed at a known upcoming assessment produces evidence; work aimed at the syllabus in general produces a feeling of progress and nothing in the folder.

The trial lesson is free, with no condition beyond scheduling it. It answers whether this tutor can teach this component to this student, which is the only question that matters on a short block. If we think a different tutor fits better, or that the work will not reach the deadline, we say so in that session rather than after four weeks of billing.

Beyond that, the honest summary of what we do here is narrow and worth repeating. We cannot move a prediction, and neither can anyone else outside the school. We can help a student produce better evidence while better evidence still counts, and we can tell you, early, when it no longer does.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get my child's predicted grades raised?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone saying otherwise is misdescribing how predictions work. A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by the subject teacher and submitted by your school's Diploma coordinator. No outside provider influences it, negotiates it or delivers it. What a tutor can do is help the student produce stronger, criteria-marked work in the weeks before the judgement is made, which genuinely changes the evidence a teacher is weighing. That distinction matters commercially as well as factually: a provider promising a predicted grade is telling you something about the rest of its claims.

faqs.question: What evidence does a Dubai school use to set a prediction?
faqs.answer: Timed assessments across both Diploma years, the DP2 mock papers, Internal Assessment drafts and their criteria marks, and the teacher's reading of the student's trajectory. Departments weight these differently, and in Dubai schools with small Diploma sets the teacher's direct knowledge carries real weight. The practical move is to ask three questions by email: what evidence exists, what will be assessed next, and against which criteria. Those answers tell you whether any outside support can still reach the folder before the prediction is submitted.

faqs.question: How late in DP2 can new work still change the picture?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which application deadline binds your child. United States early deadlines in the autumn can close the window before Dubai schools have even sat their mocks, in which case the prediction rests largely on DP1 evidence. UCAS timing falls close enough to the mock window that a December or January mock can matter a great deal. UAE institutions and some others run later still. Our first question is always which deadline is earliest for you, because where the window has closed the honest advice is to stop and redirect everything to the May session.

faqs.question: Is a higher prediction always better for my child?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the part most prediction-chasing ignores. A conditional offer is confirmed against actual results, not predicted ones. A prediction above the student's real trajectory buys an offer that may not survive results day, and the summer that follows is harder than a realistic application would have been. That is why we treat evidence-building and exam preparation as the same work: genuinely stronger assessed work improves both what the teacher sees now and what the student achieves in the May session.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects respond fastest to a few weeks of work?
faqs.answer: Economics, Biology and Mathematics tend to move quickest. Economics because diagram accuracy and evaluation structure are learnable in weeks and move whole mark bands. Biology because most lost marks are command-term shape rather than missing content. Mathematics because departments set frequent timed assessments, so new evidence appears quickly. Chemistry and Physics move more slowly on written papers, since the content load is heavier, though their Internal Assessments remain a genuine lever while still in draft. Theory of Knowledge is underrated: its criteria are learnable and it carries points.

faqs.question: How much of the Diploma total comes from TOK and the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Up to three points, awarded through a published matrix combining the grades for Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, on top of a maximum of 42 subject points for a total of 45. Three points is frequently the gap between an offer being met and missed, and these are the components Dubai families most often leave unmanaged. Both are predicted alongside subjects, so asking the coordinator what core contribution is being predicted, and on what basis, is a short conversation with a real payoff in DP2.

faqs.question: My child's mock was far below their coursework marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the two measure different things. Coursework is produced with notes, time and support; a mock answer is produced alone under a clock. A large gap between them usually means the knowledge is supported rather than secure, and that is exactly what a mock is for. The useful response is to read the script rather than the grade: blanks and one-line late answers indicate pacing, correct content scoring half marks indicates command terms, and two weak topics with everything else sound indicates coverage. Each needs different work, and only the paper distinguishes them.

faqs.question: Does the school have to tell us what it is predicting?
faqs.answer: Schools generally share predicted grades with students and families as part of the application process, since the student needs them when deciding where to apply. Practice varies between Dubai schools in how much reasoning is shared alongside the number. If a prediction surprises you, the productive question to the subject teacher is which evidence it rests on rather than whether it can be changed. That conversation often reveals a single assessment that dominated the judgement, which tells you precisely where new work should be aimed.

faqs.question: What does prediction-window support cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits with travel inside the rate, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists, with one premium provider at AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. For this job timing changes cost more than rate does: three sessions in October reach the evidence folder, while ten in February often cannot. Our rate is confirmed after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is it better to start this work in DP1 instead?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and almost nobody does. The DP1 summer is the cheapest and least pressured point to change what a teacher believes about a student's trajectory, because there is time for the change to be observed across the autumn rather than asserted in January. Specialist availability across Dubai is also at its loosest then, before every school's mock lands in the same fortnight. Families who come to us between DP1 and DP2 spend less and get more, consistently. By the January rush the same money buys fewer options.

faqs.question: Do you deliver this in our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. For evidence-building the reason is specificity: the work depends on the tutor knowing exactly what a component's criteria require, and an in-home arrangement limits you to specialists willing to drive to your community in the narrow hours a DP2 student is free. The online format also leaves a record, since annotated marked work is saved rather than left on paper, which matters when the point is to show a sequence of improving work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on my child's IA while predictions are being formed?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the boundary the IB sets, and it is often the single most useful thing available because the draft is live evidence. A tutor can explain the assessment criteria, question the research question and method, and give feedback on what the student has written. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or edit it to completion. One provider ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750, which risks a malpractice finding against the whole Diploma. No prediction is worth that exposure.

faqs.question: How many sessions does an evidence sprint usually take?
faqs.answer: Three to six in one subject, across two to four weeks, aimed at a specific upcoming assessment. The shape is deliberately narrow: find out what is coming, teach to its criteria, set a comparable task, mark it, and let the student meet the real assessment having already done one like it. Occasionally two subjects run in parallel, though a DP2 student with school, the KHDA mandatory subjects and an Internal Assessment in progress rarely has room for more. We would rather sequence two subjects than run three badly.

faqs.question: What if we are told the prediction is already submitted?
faqs.answer: Then the useful work changes completely, and we will say so rather than keep selling. Once predictions are in, the only number that matters is the final May result, because conditional offers are confirmed against real grades. At that point the plan should widen from targeted evidence production to full past-paper rotation under timed conditions, with Internal Assessment work continuing to its own deadline. That is a different and usually longer piece of work, and it is better value than trying to influence something already decided.

faqs.question: Will sessions still run through the winter break and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many Dubai families travel over the winter break, and because every session runs over live video a student can continue from wherever they are or pause deliberately and resume, provided the plan is adjusted rather than allowed to drift. Ramadan brings shortened school days and a different household rhythm; recurring slots commonly move to a post-Iftar time, which students frequently prefer because evening focus during Ramadan tends to beat late-afternoon focus. All scheduling is in Gulf Standard Time.

What is still open, usually for a few weeks, is the quality of the work a subject teacher is looking at when the judgement is made. Tell us the subject and level, the most recent assessed mark, and the earliest application deadline that binds your child, and we will say whether that window is open and whether a specialist in the right component is free. If it has closed, we will tell you to spend the money on May preparation instead. The trial lesson is free, live, one-to-one, and in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-private-tuition.tutorsIntro: Transition work needs a tutor fluent in two specifications at once: the one the pupil has just left and the one they have just joined. Each profile below states which specifications the tutor has taught, because that pairing is the whole skill here.

intro.heading: Nothing went wrong in the first term of DP1
paragraphs: A familiar Dubai conversation happens every November. A pupil who finished IGCSE with a column of 8s and 9s is sitting at 4 and 5 in three Diploma subjects, the household has decided something is badly wrong, and the first instinct is to buy content tuition in all six subjects. In most cases nothing is wrong with the pupil's knowledge. The instrument changed, the depth changed, and the kind of answer that earns marks changed, and nobody told them.

The specifics differ by route. A pupil arriving from IGCSE has been rewarded for recall and for complete, tidy answers; the Diploma rewards analysis against a command term and punishes the complete tidy answer to the wrong question. A pupil arriving from the Middle Years Programme has been marked against criteria out of 8 and finds content recall suddenly mattering. A pupil arriving from CBSE has strong mathematical technique and no experience of writing an evaluated argument. An American-system pupil has breadth and little depth in any single subject.

Those are four different gaps, and they need four different interventions. The expensive mistake is buying a weekly content slot in each weak subject, because a content slot does not fix an instrument problem and three months disappear before anyone notices. The cheap fix is identifying which gap is present, which takes one session per subject with a marked script in hand.

Dubai makes this a mass-market problem rather than an individual one. The emirate licenses 17 different curricula across 227 private schools, and pupils move between them routinely, at 11, at 14 and especially at 16. Several Dubai schools run the Middle Years Programme only to Year 9 and then IGCSE to Year 11 before splitting into the Diploma or A Level, which means a single cohort arriving in DP1 may contain pupils from three different assessment cultures.

This page also covers the two decisions that get made alongside the transition and matter for years: the mathematics route, which some degrees specify and which cannot be changed late without difficulty, and Ministry of Education equivalency, which decides whether a qualification is recognised for university entry in the UAE. Both are poorly served online, and one ranking competitor publishes the equivalency subject count incorrectly. Teaching here is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, as in-home visiting is offered only in India. That matters more here than on most pages, because the scarce person in a transition is a tutor fluent in both the specification the pupil left and the one they joined, and such people are spread thinly across a whole country rather than clustered in any one Dubai community.

dubai/ib-private-tuition.programmesIntro: Each programme hands the next one a specific set of habits, some of which help and some of which actively cost marks. The notes below describe what a pupil carries forward and what has to be unlearned.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Hands forward excellent process habits: reflection, planning, evaluating method. Hands forward a weakness in content recall, because the programme marks how a pupil works rather than what they can retrieve under time pressure. Middle Years pupils entering the Diploma usually need retrieval practice and timed conditions, not more teaching about thinking.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools that end the Middle Years Programme at Year 9 interrupt this sequence, and those pupils sit IGCSE for two years before the Diploma. They arrive in DP1 with the opposite profile from a full continuum pupil: strong recall, weak independent process, and no experience of a long self-directed written piece.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, scored out of 45 including up to three points from the core. The first term is the sharpest adjustment in the two years: command terms carry mark ceilings, coursework starts immediately, and the volume of simultaneous deadlines across six subjects is unlike anything in IGCSE. Candidates who survive the first term well usually did one thing, which was learning the command-term hierarchy early.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai candidates sit the May session. Higher Level option blocks in smaller cohorts can force a subject choice the pupil did not want, which is a genuine transition problem rather than a preference. Confirm all session and deadline dates with your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly, as the IB sets and revises them.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A real option for a pupil whose transition problem is that two of their six Diploma subjects are dead weight. Pairing at least two DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project removes the load without removing the rigour, and the DP courses are marked identically to any other Diploma course.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools license the programme, so switching into it is often not available even where it would suit. Where it is, it is worth a conversation with the Diploma coordinator in the first term of DP1 rather than after the first set of reports, because timetable changes get harder as the year goes on.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The earliest transition in the chain and the least discussed. A pupil moving from PYP into a Middle Years or IGCSE-track school meets formal marking for the first time, and the dip that follows is about measurement rather than ability. The mechanical skills that carry forward usefully are written fluency under time limits and number facts recalled without a calculator.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai a pupil transferring between curricula at primary level also changes how the mandatory UAE subjects are delivered, since KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. A transferring pupil can be placed in a different stream from the one they are used to.

dubai/ib-private-tuition.subjectsIntro: The transition gap is subject-specific, and the entries below name what actually changes in each. These are the sentences a pupil needs in September of DP1 rather than in February.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The jump from IGCSE Extended is in abstraction and in proof. Technique transfers well; the expectation of justifying a general case does not. Paper 1 without a calculator exposes pupils who used a calculator for routine manipulation throughout IGCSE, which most Dubai pupils did.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technically gentler than Analysis and Approaches and conceptually different: statistics and modelling, with marks in interpretation rather than manipulation. IGCSE pupils find the content accessible and lose marks on the final sentence of each answer, where a number must be explained in context.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: IGCSE rewards recall of reactions; the Diploma asks why, with equations balanced, state symbols present and mechanisms justified. Higher Level organic chemistry is genuinely new material rather than deeper coverage. The investigation also arrives in DP1, which no IGCSE pupil has rehearsed at that scale.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The content overlap with IGCSE is substantial and misleading. What changes is the explanation standard: an answer must set out a causal chain, and a correct number earns nothing without one. Uncertainty handling, barely touched at IGCSE, becomes a marked skill at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume increases sharply and so does the precision expected in terminology. Pupils who wrote generously at IGCSE and were rewarded for it now write long answers to short-command questions and lose time. Data-based questions require specific values from the figure rather than a described trend.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Usually a new subject at Diploma level rather than a continuation, which makes it one of the fairest starts in the programme. Pupils arriving from Business Studies at IGCSE must unlearn descriptive answering; diagrams carry marks and must be referenced in the prose to earn them.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: IGCSE English Language rewards accurate, organised writing. The Diploma rewards analysis of how meaning is constructed and, in Paper 2, genuine comparison. Strong IGCSE writers are the group most often surprised here, because fluency is not the thing being marked.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The move is from narrative to argument, with historiography and source evaluation marked explicitly. Pupils who scored well at IGCSE by knowing more facts find that more facts no longer help, and that a structured interpretive claim does.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: New to almost everyone, which levels the field, and heavily dependent on a method that pupils arriving from recall-based systems find unfamiliar: evidence first, assertion second. Each named study needs a method, a finding and a limitation held together.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pupils fluent in Python are often the ones who lose marks, because IB pseudocode conventions are examined and Python is not an acceptable substitute. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and an annually published case study, neither of which has an IGCSE equivalent.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.levels: SL, and HL for Arabic B
subjects.description: A practical route for pupils in Dubai who have studied Arabic as an additional language at school, where the Diploma courses assess productive use rather than coverage. Marks reward range used accurately rather than range attempted, which is a measurable change from a school-report view of progress.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: No prior equivalent in any arrival route, which is why it produces so many blank pages in DP1. The adjustment is recognising that a prescribed title asks about knowledge rather than about the world. Pupils who arrive from the Middle Years Programme have the best start, having argued from criteria before.

dubai/ib-private-tuition.regionsIntro: Which transition a cohort faces depends on the schools in the area, because school pathways differ sharply across the emirate. These notes name the route most common in each cluster.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Tecom
regions.note: Several continuum schools, so pupils here most often arrive in DP1 straight from the Middle Years Programme. The characteristic gap is content retrieval under timed conditions rather than thinking skills, and it responds to retrieval practice within weeks.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: A high proportion of British-curriculum schools feeding both A Level and the Diploma, so this cluster produces the classic IGCSE-to-DP1 transition. Command-term discipline is the single highest-value intervention for these pupils.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Qusais
regions.note: Strong Indian-curriculum presence, so pupils arriving at the Diploma often come from CBSE with excellent mathematical technique and no experience of evaluated written argument. The gap is in essay subjects, not in maths.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Mixed British and IB provision within a short radius, and frequent mid-phase school moves between them. Pupils here sometimes transfer at the end of Year 10, which is the most awkward point in the chain and needs explicit bridging.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer schools with growing Diploma cohorts, so option blocks are tighter and a pupil may be placed in a Higher Level subject that was the only one available. That is a transition problem worth naming early rather than treating as a weakness.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Mudon
regions.note: Established British and IB schools with strong Year 11 cohorts, producing a large IGCSE-to-Diploma flow each September. Maths route choice is the recurring question here, because many pupils are aiming at quantitative degrees.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Internationally mobile families with mid-year arrivals from American and European systems, which is the hardest transition of all because it happens outside the school calendar. These pupils need a mapping exercise before any teaching.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to several universities, so equivalency and admissions questions come up earlier here than elsewhere. Families in this cluster ask about Ministry of Education recognition in DP1 rather than discovering it in DP2.

schoolClusters.city: Continuum schools: Middle Years straight into the Diploma
schoolClusters.note: Pupils arrive having been marked against criteria for five years. Their transition gap is retrieval and timed performance, and it is usually cleared faster than families expect once it is correctly named.

schoolClusters.city: Schools running IGCSE before the Diploma or A Level
schoolClusters.note: Pupils arrive from two years of content-based external assessment and split at 16. This cluster produces the classic command-term gap and the largest share of first-term Diploma shock in the emirate.

schoolClusters.note: Mid-phase and mid-year arrivals from Indian, American and European systems. These pupils need a subject-by-subject mapping of what they have covered before anyone decides what to teach.

sections.heading: What IB private tuition in Dubai is usually needed to fix in DP1
paragraphs: The first term of the Diploma produces a specific and predictable pattern of disappointment, and it has four distinct causes depending on where the pupil came from. Naming the cause correctly is worth more than any amount of teaching, because three of the four causes are not knowledge problems and will not respond to content tuition.

Cause one is the instrument. IGCSE awards marks for complete, accurate, well-organised answers. The Diploma awards marks against a command term with a ceiling: an outline question cannot pay more than outline marks however much is written, and the extra writing costs time on a later question. A pupil who was rewarded for thoroughness is now penalised for it twice over.

Cause two is depth without warning. Several Diploma subjects cover apparently familiar IGCSE content and then ask a question two layers deeper. Physics is the clearest case: the topic list looks recognisable and the explanation standard is entirely different. Pupils read the familiar topic, answer at the familiar level, and cannot understand why a correct answer scored two out of five.

Cause three is simultaneity. Six subjects each generating coursework, plus Theory of Knowledge, plus an Extended Essay question to settle, plus CAS, is a workload-management problem rather than an academic one, and it hits hardest in October and November. Cause four, which is real and less common than families assume, is a genuine content gap left by a curriculum transfer. Only that fourth one justifies a sustained weekly content slot, and a single session with a marked script usually identifies which cause is operating.
bullets: Instrument change: command terms with ceilings, not thoroughness
Unsignalled depth: familiar topics, unfamiliar standard of explanation
Simultaneity: six coursework streams arriving at once
A genuine content gap, which is the least common of the four

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma gap, subject by subject
paragraphs: One competitor page in this market has a single subheading on the IGCSE-to-IB gap. Nobody has a structured, subject-by-subject version, which is odd, because it is the most frequently needed document in Dubai every September.

The table below sets out, for the subjects Dubai pupils most often continue, where an IGCSE pupil actually stands, what the Diploma assumes on day one, the specific gap between them, and roughly how long it takes to close with targeted support. The weeks column assumes one session a week with consolidation between, and it assumes the gap has been correctly identified, which is the harder part.

Two patterns are visible once it is laid out. The gaps in the sciences are mostly about explanation standard and about the arrival of an extended investigation, not about content. The gaps in the humanities are about argument structure. Only mathematics has a genuine content and abstraction gap, and only at Higher Level in Analysis and Approaches.

That shape has a practical consequence for spending. A family buying content tuition in three sciences has probably bought the wrong thing, and a family buying one block on explanation structure across all three has probably bought the right thing more cheaply. The subjects worth paying content rates for are the ones where the table says content. The weeks column is also worth reading as a budget rather than as a forecast: a gap listed at four to eight weeks that is still open in March was either misdiagnosed in October or was never worked on between sessions, and both of those are answerable questions rather than reasons to extend the arrangement.

sections.heading: Middle Years to Diploma: when criterion marking stops
paragraphs: Pupils moving from the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma inside the same school are assumed to have the smoothest transition, and in one respect they do. They have been assessed against published criteria for five years and they understand that a descriptor is a target. That habit is worth a great deal in coursework and in the core.

The problem is the other direction. Criterion-referenced marking out of 8 rewards how a pupil approaches work, and it does not require much retrieval under time pressure. The Diploma's examined papers do, and they do it across a two-year content load. Middle Years arrivals frequently have excellent process and thin recall, and they are surprised by an examination that simply asks what they know.

There is a second, subtler issue. Middle Years marking is formative in culture: a piece of work gets a criterion mark, feedback follows, and improvement is expected on the next piece. Examined Diploma components are terminal. A pupil used to a cycle of attempt, feedback and improvement needs to understand that the mock script is their feedback and the May session is the only attempt that counts.

The good news is that both problems respond quickly to the right instrument. Retrieval practice and timed conditions are cheap to administer and produce visible change within weeks. What does not help is more teaching about thinking skills, which is what these pupils already have most of and what a well-meaning tutor often supplies.

sections.heading: Arriving from CBSE, the American system or a British Year 11
paragraphs: Dubai's private school market licenses 17 curricula, and transfers between them are routine rather than exceptional. Each origin produces a recognisable profile, and a tutor who knows the profile can skip two weeks of discovery.

A pupil arriving from CBSE typically brings strong, drilled mathematical technique and a high tolerance for sustained work, with little experience of writing an evaluated argument or of practical investigation design. The maths transition is usually easy, Higher Level sciences are manageable, and the humanities and the core are where the work lies. These pupils are often under-placed by schools reading an overall average rather than the profile.

A pupil arriving from an American high school brings breadth, familiarity with continuous assessment and strong classroom participation, and usually less depth in any single subject than the Diploma assumes at Higher Level. The practical risk is choosing three Higher Level subjects on interest and discovering in February that two of them assume a year of prior depth. An early mapping session is worth more to this group than to any other.

A pupil transferring at the end of British Year 11 has the most straightforward path on paper and one specific risk: if they transferred mid-IGCSE or sat a reduced set, the equivalency position needs checking early. The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

sections.heading: The mathematics route, and the degree at the end of it
paragraphs: The choice between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation is made at 15 or 16 and has consequences at 18. It is the single most consequential subject decision in the Diploma and the one most often made on reputation rather than on information.

The courses are not easier and harder versions of the same material. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented with a calculator-free Paper 1. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics, technology-permitted throughout, with marks concentrated in interpreting results in context. A pupil can find either harder than the other depending on how they think.

The admissions question is where families most need a straight answer and most often get a confident wrong one. Some quantitative degrees, including engineering, mathematics, physics and several economics programmes, specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Others accept either route. Requirements differ by university, by programme and by intake year, and they are revised. The only reliable method is to read the current entry requirements on each university's own admissions page for the specific named programme, and to do it in DP1 rather than DP2.

What a route review session does is narrower than advice and more useful: it establishes which of the two problems a pupil actually has. If a candidate in Analysis and Approaches is failing Paper 1 while coping with Paper 2, that is calculator dependence and it is a four-week drill, not a wrong course. If a candidate needs Analysis and Approaches for a stated prerequisite and is sitting in Applications, that is an urgent timetable conversation with the school, and the window for it closes.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the figure one competitor gets wrong
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which a school-leaving qualification is recognised in the UAE, and it matters for university admission here. No competitor page in several of the researched query clusters mentions it at all, and one ranking page publishes the wrong subject count, which is a useful illustration of how little scrutiny this subject gets.

For the British track the published rule is specific. A student must show one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five.

For the American track the requirements are stated as test thresholds. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For the International Baccalaureate, no points threshold is published in the source that sets out the other two tracks, and this page will not invent one. Any figure you see quoted for IB equivalency should be checked on the Ministry of Education's own site or with the emirate attestation authority before you rely on it. Equivalency and attestation are processes run by the authorities, not services a tutoring platform performs or can influence, and tutoring is not a requirement for any part of them.

sections.heading: Choosing three Higher Level subjects you can actually sustain
paragraphs: Higher Level choices are made with incomplete information and are hard to change late. The failure mode is not choosing a subject that is too hard; it is choosing three whose heaviest demands all arrive in the same month, which is a scheduling error disguised as an academic one.

The sustainable question has three parts. Does the pupil need this subject at Higher Level for a stated degree prerequisite, or is it ambition. Does the Higher Level content represent genuinely new material or deeper coverage, because new material costs more time. And when does this subject's coursework fall relative to the other two, because three investigations due in the same fortnight is a predictable crisis.

There is also a prior-attainment signal worth reading honestly. A pupil who reached the top IGCSE grade in a subject through sustained, heavy work is in a different position from one who reached it comfortably, and only the second has spare capacity for a third demanding Higher Level. Schools rarely make that distinction and families know the answer.

Where a change is still possible, the window is short and it belongs to the school. A conversation with the Diploma coordinator in the first term of DP1 can produce a move from Higher to Standard Level that is simply unavailable six months later. The right time to have that conversation is after the first marked assessments and before the first report, which is a narrow and easily missed fortnight.

sections.heading: What a transition block actually contains
paragraphs: Transition support is short and specific, and it should end. A family buying it as an open-ended weekly arrangement has usually misdiagnosed an instrument problem as a content problem, which is the expensive error this page exists to prevent.

The first session per subject is mapping and diagnosis, worked from the pupil's own marked DP1 assessment alongside what their previous specification covered. The output is two written lists: topics genuinely never taught, and the mark-losing habits carried forward from the old system. Those two lists require different treatment and most pupils have more of the second.

Sessions two to four take the habit list. Command-term ceilings drilled against the pupil's own answers. Explanation chains built in the sciences. Answer length matched to the verb. These are mechanical, they are visible in the next marked assessment, and they generalise across subjects, which is why one block often improves three subjects at once.

Only after that does content teaching make sense, and only against the specific topics on the first list. A block structured this way typically runs four to six sessions per subject and then stops, with a review against school-marked work to confirm the pattern of lost marks has changed. If a family is still buying weekly sessions in April on a gap that was diagnosed as instrumental in October, something went wrong in the diagnosis and it should be revisited rather than funded. The review is the point at which that question gets asked out loud, which is why it is scheduled rather than left to arise.

process.title: Say where the pupil came from
process.description: The previous curriculum, the previous school year and the subjects taken, not just the current year group. The arrival route determines the profile, and the profile determines whether the gap is in content, in instrument or in workload management.

process.title: Send a marked DP1 assessment
process.description: One piece of marked Diploma work per subject of concern is worth more than a full set of IGCSE results. It shows which mark-losing habits have carried forward, which is the information that selects the intervention.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session with the proposed specialist at no cost and with no card required, spent mapping prior coverage against the new specification. You leave with the two written lists, whether or not anything is booked afterwards.

process.title: Deal with the decisions before the teaching
process.description: If the maths route, a Higher Level choice or an equivalency question is live, settle it first. Those decisions have windows that close, and teaching inside a subject the pupil should not be sitting is the most wasteful spending available.

process.title: Review and stop
process.description: Four to six sessions per subject, measured against the next school-marked assessment, then a decision to stop or to continue on a named content gap. A transition block that has become a permanent arrangement was probably the wrong diagnosis.

whyPoints.title: The gap mapped, not described
whyPoints.description: A subject-by-subject table of where an IGCSE pupil stands, what the Diploma assumes and how long the gap takes to close. One competitor has a single subheading on this; nobody has the structured version, which is the document every Dubai family needs in September.

whyPoints.title: Four arrival routes treated separately
whyPoints.description: CBSE, American, British post-IGCSE and Middle Years arrivals have different profiles and need different first moves. Treating them identically is why so much transition tuition is bought in the wrong subjects.

whyPoints.title: Instrument problems named as such
whyPoints.description: Three of the four causes of first-term Diploma disappointment are not knowledge problems and do not respond to content teaching. Saying so costs us the larger booking and saves families a term.

whyPoints.title: Route decisions checked against the real source
whyPoints.description: Mathematics route and Higher Level choices tested against the current published entry requirements for the specific named programmes, on each university's own admissions page, rather than against a general claim about what universities want.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency quoted accurately
whyPoints.description: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 with Arabic and Islamic education excluded, plus the Advanced Level requirement, and the American test thresholds. Where no IB figure is published, none is invented, and one ranking competitor's subject count is simply wrong.

whyPoints.title: Support that is designed to end
whyPoints.description: Four to six sessions per subject against a diagnosed gap, then a review and a stop. Transition work that becomes a two-year weekly arrangement was misdiagnosed, and continuing to bill for it is not a service.

faqs.question: Why did my child's grades drop in the first term of the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Usually because the measurement changed rather than because the pupil did. IGCSE awards marks for complete, accurate, well-organised answers. Diploma papers award marks against a command term with a ceiling, so an outline question cannot pay more than outline marks however much is written, and the extra writing costs time on later questions. A pupil rewarded for thoroughness is now penalised twice. This is diagnosable from a single marked script and is repaired in weeks, which is a very different proposition from a content gap.

faqs.question: Is the jump from IGCSE to the IB Diploma mainly about content?
faqs.answer: Only in mathematics, and mainly at Higher Level in Analysis and Approaches, where abstraction, proof and calculator-free manipulation are genuinely new. In the sciences the gap is the standard of explanation plus the arrival of an extended investigation, not the topic list. In the humanities it is argument structure. That matters for spending: a family buying content tuition across three sciences has usually bought the wrong thing, where one block on explanation structure across all three would have been cheaper and more effective.

faqs.question: What do Middle Years Programme pupils struggle with most in DP1?
faqs.answer: Content recall under timed conditions. Criterion-referenced marking out of 8 rewards how a pupil approaches work and does not require much retrieval against the clock, so continuum pupils arrive with strong process and thin recall. There is a second issue that is subtler: Middle Years assessment is formative, with feedback and an improved next attempt, while examined Diploma components are terminal. These pupils need retrieval practice and timed sections, not more teaching about thinking skills, which is what they already have.

faqs.question: My child moved from CBSE to an IB school in Dubai. Where will the problems be?
faqs.answer: Rarely in mathematics. CBSE pupils typically arrive with drilled technique and real work stamina, which transfers well into both Diploma maths routes and into Higher Level sciences. The gap is in evaluated written argument and in investigation design: writing a position and defending it against a counterposition, and designing a practical with a controllable variable. Schools often under-place these pupils by reading an overall average rather than the profile, so a subject-by-subject mapping session in the first month is worth more than any teaching.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course should a Dubai pupil choose for engineering?
faqs.answer: Several quantitative degrees, engineering among them, specify Analysis and Approaches and often at Higher Level, but requirements differ by university, by programme and by intake year and they are revised. The only reliable method is to read the current entry requirements for each specific named programme on that university's own admissions page, and to do it during the first Diploma year while a change is still possible. Any tutoring page, including this one, is the wrong source of record for an admissions requirement.

faqs.question: Can a pupil switch maths routes partway through the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it gets rapidly harder. The question to settle first is whether the route is genuinely wrong. A candidate in Analysis and Approaches failing the calculator-free paper while coping with the calculator paper has a calculator-dependence problem, which is a four-week drill rather than a wrong course. A candidate who needs Analysis and Approaches for a stated prerequisite and is sitting in Applications has an urgent timetable conversation to have with the school, and the window for it closes within the first year.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education require for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track rule requires a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. In addition a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor page states six subjects, which is wrong, and verifying on the Ministry's own site is worth the five minutes.

faqs.question: Does my child's Arabic grade count towards the five equivalency subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The published rule states explicitly that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. That is a useful fact for a family planning a subject set, because it changes which five subjects actually satisfy the requirement. It does not change the separate matter of KHDA requiring Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, which is a school obligation rather than an equivalency one.

faqs.question: What score does the UAE require for IB equivalency?
faqs.answer: The source that sets out the British and American track requirements states no International Baccalaureate points threshold, and this page will not invent one. Any figure you find quoted for IB equivalency should be checked on the Ministry of Education's own site or with the emirate attestation authority before you rely on it, because an unsourced number on a tutoring page is a liability for whoever acts on it. Equivalency and attestation are processes run by the authorities, and no tutoring provider performs, influences or accelerates them.

faqs.question: What are the American-track test thresholds for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published requirements are expressed as test scores. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. Those are the figures as published in the clarification of equivalency requirements, and as with every other number in this area the right place to confirm them before acting is the Ministry of Education's own site or the emirate attestation authority.

faqs.question: How do I know whether three Higher Level subjects are too many?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions rather than one. Does the pupil need each subject at Higher Level for a stated degree prerequisite, or is one of them ambition. Does the Higher Level content represent genuinely new material or deeper coverage, since new material costs more time. And when does each subject's coursework fall, because three investigations due in the same fortnight is a predictable crisis. The honest prior-attainment signal is comfort rather than grade: a top IGCSE grade reached through heavy sustained work leaves less spare capacity than the same grade reached easily.

faqs.question: When is the last moment to move a subject from Higher to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: The window belongs to the school and it is narrower than families expect, typically in the first term of the first Diploma year. The sensible timing is after the first marked assessments and before the first formal report, which is a fortnight that is easy to miss. A conversation with the Diploma coordinator then can produce a change that is simply unavailable six months later. Where it is still possible, a Standard Level 7 is worth more for most university offers than a Higher Level 5 in the same subject.

faqs.question: What does a mid-year transfer into a Dubai IB school need first?
faqs.answer: A mapping exercise, before any teaching. A pupil arriving from another system mid-year has an unknown coverage profile, and the school is working from a transcript rather than from knowledge of what was actually taught. One session per subject comparing the previous specification against the new one produces a written list of topics genuinely never covered. Teaching before that list exists means guessing, and the guesses tend to repeat what the pupil already knows while leaving the real gaps untouched until an examination finds them.

faqs.question: Does the Career-related Programme solve a transition problem?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is worth knowing about. Where the real problem is that two of a pupil's six Diploma subjects are dead weight, pairing at least two DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project removes the load without removing rigour, and the DP courses are marked identically to any other Diploma course. The obstacle in Dubai is availability: only a small number of schools license the programme, so the option frequently does not exist. If it does, raise it in the first term rather than after reports.

faqs.question: Are transition sessions for Dubai pupils delivered online?
faqs.answer: Yes, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE, since in-home visiting is offered only in India. For transition work the online model matters more than usual, because the scarce skill is a tutor fluent in two specifications at once, the one the pupil left and the one they joined. A tutor who has taught both Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry and Diploma Chemistry is not easy to find within one community and is reachable across a national pool.

dubai/ib-private-tuition.closingHeading: Map the gap before you buy the teaching
dubai/ib-private-tuition.closingBody: If the first term of the Diploma has gone badly, the useful first step is a map rather than a tutor. Send the previous curriculum, the subjects and one marked piece of Diploma work per subject of concern, and you will get back two written lists: topics genuinely never taught, and mark-losing habits carried forward from the old system. Most pupils have more of the second, and the second is cheaper and faster to fix. The trial lesson that follows is a full mapping session over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no card required. If the answer is a four-session block rather than a weekly slot, that is what you will be told.

intro.heading: A regulated transaction nobody describes as one
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is not an informal arrangement between consenting adults. It runs on a work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. Of the sixty-odd competitor pages examined for this project, one touched licensing at all, in a single subheading.

The permit itself is unusually unobtrusive. It is granted free of charge for two years. The ministry's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school pupils aged 15 to 18, and university students.

That breadth explains the shape of this market. A university student charging AED 60 an hour and a Diploma specialist charging AED 400 are both operating within the same permit framework, which means the permit tells a parent that the arrangement is lawful and nothing whatsoever about whether the tutor has taught Higher Level Chemistry. Those are two separate checks, and most families make neither.

There is a second licence that gets confused with the first, and the confusion is commercially convenient for some providers. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained after initial approval, with a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That is a licence for premises. It is not a badge that a tutoring platform can borrow, and the phrase to be most sceptical of in this market is any tutor described as approved by a regulator.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. It has no premises in the UAE. Teaching for every UAE family is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. The rest of this page is what that means in practice, what the alternatives cost, and how to check any of it. The verification work is genuinely small: two questions in one email, asked of anyone from any source, settle most of what a parent needs to know before money moves. The reason so few families ask them is that nothing in this market suggests there is anything to ask about.

dubai/ib-private-tutor.programmesIntro: The permit framework applies identically across every programme, but what a parent is buying changes as the stakes rise. Each note below describes what due diligence is proportionate at that stage.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: At primary level the permit question matters more than the specialism question, because the teaching itself is within reach of many competent people and the safeguarding considerations are at their highest. A parent should ask about the permit, about who else is present during a session, and about what records are kept, before asking about pedagogy.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai primary pupils also carry the mandatory UAE subjects, and KHDA requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. That requirement sits on schools rather than on private tutors, so a parent engaging support in those subjects should ask directly about the tutor's own qualifications.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The middle years are where families most often engage a tutor through an informal recommendation, and where the fewest questions get asked. The proportionate check is the permit, the subject experience and a written note of what each session covered. Criterion-referenced marking out of 8 is specific enough that a tutor either knows the descriptors or does not.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools frequently switch from the Middle Years Programme to IGCSE at Year 10, and a tutor engaged for one may be asked to continue into the other. A parent should confirm explicitly that the tutor has taught the new specification, rather than assuming continuity, because the assessment cultures are genuinely different.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Highest stakes, highest prices, and the stage where verification matters most. A Diploma candidate's coursework carries roughly a fifth of each subject grade and is subject to academic-honesty rules whose consequences fall on the candidate. Any tutor offering to produce part of a submission should be declined and reported to the school, whatever their permit status.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma candidates sit the May session, so demand for specialists peaks between February and April and the market is at its least discriminating in exactly that window. Families who verify in October face a buyer's market; families who verify in March often skip the checks entirely.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A thin market with few experienced providers, which raises the risk of paying specialist rates for general support. The reflective project has published criteria, so a usable verification question is to ask a prospective tutor to describe how the criteria differ from the Extended Essay criteria. A vague answer settles it.
programmes.countryNote: Because few Dubai schools license the programme, a family may find that the only available support is from outside the emirate. That is lawful and normal where teaching is delivered over live video, and it is worth preferring an honest non-local specialist to a local generalist describing themselves as experienced.

dubai/ib-private-tutor.subjectsIntro: Verification is easier when the question is specific. For each subject below there is a question whose answer separates someone who has taught the level from someone who has read about it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask where a candidate must show arrows originating from in an organic mechanism, and what a Paper 2 answer loses without state symbols. A tutor who has marked the subject answers in one sentence. The investigation question to ask is how many data points they would consider sufficient to evaluate a trend.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask how they would teach the uncertainty section of the data analysis paper, since that is the part most rarely taught in class and most responsive to coaching. Ask also what distinguishes an explain answer from a describe answer in the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Ask which command terms cap an answer and how they would stop a candidate writing a discuss answer to an outline question. On coursework, ask what level of replication they would require before accepting a conclusion as supportable.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask how they would diagnose calculator dependence from a pair of Paper 1 and Paper 2 scripts, and how they approach the generalisation step in the Higher Level extended investigation paper. Both questions require having taught the course rather than the maths.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Ask what a candidate must add after calculating a correlation coefficient to earn the final mark, and which conditions they check before accepting a statistical test. Interpretation in context is where this course's marks live.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask how diagram marks are earned and lost, and what the three-commentary portfolio rules require in terms of syllabus coverage and article age. Those rules are specific and a tutor either knows them or has not supervised the component.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ask what they do with the pre-released case study and when they would start on it. A tutor who begins in the spring has not run the subject before; the preparation window is known months ahead and is the whole advantage of the component.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Ask what four facts they expect a candidate to hold for each named study, and how they handle the ethical considerations section of the experimental write-up. Both are concrete and both expose a generalist quickly.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask what makes an essay comparative rather than two analyses in sequence, and how long a line of inquiry for the Higher Level essay should be before it is workable. These are structural questions with structural answers.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Ask where their role stops. A tutor who answers with a clear account of what they will not do, and why the consequence falls on the candidate, has read the academic-honesty rules. A tutor who promises to help get it finished has told you something important.

dubai/ib-private-tutor.regionsIntro: What a family can realistically verify, and what the local market looks like, differs by community. These notes concern the hiring process rather than the teaching.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: High turnover of short-term residents means a large informal tutoring market advertised through building groups, where permit status is rarely mentioned and references are hard to follow up. The convenience is real and so is the verification gap.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Community recommendation networks are strong here and produce good matches often, but a recommendation substitutes for verification rather than supplying it. Ask the referring parent what they checked, not only whether they were happy.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Tecom
regions.note: Dense concentration of tuition centres with premises, which is a different legal arrangement from an individual tutor and carries a KHDA institute permit rather than a personal one. Worth knowing which you are contracting with.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Established private tutoring market with experienced independent tutors, many of them long-term residents. This is the cluster where asking about permit status is least likely to be met with surprise.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Qusais
regions.note: A large and competitive market at lower price points, including many university-student tutors who are explicitly eligible for the permit. Verification here is about subject level rather than legality.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Short-let residents and frequent household moves make continuity the main risk. A written agreement covering notice and replacement matters more in this cluster than anywhere else in the emirate.

regions.name: Dubai South and Jumeirah Golf Estates
regions.note: Few resident tutors within practical reach, so families here are usually choosing between online delivery and a long commute priced into the rate. The verification questions matter equally in both cases.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: A substantial university-student tutoring population, which at primary and middle-years level is good value and entirely lawful with a permit. At Higher Level it is where mismatches between price and expertise occur most often.

schoolClusters.note: Named to describe where candidates come from, not to assert any relationship. Families from these cohorts most often ask about coursework boundaries and paper technique rather than content teaching.

sections.heading: What an IB private tutor in Dubai is, in law
paragraphs: A private tutor in the UAE is a person holding a private tuition work permit, issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. The ministry's service page for it, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, states no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system.

Eligibility is deliberately wide. Teachers registered in government or private schools qualify. So do employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school pupils aged 15 to 18. That last category surprises parents and is explicit in the published eligibility list, which tells you something useful about the intended scope: the resolution regularises an existing informal market rather than restricting tutoring to professionals.

The consequence of operating outside it is stated but not quantified. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and press reporting on the regime noted explicitly that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties. A figure circulates online; it could not be verified, so it does not appear here, and any provider quoting you one is repeating something unchecked.

What the permit does not do is worth saying plainly. It is not a teaching qualification, not a subject endorsement, and not a statement about Higher Level competence. A permitted tutor may be a Diploma examiner or a first-year undergraduate. Legality and expertise are two separate checks, and a parent who conflates them has done one of the two things that matter.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor privately, category by category
paragraphs: The table below sets out the eligible categories from the published rules, with what a parent can usefully check in each case. It is the only such table in this market, which is remarkable given that one competitor ranks substantially on a single subheading about licensing.

Two conditions cut across the categories. The permit carries a code of conduct, and that code bars serving pupils affiliated with the tutor's own school. Separately, in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to pupils enrolled at their own school. Those rules are press-reported rather than read from the current policy document, so verify them against ADEK directly before relying on the exact wording, but the direction is unambiguous.

For employed tutors there is an additional practical question a parent cannot answer and should still ask. A government or private-sector employee applying for a private tuition permit is operating alongside an existing employment relationship, and whether their employer's internal policy permits it is a matter between them. A tutor who has thought about this will say so; one who looks blank has not.

The verification route is simple and almost nobody uses it. Ask the individual whether they hold a current private tuition work permit, when it expires, and under which category they applied. A tutor operating properly answers without hesitation. The answer is not something a platform can supply on an individual's behalf, which is why the question belongs to the parent even when a platform made the introduction.

sections.heading: Six provider models, and what each one actually charges
paragraphs: Every competitor page in this market compares itself against an unnamed set of other platforms, which tells a parent nothing. A useful comparison compares models, with rates attributed to whoever published them and the date noted. The figures below come from published provider pages and a 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey.

What separates the models is not quality but where the risk sits. With an independent tutor, the family carries verification, record-keeping and replacement risk, and pays less for it. With a platform, the intermediary carries those and charges for them. With a tuition centre, the premises and the timetable carry the cost, and group delivery makes the hourly figure lower while making the attention per pupil lower too.

The rate column is wide in every model for the reason given earlier: subject and level drive price more than business model does. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist costs more than an SL Biology tutor in every one of these models. What the model changes is what happens in the three situations that actually arise, which are a tutor leaving mid-term, a match that is not working, and a dispute about what was agreed.

On our own row, two things are stated rather than implied. IB Gram does not offer in-home visiting anywhere in the UAE, so the in-home column reads no for us and that is a model decision rather than a shortfall. And no own-price figure appears, because a single number across every subject, level and frequency would be misleading. The figure is agreed at the consultation after the free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Five questions to ask before any money moves
paragraphs: A parent can do most of the useful due diligence in a single email, and the questions are specific enough that evasive answers are obvious. None of them is about qualifications in the abstract, because a qualification does not tell you whether someone has taught the level your child sits.

The first is the permit question: do you hold a current private tuition work permit, and when does it expire. The second is the level question, asked as a subject-specific question rather than a general one: what does a candidate lose a mark for in this specific component. The third is the record question: what will I receive after each session, and what will the four-week review measure.

The fourth is the boundary question, and it is the one that separates this market most sharply. Ask what the tutor will do if your child asks them to look over a nearly finished internal assessment the night before submission. The right answer involves declining to supply text and explaining the academic-honesty consequence. Any version of getting it finished is a reason to stop the conversation.

The fifth is the commercial question, itemised: is the rate per sixty minutes or per session, is there a minimum block, is coursework support inside the figure, what are the cancellation terms, and does the quoted amount include value added tax. On tax specifically, the treatment of tuition fees is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for any tutoring website, so the only safe question is whether the specific figure you have been quoted is inclusive.

sections.heading: What a tutoring enquiry may ask about your child
paragraphs: Lead forms in this market routinely collect a child's school, year group, grades and sometimes a photograph, with no stated purpose and no visible privacy information. That is a data protection question, and in the UAE it sits under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data.

The practical standard a parent should expect is modest and almost nobody meets it: a clear statement of what is collected, why it is needed, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted, with a privacy link on the same page as the form. Information about a minor deserves that at minimum, and a provider who cannot say why they need your child's school name probably does not need it.

Our own position is that the minimum set of facts needed to answer a tutoring enquiry honestly is the subject, the level, the target and one piece of marked work. The school name is useful context for coursework deadlines and option blocks, and it is not required. A photograph is never required. A grade history is useful and should be shared only once a family has decided to proceed.

There is a related question about who sees a child's marked work. A script shared for diagnosis is a document about a minor's academic performance, and it should be used for that diagnosis and not retained beyond it without a reason. Asking a provider what happens to the script after the assessment is a reasonable question and the answer is revealing.

sections.heading: The teacher-of-your-own-child problem
paragraphs: A recurring suggestion in Dubai parent networks is to engage your child's own subject teacher privately, on the reasoning that nobody knows the pupil or the course better. It is the arrangement to avoid, for rule-based reasons and for a practical one that families find more persuasive.

On the rules: the private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving pupils affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to pupils enrolled at their own school. Those rules are press-reported, so verify the current wording with the authority or the school rather than relying on a summary, including this one.

On the practice: the person who set your child's assessment is not the person best placed to show them how an external examiner reads an answer. Internal marking develops its own habits, generous in some places and severe in others, and a candidate coached by their own marker can become excellent at satisfying that marker specifically. The session that moves a Diploma grade is usually the one that introduces an unfamiliar, external reading of the same script.

There is also a conflict nobody discusses comfortably. A teacher who is paid by a family holds a position in relation to that family's child inside school as well as outside it, and both parties feel the awkwardness the first time an internal grade disappoints. The cleanest arrangement is a specialist who has no role in the pupil's school at all.

sections.heading: Why there is no Dubai address to visit, and what that changes
paragraphs: IB Gram has no premises, office or centre in the UAE, and no page on this site will suggest otherwise. Two competitor pages examined for this project show a UAE footer address on a page about a different emirate, and two route UAE parents to a non-UAE phone number as the conversion path. Both are trust failures, and an address a business does not occupy is a misrepresentation.

The operating consequence is that teaching for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and that in-home visiting is available only in India. A parent who wants a person in the room should hire locally, and should do so with the verification questions above in hand rather than on a recommendation alone.

What the model buys is the thing that is actually scarce in Dubai. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist, or a tutor who has supervised an Economics commentary portfolio, is rare within any single community and considerably less rare across a national pool. A family in Dubai South chooses from the same specialists as a family in Al Barsha, and neither pays for a drive.

What it costs is the things presence provides, and they are worth naming rather than dismissing. A tutor in the room reads a pupil's body language more fully than a camera does. For younger children, physical presence helps with attention. For a pupil with specific access requirements, in-person support may be the right answer, and a family in that position should hire locally and pay the premium without apology.
