sections.heading: Replacement, cancellation and the three things that actually go wrong
paragraphs: Over a two-year Diploma, three failures account for almost every unhappy tutoring arrangement in this market, and none of them is about teaching quality. Knowing them in advance is how a family writes an agreement that survives them.

The first is departure. Dubai's population moves, and a tutor leaving the country in March of DP2 is a genuine and common event. A family contracting directly with an individual has no remedy and starts the search in the worst month of the year. The protection is not a longer contract; it is knowing in advance who, if anyone, is responsible for finding a replacement.

The second is the quiet mismatch. The sessions happen, everyone is pleasant, and nothing moves. This is why a review instrument agreed in advance matters so much: without one, the arrangement continues on goodwill until the mock arrives. With one, the four-week review either shows a changed pattern of lost marks or it does not, and the conversation is about evidence rather than about anyone's feelings.

The third is the boundary failure, and it usually arrives at 10pm the night before a coursework deadline. A candidate under pressure asks for more than feedback, and a tutor who wants to be helpful supplies a paragraph. The consequence falls on the candidate and can extend to the loss of a Diploma. The protection is to have agreed the boundary in writing at the start, so that the answer in the moment is a reference to something already settled rather than a judgement made at 10pm.

process.title: Ask the permit question first
process.description: Of any individual tutor, from any source, including one a platform introduced: do you hold a current private tuition work permit, under which category, and when does it expire. It is free to obtain and takes two working days, so there is no legitimate reason for the answer to be complicated.

process.title: Ask one subject-specific question
process.description: Not what are your qualifications, which anyone can answer, but a question only someone who has taught the level can answer in a sentence. The subject entries above give one for each. A general answer about exam technique is itself the answer.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session with the proposed specialist, at no cost and with no card required. Use it to test the two things that matter: whether they can diagnose from a marked script, and whether they are clear about where their role stops on assessed work.

process.title: Get the quote itemised in writing
process.description: Session length, minimum block, whether coursework support is inside the figure, written records, cancellation terms, replacement obligation and the tax position. Six lines. A provider unwilling to put them in writing has told you how a dispute would go.

process.title: Agree the review instrument and the boundary
process.description: Which piece of school-marked work the four-week review will measure, and exactly what will and will not be provided on coursework. Both settled before the first session, so that neither is being decided under pressure later.

faqs.question: Is it legal for a Dubai family to hire a private IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor holds the right permit. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. The obligation sits on the tutor rather than the family, but a parent engaging an unpermitted tutor is building a two-year arrangement on an unlawful footing, which is a poor foundation whatever the teaching is like.

faqs.question: How long does a UAE private tuition work permit last and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: It is granted free of charge for two years. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. Because it costs nothing and takes two days, a tutor without one has either not looked into it or has decided not to, and both answers are informative. Ask for the expiry date rather than simply whether they hold one.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the private tutor permit in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The published eligibility list is wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school pupils aged 15 to 18. That breadth tells you the resolution was written to regularise an existing informal market rather than to restrict tutoring to professionals. It also means the permit says nothing about expertise. A permitted tutor may be a Diploma examiner or a first-year undergraduate, and establishing which is a separate question entirely.

faqs.question: Can the same permit be used for online lessons as for in-person ones?
faqs.answer: The permit regularises private tuition as an activity rather than a venue, so the sensible assumption is that it covers the work however it is delivered, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation is the authority to confirm that with directly. What a parent can rely on is simpler: ask the individual whether their current permit covers the arrangement you are proposing, and take the answer in writing. Any provider telling you the question does not apply to online teaching is guessing on your behalf about something they could check.

faqs.question: Can a tutoring centre be opened on a private tutor permit in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained after initial approval, with a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. The personal permit covers an individual providing private tuition. The two are routinely conflated in marketing, and a platform describing itself as holding a KHDA permit when it has no premises is describing something it cannot hold.

faqs.question: Are there fines for using a tutor without a permit, and how much?
faqs.answer: The published position is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published. Press reporting on the regime stated explicitly that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and a figure circulating online could not be verified. For that reason no amount appears on this page, and any provider quoting you a specific number is repeating something unchecked. The absence of a published figure is not an absence of consequence.

faqs.question: Can a 15-year-old be paid to tutor in the UAE?
faqs.answer: School pupils aged 15 to 18 are explicitly listed among those eligible to apply for the private tuition work permit, which surprises most parents reading the rules for the first time. Whether that is a suitable arrangement for your child is a separate judgement from whether it is lawful. For primary numeracy or middle-years content practice, a capable older pupil can be genuinely effective and inexpensive. For a Higher Level Diploma subject, buying a tutor one or two years ahead of the candidate purchases reassurance rather than marks.

faqs.question: How can I check whether an IB tutor is permitted to teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask the individual directly: do you hold a current private tuition work permit, under which eligibility category, and what is the expiry date. A tutor operating properly answers in one line. A platform cannot hold the permit on an individual's behalf, so a reply along the lines of all our tutors are fully licensed is not an answer to the question you asked. Ask the same question regardless of how the introduction was made, including through a recommendation from another parent in your community.

faqs.question: Why should I avoid hiring my child's own subject teacher privately?
faqs.answer: Two reasons. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving pupils affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school. Those rules are press-reported, so verify the current wording with the authority or the school. The practical reason is stronger: the person who set the assessment is not the person best placed to show a candidate how an unfamiliar external examiner reads the same answer.

faqs.question: Who employs the tutor, and who is accountable if the arrangement fails?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the model, and this is the question families most often skip. Contracting directly with an independent tutor means there is no third party, which keeps the rate lower and leaves verification, record-keeping and replacement with you. Contracting through a platform means a named contact is responsible for changing a match that is not working. A tuition centre is accountable for the service but will usually offer a different class rather than a different teacher. Establish which arrangement you are in before the first payment.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai tutoring agreement actually say?
faqs.answer: Six things, in writing, before the first session. Whether the rate is per sixty minutes or per session. Whether a minimum block applies. Whether coursework support is inside the figure or billed separately. What the cancellation terms are, including for a prepared session. Who is responsible for finding a replacement if the tutor becomes unavailable. And exactly what will and will not be provided on assessed work. Everything that later becomes a dispute in this market is one of those six left unstated.

faqs.question: What happens if the first private tutor turns out to be the wrong match?
faqs.answer: With a platform arrangement, a named contact changes the match and the four-week review exists precisely to surface the problem early rather than at the mock. Contracting directly, the family starts the search again, which in February or March of the Diploma second year is a genuinely difficult position. Either way the protection is the same: agree in advance which piece of school-marked work the review will measure, so that a mismatch shows up as evidence rather than as a slowly growing suspicion that nobody wants to raise.

faqs.question: What personal information should a tutoring enquiry form ask about a child?
faqs.answer: As little as answers the question. Subject, level, target grade and one piece of marked work is enough to give an honest response. UAE data protection sits under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, and the standard a parent should expect is a clear statement of what is collected, why, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted, with a privacy link on the same page as the form. A tutoring enquiry does not need a photograph of your child, and it is reasonable to ask what happens to a marked script after the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor cost more than a tuition centre in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Per hour, one-to-one is more expensive than a group class in a centre, and that is the clearest genuine saving available in this market. Published one-to-one rates run from AED 45 at the budget online end to AED 650 for a named premium provider, with qualified subject teachers at AED 150 to AED 300 and specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 or above. A centre group class undercuts all of those. What it cannot offer is a diagnosis of one candidate's specific fault, which is what a Diploma family is usually paying for.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram not have a Dubai office or centre to visit?
faqs.answer: Because it has none, and saying otherwise would be a misrepresentation. Two competitor pages examined for this project display a UAE address on a page about a different emirate, and two route UAE parents to a non-UAE phone number. IB Gram operates no premises in the UAE, holds no KHDA institute permit, and delivers teaching one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In-home visiting is a service offered only in India. A family who wants someone physically present should hire locally, using the verification questions on this page.

dubai/ib-private-tutor.closingHeading: Two questions, one email, before anything is paid
dubai/ib-private-tutor.closingBody: If you are hiring an IB private tutor in Dubai, two questions do most of the work and cost nothing to ask: whether the individual holds a current private tuition work permit with its expiry date, and one subject-specific question only someone who has taught that level can answer in a sentence. Ask them of anyone, from any source, including us. The trial lesson that follows here is a full diagnostic session over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no card required and nothing to cancel, and it is the right place to test whether the proposed specialist can read a marked script and is clear about where their role stops.

dubai/ib-psychology-ia-help.tutorsIntro: The tutors below supervise Psychology internal assessments specifically. Each has read reports against the four criteria, can say whether a published study can realistically be replicated with classmates in a Dubai school, and works from the student's own data and draft.

intro.heading: The study chosen in week one decides most of the mark
paragraphs: The Diploma Psychology internal assessment is a replication of a published experimental study. The student selects a study, modifies one element of it, runs it with participants they can actually recruit, analyses the results with an appropriate inferential test and writes a report of around 2,200 words. It is marked across four criteria by the school teacher, externally moderated by the IB, and carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade depending on level.

The word replication is doing a great deal of work in that paragraph and students consistently underestimate it. This is not an invitation to design an original experiment about something interesting. It is a requirement to take an existing published study with a known method and a known result, change one aspect of it deliberately, and see what happens. A student who proposes an original investigation into social media and anxiety has misread the task, and the introduction criterion will mark them against a theoretical background they cannot build.

The second thing students underestimate is feasibility. A great many famous psychological studies cannot be replicated in a school: they involve deception that would not be ethical with classmates, stress that cannot be induced on minors, equipment no school has, or participant numbers no sixteen-year-old can recruit. The time to discover that is the week the study is chosen, not the week before data collection. Almost every Psychology internal assessment that goes badly in Dubai went badly here.

Third is the inferential test. The analysis criterion asks not only for the correct test but for a justification of why it is correct, with reference to the design and the level of measurement, and a statement about significance. Students run a comparison of means because they have seen one, report a value, and say the result was significant. The marks are in the justification, and it is three sentences of work that almost nobody writes.

Our role is narrow. We check that a proposed study can be replicated in a school setting, help the student think through what single element they will modify, teach the test selection and its justification, read the student's own draft against each criterion and state where it sits, and name the next job. The student recruits, runs the study, analyses the data and writes the report. Nothing is supplied, because the report carries an academic honesty declaration the student signs.

Sessions run online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared screen. A Psychology internal assessment session is a results table, a test output and a draft on one screen, annotated live, with the file staying with the student. It also means a Dubai family can book somebody who has supervised these reports rather than whichever humanities tutor can reach their community in the evening.

dubai/ib-psychology-ia-help.programmesIntro: Psychology is a Diploma subject, but the research habits the internal assessment rewards are built earlier, and Dubai students reach it from several different routes.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Psychology at standard or higher level, with the same experimental study required at both. Higher level adds syllabus content and an extra paper rather than a different internal assessment, so the weighting of the report differs between levels while the task itself does not.
programmes.countryNote: Psychology is a fast-growing Diploma choice in Dubai and in several schools it is taught by one specialist for the whole cohort. That concentration means individual supervision of replications is thin, and students frequently choose a study without anyone experienced checking whether it can be run with classmates.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: There is no MYP Psychology, but Individuals and Societies and the Sciences both assess investigation design and the evaluation of method, which are the transferable parts. Students who have run MYP science investigations understand variables and controls before they meet an experimental hypothesis.
programmes.countryNote: Continuum students in Dubai arrive used to operationalising a variable, which is half the introduction criterion. Students joining from an IGCSE route with no science investigation background often need a session purely on the difference between a concept and a measurable variable before anything else is useful.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A CP student taking Diploma Psychology submits the same experimental study against the same criteria. The core differs, with a reflective project instead of TOK and the Extended Essay, and the reflective project's ethical focus sometimes pairs usefully with psychological content.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is a minority route in Dubai. Where Psychology is included, families should budget and plan as for a Diploma subject, since the internal assessment requirement and its ethical approval process are unchanged by the programme.

dubai/ib-psychology-ia-help.subjectsIntro: Replications come from the research areas of the syllabus, and they differ enormously in how practical they are with classmates in a school. These are the areas Dubai students use most, with the practical reality of each.

subjects.name: Memory: serial position and recall
subjects.description: The most reliably replicable area in a school. Word-list recall studies need only paper, a timer and volunteers, give numerical data suited to a straightforward comparison, and the original studies are well documented. The risk is choosing a replication so standard that the modification is trivial.

subjects.name: Schema and reconstructive memory
subjects.description: Replications involving leading questions or altered descriptions work well and raise genuine ethical questions about mild deception, which the exploration criterion rewards addressing properly rather than avoiding.

subjects.name: Cognitive load and dual-task performance
subjects.description: Practical with simple tasks and a stopwatch, and the within-participants design is statistically powerful with small numbers. Needs care that the tasks are standardised identically for every participant.

subjects.name: Priming and framing effects
subjects.description: Short, clean and easy to administer, with large published literatures to draw a theoretical background from. Effect sizes are often small, which makes sample size and a properly justified test more important than usual.

subjects.name: Social conformity and group influence
subjects.description: Conceptually attractive and often infeasible, because the original studies rely on confederates and deception that a school setting cannot support. Scaled-down versions exist but need careful ethical handling and the modification must be stated honestly.

subjects.name: Stereotype and attribution studies
subjects.description: Replicable with vignettes and rating scales, and well suited to a multilingual Dubai cohort where the student can modify the cultural content of the material. Sensitive topics must be avoided or handled with the teacher's explicit approval.

subjects.name: Anchoring and decision making
subjects.description: Among the easiest replications to administer and among the easiest to run badly, because the anchor must be delivered identically to every participant. Standardised written instructions are what rescue it.

subjects.name: Perception and visual illusions
subjects.description: Equipment-light and reliable, with clear numerical measurement. The modification is usually a change in stimulus properties, which is easy to describe precisely and therefore easy to justify in the introduction.

subjects.name: Sleep, time of day and performance
subjects.description: Appealing and logistically difficult, because testing at genuinely different times requires access to participants across a day. Workable where a student can recruit within a school timetable, and a good source of honest limitations.

subjects.name: Language, bilingualism and processing
subjects.description: A genuine local strength. In a city where most students speak two or more languages, replications involving language processing have a natural modification available and a participant pool that makes the variable meaningful.

dubai/ib-psychology-ia-help.regionsIntro: Psychology internal assessment support is booked from across Dubai, and the limiting factors are the size of the Psychology department and the student's ability to recruit participants. These are the areas we hear from.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: The densest IB cluster in the emirate, with established Psychology provision. Students here usually understand the replication requirement and need help with test selection and the justification.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Large continuum schools where one specialist may supervise the whole Psychology cohort. Study feasibility is the recurring problem, because nobody has time to screen thirty proposed replications.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Established IB provision beside British schools. Transition students arrive with no experience of operationalising a variable, which is the first thing their introduction criterion needs.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Continuum schools with growing Psychology uptake. Students here often propose social influence replications that cannot be run ethically with classmates, and need steering to memory or cognition.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Newer Diploma cohorts with few previous reports on file. Online samples fill the gap and many of them predate the current criteria, which produces well-written reports marked against the wrong structure.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Mixed British and IB provision along the coast. Recruitment is easier for students in larger year groups here, which makes within-participants designs less necessary but still advisable.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Apartment communities where out-of-school recruitment is harder. Students here benefit from designs that can be administered entirely within a single school lesson.

sections.heading: What a replication means, and why it is not an original study
paragraphs: The task requires the student to replicate a published experimental study with one modification. That constraint is what makes the whole assessment work: because the original study exists, the student has a theoretical background to build an introduction from, a method to follow, a result to compare against, and a literature to evaluate within. An original study has none of those, which is why an original design scores badly however interesting it is.

The modification is where the student's own thinking appears. It should be one element, chosen for a reason, and the reason should connect to the theory. Changing the stimulus language in a memory study because the participant pool is bilingual is a modification with a rationale. Changing the number of words from fifteen to twenty for no stated reason is a modification with none, and the introduction criterion asks why the modification was made.

Students often want to modify several things at once, usually because the original method is inconvenient in some way. Resist that. Every additional change weakens the comparison with the original result, which is the backbone of the discussion. If the original method genuinely cannot be followed in a school, the answer is usually a different study rather than a heavily altered one.

It follows that the quality of the original study matters. A clearly reported experiment with a numerical outcome, a stated procedure and an accessible published account gives the student everything the criteria need. A famous study known mainly through textbook summaries, with a method nobody can reconstruct precisely, leaves them guessing, and guessing shows in the introduction.
bullets: Replicate a published study; do not design an original one
Modify exactly one element, and explain why
Multiple changes break the comparison with the original result
Choose a study whose method is reported in enough detail
The original study supplies the theory the introduction needs

sections.heading: The four criteria and the twenty-two marks
paragraphs: The report is marked on introduction, exploration, analysis and evaluation. The distribution rewards thinking at both ends: the introduction has to build a theoretical case for the hypothesis, and the evaluation has to assess the student's own study rather than the original one. The two criteria in between reward method and statistics, and are the most mechanical marks available.

The introduction is marked on whether the theory and the original study are used to justify the aim and the hypotheses. Describing the original study is not the same as using it: the marks are in the chain of reasoning that runs from the theory, through the original finding, to the specific prediction this study makes. Students write the first and third parts of that chain and leave out the middle.

Exploration covers the design, the sampling, the variables as operationalised and the ethical considerations, and it is marked on appropriateness and on explanation. Listing ethical considerations earns little; explaining how consent was obtained, what participants were told, how they were debriefed and how anonymity was preserved earns the band. The same applies to sampling: naming an opportunity sample is a start, acknowledging what it does to generalisability is the mark.

Treat the structure below as a planning frame and confirm the current criteria and mark allocations in the Psychology subject guide your child's teacher is working from. The IB publishes the authoritative version and revises guides on a cycle; where this page and the guide disagree, the guide governs.

The original study described but not connected to the prediction

sections.heading: Can this study actually be run in a Dubai school?
paragraphs: This is the question that should be asked in the first week and usually is not. School replications face four hard constraints: what the school's ethics position permits, who the student can recruit, what equipment exists, and how much administration time a lesson allows. A study that fails any of those is not a study, however compelling the original finding.

Ethics is the first filter. Studies that depend on meaningful deception, on inducing stress or discomfort, on confederates misleading participants, or on sensitive personal topics are generally not viable with classmates who are minors. Scaled-down versions sometimes exist and should be discussed with the teacher before any planning. The rule of thumb is that if the student would be uncomfortable explaining the procedure to the participant's parent, it needs rethinking.

Recruitment is the second. A sixteen-year-old can usually recruit between fifteen and thirty volunteers from their year group with permission, and only during times the timetable allows. Designs requiring sixty participants, or participants from several age bands, or testing at multiple times of day, run into the limits of a school day rather than of the student's ambition. Within-participants designs, where each person experiences both conditions, get far more power from the same number of volunteers and should be the default where the study permits.

The table maps common choices against these constraints. Confirm everything with the Psychology teacher before committing, because school policy on consent, recruitment during lessons and topics considered sensitive differs across Dubai schools and the school's position is the one that applies.

Access to participants at different hours

sections.heading: Ethics as something done, not something listed
paragraphs: The exploration criterion marks ethical considerations on whether they were addressed, and the difference between a mark at the bottom of the band and one at the top is almost entirely whether the report describes actions or lists principles. A sentence noting that informed consent was obtained is a principle. A description of the consent form, what participants were told about the study's purpose, what they were not told and why, and how they were informed of their right to withdraw at any point, is an action.

Five things need to be in place before data collection and documented afterwards. Informed consent, in writing, with parental consent where participants are minors, which in a school replication they usually are. A clear statement of the right to withdraw at any point without giving a reason. A debriefing, especially where the procedure involved any mild deception, in which participants are told the true purpose and given the chance to withdraw their data. Anonymity, so no participant is identifiable in the report or the appendices. And protection from harm, which in a school context mainly means avoiding distress, embarrassment and sensitive topics.

Data protection deserves its own paragraph because students overlook it. A replication collects personal data about identifiable young people, usually classmates. Collect only what the study needs, replace names with participant numbers at the point of recording, keep nothing identifiable in the appendices, and delete the raw records once the report is marked. Stating in the method what was collected, why and how it was protected is both good practice and consistent with the UAE's personal data protection framework.

Consent forms, debriefing scripts and standardised instructions belong in the appendices, where they sit outside the word count. That matters practically: a student can be thorough about ethics without spending any of their 2,200 words on it, provided the body of the report refers the reader to the appendix properly.
bullets: Written informed consent, with parental consent for minors
An explicit right to withdraw, stated before participation
A debriefing, essential where any deception was involved
Participant numbers rather than names, everywhere
No sensitive topics without the teacher's explicit approval
Forms and scripts go in the appendices, outside the word count

sections.heading: The inferential test and the justification nobody writes
paragraphs: The analysis criterion asks for appropriate descriptive statistics, an appropriate inferential test, and the justification of both. Students reliably produce the first and the second and omit the third, which is where a third of the criterion's marks sit. The justification is three sentences: what the design was, what level of measurement the dependent variable used, and therefore which test applies.

Choosing correctly is not difficult. Two independent groups with a measured quantity call for an independent comparison of means. The same participants in both conditions call for a paired or repeated-measures version, which is more powerful and should be preferred where the design allows. Ranked or ordinal data call for the rank-based equivalents. Frequencies in categories call for chi-squared. More than two conditions need a test designed for that rather than several two-group tests.

The significance statement needs precision. State the level used, conventionally 0.05, say whether the hypothesis was one-tailed or two-tailed and why, report the obtained value against the critical value or the probability, and then say what that means for the hypothesis. The sentence that loses marks is the one saying the result was significant, with no level, no direction and no reference to the hypothesis as stated in the introduction.

Then interpret psychologically. A statistically significant difference is a statement about probability, not an explanation. The discussion has to say what the result means in relation to the theory the introduction set out and to the original study's finding, including when the replication did not reproduce it. A failed replication, honestly analysed, scores better than a successful one described loosely.

table.caption: CHOOSING AND JUSTIFYING THE INFERENTIAL TEST
rows: Separate participants, continuous measure, two conditions
Each participant is their own control, so pairing applies
Measure is ranked, so means are not appropriate
Data are counts in categories, not measured quantities
Avoids repeated two-group tests inflating error

sections.heading: Where Dubai Psychology reports lose marks
paragraphs: Evaluating the wrong study comes first and it is remarkably common. The criterion asks the student to evaluate their own design, sample and procedure. A great many reports instead evaluate the original study, criticising a famous experiment's ecological validity at length while saying nothing about the opportunity sample of twenty classmates tested in a noisy classroom at lunchtime. The second is what the marks are for.

Second is an introduction that describes rather than argues. The chain has to run from theory, through the original study's finding, to this study's specific prediction. Reports frequently present a summary of the theory, a summary of the original study, and then a hypothesis that appears without being derived from either. The missing sentences are the ones explaining why this theory, applied to this modification, predicts this result.

Third is the unjustified test, covered above, and fourth is the procedure that was not standardised. If different participants received different instructions, different timing or different conditions, the study has introduced variation the design did not intend, and that is both a real limitation and a procedural weakness. Writing standardised instructions word for word in advance, and putting them in the appendix, prevents it.

Fifth, and specific to this market, is topic choice driven by online sample reports. Young Psychology cohorts in newer Dubai schools have few internal exemplars, so students find reports online, many written against earlier criteria, and reproduce a structure that no longer matches what is marked. Reading the current criteria directly, once, prevents an entire category of avoidable loss.
bullets: Evaluating the original study instead of the student's own
A hypothesis that is stated rather than derived
A test run without a justification of the choice
Instructions and conditions that varied between participants
A structure copied from a sample written against older criteria

sections.heading: The appendices: thoroughness that costs no words
paragraphs: The report body runs to around 2,200 words and the appendices do not count towards it. That is a structural gift and most students use it badly, attaching raw data and nothing else. A complete appendix set supports several criteria at no cost to the word count, provided the body refers to each appendix at the right point.

What belongs there: the raw data with participants identified only by number, the standardised instructions exactly as read to participants, the consent form, the debriefing script, the materials used such as word lists or vignettes, the descriptive statistics calculations, and the inferential test working or output. Each of those is evidence that something the criteria ask about was actually done, and each takes the pressure off the prose.

The practical discipline is to refer rather than reproduce. In the body, state what was done in one sentence and point to the appendix for the detail. That keeps the 2,200 words for the reasoning the criteria actually reward, which is the derivation of the hypothesis, the justification of the test and the evaluation of the student's own study.

Students assemble appendices in the final evening and that is when things go missing. Build them as the study proceeds: the consent form exists before recruitment, the instructions before administration, the raw data as it is collected. By the time the report is written the appendix set is already complete, which also means the method can be written accurately rather than reconstructed from memory.
bullets: Appendices sit outside the 2,200-word guideline
Include raw data by participant number, never by name
Include the exact standardised instructions and materials
Include consent form, debriefing script and statistical working
Refer to each appendix from the body rather than reproducing it
Build the appendix set as the study runs, not at the end

sections.heading: What Psychology internal assessment support costs in Dubai, and why it is online
paragraphs: Published Dubai market rates, read in October 2026, run from AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik at the budget online end, through Unitors at AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate's AED 200-450 and above for specialist IB and IGCSE support, reaching AED 650 at BartyED for premium examiner-branded provision. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors up to AED 500 once travel is included. These are market figures, not an IB Gram price list.

Psychology replications sit at the specialist end because the decisive skill is a judgement call: whether a particular published study can be replicated with minors in a school, and what single modification makes it both feasible and defensible. That is not syllabus knowledge. Four to six sessions covers a complete report, which at market rates is a project cost in the high hundreds to low thousands of dirhams rather than a monthly commitment.

The question to ask a prospective tutor is whether they will look at two proposed studies and say which one can actually be run. A tutor who answers only in terms of which topic is more interesting has not understood where this assessment goes wrong. The second question is whether they will state a band position on a draft for each of the four criteria.

IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For this task the online format is better on its own terms. The session is a results table, a test output and a draft on a shared screen, annotated live, with the file staying with the student. It also means the person advising on feasibility is chosen for having supervised replications rather than for living near Mirdif or Al Barsha.

whyPoints.title: We ask whether the study can be run before anything else
whyPoints.description: Most Psychology internal assessments that go wrong were decided in the week the study was chosen, on grounds of ethics or recruitment rather than psychology. The feasibility session is the cheapest and most useful hour in the whole project.

whyPoints.title: The test justification is treated as marks, not as paperwork
whyPoints.description: A third of the analysis criterion sits in explaining why the chosen test fits the design and the level of measurement. It is three sentences of work and almost nobody writes them, which makes it the most reliable gain available.

whyPoints.title: Ethics planned as actions, not principles
whyPoints.description: Consent forms, debriefing scripts, participant numbering and the right to withdraw are built before recruitment and documented in the appendices. Listing ethical principles after the fact sits at the bottom of the band.

whyPoints.description: Appendices sit outside the word count, so thoroughness there costs nothing. Building them as the study runs produces an accurate method and frees the 2,200 words for the reasoning that actually earns marks.

whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read, and is presented as the market rather than as our price. A parent should be able to check a page rather than trust it.

whyPoints.description: A replication that does not reproduce the original finding is not a failure and scores better than a loose account of a successful one. We will say so rather than letting a student quietly reshape their analysis towards the expected result.

faqs.question: Does the Psychology IA have to replicate a published study?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the requirement is central rather than incidental. The student replicates a published experimental study with one modification, which is what gives them a theoretical background for the introduction, a method to follow, a result to compare against and a literature to evaluate within. An original design has none of those and scores poorly however interesting it is. Choose a study whose method is reported in enough detail to reconstruct precisely, rather than one known mainly through textbook summaries.

faqs.question: How many things can my child change from the original study?
faqs.answer: One, chosen deliberately and explained. The modification is where the student's own thinking appears, so it should connect to the theory: changing stimulus language because the participant pool is bilingual has a rationale, changing a word list from fifteen to twenty items usually does not. Multiple changes weaken the comparison with the original result, which is the backbone of the discussion. If the original method genuinely cannot be followed in a school, the better answer is a different study.

faqs.question: Is a repeated-measures design better for a Dubai school study?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because recruitment is the binding constraint. Commonly between fifteen and thirty participants are needed, depending on the design. A repeated-measures design, where each participant experiences both conditions, gets substantially more statistical power from the same number of volunteers and should be preferred wherever the study permits. Independent-groups designs need more participants to detect the same effect. The practical ceiling is what a sixteen-year-old can actually recruit from their year group with permission, during times the school timetable allows.

faqs.question: Which published studies cannot be replicated in a school?
faqs.answer: Those depending on meaningful deception, on inducing stress or discomfort, on trained confederates misleading participants, or on sensitive personal topics. Classic conformity and obedience paradigms generally fall into this group. Scaled-down variants sometimes exist and must be discussed with the teacher before planning. A useful rule of thumb is whether the student would be comfortable explaining the full procedure to a participant's parent; if not, the design needs rethinking rather than defending.

faqs.question: What ethical steps must be documented in the report?
faqs.answer: Written informed consent, with parental consent where participants are minors; an explicit right to withdraw at any point without giving a reason; a debriefing, which is essential where any mild deception was involved; anonymity, with participants identified only by number; and protection from harm, meaning distress, embarrassment and sensitive topics are avoided. The criterion rewards describing what was done rather than listing principles, and the forms and scripts belong in the appendices where they do not consume the word count.

faqs.question: Which inferential test should my child's study use?
faqs.answer: It follows from the design and the level of measurement. Two independent groups with a continuous measure call for an independent comparison of means; the same participants in both conditions call for the repeated-measures version; ranked data call for the rank-based equivalents; frequencies in categories call for chi-squared; three or more conditions need a test built for that. The marks are as much in writing the justification, naming the design and the measurement level, as in running the test correctly.

faqs.question: How should significance be reported in a Psychology IA?
faqs.answer: Precisely. State the significance level used, conventionally 0.05, say whether the hypothesis was one-tailed or two-tailed and why, report the obtained value against the critical value or the probability, and then state what that means for the hypothesis as it was worded in the introduction. The sentence that loses marks is one saying only that the result was significant, with no level, no direction and no link back to the stated hypothesis. Then interpret the result psychologically, not just statistically.

faqs.question: What if the replication does not reproduce the original finding?
faqs.answer: That is a perfectly good outcome and often produces a better report. A failed replication gives the discussion real work to do: what differed between this study and the original, whether the modification explains it, what the sample or procedure contributed, and what that implies for the theory. The criteria reward honest analysis of what happened, not a successful result. What does lose marks is quietly reshaping the analysis or the hypothesis to make the outcome look expected.

faqs.question: What goes in the appendices and does it count towards the words?
faqs.answer: Appendices sit outside the word guideline, which makes them the most underused resource in this assessment. Include the raw data by participant number, the standardised instructions exactly as read, the consent form, the debriefing script, the materials such as word lists or vignettes, and the statistical calculations or output. Refer to each from the body in one sentence rather than reproducing the detail. Build them as the study runs, because assembling them at the end is when documents go missing.

faqs.question: Why did a well-written Psychology report score in the middle?
faqs.answer: Most often because the evaluation assessed the original study rather than the student's own. The criterion asks about this design, this sample and this procedure: the opportunity sample of twenty classmates, the noisy room, the instructions that varied slightly between sessions. The second common reason is an introduction that summarises theory and the original study without deriving the hypothesis from either. Both are structural faults rather than writing faults, and both are fixable in one revision.

faqs.question: How much of the Psychology grade comes from the internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Roughly a fifth to a quarter depending on level, with the proportion higher at standard level because higher level candidates sit an additional paper. The report is marked by the school teacher across four criteria and a sample of each school's marking is externally moderated by the IB, so the mark needs to be defensible against the band descriptors. Confirm the current weighting and criteria in the subject guide your child's teacher is working from.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai Psychology student choose their study?
faqs.answer: Early in the course and at least five to six months before the school's internal deadline, because recruitment, ethical approval and data collection all take calendar time that cannot be compressed. The feasibility question in particular should be settled in the first fortnight of planning. Students who discover in February that their chosen study cannot be run ethically with classmates have lost months, and that is the single most common way this assessment goes wrong.

faqs.question: Is an opportunity sample from one year group acceptable?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the school's agreement and proper consent, and it is the normal participant pool for this assessment. The requirements are informed consent in writing, parental consent because participants are typically minors, an explicit right to withdraw, a debriefing and anonymity throughout. The limitation it creates, an opportunity sample from one age group in one school, is real and should be discussed honestly in the evaluation rather than glossed over, because acknowledging it is what the criterion rewards.

faqs.question: What does Psychology IA support cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 run from about AED 33-65 an hour at budget online platforms up to AED 650 for premium examiner-branded providers, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate putting specialist IB support at AED 200-450 and above. Replication work sits at the specialist end because judging whether a study can be run in a school is not syllabus knowledge. Four to six sessions is the usual block, so budget it as a project rather than monthly.

dubai/ib-psychology-ia-help.closingHeading: Ask first whether the study can be run
dubai/ib-psychology-ia-help.closingBody: If your child has two or three published studies in mind, the most valuable hour available is the one that says which of them can actually be replicated with classmates in a Dubai school, and what single element to modify. If the data is already collected, send the results table and the draft and the first session will report where each of the four criteria sits. The trial is free, uses your child's own work rather than a sample, and ends with a verdict rather than encouragement.

dubai/ib-psychology-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work on IB Psychology at Standard and Higher Level, including the experimental Internal Assessment and the Higher Level research methodology paper. Every match is made from a piece of the student's marked work, because a returned script shows which band the examiner could actually reach and a conversation does not.

intro.heading: What evidence that Psychology tutoring is working actually looks like
paragraphs: Psychology is a subject where a student can feel more confident every week and score exactly the same in August. The content is interesting, the discussion is enjoyable, and none of that is assessed. What is assessed is whether a short-answer response does what the command term asked, whether an extended response evaluates rather than describes, and whether an Internal Assessment report meets five criteria with specific mark allocations. Those are all visible on paper, which means progress in this subject can be proved rather than asserted.

So this page is built around a record. The first marked script a Dubai family sends becomes the baseline: which command terms were misread, how many studies were used accurately, whether the ethical consideration was named or gestured at. Each subsequent script is marked the same way, and the comparison is the evidence. A parent who cannot see that comparison after six weeks of paid sessions has no way to tell whether the money is working.

The same logic applies to the Internal Assessment, which is where the most arguable marks in the subject sit. An IA draft can be annotated criterion by criterion, with the letter and the available marks written against each section. A second draft can be annotated the same way. That is a readable record of movement on a component worth a quarter of the Standard Level grade, and it is the single most informative document a Psychology family can hold.

Dubai supplies a useful calendar for this. Schools here run mock examinations in a window from roughly late November to February, which gives every candidate at least one fully marked set of scripts before the real session. A tutoring plan anchored to that window has a natural before and after. Families who start in October have a baseline, a mid-point and a mock to measure against; families who start in March have a deadline and no measurement.

Delivery is stated plainly once. Psychology support for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school day. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Marked scripts and IA drafts are annotated on a shared screen, which keeps the record in one place rather than in a pile of paper.

A note on what this page deliberately does not contain. There are no claims about how many of our students improved by how much, because a figure like that is worthless without the number of students it covers, the date it was measured and the method used to measure it, and nobody in this market publishes those. Several ranking competitors do publish satisfaction percentages and self-asserted star ratings; one shows two different review totals on the same page. A record about your own child, with dates and scripts attached, tells you more than any of it.

dubai/ib-psychology-tutor.programmesIntro: Psychology exists as a formal course only in the Diploma Programme, but the research-literacy habits it assesses begin in the Middle Years Programme, and Dubai families often ask about the subject a year before the choice is made.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Psychology sits in Group 3 at Standard or Higher Level. Every candidate studies the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches to behaviour, one option from abnormal, developmental, health or human relationships, and research methodology. Assessment is Paper 1 on the approaches, Paper 2 on the option, and an Internal Assessment reporting a simple experimental replication. Higher Level adds extension content and a third paper on research methodology.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Psychology cohorts are generally healthy, because the subject recruits well from students who did not enjoy Economics or Business. That produces a particular problem: a cohort containing many students who chose Psychology to avoid something else, who then discover that the subject demands precise study recall and tight evaluation. Diagnosing that early from a marked script saves a disappointing DP2.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Individuals and Societies and the MYP sciences both contribute. The criterion-referenced rubric trains students to address stated requirements rather than write generally, and MYP science investigations introduce variables, controls and ethical consideration. A student who has taken MYP investigation seriously finds the Psychology Internal Assessment familiar in shape if not in detail.
programmes.countryNote: The transition most Dubai students feel is the move from a rubric they can read while writing to a timed paper with a command term they must decode. MYP5 students write good analytical prose with time to think, then produce a short-answer response under time pressure that answers a question nobody asked. A short block on command terms in DP1 is the cheapest fix available.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Psychology pairs naturally with career-related studies in health, social care and sport, and CP students sit the same papers and submit the same Internal Assessment as Diploma Programme candidates. The reduced overall load usually leaves more time for the experimental report, which is an advantage in a component where careful write-up beats clever design.
programmes.countryNote: CP cohorts in Dubai remain small, and a CP Psychology student is frequently the only one taking the course in their year group. For an evidence-led approach that is actually convenient: with no classmates to compare against, a tutor's dated record of marked scripts becomes the only benchmark available, and it does the job well.

programmes.name: Year 11 into DP1
programmes.description: The decision point for Psychology in Dubai schools, and worth treating as its own phase. Students choose the subject on the basis of a taster lesson or a friend's recommendation, with little sense of what the assessment demands. A single session spent on a real past short-answer question and a real Internal Assessment extract answers the question better than any prospectus.
programmes.countryNote: Where Dubai differs from most markets is school mobility: a student may choose Psychology at one school and start it at another, with a different option topic selected by the new school. Because the option carries Paper 2 entirely, that is not a detail. Confirm the option with the teacher before buying any tutoring at all.

dubai/ib-psychology-tutor.subjectsIntro: Psychology is requested alongside a predictable set of courses, and the overlaps are worth naming because they affect how a tutoring plan should be sequenced across a term.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Three approaches, one option, research methodology, and an experimental Internal Assessment. Marks go missing on command terms, on studies recalled vaguely, and on evaluation that lists strengths and weaknesses without weighing them against the question asked.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Directly supports the biological approach: hormones, neurotransmission, genetics and brain localisation all appear in both courses. Students taking both can usually describe a mechanism accurately, which is where Psychology-only candidates tend to be vague.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics content supports the Internal Assessment and the Higher Level research methodology paper. Descriptive statistics, measures of central tendency and dispersion, and the logic of inferential testing all appear in the experimental report.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Carries the writing control extended responses need. A Psychology extended response is a structured argument under time pressure, and students whose paragraphing drifts produce answers that contain the right material in an order an examiner cannot credit.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Shares Group 3 and an evaluation requirement. Behavioural content in Economics sits close to the cognitive approach, and students taking both tend to write more disciplined conclusions because both courses penalise unweighed assertion.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Overlaps on motivation, leadership and organisational behaviour. Students taking both often find the human resource management content in Business easier, and can use real organisational examples to anchor abstract Psychology models.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Supports the sociocultural approach with material on identity, conflict and culture. Students taking both write more confident cultural dimension answers, which is a recurring weak point for candidates relying on a single textbook chapter.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Pairs well where the Psychology option is health psychology. Shared content on stress, physiology and behaviour change means two courses reinforcing one another, and the practical investigation discipline transfers to the Psychology Internal Assessment.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Unusually relevant here. Psychology's methodological debates are TOK questions in disguise, and students who engage with TOK write stronger evaluations of research because they can discuss the limits of a method rather than list them.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Carried alongside Psychology by many Dubai students, and relevant where an Internal Assessment replication involves participants who are more comfortable in Arabic. Materials and briefings have to be handled carefully and documented honestly.

sections.heading: Reading a marked Psychology script: the baseline a tutor should start from
paragraphs: A returned Psychology script carries more information than most families extract from it. The mark is the least useful part. What matters is the pattern: which question types lost proportionally most, whether the loss was in knowledge or in response structure, and whether the same error appears in more than one answer. Five minutes with a marked script and the published criteria produces a diagnosis that a term of general revision would not reach.

The first thing to check is the command term in each question against what the student actually wrote. In Psychology the short-answer questions use a tight set of terms, and each one has a defined demand. A response to outline that explains at length wastes time and collects no extra credit. A response to evaluate that describes two studies has not met the demand at all. This mismatch is the commonest single reason a knowledgeable student scores modestly.

The second check is study detail. Candidates are expected to use research to support claims, and the difference between a credited use and an uncredited one is specificity: who was studied, what was manipulated, what was found, and why that supports the point being made. Students who write the researcher's name and a one-line conclusion are offering a label rather than evidence, and examiners cannot reward a label.

The third check is whether evaluation weighs anything. Listing a strength and a limitation is a description of a study's properties. Evaluation requires saying what that limitation does to the conclusion in the context of the question asked. The gap between those two is usually a band, and it is the gap most visible on a marked script once a parent knows to look for it.

sections.heading: Where the Psychology grade is actually decided, component by component
paragraphs: Psychology is unusual in how much of the grade sits in a single paper. At Standard Level, Paper 1 on the three approaches to behaviour carries 50% of the total, Paper 2 on the chosen option carries 25%, and the Internal Assessment carries 25%. At Higher Level, Paper 1 carries 40%, Paper 2 20%, the research methodology paper 20% and the Internal Assessment 20%. Families should confirm current weightings with the school's coordinator, since subject guides are periodically revised.

The practical consequence is that a Standard Level student who neglects Paper 1 is neglecting half the grade. Paper 1 contains both short-answer questions on the approaches and an extended response, and the extended response is where the largest single block of marks in the subject sits. A student who writes competent short answers and a disorganised extended response has capped their grade regardless of content knowledge.

Paper 2 depends entirely on which option the school chose, which is why confirming it matters before any tutoring is bought. Abnormal, developmental, health and human relationships are substantially different bodies of content, and preparing the wrong one is a total loss rather than a partial one. This is a real risk for students who move school mid-programme in a mobile city.

The Internal Assessment is the component most amenable to planned improvement, because it is written over weeks rather than produced in two hours. It is also the component where the most arguable marks sit, since criterion judgements have discretion built into them. A draft annotated criterion by criterion, revised, and annotated again is the clearest evidence of progress available anywhere in this course.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment: a replication, its criteria, and what a tutor may do
paragraphs: The Psychology Internal Assessment asks the student to replicate a simple published experimental study, report it formally, and evaluate it. It is marked against criteria covering the introduction, the exploration of method, the analysis of results and the evaluation, with a specific number of marks attached to each. Families should get the exact criteria and mark allocations from the school's teacher, because quoting them from an aggregator risks quoting a previous version.

Most lost marks are structural. The introduction has to justify the replication against the original study and state a hypothesis that the chosen design can actually test. Students frequently write an interesting introduction about the topic in general, which earns little, and then run a design that tests something adjacent to the hypothesis they stated. Those two errors compound: the analysis answers a question the introduction did not ask, and the evaluation has nothing coherent to evaluate.

The second cluster of lost marks is in the analysis. Descriptive statistics have to be appropriate and correctly presented, the inferential choice has to be justified rather than asserted, and the results have to be stated in relation to the hypothesis. Students routinely produce a graph that does not show what they claim it shows, which a reader notices immediately and the student does not.

The boundary is the same across every IB internal component and worth stating plainly, because parts of this market cross it. A tutor may explain each criterion and its marks, question whether the design replicates the original study, ask what justifies a statistical choice, check that ethical considerations are specific, read a draft the student wrote and annotate it by criterion. A tutor may not write any section, rewrite prose, produce the analysis or supply text. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate.

sections.heading: How many studies a Psychology candidate actually needs
paragraphs: Students collect studies the way some people collect receipts: in quantity, without organisation, and without being able to find the right one when needed. The useful number is smaller than most candidates believe and the required depth is greater. A small set of studies known in full detail outperforms a long list known as names.

Full detail means four things that can be written from memory: who the participants were and in what context, what was manipulated or measured, what was found with some indication of magnitude or direction, and what the study's design limits about the conclusion. A student who can produce those four elements for a study can use it as evidence in a short answer, in an extended response and in an evaluation. A student with the researcher's name and a slogan can use it nowhere.

The organising principle that works is a grid rather than a list: approaches down one axis, the demands of likely questions across the other, with each study placed where it can actually be used. Built properly, that grid shows immediately where a student is over-supplied and where they have nothing, and it makes revision a filling-in exercise rather than a rereading one.

This is also where evidence of progress is easy to generate. Ask a student to write a study in full detail from memory, cold, at the start of a term and again six weeks later. The two pieces of paper are the record. It costs five minutes of a session and produces something a parent can read without knowing any Psychology at all.

sections.heading: Higher Level Paper 3 and research methodology as examinable content
paragraphs: Higher Level candidates sit an additional paper on research methodology, built around an unseen stimulus describing a piece of research. It asks candidates to identify and discuss methodological features, consider ethical issues, and evaluate what can legitimately be concluded. It is widely under-prepared because methodology is taught as a tool for the Internal Assessment rather than as examinable content in its own right.

The content is specific and learnable. Sampling methods and their consequences, research designs and their trade-offs, the distinction between credibility and generalisability in qualitative work, reflexivity, triangulation, and the ethical considerations that apply at each stage of a study. None of it is conceptually hard. All of it requires precise vocabulary used correctly under time pressure, which is a drilling job.

The characteristic failure on this paper is answering about the content of the stimulus rather than about its methodology. A student reads an interesting study about memory and writes about memory. The paper is not asking about memory. Recognising that distinction reliably takes practice on several stimuli, which is exactly the sort of work that shows up as band movement across dated attempts.

For an evidence-led plan, Paper 3 is convenient: the questions are short, the attempts are quick to produce, and marking is relatively unambiguous. A student can generate one attempt a week with little effort, which means six weeks of work leaves six dated scripts behind. Higher Level families who want to see whether tutoring is working should start here.

sections.heading: A progress record a Dubai parent can actually read
paragraphs: The common complaint about tutoring is not cost, it is opacity. Sessions happen, reports say the student is engaging well, and nobody knows whether anything has changed. In Psychology that is avoidable, because every component produces paper. The table below is the shape of record we think any provider should be able to hand over, and which a Dubai family should ask for from whoever they hire.

Note what it does not contain. No percentage improvement claims, no satisfaction scores, no statistics about other students. Those numbers circulate widely in this market and almost none of them come with the sample size, date and method that would make them meaningful. A record about one student, with dates and scripts attached, is worth more than any aggregate claim about a cohort nobody can inspect.

The record also makes the stopping decision possible. If six weeks of marked scripts show the same command-term error repeating, the plan is wrong and should change, or the tutor should. If the scripts show movement on the two errors targeted and the student is now losing marks somewhere new, the block has done its job and a new, shorter block addresses the next thing. Open-ended tutoring without a record has no natural end.

One practical note for Dubai families specifically. Keep the mock scripts. Schools return them, students lose them, and they are the most valuable diagnostic document in the two years. A marked mock paper with examiner-style annotations, read properly, is worth more than several hours of tutoring bought without it.

sections.heading: KHDA inspection bands and what a school report does and does not tell you
paragraphs: Dubai parents have an unusual amount of public information about their children's schools, and it is often misread when tutoring decisions are made. KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and it inspects private schools on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak.

What an inspection band describes is the school's provision across many measures: teaching, leadership, inclusion, student outcomes across phases and subjects. What it does not describe is the quality of Diploma Programme Psychology teaching in a particular year, which depends on one or two individuals. A school in a high band can have a weak year in a minority subject after a staffing change, and a school in a lower band can have an excellent Psychology department. Parents should read the subject-level detail in the report rather than the headline.

The context around those reports is worth knowing. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK schools at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. Seven new private schools join for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 places; KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year.

Two cautions follow. KHDA regulates schools and does not license individual private tutors, which is MoHRE's responsibility, so no tutoring service should present a regulator's name as a credential. And an inspection band is not a reason to buy tutoring or to avoid it. The reason to buy tutoring is a marked script showing a specific, fixable loss, which is where this page started.

sections.heading: Online Psychology tuition against the in-home market in Dubai
paragraphs: For a subject built on annotated paper, the delivery comparison has a clear answer, and it is worth setting out with the market numbers attached rather than asserting it. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is part of our India service only. The table reports what the Dubai market charges and then states our position.

The specific advantage for Psychology is document handling. A marked script annotated on a shared screen stays in one place, accumulates, and can be compared with the one from six weeks ago in two clicks. The same work done on paper in a living room produces a pile that is somewhere in the house by March. For an approach that depends on a readable record, that difference is not trivial.

The in-home premium is real and quantifiable. Bestimate puts Dubai home visits at AED 180 to 350 and market home tutors at AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and advertised monthly packages run AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits against AED 799 for eight online sessions. The difference is travel, and in an emirate where a cross-city drive at 6pm takes an hour, it is a substantial sum for road time.

The honest case for presence remains for younger students and for households where connectivity is poor. For a Diploma Programme Psychology candidate working on command terms and criterion-level Internal Assessment feedback, the decisive factor is whether the tutor marks this subject against these criteria, and video delivery means that question can be answered on merit rather than on geography.
