process.title: Tell us the unit, not just the year group
process.description: The enquiry form asks for the current central idea and lines of inquiry, the school and the year group. Those three things decide which tutor is the right match far more reliably than a general statement that science is hard. If you do not have the unit letter to hand, the school's parent portal almost always does.

process.title: A free 45-minute trial lesson, one per family
process.description: The trial is a real diagnostic session, not a sales call. The tutor sets a short task from the current unit, watches how your child reasons through it, and ends by telling you plainly what they found. No card details are taken to book it and there is one trial per family.

process.title: You get the diagnosis in writing before you decide
process.description: After the trial you receive a short written note: what your child can do, the specific misconception or skill gap found, how many sessions the tutor thinks it needs and what they would work on first. If the answer is that tutoring is not the right purchase right now, the note says that instead.

process.title: Pick the shape, then lock the slot
process.description: Weekly 45 minutes, a unit-linked block, Exhibition-year support or a summer intensive. The slot is fixed in Gulf Standard Time and stays with the same tutor, because a primary child who has to rebuild rapport every fortnight makes slower progress than one who does not.

process.title: A short note after every session
process.description: Each session ends with two or three lines to you: what was taught, what the child could do unaided by the end, and what is still wrong. It is deliberately short enough to read on a phone and specific enough to raise at a parent-teacher meeting.

process.title: Review at six sessions, and say stop if it is time
process.description: At six sessions we review against the original diagnosis. Sometimes the answer is to continue, sometimes to switch to a different specialism such as Arabic or reading, and sometimes to stop because the gap has closed. A provider who never recommends stopping is not reviewing anything.

whyPoints.title: Primary teaching is treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: A tutor who can carry a Diploma chemistry class is not automatically the right person for a seven-year-old. Matching for a PYP science enquiry starts from primary experience and the ability to teach through questions rather than explanation, then looks at subject depth second.

whyPoints.title: The AED figures on this page are somebody else's
whyPoints.description: Every rate quoted here is attributed to the provider that published it, with the month we read it. We do not publish an invented price list for primary science, and we quote only after a trial lesson has established what is actually needed.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is written down in advance
whyPoints.description: In the Exhibition year the work must be the student's own. A tutor teaches research skill, stress-tests the question and rehearses the presentation. A tutor does not choose the topic, write the text, make the slides or produce any part of the submission, and that boundary is agreed before the first session.

whyPoints.title: You are told when tutoring is the wrong purchase
whyPoints.description: Some primary science enquiries are reading enquiries, some are language enquiries and some are pace enquiries that a conversation with the class teacher would solve. The trial lesson exists partly to find that out, and the written diagnosis says so when it is the case.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated plainly, not implied
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one on live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. No page on this site implies a tutor will arrive at a Dubai address, because none will.

whyPoints.title: The session is built around your school's unit
whyPoints.description: Tutors read the central idea and lines of inquiry before session one and work inside them. Where the school's sequence and the child's gap disagree, you are told which one the sessions are following and why, rather than discovering it from your child in week four.

faqs.question: What does an hour of IB PYP science support cost in Dubai at the moment?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai in October 2026 put a generalist homework helper at AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, a qualified teacher working online at AED 150 to AED 300, a tutor who travels to your community at AED 180 to AED 500 with travel inside the price, and a named or examiner-tier tutor as high as AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, attributed in the rate table on this page. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, because the honest number depends on the year group, the number of weeks and whether the Exhibition year is involved.

faqs.question: Is a science specialist worth paying more for when my child is only nine?
faqs.answer: Usually not in the way parents expect. At primary level the scarce skill is not science depth but diagnosis: finding the one wrong sentence in a child's head and replacing it with evidence the child collected themselves. A primary-trained teacher with solid general science nearly always outperforms a subject graduate with no primary experience for a nine-year-old. Pay more for primary pedagogy, for planning against your school's unit, and for Exhibition-year judgement. Paying at the top of the Dubai market buys examination seniority, which is the wrong expertise for this age group however good it is.

faqs.question: My son's school teaches science inside units of inquiry, so what does a tutor follow?
faqs.answer: The school's current central idea and lines of inquiry, which are usually on the parent portal or in the termly unit letter. A good provider asks for those before the first session rather than asking only for a year group. Science in the PYP is distributed across six transdisciplinary themes, with 'How the world works' carrying the heaviest science content, so a generic primary science scheme will pull against what the class is doing. Hand over the unit letter and the first hour becomes teaching rather than guesswork about what your child is meant to be learning.

faqs.question: Which of the PYP science strands causes the most trouble in Dubai classrooms?
faqs.answer: Earth and space, specifically the seasons, is the most persistent. Children reason that summer is hotter because the Earth is closer to the sun, and a Gulf climate makes that inference feel obviously right. Materials and matter runs a close second, because dissolving and melting collapse into one idea and stirred sugar is believed to have gone. Forces produces the belief that heavy objects fall faster. All three are fixable in a session or two with household apparatus, provided the child collects the evidence rather than being told the correct answer.

faqs.question: Can practical science actually happen in a live video lesson?
faqs.answer: For primary science, yes, because the strands use household objects anyway. A kitchen scale, measuring jugs, ice, salt, a torch, magnets, string and a phone camera cover most of what a PYP unit needs. The method matters more than the kit: the child sets the test up on their own table with the camera on it, takes the readings and says them aloud, while the tutor asks what is being changed and what is being held constant. Flames, chemicals, microscopes and sealed electrical supplies are out, and none of the four PYP strands requires them.

faqs.question: Do we need to buy equipment before the first science session?
faqs.answer: No. An apparatus list goes out the day before each session and is drawn from what a Dubai household already owns: glasses of the same size, a kitchen scale, a measuring jug, ice, cooking oil, bicarbonate of soda, vinegar, a torch, tape and paper. If a session needs something genuinely unusual, it is swapped for something that is not. Nothing is bought, and nothing is hunted for during paid time. Where a step needs an adult nearby for two minutes, the plan says so in advance so somebody can be available.

faqs.question: How many sessions before a PYP report says something different?
faqs.answer: Report cycles are slow, so the report is a poor early signal. A specific misconception usually shifts in one to three sessions and is testable immediately: ask your child to predict what will happen in a situation they have not seen. A skill such as fair testing or writing a conclusion takes six to ten sessions to become automatic, because it has to survive a week without practice. If you want a faster read than the report, ask the class teacher at the next meeting whether the written explanations have changed.

faqs.question: Is group science tutoring cheaper than one-to-one for a Grade 4 child?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour and often more expensive per outcome. Groups of two to four work well for vocabulary, revision games and the social side of talking about science, and they are poor at diagnosis, because the whole value of a primary science session is finding the one belief this particular child holds. In a group the confident child handles the apparatus and the quiet one watches, which is the exact passivity a one-to-one video session makes impossible. For a stuck Grade 4 learner, fewer one-to-one sessions usually beat more group hours.

faqs.question: Does somebody teaching primary science privately in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

faqs.question: How is science in the PYP different from science in a British primary school?
faqs.answer: Mostly in how it is organised and reported. A British primary school timetables science, teaches a defined national curriculum sequence and reports against age-related expectations. A PYP school distributes the same kind of content through transdisciplinary units, builds it around key concepts such as causation and change, and reports narratively against learning outcomes and approaches to learning. Children from both systems end up knowing similar science. The difference families notice on transfer is written method and subject-specific vocabulary, which the British route expects earlier and more formally.

faqs.question: Should we spend on science now or wait until the MYP starts?
faqs.answer: If the gap is skills rather than content, now is far cheaper. Writing a method before the practical, putting units in table headings, choosing axes and evaluating reliability are all mechanical skills that cost one strand of an ordinary primary session to build. The same work in the first term of MYP Sciences becomes remedial, is charged at secondary rates and competes with new content while the child adjusts to separate teachers. If the gap is pure content, waiting is defensible, because primary content gaps close quickly once the child is motivated.

faqs.question: What should I ask before agreeing an AED rate for primary science?
faqs.answer: Four questions sort the market quickly. Which year groups have you taught, and under which curriculum? Will you read our school's central idea and lines of inquiry before the first session? Is a 45-minute price three-quarters of your hourly rate, or close to the full hour? And in the Exhibition year, what will you refuse to do? Answers that arrive in a sentence tell you the provider has priced the work. Answers about confidence, passion and bespoke programmes tell you the hour has not been thought about.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school fee freeze change what we should budget for tutoring?
faqs.answer: It changes the context rather than the tutoring price. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a household that had planned for a fee rise, that is unallocated budget rather than a reason to spend it. The sensible use of it at primary level is a short diagnostic block rather than an open-ended weekly commitment, because primary gaps are usually specific and close faster than a yearly plan assumes.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect when a science session can start?
faqs.answer: They lengthen the fixed part of the school day rather than the school day itself. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and a recommendation that no mandatory lesson runs under 25 minutes. Schools absorb that by compressing transdisciplinary time, so children often arrive home with less consolidation than the unit plan implies. In practice it argues for a shorter, later session rather than an early long one.

faqs.question: What does the free trial science lesson actually cover, and is a card needed?
faqs.answer: It is 45 minutes, one per family, and no card details are taken to book it. The tutor sets a short task from your child's current unit, watches how they reason, probes one likely misconception and finishes by telling you what they found. You then get that in writing: what your child can do unaided, the specific gap, and how many sessions it is likely to need. If the honest answer is that tutoring is not what this child needs right now, the note says so and nothing follows.

dubai/ib-pyp-science-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the diagnosis, then decide what the hour is worth
dubai/ib-pyp-science-tutor.closingBody: Primary science money is wasted in a specific and avoidable way: a pleasant hour that finishes the worksheet and leaves the wrong idea in place. The way to avoid it is to find out what your child actually believes before agreeing a rate. intro.heading: What an IB PYP tutor in Dubai costs, and what actually changes the price
paragraphs: Market rates for an IB PYP tutor in Dubai run roughly AED 120 to AED 280 for a sixty-minute one-to-one session, as read across published Dubai rate cards in October 2026. The floor is a university student or a generalist primary tutor; the ceiling is a trained primary teacher who has run units of inquiry inside a KHDA-inspected school and can read a PYP report card without translation. Above AED 300 you are usually paying a Diploma subject specialist, and for a Grade 2 reader or a Grade 4 fractions gap that premium buys very little. This is the single most useful number a Dubai parent can have before the first phone call, and almost nobody publishes it.

The reason the figure is so hard to find is that primary tutoring sits in the shadow of the Diploma. Agencies price around Chemistry HL and Maths Analysis and Approaches, then quote the same hourly figure for a seven-year-old learning place value. Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for Dubai publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, a currency no Dubai family actually transacts in. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one work at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. None of those bands was built for a primary learner.

Four things move the number in Dubai specifically, and none of them is the tutor's confidence. The first is the Arabic stream: a child placed in Arabic as a first language carries a different KHDA-mandated workload from a child in Arabic as an additional language, and the second needs a different tutor entirely. The second is year group, because the gap between Grade 1 phonics and the Grade 5 Exhibition is a change of job, not a change of difficulty. The third is session length, since forty-five minutes is the realistic ceiling for a six-year-old and most rate cards are built around sixty. The fourth is the calendar: demand spikes in the eight weeks before the long winter break and again in the run-up to MYP placement, and rates follow demand.

The honest version of our own position: IB Gram does not publish a price list on this page. What we publish is the market, with the source attached to each band, and then a free 30-minute trial lesson so the rate you are quoted is attached to a tutor you have already watched teach your child. A quoted figure before a trial is a figure about nothing. We also decline work we cannot staff properly — if no primary-trained tutor is free for a Grade 3 Arabic-as-an-additional-language slot, we say so rather than putting a Diploma teacher in the chair and charging the Diploma rate for it.

Delivery is worth stating plainly before anything else on this page. Tutoring for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time and booked around the school run. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is not a compromise for a primary learner — it is what lets an Emirates Hills family work with a tutor who has actually taught the PYP Exhibition, instead of whichever generalist is willing to drive to Emirates Hills at 4pm on a Tuesday.

dubai/ib-pyp-tutor.programmesIntro: Dubai families usually arrive on a PYP page because of a report card, not a results sheet. These four bands cover the phase your child is in now and the two ahead of it, because the price and the point of primary tutoring both depend on how far away the next transition is.

programmes.name: PYP Early Years
programmes.description: The early years of the Primary Years Programme are play-based and inquiry-led, with no graded assessment and no reporting against a subject syllabus. Support at this stage is narrow and specific: letter-sound correspondence, blending, counting with one-to-one correspondence, subitising to ten, and the fine-motor control that written output depends on. Sessions run twenty-five to thirty minutes with a parent in the room. Anything longer is a waste of your money, because attention rather than ability is the binding constraint.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this band is complicated by language. Many FS2 children are hearing English at school, Arabic in mandatory lessons and a third language at home, and a wobble in one of the three reads as a general delay. A tutor who has taught early years in a Dubai classroom will separate an English-as-an-additional-language lag from an actual phonics gap before recommending anything.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP organises learning through six transdisciplinary themes — who we are, where we are in place and time, how we express ourselves, how the world works, how we organise ourselves, and sharing the planet — and runs maths and language alongside them as explicit strands. The final year ends with the PYP Exhibition, a long collaborative inquiry presented to the school community. Tutoring here is about number fluency, reading comprehension, structured written output and research skills, in that order of frequency.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools vary widely in how much number practice they set outside the units of inquiry, which is why two children in the same grade at two Al Barsha schools can arrive with very different arithmetic. A Dubai tutor works from your child's own unit planner and report descriptors rather than a generic Year 4 scheme, because the school's wording is what you will be reading in April.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP introduces eight subject groups, criterion-referenced marking out of eight per criterion, and the first real experience of being assessed against published descriptors rather than a teacher's judgement. For a child leaving the PYP, the shock is rarely the content. It is the volume of independent written work and the expectation that they can plan, draft and revise without being asked to. A Year 6 to Year 7 bridge block is the most commonly requested piece of work on this page.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai IB continuum schools move children to a different campus or a different building at Year 7, so the academic step and a social step land in the same September. Families who plan the bridge in the spring term of Year 6 — while the PYP Exhibition is still fresh and the research habits are live — get a much easier term than families who wait for the first MYP report.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma sits six years away from a Grade 5 learner, and it is still worth understanding now, because the two decisions that constrain it are made early: whether a child keeps a second language running, and whether their number work is strong enough to leave Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches open at sixteen. Nothing about the Diploma needs rehearsing in primary. The habits it rewards — reading closely, writing to a brief, finishing a long piece of work — are exactly what the PYP Exhibition builds.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. For a current PYP family that means the Diploma landscape your child enters will not be the one you researched at FS2, and the second-language choice you make in Grade 4 is the one that stays expensive to reverse.

dubai/ib-pyp-tutor.subjectsIntro: Primary tutoring requests cluster tightly. Across Dubai enquiries the same ten strands account for almost everything, and eight of the ten are language or number rather than the units of inquiry themselves. Each entry below is what the strand actually assesses and where primary marks and confidence are lost.

subjects.name: Mathematics: number and place value
subjects.description: Place value, partitioning, mental strategies and the four operations. The commonest Dubai referral: a child who can follow a written algorithm but cannot estimate whether the answer is sensible. Fixing it means going back to quantity, not to more worksheets, and it is quick work when caught before Grade 4.

subjects.name: Mathematics: fractions, decimals and percentages
subjects.description: The single biggest primary cliff. Fractions as part-whole, as measure and as division are three different ideas taught under one word, and most Grade 4 confusion traces to the switch between them. Children who leave the PYP shaky here meet it again as ratio in MYP Year 7 and lose ground twice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: measurement, shape and space
subjects.description: Perimeter against area, units and conversion, angle, and reading scales that do not start at zero. Low-stakes in a PYP report and heavily weighted in MYP entry assessments, which is why it is so often the hidden gap behind a confident-looking Year 6 maths profile.

subjects.name: Mathematics: data handling and probability
subjects.description: Tally, pictogram, bar and line graph, mean and mode, and the beginnings of chance. The strand the units of inquiry use most and teach least explicitly. Dubai Exhibition projects almost always need a graph, and a child who cannot choose between a bar and a line chart will produce a weak one.

subjects.name: English: reading comprehension
subjects.description: Decoding, fluency, inference and retrieval. A Dubai primary report that says a child reads well often means they decode well. Inference is the strand that separates a comfortable Grade 5 reader from a struggling one, and it is tested directly by every MYP language and literature task that follows.

subjects.name: English: writing and structured output
subjects.description: Sentence control, paragraphing, planning to a purpose and editing one's own draft. Most primary tutoring hours in Dubai go here. The skill the MYP expects at Year 7 is drafting and revising without prompting, and that is a habit built over months rather than a technique taught in a session.

subjects.name: English as an additional language
subjects.description: Academic vocabulary, the language of instruction, and the gap between conversational fluency and classroom fluency. Common in Dubai, routinely mistaken for a learning difficulty, and the first thing a primary-trained tutor rules in or out before recommending a maths or literacy programme.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Script formation, phonics, high-frequency vocabulary and the weekly assessment pattern Dubai schools run. A mandatory subject in every Dubai private school regardless of curriculum, and the one most families never think to support until a report comes back weak in Grade 3.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: Standard Arabic reading, grammar and extended writing for Arab learners, taught in a class that KHDA requires to be kept separate from the additional-language group. Expectations are materially higher than in the additional-language stream, and a tutor matched to the wrong stream will do nothing useful.

subjects.name: Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools, taught in Standard Arabic for Arab learners and in the school's curriculum language for non-Arabs. Support is about terminology, memorisation structure and reading the set material accurately, never about supplying content outside what the Ministry of Education has approved.

subjects.name: Units of inquiry and research skills
subjects.description: Question framing, source selection, note-taking, and turning notes into something presentable. These are the skills the PYP Exhibition is actually assessing, and they are the only part of primary tutoring that transfers directly to the Extended Essay six years later.

subjects.name: Science in the PYP
subjects.description: Observation, fair testing, recording and explanation. Primary science tutoring in Dubai is rarely about content knowledge and almost always about writing up: a child who understands evaporation perfectly and cannot write three sentences about it will be reported as weak at science.

dubai/ib-pyp-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities, and what the school run does to a 4pm session
dubai/ib-pyp-tutor.regionsIntro: Primary scheduling is more constrained than Diploma scheduling, because a nine-year-old has a bedtime and a Diploma student does not. These are the Dubai communities we book most often for PYP families, with the operational detail that actually decides what time a session can start.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Villa communities feeding two IB continuum schools within a short drive. Buses return between 15:20 and 16:00, so a 16:30 start works for Grades 3-5 and a 17:00 start is better below that. Friday mornings are the most-requested primary slot here.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: The densest cluster of IB continuum provision in the emirate, which means siblings in the same family are often in two different programmes at once. Back-to-back staggered sessions from 16:00 are common; traffic on Umm Suqeim Street makes anything before 16:00 unreliable.

regions.name: Mirdif and Uptown
regions.note: An IB continuum catchment with long bus runs. Children frequently arrive home after 16:15, so primary sessions here work best at 17:00 and the forty-five-minute format matters more than elsewhere. Weekend morning slots are heavily booked in the Exhibition term.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: A mix of IB continuum and British primary schools, so PYP and Year 2 national-curriculum requests arrive from the same street. Short school runs mean 16:00 starts are genuinely possible, which is unusual in Dubai.

regions.name: Dubai Hills and Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Primary-heavy communities with a strong British intake and a smaller PYP population, often with a planned move into an IB continuum school at Year 7. Bridge and transition work is the dominant request rather than catch-up.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Newer villa developments with children spread across schools in three directions. Pickup times vary by twenty minutes week to week, so families here usually fix a 17:15 slot and keep it rather than chasing the earliest available.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf, Dubai Festival City and Al Garhoud
regions.note: Shorter commutes and a bilingual-school presence, which raises the proportion of Arabic-as-a-first-language requests well above the Dubai average. Early-evening Arabic slots fill before anything else on the timetable.

regions.name: Al Furjan, Dubai South and The Sustainable City
regions.note: Long commutes against the morning flow and a young primary population. Weekend sessions outnumber weekday ones here more than in any other Dubai cluster, and holiday blocks in the December and spring breaks are the practical way to make up ground.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JLT and Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Apartment living, so a quiet room for a video lesson is the real constraint rather than travel. Families often run sessions at the dining table with a parent nearby, which suits primary work better than it suits Diploma work.

schoolClusters.city: IB continuum schools, central and new Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Schools running the PYP, MYP and Diploma on one campus, so a Grade 5 learner's next three years are usually already decided. Families here mostly want Exhibition support and a Year 6 to Year 7 bridge rather than remedial work, and they ask for a tutor who can read their own school's unit planner.

schoolClusters.city: IB continuum and bilingual schools, Jumeirah to Al Jaddaf
schoolClusters.note: A cluster where Arabic sits closer to the centre of the timetable, including bilingual provision. Requests skew towards Arabic as a first language, Standard Arabic reading and Islamic Education terminology, alongside the usual primary maths and writing work.

schoolClusters.city: British primary schools with an IB destination
schoolClusters.note: Children in a national-curriculum primary whose families plan a move into an IB continuum school, usually at Year 7. The work here is translation: mapping where a Year 6 British learner sits against what an MYP Year 7 class will expect in its first assessed task.

sections.heading: What an IB PYP tutor in Dubai charges, band by band
paragraphs: An IB PYP tutor in Dubai costs roughly AED 120 to AED 280 for a sixty-minute one-to-one session at market rates read in October 2026, and AED 90 to AED 210 if the session is the forty-five minutes that actually suits a primary learner. Those are the market bands, not an IB Gram price list. The table below separates them by provider model, names the source for each figure and states the date it was read, because a rate with no source behind it is a number somebody chose.

Two patterns are worth noticing before you read it. The first is that the gap between the cheapest and the dearest primary tutoring in Dubai is a factor of five, which is wider than the gap for Diploma work. That is because primary tutoring has no external exam to anchor it, so sellers price on confidence rather than on outcome. The second is that the dearest band is almost never the right band for a primary child: a named Diploma specialist at AED 650 an hour has spent years learning things a Grade 3 learner does not need, and will often teach place value less well than a Grade 3 teacher does.

Monthly figures matter more than hourly ones for most Dubai families, because primary tutoring is a term-long habit rather than a six-week exam push. Published monthly packages in this market include online plans at around AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home plans at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for one hour a week run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work, which is a band a primary family should never need to enter.

What IB Gram does instead of a published rate card: a free 30-minute trial lesson with the tutor who would actually teach your child, then a written quote attached to that specific tutor, that year group and that session length. One trial per family, no card details taken. If the rate we quote sits above the band you expected, the reason will be in the quote — a first-language Arabic specialist and a generalist primary tutor are not interchangeable and are not priced as if they were.

sections.heading: Eight things that move a Dubai PYP rate, and what to ask about each
paragraphs: A quoted rate for primary tutoring in Dubai is the sum of eight decisions, and a parent who knows all eight can tell a fair quote from a lazy one in about two minutes. None of the eight is the tutor's personality, and only one of them is the subject. The table sets out each variable, the direction it moves the price and the question that exposes whether the quote was built or guessed.

The two that catch Dubai families most often are stream and session length. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab learners in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. A quote that does not ask which stream your child is in has not been built for your child. Session length is the other one: a rate card priced per hour and delivered to a seven-year-old who fades at thirty-five minutes is a rate card charging you for the fade.

Timing matters more in Dubai than in most markets because the academic calendar is crowded at both ends. Demand rises in the weeks before the long winter break and again in the spring term when MYP placement conversations begin, and anyone selling a fixed-term block in those windows is selling into a seller's market. Ramadan shifts the whole evening timetable, and a tutor who cannot move to a post-Iftar slot will quietly cost you four weeks of continuity. Ask about both before you agree a term.

The last variable is honesty about coverage. A primary-trained tutor who can teach Arabic as a first language to a Grade 4 learner is a narrow specialism, and in any given week there may be nobody free. The correct answer to that is to say so. What you should be alert to is a quote at the generalist rate for a specialist need, or a Diploma teacher offered at the Diploma rate for a job that does not require one.
bullets: Ask which Arabic stream the quote assumes before you compare two prices
Ask for the session length the rate is built around, not just the hourly figure
Ask whether the tutor has taught a primary classroom, not simply primary children
Ask what happens to the slot during Ramadan and the December break
Ask what the tutor will not do, and listen for a straight answer about coursework

sections.heading: Tutoring spend in context: what a Dubai primary term actually costs
paragraphs: Hourly rates tell you very little until they are turned into a term. A Dubai primary family deciding between one session a week and two is deciding between roughly AED 3,400 and AED 6,800 across a thirty-four-week academic year at the mid-band rate, and that is a different kind of decision from a per-hour one. The table converts the market bands above into the four spend patterns Dubai families actually choose, so the comparison is between plans rather than between prices.

One piece of Dubai context makes this easier to judge. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For most families this is the first year in a long time when the school bill is flat, and a tutoring decision made against a flat fee is a cleaner decision than one made against a rising one.

The pattern we see most often in primary is not the one families expect. A four-session diagnostic block followed by nothing is a common and perfectly good outcome: the report said a child was weak at maths, four sessions found the gap was fractions-as-division, the class teacher was told, and the problem went away. The expensive mistake is the open-ended weekly slot with no named target, running from October to June because nobody cancelled it. Every plan in the table has an end condition for that reason.

They assume AED 200 an hour for a sixty-minute session and AED 160 for forty-five minutes, a thirty-four-week Dubai academic year, and no holiday blocks. Your own quote will differ with stream, grade and specialism, which is exactly the point of the previous table.

sections.heading: The PYP has no exams, so what are you actually buying?
paragraphs: This is the question that separates a primary tutoring decision from every other one on this site. There is no Paper 1, no grade boundary and no results day in the Primary Years Programme. Assessment is internal, school-designed and reported against descriptors the school writes itself, which means a parent cannot buy a mark and should be suspicious of anyone implying otherwise. What you can buy is diagnosis, fluency and habit, and those three things are measurable if somebody bothers to measure them.

Diagnosis is the first and often the only thing a family needs. A Dubai primary report that reads approaching expectations in mathematics can mean six entirely different things: a number-sense gap, a fractions gap, a reading gap masquerading as a word-problem gap, an English-as-an-additional-language gap, a written-output gap, or nothing at all beyond a child who was eight months younger than the class average. The four-session diagnostic block exists because distinguishing those six costs far less than treating the wrong one for a year.

Fluency is the second. Number facts, phonics, handwriting speed and reading rate are the components of primary work that respond to short, frequent, boring practice and to almost nothing else. A tutor's value here is not inspiration; it is setting the right ten minutes of practice and checking it actually happened. This is also where parents overbuy, because fluency work is cheap to deliver and easy to extend indefinitely. A good tutor tells you when to stop.

Habit is the third, and it is the one that pays off at Year 7 rather than this term. The MYP expects a child to plan a piece of work, draft it, look at the criteria, and revise it without being asked. That is a habit built across the Grade 5 Exhibition and the months either side of it, and it is the single most durable thing primary tutoring can leave behind. Progress on all three is reported to you in writing every fourth session, with the specific thing that changed named — not a score, because a score in the PYP would be invented.
bullets: Diagnosis: naming which of six possible gaps a vague report is describing
Fluency: number facts, phonics, reading rate and handwriting speed
Habit: plan, draft, check against criteria, revise — the MYP entry skill
Evidence: a written note every fourth session naming what changed
No invented scores, percentages or rankings, because the PYP does not produce them

sections.heading: Where PYP learners in Dubai actually lose ground
paragraphs: Five failure modes cover most of what arrives on this page, and four of the five are invisible on a primary report card. Knowing which one you are looking at is worth more than any amount of general tutoring, because the remedies are different and three of them are short.

The first is fractions as three different ideas. Part-whole, measure and division are taught under one word in Grade 3 and Grade 4, and a child who has only built the part-whole meaning will handle a pizza diagram and fall apart on sharing problems. This recurs as ratio and proportion in MYP Year 7, so the same gap costs marks twice. It is usually six to eight sessions of work, not a year.

The second is comprehension hidden behind fluent decoding. A Dubai child who reads aloud confidently is often reported as a strong reader, and the inference questions are where the actual difficulty sits. Because the PYP reports reading as a single descriptor, this can run undetected from Grade 2 to Grade 5 and then surface as a sudden drop in the first MYP language assessment.

The third is written output lagging oral ability — extremely common in a city where many children speak better than they write in their school language. The fourth is the Arabic stream: a child placed in the first-language class whose home Arabic is colloquial rather than Standard will struggle against materially higher expectations, and KHDA requires those classes to be kept separate precisely because the two groups are not doing the same subject. The fifth is scheduling, which sounds trivial and is not. A Grade 2 child in a 19:30 slot after a bus from Mirdif is not being tutored; they are being kept awake. Half the failed primary tutoring arrangements we see in Dubai failed on the clock, not on the content.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against in-home primary tutoring in Dubai
paragraphs: This page targets a search that many Dubai parents type expecting someone to arrive at the villa, so the comparison deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. In-home primary tutoring in Dubai is a real market, priced by Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour and by independent listings at AED 200 to AED 500, with travel inside the figure. It works, families like it, and it carries two costs that are easy to miss.

The first cost is the tutor pool. A household in Dubai South or Nad Al Sheba choosing in-home tuition is choosing from the primary-trained tutors willing to drive to Dubai South or Nad Al Sheba at 16:30, which in practice is a short list with the specialists missing from it. First-language Arabic, early-years phonics and PYP Exhibition coaching are narrow specialisms, and geography removes most of them. The second cost is the clock: travel is priced into the hour whether or not it is itemised, and a cancelled session at the last minute is a wasted journey somebody pays for.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the screen shared both ways so a Grade 4 child's working is visible as they write it. For primary specifically that has one real advantage and one real limitation. The advantage is that the tutor is chosen for having taught the PYP rather than for living nearby. The limitation is that below Grade 2 a parent needs to be in the room for the first few weeks, and we say so before the trial rather than after it.

The table compares the formats on the things that actually decide between them for a primary family. It does not score them, because the right answer genuinely differs: a Grade 1 child in a quiet villa with an available parent and a Grade 5 Exhibition student in a Marina apartment are two different problems.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the PYP
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with an April 2026 date for schools whose year starts in April. No competitor page in this market has a section on this at all, which is remarkable, because for a Dubai PYP family these subjects are a third of the report card and the commonest source of an unexplained weak descriptor.

Three rules govern them and all three affect what tutoring is even possible. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab learners and for Arabic as a first language, with Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

The third rule is the one families should know before they buy any material. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That means honest tutoring in these subjects is about reading the set material accurately, building terminology, and structuring memorisation — not about supplying a parallel syllabus. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the relevant approval from KHDA to teach those subjects, which is a credential question worth asking of any tutor offering them.

Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit; schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. That is useful context for a parent deciding how much outside support is proportionate. If a child has the mandated weekly minutes at school and is still behind, the issue is usually stream placement or home language, and a diagnostic session will say which.

sections.heading: The PYP Exhibition, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Exhibition in the final PYP year is the first piece of work a child owns from end to end: they choose a line of inquiry, research it, build something, and present it to the school community. It is also the first point at which a family can accidentally buy academic dishonesty, usually with the best intentions, by hiring someone who treats it as a product to be delivered rather than a process to be learnt.

The boundary is simple and we state it the same way on every page. A tutor may teach research skills, ask hard questions, model how a paragraph is structured, read what a student has written and say where it is unclear, and rehearse a presentation with real questioning. A tutor may not supply the content, hand over finished text, or take a draft away and return it rewritten. The work, the words and the data stay the student's own. At primary this matters less for the Exhibition mark, which is not a public qualification, and enormously for what happens six years later: a child who learns in Grade 5 that a hard piece of writing can be outsourced carries that into the Diploma, where it is an expulsion risk.

Practically, Exhibition coaching looks dull from the outside. Most of a session is narrowing a question that is far too broad, because a nine-year-old who wants to research the ocean has to be walked to something a ten-week project can actually answer. After that it is source selection, keeping notes in the child's own words, and a presentation rehearsal where somebody asks the awkward question the audience will ask. One competitor in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is an academic-integrity breach and the reason we are explicit about the line rather than polite about it.

A reasonable Exhibition block is eight to twelve sessions across the spring term, overlapping with the Year 6 to Year 7 bridge described below. It is also the one piece of primary tutoring with a clean end condition: the Exhibition is presented, and the block ends. If a provider wants to keep the slot running afterwards without naming a new target, that is a commercial decision rather than an educational one.

sections.heading: From PYP to MYP: the Year 6 to Year 7 step in a Dubai school
paragraphs: The PYP-to-MYP step is where primary tutoring in Dubai either pays off or turns out to have been aimed at the wrong thing. The content gap is small. The gap in independence, volume and assessment literacy is large, and it arrives in a single September alongside new teachers, often a new building and sometimes a new campus.

Three changes do most of the damage. Marking moves from a teacher's descriptor to criterion-referenced levels out of eight, and a child who has never been shown a criterion grid reads a four as a failure rather than as a mid-band mark on one of four criteria. Written volume roughly doubles, and nothing in the PYP requires a child to produce eight hundred words to a brief in their own time. And subject teachers replace a single class teacher, so a struggling child must now tell five adults what they do not understand, which is a social skill as much as an academic one.

Dubai adds its own wrinkle. Several continuum schools move children at Year 7, and some families also move school at this point, so the first MYP report can be the first time a parent sees their child measured against a different cohort. Planning the bridge in the spring term of Year 6 — while the Exhibition research habits are still live — is substantially easier than reacting to a November report. The table maps the strands we are asked about most, where a Dubai PYP leaver usually sits, and roughly how long each gap takes to close.

Weeks in the final column are typical ranges from a primary-trained tutor working one session a week, not a promise about any individual child. A gap that has been in place since Grade 3 takes longer than one that opened in Grade 6, and a child closing two strands at once closes neither quickly. The honest planning assumption for a Dubai family is one strand per half-term.

sections.heading: KHDA, the regulator, and how to read a Dubai primary report
paragraphs: In Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and it inspects private schools annually on a six-band scale. Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. Those proportions explain why a PYP family in Dubai is a minority inside a very large market, and why primary PYP specialists are scarcer than their Diploma equivalents.

The regulator map matters if you move emirate, which Dubai families do. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education there; Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same; and the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits with the emirate.

What an inspection band tells a primary parent is narrower than most people assume. A school rated highly overall can still have a weak primary phase or a thin Arabic department, because the published band is an aggregate. The useful move is to read the body of your own school's report for the primary phase and for Arabic specifically, since those two sections are where a PYP family's actual experience lives. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit and makes no claim to any regulator's endorsement; what follows is a reading guide, not a credential.

One permit question belongs here because parents ask it constantly. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

process.title: Send the year group, the school and the report wording
process.description: Start with three things: your child's grade, the Dubai school they attend, and the exact wording of the descriptor that worried you. The wording matters more than a summary of it, because a primary-trained tutor can usually tell from the phrasing whether the school is describing number sense, written output or language.

process.title: A short written read of what we think the gap is
process.description: Within a day you get a written note naming which of the likely gaps the report is probably describing, what the trial lesson will test, and which tutor we would put in the chair. If the honest answer is that no tutoring is needed yet, that is what the note says.

process.title: One free 30-minute trial lesson
process.description: The trial runs with the tutor who would actually teach your child, over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Thirty minutes, one per family, no card details taken. You watch it. Afterwards you get a written summary of what the tutor found and a quote in AED attached to that tutor, grade and session length.

process.title: Fix the slot around the school run, not around the rate card
process.description: We set the time against your child's actual bus arrival and bedtime, in forty-five-minute blocks below Grade 4. Ramadan timings move to post-Iftar slots by arrangement, and the December and spring breaks can be used as blocks instead of weekly sessions if that suits the family better.

process.title: One named target per half-term
process.description: Each half-term has a single named target written down at the start — fraction-as-division, unprompted inference, Standard Arabic reading — so there is something specific to close rather than a slot to keep filling. Two targets at once is how primary tutoring becomes permanent.

process.title: A written note every fourth session, and an end condition
process.description: Every fourth session you get a short written note saying what changed, what did not, and whether the target is closed. When it closes we tell you, and we say whether to stop, reduce or move to the next strand. Ending well is part of the service rather than an awkward conversation.

whyPoints.title: Primary-trained tutors, not Diploma teachers scaling down
whyPoints.description: A Chemistry HL specialist is not better at place value than a Grade 3 teacher. For PYP work we match tutors who have run a primary classroom and can read a unit planner, and we price that specialism honestly rather than selling the Diploma rate for a primary job.

whyPoints.title: AED rates published with the source and the date attached
whyPoints.description: Every band on this page names where the figure came from and when it was read. Three of the six strongest-ranking tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars. A rate without a source is a number somebody chose.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly, before you ask
whyPoints.description: Lessons for Dubai families are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, and says so on the page rather than in a phone call after a booking. Home visits are a service we run only in India.

whyPoints.title: The line on assessed work, in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on what the student has written. Nobody supplies content for an Exhibition or hands back a rewritten draft. We state it in primary because the habit a child learns at ten is the one they carry into the Diploma at seventeen.

whyPoints.title: Arabic and Islamic Education treated as real subjects
whyPoints.description: The mandatory UAE subjects are a third of a Dubai primary report card and absent from almost every competing page. We match by stream, because KHDA requires Arab and non-Arab classes to be separate and the two groups are not studying the same thing.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed rather than hidden
whyPoints.description: First-language Arabic and early-years phonics are narrow pools in Dubai, and some weeks nobody suitable is free. We say so and offer a date rather than putting a generalist in a specialist slot. A platform that is never unavailable is not telling you something.

faqs.question: How much does an IB PYP tutor in Dubai cost per hour in 2026-27?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put primary PYP work at roughly AED 120 to AED 280 for sixty minutes one-to-one, or about AED 90 to AED 210 for the forty-five-minute session that suits most primary learners. Below that band you are usually buying homework supervision from a university student; above AED 300 you are usually paying a Diploma specialist whose premium buys a primary child very little. Those are market bands from published Dubai rate cards, not an IB Gram price list. Our own quote comes after a free 30-minute trial lesson and is attached to a named tutor, your child's grade and the session length.

faqs.question: Why is PYP tutoring priced below IB Diploma tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the scarcity sits elsewhere. Diploma rates are driven by subject-specialist supply — Chemistry HL, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Physics — and by an external exam with a published grade at the end of it. Primary work has no external exam, and the pool of competent primary tutors in Dubai is larger than the pool of Diploma subject specialists. There are two exceptions where primary rates meet Diploma rates: Arabic as a first language, and early-years phonics for a child with an additional-language profile. Both are narrow specialisms in this city, and scarcity rather than difficulty sets the price.

faqs.question: The PYP has no exams, so how will I know the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: By what is written down at the start and checked every fourth session. Each half-term has one named target — fraction-as-division, unprompted inference from an unseen text, Standard Arabic reading rate — and the note you receive says whether it moved, with the evidence attached: the task the child could not do in week one and can do now. What you will not get is a score or a percentage, because the Primary Years Programme does not produce one and any number quoted to you would be invented. If a provider offers a primary grade improvement figure, ask how it was measured.

faqs.question: Does the PYP Exhibition in the final primary year need a tutor?
faqs.answer: It rarely needs one and often benefits from one, which are different statements. The Exhibition is assessed internally and is not a public qualification, so nothing hangs on it externally. What it does is teach a child to narrow a question, keep notes in their own words, and present to adults who ask awkward questions — the habits the MYP expects at Year 7. A block of eight to twelve sessions across the spring term is reasonable. The tutor coaches the process only: the content, the words and the final presentation stay entirely the student's own work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Arabic as an additional language alongside the PYP?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most common Dubai requests on this page. Arabic is mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires the additional-language class to be organised separately from the first-language class because the expectations and language of instruction differ. Support covers script formation, phonics, high-frequency vocabulary and the weekly assessment pattern your school runs. We match tutors by stream, so tell us which class your child sits in — a first-language specialist and an additional-language specialist are not interchangeable.

faqs.question: Is a Diploma teacher a sensible choice for a Grade 3 learner?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and the price makes it worse. Teaching place value, fraction meanings and early inference is a primary specialism with its own methods, and a teacher whose expertise is Higher Level subject content has typically never used them. The failure mode is subtle: the session goes well, the child enjoys it, and the underlying gap is bridged with the tutor's explanation rather than closed in the child's own understanding. For PYP work we match tutors who have run a primary classroom, and we would rather give you a date for one than put a Diploma specialist in a Grade 3 chair.

faqs.question: How many weekly sessions do Dubai PYP families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One, almost always. The common pattern is a four-session diagnostic block, then a single forty-five-minute session a week against one named target, reviewed each half-term. Two sessions a week makes sense when maths and writing are both genuinely behind and the family has decided to spend the year on it, and we usually drop back to one as soon as the weaker strand closes. Starting with two is how primary tutoring becomes a permanent fixture nobody reviews. At the mid-band market rate, one session a week is roughly AED 640 a month across a Dubai term.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson include, and is a card required?
faqs.answer: Thirty minutes, one per family, over live video with the tutor who would actually teach your child, and no card details are taken at any point. The tutor works on the strand your report flagged rather than running a generic assessment, and you are welcome to watch — for Grades 1 and 2 we prefer it. Afterwards you receive a written summary of what the tutor found and a quote in AED attached to that tutor, grade and session length. If the trial suggests tutoring is not what your child needs, the summary says that instead.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with primary children in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount with scepticism. Apply through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: Will the tutor follow my child's units of inquiry or teach a separate programme?
faqs.answer: The unit planner your school issues is the starting point, because that is the vocabulary your child hears all week and the wording you will read in the report. Where primary tutoring diverges is in the explicit strands: number fluency, phonics, reading inference and written structure are taught directly rather than through the current unit, because they do not emerge reliably from inquiry alone. In practice a session runs ten minutes of recall, twenty-five minutes on the named strand, and ten minutes connecting it to whatever the class is inquiring into that half-term.

faqs.question: What happens to the price if two siblings have sessions in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Staggered back-to-back sessions for two children in one household are common in Dubai, particularly in Al Barsha and Emirates Hills where siblings are often in two different IB phases at once. A second-child rate of roughly ten to twenty per cent below the first is normal across this market, and it reflects a real saving in scheduling rather than a discount for its own sake. Ask for it explicitly, and ask whether it survives if one child's session length differs from the other's — a forty-five-minute primary slot beside a sixty-minute Diploma slot is two different rates.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan for a seven-year-old?
faqs.answer: Yes, by arrangement, and for a primary child it is usually the better option. Dubai school hours shorten during Ramadan and the whole evening timetable shifts, so a fixed 17:00 slot that worked in February often collapses in the Ramadan weeks. Families either move to a post-Iftar slot, move to a late-morning weekend session, or pause for the month and use the spring break as a block instead. Continuity across the month matters less at primary than it does for a Diploma student facing exams, so pausing is a legitimate choice rather than a setback.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring sensible for a six-year-old, or is that too young?
faqs.answer: It works with two conditions, and we state them before the trial rather than after it. The first is length: twenty-five to thirty minutes, not an hour, because attention rather than ability is the limit at that age. The second is a parent in the room or nearby for the first few weeks, to manage the screen and keep the session from becoming a negotiation. With those in place, screen-shared work has one real advantage at this age — the tutor sees the child's handwriting and working as it is produced. Without them, a six-year-old online session is rarely worth the money.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai parent do in Year 6 to prepare for the MYP step?
faqs.answer: Plan in the spring term rather than reacting to the first MYP report in November. Three things matter more than content: showing your child a criterion grid so a four out of eight reads as a mid-band mark and not a failure; building the habit of planning, drafting and revising a long piece of work without being asked; and unifying the fraction meanings before ratio and proportion arrive in Year 7. Assessment literacy takes three or four weeks, the drafting habit ten to fourteen. Doing it while the Exhibition research is still live is substantially easier than starting in September.

faqs.question: How does a KHDA inspection band help me read my own child's primary report?
faqs.answer: Less than you would hope, because the published band is an aggregate across the whole school. A Dubai school rated highly overall can still have a thin Arabic department or a weaker primary phase, and that is exactly what a PYP family experiences day to day. The useful move is to read the body of your own school's report for the primary phase and for Arabic specifically, then compare it with the descriptors on your child's report card. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit and claims no regulator endorsement; this is a reading guide, not a credential.

dubai/ib-pyp-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the report wording, not with a rate
dubai/ib-pyp-tutor.closingBody: If you have a Dubai primary report in front of you and a descriptor you cannot interpret, send the exact wording along with your child's grade and school. You will get a written read of what we think it describes, which tutor we would put in the chair, and what the free 30-minute trial lesson will test — one trial per family, no card details. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, in forty-five-minute blocks below Grade 4, around your actual bus arrival. If the honest answer is that no tutoring is needed this term, we will say so in writing and you can come back in April.

intro.heading: What a retake costs, in money and in months
paragraphs: The first thing to establish is the size of the bill, because it decides everything else. A retake carries three separate costs. There is the examination registration itself, which is set by the IB and administered through a school or an authorised centre, and which your school's Diploma coordinator will quote: we do not publish a figure for it because the amount depends on the centre and the number of subjects, and an invented number here would be worse than none. There is tutoring, which is the part this page can price from published market data. And there is the opportunity cost of the months, which is usually the largest of the three and almost never counted.

On tutoring, published Dubai market rates read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. Bestimate's Dubai monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. A retake in two subjects across a six-month run therefore sits in a predictable range, and the right way to budget it is monthly.

Those are market figures, not IB Gram's price list, and they are published here because most pages ranking for Dubai IB queries publish no price at all. What they tell a family is useful: the tutoring cost of a focused two-subject retake is usually smaller than parents fear, and considerably smaller than a repeated school year. The expensive part of a retake is rarely the teaching.

The second thing to establish is scope, and this is where money is most often wasted. A retake is not a repeat of the Diploma. Candidates retake individual subjects, and within a subject the written papers are re-sat while the internally assessed work may in some circumstances be carried forward rather than redone. The rules on what can be carried forward and for how many sessions are set by the IB and administered by your coordinator, so confirm your own case with them before paying for anything. A plan built on the wrong assumption here wastes months.

Every UAE session runs one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For retake work that matters because the candidate is often no longer at school, sometimes no longer in Dubai, and needs a specialist in one specific component rather than a general tutor nearby.

dubai/ib-retake-tutor.programmesIntro: A retake decision depends on which part of the Diploma fell short. Here is how each component behaves when a candidate goes again.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme subjects
programmes.description: Each of the six subjects can be retaken separately, and most candidates retake one or two rather than all. The written papers are re-sat in a later session; internally assessed components follow the IB's carry-forward rules as administered by the centre.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai candidates usually retake through their own school, which continues to act as the registering centre after graduation in many cases. Where a school will not or cannot register a former student, the coordinator can point to the process for registering through another centre, and that question should be asked in the first week after results.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Both are externally assessed and contribute up to three points through the published matrix. A candidate short on points sometimes finds the cheapest available improvement here rather than in a subject, and the work is writing to criteria rather than re-sitting papers.
programmes.countryNote: Core components are the most overlooked part of a Dubai retake plan. A candidate one or two points short of an offer should ask the coordinator what the core contributed and whether either component is in scope for resubmission, before committing to months of subject revision.

programmes.description: CP candidates sitting DP courses retake those courses on the same basis, with the career-related study and reflective project following the programme's own rules. The smaller subject load usually makes a focused retake simpler to plan.

programmes.name: Enquiry upon results, before any retake
programmes.description: Before committing to a retake there is a separate route: asking for a re-mark or a clerical check through the school within the IB's published deadlines. It is cheaper and faster than a retake and sometimes resolves the problem entirely.
programmes.countryNote: The deadlines for this are short and run from the results release, so it is the first conversation to have rather than the second. Dubai coordinators handle these requests routinely, and a candidate two marks below a grade boundary should always ask about it before pricing a retake.

dubai/ib-retake-tutor.subjectsIntro: Not every subject responds to a six-month retake run at the same speed. Below is what can realistically change in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Responds well to a retake run if the losses were technique: unwritten method, the final parts of long questions, non-calculator fluency. Genuine content gaps across calculus take longer than one session cycle.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical interpretation and modelling justification improve quickly with marked practice. The exploration, where in scope, is a second lever because its criteria are published and learnable.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: A heavy content load makes a full re-learn impractical in a short window, but targeted work on Paper 2 extended responses and organic mechanisms produces measurable movement.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: One of the better retake subjects, because most lost marks are command-term shape rather than missing content. A candidate who learns the required answer structures can move a grade without learning new material.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Data-booklet discipline, uncertainty treatment and significant figures are quick wins. Fields and induction gaps need sustained work, so a retake plan usually prioritises the former.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Among the fastest subjects to improve in a retake window. Diagram accuracy and a supported evaluation move whole mark bands, and both are teachable within weeks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis responds to marked timed practice. The oral and HL essay components are constrained by the centre's arrangements, so confirm with the coordinator what is in scope.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study technique improves quickly once the candidate applies tools to the stimulus rather than reciting them. A good retake subject for a candidate short by one grade.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Narrowing the study bank and learning a smaller set precisely is a few weeks of work with a clear mark effect, which makes this a practical subject to add to a retake plan.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Where resubmission is in scope, work is feedback on the candidate's own claims, counterclaims and examples against published criteria. Core points can decide an offer and cost less to pursue than a subject grade.

sections.heading: Pricing a Dubai retake honestly
paragraphs: A retake budget has three lines and most families only see one. The registration cost is set by the IB and administered by the centre, and your Diploma coordinator will quote it for your specific subject count; we publish no figure for it because it varies by centre and an invented number would be worse than silence. The tutoring line can be priced from published market data. The third line, the months, is the one that decides whether the first two are worth paying.

The tutoring figures below are other providers' published Dubai rates read in October 2026. Read them as a monthly commitment rather than an hourly one, because a retake run is measured in months. A two-subject plan at one weekly hour each, at the specialist band, lands in Bestimate's AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above monthly range for exam-year specialist support; the same plan in the mid band lands nearer AED 600 to 1,200. Across a five or six-month run those are materially different totals, and the right band depends on whether the work is content or mark-scheme level.

Three variables move the number. Subject count is the first and the one families control most directly: two subjects costs roughly twice one, and candidates frequently plan to retake more subjects than their results statement justifies. Level is the second, with Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at the top of every band. Component is the third: work on one paper is cheaper than work across a whole subject, and a results statement broken down by component shows whether that narrower option exists.

The useful comparison is not between tutoring providers. It is between a retake and the alternatives: accepting a different offer, taking a foundation route, deferring, or applying again with the same grades to institutions where they are sufficient. A retake that costs several months and a four-figure sum in AED to move one subject by one grade may be worth it for a medicine applicant and clearly not worth it for someone whose target course would have accepted the original result.

sections.heading: What carries forward and what must be re-sat
paragraphs: This is the question that decides the size of the job, and the answer is specific to the candidate. In general terms, a retake candidate re-sits the written papers for the subjects they are retaking in a later session, while internally assessed work may in some circumstances be carried forward from the original session rather than produced again. The rules on which components can be carried forward, for how many sessions, and under what conditions are set by the IB and administered by the registering centre.

That means the authoritative answer comes from your Diploma coordinator and from current IB documentation, not from a tutoring page. We say that plainly because the cost of getting it wrong is months: a candidate who assumes an Internal Assessment must be redone may spend half the run on a component that was already banked, and a candidate who assumes the opposite may arrive at a deadline with nothing to submit.

Ask the coordinator four things in the first conversation. Which components for each retake subject must be re-sat. Which may be carried forward, and whether that is automatic or requested. What the registration deadline is for the next session. And whether the school will act as the registering centre for a former student. Those four answers, written down, are the foundation of any retake plan worth paying for.

The table below sets out the shape of the question rather than the rules themselves, which belong to the IB. Use it as the list to take to the coordinator meeting, and write their answers in the right-hand column before any tutoring is booked.
