sections.heading: Deciding whether to retake at all
paragraphs: The most valuable thing we do on this page is talk some families out of a retake. A retake makes sense when a specific, named outcome depends on a specific, identifiable grade change that the evidence suggests is achievable. It makes much less sense as a general response to disappointment, and that is the version that most often gets bought in the fortnight after results.

Start with the results statement broken down by component, which the coordinator can obtain. A candidate who missed a grade by a mark or two in one paper is in a different position from one who was well below across all components. The first is a strong retake case and may even be a re-mark case. The second usually means the underlying learning was not there, and five months of tutoring at specialist rates may still not reach the target.

Then establish what the grade is actually for. Universities differ enormously: some will accept the original offer after a short conversation, some hold places for a year, some require a fresh application cycle, and some will not consider a retake candidate for competitive programmes at all. That is a question for the admissions office in writing, not for a tutoring provider or a forum, and the answer sometimes makes the whole decision for you.

The decision matrix below is the one we use in a first session. It is deliberately blunt, because a retake consumes months that cannot be returned and the cost of a wrong decision is much larger than the cost of the tutoring that follows it.

sections.heading: Planning a retake run backwards from the session
paragraphs: The IB runs two examination sessions a year, in May and November, and UAE schools sit the May session as standard. A retake candidate chooses a session and then works backwards. We do not publish specific IB session or results dates on these pages, because the IB's own site is the authoritative source and the coordinator holds the centre's version; any date we restated could be revised without this page noticing.

The order, though, is stable and worth planning around. Registration closes well before the session. Where internally assessed work is in scope, its submission deadline sits months before the papers. Revision rotation needs to finish with several full papers under timed conditions, which means the content work has to be done before the final weeks rather than during them. A plan that arrives at the last month still teaching content has already failed.

A six-month run divides naturally into three phases. The first six to eight weeks are content repair on the specific topics the component breakdown identified. The middle phase is mixed: topic work plus timed questions, with marking in between so the pattern is visible. The final six weeks are full-paper rotation under exam conditions, with the content work closed off. Candidates who invert that order, leaving papers until the end without having practised them, find out too late that pacing is the problem.

Two Dubai-specific notes. Retake candidates are often no longer on a school timetable, which frees daytime hours and widens specialist availability considerably, and the better plans use that rather than defaulting to evening slots. And Ramadan will fall inside most retake runs: shortened days, a different rhythm, and sessions commonly moving to a post-Iftar time, which candidates frequently prefer.
bullets: Confirm the session and the registration deadline with the coordinator first

sections.heading: What actually improves in five months, and what does not
paragraphs: A retake run is long enough to change technique completely and not always long enough to rebuild a subject. Knowing which applies is the difference between a plan that works and one that spends five months confirming the first result. The component breakdown from the results statement is what tells you, which is why we ask for it before anything else.

Technique moves fast. Unwritten method in Mathematics and Physics, command-term mismatch in Biology, missing evaluation in Economics and Business, imprecise reference in English: all of those are patterned losses that respond to marked practice within weeks. A candidate whose breakdown shows good coverage and poor execution is the ideal retake case, and often needs fewer sessions than they expect.

Content rebuilds slowly, and honesty here saves money. A Higher Level Chemistry candidate who was weak across organic chemistry, energetics and equilibrium is looking at most of a syllabus, and five months at one hour a week will not cover it. Either the hours go up substantially, or the plan narrows to the papers where the most marks are recoverable, or the retake is the wrong instrument. We say which of those we think applies rather than taking the booking and discovering it in March.

The third category is components whose availability is constrained rather than academic: oral assessments, performance work, practical arrangements for a former student. Those are centre questions, and if the answer is that the arrangement is not available, no amount of teaching changes the outcome. Ask early, because the answer can rule a subject out of the plan entirely.

sections.heading: Why retake support works better online in the UAE
paragraphs: Retake candidates are the clearest case for online delivery in this entire market. They often have no school timetable, they are frequently travelling or working, their need is one or two specific components rather than a general subject, and their deadline is fixed. The right tutor is defined by knowing that component, and in Dubai the chance that such a person also lives within a reasonable drive of a given community is small.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. All UAE sessions run one-to-one over live video, consistent with every other country page on this site. For a retake run that also solves the continuity problem: a candidate who spends August abroad, or who moves cities mid-run, keeps the same tutor and the same plan. In-home arrangements pause when either party moves, and on a five-month run with a fixed session date those pauses are expensive.

The published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour carry travel inside them, and across a long run that is a significant sum spent on movement rather than teaching. Monthly in-home packages appear in the market at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits, against around AED 799 for eight online sessions. For a candidate paying for their own retake, that difference is often the difference between two subjects and one.

Where in-home genuinely helps is with a candidate who cannot self-direct at all, and for whom someone arriving at the door is the only reliable mechanism for getting work done. That is a real situation. It is also one worth naming honestly rather than solving with a tutoring purchase, because a five-month retake run requires independent study between sessions regardless of how the sessions are delivered.

sections.heading: Honesty, re-marks and what nobody can promise
paragraphs: Three cautions belong on any retake page. The first is that no provider can guarantee a grade or a points total. Grade boundaries are set after each session and move with the paper, and examination performance varies on the day. Any guarantee is either a conditional refund arrangement or an unhonourable claim, and we offer neither.

The second concerns internally assessed work. Where an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay is being produced or resubmitted, it must be the candidate's own work. A tutor can explain criteria, interrogate a research question, teach a technique and give feedback on a draft the candidate wrote. A tutor cannot write it or edit it to completion. At least one provider ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750; for a retake candidate, a malpractice finding would end the attempt it was meant to rescue.

The third is that the re-mark route should always be considered before the retake route. An enquiry upon results is cheaper, faster, and handled through the school within short published deadlines that run from results release. A candidate one or two marks below a boundary should ask about it in the first days, not after a month of deciding. Coordinators in Dubai handle these requests routinely.

Finally, on documents: we link to official IB material rather than redistributing subject guides, mark schemes or grade boundary tables, and we do not publish IB session dates because ibo.org is the authoritative source and the coordinator holds the centre's version. A page that restates exam dates it cannot maintain is a page that will eventually tell a candidate the wrong thing.

sections.heading: Starting a retake plan in the fortnight after results
paragraphs: Send three things: the results statement, the component breakdown if the coordinator has provided it, and the specific outcome the retake is meant to achieve, named precisely. 'A better score' is not a target. 'Grade 6 in Chemistry HL, because the offer requires it and the university has confirmed it will consider a November retake' is, and it makes every later decision obvious.

The first session is a decision session rather than a lesson. We read the breakdown, consider whether a re-mark should come first, identify which components are in scope, and say what we think the realistic outcome is. Sometimes the answer is that one subject is worth retaking and the second is not. Sometimes it is that the retake is the wrong instrument altogether, and we would rather say that in the first hour than sell five months.

The trial lesson is free and carries no condition beyond booking a time. For retake candidates it is usually most useful spent on a real question from the paper that lost the marks, because that is the fastest way to find out whether the problem is technique or content, and the two carry very different costs.

After that the plan is monthly, costed in advance, and reviewed at the halfway point against marked work rather than impressions. If the evidence says the target is out of reach, we say so with enough time left for the candidate to choose a different path. On a retake, that warning is worth more than the sessions it ends.

faqs.question: How much does an IB retake cost in Dubai altogether?
faqs.answer: Three lines. Examination registration is set by the IB and administered through the centre, and your Diploma coordinator will quote it for your subject count; we publish no figure because it varies and an invented one would mislead. Tutoring at published Dubai market rates read in October 2026 runs AED 150 to 300 an hour in the mid band and AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists, which Bestimate's monthly estimates put at AED 600 to 1,200 and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above respectively. The third line is the months, which is usually the largest cost and the least counted.

faqs.question: Do I have to retake the whole Diploma or just one subject?
faqs.answer: Retakes are by subject, and most candidates retake one or two rather than all six. Within a subject, the written papers are re-sat in a later session, and internally assessed work may in some circumstances be carried forward rather than produced again. The rules on what carries forward, for how long and on what basis are set by the IB and administered by the registering centre, so confirm your own case with the Diploma coordinator before paying for anything. Planning on the wrong assumption here is the most common way a retake run wastes months.

faqs.question: Should I ask for a re-mark before deciding to retake?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you are close to a boundary. An enquiry upon results runs through the school within published deadlines that start from the results release, and it is cheaper and faster than a retake. A candidate one or two marks below a grade should ask in the first days rather than after a month of deliberation, because the deadlines are short. Dubai coordinators handle these requests routinely. It sometimes resolves the problem entirely, which makes it the first call rather than a fallback after the retake plan is already paid for.

faqs.question: Will my university still consider me if I retake?
faqs.answer: It varies enormously and you need the answer in writing from the admissions office, not from a forum or a tutoring provider. Some institutions will hold a place for a year, some will accept a short conversation and keep the original offer, some require a fresh application cycle, and some will not consider retake candidates for competitive programmes at all. That answer sometimes makes the whole decision for you, which is why we ask for it before designing a plan. It costs nothing to ask and it can save five months.

faqs.question: How many months does a realistic retake run need?
faqs.answer: Five to six is the usual shape, divided into three phases: content repair on the specific topics the breakdown identified, then mixed topic and timed work with marking in between, then full-paper rotation under exam conditions in the final six weeks. The order matters. Candidates who leave full papers until the last fortnight discover pacing problems too late to fix them. A shorter run can work where the losses were purely technical, and a longer one is needed where content was weak across a whole syllabus.

faqs.question: Which subjects are realistic to improve in one retake cycle?
faqs.answer: Economics, Business Management, Biology and Psychology move fastest, because their lost marks are usually structural: missing evaluation, command-term mismatch, imprecise study detail. Mathematics improves quickly where the losses were unwritten method or the final parts of long questions, and slowly where calculus content was never secure. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics are the hardest to rebuild in one cycle because of content volume, so plans in those subjects usually narrow to the papers where most marks are recoverable rather than attempting the whole syllabus.

faqs.question: Can a retake candidate still gain the three core points?
faqs.answer: Core points come from the published matrix combining Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay grades, and whether either is in scope for a retake candidate depends on the candidate's circumstances and the centre's arrangements. It is worth asking early, because a candidate one or two points short of an offer sometimes finds the cheapest available route is a core component rather than months of subject revision. The coordinator is the authoritative source. If resubmission is in scope, the work is writing to published criteria, which is tractable and short.

faqs.question: Is a retake worth it if I was below target in all six subjects?
faqs.answer: Usually not within a single session. A results statement that is well below target across every component generally means the underlying learning was not secure, and five months of weekly tutoring will not rebuild six subjects. The honest options then are a longer plan, a narrower retake on two subjects where the most marks are recoverable, or a different route altogether such as a foundation programme or an alternative course. We would rather set that out in the first session than take a booking that the evidence does not support.

faqs.question: Do you provide a tutor at home in Dubai for a retake?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. Retake candidates are the clearest case for the online format: they often have no school timetable, frequently travel or work during the run, and need a specialist in one or two specific components rather than a general tutor nearby. Published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour also carry travel inside them, which across a five-month run is a large sum spent on movement rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Can I keep my original Internal Assessment mark?
faqs.answer: In some circumstances internally assessed work can be carried forward rather than produced again, but the conditions are set by the IB and administered by the registering centre, so this is a question for your Diploma coordinator rather than for a tutoring page. Ask whether it is automatic or has to be requested, and get the answer in writing before planning. A candidate who assumes the Internal Assessment must be redone may spend half the run on work that was already banked, and the reverse mistake is worse.

faqs.question: What if my old school will not register me for the session?
faqs.answer: Ask the coordinator anyway, because they can usually explain the route to registering through another school or authorised centre. This belongs in the first week after results rather than later, since registration deadlines sit well before the session and a candidate without a registering centre has no plan at all, whatever tutoring is in place. Some Dubai schools register former students routinely and others do not, so the answer is institution-specific and worth getting early and in writing.

faqs.question: How do sessions work if I am working or travelling during the run?
faqs.answer: They continue, which is the practical argument for the online format. Retake candidates are frequently working, interning or abroad for part of the run, and a recurring slot over live video keeps the same specialist and the same plan through all of it. Candidates no longer at school also have daytime availability, which widens the specialist options considerably compared with evening-only slots. Ramadan falls inside most retake runs, and sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar time, which many candidates prefer.

faqs.question: Can anyone promise the grade I need on a retake?
faqs.answer: No. Grade boundaries are set after each session and move with the difficulty of the paper, and performance on the day varies for reasons nobody controls. Any guarantee in this market is either a conditional refund arrangement with terms buried somewhere or a claim that cannot be honoured. What a retake plan can do is remove the predictable losses that the component breakdown identified. That is the part anyone can act on, and it is the part we price and plan against.

faqs.question: What is the single biggest mistake retake candidates make in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Deciding in the first week of disappointment rather than in the second week with the component breakdown in hand. The breakdown changes the decision more often than not: it reveals that one paper rather than one subject lost the marks, or that the gap is in the core, or that the shortfall was broad enough to make a one-session retake unrealistic. The second most common mistake is not asking the university what it will accept before committing, which is a free question with a decisive answer.

intro.heading: Three products, one word, very different prices
paragraphs: The phrase 'revision classes' covers at least three different purchases in Dubai, and the price difference between them is large enough to change a family's plan. The first is a holiday revision course: a fixed programme over several days in a school break, taught to a group, usually covering a subject's main topics at pace. The second is small-group work at a tuition centre, typically two to six students, running weekly. The third is one-to-one revision, which is not a class at all but is what most families mean when they describe the problem they want solved.

Published Dubai market rates read in October 2026 give the shape of the difference. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300 an hour, IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and one premium provider at AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. Group formats are cheaper per student because the hourly fee is divided, and tuition centres price accordingly. Bestimate's Dubai monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Those are the market's figures, not ours.

What the price difference buys is diagnosis. A group class teaches content to a room; it cannot tell you that your child's Economics marks are going because the evaluation paragraph never reaches a judgement, or that their Biology answers are strong content in the wrong command-term shape. Those are individual findings, visible only in that student's marked script. A family paying for a group course to solve an individual problem is buying the wrong product cheaply, which is the most common way revision money is wasted in this emirate.

The reverse case is just as real and just as costly when it is missed. A student with genuine content gaps across a whole syllabus, who needs coverage rather than diagnosis, is well served by a group course and badly served by paying specialist one-to-one rates to be taught what a class could teach. The honest answer depends on the marked evidence, and the first job is to establish which kind of problem is in front of you. That takes one look at a script.

IB Gram's own model is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not run group classes in the UAE, and IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Where a group course is the right purchase, we will say so, including when it means we are not the right provider.

sections.heading: What each revision format costs per student in Dubai
paragraphs: Comparing these products properly means comparing cost per student per hour, and then asking what that hour contains. The figures below are other providers' published Dubai rates read in October 2026, together with the structural economics of group delivery. They are the market rather than IB Gram's price list, and we publish them because most pages ranking for these queries publish nothing at all.

A group course divides a tutor's hourly fee across the room, which is why a holiday programme can be advertised at a fraction of a one-to-one rate. That arithmetic is real and it is not a trick. What changes with group size is attention: in a room of twelve, no individual script is read; in a group of four, some individual feedback is possible; at one-to-one, the whole hour is spent on one student's errors. The right question is not which is cheapest but which contains what your child's marked paper says they need.

The hidden costs belong in the comparison too. A centre course involves travel at the busiest hour of a Dubai weekday, which for a family in Arabian Ranches or Dubai Hills can be an hour each way. Holiday courses are often sold as a fixed block, so a missed day is a paid-for day. And a course designed for a mixed curriculum room may spend a third of its time on material that does not match the IB's assessment at all.

For most DP2 students who have had mocks returned, the cheapest effective purchase is a short diagnostic one-to-one block rather than a longer group course, because the problem the mock revealed is individual. For a DP1 student with genuine content gaps across a subject, the group course is the better value. The marked paper tells you which case you are in, and that is a free piece of information.

sections.heading: What a revision class cannot do
paragraphs: A class can teach content, model answers, set practice and create the social pressure that gets a reluctant student working. Those are real goods. What it cannot do is read your child's script. That limitation sounds minor and is the reason many Dubai families buy revision twice: once as a course, and then again as individual sessions when the course has not moved anything.

The pattern inside a mock paper is individual by nature. Two students with the same grade 4 in the same class can have opposite problems: one lost marks through pacing and blank final questions, the other through answering 'explain' questions as though they said 'describe'. A class addresses neither, because it does not know. The content it teaches will be partly already known and partly irrelevant to that student's losses.

The second thing a class cannot cover is the core. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry up to three points through the IB's published matrix, and no Dubai revision course we have seen addresses them, for the obvious reason that they are written coursework assessed against criteria rather than examinable content. A family that buys only group revision frequently leaves those three points entirely unmanaged, which is often the cheapest improvement available.

The third is Internal Assessment work. That must be the student's own, and it needs individual feedback on their own draft against published criteria, which is incompatible with a class format and with any provider offering to produce it. We say this plainly because at least one provider ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750, which risks a malpractice finding against the whole Diploma.

sections.heading: The Dubai revision calendar, and when courses actually run
paragraphs: Revision provision in Dubai clusters into the school breaks, which means the market's supply and a student's genuine need are not always aligned. Holiday courses run in the winter break, the spring break and occasionally in the weeks between, and they are advertised heavily in the fortnight before each. The useful discipline is to decide what the student needs first and then see whether a course happens to supply it, rather than buying what is on sale.

The Diploma runs two sessions a year, in May and November, and Dubai schools sit the May session as standard. We publish no specific IB session or results dates on these pages because the IB is the authoritative source and your coordinator holds the centre's version; any date restated here could be revised without this page noticing. The order of events, though, is stable enough to plan against.

Working backwards from the May session: the final six weeks should be full-paper rotation under timed conditions, which means content work has to be finished before that. The two months before that are mixed topic repair and timed questions. The winter break sits inside or beside the mock window, which makes it either a fortnight of lost momentum or the single most productive block of the year, depending on the decision made in November. Ramadan brings shortened school days and a shifted rhythm, with sessions commonly moving to a post-Iftar slot.

One Dubai-specific trap: the spring break often falls close enough to the May session that a family treats it as the main revision window. By then, content teaching is the wrong activity. The highest-value use of that fortnight is full papers, marked, with the errors from each one worked through the next day, and a course that spends it on topic coverage is spending it badly.

sections.heading: Making past papers count
paragraphs: Most revision failure in Dubai is not a shortage of past papers. It is papers sat without being marked, or marked without the errors being worked through. A paper that produces a mark and no change is an expensive way to pass an afternoon, and students do it repeatedly because it feels like work.

The method that produces movement has four steps and most students skip two of them. Sit the paper under real timing, without notes. Mark it against the published scheme, which means reading what the scheme actually required rather than deciding whether the answer was close enough. Classify each lost mark: content, command term, method, or time. Then work the next session entirely on whichever class of loss was largest.

That classification step is what converts practice into a plan. A student who discovers that two-thirds of their lost marks were command-term errors has learned something they can act on in a fortnight. A student who discovers the losses were spread evenly across unfamiliar content has learned that they need teaching rather than practice, which is a different purchase. Either way the next decision is evidence-based rather than anxious.

The volume question has a simple answer: as many full papers as the calendar allows, with marking in between, which is why the start date matters more than the weekly hour count. Three marked papers worked through properly beat ten sat and filed. And on materials, we link to official IB resources rather than redistributing papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables; the school is the correct source for its own mock papers and for the department's criteria sheets.

sections.heading: Why our revision work runs one-to-one and online
paragraphs: IB Gram does not run group classes in the UAE and does not offer home visits; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and every UAE session is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The reason is the nature of the work. Revision that moves a grade is built on one student's marked script, and the specialist who can read that script for a Higher Level subject is defined by what they know rather than by where they live.

There are two secondary advantages that matter in a revision run. Annotated papers are saved, so a student accumulates a file of their own corrected answers with the specific error flagged on each: by the spring that archive is a better revision resource than any published guide, because it contains that student's recurring mistakes. And a recurring online slot survives travel, which Dubai families do over every break, as well as the timetable disruption of the mock fortnight.

Against that, a centre course has one genuine advantage worth naming: other students in the room. For a student who will not work alone, social pressure is a real mechanism, and a family that knows this about their child should weigh it seriously. Our honest position is that the mechanism is valuable and the diagnosis is more valuable, and the ideal arrangement for such a student is often the school's own revision sessions plus a short individual diagnostic block.

The in-home option occupies an odd middle ground for revision specifically. It costs the most per hour, at a published AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate, and it narrows the specialist pool to whoever will drive to your community in the hours a DP2 student is free. For content coverage it works perfectly well. For criteria-level script analysis in a Higher Level science, it is the format least likely to find you the right person.

sections.heading: Regulators, timetables and the week revision actually has
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Its annual inspections run on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the published report for your child's school often comments at department level, which is useful context when judging whether a subject's revision provision is strong.

KHDA also determines part of the week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met. Separate classes are required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. For a revising DP2 student those lessons are fixed, and the revision plan has to fit around them rather than assume them away.

The sector's scale is worth knowing when judging how crowded revision provision is: 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai in 2024-25, with seven new schools for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places. Demand for revision support concentrates into the same few weeks across all of them, which is why booking a specialist in January is harder than booking one in October.

On the regulation of tutors: private tuition in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule. A tuition centre with premises needs a separate KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different thing. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry endorsement and claims none.

sections.heading: Choosing a revision provider in Dubai: what to ask
paragraphs: Five questions separate a useful revision purchase from an expensive one, and all five are answerable before any money changes hands. The first is whether the provider will look at a marked script before recommending anything. A provider who recommends a package without seeing evidence is selling a product rather than solving a problem.

The second is group size, if it is a class. 'Small group' is not a number, and the difference between four students and fourteen is the difference between some individual feedback and none. The third is whether marking is included: on a revision run the marking is the part that produces change, and providers differ on whether it sits inside the fee or outside it.

The fourth is which assessment the content is built around. A revision course serving a mixed curriculum room may spend a third of its time on material that does not match IB assessment, and a tutor who cannot name the paper weightings for the subject they are revising is not revising for the IB specifically. The fifth is what happens if the match is wrong, which should have a plain answer rather than a policy document.

Two red flags to weigh against those answers. Statistics with no sample, date or method behind them, including satisfaction percentages and star ratings, which appear widely in this market and mean nothing. And any grade guarantee, which cannot be honoured because boundaries are set after each session and performance varies on the day. We offer no guarantee and publish no results statistic, and we would treat a competitor's version of either as information about the rest of its claims.

sections.heading: Starting revision work, and what we will say first
paragraphs: Send the subject and level, the most recent marked paper, and how many weeks remain before the assessment that matters. With those three we can say whether the problem is content or technique, which determines whether a class or individual work is the better purchase, and whether a specialist in that subject and level is actually free.

We will tell you when a group course or the school's own revision sessions are the better buy. That happens most often with DP1 students who need coverage, and with students whose school already runs subject revision that nobody in the family has asked about. School-run sessions are usually included in fees, matched to the department's own teaching and mock scope, and are the cheapest revision available in the emirate.

The trial lesson is free with no condition beyond booking a time, and for revision we spend it on a real question from the student's own marked paper. That answers the only question worth answering in the first hour: can this tutor name precisely where the marks went and what to do differently. If the answer is unconvincing, stop there.

After that the plan is short by design. Revision blocks should end, not renew: once the patterned losses the script identified have gone, the marginal hour buys very little and we say so. For most Dubai DP2 students that is four to six sessions in one subject, not a term of weekly classes, and the honest version of this market is that the cheaper purchase is usually the smaller one.

faqs.question: Are group revision classes in Dubai cheaper than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, because the tutor's hourly fee is divided across the room. Published Dubai one-to-one rates read in October 2026 run AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists, while group formats price below that per student. The arithmetic is genuine. What changes with group size is attention: in a room of twelve no individual script is read, and if your child's problem is an individual pattern of lost marks, the cheaper product does not address it.

faqs.question: When is a group revision course actually the right choice?
faqs.answer: When the problem is content coverage rather than technique. A DP1 student who has genuine gaps across a subject, or a student who needs the social pressure of other people working in the room, is well served by a class and badly served by paying specialist one-to-one rates for teaching a group could deliver. The marked script tells you which case you are in: evenly spread losses across unfamiliar content point to a class, while patterned losses on command terms or method point to individual work.

faqs.question: Does my child's school already run revision sessions?
faqs.answer: Many Dubai schools do, in the weeks before mocks and the May session, usually included in fees and often not advertised to parents. They are the cheapest revision available and they are matched to the department's own teaching and to the mock scope, which no external course can claim. Ask the subject teacher or the Diploma coordinator before paying for anything outside. Families regularly buy an external course while a school session in the same subject runs in the same week unattended.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a DP2 student do before the May session?
faqs.answer: As many full papers under timed conditions as the calendar allows, with marking in between, which is why the start date matters more than the weekly hour count. Three papers marked and worked through properly beat ten sat and filed. The method is: sit it under real timing without notes, mark it against the published scheme, classify every lost mark as content, command term, method or time, then spend the next session on whichever class of loss was largest. Most students skip the classification step, which is the step that produces a plan.

faqs.question: What should a revision plan contain in the final six weeks?
faqs.answer: Full papers and error review, with content teaching closed off. By that point new material is the wrong activity: it displaces the practice that converts knowledge into marks and it rarely sticks. The highest-value pattern is a full paper under timed conditions, marked, then a session spent entirely on the errors it produced, repeated. Dubai families often treat the spring break as the main revision window and fill it with topic coverage, which is spending the most valuable fortnight of the year on the least valuable activity.

faqs.question: Can revision classes help with Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: In practice, no, and this is the clearest gap in Dubai's revision market. The core carries up to three points through the IB's published matrix, and both components are written coursework assessed against criteria rather than examinable content, so no group course we have seen addresses them. They need individual feedback on the student's own draft. Families who buy only group revision frequently leave three points unmanaged, which is often the cheapest improvement available in the whole Diploma for the smallest number of hours.

faqs.question: Do you run IB revision classes in Dubai yourselves?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram's UAE model is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and we do not run group classes in the emirate or send tutors to homes; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The reason is that revision which moves a grade is built on one student's marked script, and the specialist who can read that script for a Higher Level subject is defined by what they know rather than where they live. Where a group course is the better purchase, we will say so.

faqs.question: What is the hidden cost of a centre-based revision course?
faqs.answer: Travel and prepaid absence, mostly. A 5pm class means leaving school and crossing Dubai at the worst hour, which for a family in Arabian Ranches or Dubai Hills can be an hour each way, and that hour is revision time spent in a car. Holiday courses are usually sold as a fixed block, so a missed day is still a paid day. And a course serving a mixed-curriculum room may spend a share of its time on material that does not match IB assessment at all, which is the cost nobody itemises.

faqs.question: How do I judge whether a revision tutor knows the IB specifically?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the assessment structure for the subject and level in question: the papers, roughly what each is worth, and where in the mark scheme marks are most commonly lost. A tutor who can do that is revising for the IB. One who talks in general terms about confidence and exam strategy is revising for an exam in the abstract. Also ask whether they will read a marked script before recommending a plan, and whether marking is included in the fee or charged separately.

faqs.question: Is the winter break a good time for IB revision in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It is the most decisive fortnight of the DP2 year, and the decision is made in November rather than in December. The break usually sits inside or immediately beside the mock window, so it becomes either lost momentum or the single most productive block available. The highest-value use is diagnosis and repair: read the marked mock, identify the patterned losses, and work on those specifically. Because sessions run over live video, families who travel can continue from wherever they are rather than pausing by accident.

faqs.question: Can one revision block cover two subjects at once?
faqs.answer: It can, but sequencing them usually works better than running them in parallel. A DP2 student with school, the KHDA mandatory subjects on the timetable and an Internal Assessment in progress has limited capacity, and two subjects plus marked practice in each fills it. Three means none is done properly. If two subjects genuinely need work we would normally start with the one where the script shows technique losses rather than content gaps, because technique moves faster and the early win changes how the student approaches the second subject.

faqs.question: Will sessions run during Ramadan and the school breaks?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing moved deliberately. Ramadan brings shortened school days and a different household rhythm, and recurring slots commonly shift to a post-Iftar time, which many students prefer because evening focus is often better than late-afternoon focus. Dubai families travel over the winter and spring breaks, and because every session runs over live video a student can continue from wherever they are, or pause and resume on a plan rather than by drift. All scheduling is in Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: How long should a revision block last?
faqs.answer: Shorter than most families expect. For a DP2 student whose mock has been returned, four to six sessions in one subject aimed at the losses the script identified is the usual shape, not a term of weekly classes. Blocks should be designed to end: once the patterned losses have gone, the marginal hour buys very little, and we raise that at the review rather than letting a slot renew by default. A student with genuine content gaps across a syllabus is a different and longer case.

faqs.question: Can a revision provider promise a grade improvement?
faqs.answer: No, and one that does is making a claim it cannot honour. Grade boundaries are set after each session and move with the difficulty of the paper, and performance on the day varies for reasons nobody controls. Treat satisfaction percentages, star ratings and improvement statistics with no stated sample, date or method as decoration; they are common in this market and they mean nothing. What revision can honestly offer is the removal of patterned, diagnosable losses, which is the part a marked script makes visible and actionable.

dubai/ib-revision-classes.closingHeading: Buy the product the script calls for
dubai/ib-revision-classes.closingBody: Revision in Dubai is sold as three different products at three very different prices, and the marked paper tells you which one your child needs. Send the subject, the level, the most recent marked script and the weeks remaining, and we will say whether the problem is content or technique, whether a group course or the school's own sessions would serve you better, and whether a specialist in that subject is free. The trial lesson is free and runs on a real question from your child's own paper, one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-score-45-coaching.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work at the top of the grade range, where the questions are about the last two marks on a question rather than about the topic. Each marks to published criteria and reports honestly on whether a 7 is in reach.

intro.heading: What a 45 costs in money, time and realism
paragraphs: Start with the arithmetic, because it governs everything else. Forty-five points means grade 7 in all six subjects, which gives 42, plus the full three points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination. There is no spare capacity anywhere in that total. A single 6 caps the score at 44, and a 6 with two core points caps it at 43. That is why 45 coaching is structurally different from grade improvement work: it is not about lifting a weak subject, it is about preventing any subject from being the one that slips.

The cost follows from the structure. A family targeting 45 is usually buying support across two or three subjects over most of two years, rather than six weeks in one subject before an exam. Published Dubai market rates in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutoring at AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with one premium provider publishing AED 650. At the specialist band, two one-hour sessions a week across a Dubai school year is a meaningful household line item, and the monthly view is the honest one. Bestimate's own Dubai monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

That number is worth setting against the thing it is bought alongside. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are frozen; tutoring is not, and families aiming at 45 often find the tutoring line grows faster than the fee line across DP2.

The second honest point concerns who 45 coaching is for. Students who reach the top of the Diploma range are usually already strong, and the work is therefore narrow: the last two marks on a seven-mark question, the evaluation sentence in an Economics answer, the criterion-C detail in an Internal Assessment. A student currently at a 5 who wants a 7 needs a different and longer piece of work, and we will say so rather than sell a package with the wrong label on it. No provider can guarantee a score, and one offering it is telling you something useful about its other claims.

All of our UAE sessions run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For work this specific the online format is what makes it possible at all, since a Dubai family needing someone who can mark Chemistry HL Paper 3 at the 6-to-7 boundary is choosing from a very small pool and should not also be choosing by postcode.

dubai/ib-score-45-coaching.programmesIntro: A 45 is built across the whole Diploma and influenced by what happened before it. Here is where the points are won and lost at each stage.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Year 2
programmes.description: Where the score is realised. Internal Assessments are finalised across six subjects, mocks are sat, and the May session arrives. Costs peak here because families typically run support in two or three subjects simultaneously, and the work is boundary-level rather than remedial.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP2 students carry an unusually dense winter: mocks between late November and early February, Internal Assessment deadlines spread across the same weeks, the KHDA mandatory subjects still timetabled, and university applications running in parallel. Families aiming at 45 who have not costed DP2 before it begins almost always find the monthly figure higher than expected.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Year 1
programmes.description: The cheaper year to buy support in, and the more decisive one. Content taught in DP1 underpins half of every paper, and a topic left shaky in DP1 costs marks in DP2 at a much higher hourly rate. Extended Essay work also begins here.
programmes.countryNote: The best-value 45 plans we see in Dubai start in DP1 with one subject and one hour a week, not DP2 with three subjects and six. Specialist availability across the emirate is also loosest in DP1, before every school's mock lands in the same fortnight and the specialist bands tighten.

programmes.name: TOK, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Three points sit here, awarded through the IB's published matrix combining the TOK and Extended Essay grades. CAS is a completion requirement rather than a graded one. For a 45 the core must deliver its full three points, which makes these the least optional components in the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Core support is the cheapest point-per-dirham available to a Dubai family chasing 45, and the least bought. Two or three sessions reading the published criteria alongside a student, then giving feedback on their own drafts, costs a fraction of a term of subject tutoring and protects points that are otherwise left to chance.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Year 5
programmes.description: Where the subject combination is chosen. A 45 is far harder from three Higher Levels chosen against a student's strengths than from three chosen with them, and that decision is made here, usually quickly and with limited information about what each course actually assesses.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students arriving in DP1 from MYP rather than IGCSE often have no experience of timed external-style papers, which costs them early DP1 marks and can set a low expectation in a department. For a family with 45 in mind, a short block on exam technique in the MYP5 summer is unusually good value.

dubai/ib-score-45-coaching.subjectsIntro: At the top of the range, the question is never whether the student knows the topic. The list below names what separates a 6 from a 7 in each subject and what that costs in hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The 7 lives in the last parts of the long questions and in proof. Students at 6 usually complete the routine work and lose the final three or four marks of each extended question. Expect sustained weekly work rather than a short block, which is why this is the most costly subject on a 45 plan.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Separation happens in fields, induction and the option topic, plus data analysis precision on Paper 3. A 6 is a student who can do the physics; a 7 is one who also manages uncertainty, significant figures and the data booklet without thinking about them.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 2 extended responses and organic mechanisms decide it, with the Internal Assessment's data treatment criteria the second lever. Hours here are usually front-loaded in DP1, because the content volume makes late repair expensive.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The 7 is earned on command-term precision and on the detail the mark scheme names: specific examples, specific terminology, causal chains rather than correlations. Comparatively cheap to improve, because the work is technique rather than content.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Evaluation and diagram accuracy, plus HL Paper 3 quantitative work. One of the faster subjects to move at the boundary, since a student who reaches a judgement supported by a correct diagram gains marks immediately.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis and the HL essay separate the top two grades. The difference is analytical precision about how a text produces meaning rather than what it says, and it responds to regular marked practice on unseen extracts.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Historiography and the depth of the HL Paper 3 answers decide the grade. A 7 answer uses historians' arguments as evidence rather than decoration, which is a habit built across a year rather than a term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The boundary sits in statistical interpretation, modelling justification and the exploration. Students lose the top marks by calculating correctly and then failing to state what the result means in context.

subjects.name: Spanish, French and Arabic B
subjects.description: A 7 requires range and accuracy under time in the productive skills, plus confident handling of the oral. Sustained short sessions work better than long ones, which changes the cost shape to more frequent and shorter bookings.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay and exhibition are graded and feed the three core points. Work is feedback on the student's own claims, counterclaims and examples against the published criteria, with nothing drafted for them. Cheapest point-movement in the Diploma.

sections.heading: The AED cost of a 45 plan, by the month
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages quote an hourly figure because it is the smaller number. For a family aiming at 45 it is also the least useful one, since the commitment is measured in school years. The figures below are other providers' published Dubai rates read in October 2026, converted into the monthly shape a household actually budgets in. They are the market, not IB Gram's price list.

Work from the bottom row upwards. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages visible in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. A 45 plan running two subjects weekly at the specialist band therefore sits well above a single-subject budget arrangement, and the gap compounds over 24 months.

Three things move the figure more than the provider's brand does. Level is the first: Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches command the top of every band, while an SL humanities subject sits lower. Frequency is the second, and it is the variable families control: one weekly hour in DP1 and two in DP2 costs far less in total than three weekly hours from January of DP2, and usually produces more. Timing is the third, because Dubai specialist availability tightens each winter when every school's mock returns at once, and tight availability firms prices.

A useful planning discipline is to cost the whole Diploma before starting rather than month by month. Two subjects at a weekly hour across both years, plus a short core block and a boundary block in the spring of DP2, is a budget a family can actually hold. Six subjects at two hours a week from the start of DP2 is a budget almost nobody holds, and the plans that collapse mid-year are usually the ones that were never costed end to end.

sections.heading: Where the 6 becomes a 7
paragraphs: Students aiming at 45 rarely lose marks to ignorance. They lose them in a pattern that is remarkably consistent across subjects: the final marks of extended questions, the precision the mark scheme names, and the judgement sentence that converts analysis into evaluation. A tutor's job at this level is to find that pattern in marked work and drill the specific question types where it appears, which is a narrower activity than revision.

The pattern differs in texture by subject group. In the sciences it is usually precision: uncertainty treatment, significant figures, naming the control variable, giving the mechanism rather than the correlation. In Mathematics it is the last parts of long questions, where routine technique runs out and the question asks for structure. In the humanities it is evaluation: students at 6 present both sides fully and never reach a defensible judgement, which caps the band regardless of knowledge.

Internal Assessments are the other half of the picture, and the half that is more controllable. Every subject's IA is marked against published criteria that the student can read, and the top criterion bands are specific about what they require. A student who has read the criteria and a student who has not produce visibly different work, and the second kind is more common than it should be, including among strong students in good Dubai schools.

The honest limit on all of this: no amount of coaching makes a 7 certain, in any subject, and nobody who says otherwise should be trusted with the money. Grade boundaries move session to session, papers vary in difficulty, and examination days are human events. What boundary work does is remove the predictable losses, which is the only part of the outcome anyone can actually act on.

sections.heading: The three core points nobody budgets for
paragraphs: A 45 is impossible without the full three core points, and they are awarded through the IB's published matrix combining the Theory of Knowledge grade with the Extended Essay grade. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds that matrix and will show it to you. The practical consequence is simple: a student with six 7s and a weak core does not score 45, and the components involved are among the least coached in the entire Diploma.

That is strange, because they are the most tractable. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece written to published criteria over many months, with a supervisor attached. Theory of Knowledge is an essay to a prescribed title plus an exhibition. In both cases the criteria are available, the deadlines are internal and knowable, and the work is produced slowly enough for feedback to be absorbed. Compare that with trying to move a Higher Level science grade in the spring of DP2.

The boundary matters here more than anywhere else on this page. A tutor can discuss a research question, ask whether the method answers it, point out that an argument has no counterclaim, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it or edit it to completion. At least one provider ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750, and a student submitting bought work risks a malpractice finding against the whole Diploma. For a 45 candidate that is the single worst trade available.

Practically, three to five sessions across DP1 and early DP2 covers this ground: reading the criteria together, interrogating the research question early enough that it can still change, and one round of structured feedback on the student's own draft. On a two-year budget it is the smallest line and the one protecting three of the 45 points.

sections.heading: Building a two-year plan a Dubai household can hold
paragraphs: The plans that survive are the ones built against the school's real calendar. In Dubai that means the mock window between late November and early February, Internal Assessment deadlines spread across the same period, the KHDA mandatory subjects of Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies which remain timetabled throughout, the winter break, and Ramadan. A plan that assumes 48 clear weeks a year is fiction, and the first version families write usually does.

A workable shape looks like this. DP1: one subject at a weekly hour, chosen as the one most likely to cause trouble later, plus an early Extended Essay conversation. DP1 summer: a short block on whatever the end-of-year examinations exposed, which is the cheapest repair window in the two years. DP2 autumn: a second subject added, core work scheduled before the application rush. DP2 winter: boundary work on marked mock papers. DP2 spring: timed full-paper rotation.

Deliberate pauses matter as much as sessions. The fortnight a student is sitting mocks is not a fortnight to add tutoring hours; the week an Internal Assessment is due is not either. Families who plan the pauses in advance keep the plan; families who improvise them tend to drop the plan entirely and restart it late at a higher cost. Ramadan commonly moves a recurring slot to a post-Iftar time, which students frequently prefer.

On where the hours should go when the budget is finite, the ranking we would argue for is: core components first because the points are cheap, then the Higher Level subject most likely to slip, then a second Higher Level, then anything else. Spreading a fixed budget thinly across six subjects is the pattern that most reliably produces no change anywhere, and it is the pattern an anxious January produces by default.

sections.heading: Online delivery against in-home coaching at this level
paragraphs: At the top of the grade range the tutor's exactness is the whole product. The person reviewing a Mathematics AA HL script has to know where the final marks of a long question are won, and that is a narrow specialism. Dubai's in-home market is real and large, with published rates from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, but it is bounded by who will drive to your community in the hours a Diploma student is free.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. All UAE sessions run one-to-one over live video, as stated on every other country page on this site. The practical gain for boundary work is twofold. The tutor pool is the whole pool rather than the drivable subset, and marked work is annotated on a shared screen and saved, so across two years a student accumulates a reviewable archive of their own corrected long answers, which is itself a revision resource at the end.

The in-home premium also looks different on a two-year plan than on a six-week block. Travel sits inside the hourly rate, and across 60 or 70 sessions that is a substantial sum spent on moving a person around Dubai rather than on teaching. Families costing a 45 plan tend to notice that line once the arithmetic is monthly rather than hourly.

Where in-home genuinely wins is with younger students who need someone physically present. A DP1 or DP2 student working at the 6-to-7 boundary does not need presence; they need the right examiner-literate specialist and a stable weekly hour.
