sections.heading: What nobody can promise, and what that means for the money
paragraphs: No tutoring provider can guarantee a 45, a 7, or any specific point total. Grade boundaries are set after each session and move with the paper's difficulty; the IB publishes no advance boundary; and examination performance on the day varies for reasons nobody controls. A guarantee in this market is either a refund scheme with conditions buried somewhere, or a claim that cannot be honoured. We offer neither, and we would treat a competitor's guarantee as information about the rest of its page.

What a family is actually buying is the removal of predictable losses. Marks lost to command-term errors, to unshown method, to unread Internal Assessment criteria, to an Extended Essay research question that was never interrogated, to timing collapse on a paper the student had never sat under full conditions: all of those are foreseeable and addressable. The unpredictable remainder is the examination itself.

That framing also tells a Dubai family when to stop spending. If a student is already handling the boundary question types cleanly, has read the criteria for every Internal Assessment, and is completing full papers under time with marks to spare, the marginal hour is buying very little. We would rather say that and lose the booking than run a plan with nothing left to fix, and we tell families at the week-three review when we think that point has arrived.

One final caution about claims in this market. Statistics about results, satisfaction and tutor quality circulate freely on these pages with no stated sample, date or method behind them, and self-asserted star ratings appear in schema that contradict the visible page. Treat any figure without a source as decoration, including on this page: every number here is attributed, and the AED figures all carry the provider that published them and the month we read them.

sections.heading: Starting a 45 plan, and what we will tell you first
paragraphs: Send the subject list with levels, the most recent marks and what they were marked against, and which year the student is in. With that we can say whether the target is realistic from the current position, which subjects should be prioritised on a finite budget, and whether a specialist in the relevant Higher Levels is actually free. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL and the HL sciences are where Dubai availability tightens first.

We will also be direct about the gap between the aspiration and the evidence. A student averaging 5s in DP1 can improve substantially, and we will say what that looks like, but we will not label it a 45 plan. Mislabelling the target is how families end up spending two years disappointed by genuine progress, and it is a sales habit rather than a teaching one.

The trial lesson is free and carries no condition beyond booking a time. On a two-year plan the match matters more than on a six-week block, so the trial exists to test it properly: the student works on real material at the boundary and says afterwards whether the teaching was useful. If the fit is wrong we would rather find out in the first hour than the tenth.

After that the plan is written against the school calendar, costed by the month, and reviewed with marked evidence rather than impressions. We will tell you when a subject no longer needs the hour, and we will tell you when the right answer is to spend the remaining budget on the Extended Essay instead of a sixth subject. On a 45 plan, knowing where not to spend is most of the value.

process.title: Send the subject list, levels and recent marks
process.description: Six subjects with Higher and Standard Levels, the latest assessed marks and what each was marked against. That is enough for us to say which subjects a finite budget should go to first and whether the target is realistic from here.

process.title: Cost the whole Diploma, not the first month
process.description: We work out what the plan costs across the remaining months at market specialist rates before it starts. Plans that collapse mid-year are almost always plans that were never costed end to end, and they restart later at a higher price.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One live session with no condition beyond finding a time. The student works at the boundary on real material and judges the teaching. On a two-year commitment the match matters more than on a short block, so we test it properly.

process.title: Schedule the core components early
process.description: The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge carry the three points a 45 requires and are the cheapest to protect. They get dates in the plan in DP1, rather than attention in DP2 when everything else is already competing.

process.title: Review monthly against marked work
process.description: Each month the plan is checked against marked evidence. Subjects come off the plan when the boundary losses have gone, which is how the total cost stays bounded rather than growing by default.

whyPoints.title: Costed by the month, with sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands here are other providers' published Dubai rates with the month they were read, shown as monthly figures because that is how a two-year plan is actually paid for. Most pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: Boundary work, not general revision
whyPoints.description: Sessions target the specific places the last marks go: the final parts of long questions, the precision a mark scheme names, the judgement sentence. That is a narrower and shorter activity than revising a syllabus.

whyPoints.title: Core points scheduled, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Three of the 45 points come from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. They are the cheapest points on the plan and the ones families most often leave to chance, so they get dates rather than hopes.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, and no unsourced statistics
whyPoints.description: Nobody can guarantee a 45 or a 7. We publish no results claims without a sample, date and method, which rules out most of the figures circulating in this market, including the self-asserted star ratings.

whyPoints.title: We say when to stop buying hours
whyPoints.description: Once the predictable losses are gone, the marginal hour buys very little. We tell families that at the monthly review rather than letting a plan run on, and we say which subject to drop first.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry or IB endorsement and claims none. Every regulator mentioned here is explained with a link to its own pages so that anything on this page can be checked.

faqs.question: What exactly does a score of 45 require?
faqs.answer: Grade 7 in all six subjects, which gives 42 points, plus the full three points from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. There is no spare capacity: one grade 6 caps the total at 44, and a 6 with only two core points caps it at 43. That structure is why top-band coaching is different from grade improvement. The work is not about lifting a weak subject; it is about ensuring that no subject becomes the one that slips, and about treating the core as three points rather than as paperwork.

faqs.question: What does a two-year 45 plan cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Costed monthly, which is how families actually pay for it. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Market monthly packages include around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Two Higher Level subjects weekly at the specialist band therefore sits at the top of those ranges and compounds across 24 months. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026, not our price list.

faqs.question: Can anyone guarantee my child a 45 or a grade 7?
faqs.answer: No. Grade boundaries are set after each session and move with paper difficulty, the IB publishes no advance boundary, and examination performance varies on the day for reasons no tutor controls. Any guarantee in this market is either a conditional refund scheme or a claim that cannot be honoured, and we offer neither. What coaching can do is remove predictable losses: command-term errors, unshown method, unread Internal Assessment criteria, an uninterrogated Extended Essay question, timing collapse on a paper never sat in full. The remainder is the examination itself.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start a top-band plan in DP1 or DP2?
faqs.answer: DP1, substantially, and it also works better. An hour spent while content is still being taught prevents a repair bought at the specialist rate eighteen months later, and Dubai specialist availability is loosest in DP1 before every school's mock lands in the same fortnight. The best-value plans we see start with one subject and one weekly hour in DP1, add a second in DP2, and finish with boundary work in the spring. The most expensive plans start in January of DP2 with three subjects at once, and they rarely survive the term.

faqs.question: Which single Diploma subject usually needs the most hours for a 7?
faqs.answer: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, consistently. The grade is decided in the final parts of long questions and in proof, where routine technique runs out and the question asks for structure, and that capability is built across a year rather than a term. Higher Level Physics and Chemistry are next, with the content volume making late repair expensive. Humanities subjects move faster at the boundary, because evaluation structure and diagram accuracy are learnable in weeks, which is why a finite budget usually goes to Mathematics first.

faqs.question: How do the three core points actually work?
faqs.answer: They come from a published IB matrix combining the Theory of Knowledge grade with the Extended Essay grade, and your school's Diploma coordinator holds that matrix and will show it to you. The combination awards up to three points on top of a maximum 42 subject points, giving the total of 45. For a top-band candidate the core is non-optional, and it is also the most tractable part of the Diploma: criteria are published, deadlines are internal and knowable, and the work is slow enough that feedback can be absorbed and acted on.

faqs.question: Where should a limited tutoring budget go first?
faqs.answer: Core components, then the Higher Level subject most likely to slip, then a second Higher Level, then anything else. The reasoning is cost per point: three core points are protected by a handful of sessions, while moving a Higher Level science grade takes sustained work. The pattern to avoid is spreading a fixed budget thinly across all six subjects, which reliably produces no visible change anywhere. That is also the pattern an anxious January produces by default, which is why costing the plan in advance matters.

faqs.question: My child is averaging 5s. Is 45 realistic?
faqs.answer: Probably not, and we will say so rather than relabel the work. A student averaging 5s can improve a great deal, and a well-built two-year plan might target the high thirties, which opens most university doors. Calling that a 45 plan sets a family up to be disappointed by genuine progress, which is a sales habit rather than a teaching one. We would rather describe the realistic target from the current evidence, name which subjects move fastest, and let you decide whether the plan is worth buying on those terms.

faqs.question: Do you work on Internal Assessments for top-band students?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the boundary the IB sets, and it is among the highest-value work on a 45 plan. Every Internal Assessment is marked against published criteria the student can read, and the top bands are specific about what they require. A tutor can explain those criteria, question the research question and method, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or edit it to completion. Bought coursework risks a malpractice finding against the whole Diploma, which for a 45 candidate is the worst possible trade.

faqs.question: How many hours a week can a DP2 student realistically absorb?
faqs.answer: Two to three hours of tutoring plus the marked practice between sessions is the usual ceiling, and often less during the mock fortnight or an Internal Assessment deadline week. Dubai DP2 students also carry the KHDA mandatory subjects on their timetable throughout, which does not pause for exam season. Plans that assume more time than that are abandoned rather than completed. We build in deliberate pauses, because families who schedule the pauses keep the plan while families who improvise them tend to drop it and restart late.

faqs.question: Do you provide in-home coaching in Dubai for this?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. On a two-year plan the arithmetic is unusually clear: in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour carry travel inside them, and across sixty or seventy sessions that is a large sum spent moving a person around Dubai. Online, the specialist pool is the whole pool rather than the drivable subset, and annotated marked work is saved session by session, which becomes its own revision archive by the May session.

faqs.question: How does a tutor know where the last two marks are?
faqs.answer: From published assessment criteria and from marked scripts, read together. The pattern at the top of the range is consistent: in sciences it is precision, meaning uncertainty treatment, named variables and mechanisms rather than correlations; in Mathematics it is the final parts of long questions; in humanities it is reaching a defensible judgement rather than presenting both sides. A tutor who can point to the specific sentence that would have earned the mark is doing the job. One who talks about general exam confidence is not, at this level.

faqs.question: When is the right time to stop paying for sessions?
faqs.answer: When the predictable losses are gone. If a student handles the boundary question types cleanly, has read the criteria for every Internal Assessment, and completes full papers under time with marks in hand, the marginal hour buys very little. We raise that at the monthly review rather than letting a plan run on, because a plan with nothing left to fix is just a standing order. Knowing where not to spend is a real part of the value on a two-year commitment, and most providers have no incentive to tell you.

faqs.question: Does school fee pressure in Dubai affect what families spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: It shapes the decision more than most pages admit. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are therefore flat while tutoring is not, and families aiming at the top of the Diploma range often find the tutoring line grows faster than the fee line through DP2. That is the argument for costing the full plan before starting rather than approving it month by month.

faqs.question: Should we use a tuition centre class alongside one-to-one sessions?
faqs.answer: For a top-band candidate, rarely. Group classes are taught to the middle of the group, which is exactly where a student aiming at a 7 is not. They can be useful for broad coverage if a student has genuine content gaps across a subject, and they are cheaper per hour. But the work that moves a 6 to a 7 is individual by nature: it depends on the particular marks that particular student keeps losing, which no class of fifteen can address. If the budget is finite, fewer individual hours beat more group hours here.

dubai/ib-score-45-coaching.closingHeading: Cost the plan, then build it
dubai/ib-score-45-coaching.closingBody: A 45 is six 7s and three core points with nothing spare, and it is bought by the month rather than the hour. Send the subject list with levels, the latest marks and the year your child is in, and we will tell you what a realistic plan costs at market specialist rates, which subjects a finite budget should reach first, and whether the target matches the evidence. If it does not, we will say what does. The trial lesson is free, one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with no condition beyond finding an hour that works.

dubai/ib-spanish-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Spanish at Language B Standard and Higher Level and Spanish ab initio, including oral preparation and the Higher Level literary works. Each engagement starts from four short diagnostic tasks rather than a conversation, because a conversation measures confidence and the examination does not.

intro.heading: How a Dubai parent can tell whether Spanish tutoring is changing marks
paragraphs: Spanish is a comfortable subject to be tutored in and an uncomfortable one to measure. Sessions are enjoyable, the student becomes more willing to speak, and a parent who does not speak Spanish has no way to judge whether anything examinable has changed. Six months later a mock result arrives and either confirms the impression or contradicts it. This page is about removing that uncertainty before the mock, using records a non-Spanish-speaking parent can read.

Four artefacts do the work. The first is an error log: a running list the student maintains of their own recurring mistakes, by category, with a correction and a date. The second is timed written tasks marked twice, once for language and once for task conventions, kept in order. The third is recorded oral rehearsals, where specific features can be counted rather than impressions reported. The fourth is listening scores from past papers, written down, because listening is the one skill where a raw number is available.

The error log is the most useful and the least used. Spanish errors for English-speaking learners fall into a small number of categories that repeat endlessly: the choice between ser and estar, the preterite against the imperfect, gender and number agreement, por against para, and the subjunctive avoided entirely. A student who logs their own instances sees the pattern within a fortnight. A student who is simply corrected each time forgets each correction separately.

Recorded orals turn a subjective component into a countable one. Play back a rehearsal and count four things: seconds spent describing before any discussion starts, number of fillers, number of self-corrections completed rather than abandoned, and number of complex structures attempted. All four move in a measurable direction over six weeks, and all four are visible to a parent watching the two recordings back to back, whatever language they speak.

Dubai supplies the natural measurement point. Schools here hold mock examinations across a window from roughly late November to February, which means every candidate gets a marked set of papers before the real session. A plan that begins in October has a baseline, a six-week check, and a mock to validate against. A plan that begins in March has none of those, which is why the same money buys less later.

Delivery is stated once. Spanish support for Dubai families runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For a record-based approach, a screen is an advantage: the log, the marked tasks and the recordings all live in one shared place rather than in a folder somebody has mislaid halfway through the term.

dubai/ib-spanish-tutor.programmesIntro: Spanish sits in the Diploma Programme as a language acquisition course, but the Dubai picture is complicated by how varied students' starting points are, and the IB stage a student is at changes what can usefully be measured.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Spanish is offered as Spanish B at Standard or Higher Level, or as Spanish ab initio at Standard Level for genuine beginners, with Spanish A available in Group 1 for students whose best language it is. Assessment across the Language B routes combines a productive writing paper, a receptive paper covering listening and reading, and an individual oral, with two literary works required at Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: Spanish is a smaller Group 2 option than French or Arabic in most Dubai schools, which has a measurement consequence: with a class of eight or nine, a student has almost no sense of where they stand. An individual record of marked tasks and recorded orals becomes the only available benchmark, which is one reason this approach suits the subject here.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language Acquisition places students in phases by proficiency rather than year group and assesses listening, reading, speaking and writing against four criteria. The phase a student reaches by the end of MYP5 is the best available predictor of whether Spanish B or ab initio fits, and it is a number worth asking the school for directly.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools that offer Spanish from MYP tend to start it later than French, so students often arrive in DP1 from a lower phase. That is not a problem if the route matches, and it is a serious problem if a student at phase 2 is placed in Spanish B Standard Level. The baseline tasks described on this page expose that mismatch in an hour.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students complete a language development component alongside their career-related study, and may take Spanish as a DP course as well. The two are assessed differently, and families sometimes assume all Spanish study in the IB leads to the same outcome. Establishing which one applies is the first step before any measurement plan makes sense.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, CP Spanish is often chosen for employment-related reasons connected to hospitality, tourism and aviation. Where the aim is functional competence rather than a Diploma Programme grade, the measurements change: recorded conversations and task completion matter more than written accuracy, and the sessions should be cheaper.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP additional language learning builds oral confidence without external assessment, and for Spanish in Dubai it is less commonly offered than French or Arabic. Where it exists, the measurable outcome at this stage is willingness to speak and basic listening comprehension, neither of which should be dressed up as Diploma Programme preparation.
programmes.countryNote: For families planning ahead, the useful observation is that Spanish started in primary school in Dubai usually means a comfortable Spanish B Higher Level candidate eight years later, while Spanish started in Year 10 usually means ab initio. The route follows the start date more reliably than it follows aptitude.

dubai/ib-spanish-tutor.subjectsIntro: Spanish requests from Dubai families usually come packaged with another subject, and the pairings matter for scheduling because written deadlines cluster in the same weeks.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: Five prescribed themes, a writing task in a specified text type, a receptive paper covering listening and reading, and an individual oral, with two literary works at Higher Level. Measurable weaknesses cluster in ser and estar, past tense choice, agreement and avoidance of the subjunctive.

subjects.name: Spanish ab initio
subjects.description: For genuine beginners, with a defined vocabulary and narrower themes. The same three components in simplified form. The measurable risk here is a student with prior Spanish hitting the course ceiling early and losing interest, which shows up as static written marks.

subjects.name: Spanish A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Group 1 course for students whose best language is Spanish, studying literary and non-literary texts. Dubai students from Spanish-speaking households are sometimes placed in Spanish B, where they score well without learning and lose a university-relevant qualification.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Carried alongside Spanish by most Dubai students, since the emirate's private schools must teach Arabic regardless of curriculum. Two languages in one week means written load collides, and an error log for each prevents the two sets of mistakes blurring together.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: Occasionally taken alongside Spanish. The assessment architecture is identical, so technique transfers completely and a single record-keeping system covers both, which is more efficient than running two separate plans.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The text-type analysis overlaps directly with the Spanish writing task. A student who can name the conventions of a persuasive text in English applies the same framework in Spanish once the vocabulary exists, which is faster than learning the conventions twice.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Supplies substance for the oral conversation phase, where candidates with opinions outperform candidates with accuracy and nothing to say. Students studying twentieth-century history have material for the social organisation theme in particular.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Supports the sharing the planet and social organisation themes with studied content rather than general awareness. The measurable effect appears in oral recordings as longer stretches of speech before a filler.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frequently paired by Dubai students planning commerce degrees in Spain or Latin America. Useful for the human ingenuity theme, and the shared habit of writing to a specified format transfers to the Spanish text-type task.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Relevant to the Higher Level literary works, where a response is required rather than a summary. The TOK habit of questioning an interpretation shows up measurably as fewer plot-retelling seconds in a recorded oral.

sections.heading: Four short tasks that set a Spanish baseline in an hour
paragraphs: Measurement needs a starting point, and a conversation is a poor one. A confident student with a good accent sounds stronger than they are; a careful student who is shy sounds weaker. Four short tasks done cold in a single hour produce a baseline that is specific enough to plan from and quick enough that nobody minds doing it.

The first task is a piece of timed writing in a specified text type, short enough to mark in ten minutes. It reveals three things at once: control of tense and agreement, whether the student knows what the text type requires, and how fast they write under pressure. The second is a listening passage from a past paper at natural speed with its questions, which gives the only raw score available in the whole subject.

The third is a two-minute recorded response to an image, which establishes the oral baseline with countable features rather than impressions. The fourth is a short reading passage with comprehension questions, which separates a vocabulary problem from a question-reading problem. Together they take about an hour and they sort the student into one of four useful categories.

The categories matter because they point at different work. A student with strong writing and weak listening needs audio at speed, not grammar. A student with accurate language and poor conventions needs an afternoon on text types and nothing else. A student whose recorded oral is all description needs timing discipline. And a student who struggles with all four may be in the wrong route, which is a conversation with the school rather than a tutoring purchase.

sections.heading: The error log: five categories that cover most Spanish mistakes
paragraphs: English-speaking learners of Spanish make a small number of errors repeatedly, and the value of logging them is that the pattern becomes visible to the student rather than only to the teacher. Five categories cover the great majority, and a log with five headings is simple enough that a student will actually maintain it.

The first is the choice between ser and estar, where English offers no distinction and students default to whichever they learned first. The second is past tense selection between preterite and imperfect, which is a question about how the speaker frames an event rather than about when it happened, and which no amount of rule-learning fixes without practice on real sentences. The third is gender and number agreement, where errors are mechanical and high-frequency and therefore cheap to eliminate.

The fourth is prepositions, dominated by por against para but including the smaller traps around a and en. The fifth is the subjunctive, where the characteristic error is not misuse but avoidance: students restructure sentences to escape it, which costs the complexity marks their language level would otherwise earn. Avoidance is invisible in conversation and obvious in a written log, which is precisely why the log is worth keeping.

What makes this measurable is counting. Each session, the number of new entries in each category goes down on paper. A category that keeps growing after four weeks of targeted work is a sign the approach is wrong, not that the student is careless. A category that stops growing is finished, and the sessions should move on. That is a decision procedure a parent can audit without speaking a word of Spanish.

sections.heading: Marking written work twice, and why one mark hides the truth
paragraphs: A single mark on a Spanish writing task tells a student almost nothing useful, because two independent things are being judged. One is language: accuracy, range, control of tense and mood. The other is whether the response behaves like the text type it was supposed to be, with the right register, the right opening and closing, the right layout. Those two improve at completely different speeds.

Conventions move fast. A student who learns that an article needs a headline, that a formal letter needs a matched salutation and sign-off, that a set of instructions needs sequenced imperatives, picks up marks within two weeks. Language moves slowly, over months, because it depends on accumulated exposure and corrected practice. Combine them into one number and a student who has fixed their conventions sees a mark that barely moved and concludes nothing is working.

Marking twice makes both visible. On a two-column record, the conventions column should rise quickly and then plateau near the top, and the language column should creep up. If the conventions column is not moving after three tasks, the student is not applying feedback, which is a different problem from a language problem and needs a different conversation. If language is static over a term while conventions are maxed out, the sessions should shift towards reading volume and the error log.

This is also where a non-Spanish-speaking parent gets purchase. The conventions mark can be explained in plain English: did the piece have a headline, was the register right, was it the length asked for. A parent can check that against the script themselves. The language mark they have to trust, but the conventions mark they can verify, and a provider whose conventions marks never move is telling you something.

sections.heading: Counting what a recorded oral shows
paragraphs: The individual oral is the component families worry about most and measure least. A rehearsal is held, the tutor says it went well, and nobody can compare it with the one three weeks earlier. Recording solves that, and the four features worth counting are simple enough that a student can count them on their own playback.

Description time is the first. In the visual-stimulus task at Standard Level and ab initio, candidates must describe and then discuss, and the overwhelming failure is a thorough description that consumes the time available. Counting the seconds before the first genuinely discursive sentence turns that into a number, and the number falls with practice in a way that feels like nothing at all in the moment.

Fillers are the second: the sounds and phrases a student uses while thinking. The aim is not elimination, since fluent speakers use them, but awareness, because a student who hears forty of them in two minutes will reduce them without being told how. Completed self-corrections are the third and most encouraging: a student who starts a correction and finishes it is monitoring their own output, which is exactly what the assessment rewards, and the count usually rises as the others fall.

The fourth is complex structures attempted, which catches avoidance. A student who never attempts a subjunctive, a conditional or a relative clause in two minutes is speaking well below their knowledge. Counting attempts, including failed ones, rewards the risk-taking the mark scheme rewards. Two recordings six weeks apart, with those four counts written beside them, is a progress report that needs no language expertise to read.

sections.heading: Listening: the one number in the subject, and how to use it
paragraphs: Everything else in Spanish B requires judgement to assess. Listening does not. Past-paper listening sections have answers, a student can sit one in fifteen minutes, and the result is a raw score that can be written in a list. For an evidence-led plan this is the most valuable property available anywhere in the course, and almost nobody exploits it.

The method is unglamorous. One listening section a week, at natural speed, under proper conditions with the audio played the permitted number of times and no pausing. Score it, write the score down, and note which question types were missed: gist, specific detail, inference, numbers. Over eight weeks a line of scores appears, and that line either rises or it does not.

What makes the scores move is usually technique rather than vocabulary. Students lose clusters of marks after one unknown word triggers panic, so they miss the following sentences too. They fail to note numbers, names and negations, which are exactly what questions turn on and what memory distorts first. They answer from a half-heard phrase rather than from the question asked. Each of those is correctable in a session and then confirmed by the next score.

There is a Dubai-specific point here. Spanish-language audio is freely available and a student with a thirty-minute school commute has an hour a day of listening opportunity they are currently spending on something else. Four commutes a week of unsimplified Spanish, not comprehended fully, does more for the receptive paper than any amount of structured conversation. The scores confirm it within a month, which makes the habit easier to sustain than instruction alone.

sections.heading: Dubai's mock window as the validation point
paragraphs: Every measurement system needs an external check, and Dubai schools provide one. Mock examinations run across a window from roughly late November to February depending on the school, and they are marked by teachers against the real criteria. That makes a mock the one point where a tutor's internal record meets an independent judgement.

The right use of a mock is comparison rather than celebration or panic. If the error log shows agreement errors clearing and the mock script shows agreement errors throughout, the log is not being maintained honestly. If the recorded orals show description time falling and the mock oral mark is unchanged, something in the rehearsal is not transferring to the real task. Those are useful findings and they only appear if a record existed beforehand.

The second right use is re-aiming. A mock script names the components where marks were actually lost, which may not be the components the tutoring targeted. A student whose writing improved and whose listening collapsed should have their sessions redirected, and that decision is easier to make against a record than against an impression. Families who start in October have time to act on it; families who start in March do not.

Keep the scripts. Dubai schools return mock papers, students mislay them within a week, and they are the most informative document produced in the two years. A marked mock with teacher annotations, read alongside the error log and the task sequence, usually makes the next six weeks of work obvious without any further diagnosis.

sections.heading: What a six-week record should show, and when to stop paying
paragraphs: Open-ended tutoring is the expensive pattern in every market, and it survives because nobody can tell when the work is finished. A record makes stopping possible. Six weeks is the right review interval for Spanish: long enough for conventions and oral features to move, short enough that a wrong plan is caught before a term is lost.

At six weeks, four things should be visible. New entries in the targeted error category should have slowed noticeably. The conventions mark on written tasks should be at or near the top of its range. The oral recordings should show less description time, more completed self-corrections and more complex structures attempted. And the weekly listening scores should form a line that is rising rather than flat.

If three of those four have moved, the plan is working and the sessions should continue with a new target category. If one or none has moved, something is wrong, and the honest options are a different approach, a different tutor, or a conclusion that the student is not doing the work between sessions, which no tutor can fix by being paid more. Saying that out loud is uncomfortable and it is the reason a record exists.

If all four have moved and the student has run out of target categories, the work is done. That is a real outcome and it should end the engagement rather than converting into a standing weekly slot. A short block before the mock window and another before the May session is a better use of a Dubai family's money than eighteen months of continuous sessions with nothing being measured.

sections.heading: Delivery, rates and the Dubai market for a minority language
paragraphs: Spanish is a smaller Group 2 option than French or Arabic in most Dubai schools, and that has a supply consequence that matters more than price. The number of people in or near the emirate who have taught Spanish B Higher Level, including the two literary works and the extract-based oral, is small. Published rate bands do not rise in the exam term, but availability does narrow, which makes early booking worth more than negotiation.

The published Dubai bands are the same as for any subject. A qualified online subject tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above on Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. Unitors lists IB from AED 200 and TutorChase quotes AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate with market home tutors at AED 200 to 500. At the floor, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65.

For a record-based approach there is a practical argument for a screen beyond cost. The error log, the dated task sequence and the oral recordings all need to live somewhere both parties can reach between sessions, and a shared folder does that while a ring binder in a teenager's bedroom does not. The recordings in particular are difficult to make routinely in someone's living room and trivial over video.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. Spanish support for Dubai families runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school day, mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons, activities and prayer times. The free trial session is the right place to run the four baseline tasks and see whether the record-keeping actually happens.

process.title: Run the four baseline tasks
process.description: A timed written task, a past-paper listening section, a two-minute recorded oral and a short reading passage, all cold. One hour, and it sorts the student into a category that points at specific work rather than at general improvement.

process.title: Start the error log with five headings
process.description: Tense choice, agreement, ser and estar, prepositions and mood. The student maintains it, adds the correction and the date, and brings it to every session. It belongs to them and it travels with them after the sessions end.

process.title: Pick one target category and a date
process.description: One category, six weeks, with the measurement agreed in advance: fewer new entries, conventions mark near maximum, oral features moving, listening scores rising. Narrow targets are the only kind anyone can check.

process.title: Run short sessions over live video
process.description: Two shorter slots a week rather than one long block, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the Dubai school day, mandatory Arabic lessons and activities. Language learning rewards frequency, and nobody has a journey to make.

process.title: Review at six weeks and decide honestly
process.description: Three of four measures moving means continue with a new target. One or none means change the approach, change the tutor, or accept that the work between sessions is not happening. Running on without that review is how families overspend.

whyPoints.title: A record a non-Spanish-speaking parent can read
whyPoints.description: An error log by category, written tasks marked in two columns, oral recordings with four counted features, and a weekly listening score. None of that requires the parent to speak Spanish to audit it.

whyPoints.title: No invented statistics
whyPoints.description: There are no percentage improvement claims, satisfaction scores or cohort averages on this page, because a figure without the number of students, the date and the method behind it is not evidence. Several ranking competitors publish exactly those.

whyPoints.title: Listening treated as the measurable skill
whyPoints.description: Past-paper listening sections give the only raw score in the subject. One a week, written down, under proper conditions, produces a line that either rises or does not, which is worth more than any impression of progress.

whyPoints.title: Written work marked twice
whyPoints.description: Conventions and language move at different speeds, and one combined mark hides both. Two columns show which half is improving, and the conventions column is the one a parent can verify against the script themselves.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end
whyPoints.description: Six-week review intervals with an agreed measurement, and a genuine willingness to say that the work is finished or that the plan is not working. Open-ended monthly sessions with no record is the pattern we would rather you did not buy.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: One-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the log, the task sequence and the recordings in one shared place. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether Spanish tutoring is improving my child's marks?
faqs.answer: Ask for four records. An error log the student maintains, by category, with corrections and dates. Written tasks marked in two columns, one for language and one for text-type conventions, kept in order. Oral rehearsals recorded every two or three weeks with four counted features. And a weekly past-paper listening score written in a list. After six weeks those four either show movement or they do not, and a parent who speaks no Spanish can read three of them without help.

faqs.question: What should go in a Spanish error log?
faqs.answer: Five categories cover most of what English-speaking learners get wrong: the choice between ser and estar, past tense selection between preterite and imperfect, gender and number agreement, prepositions led by por against para, and the subjunctive. The student adds each instance with the correction and the date. The value is that the pattern becomes visible to them rather than only to the teacher, and that the number of new entries per category can be counted session by session.

faqs.question: Why record my child's Spanish oral rehearsals?
faqs.answer: Because it converts an impression into four numbers. Count the seconds spent describing before any discussion begins, the fillers used, the self-corrections actually completed, and the complex structures attempted including failed attempts. All four move measurably over six weeks, and two recordings played back to back are readable by a parent in any language. Students also reduce fillers and description time simply by hearing themselves, which no amount of being told achieves.

faqs.question: Is avoidance of the subjunctive a real problem in Spanish B?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the error most easily missed. Students who are uncertain about the subjunctive restructure sentences to avoid needing it, which produces accurate Spanish that scores below the student's actual knowledge because the complexity marks are never attempted. Avoidance is invisible in conversation, where the listener only hears what was said. It shows up in a written log and in a counted oral recording, which is the main argument for keeping both rather than relying on correction in the moment.

faqs.question: Does anyone come to our home in Dubai for Spanish lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Spanish support for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a record-based approach this helps: the error log, the dated written tasks and the oral recordings all live in one shared place both parties can reach, rather than in loose paper and a notebook that is somewhere in the house by March.

faqs.question: How do I practise Spanish listening if there is no mark scheme at home?
faqs.answer: Use past-paper listening sections, which do come with answers. One a week, at natural speed, with the audio played only the permitted number of times and no pausing, scored and written down. That gives the only raw number available anywhere in the course. Note which question types were missed, because the pattern is usually technique rather than vocabulary: panic after an unknown word, numbers and negations not noted, or answers given from a half-heard phrase instead of the question asked.

faqs.question: My child is in Spanish B but speaks Spanish at home. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It may be. Students whose best language is Spanish belong in Spanish A, the Group 1 course, which studies literary and non-literary texts in Spanish and carries more weight for applications to Spanish-speaking destinations. A near-native student in Spanish B will score highly without learning much, which looks like success and wastes two years. Raise it with the school in the first term of DP1, supported by the four baseline tasks rather than by an impression, because a route change later is usually impossible.

faqs.question: Why mark a Spanish writing task twice instead of giving one grade?
faqs.answer: Because two independent things are being judged and they improve at different speeds. Text-type conventions, meaning register, layout, salutations, headlines and length, improve within two weeks once a student knows them. Language accuracy and range improve over months. A single combined mark that barely moves tells a student who has fixed their conventions that nothing is working. Two columns show which half moved, and the conventions column is one a parent can check against the script themselves.

faqs.question: What should six weeks of Spanish sessions have changed?
faqs.answer: Four things should be visible. New entries in the targeted error category should have slowed noticeably. The conventions mark on written tasks should be at or near the top of its range. The oral recordings should show less description time, more completed self-corrections and more complex structures attempted. And the weekly listening scores should form a rising line. Three of four moving means continue with a new target. One or none moving means the approach, the tutor, or the work between sessions needs to change.

faqs.question: How should we use a Spanish mock result in Dubai?
faqs.answer: As a check on the internal record rather than as a verdict. If the error log shows agreement errors clearing and the mock script is full of them, the log is not honest. If recorded orals show improvement and the mock oral mark is static, the rehearsal is not transferring. Both findings are useful and both require a record to have existed first. Keep the marked scripts: Dubai schools return them, students mislay them within a week, and they are the most informative document of the two years.

faqs.question: Is Spanish harder to find a tutor for in Dubai than French?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, because it is a smaller Group 2 option in most schools here, so fewer local teachers specialise in it. Published rate bands do not differ by subject, but the pool of people who have taught Spanish B Higher Level including the two literary works and the extract-based oral is thin. Rates do not rise in the exam term; availability narrows. A family looking in October has a choice of specialists and the same family in February has whatever is left.

faqs.question: How often should Spanish sessions happen?
faqs.answer: Two shorter sessions a week usually beat one long one, because language gains come from frequency of contact rather than from duration, and concentration for listening and oral work fades well before ninety minutes. That pattern is practical over video and awkward for a tutor who has to drive across the emirate twice a week, which is one of the quieter ways the in-home model pushes families towards a session shape that suits the logistics rather than the subject.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Higher Level Spanish literary works?
faqs.answer: Yes, by pointing the student back at the text rather than around it. A tutor can explain what the extract-based oral requires, select passages the student has not seen and ask for a two-minute response, and show the difference between summarising an extract and responding to it. What a tutor should not do is supply a summary that substitutes for reading, or reproduce copyrighted material. The conversation phase exposes a student who prepared from a study guide, usually within the first question.

faqs.question: Do Spanish tutors in the UAE need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time via its smart app, website and e-services system, and warns that tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties.

faqs.question: What if no Spanish Higher Level specialist is available when we ask?
faqs.answer: We say so and name what we can offer instead. The options are a start date in the future, a tutor who can work on writing, listening and the error log while a route-specific match is found, or a recommendation to wait until after the mock window when demand eases. Families should know which of those is on the table. No competitor page found in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all, so silence about availability is worth reading as a warning rather than as reassurance.

dubai/ib-spanish-tutor.closingBody: Book the free trial session and spend it on the four baseline tasks: a timed written piece, a past-paper listening section, a two-minute recorded oral and a short reading passage. That hour produces a specific starting point, a target category for the error log, and a date six weeks out to check it against. From then on the record does the arguing, which means you never have to take anyone's word for whether the sessions are working. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are not part of our UAE service.

dubai/ib-subject-selection-guidance.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the Diploma subjects families most often weigh against each other, so the advice comes from people who mark the papers rather than from a brochure. The school's own coordinator remains the authority on what the timetable allows.

intro.heading: The cheapest decision in the Diploma, and the most expensive to get wrong
paragraphs: Subject selection is a two-hour conversation that governs two years. A student who takes Higher Level Chemistry because a friend did, and spends DP1 and DP2 at a grade 4 in it, has paid for that choice in a way no tutoring budget can recover. A student who drops Mathematics Analysis and Approaches without checking their intended degree's prerequisites may find the door to engineering closed before they have applied. Both outcomes are common in Dubai, and both are avoidable in an afternoon.

Put the money side by side. Published Dubai tutoring rates read in October 2026 run AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists, with one premium provider at AED 650. Two or three sessions of selection guidance therefore sit in the low hundreds to around a thousand dirhams. A year of weekly support in a Higher Level subject the student should never have taken sits, on Bestimate's own Dubai monthly estimates, at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above per month for specialist exam-year work. The ratio is not close.

What selection guidance actually does is narrow. It maps the student's marked evidence from MYP or IGCSE against the six Diploma groups, checks the intended university destinations for prerequisites, and tests the resulting combination against what the school's timetable can actually deliver. Those three steps produce a shortlist and, more usefully, a list of the combinations that will not work and why.

The Dubai-specific layer matters more than families expect. Not every Dubai school offers every subject, and those that do often block them against each other on the timetable, so a theoretically ideal combination can be impossible in practice. Schools also differ in which Mathematics routes they run and at which levels. The coordinator and the published options booklet are the authority on this, and the honest sequence is to ask them first and then take the real constraints into a guidance conversation. Ask for the current options booklet and the timetable block structure in the same email, because a subject list without its blocks tells a family nothing about which pairs are genuinely available together. Where a wanted combination turns out to be blocked, the two realistic fixes are a different level in one subject or a different Mathematics route, and both are easier to weigh before the option form is signed than after.

All of our UAE sessions run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For this work the format matters because the people worth asking are subject teachers for the specific courses under consideration, and online delivery means a Dubai family can speak to a Chemistry HL specialist and a Mathematics AA specialist in the same week.

dubai/ib-subject-selection-guidance.programmesIntro: The choice is made at a specific point in a Dubai school career, and what comes before it determines how much evidence there is to decide on.

programmes.name: Choosing from MYP Year 5
programmes.description: Students in Dubai schools running MYP to Year 11 choose Diploma subjects on criterion-referenced evidence rather than examination grades. That makes the choice harder to ground, because MYP levels do not convert simply into expected Diploma grades.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students also arrive in DP1 without timed-paper experience, which depresses their first DP1 marks regardless of subject fit. Families should separate the two effects when judging a choice, because a weak first term in Higher Level Physics may be exam technique rather than evidence the subject was wrong.

programmes.name: Choosing from IGCSE
programmes.description: The commonest route in Dubai, and the one with the most usable evidence. IGCSE marks by component, with the tier the student sat, give a reasonable signal: a student who needed the Extended tier's easier questions to reach a grade 6 is being told something about Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: The clearest single predictor we see for Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches in Dubai is whether the student sat Additional Mathematics 0606 or Further Pure 4PM1. Not having done so is not disqualifying, but it usually means a bridging block before DP1 rather than a surprise in the first term.

programmes.name: Changing during DP1
programmes.description: Changes are possible early in DP1 and get harder as the year proceeds, because content accumulates and registration deadlines approach. A level change from Higher to Standard is usually easier than a subject change, and both are administrative decisions owned by the school.
programmes.countryNote: The practical Dubai window for a comfortable change is the first term of DP1, and the decisive conversation is with the coordinator rather than the subject teacher. Families who wait for the DP1 end-of-year results to confirm what October already suggested have usually lost the easy option.

programmes.name: Core components in the decision
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is written in one subject, Theory of Knowledge runs across all of them, and CAS is a completion requirement. The Extended Essay subject should be part of the selection conversation, because it is far easier in a subject the student enjoys reading in.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students frequently choose an Extended Essay subject late and badly, picking a Higher Level science because it feels serious and then struggling to find a researchable question. Thinking about it at selection time costs nothing and prevents a difficult DP1 spring.

dubai/ib-subject-selection-guidance.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects Dubai families weigh most often, with what each actually demands rather than how it sounds.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic and analytic route, expected by most engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics programmes. At Higher Level it is the heaviest single commitment in most timetables, and proof is the part students have practised least.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, accepted by many business, social science and design programmes. A genuine fit for students who reason well with data, and a mistake for anyone whose target degree names the other course.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Required for most medicine and many life-science routes, and the Higher Level course carries a heavy content load. The commonest Dubai selection error is taking it at Higher Level without checking whether the target degree asks for it.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and precision-dependent rather than conceptually difficult. Suits students who can hold detailed terminology accurately; the marks go on command terms and specific wording rather than on broad understanding.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mathematically demanding at Higher Level, and a poor pairing with Standard Level Mathematics for most students. If Physics HL is on the list, the Mathematics choice has to be considered in the same breath.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A frequent Dubai choice and often a good one. Rewards clear evaluative writing and accurate diagrams. Students expecting a numerical subject are sometimes surprised by how much of the grade is written argument.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study based and accessible, but it rewards applying tools to evidence rather than reciting them. Rarely a prerequisite for anything, which makes it a useful sixth subject rather than a Higher Level anchor.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Group 1 for most Dubai students. The Higher Level course adds a written essay and more texts, and it suits students who already read widely. Taking it at Higher Level for prestige is a common and costly error.

subjects.name: Language B: French, Spanish, Arabic
subjects.description: Level choice matters more here than in any other group. A student placed at Higher Level on the strength of a conversational background can struggle with the written and oral demands, and the reverse wastes a capable linguist's points.

subjects.name: Visual Arts, Music and Theatre
subjects.description: Group 6 options with substantial coursework and exhibition or performance requirements spread across both years. Workload is front-loaded differently from examined subjects, which changes how the overall timetable feels in DP2.

dubai/ib-subject-selection-guidance.regionsIntro: What a student can choose depends on where they study, because option availability and timetable blocking differ school by school across the emirate.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Large Diploma cohorts, so option blocks are usually wide and most combinations are deliverable. Questions here are about prerequisites for competitive overseas courses rather than availability.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Science Park
regions.note: Several Diploma schools within a short radius offering different subject menus. Families comparing schools at Year 11 should compare options booklets rather than reputations.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer cohorts where some Group 6 and Language B options may run only if numbers allow. Confirm with the coordinator before building a combination around them.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Many students arrive from IGCSE, so there is good marked evidence to base a choice on. The commonest issue is Mathematics route selection rather than subject availability.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Mudon

sections.heading: The six groups, and what each one actually asks of a student
paragraphs: The Diploma takes one subject from each of the first five groups and a sixth from either Group 6 or a second subject from an earlier group, with three taken at Higher Level and three at Standard. That structure is deliberately broad, and it means a student cannot assemble six subjects purely from their strengths. The skill in selection is choosing well inside the constraints rather than wishing them away.

Each group makes a different demand, and the demands are not interchangeable. Group 1 asks for sustained analytical writing about texts. Group 2 asks for productive language use under time, including orals. Group 3 asks for evaluative argument supported by evidence or diagrams. Group 4 asks for precision and, in Physics, for mathematics. Group 5 is either algebraic or statistical depending on the route. Group 6 asks for sustained coursework and a public outcome.

Where Dubai families most often go wrong is treating the Higher Levels as a ranking of prestige rather than a match to demand. Three Higher Level sciences is a popular Dubai combination and a poor one for most students, because it loads three content-heavy subjects with three Internal Assessments into the same months. A student aiming at medicine needs specific subjects, not the maximum number of difficult ones, and the specific list is shorter than the instinctive one.

The table below sets out the groups with the demand each makes and the pitfall we see most often in Dubai cohorts. Read the right-hand column as a diagnostic: if the pitfall describes your child's reasoning, the choice is being made on the wrong basis and that is worth an hour to fix now.

sections.heading: Choosing the three Higher Levels
paragraphs: Three Higher Levels is where the real decision sits, because Higher Level is where the workload and the university prerequisites live. The sequence that works is: start from the destination, then the evidence, then the enjoyment, and only then the timetable. Reversing that order is how students end up with a combination that looks balanced and serves nothing.

Start with destination because prerequisites are non-negotiable and vary. Medicine routes typically name Chemistry and often Biology at Higher Level. Engineering routes typically name Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Physics. Economics programmes vary widely, with some naming Mathematics at Higher Level and others accepting either route at Standard. Those requirements are published by each institution and should be read from the institution's own page rather than from a summary, including this one.

Then test against the evidence. A student with a grade 6 at IGCSE in a subject they found hard is not usually a Higher Level candidate in it, and a student who reached a 9 comfortably probably is. Component-level marks help: a Chemistry grade built on strong recall and weak calculation predicts difficulty in Higher Level Chemistry, where the calculation load rises. This is exactly the reading a subject specialist can do in twenty minutes and a brochure cannot do at all.

Enjoyment matters third, and it matters genuinely: two years is a long time in a subject a student dislikes, and the Extended Essay is far easier in a subject they want to read about. Timetable comes last because it is a constraint rather than a preference, but it can still override everything, which is why the school's option blocks should be in hand before a shortlist becomes a decision.

sections.heading: University prerequisites, including inside the UAE
paragraphs: Prerequisite checking is the part of selection that families most often do late, and it is the only part with hard edges. Every university publishes its own requirements, and they differ not only between countries but between programmes in the same institution. The rule we give Dubai families is simple: read the requirement on the admitting institution's own page, for the specific programme, and write it down with the date you read it.

The Mathematics route is the decision most often caught out by this. Many quantitative degrees name Analysis and Approaches specifically, while others accept either course, and some accept Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level where they would not accept it at Standard. A student who chooses the route for comfort in Year 11 can discover in DP2 that the course they want is unavailable to them, and at that point the only remedies are changing the target or adding a year.

For students intending to study in the UAE, there is a separate administrative layer that is not an admissions requirement but is frequently confused with one. Ministry of Education equivalency is the process by which a non-UAE school certificate is recognised here. On the British track the published requirements, as reported in July 2026, are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so no IB equivalency figure should be quoted without a Ministry page behind it.

Two cautions belong with that. Equivalency is a Ministry process that no tutoring provider performs, influences or guarantees, and tutoring is not required for it. And admission and equivalency are different gates: a student can satisfy one and not the other. Ask the admitting institution about admission and the Ministry's own channel about equivalency, and do both before the Diploma choice is finalised rather than after.

sections.heading: What your Dubai school's timetable will actually allow
paragraphs: A combination that passes every other test can still be undeliverable. Dubai schools build option blocks, placing subjects in parallel columns, and a student can take only one subject from each block. Two subjects a student wants may sit in the same column, in which case one of them has to go whatever the prerequisites say. This is not a flaw in the school; it is arithmetic about teacher numbers and room availability.

Smaller Diploma cohorts add a second constraint. A subject may be listed in an options booklet and run only if enough students choose it, which means a provisional choice can disappear in September. In practice this most often affects Group 6 arts subjects, less common Language B options, and Higher Level routes in subjects with small uptake. Ask the coordinator which options are guaranteed and which are conditional on numbers.

The third constraint is level availability. Not every Dubai school runs both Mathematics courses at both levels, and some run Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level only or Applications and Interpretation at Standard only. For a student whose target degree names a specific route, that can be decisive, and in a small number of cases it is a reason to consider a different school at the Diploma entry point rather than to compromise the degree plan.

The practical sequence is therefore: get the options booklet and the block structure, ask which options are conditional, confirm the Mathematics routes offered at each level, and then shortlist. Families who shortlist first and check later spend a fortnight attached to a combination that was never available, which is a specifically Dubai frustration given how much the option menus differ between schools a few kilometres apart.

sections.heading: What selection guidance costs, against what a wrong choice costs
paragraphs: This is the only decision in the Diploma where the cost comparison is genuinely one-sided, so it is worth setting out in figures. Published Dubai market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, not ours, and they are the market for an hour of specialist time.

Selection guidance is two or three such hours, sometimes with a short taster session in each of two subjects. Set that against the alternative. A student in the wrong Higher Level subject typically buys weekly support in it, which on Bestimate's Dubai monthly estimates is AED 600 to 1,200 a month in the mid band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Over eighteen months of DP1 and DP2, that is an order of magnitude more than the guidance would have cost, and it does not fix the underlying mismatch.

There is a second cost that does not appear on an invoice. A wrong Higher Level choice consumes the student's capacity across all six subjects, because the subject they are struggling with takes the hours the others needed. Families often notice the effect as a general decline in DP2 rather than as a problem in one subject, which is why the diagnosis is frequently made late and why the choice is worth getting right rather than fixing.

The honest limit on what guidance can do: it cannot tell you what grade a student will achieve, and it cannot promise a university place. What it can do is prevent the two specific errors that are expensive and irreversible: a combination that fails a prerequisite, and a Higher Level the marked evidence never supported. Both are identifiable in an hour, and neither is identifiable from a prospectus.

sections.heading: The four selection mistakes we see most in Dubai
paragraphs: The first is three Higher Level sciences. It is a popular Dubai combination, chosen because it signals seriousness, and it loads three content-heavy courses with three Internal Assessments into the same months of DP2. Very few degrees require it. A student aiming at medicine needs the named subjects, usually Chemistry and often Biology, not the maximum quantity of difficult ones.

The second is choosing the Mathematics route for comfort. Applications and Interpretation is a real and demanding course, not an easier version of Analysis and Approaches, but it is not accepted everywhere Analysis and Approaches is. Choosing it without reading the target programme's requirement is the single most common irreversible error in this decision, because the content diverges early and a late switch is rarely practical.

The third is the Language B level, set by family background rather than by written ability. A student who speaks a language at home may be placed at Higher Level and then struggle with the written components and the formal oral, while a capable classroom linguist placed at Standard Level gives away points they could have earned. Ask the language department for a view based on written work rather than conversation.

The fourth is treating Group 6 as unserious. An arts subject with coursework spread across two years can balance a timetable better than a third examined science, because its workload sits differently and it offers a genuinely different kind of assessment. Dismissing it in favour of a subject the student does not need is a choice made for how the combination reads rather than for how the two years will go.

sections.heading: When the choice can still be changed, and who decides
paragraphs: Changes are possible and they get harder with time. The easiest window is before the Diploma starts, when a choice is still a form rather than a timetable. The next easiest is the first term of DP1, when content has not accumulated far and the school can usually reorganise. After that, a level change from Higher to Standard remains more feasible than a subject change for longer, because the course content overlaps.

The decision belongs to the school. A coordinator weighs timetable capacity, teaching groups, registration deadlines and the student's evidence, and no outside provider influences that. What a family can do is arrive with the right information: marked work showing the pattern, a clear statement of the destination requirement, and a specific request. A vague concern produces a reassuring conversation; a marked paper and a named prerequisite produce a decision.

Timing matters in a way that catches Dubai families out. Registration deadlines for the examination session sit months ahead of the papers, and the administrative window for a change closes well before the academic case for one becomes obvious. If a Higher Level subject is clearly wrong in October of DP1, that is the month to raise it, not after the DP1 end-of-year examinations confirm what October already showed.

One honest caution about the alternative. A level change is not failure and it frequently improves the overall points total, because the capacity it frees is spent across the other five subjects. Families sometimes resist it for reasons that have nothing to do with the Diploma, and the result is two years of strain and a lower total than a Standard Level entry would have produced.

sections.heading: Starting a selection conversation
paragraphs: Bring four things: the student's most recent marked work with component marks if available, the school's options booklet and block structure, a list of intended destinations or at least course families, and any prerequisite requirements already written down with their source. With those, a single session produces a shortlist and a list of what will not work.

We will tell you when the answer is already clear and no sessions are needed. That happens often: a student with strong marked evidence, a clear destination with published requirements, and a school with wide option blocks usually has an obvious combination, and the useful output is confirmation plus two questions for the coordinator rather than a paid programme.

The taster option exists for the genuinely close calls, which in Dubai are most often Chemistry against Physics, Economics against Business Management, and the two Mathematics routes. An hour of real course content with a specialist in each resolves more than weeks of family discussion, because the student experiences the demand rather than imagining it. The specialists are asked for an honest view on fit, including when the answer is that neither is a good match.

The trial lesson is free with no condition beyond booking a time. Whatever is decided, the authority on what the school can deliver is the coordinator, and the authority on what a university requires is that university's own admissions page. Our role is to read the marked evidence against the course demands and to say plainly what the evidence supports, which is the one part of this decision that needs a subject teacher rather than a brochure.

process.title: Get the options booklet and block structure
process.description: Ask the coordinator which subjects run at which levels, which are conditional on numbers, and how the option blocks are arranged. A combination that cannot be timetabled is not a shortlist, however well it fits on paper.

process.title: Test the shortlist in order
process.description: Prerequisite, then marked evidence, then workload shape, then enjoyment, then availability and blocking. Reversing that order produces combinations that look balanced and serve no destination.

process.title: Take the questions back to the coordinator
process.description: The school owns the decision. Arriving with marked work, a named prerequisite and a specific request produces a decision; arriving with a general concern produces a reassuring conversation and no change.

whyPoints.title: Costed against the alternative
whyPoints.description: Two or three specialist hours at published market rates against eighteen months of weekly support in a mismatched Higher Level. We set both figures out with their source so the comparison is visible rather than asserted.

whyPoints.title: Prerequisites before preferences
whyPoints.description: The only hard edges in this decision are published admissions requirements, and they differ programme by programme. We work from the institution's own page and tell families to record the date they read it.

whyPoints.title: Marked evidence read by a subject specialist
whyPoints.description: Component-level marks predict Higher Level difficulty in ways a grade does not. A Chemistry 6 built on recall rather than calculation is a different signal, and reading that takes a teacher rather than a brochure.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what your school can deliver
whyPoints.description: Option blocks, conditional subjects and which Mathematics routes run at which levels decide what is possible. We build the shortlist after those constraints rather than presenting an ideal combination that cannot be timetabled.
