whyPoints.description: Where the evidence, the destination and the option blocks all point one way, the useful output is confirmation and two questions for the coordinator. That conversation is short and we are willing to have it.

faqs.question: How are IB subjects chosen, and how much freedom is there?
faqs.answer: The Diploma takes one subject from each of the first five groups, with a sixth from the arts or a second subject from an earlier group, and three subjects are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard. That structure is deliberately broad, so a student cannot build six subjects purely from their strengths. The freedom lies in which subject within each group, and at which level. Real freedom is further limited by what your school offers and by how its option blocks are arranged, which is why the options booklet matters as much as the ideal combination.

faqs.question: Should my child take three Higher Level sciences?
faqs.answer: Usually not. It is a popular Dubai combination chosen because it signals seriousness, and it loads three content-heavy courses with three Internal Assessments into the same months of DP2. Very few degrees require it. Medicine routes typically name Chemistry at Higher Level and often Biology; engineering routes name Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Physics. The requirement is specific subjects, not the maximum quantity of difficult ones, and the student's capacity is finite across all six subjects rather than per subject.

faqs.question: Which Mathematics route should we pick for engineering or economics?
faqs.answer: Read the requirement on the admitting institution's own page for the specific programme, because this is the decision most often caught out. Many quantitative degrees name Analysis and Approaches specifically; some accept either course; a few accept Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level where they would not at Standard. Content diverges early, so a late switch is rarely practical. Write down what you find with the date you read it, and check each target programme separately rather than assuming a pattern across a country.

faqs.question: What evidence should a Higher Level choice be based on?
faqs.answer: Marked work at component level rather than an overall grade. A grade 6 in IGCSE Chemistry built on strong recall and weak calculation predicts difficulty in Higher Level Chemistry, where the calculation load rises; the same grade built the other way predicts the opposite. The tier matters too: a student who needed the Extended tier's more accessible questions to reach a 6 is being told something. That reading takes a subject specialist about twenty minutes and it is the part of the decision no prospectus can supply.

faqs.question: Can my child change a subject or level after DP1 starts?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it gets harder with time. The easiest window is before the Diploma starts; the next easiest is the first term of DP1, before content accumulates. A level change from Higher to Standard stays feasible longer than a subject change because the content overlaps. The decision belongs to the school, which weighs timetable capacity, teaching groups and registration deadlines. The practical warning is that the administrative window closes well before the academic case becomes obvious, so October concerns should be raised in October.

faqs.question: Is dropping to Standard Level a failure?
faqs.answer: No, and it frequently improves the overall points total. A Higher Level subject that is not working consumes capacity across all six subjects, so the hours it takes come from somewhere, usually from the subjects that were fine. Moving it to Standard Level releases that capacity and often lifts three other grades. Families sometimes resist for reasons unconnected to the Diploma, and the result is two years of strain and a lower total than the Standard Level entry would have produced. It is a timetable decision, not a verdict.

faqs.question: What does subject selection guidance cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Two or three hours of specialist time, which at published Dubai rates read in October 2026 sits in the AED 200 to 450 and above band per hour, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider AED 650. Compare that with the alternative: weekly support in a mismatched Higher Level runs AED 600 to 1,200 a month in Bestimate's mid band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work, across eighteen months. Those are market figures rather than our price list, and the ratio is not close.

faqs.question: How do we know whether a subject is actually offered at our school?
faqs.answer: Ask the Diploma coordinator for the options booklet and the option block structure, and ask two further questions: which subjects are guaranteed to run and which depend on how many students choose them, and which Mathematics routes are offered at which levels. Dubai schools a few kilometres apart differ considerably, and a subject listed in a booklet can still fail to run in September if numbers are short. Smaller cohorts are most affected in Group 6 arts subjects and less common Language B options.

faqs.question: How should we set the level for Language B?
faqs.answer: On written evidence rather than on how fluently the student speaks at home. A student with a conversational background is sometimes placed at Higher Level and then struggles with the written components and the formal oral, while a strong classroom linguist placed at Standard Level gives away points they could have earned. Ask the language department for a view based on marked written work. This is the group where level placement goes wrong most often in Dubai schools, and it is also one of the easiest to get right by asking.

faqs.question: Is an arts subject a weaker choice than a second science?
faqs.answer: Not inherently, and dismissing Group 6 is a common Dubai error. An arts subject carries substantial coursework spread across both years with an exhibition or performance outcome, which sits differently in a timetable from a third examined science with another Internal Assessment in the same months. If the target degree does not require a second science, choosing one anyway is a decision about how the combination reads rather than about how the two years will actually go for that student.

faqs.question: Does the Extended Essay subject need deciding at selection time?
faqs.answer: It does not have to be, but thinking about it then costs nothing and prevents a hard DP1 spring. The Extended Essay is a long independent piece in one subject, and it is far easier in a subject the student actively wants to read about. Dubai students frequently choose late, picking a Higher Level science because it feels serious and then struggling to find a researchable question. If one of the six subjects is an obvious fit for that, it is a point in that subject's favour at selection time.

faqs.question: Do UAE universities have different IB requirements?
faqs.answer: Programme-specific admission requirements are published by each institution and should be read there. There is also a separate administrative layer that families often confuse with admission: Ministry of Education equivalency, by which a non-UAE school certificate is recognised in the UAE. On the British track the published requirement, as reported in July 2026, is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus A Level or AS Level passes. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so verify your own case through the Ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: Can a tutoring provider influence what my school lets us choose?
faqs.answer: No, and any that implies otherwise is misdescribing a school process. Option availability, block structure and level changes are decided by the Diploma coordinator on timetable capacity, teaching groups and registration deadlines. What a family can do is arrive with the right material: marked work showing the pattern, a named prerequisite from the institution's own page, and a specific request. That combination produces a decision; a general concern produces a reassuring conversation and no change to the timetable.

faqs.question: What if our child cannot decide between two subjects?
faqs.answer: Try an hour of real course content in each, taught by a specialist in that subject, and let the demand rather than the reputation decide. In Dubai the close calls are most often Chemistry against Physics, Economics against Business Management, and the two Mathematics routes. Students usually know within thirty minutes. We also ask each specialist for an honest view on fit, including when the answer is that neither subject is a good match and a different group entirely would serve the student better.

dubai/ib-subject-selection-guidance.closingHeading: Two hours now, or eighteen months later
dubai/ib-subject-selection-guidance.closingBody: Subject selection is the one Diploma decision where a small amount of specialist time prevents a cost that no later tutoring can recover. Send the most recent marked work with component marks, the school's options booklet and block structure, and the destinations or course families in mind, and one session will produce a shortlist, a list of combinations that will not work, and the questions to take to your coordinator. If the answer is already obvious we will say so and charge you for nothing. The trial lesson is free, one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-tok-essay-help.tutorsIntro: The tutors here coach the TOK essay specifically rather than treating it as general essay writing. Each has read and marked student drafts against the global impression bands, works across the areas of knowledge Dubai candidates draw on most, and will tell a student when a chosen title does not suit the examples they have.

intro.heading: A TOK essay is marked as one judgement, which is why drafts matter
paragraphs: The Theory of Knowledge essay is the externally assessed part of TOK and carries two thirds of the TOK grade, with the exhibition carrying the other third. A candidate picks one of six prescribed titles released by the IB for their session, writes up to 1,600 words, and submits it to an examiner who marks it as a single global impression against five bands rather than adding up scores for separate criteria. There is no part-marks structure to game. There is one question the examiner is answering: does this essay explore its title clearly, coherently and critically.

That single-judgement structure is exactly why progress on a TOK essay has to be measured in drafts. A subject essay can be improved by adding a missing section. A TOK essay improves when the quality of its thinking changes, and that shows up as a different band, not as a few extra marks. A student who writes four drafts and gets a band position on each one can see movement. A student who writes one draft the week before the deadline has no information about where they stand until the grade arrives, by which point nothing can be done.

What makes this harder in Dubai than families expect is the TOK teaching allocation. TOK is timetabled thinly in most schools, often as a single period taught by a teacher drawn from another department, and the IB expects only one formally marked draft to be commented on before submission. That one round of comments is the whole structured feedback the course offers. A candidate who has not understood what a knowledge question is by then has used it up on surface problems.

The commonest misreading of TOK is that it rewards opinion. It does not. It rewards the careful handling of claims about knowledge: how a conclusion in one area of knowledge is established, what counts as evidence there, why the same move would fail in another area, and what follows for the title's question. A candidate who writes a strong, well-structured argument about whether social media is good for society has written a good essay in the wrong subject and will sit in a low band.

Our work on it is narrow and mechanical in the best sense. We read the student's own draft, state the band it currently sits in, name the specific feature that holds it there, and say what the next draft has to contain to move. Then the student writes that draft. Nothing is supplied, nothing is rewritten, and the essay submitted is the student's own work, which is what the academic honesty declaration attached to it asserts.

Delivery for UAE families is online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared document. A TOK session is two people reading the same paragraph and arguing about whether it does what the title needs, which works better on a shared screen than across a kitchen table, and leaves the annotated draft in the student's hands afterwards.
bullets: Six prescribed titles per session, one chosen, 1,600 words maximum
Marked as a single global impression across five bands
The essay is two thirds of the TOK grade; the exhibition is one third
One formally commented draft is the school norm
Opinion essays sit low; knowledge claims and their justification sit high
Progress is tracked as band movement between the student's own drafts

dubai/ib-tok-essay-help.programmesIntro: TOK belongs to the Diploma core, but the thinking it assesses is built earlier in the IB continuum, and families moving between Dubai schools meet it at different points. Here is where it sits at each stage.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: TOK runs across both years as a core element alongside the Extended Essay and CAS. The assessment is two pieces: the internally assessed exhibition and the externally assessed essay on a prescribed title. The TOK grade combines with the Extended Essay grade in a matrix worth up to three Diploma points, and the lowest grade in both components is a failing condition.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools generally timetable TOK lightly and often staff it from volunteers across departments, so the quality of TOK teaching varies more school to school than any Diploma subject does. Candidates in schools where it is taught by a committed specialist rarely need outside help; candidates where it is a timetable filler frequently do.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: No TOK, but the MYP's interdisciplinary units and its criterion on evaluating sources build the same habits. Students who have written MYP reflections that genuinely weigh evidence find the step into knowledge questions much shorter than students arriving from a terminal-examination system.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run the full continuum, so a student may reach DP1 already comfortable with interdisciplinary thinking. Students joining at Year 12 from an IGCSE stream usually need the first term simply to accept that a question can have more than one defensible answer.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP candidates do not take TOK. The core includes personal and professional skills and a reflective project instead, which examines an ethical dilemma connected to the career-related study. The reflective project is internally assessed with external moderation and asks for a different kind of writing from a TOK essay.
programmes.countryNote: The CP remains a minority route in Dubai. A family comparing programmes should confirm with the school exactly which core components apply, because the difference between a reflective project and a TOK essay plus Extended Essay is a substantial difference in workload and in what the student is being taught to do.

dubai/ib-tok-essay-help.subjectsIntro: A TOK essay has to draw on areas of knowledge, and the student's Diploma subjects are where their real examples live. These are the subject sources Dubai candidates use most, with what each contributes and what it tempts them into.

subjects.name: Natural sciences
subjects.description: The strongest source of examples about method, replication and what counts as evidence. The trap is writing about science as if it produced certainty, when the more useful TOK point is usually about provisional conclusions and how they are revised.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Useful precisely because it behaves differently from the sciences: proof rather than evidence, and conclusions that do not depend on observation. Candidates misuse it by treating a theorem as a fact about the world rather than as a consequence of axioms.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Rich on perspective, selection and the status of sources. The trap is retelling an event as an example instead of making a point about how historical knowledge is constructed, which is the only reason history appears in a TOK essay at all.

subjects.name: Human sciences
subjects.description: Good ground for questions about models, prediction and whether a method borrowed from the natural sciences survives contact with people. Candidates tend to cite a famous study without saying anything about how its knowledge was produced.

subjects.name: The arts
subjects.description: The area most often used badly and most rewarding when used well. A strong essay says something about what kind of knowledge an artwork can convey; a weak one asserts that art is subjective and moves on.

subjects.name: Knowledge and technology
subjects.description: Heavily chosen because it feels current. The risk is an essay about the effects of technology on society rather than about knowledge, which is a different subject and sits in a low band however well it is argued.

subjects.name: Knowledge and language
subjects.description: Strong for questions about classification, translation and what a vocabulary makes it possible to notice. Dubai candidates in multilingual households often have genuinely original examples here, which examiners reward.

subjects.name: Knowledge and politics
subjects.description: Productive on expertise, consensus and contested claims. It needs care: an essay that becomes a political argument rather than an analysis of political knowledge loses the thread the examiner is following.

subjects.name: Knowledge and the knower
subjects.description: The compulsory starting point of the course and a legitimate source of examples about perspective and personal experience. Examples drawn from here must still do analytical work, not simply illustrate that people differ.

dubai/ib-tok-essay-help.regionsIntro: TOK essay coaching is booked from across Dubai, and the school's TOK staffing matters more than the neighbourhood does. These are the areas we hear from, and what the local pattern tends to be.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: The thickest IB cluster in the emirate, with several full-continuum schools. Candidates here usually arrive able to frame a knowledge question and need help on example selection and the 1,600-word cut.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Established IB provision beside British schools. The recurring case is a student who entered DP1 from an IGCSE stream and is meeting open-ended assessment for the first time.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Large continuum schools where TOK is timetabled against heavy subject loads. Requests cluster in the fortnight before a school's draft deadline, which is later than is ideal.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Continuum schools with families who stay from primary. Students here tend to be comfortable with reflection and weaker on using a subject example to make a point about knowledge rather than about the subject.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer Diploma cohorts with few internal exemplars to study. That absence of locally marked examples is the specific thing outside coaching replaces here.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: A coastal mix of British and IB schools. Evening slots dominate because the study window after activities and the commute home is short on weekdays.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Diploma provision on the Creek side of the city. Weekend morning sessions are requested more often here, which suits essay work better than a late weekday hour.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Al Sheif
schoolClusters.note: Dubai's densest concentration of IB World Schools, several on the full continuum. TOK candidates from this cluster generally handle knowledge questions competently and come to us for band movement on a specific draft.

schoolClusters.city: Nad Al Sheba, Mirdif, Festival City and Dubai Hills
schoolClusters.note: Continuum and Diploma schools across the eastern and southern communities, including several young DP cohorts. Enquiries here are more often about what the essay is supposed to do at all, which is a different starting point.

dubai/ib-tok-essay-help.modesIntro: TOK essay coaching is organised around drafts, because a band is the only honest measure of progress and a band only exists once something is written.

modes.title: Title selection and knowledge-question mapping
modes.description: One or two sessions when the prescribed titles are released. The work is reading all six titles properly, identifying what each one actually asks, and matching them against the examples and subjects the student genuinely has. Most low-band essays were decided here, by a student picking the title that sounded easiest to understand rather than the one they could argue about.
bullets: All six titles analysed for what they demand, not what they mention
Titles matched against the student's real subject examples
Knowledge questions drafted in the student's own words
A reasoned choice the student can explain

modes.title: Draft-by-draft band reporting
modes.description: The student writes a draft. We read it, state the band it sits in, name the single feature holding it there, and set out what the next draft must contain. Then the student writes the next draft. Three or four cycles of this is the whole method, and it is the only way a student can see movement before the external grade arrives.
bullets: A stated band position on every draft, with the reason
One primary job per cycle rather than twenty comments
Written notes the student works from alone
No sentences supplied and no paragraphs rewritten

modes.title: The 1,600-word cut
modes.description: Nearly every serious TOK draft arrives over length, and cutting it is a skill rather than a chore. The useful cuts are the explanatory passages where the student was teaching themselves the subject material, and they usually free three hundred words for the analysis that moves the band. A session on this is short and unusually productive.

Protects the evaluative moves that carry the band

modes.title: Joint core planning with the Extended Essay
modes.description: TOK and the Extended Essay are graded together in the core points matrix, so planning them separately leaves value on the table. A single session mapping both deadlines, both current positions and where effort is best spent is often worth more than another hour on either one.
bullets: Both core components on one calendar

sections.heading: What the TOK essay asks for, in plain terms
paragraphs: The IB releases six prescribed titles for each examination session. A candidate chooses one, must use it exactly as worded, and writes up to 1,600 words in response. The essay goes to an external examiner who awards a single grade from five bands, guided by one overarching question about whether the essay explores its title clearly, coherently and critically. There are no separate criterion scores to balance and no way to compensate a weak argument with strong presentation.

The essay must be about knowledge. That sounds obvious and it is the thing most low-band essays get wrong. A title that mentions technology is not an invitation to write about technology; it is an invitation to write about how knowledge is produced, justified or limited in contexts where technology matters. The examiner is following a thread about knowledge claims and their justification, and an essay that drops that thread to argue a substantive position loses the band regardless of how well the position is argued.

Examples are mandatory in practice even though the instrument does not list them as a criterion. An essay that stays abstract cannot demonstrate critical exploration, because there is nothing concrete for its claims to be tested against. The examples that work are specific, drawn from areas of knowledge the student actually studies, and used to make a point rather than to illustrate one. A named study, a particular historical interpretation or a specific mathematical result does more work than a paragraph about science in general.

The structure that tends to serve the band well is simple: establish what the title is asking, take a position, develop it through two areas of knowledge with real examples, give genuine weight to the strongest objection, and reach a conclusion that is narrower and more honest than the opening promised. That is not a template to fill. It is the shape an argument takes when it is actually being made.
bullets: Six titles per session, used exactly as worded, 1,600 words maximum
One global impression grade across five bands
The subject is knowledge, not the topic the title mentions
Specific examples from real areas of knowledge, used to argue

sections.heading: Reading the six prescribed titles before choosing one
paragraphs: Candidates choose a title in about ten minutes and then live with the consequence for three months. The choice should take an afternoon. Each title has a different structural demand, and the right title for a student is the one whose demand matches the examples and subjects they actually have, not the one whose wording is easiest to understand.

The table below sets out the recurring shapes prescribed titles take and what each demands. The shapes repeat across sessions even though the wording never does, so a student who can recognise the shape of their title knows what the essay has to do before writing a sentence. A title built on a contrast between two areas of knowledge, for example, cannot be answered well by an essay that treats both the same way; the contrast is the work.

The practical test is to write, for each of the six titles, the two best examples the student could use and the objection they would have to answer. Most students find that three of the six collapse immediately because they have no real examples, two are workable, and one is clearly best. That exercise takes two hours and it is the highest-value two hours in the whole TOK course.

Treat the shapes below as a reading aid rather than as a list of titles. The IB publishes the actual prescribed titles for each session, they must be used exactly as worded, and the school's TOK teacher is the authority on which session's titles apply to your child.

sections.heading: How a TOK draft moves up a band
paragraphs: Because the essay is marked as one judgement, band movement is the only meaningful measure of progress, and it is visible to anyone who reads drafts against the instrument. The pattern is remarkably consistent. A first draft that is descriptive sits low. Adding examples lifts it. Making the examples do argumentative work lifts it again. Giving the strongest counter-position genuine weight lifts it further. Each of those is one job, and trying to do all four in a single revision produces a mess.

That is why we report one primary job per draft rather than a page of comments. A student who is told that their essay describes two areas of knowledge without comparing them has something they can act on this week. A student handed twenty observations of varying importance will fix the easy ones, which are the presentational ones, and the band will not move.

The table below describes what an examiner tends to see at each level and what the next draft has to add. It is a working aid rather than the official instrument, and the IB's own assessment guidance is what the examiner uses. Use it to locate a draft, not to predict a grade.

The timing implication matters in Dubai, where TOK competes with six subjects and the Extended Essay for the same evenings. Three or four draft cycles need six to eight weeks with gaps between them, because a student has to go away and think. A student starting four weeks out can realistically complete two cycles, which is usually one band of movement rather than two. That is worth knowing before the family decides when to start.

table.caption: WHAT MOVES A TOK ESSAY DRAFT UP ONE LEVEL
columns: What the next draft must add
rows: The topic discussed, the title barely engaged
Reframe every paragraph to answer the title as worded
The title engaged, but only described
Two specific examples from real areas of knowledge
Examples made to carry the argument, not decorate it
A clear argument with the objection waved through
The strongest counter-position given real weight
Precision in the conclusion and the 1,600-word cut

sections.heading: Choosing two areas of knowledge that do real work
paragraphs: Most prescribed titles are best answered through two areas of knowledge, and the choice determines how much the essay can say. The rule that helps is to pick two areas that behave differently with respect to whatever the title is about. Mathematics and the natural sciences differ on what counts as justification. History and the natural sciences differ on repeatability. The arts and the human sciences differ on what kind of claim is even being made. Pairs that differ generate argument; pairs that agree generate description.

Dubai candidates have an advantage here that they rarely use. Many are genuinely multilingual and have moved between education systems, which gives them first-hand examples about classification, translation and what a curriculum makes visible. A student who has studied the same historical period in two countries has a better example about perspective in history than anything in a textbook, and examiners reward examples that are specific and clearly the student's own.

The commonest error is using an area of knowledge the student does not study. An essay that reaches for the arts because the title seems to invite it, written by a student who takes no arts subject, produces exactly the vague assertions the band descriptors punish. Two areas the student knows well will always outperform one they know and one they have read about.

The second commonest error is imbalance: nine hundred words on the first area and three hundred on the second. If the title asks for a comparison, the comparison is the essay, and a lopsided treatment signals that the second area was an afterthought. Allocate the word count before writing and hold to it.
bullets: Pick two areas that behave differently on the title's issue
Use areas the student actually studies, not ones that sound apt
Multilingual and multi-system experience is a real example source
Allocate the 1,600 words between the two areas before writing

sections.heading: Where Dubai TOK candidates lose the most ground
paragraphs: The first and largest loss is writing about the topic rather than about knowledge. A title mentioning artificial intelligence produces essays about the effects of artificial intelligence; a title mentioning history produces essays about historical events. Both can be well written and both sit in a low band, because the examiner is looking for an exploration of how knowledge is produced and justified, and the essay has not attempted one.

The second is the unexamined counter-position. Students are taught to include a counter-argument and so they include one, in a single sentence, immediately conceded. An examiner reads that as a formality rather than as critical engagement. The move that earns the band is to state the strongest version of the opposing case, show why a reasonable person holds it, and then explain precisely what it fails to account for.

The third is example quality. Generic examples, invented examples and examples the student has clearly read in a revision guide all fail for the same reason: they cannot be interrogated. A specific named study with a stated method, a particular contested historical interpretation, a named mathematical result, or a documented case from the student's own subject course gives the argument something to push against.

The fourth is length discipline, which is a band issue rather than a rule issue. Drafts arrive at 2,100 words and the cut is made in the last hour, usually by deleting the conclusion and the counter-argument because they come last. That is the worst possible cut. The material to remove is the explanatory background the student wrote while working out their own thinking, which is invisible to them precisely because it was useful at the time.
bullets: Writing about the topic instead of about knowledge
A counter-position stated in one sentence and conceded
Examples too generic to interrogate
Cutting the analysis instead of the background to reach 1,600 words
Starting too late for more than two draft cycles

sections.heading: One commented draft from school: making it count
paragraphs: Schools are expected to comment formally on one TOK essay draft before submission, and that round of feedback is the whole structured support the course provides. In a Dubai school where TOK is a single timetabled period taught alongside a full subject load, it may also be the only sustained attention the essay gets from a teacher. Spending it well is therefore a planning decision rather than a matter of luck.

Spending it badly means submitting a draft that is still working out what the title asks. The teacher's comments then go on structural problems the student already suspected, and the one chance to have a specialist read a mature argument is used up. Spending it well means submitting a draft that has already been through the obvious revisions, so the comments land on the argument itself.

That sequencing is where outside coaching fits legitimately. A tutor can read an early draft, report the band and the main job, and send the student away to revise, so that the version reaching the school teacher is the third draft rather than the first. None of that displaces the school's role, and all of it increases what the school's single intervention is worth.

Keep a copy of every draft, dated. It is useful for the student, who can see movement rather than only being told about it, and it is useful evidence of process if any question about authorship ever arises. A folder of six dated drafts in the student's own writing voice is the most straightforward answer to that question there is.
bullets: One formally commented draft is the school norm for TOK
Submit a mature draft to school, not a first attempt
Outside coaching should precede the school's round, not replace it
Keep every draft dated, as both a progress record and process evidence

sections.heading: What TOK coaching costs in Dubai, and why it runs online
paragraphs: Published market rates in Dubai, read in October 2026, start around AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik for budget online tutoring, rise through Unitors at AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate's AED 200-450 and above for specialist IB and IGCSE work, reaching AED 650 at BartyED for premium examiner-branded provision. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate, with independent home tutors asking up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. Those are the market's figures and not an IB Gram price list.

TOK is unusual in this market because the budget end is genuinely unsuitable rather than merely weaker. A tutor who has not read student essays against the global impression bands cannot tell a student which band they are in, and that single piece of information is the service. The relevant comparison for a family is therefore not hourly rate but whether the person reading the draft can place it and justify the placement.

A realistic shape for TOK is three or four draft-review sessions plus one title-selection session, spread over six to eight weeks. That is a project cost rather than a recurring commitment, and it is considerably less than the AED 1,000-2,000 a month Bestimate attributes to specialist exam-year weekly tutoring. Ask what written feedback between sessions is included, because in this market that varies more than the headline hourly figure does.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For TOK that costs the family nothing. The work is a shared document and an argument about a paragraph, and the student keeps the annotated file afterwards. What the online format does buy is a tutor who has actually marked TOK essays, rather than whichever generalist can reach Mirdif or Arabian Ranches by seven in the evening.

sections.heading: Six to eight weeks of TOK work, week by week
paragraphs: Families ask what the work actually looks like, so here it is as a sequence rather than as a promise. Week one is title selection: all six prescribed titles read properly, two examples and one objection written out for each, and a reasoned choice made. Week two is the first draft, written badly on purpose, because the point of a first draft is to find out what the student thinks rather than to impress anyone.

Week three is the first band report and the first revision job, which at that stage is almost always about engaging the title as worded rather than the topic it mentions. Week four is the second draft and the second report, usually about making examples argue instead of illustrate. Week five is the counter-position: finding the strongest opposing case and giving it room. Week six is the third draft, which is typically the one worth sending to the school teacher for the formal comment.

Weeks seven and eight are the school's comments, a final revision and the 1,600-word cut, in that order. Cutting last is deliberate, because material cut from a mature draft is material whose loss can be judged, whereas cutting early removes things the argument turned out to need. The academic honesty declaration is signed at the end of a process in which the student wrote every version.

A student with four weeks instead of eight compresses this to title choice, two drafts and the cut, which is realistically one band of movement rather than two. A student with twelve weeks does not need twelve; three or four cycles with real gaps between them is the useful maximum, because the thinking has to happen away from the desk.
bullets: Week 1 title analysis, week 2 first draft written for information
Weeks 3-5 one band report and one revision job per cycle
Week 6 the draft that goes to school for formal comment

process.title: Send the title and the current draft
process.description: The prescribed title as worded, whatever the student has written so far, and the school's draft deadline. If there is nothing written yet, send the six titles and the student's subject combination instead. Either way we can say within one session where the work stands and how many draft cycles the remaining time allows.

process.title: We match a tutor who has marked TOK essays
process.description: Not a subject teacher who also covers TOK. The service is placing a draft in a band and justifying the placement, which requires someone who has read essays against the instrument. Where nobody suitable is free at your preferred hour we say so and offer the next slot rather than substituting a generalist.

process.title: A free trial that produces a band and a job
process.description: The first session ends with two things: where the current draft sits, and the single most important thing the next draft must do. That is deliberately concrete. If the session cannot produce those two outputs, the family should not book a second one, and we will say so.

process.title: Draft cycles with real gaps
process.description: The student revises, we read, we report, the student revises again. Three or four cycles over six to eight weeks is the working pattern. The gaps are part of the method rather than scheduling slack, because the shift from describing to arguing happens away from the screen.

process.title: The cut, and then it is theirs
process.description: The final session is usually the 1,600-word cut and a last read for coherence. Every sentence in the submitted essay is the student's own, written across a folder of dated drafts, which is both how the band gets earned and the plainest possible answer to any question about authorship.

whyPoints.title: We report a band, not an impression
whyPoints.description: Every draft comes back with a stated band position and the specific feature holding it there. A student who is told their essay is good but could go deeper has learnt nothing. A student told their examples illustrate rather than argue has a job for the week.

whyPoints.title: One job per draft
whyPoints.description: Twenty comments produce a tidier essay in the same band. One well-chosen job moves it. We name the primary job and leave the secondary ones until it is done, which is slower to read and faster to work.

whyPoints.title: The core is planned together
whyPoints.description: TOK and the Extended Essay are graded jointly in the points matrix, and the lowest grade in both is a failing condition. We will always ask about the Extended Essay, because effort is often better spent on the other component than on the one the family called about.

whyPoints.title: Drafts stay the student's own
whyPoints.description: No sentence is supplied and no paragraph rewritten. The folder of dated drafts in the student's own voice is both how the band is earned and the clearest evidence of process a school could ever want to see.

whyPoints.title: AED figures that carry a source
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is attributed to the provider that published it and dated to October 2026, and described as the market rather than as our price. We would rather be checkable than impressive.

whyPoints.title: TOK markers, not nearby tutors
whyPoints.description: Because delivery is online, the person reading the draft is chosen for having marked TOK essays rather than for living near your community, which in a market where in-home rates price travel into every hour is the whole argument for the format.

faqs.question: How long should my child's TOK essay be?
faqs.answer: The upper limit is 1,600 words and examiners stop reading there, so anything beyond it is lost rather than separately penalised. Most serious drafts arrive at 1,900 to 2,200 words and have to be cut, which is normal and should be done last rather than first. The material to remove is almost always the explanatory background the student wrote while working out their own position, not the counter-argument or the conclusion, which are the parts that carry the band and which unfortunately come last in the document.

faqs.question: How is the TOK essay actually marked?
faqs.answer: As a single global impression rather than as a set of separate criterion scores. An external examiner reads the essay and places it in one of five bands, guided by one overarching question about whether the essay provides a clear, coherent and critical exploration of the prescribed title. There are no part-marks to accumulate, which is why strong presentation cannot compensate for a weak argument. It is also why progress has to be tracked as band movement between drafts rather than as an improving score.

faqs.question: Can my child choose their own TOK essay question?
faqs.answer: No. The IB releases six prescribed titles for each examination session, and the candidate must choose one and use it exactly as worded. Rewording a title, narrowing it or combining two of them is a significant error that undermines the essay's entire basis, because the examiner is assessing exploration of that title specifically. Choosing well matters enormously: the right title is the one whose demand matches the examples and subjects the student actually has, not the one whose wording reads most easily.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the TOK essay and the TOK exhibition?
faqs.answer: They are the two assessed components of the same course and they ask for different things. The exhibition is internally assessed, built around real objects and an internal assessment prompt, and carries one third of the TOK grade. The essay is externally assessed, responds to a prescribed title in 1,600 words, and carries the other two thirds. Students often find the exhibition easier because objects are concrete, then underestimate the essay, which is the component where the grade is mostly decided.

faqs.question: How many areas of knowledge does the essay need?
faqs.answer: Most prescribed titles are answered best through two, and the choice matters more than the number. The pairing that generates argument is one where the two areas behave differently on whatever the title is about: mathematics and the natural sciences differ on justification, history and the natural sciences on repeatability, the arts and the human sciences on what kind of claim is being made. Two areas the student genuinely studies always outperform one they know and one they have only read about.

faqs.question: Why did my child's well-written TOK essay get a low grade?
faqs.answer: The commonest reason is that it was about the topic rather than about knowledge. A title mentioning technology invites an exploration of how knowledge is produced and justified where technology matters; an essay arguing that technology harms society can be clear, organised and persuasive and still sit low, because it never attempted the thing being assessed. The second commonest reason is a counter-position stated in one sentence and immediately conceded, which an examiner reads as a formality rather than as critical engagement.

faqs.question: How many drafts does a TOK essay normally need?
faqs.answer: Three or four, with real gaps between them. The pattern is consistent: a first draft that describes, a second that adds specific examples, a third that makes those examples argue, and a fourth that gives the strongest objection genuine weight. Each of those is one job, and attempting several in a single revision produces a longer essay in the same band. Six to eight weeks allows that sequence comfortably. Four weeks allows two cycles, which is about one band of movement rather than two.

faqs.question: How many commented drafts will my child's school give?
faqs.answer: One formally commented draft is the expected norm for TOK, in line with the rules on how much support an externally assessed piece may receive. In Dubai schools where TOK is a single timetabled period taught alongside a full subject load, that may also be the only sustained teacher attention the essay gets. The practical implication is to send the school a mature draft rather than a first attempt, so that the comments land on the argument rather than on problems the student already knew about.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of a TOK essay for my child?
faqs.answer: No, and no reputable tutor would. The essay carries an academic honesty declaration, and work that is not the student's own is malpractice with consequences that fall on the student rather than on whoever was paid. What a tutor can legitimately do is explain what the title demands, place a draft in a band and justify it, name the next revision job, teach what a knowledge question is, and challenge an example. Every sentence in the submitted essay must come from the student's own keyboard.

faqs.question: What kind of examples earn marks in a TOK essay?
faqs.answer: Specific ones that can be interrogated. A named study with a stated method, a particular contested historical interpretation, a named mathematical result, or a documented case from the student's own Diploma course all give the argument something to push against. Generic examples about science or history in general cannot be examined and so cannot demonstrate critical exploration. Dubai candidates who have studied in more than one education system or language often have genuinely original examples about perspective and classification, and examiners reward originality that is clearly the student's own.

faqs.question: Does the TOK grade affect my child's Diploma points?
faqs.answer: Yes. The TOK grade combines with the Extended Essay grade in the core points matrix, which awards up to three points towards the Diploma total of 45. Consistency across the two components pays more than strength in one. There is also a failing condition: the lowest grade in both TOK and the Extended Essay means the Diploma is not awarded regardless of subject points. Confirm the current matrix values with your child's Diploma coordinator, since the IB publishes the authoritative version.

faqs.question: My child says TOK is pointless. How do I answer that?
faqs.answer: With the arithmetic. TOK and the Extended Essay together are worth up to three Diploma points, which at the margin of a university offer is worth more per hour invested than any single subject. Beyond that, the skill being assessed is judging how far a claim is justified, which is what most university work turns out to consist of. The frustration is usually with how thinly the course is timetabled rather than with the subject itself, and a student who sees band movement on their own drafts generally stops finding it pointless.

faqs.question: What does TOK essay coaching cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run from about AED 33-65 an hour at the budget online platforms up to AED 650 for premium examiner-branded providers, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate putting specialist IB support at AED 200-450 and above. For TOK the budget end is genuinely unsuitable rather than just cheaper, because the service is placing a draft in a band and that needs someone who has marked essays. Three or four review sessions is the usual shape, so budget it as a project.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start if the deadline is three weeks away?
faqs.answer: Not pointless, but be realistic about what three weeks buys. Two draft cycles are possible, which in practice means one band of movement rather than two, and the work has to be ruthlessly prioritised: engage the title as worded, make two examples argue, give the objection real weight, then cut to 1,600 words. What is not possible in three weeks is changing the prescribed title or rebuilding the essay around different areas of knowledge. We will say at the end of the first session which of those applies.

dubai/ib-tok-essay-help.closingHeading: Send the draft and find out the band
dubai/ib-tok-essay-help.closingBody: The single most useful thing a TOK candidate can have is an honest answer to where their current draft sits and what the next one has to do. That is what the free trial session produces: a band position, the reason for it, and one job for the coming week. Sessions run over live video on Gulf Standard Time, the student keeps the annotated draft, and every sentence that reaches the examiner is theirs. If the honest answer after reading the draft is that it is already near the top band and needs a word cut rather than a rebuild, that is what we will tell you.

intro.heading: The exhibition is the part of TOK a DP1 student can actually bank
paragraphs: The TOK exhibition is the internally assessed component of Theory of Knowledge. A student selects one internal assessment prompt from the list of thirty-five in the TOK guide, chooses three objects from the real world, and writes a commentary of up to 950 words explaining how each object connects to that prompt. The school marks it against a single assessment instrument and the IB externally moderates a sample. It carries a third of the TOK grade, and most Dubai schools complete it during the first Diploma year.

That timing is the opportunity. A DP1 student has not yet met the pressure of six subjects running towards examinations, the Extended Essay deadline is still some way off, and the exhibition is a short, self-contained task with a clear specification. A third of a TOK grade, which feeds the core points matrix alongside the Extended Essay, can be secured early and then left alone. Students who treat it as a small assignment and submit something vague in a week have given away that advantage for no reason.

The thing that decides the band is object specificity, and it is the thing students get wrong first. An object in this task is not a category. A smartphone is not an object; a particular student's own phone, with a named photograph on it taken on a specific date, is. A newspaper is not an object; a named edition carrying a named headline is. Examiners and moderators can only judge whether an object illuminates a prompt if the object is particular enough to be examined, and the single commonest cause of a low exhibition mark is three objects that are really three categories.

The second decider is the link. Each object has to be connected explicitly to the chosen prompt, and the commentary has to do that work in writing rather than leaving it implied. Three excellent objects with weak links score below three ordinary objects with precise links. That is counter-intuitive to students, who spend most of their effort choosing interesting objects and almost none on articulating why each one answers the prompt.

Our work is the same shape as our TOK essay work: the student does the choosing and the writing, we read what they produce, state the band it sits in, and name the one thing the next draft has to do. Three cycles usually finishes an exhibition comfortably. The commentary that goes to the school is the one the student typed, which is what the academic honesty declaration attached to internally assessed work asserts.

Sessions run online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared screen. An exhibition session involves looking at the student's three photographs and their draft side by side, which suits a shared document better than a laptop on a dining table, and leaves the annotated draft with the student afterwards.

dubai/ib-tok-exhibition-help.programmesIntro: The exhibition sits in the Diploma core, and its requirements are specific to it. Families moving between IB stages in Dubai meet different versions of the same demand to connect an artefact to an idea.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: TOK is assessed in two parts: the exhibition, internally marked and externally moderated, worth a third of the grade, and the essay on a prescribed title, externally marked, worth two thirds. The resulting TOK grade feeds the core points matrix with the Extended Essay, where up to three Diploma points are available.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai schools schedule the exhibition in DP1, often in the second or third term, with an internal deadline set by the TOK teacher. Because it is internally marked, the school's own standard matters: a school that marks generously may see its cohort's marks adjusted downwards at moderation, which is one reason a commentary should be defensible against the instrument rather than merely liked.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: No exhibition, but the Personal Project's process journal and report ask a student to justify choices in writing, which is the same muscle. MYP students who have written genuine justifications rather than descriptions find the exhibition's demand familiar.

Students arriving at Year 12 from an IGCSE stream have typically never been asked to justify why a particular object illustrates an idea, and that is the gap the first session usually addresses.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: There is no TOK exhibition in the CP. The core comprises personal and professional skills, service learning, a language development portfolio and the reflective project, which examines an ethical dilemma arising from the career-related study and is internally assessed with external moderation.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by a small number of Dubai schools. A family weighing it against the Diploma should confirm the exact core requirements with the school, since the absence of TOK and the Extended Essay changes both the workload and the points structure substantially.

dubai/ib-tok-exhibition-help.subjectsIntro: Exhibition objects come from a student's own life and from the subjects they study, and some sources work far better than others. These are the places Dubai candidates find usable objects, with what each tends to deliver.

subjects.name: Natural sciences
subjects.description: A specific piece of apparatus, a named dataset or a particular published graph makes a strong object because its provenance can be examined. A generic reference to laboratory equipment makes a weak one, for exactly the same reason.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: A named theorem on a specific page, a particular proof a student found unconvincing, or a graph the student generated themselves all work. Mathematics objects are often the most precise in an exhibition and the least used.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A named primary document, a specific monument, a textbook page from a particular country's curriculum. The last of these works unusually well in Dubai, where students have often studied the same period in two education systems.

subjects.name: Human sciences
subjects.description: A particular survey instrument, a named index, a specific advertisement. The trap is choosing a study rather than an object; the object has to be a thing in the world that can be photographed or pointed at.

subjects.name: The arts
subjects.description: A named work seen in a particular place, a specific recording, a student's own piece. Strong because the knowledge question about what an artwork conveys is genuinely open rather than rhetorical.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: A specific translated passage set against its original is one of the most productive object types available to a multilingual Dubai student, because the comparison does analytical work by itself.

subjects.name: Personal and family objects
subjects.levels: Core theme, knowledge and the knower
subjects.description: A named family photograph, a document from a move between countries, an item carried from another place. These earn marks when the commentary says what the object shows about how knowledge is held, and nothing when it is merely sentimental.

subjects.name: Public and civic objects
subjects.description: A specific street sign, a named public notice, a particular official form. Dubai's multilingual public signage is a readily available source of precise objects that most candidates walk past daily without noticing.

subjects.name: Digital objects
subjects.description: A named post with a date, a specific search result, a particular output from a software tool. Workable if specified exactly; useless if described as a type of content rather than as one instance of it.

sections.heading: What the TOK exhibition actually requires
paragraphs: Three objects, one prompt, 950 words. The student chooses one internal assessment prompt from the thirty-five published in the TOK guide and uses it exactly as worded. They then select three objects from the real world, each with a specific real-world context, and write a commentary explaining how each object connects to the prompt. The commentary is submitted with images or identification of the objects and with appropriate references. The school marks it and the IB moderates a sample.

Two features of the specification do most of the work. The objects must be real and particular rather than types or categories, and each must have a specific real-world context the student can state. The links to the prompt must be made explicitly in the commentary rather than left for a reader to infer. A commentary that satisfies both of those, even with unremarkable objects, outscores a commentary with striking objects that satisfies neither.

The task is deliberately short, which students read as easy and markers read as demanding. Three hundred words per object leaves no room for scene-setting. Each object's section has to identify the object and its context, state the connection to the prompt, and justify why that object illuminates that prompt rather than some adjacent idea. Anything else in those three hundred words is displacing something that earns.

It is also worth noting what the exhibition is not. It is not a presentation, although some Dubai schools stage a display for parents alongside it, and it is not a group task. The assessed artefact is the individual written commentary. A student who spends three evenings on a display board and one on the commentary has optimised for the part that carries no marks.

sections.heading: The internal assessment prompts, and how to choose between them
paragraphs: Thirty-five prompts is enough choice to paralyse a student, and the usual outcome is that they pick whichever one they understood first. A better method is to work backwards: list the objects available in the student's own life and studies, then ask which prompts those objects could genuinely answer. Objects are harder to find than prompts, so the objects should lead.

The prompts fall into recognisable families, and knowing the family tells a student what their commentary has to do. Prompts about evidence and justification need objects whose provenance can be examined. Prompts about perspective need objects that look different from two positions. Prompts about values need objects where a judgement is visible. Prompts about method need objects produced by a method the student can describe. Matching the family to the object type is most of the selection problem solved.

The table below sets out those families with the object types that tend to work in each and the characteristic mistake. It is a reading aid; the authoritative list of prompts is in the TOK guide and the student's TOK teacher is the person to confirm which prompt wording applies.

One practical warning. Prompts that mention technology or the internet attract a disproportionate share of candidates and produce the most generic objects, because every student has a phone and a search engine. They are not bad prompts, but a student choosing one should be unusually disciplined about specificity: a named post with a date, a particular search result captured on a particular day, not a category of content.

sections.heading: What makes an object specific enough to score
paragraphs: This is the whole game and it is worth being blunt about. An object with a specific real-world context is one a reader could in principle locate: this photograph, taken by this person, on this date, in this place. An object without one is a category: a photograph, a newspaper, a phone. Categories cannot be examined, so a commentary about a category has nothing to analyse and the band reflects that.

Students resist this because specific objects feel less impressive. A named entry in a particular dictionary sounds smaller than language as a system. In the exhibition the smaller object scores higher, every time, because the task is to show how a real thing in the world connects to a knowledge prompt. The grandeur has to live in the analysis, not in the object.

The table below takes common weak choices and shows the specific version alongside what the specific version then makes arguable. The pattern is always the same: adding a date, a place, a name or an owner turns a category into an object and simultaneously creates the material the commentary needs.

A useful discipline is the photograph test. If the student cannot photograph the object or point to a single identifiable instance of it, it is not yet an object. Objects that exist only as descriptions in the commentary are the ones that cost the most marks, and the fix takes an afternoon with a phone camera and a notebook.

sections.heading: Budgeting 950 words across three objects
paragraphs: Three hundred words per object plus a short frame is the working shape, and departures from it are usually accidents rather than choices. The typical first draft gives the first object four hundred and fifty words, the second three hundred, and the third a hundred and eighty, because the student learnt what they were doing as they wrote. The third object then looks like an afterthought to the marker, and the band falls to the weakest section.

Within each three hundred words the allocation that works is roughly a third to identifying the object and its specific real-world context, a third to the link with the prompt stated explicitly, and a third to the justification of why this object illuminates this prompt. Students routinely spend two thirds on description, which is the part that earns least.

The frame should be short. A couple of sentences naming the prompt as worded and indicating the direction of the commentary is enough, and a long introduction is words taken from the objects. Conclusions are optional in a commentary of this length and are often better omitted entirely in favour of one more sentence of justification on the third object.

References and the identification of objects sit outside the student's analytical word budget in practice, but they must be present and complete. Missing identification is one of the few faults in this task that is pure administration and costs real marks, and it is almost always discovered the evening before submission.

sections.heading: How an exhibition commentary moves up a band
paragraphs: The exhibition is marked as a single judgement against one instrument, so progress shows up as band movement rather than as accumulating points. Reading a sequence of student drafts, the movement is predictable. A commentary that describes three objects sits low. Making the link to the prompt explicit lifts it. Making the justification specific to that object rather than generic lifts it again. Balancing the three objects and tightening the frame secures the top.

Each of those is one job, and we report one per draft for the same reason as on the essay: a student given fifteen comments fixes the easy ones and the band does not move. A student told that object two is linked to the prompt by implication only has a job they can finish in an evening, and the band does move.

The table shows what a marker tends to see at each level and what the next draft has to add. It is a working aid rather than the official instrument, which is published by the IB and is what the school and the moderator use. Use it to locate a draft, not to forecast a mark.

Two or three cycles usually completes an exhibition, which at one draft a week is a fortnight or three weeks of real work. That is why the exhibition is the cheapest third of a TOK grade available: short task, clear specification, predictable band movement, and it is sat in DP1 when the calendar has room.

sections.heading: Where Dubai exhibition candidates lose marks
paragraphs: Generic objects first, because they account for more lost marks than everything else combined. The pattern is a student choosing a category, writing well about it, and receiving a mark that bears no relation to the quality of the prose. The diagnosis is easy and the fix is cheap: add a date, a place, an owner and a photograph, and the same argument becomes examinable.

Implied links second. A student who has chosen objects thoughtfully often believes the connection to the prompt is obvious, and therefore does not write it. Markers and moderators cannot credit an inference they had to make themselves. The sentence that begins with the prompt's own wording and then says what this object shows about it is the sentence that earns, and it has to appear for each object.

Third, and specific to Dubai: the display. Several schools stage an exhibition evening where students present their objects to parents, which is a good thing educationally and carries no marks. Students regularly spend the bulk of their effort on the board, the layout and the talk, then write the commentary in one evening. The commentary is the assessed artefact.

Fourth, timing. Because the exhibition falls in DP1 it competes with the first Internal Assessments and the start of Extended Essay work, and it is the task most easily deferred because it looks small. A deferred exhibition becomes a one-draft exhibition, and a one-draft exhibition is a mid-band exhibition. Three short cycles over a fortnight, started early, is the whole difference.

sections.heading: What exhibition coaching costs in Dubai, and why it is online
paragraphs: Published Dubai market rates, read in October 2026, run from AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik at the budget online end, through Unitors at AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate's AED 200-450 and above for specialist IB and IGCSE work, up to AED 650 at BartyED for premium examiner-branded provision. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate, with independent tutors up to AED 500 once travel is included. These are the market's published figures, not our price list.

The exhibition is the cheapest piece of TOK to support because it is short. One selection session and two or three draft reviews is a complete arrangement, which at mid-range market rates is a few hundred to a thousand dirhams in total rather than a monthly commitment. Set against Bestimate's AED 1,000-2,000 a month for specialist exam-year weekly tutoring, a third of a TOK grade is inexpensive to secure, which is the argument for doing it properly in DP1 rather than later.

What to ask before booking anything is whether the person reading the draft has marked exhibitions against the instrument. Placing a commentary in a band is the service. A tutor who offers general feedback on the writing will make the prose better and leave the band where it was, and at any hourly rate that is poor value.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending tutors to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For this task nothing is lost by that. The session is three photographs and a draft on a shared screen, and the student keeps the annotated file. What the online format buys is somebody who has read exhibitions before rather than whoever can reach Al Barsha or Nad Al Sheba on a weekday evening, which in a market that prices travel into every in-home hour is both better and cheaper.
