process.title: Send the prompt and the candidate objects
process.description: The internal assessment prompt the student is drawn to, five or six objects they are considering, and the school's internal deadline. If a commentary already exists, send that instead. Either way the first session can say which objects are specific enough to survive and which need a date, a place or an owner attached.

process.title: We match a tutor who has marked exhibitions
process.description: The useful skill here is narrow: reading a commentary against the exhibition instrument and placing it. A subject specialist who has never seen an exhibition cannot do that. Where nobody suitable is free at your preferred time we say so and offer the next slot rather than sending a generalist.

process.title: A free trial that filters the objects
process.description: The first session usually ends with half the candidate objects discarded and the surviving three sharpened with a date, a place or an owner. That is deliberately practical. A student who leaves that session knowing which three objects they are writing about has had the most valuable hour available in this task.

process.title: Two or three draft cycles
process.description: The student writes, we read and report a band and one job, the student revises. A fortnight at one cycle a week usually finishes an exhibition. We will say when it is done rather than extending the block, because 950 words does not sustain six sessions of review.

process.title: Final checks, then it goes to school
process.description: The last session covers the word budget across the three objects, the completeness of identification and references, and the final cut. The commentary submitted is the one the student typed, which is what the academic honesty declaration on internally assessed work asserts.

whyPoints.title: We fix objects before words
whyPoints.description: Most low exhibition marks are object problems, not writing problems. An hour spent turning three categories into three particular objects with dates and places is worth more than five hours of editing a commentary built on categories.

whyPoints.title: A band and a job, every draft
whyPoints.description: Each draft comes back with a stated band and the single thing the next version must do. General encouragement is what students already get and does not move an internally marked component through moderation.

whyPoints.title: We say the display carries no marks
whyPoints.description: Several Dubai schools stage an exhibition evening, which is worth doing and is not assessed. We will tell a student to put their last three evenings into the commentary rather than the board, even when that is not what they want to hear.

whyPoints.title: The core gets planned as one thing
whyPoints.description: The exhibition is a third of TOK, the essay two thirds, and the TOK grade pairs with the Extended Essay for up to three Diploma points. We always ask about the other components, because DP1 is when all of this can still be sequenced sensibly.

whyPoints.title: Short blocks, honestly ended
whyPoints.description: A 950-word task does not need an open-ended arrangement. One selection session and two or three reviews is usually the whole job, and we will say when it is finished rather than booking another hour.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every rate here is attributed to the provider that published it and dated to October 2026, and presented as the market rather than as our price. A parent should be able to check a page like this rather than trust it.

faqs.question: How many objects does the TOK exhibition need and how long is the commentary?
faqs.answer: Three objects and a commentary of no more than 950 words in total, which works out at roughly three hundred words per object plus a short frame. Each object must be a specific real-world thing with a context the student can state, not a category. The commentary is submitted with identification of the objects and appropriate references. The school marks it against a single assessment instrument and the IB moderates a sample of the school's marking, so the mark needs to be defensible rather than merely generous.

faqs.question: What counts as a specific object for the exhibition?
faqs.answer: Something a reader could in principle locate: this photograph, taken by this person, on this date, in this place. A smartphone is a category and earns little; the student's own phone displaying one named photograph taken on a stated date is an object and earns. The practical test is whether the student can photograph it or point to a single identifiable instance. Adding a date, a place, an owner or a name is usually all that separates a weak choice from a strong one, and it takes an afternoon.

faqs.question: Can my child choose their own question for the exhibition?
faqs.answer: No. The student selects one of the thirty-five internal assessment prompts published in the TOK guide and must use it exactly as worded. Rewording, narrowing or combining prompts undermines the whole commentary, because the assessment is of how the three objects connect to that prompt as written. The useful method is to work backwards from the objects actually available in the student's life and studies, then choose the prompt those objects can genuinely answer, since objects are harder to find than prompts.

faqs.question: How much of the TOK grade comes from the exhibition?
faqs.answer: One third, with the externally assessed essay carrying the other two thirds. The resulting TOK grade then combines with the Extended Essay grade in the core points matrix, where up to three Diploma points are available. Because the exhibition is short, specified clearly and usually sat in the first Diploma year, it is the most efficiently secured part of the core. Students who treat it as a minor assignment give away a third of a TOK grade for no reason other than timing.

faqs.question: When do Dubai schools usually set the exhibition?
faqs.answer: Most schedule it during the first Diploma year, commonly in the second or third term, with an internal deadline set by the TOK teacher. That timing is an advantage because it sits before examination pressure and before the Extended Essay reaches its heavy phase. It also means the exhibition is the task most easily deferred, since it competes with the first Internal Assessments and looks small by comparison. Ask the TOK teacher for the internal deadline at the start of the year and work back three weeks from it.

faqs.question: Does the exhibition have to be displayed to an audience?
faqs.answer: The assessed artefact is the written commentary, not any physical display. Several Dubai schools stage an exhibition evening where students present their objects to parents and staff, which is valuable educationally and carries no marks. Students regularly spend most of their effort on the board and the talk, then write the commentary in a single evening. If time is short, the commentary is where it should go. Ask the school whether its exhibition evening is a requirement or an invitation, because practice differs.

faqs.question: Why did a good-looking exhibition get a middling mark?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of two reasons. Either the objects were categories rather than particular instances, so there was nothing the marker could examine, or the connection to the prompt was left implied rather than stated. Markers and moderators cannot credit an inference they had to make for themselves. The fix for the first is a date, place and owner; the fix for the second is one sentence per object that begins from the prompt's own wording and says what that object shows about it.

faqs.question: How many drafts does the commentary need?
faqs.answer: Two or three is usually enough, which at one a week is a fortnight or three weeks of real work. The movement is predictable: a first draft that describes the objects, a second that makes the link to the prompt explicit, and a third that makes the justification specific to each object and balances the word budget across all three. Attempting all of that in one revision produces a longer commentary in the same band, which is why one job per draft works better.

faqs.question: Can a tutor choose my child's objects or write the commentary?
faqs.answer: No. The exhibition is internally assessed work covered by an academic honesty declaration, and submitting anything other than the student's own work is malpractice, with consequences that fall on the student. What a tutor can legitimately do is test whether a candidate object is specific enough, ask whether it can be linked to the chosen prompt, place a draft in a band and explain why, and name the next revision job. The objects and every sentence remain the student's own.

faqs.question: Do the objects have to belong to my child?
faqs.answer: They do not have to be owned, but each must have a specific real-world context the student can identify, and the commentary has to establish that context. An object seen in a museum, a public notice in a particular street, or a named page in a textbook used in another country all qualify. What does not qualify is an object that exists only as a description. Objects from the student's own life often work best because the context is naturally specific and the justification is easier to write honestly.

faqs.question: Can two students in the same class use the same object?
faqs.answer: The exhibition is an individual task, and two students in the same cohort choosing the same well-known object will produce commentaries that look alike to a marker who reads both. That is a presentational risk rather than a rule breach, and it is avoidable. Objects drawn from the student's own household, their own subject practicals or their own experience of moving between countries are naturally unique, which is one more argument for the personal and specific over the impressive and general.

faqs.question: What should the three hundred words about each object contain?
faqs.answer: Roughly a third identifying the object and its specific real-world context, a third stating the link to the prompt explicitly, and a third justifying why this object illuminates that prompt rather than some adjacent idea. Students typically spend two thirds on description, which is the part that earns least. Cutting description is also where the words come from when a draft runs long, in preference to shortening the third object, which is the most common and most costly cut.

faqs.question: What does exhibition coaching cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 33-65 an hour at the budget online platforms up to AED 650 for premium examiner-branded providers, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate putting specialist IB support at AED 200-450 and above. Because the task is 950 words, one selection session plus two or three draft reviews is normally the whole arrangement, so it is a few hundred to about a thousand dirhams in total rather than a monthly commitment.

faqs.question: Is it worth getting help on a component worth only a third of TOK?
faqs.answer: The arithmetic says yes, because the effort is small. A third of the TOK grade feeds a core points matrix worth up to three Diploma points, and the exhibition is a short, clearly specified task sat in DP1 when the calendar still has room. Three weeks of disciplined work on 950 words is a better return per hour than almost anything else in the Diploma. The honest caveat is that it is also a task many students can do well unaided once somebody has explained what a specific object is.

dubai/ib-tok-exhibition-help.closingHeading: Start with the objects, not the words
dubai/ib-tok-exhibition-help.closingBody: If your child has three objects and no commentary yet, the first session is the one that matters: half the candidate objects usually get discarded and the survivors gain a date, a place or an owner. If there is already a draft, we will read it against the instrument and tell you the band and the one job for the next version. Sessions run over live video on Gulf Standard Time, the student keeps the annotated file, and every word submitted is theirs. If the commentary is already near the top band and needs nothing but a word cut, that is what we will say.

intro.heading: Four arrangements, one word, very different purchases
paragraphs: The word tuition does a lot of work in Dubai and hides most of what a parent needs to know. A Grade 10 student sitting in a group of eight at a learning centre in Al Quoz, a visiting tutor driving out to Jumeirah Park on a Tuesday, an agency placing a candidate it has never watched teach, and a platform running one-to-one video sessions are four separate products with different ratios, different permit obligations, different evidence trails and dirham costs that differ by a factor of ten. Choosing between them on the word alone is how families end up disappointed by something that was never going to do the job.

The second thing hidden by the word is who is accountable. In a group arrangement the accountable party is the centre, which holds a permit, employs staff and can be asked for a written policy. With a freelance visiting tutor the accountable party is an individual, and the question of whether that individual holds the permit the law requires is one parents are often too polite to ask. On a platform the accountable party is the platform, which is why what a platform publishes about its own limits is worth reading carefully before anything is booked.

This page is therefore built as an audit rather than a pitch. It compares the four arrangements on the dimensions that actually differ. It explains the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry's own smart app and e-services system. It works through the arithmetic of group versus individual attention honestly, including the cases where a group is the better buy. And it lists the documents a parent can ask any provider for every month, which is the part nobody publishes.

There is also a set of decisions that sits upstream of tuition and gets confused with it. Whether a student takes Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation shapes two years of study and some university applications. What the Ministry of Education requires for certificate equivalency decides whether a qualification is usable in the UAE at all. How a student moves from IGCSE, from the Middle Years Programme or from an American high school into the Diploma determines what the first term of tuition should even be about. Each gets its own table below, because getting those wrong costs more than any hourly rate.

Where IB Gram fits is narrow and stated plainly. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one student with one tutor, over live video, with the student writing on a shared whiteboard. IB Gram operates no premises in Dubai and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. Dirham figures quoted anywhere on this page are market rates with the publisher named, not a price list, and the single commitment made is one free trial lesson per student with no card details collected.

dubai/ib-tuition.programmesIntro: Tuition means something different in each IB programme, and the arrangement that suits a Grade 4 reader is the wrong arrangement for a Grade 12 candidate with two internally assessed components outstanding. These are the three programmes Dubai schools run, described from the point of view of how support should be organised rather than what the syllabus contains.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: There is no external examination in the PYP, so tuition here cannot be organised around papers. It is organised around a small number of measurable skills: reading accuracy and fluency, number facts and place value, written sentence construction, and the ability to explain a method aloud. Short, frequent sessions beat long ones at this age, and the honest review point comes sooner, because a reading difficulty that does not respond to six weeks of good teaching needs a different kind of assessment altogether.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's primary IB cohort is large and highly mobile, with families arriving part way through a year from systems that sequence early maths differently. The gap is usually written explanation rather than number work. KHDA's mandatory Arabic provision also begins in these years, taught in separate streams for Arab and non-Arab students, and parents moving in mid-primary frequently meet it for the first time on a report card.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each MYP subject is marked against four criteria labelled A to D, each out of 8, with the school converting criterion totals into a 1-7 grade. Tuition that ignores the criteria and teaches content alone cannot move an MYP grade reliably, because a student who knows the material and never addresses criterion wording is capped in that strand. Year 5 adds the Personal Project, which is supervised in school and needs process management more than subject teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai continuum schools run MYP to Grade 10 and then offer both a Diploma and a British route, which means a Grade 9 or 10 family in this emirate is often choosing a programme and fixing a grade in the same term. A sensible tuition brief at that point covers both: the criterion strand that is costing marks now, and whether writing stamina and algebraic fluency will survive Higher Level.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, normally three Higher Level and three Standard Level, graded 1-7 on a 45-point total, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Every subject carries internally assessed work marked in school and moderated by the IB. Tuition in the Diploma has to be scheduled against the school's own internal deadlines rather than against the examination window, because the internal calendar is what actually constrains a Grade 12 student's time.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision in Dubai is concentrated in fewer schools than the British-curriculum provision surrounding it, so families in the newer southern and eastern communities often travel for a school place and then find no local specialist in a minority subject. That is the practical argument for online delivery in this emirate: the shortlist is set by subject expertise rather than by who can reach a given community before five o'clock.

dubai/ib-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Dubai families most often arrange tuition for outside the obvious core, with the component that usually decides the grade. Each description names something checkable, because a subject list that says every topic covered tells a parent nothing about whether the tutor has marked that paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology carry this course, and the written interpretation is where marks leak. A correct regression with no comment on its validity scores poorly, and a graphics calculator learned informally costs minutes a student cannot spare. HL adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistics. The exploration rewards a narrow statistical question answered with real data.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work is a technique, not a talent: provenance, purpose, value and limitation each earn marks and each is routinely left out. Essay answers lose bands for narrative that never argues. HL adds a regional depth study with far more content, and the historical investigation is marked on method and evaluation of sources as much as on the history itself.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case studies have to be specific, named and used, and generic examples are the commonest cause of a capped answer. Command terms do heavy work in the longer questions. The fieldwork component stands on a measurable question and a defensible method, and students who choose an interesting topic over a manageable one lose marks on data collection they cannot repair later.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Concepts such as legitimacy, sovereignty and interdependence have to structure answers rather than decorate them, and students who write current affairs without the conceptual frame score in the middle. HL adds the global political challenges extension with oral presentations. The engagement activity needs a genuine, documented involvement rather than a retrospective write-up.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Systems diagrams, named environmental value systems and quantitative data handling all carry marks, and the subject is often chosen as a lighter option and then marked harder than expected. The practical scheme needs a measurable variable and honest uncertainty treatment. Students who revise definitions without practising data questions tend to stall around a 4.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: The written components decide more of the grade than students assume. The comparative study is marked on analysis and on cultural significance, not on how much the student likes the work, and the process portfolio is marked on documented experimentation rather than finished pieces. Tuition here is mostly about writing about art precisely and keeping the portfolio honest as it is made.

subjects.name: French B and Spanish B
subjects.description: Productive skills carry the grade and most students over-prepare receptive ones. The written task is marked on message, language and conceptual understanding of audience and purpose, and the individual oral rewards fluency built on a small, well-drilled set of structures rather than a large passive vocabulary. Weekly speaking practice with correction is the component tuition improves fastest.

subjects.name: Spanish ab initio
subjects.description: An ab initio course is shorter and less forgiving than it looks, because the whole grade rests on a narrow set of themes and a small grammatical range used accurately. Students who learned the language informally often carry errors that cost marks across every component. Regular corrected speaking and tightly limited vocabulary lists outperform broad reading at this level.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most lost marks at Higher Level, and data-based questions reward slow reading of the stem more than extra content. A student who has memorised reactions without the electron behaviour underneath cannot handle an unfamiliar mechanism, which is why rebuilding bonding properly usually comes before any past paper work.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The subject looks like memory work and is marked as precision work. Command terms separate a 4 from a 6, and a student who writes everything they know about a topic lands in the middle every time. Statistical handling in the investigation is the single most common place internally assessed marks are left unclaimed.

dubai/ib-tuition.regionsTitle: Dubai communities, and what each one changes about a tuition timetable
dubai/ib-tuition.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Dubai does not change the tutor pool, because lessons run over live video. It changes the timetable, and the timetable is what makes tuition stick or fail. These are the communities where enquiries cluster, with the specific scheduling constraint each one tends to carry.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Apartment households with both parents working inside the same corridor, so the realistic slot is after 18:30 rather than straight after school. Grade 11 and 12 enquiries dominate here, and Economics and Business Management are disproportionately requested in this cluster.

regions.name: The Greens, The Views and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Short school runs and a high proportion of mid-year arrivals, which produces a steady stream of curriculum-transition work. A 16:30 start is genuinely achievable in these communities, and that earlier slot matters for Middle Years students who fade after seven o'clock.

regions.name: Motor City, Sports City and Arjan
regions.note: The nearest Diploma school is often a real drive, so families here are usually managing a long commute before any tuition begins. Online delivery removes a second journey from the evening, which is frequently the difference between a plan that holds for a term and one that collapses by week four.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park, Jumeirah Islands and Al Furjan
regions.note: Villa communities with younger cohorts and more siblings in different programmes at once. The common request is staggered short sessions for two children rather than one long block, which is a scheduling job and the reason fixed weekly slots are agreed before a match is confirmed.

regions.name: Al Quoz, Al Safa and Umm Al Sheif
regions.note: The emirate's learning-centre district sits here, so families in this cluster have usually already tried a group arrangement before enquiring. The useful first conversation is about what the group did and did not cover rather than about the subject in the abstract.

regions.name: Mudon, Town Square and Serena
regions.note: Newer family communities with long bus routes and children who arrive home late and tired. Weekend morning sessions work better here than weekday evenings, and we would rather schedule one good Saturday slot than three weekday sessions that get cancelled.

regions.name: International City and Academic City
regions.note: A dense, mixed-curriculum area close to several higher-education campuses. Enquiries here often involve students moving between curricula and needing an equivalency question answered before a tuition plan makes any sense at all.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and The Gardens
regions.note: High-density apartment living where a quiet room is the binding constraint rather than the timetable. Shorter 45-minute sessions with headphones and a written follow-up task work better than 90-minute blocks in a shared living space.

schoolClusters.city: Central Dubai IB schools
schoolClusters.note: This cluster produces the most tuition enquiries in the emirate, and the practical complication is that each school runs its own internal assessment calendar. A tutor working with students from three of these schools is managing three different autumn deadlines, which is why the school name is asked for at enquiry rather than later.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern and Creek-side continuum schools
schoolClusters.note: Schools running the programme sequence from primary upward, with Middle Years cohorts that are large relative to the rest of Dubai. Criterion-based reporting is the dominant source of confusion for parents in this cluster, and it is usually the first thing a tuition conversation has to unpick.

schoolClusters.city: Southern and western villa-community schools
schoolClusters.note: Serving Arabian Ranches, Emirates Hills, Dubai Hills and the Meadows. Diploma cohorts here are big enough that several students want the same paper in the same week, and we keep every match one-to-one rather than grouping them, which is a deliberate limit on how much we can take in a given week.

dubai/ib-tuition.modesIntro: Three ways tuition is organised through IB Gram, all one-to-one and all over live video. The difference between them is the job being done, not the price band, and most families in Dubai use more than one across a school year as the calendar changes what matters.

modes.title: Fixed weekly subject slot
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same time each week in Gulf Standard Time. The reason to fix the slot rather than book flexibly is that flexible tuition quietly becomes occasional tuition, and occasional tuition does not move a grade. Families who travel often or whose children board part of the year can agree a reduced but still fixed pattern instead, which holds far better than ad hoc booking.
bullets: Same tutor, same weekday, 45 or 60 minutes
A written note after each lesson, sent to the parent
Work set between sessions marked rather than only assigned
A review at four sessions that can end the arrangement cleanly

modes.title: Short diagnostic block
modes.description: Two or three sessions to answer a specific question: whether Higher Level is realistic, which of two subjects is actually the weak one, whether an internally assessed component is salvageable in the time available. A diagnostic block has an end date built in. It is the honest option for a family that is not sure tuition is the right purchase, and it is sold as a question rather than as a course.
bullets: A stated question answered in writing at the end
Built from the student's own marked work, not a placement test
No commitment to continue and no package to cancel
A clear recommendation, including no further tuition where that is the answer

modes.title: Internal assessment and core cycle
modes.description: Scheduled feedback on drafts the student has produced, across an exploration, investigation, commentary, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. The cycle is built backwards from the school's internal deadlines rather than the examination series, and every feedback conversation is logged with a date. The student produces every word that is submitted; the tutor reads against the criteria and asks the questions the criteria ask.
bullets: Planned backwards from the school's own draft deadlines
Feedback expressed in the language of the published criteria
A dated feedback log the student can show a supervisor
No sentences supplied and no restructuring done on the student's behalf

sections.heading: Four tuition arrangements in Dubai, compared on what differs
paragraphs: IB tuition in Dubai is sold in four shapes. A learning centre runs scheduled group classes on premises and holds an educational services permit for doing so. A freelance tutor visits homes or works online as an individual. An agency matches families with tutors it recruits and takes a margin. A platform runs one-to-one lessons online at scale. The hourly rates overlap in places and the products do not.

The dimension families most often fail to check is ratio. A group of eight students for sixty minutes is not eight hours of teaching divided by eight; the attention each student receives is a fraction of the hour and the pace is set by the middle of the room. For a confident student revising familiar content that can be perfectly adequate and much cheaper. For a student losing marks for a reason nobody has yet identified, it is close to useless, because identifying that reason requires someone to read their work.

The second dimension is the evidence trail. A centre can usually produce attendance and a scheme of work. A freelance tutor may produce nothing written at all. A good agency or platform produces per-session records. The question is not whether a provider is willing to talk about progress but whether there is a document with a date on it, and the table below sets out what each arrangement typically yields.

Nothing here is a judgement about any particular provider, and comparing models rather than brands is deliberate. The dirham bands are market figures with their publishers named in the rates table further down this page. What matters for a decision is matching the arrangement to the job: group revision, individual diagnosis, deadline management, or subject teaching that is simply not available locally.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit and this is the part of the market most families never ask about. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation lists eligible applicants as including teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

The official application route is the Ministry's own service, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the Ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed and a two working day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the Ministry's own wording, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you, and a provider who cites a precise penalty amount is repeating something unverified.

There is a separate and often confused question about organisations. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs an educational services permit for a training institute from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific thing issued to institutions with a physical site. It is not something an individual tutor holds, and it is not something IB Gram claims.

A further rule catches families who ask their child's own teacher for paid help. Abu Dhabi's Department of Education and Knowledge has professional ethics rules barring private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct also restricts serving students affiliated with the tutor's school. Treat the exact wording as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document, but take the principle seriously: your child's own subject teacher is the wrong person to pay privately.

sections.heading: Group tuition versus one-to-one: the minutes arithmetic
paragraphs: A sixty-minute group class with eight students does not give each student sixty minutes of teaching. It gives each student a share of the teacher's attention, a pace set by the median of the room, and a question allowance of perhaps three or four. That is not an argument against groups. It is an argument for knowing what you are buying, because the per-hour price difference between a group seat and an individual session in Dubai is roughly the ratio itself, which means the real comparison is cost per useful minute rather than cost per hour.

Groups work well in three situations. The first is revision of content the student already broadly knows, where hearing other students' questions genuinely adds value. The second is motivation, where a student works harder in company than alone. The third is cost, where a family needs some support across four subjects and cannot fund individual sessions in all of them. In all three the student has to be able to keep up with the room, because a student who cannot is paying to be confused in company.

One-to-one earns its premium in the opposite case: when nobody yet knows why the marks are being lost. Diagnosis requires someone to read that student's work, sort the lost marks, and change the explanation until it lands. None of that is possible at a ratio of eight, and no amount of good group teaching substitutes for it. The same is true of internally assessed work, where the feedback has to be about one student's specific draft and criteria.

The sensible pattern for many Dubai families is a mixture, sequenced rather than simultaneous. Start with a short individual diagnostic block to find out what is actually wrong. Fix the identified error class individually. Then, if the student is stable and the issue was content rather than technique, move the ongoing revision into a cheaper group or into supervised independent work. Paying individual rates for revision a student could do in a group is as wasteful as paying group rates for a diagnosis that needs an individual.

sections.heading: The monthly tuition audit: five documents to ask for
paragraphs: Any tuition arrangement in Dubai should be able to produce five things once a month, and a provider that cannot produce them is being managed on trust alone. None of the five is onerous and none requires the parent to understand the subject. They exist so that a disappointing term is identified in week five rather than week fifteen.

The first is a session log with dates, showing what was attempted and what it scored. The second is at least one piece of marked work per month with the lost marks identified by type rather than by topic. The third is the current error list, ranked, so you can see whether the top item is the same one as last month. The fourth is the task record: what was set between sessions and whether it was done and marked. The fifth is a forward plan naming the next deadline the work is pointed at.

The reason to insist monthly rather than termly is the length of a Diploma. Two years is long enough that a slow failure feels like patience. A month is short enough to change course cheaply, and the cost of changing a tutor at week four is nothing while the cost of changing at week thirty is a term of a student's time. Monthly also matches the rhythm of school reporting, so the two records can be read side by side.

If a provider resists, the useful question is which of the five they object to producing. A reasonable answer exists for some arrangements: a group centre genuinely cannot produce individually marked work for every student every month, which is itself informative. An individual tutor charging a specialist rate has no such excuse.

sections.heading: Maths AA or AI: the route choice, and what UAE universities expect
paragraphs: The decision between Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is made in Grade 10 or early Grade 11 and it shapes everything afterwards. It is also made badly in a predictable way: families treat Analysis and Approaches as the prestigious option and Applications and Interpretation as the fallback, when the two courses genuinely suit different students and different destinations.

Analysis and Approaches is algebra-first and proof-oriented, with calculus at its centre. Applications and Interpretation is modelling-first, statistics-heavy and expects confident technology use. A student who enjoys structure, manipulation and abstraction belongs in the first. A student who thinks well about real data and dislikes abstraction belongs in the second, and will often score higher there than in a course that fights their instincts for two years.

The admissions question has to be answered specifically rather than generally. Engineering, mathematics, physics and many economics courses commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level, and some will not accept the alternative at all. Medicine, life sciences, business and social sciences are more often flexible. The only safe method is to read the published entry requirements for the actual course at the actual university, including the UAE institutions a student may apply to, and to do it before the subject choice is locked rather than after.

sections.heading: Word and page limits, and what overrunning costs
paragraphs: Several IB components carry a stated limit, and students lose marks for exceeding them in ways that feel disproportionate until you understand the mechanism: beyond the limit, work may simply not be read. That makes a limit a structural constraint on planning rather than a formatting detail, and it is one of the few parts of the Diploma where a tutor can save a grade by insisting on arithmetic in October.

The limits also change what a draft should look like. A student who writes a long first draft and then cuts loses the argument's shape; a student who plans to the limit from the start writes a tighter piece and has time to improve it. For the Extended Essay in particular, the practical implication is that the research question has to be narrow enough to answer inside the allowance, and a question that cannot be is a planning failure rather than a writing one.

Exact limits for your child's components must come from the current subject guide and from the school, because they are revised between syllabus cycles and they differ by subject and by level. The table below names the components, who enforces the limit and what the real consequence of overrunning is. It is written so a parent can ask the right question rather than so a student can skip reading the guide.

The useful habit is to treat the limit as a design constraint discussed in the first supervision meeting, alongside the research question. Students who meet their limit comfortably almost always wrote a better piece, because the discipline of fitting an argument into an allowance is the same discipline that produces a clear argument.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the Dubai school calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: Dubai's academic year carries fixed points that reshape any revision plan, and tuition that ignores them produces a schedule nobody can keep. Term dates, the winter and spring breaks, the National Day period and Ramadan all land in predictable places relative to the examination series, and the weeks that look available on paper are frequently not available in practice.

Ramadan is the one most often handled badly by providers who are not based in the region. School days shorten, energy in the late afternoon drops markedly, and the useful study window for many families moves to after Iftar. A tuition schedule that keeps a 17:00 slot through Ramadan because that is when the slot was agreed will simply be missed. Moving the same session to a later evening slot for the month is a small administrative act that preserves a term of continuity.

The second calendar effect is the gap between the end of taught content and the examination window. In the Diploma that gap is filled by school revision and study leave, and it is the point at which families often try to add hours. Adding hours then is less effective than it feels, because technique built in the last fortnight has no time to become habit. The weeks that repay investment sit earlier, in the autumn of the second year, when there is still time for a changed approach to bed in.

The practical response is to agree the exceptions when the slot is agreed. Which weeks are off. What Ramadan timing will be. Whether sessions continue through the school's study leave or stop. Writing that down at the start removes the monthly negotiation that quietly erodes an arrangement, and it also tells a family honestly how many sessions the year actually contains.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: what each curriculum must show
paragraphs: Certificate equivalency is the process by which a school-leaving qualification is recognised in the UAE, and it is almost entirely absent from the pages competing for this search. It matters because a family can complete an international programme and discover a documentation problem at the point of applying to a UAE university, which is the worst possible moment to find out.

For the British track the requirements have been published clearly. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That five-subject rule is worth noting because at least one competing page in this market publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong.

For the American track, English proficiency is satisfied by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold published in the source behind these figures, so no IB equivalency number appears on this page. Check it on the Ministry's own site or with the emirate attestation authority before relying on any figure you are given.

Two cautions apply to the whole process. Equivalency is performed by the Ministry and the relevant authority, not by a tutoring provider, and nobody in this market can guarantee an outcome in it. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Moving into the Diploma from IGCSE, MYP or an American route
paragraphs: Dubai moves students between curricula more than almost anywhere, and the first term of the Diploma is where the consequences surface. A student arriving from IGCSE has usually been taught to a specification and rewarded for recall. A student arriving from the Middle Years Programme has criterion habits but may have met less content. A student arriving from an American high school has breadth and often a gap in algebraic fluency. These are different first terms and they need different tuition.

The common mistake is to treat the transition as a general adjustment period and wait for it to resolve. It usually does not resolve on its own in the subjects where the gap is technical. Algebraic manipulation, scientific notation and unit discipline, and extended writing under time pressure are the three that most often need explicit teaching rather than time, and all three are cheap to fix in the first term and expensive to fix in the second year.

The useful diagnostic is narrow. Give the student a question from the new course rather than a test of the old one, and read what happens. A student who understands the concept but cannot execute the algebra has a fluency problem with a known cure. A student who executes well but cannot structure a long answer has a writing problem. A student who cannot start has a content gap that needs mapping against the subject guide before any plan is made.

sections.heading: What tuition cannot fix, and how we say so
paragraphs: Some problems presented as subject weaknesses are not subject weaknesses, and selling tuition for them is the most common quiet dishonesty in this market. A Grade 12 student with three internally assessed components overdue and five hours of sleep a night does not have a chemistry problem. A Grade 7 student who cannot read fluently does not have a science problem. An undiagnosed need, a family upheaval or straightforward exhaustion all present as a grade and none of them responds to weekly subject teaching.

The first conversation on every match therefore asks what else is happening, and sometimes ends with a recommendation not to buy tuition at all. That recommendation is worth more than a booking, and a provider unwilling to give it is a provider whose advice cannot be trusted in the cases where tuition genuinely is the answer.

The second limit is availability, and it is disclosed rather than concealed. Coverage is deep in Diploma mathematics, the sciences, economics, business and English, and thinner in several group two languages, in the arts and in less commonly taken options. Where no suitable specialist is free at the time a family needs, we give a realistic wait rather than filling the slot with someone teaching an adjacent subject. Marked work exposes that substitution within a fortnight anyway.

What happens next is short. Send the subject, the level, the school and a recent piece of marked work. We come back with a named tutor and a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, usually within two working days. The first lesson is free for one student per family, with no card details taken. Lessons are one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and anyone promising a tutor at a Dubai address is describing a different arrangement from ours.

process.title: Decide which arrangement you are actually buying
process.description: Group revision, individual diagnosis, deadline management or access to a subject nobody local teaches. These need different arrangements and different budgets, and the commonest expensive mistake in Dubai is buying one and expecting another. The comparison table on this page is designed to be used before you enquire anywhere, including here.

process.title: Ask the permit question once, early
process.description: Whoever you use, ask whether the individual teaching your child holds the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit. It is free, valid two years, and applied for through the Ministry's own e-services. A provider who cannot answer clearly has told you something useful about how it recruits.

process.title: Send the school, the subject and marked work
process.description: The school name matters because internal assessment calendars differ across Dubai, and the marked work matters because it replaces a week of diagnosis with five minutes of reading. With both, a first session starts on the actual problem instead of on introductions and a placement test.

process.title: Use the free lesson to test the marking, not the manner
process.description: One free trial lesson per student, no card details collected. Everyone is personable in a trial. What distinguishes a specialist is whether they can mark your child's work against the published criteria and explain the lost marks by category. Ask for exactly that and judge the written note you get afterwards.

process.title: Run the five-document audit monthly
process.description: Session log, one marked piece, a ranked error list, the task record and a forward plan. Five minutes a month, no subject knowledge required, and it moves the decision point from week fifteen to week five. Any provider's reaction to being asked is itself part of the answer.

whyPoints.title: The arrangement is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: One-to-one lessons over live video, no premises in Dubai, no group pricing dressed up as individual attention, and no home visits anywhere in the UAE. Knowing exactly what is being sold is the first thing a Dubai family should get from a tuition page and the thing this market most often withholds.

whyPoints.title: Permit and regulator facts cited to their sources
whyPoints.description: The private tuition permit, its two-year validity, its absence of a fee and its official application route all come from Ministry guidance rather than from marketing. Where a figure is unverified, including fine amounts and IB equivalency points, this page says so instead of repeating it.

whyPoints.title: Market rates in dirhams, with publishers named
whyPoints.description: Three of the best-ranking pages for this search publish no price and two quote in dollars. Every band here names who published it, and none of it is presented as an IB Gram quote. The only priced commitment is one free first lesson with its condition in the same sentence.

whyPoints.title: The upstream decisions handled properly
whyPoints.description: Maths route choice, Ministry equivalency and curriculum transition are decisions that outlast any tutor, and they get tables rather than a sentence. Getting these right is worth more to a Dubai family than any hourly rate, and almost nobody competing for this search addresses them at all.

whyPoints.title: A stated willingness to say no
whyPoints.description: If the problem is not a tuition problem, or no suitable specialist is free, or the remaining weeks cannot do what a family hopes, we say that. Disclosing a coverage limit costs a booking occasionally and it is the only way the advice means anything in the cases where we do take the work.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB tuition at a Dubai centre and one-to-one online tuition?
faqs.answer: Ratio, accountability and evidence. A centre group means a share of a teacher's hour at a pace set by the middle of the room, backed by a permit held for the premises and usually an attendance record. One-to-one online means the whole hour, a pace set by your child, and per-session written notes if the provider produces them. Centres are cheaper per hour and genuinely good for revising known content. Individual sessions are what diagnosis and internally assessed feedback require, because both depend on someone reading your child's own work.

faqs.question: Does my child's IB tutor in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation grants the private tuition work permit free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through the Ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount with caution.

faqs.question: How many students should be in an IB group class before it stops being useful?
faqs.answer: There is no official number, so judge it by what your child needs. For revising content they already broadly know, a group of six or eight can work well and hearing other students' questions adds something. For identifying why marks are being lost, any group is too large, because the diagnosis requires someone to read that student's script and change the explanation until it lands. A practical test: ask how many questions your child asked last session. If the answer is none, the ratio is wrong for them whatever the group size is.

faqs.question: Which five documents should I ask a Dubai tuition provider for each month?
faqs.answer: A dated session log showing what was attempted and what it scored; at least one piece of marked work with lost marks sorted by type rather than topic; a ranked error list you can compare with last month's; the task record showing what was set, done and marked; and a forward plan naming the next deadline the work targets. None needs subject knowledge to read. Their purpose is to move the moment you notice a term is not working from week fifteen to week five, when changing course still costs almost nothing.

faqs.question: Which maths route should a Dubai student pick, AA or AI, and who decides?
faqs.answer: It depends on how they think and where they are applying, not on which sounds more impressive. Analysis and Approaches is algebra-first and proof-oriented with calculus at its centre. Applications and Interpretation is modelling-first, statistics-heavy and expects confident technology use. Engineering, mathematics, physics and many economics courses commonly expect the former, often at Higher Level. Life sciences, business and social sciences are frequently flexible. Read the published entry requirements for the actual course at the actual university before the choice is locked, and use a short diagnostic rather than a conversation to test fit.

faqs.question: Do word limits on IB components really cost marks if we go over?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the mechanism surprises families: beyond the stated limit, work may simply not be read, so the criteria that section was meant to satisfy go unmet. That makes a limit a planning constraint rather than a formatting rule. The practical consequence is that a research question has to be narrow enough to answer inside the allowance, and a question that is not is a planning failure. Confirm the current figure for each component with your school and the relevant subject guide, because limits are revised between syllabus cycles.

faqs.question: How should IB tuition in Dubai be scheduled around Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Agree it when the slot is agreed, not when the month arrives. School days shorten, late-afternoon energy drops noticeably, and for many Dubai families the usable study window moves to after Iftar. A session fixed at five o'clock because that is when it was arranged in September will be missed through Ramadan, and missed sessions are how an arrangement quietly dies. Moving the same slot later for the month preserves continuity. Write the exceptions down at the start, including term breaks and whether sessions run through school study leave.

faqs.question: What does the UAE Ministry of Education require from a British-curriculum student for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Published guidance requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, plus passes in five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. At least one competing page in this market states six subjects, which is incorrect. Equivalency is performed by the Ministry and the attestation authority, never by a tutoring provider, and no provider can guarantee the outcome.

faqs.question: Has anyone published an IB points threshold for Dubai equivalency paperwork?
faqs.answer: Not in the sources behind this page, which is why no figure appears here. The British-track requirements are clearly published and the American-track test thresholds are too, but the guidance consulted states no IB points threshold. Anyone quoting one to you should be asked where they read it, and the only acceptable answer is the Ministry's own site or the emirate's attestation authority. Check it directly before making a decision that depends on it, and be wary of any provider that treats tutoring as a requirement for the process.

faqs.question: My child is joining DP1 mid-year from an American school. Where should tuition start?
faqs.answer: With a mapped list of what has not been covered, before any teaching. Students arriving from an American high school usually bring breadth, good coursework habits and a gap in algebraic fluency and in extended writing under timed conditions. Two or three sessions spent mapping actual coverage against the subject guide saves a term of teaching in the wrong order. After the map, the first targets are almost always algebraic manipulation and the structure of a long evaluative answer, both of which are far cheaper to fix in the first term than the second year.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a few sessions to answer one question rather than commit to a term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some families that is the right purchase. A short diagnostic block of two or three sessions can answer a specific question in writing: whether Higher Level is realistic, which of two subjects is the real weakness, whether an internally assessed component can still be rescued in the time available. It has an end date built in and no commitment to continue. The honest outcome is sometimes a recommendation against further tuition, which is more useful than a term booked on an unexamined assumption.

faqs.question: Is it acceptable to pay my child's own school teacher for private lessons in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Treat it as the wrong arrangement. Abu Dhabi's Department of Education and Knowledge has professional ethics rules barring private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the Ministry permit carries a code of conduct that also restricts serving students affiliated with the tutor's school. Verify the exact current wording with the authority before relying on it, but the principle is sound and the conflict is obvious: the person setting internal marks should not also be paid privately by the family.

faqs.question: How quickly can IB tuition in Dubai actually start?
faqs.answer: Usually a named tutor and a proposed weekly slot within two working days of receiving the subject, level, school and a sample of marked work, with the free first lesson in the following few days. The honest exception is subject coverage. Diploma mathematics, the sciences, economics, business and English are deep. Several group two languages, some arts subjects and less commonly taken options are thinner, and when nothing suitable is free we give a realistic wait rather than offering a tutor who teaches the adjacent subject.

faqs.question: Do you hold a KHDA permit for tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, and the distinction matters. The educational services permit for a training institute is issued by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority to organisations with premises and staff in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram operates no premises in Dubai, so that permit does not apply to us and we do not claim it. Any provider describing its tutors as approved by a regulator is making a claim worth asking them to evidence with a permit number.

faqs.question: What if we try one month of tuition and nothing changes?
faqs.answer: Then the five documents should already have told you why, and the answer is usually one of three things. The teaching has not reached the error class that is costing the most marks, in which case the approach changes. The subject chosen is not where the marks actually are, in which case the subject changes. Or the problem is not a tuition problem at all, in which case stopping is the correct decision and we will say so. What should not happen is a second month bought on the hope that the first was an exception.

dubai/ib-tuition.closingHeading: Audit the arrangement before you buy the hours
dubai/ib-tuition.closingBody: Work out which of the four arrangements your child actually needs, ask the permit question once, and then send the subject, the level, the school and a recent piece of marked work. We come back with a named specialist and a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, usually inside two working days. The first lesson is free for one student per family, with no card details collected, and it is spent on the work you sent. Tuition runs one-to-one over live video to every Dubai community, and if no suitable specialist is free when you need one, you will be told that rather than offered a substitute.

intro.heading: Four different things are called IB tuition in Dubai
paragraphs: The phrase hides more than it reveals. A parent searching for IB tuition near me in Dubai is shown tuition centres in Al Quoz and Al Barsha, freelance tutors advertising by community, international marketplaces with no UAE presence, and one-to-one teaching services. These are not variations on one product. They differ in group size, in what permission they need to operate, in whether anybody marks work against a published scheme, and in cost by a factor of ten.

Group size is the variable that changes the most and is discussed the least. A tuition centre running an IB Mathematics group of six is a small class, and a small class is a perfectly reasonable thing to buy for syllabus coverage. It is not a diagnostic instrument. In a group of six nobody watches one student's working line by line, which is where the information about why marks are being lost actually lives. For some Diploma components that matters enormously and for others it hardly matters at all.

The permissions differ too, and the distinction is worth knowing before a cheque is written. An individual tutor in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. A tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry.

The geography is misleading as well. Dubai's tuition premises cluster where commercial rent and footfall make sense — Al Quoz, Al Barsha, Karama, Oud Metha, parts of Deira — and that is not where the Diploma cohorts are largest. A family in Nad Al Sheba or the Sustainable City searching locally will be shown centres twenty minutes away whose main business is a different curriculum entirely, and whose IB group may have three students in it.

So this page is organised around a different question: what does your child's specific component need. A Theory of Knowledge essay needs an hour of argument with one person. An Economics evaluation paragraph needs somebody reading the student's own sentences. Arabic script practice genuinely benefits from a pair. Working out which of those you have is worth more than comparing hourly rates across four products that are not alike.

On delivery, the plain version. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing and a shared annotation surface. We do not run premises in Dubai and we do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. There is no group option, and there is no centre to drive to.

dubai/ib-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Tuition is sold at every stage of the IB continuum, but what it should be doing changes completely between them. The notes below say what each programme is actually examined on, which determines whether a group can help at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Externally examined papers plus internally assessed work worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade. The externally examined half responds reasonably to group teaching for coverage; the internally assessed half does not, because it is one student's own piece of work marked against criteria and nobody else's draft is relevant to it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts sit the May session. The tuition centres in the emirate tend to advertise Diploma group classes in the final two terms, which is the point at which coverage is least useful and diagnosis is most useful. A family buying group tuition in DP2 is often buying a second pass through content the student has already seen.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Marked on criteria A to D rather than by percentage, and that is the single thing most tuition at this stage ignores. A group class teaching Year 9 mathematics content is teaching the wrong thing: the student usually knows the content and does not know what a 7-8 band descriptor is asking for. That translation needs somebody looking at their own work.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running MYP into the Diploma set the personal project in Year 11, and it is the student's own work, so no group class can touch it. What a tutor can do is process coaching and criterion feedback. The most common useful MYP brief in the emirate is mathematics in the two terms before DP1 begins.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations, no percentages, continuous teacher assessment. Tuition at this stage is almost never about the IB and almost always about reading fluency, number sense or English as an additional language. Small groups work well for all three, which makes primary the one stage where a local centre is often the sensible answer.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in every Dubai private school, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils and combined classes explicitly prohibited. Any centre offering an Arabic class should be able to say which of the two streams it is teaching, and the use of content other than the Ministry's approved material is not permitted without prior permission.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. The Diploma courses are examined identically to the full Diploma, so tuition for those is a familiar brief. The career-related units are assessed by the provider, and no general tuition centre will know their criteria.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Dubai schools license the Career-related Programme, so a local search returns nothing specific to it and group classes do not exist at any sensible size. The practical approach is one-to-one on the Diploma courses and a conversation with the school's coordinator about what the reflective project criteria require.

dubai/ib-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: The useful question is not which subjects we cover but which ones tolerate a group. Below, by subject, whether a class of six can genuinely help and what has to happen one-to-one regardless of how the tuition is bought.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Content coverage survives a group; diagnosis does not. The marks here are lost in the working, and in a class of six nobody reads six students' working. Calculus and proof at Higher Level need one-to-one. Topic revision at Standard Level is reasonable in a pair.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical tests can be taught to a group. The written conclusion that must follow a test cannot, because it is a writing problem dressed as a maths problem and each student writes differently. Documented calculator work also needs watching individually.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Equilibrium and energetics teach well to a small group. Paper 3 data handling and the internal investigation do not: both are about responding to unfamiliar material, which is individual by definition. Mechanism work sits in between and benefits from a pair.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Numerical topics are group-friendly. The written-explanation questions that ask for a reason rather than a value are the opposite, because the fix is to each student's own prose. Dubai cohorts are typically strong on the first and thin on the second.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Recall-heavy topics are efficient in a group. Data-based questions on unfamiliar contexts are not, since the whole skill is reading a graph nobody has seen before. A group class usually ends up teaching content the student already had.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams and definitions are genuinely better in a group, where students can challenge each other's curves. Evaluation paragraphs are strictly one-to-one: the mark is in the judgement a particular student reaches, and nobody else's version helps them write it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study discussion is one of the few places where a group adds something real, because hearing another reading of the stimulus is useful. Quantitative questions and the internal assessment are individual work and should be bought as such.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Technique vocabulary teaches well to a group. Paper 1 unseen analysis does not, because the whole assessment is one student's response to a text in front of them. The Individual Oral is individual in name and in practice.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Text-type conventions suit a small group, and the oral practice benefits from more than one voice in the room. This is the subject where a pair or a trio is most defensible across the whole Diploma.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Building a case-study bank of named dates, figures and actors works in a group and is faster there. Source analysis in Paper 1 needs one-to-one, because the skill is a particular student's reading of a particular extract under time.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Discussion genuinely improves with more than two people, which is why schools teach it as a class. The essay does not: it is one student's argument, and the only useful help is criterion feedback on their own draft. Never a group product.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Script formation and vocabulary retention respond well to a pair or small group, with repetition doing the work. KHDA sets the content and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils, so ask any provider which stream they are actually teaching.

dubai/ib-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: The notes below record where Dubai's tuition premises actually sit and what that means for a family searching locally — including the districts where a local result is almost certainly the wrong curriculum.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Khail
regions.note: One of the emirate's two main tuition-centre belts, built around warehouse and light-industrial units with cheap floorspace. Most of the IB-labelled groups here are small, and the centres' core business is other curricula.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: The other centre belt, and the one closest to the city's densest IB school cluster. A local search from here returns the most genuinely IB-relevant centres in Dubai, which is not true of anywhere else in the emirate.

regions.name: Karama and Oud Metha
regions.note: A long-established tuition district serving a largely Indian-curriculum school population. IB group classes advertised here are usually small, and the subject range narrows sharply above Standard Level.

regions.name: Bur Dubai and Al Mankhool
regions.note: Dense, walkable and full of small education businesses, which makes it the easiest place in the city to visit three centres in an afternoon. Diploma-specific provision is thin relative to the number of signs.

regions.name: Deira and Al Rigga
regions.note: High footfall and low rents, so plenty of listings. The school population nearby is dominated by other curricula, so an IB family searching here is usually matched to a generalist rather than a Diploma specialist.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Two established IB continuum schools and almost no tuition premises, which is the clearest example in Dubai of supply and need sitting in different postcodes. Families here search locally and find nothing relevant.

regions.name: The Sustainable City and Dubai Investments Park
regions.note: Continuum IB schools on the city's southern edge with no local centre belt at all. The nearest premises are a twenty-five minute drive in evening traffic, which is most of a usable evening for a round trip.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Mizhar
regions.note: A full IB continuum school plus large schools on other curricula, and a scattering of small local centres. Early school returns here make a 4pm one-to-one slot realistic, which a centre's fixed class timetable rarely offers.

schoolClusters.city: Oud Metha, Karama and Bur Dubai
schoolClusters.note: A dense school district where most pupils are on Indian or British curricula and the IB cohort is comparatively small. Students we support here are often the only Diploma candidate on their street, which is exactly the case where a local group class has nobody to group them with.

schoolClusters.city: Al Quoz, Al Khail and Al Safa
schoolClusters.note: Schools sitting beside the emirate's largest tuition-centre belt, which means families here have the most local options and the least clarity about what each one is. The useful question in this cluster is always group size and who marks the work.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Barsha Heights and The Greens
schoolClusters.note: The closest thing Dubai has to a district where local tuition and IB provision overlap. Students we support in this cluster ask most often for Higher Level sciences, and the honest answer is frequently that the component they need help with cannot be taught in a group at all.

dubai/ib-tuition-near-me.modesIntro: Three ways we structure one-to-one tuition. None of them is a group, and the choice between them is made by what the next assessment is rather than by how much coverage sounds reassuring.

modes.title: Component block
modes.description: Four to six sessions aimed at one named thing: Paper 3 data handling, source analysis in History Paper 1, documented calculator work, or the structure of a Theory of Knowledge exhibition. It has a start date, an end date and a marked piece of work at each end so the block can be judged rather than renewed by default.
bullets: One component, four to six sessions, a stated endpoint
Baseline and closing scripts both marked against the scheme
No automatic rollover into an open-ended arrangement
Priced and agreed as a block before it starts

modes.title: Standing weekly subject slot
modes.description: A fixed 60-minute session each week on one subject at one level, across a term. Suits a Higher Level subject where the problem is cumulative rather than a single component, and suits a DP1 student who is working hard without the result moving. Every session produces a written note and a topic checklist entry.

Topic checklist updated every third or fourth session
Week-six review against the baseline script
Marking done between sessions, not inside the hour

modes.title: Coursework supervision to the student's own draft stages
modes.description: Sessions tied to internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge deadlines, working to the stages the school has set. Feedback is written by criterion and delivered separately from the document, so the draft stays entirely the student's work and the record stands up if a coordinator asks.
