sections.heading: The four products a Dubai search calls IB tuition
paragraphs: Sorting the results page by what each provider actually is takes about five minutes and saves a term. A tuition centre sells a seat in a class, usually of three to eight students, on a fixed timetable, at premises you drive to. A freelance tutor sells an hour of their own time, often travelling. An international marketplace sells access to a list and takes a cut. A one-to-one teaching service sells a matched specialist and the marking that goes with them.

Each is a reasonable purchase for a different problem. For syllabus coverage after a term of disrupted teaching, a centre class is efficient and cheap per hour. For a student who needs an adult present to start work at all, a freelance visit is the service. For a rare Language B option, a marketplace may be the only place anyone exists. For a Higher Level component where marks are being lost for reasons nobody has identified, one-to-one is the only one of the four that can find out why.

The question that separates them fastest is: who reads my child's working. In a group of six, nobody does, because there is not time. On a marketplace, whoever you picked, to a standard you cannot see in advance. With a travelling freelancer, usually during the lesson, which costs you ten minutes of the hour. With a one-to-one service that marks between sessions, before the lesson, which is the only arrangement where the hour starts with a diagnosis already in hand.

The second question is what happens when it is not working. A centre will offer a different class. A marketplace will offer a different name and the same process. A good one-to-one service will change the specialist on request without requiring a reason, and should say so before you book rather than after you complain.
The table sets the four side by side with the group size and the honest use case for each, so you can place the listings a local search returns before ringing any of them.

sections.heading: A centre's permit and a tutor's permit are different documents
paragraphs: Parents often ask whether a provider is licensed, which is a good question with two different answers depending on what the provider is. The two permissions are separate instruments issued by separate authorities for separate activities, and a provider holding one does not hold the other.

For an individual, the instrument is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists a two-working-day completion time and is the official route. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

For a business with premises and staff in Dubai, the instrument is a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. That process begins with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requires renewal to be requested at least 30 days before expiry. It is a specific permission issued to a specific address. A provider without premises in Dubai does not hold it and should not imply that it does.

That second point applies to us, so it is worth saying directly. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, no ADEK or SPEA registration, no Ministry of Education licence, and no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We are an independent tutor-matching platform. Any provider in this market describing its tutors as approved by a regulator is making a claim worth asking to see in document form.

What a parent can reasonably verify is in the table. All of it is a question you can ask by email and keep the answer to, which is the practical point: a provider comfortable answering in writing is telling you something, and so is one that is not.

sections.heading: Where the centres are, and where the Diploma students are
paragraphs: These two maps do not overlap, and that single fact explains most of the frustration families report with local tuition searches in Dubai. Tuition premises need affordable floorspace and passing trade, which puts them in Al Quoz, Al Barsha, Karama, Oud Metha, Bur Dubai and parts of Deira. IB continuum schools have been built where new family housing has been built, which puts their cohorts in Nad Al Sheba, Meydan, the Sustainable City, Dubai Investments Park, Mirdif and Al Jaddaf.

A family in the Sustainable City searching for IB tuition near me gets results from a belt twenty-five minutes away in evening traffic. That round trip is fifty minutes of a usable evening that is only about 150 minutes long, before any teaching happens. For a 60-minute group class, the family is spending nearly two hours of the student's evening to buy a sixth of a teacher's attention.

Al Barsha is the exception worth naming, because it is the one part of Dubai where the centre belt and the densest IB school cluster genuinely coincide. A local search from Al Barsha or Barsha Heights returns centres that actually run IB groups with enough students in them to be classes rather than small huddles. Everywhere else in the emirate, the IB label on a local centre is likely to sit on a group of two or three.

Group size is worth asking about explicitly and in writing. A class of six teaching Standard Level Economics diagrams is a class. A class of two is a very expensive form of one-to-one with a third of the attention, and families are rarely told the number before they arrive. The honest question is: how many students will be in the room on the evening we come, in this subject, at this level.

None of this argues that centres are bad. It argues that proximity is a poor way to choose one, because the nearest centre's main business is probably a different curriculum, and the distance you are being asked to drive is coming out of the only part of the day in which your child can still learn anything.

sections.heading: Group of six, group of two, one-to-one: what each does to a subject
paragraphs: Attention divides. That is not a criticism of group teaching, it is arithmetic, and it has different consequences depending on what the hour is supposed to achieve. For content coverage, division costs little: one explanation of equilibrium serves six students as well as one. For diagnosis, division is fatal, because the information lives in each student's own working and nobody can read six sets of working in sixty minutes.

The practical rule that follows is about the stage of the problem rather than the subject. If the student has not met the content, a group is efficient. If the student has met the content, can explain it, and is still losing marks, the problem is in their execution and only individual attention will locate it. Most Dubai families buying tuition in DP2 are in the second situation and buying the first product.

There is a social dimension that matters more than it sounds. A student who will attempt a hard question with one adult will not attempt it in front of five classmates from a nearby school, and the question they avoid is the one carrying the diagnosis. In a city as socially interconnected as Dubai's school market, that is not a trivial consideration for a 17-year-old.

Where a group genuinely wins is in the handful of places where another student's answer is useful to hear: Theory of Knowledge discussion, Business Management case readings, Language B oral practice, Economics diagram challenges, Arabic repetition drills. That is a real list and it is shorter than the one centres advertise.

The table below places group sizes against what a Diploma subject actually needs, so the conversation with a centre can be about the specific component rather than about the subject name on the timetable.

sections.heading: Subject by subject: what the tuition should be fixing
paragraphs: Tuition sold by the subject tends to teach the subject. Tuition sold by the component fixes the thing that is costing marks. The difference shows up in the first invoice: eight hours of Chemistry, or four hours of Paper 3 data handling and the internal investigation method. The second is cheaper and more likely to move a grade, and it requires somebody to have read a marked script first.

The patterns in the table are the ones that repeat across Dubai cohorts. Two of them deserve pulling out. In the sciences, students are usually competent numerically and thin on written explanation, so the remedy is a writing intervention inside a science subject — which a group class covering content will never deliver. In the humanities, the constraint is nearly always named detail rather than argument, so building a case-study bank beats more essay practice.

The session counts are rough and they are deliberately small. Most component problems are four to six sessions of work, not a two-year subscription. A provider quoting an open-ended weekly commitment for a single identified component is selling continuity rather than a fix, and a family should ask what the endpoint looks like and how it will be measured.

The way to use the table is backwards. Find the component your child's last marked paper shows the loss in, read across to the session count, and compare that against what you have been quoted. If the quote is three times the number, ask what the extra sessions are for.

If the loss is not identifiable from the papers you have, that is the first thing tuition should buy: one timed question, marked against the published scheme, with a written diagnosis. In our process that happens in the free trial lesson, before anybody has paid for anything.

sections.heading: What a monthly tuition package in Dubai actually contains
paragraphs: Packages are how most tuition in this market is sold, and they are the hardest thing to compare because the unit is a month rather than an hour. Figures published in this market, read in October 2026, cluster around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other providers' published prices, not ours, and they are not the same product.

Convert everything to minutes and to notes before comparing. Eight 60-minute sessions give weekly contact and eight separate written records; four two-hour visits give the same total minutes with half the contact points and a chunk of each visit spent arriving and settling. For a student who needs steady pressure, the first is better. For one with a single large piece of coursework, the second may be.

Then ask what is inside the number. Marking and written feedback outside the session is the line that most changes the real value per hour, and it is rarely stated. So is whether unused sessions roll over, what notice is needed to cancel, whether the rate changes closer to the May session, and whether VAT is included. Get those four answers in writing before the first payment, because all four become arguments in month three otherwise.

Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions in Dubai give a wider frame: roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those bands are a useful sanity check against any single package price you are quoted.

Our own model is deliberately simpler to compare: a free trial lesson with no card details, then sessions agreed by the week or as a defined component block, with marking between lessons and a written note after each one. What a plan costs depends on subject, level and how many sessions it actually needs, which is a conversation rather than a shelf price.

sections.heading: Private candidates, exam entry, and what nobody can do for you
paragraphs: Some families arrive at tuition because of an entry problem rather than a teaching problem: a subject the school does not offer, a resit, or a student outside school for a term. Entry rules are set by the boards and administered through recognised centres, not by tutors, and this is an area where confident misinformation is common.

Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May/June and November each year, with provisional timetables published ahead of each series.

The worked example of why deadlines sit so far ahead is the Cambridge June series, the main window for a UAE candidate: entries close in the spring, well before the first paper, and forecast grades are collected after that, so a private candidate who starts asking about entry in April has usually already missed June and is in fact choosing the November series. November is both a sitting in its own right and the resit route, which is why the real decision a family makes early in the year is which of those two windows they are entering, not whether they can still join the nearest one. The closing date for a given series is printed on the centre's statement of entry, and it is revised, so take it from there rather than from any page restating it. For IB dates, confirm everything with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org directly, because no IB session or results date in this project has been verified from the IB itself.

What a tutoring provider can do is teach and advise. What it cannot do is enter your child for an examination, choose your zone's timetable, obtain a certificate, or perform Ministry of Education equivalency and attestation. Those sit with recognised examination centres and with the authorities, and any provider presenting them as a service it performs on your behalf is overstating what it can deliver.

Nor should anyone imply that tuition is required for equivalency, admission or progression. It is not. Equivalency is a documentary process run by the Ministry, and the right route is the official channel rather than a tutoring company's assistance package.

sections.heading: Why our tuition runs over live video rather than at a Dubai centre
paragraphs: Said plainly: there is no IB Gram centre in Dubai to attend, and we do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE — visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Every session is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing and a shared annotation surface so a scanned past paper can be marked up by tutor and student together.

The first reason is the one this whole page has been building towards. A centre's economics require a group, and a group cannot do diagnosis. Removing the premises removes the pressure to fill a room, which is what makes one student per session affordable at all. Nobody is being asked to subsidise floorspace in Al Quoz.

The second is the match. Teaching over video means a Higher Level Chemistry student in Mirdif is matched to a Higher Level Chemistry specialist rather than to whichever subject the nearest centre happens to have a teacher for. For the tight combinations — Higher Level sciences in the early-evening Gulf window, Higher Level Computer Science, less common Language B options — that is the difference between a specialist and a substitute.

The third is the evening. A round trip to a centre in Dubai's 5pm traffic is routinely forty to fifty minutes out of a usable window of about 150. A video session starts when your child sits down, which means a Higher Level subject can be taught while they are still able to learn rather than after two car journeys.

The honest limitation is physical work. Bench practicals and arts exhibitions happen at school and belong to the school, and no tuition format changes that. What a video session does with those components is the design, the data treatment and the write-up against the published criteria, which is where most of their marks sit anyway.

sections.heading: The first session: diagnose before teaching anything
paragraphs: A first tuition session that begins by teaching has skipped the only step that was genuinely scarce. Content is available everywhere, including free. What is not available is somebody reading your child's own working and saying, specifically, which four marks went where and why. That is what a first session should produce, and it is what makes everything after it cheaper.

Ours works to a fixed shape. The student attempts one timed question or paper section, unassisted, while the tutor watches the working rather than waiting for the answer. The tutor then marks it against the published scheme and talks through where the marks sat. You receive a written note naming the secure topics, the gaps, the error categories and what the first three sessions would target.

The note is yours whether or not you continue, and no card details are taken for the trial. That is deliberate: a trial lesson whose only output is a good impression of the tutor's manner has told you about the tutor and nothing about your child. Two written diagnoses from two providers, set side by side, make the decision for you in about five minutes.

Bring three documents if you can. The last marked script, including the teacher's comments. The school's assessment calendar, with the internal deadlines on it. And the subject guide's criterion list if the problem involves coursework. Dubai schools hold all three, and a tutor working to the wrong dates is useful in the wrong month.

If, after the diagnosis, the honest answer is that no specialist is free in the subject and level you need, we will say so and give a date rather than putting a Higher Level student with a generalist. That answer is worse than yes and much better than six weeks of the wrong person.

process.title: Name the component, not the subject
process.description: "Chemistry" is eight hours of tuition. "Paper 3 data handling and the investigation method" is four. Tell us the subject, the level and the component the last marked paper shows the loss in, and the plan gets smaller and more measurable before anybody quotes you anything.

process.title: Send the marked script and the school calendar
process.description: One marked page lets the specialist arrive with a hypothesis. The school's assessment calendar makes sure the work happens in the right month, because Dubai schools set their own internal coursework deadlines and mock windows and they do not all coincide.

process.title: Ask us the group-size question
process.description: There is only one answer here and it is one: one student per session, every session. If a group would genuinely serve you better for the component you have named, we will say so, and for a few things — Theory of Knowledge discussion, language oral practice, Arabic drilling — it honestly might.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with a written diagnosis
process.description: Sixty minutes with the matched specialist, no charge and no card details. One timed question attempted unassisted, marked against the published scheme, and a written note naming the secure topics, the gaps and what the first three sessions would do. Yours whether you continue or not.

process.title: Agree a block or a slot, with an endpoint
process.description: Either a component block with a fixed number of sessions and an end date, or a standing weekly slot with a week-six review written into the arrangement. Both are priced before they start, and both produce a session note within 24 hours of each lesson.

whyPoints.title: One student per session, always
whyPoints.description: No groups of six, no groups of two described as personal attention. The information about why marks are being lost lives in one student's working, and reading it is the service. For the few components where another voice genuinely helps, we will tell you so.

whyPoints.title: Sold by component, not by subject
whyPoints.description: A named component, a rough session count and an endpoint, agreed before the first payment. Most identified component problems are four to six sessions of work rather than an open-ended weekly commitment, and we would rather say that than sell continuity.

whyPoints.title: No premises, so no room to fill
whyPoints.description: A centre's economics require a group because floorspace has to be paid for. Teaching over video removes that pressure, which is what makes one-to-one affordable, and it removes a forty-minute round trip from an evening that only has about 150 usable minutes in it.

whyPoints.title: Straight about permissions
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, no ADEK or SPEA registration and no approval from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Individual tutors need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and you can ask us about permit status and get the answer in writing.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help that stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Feedback by criterion letter, on a separate sheet, with the student's dated drafts untouched. We do not write, complete, edit or proofread internal assessments, Extended Essays or Theory of Knowledge essays at any price, and the record is built to show it.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Higher Level sciences in the early-evening Gulf window are genuinely tight. If nobody suitable is free, you get a date rather than a substitute, plus a note on what is worth working on unsupervised in the meantime.

faqs.question: Is IB tuition near me in Dubai usually a centre or a private tutor?
faqs.answer: A local search returns both, plus marketplaces with no UAE presence. Centres sell a seat in a class of roughly three to eight on a fixed timetable at premises you drive to; private tutors sell an hour of their own time, often travelling. They are different products with different permissions and a tenfold spread in cost. The question that separates them quickest is who reads your child's own working, because in a group of six the honest answer is nobody, individually.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA Educational Services Permit cover that a tutor permit does not?
faqs.answer: Premises and staff. A training institute operating in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, issued to a named address, beginning with initial approval, allowing a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requiring renewal at least 30 days before expiry. An individual tutor instead needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge and valid for two years. A provider without premises in Dubai holds no KHDA permit, and IB Gram does not hold one.

faqs.question: How many students sit in a typical Dubai tuition-centre IB group?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the brochure suggests, outside Al Barsha. The IB cohort in most Dubai districts is small relative to other curricula, so an advertised IB group in Karama, Deira or Al Quoz may be two or three students at a particular level. That is a very expensive form of one-to-one with a third of the attention. Ask in writing how many students will be in the room, in that subject, at that level, on the evening you would attend.

faqs.question: Does a group of six work for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level?
faqs.answer: For meeting content, yes. For finding out why marks are being lost, no. Higher Level calculus and proof marks are lost inside the working, and nobody can read six students' working in sixty minutes. The practical rule is about the stage of the problem: if your child has not met the topic, a group is efficient and cheap; if they can explain it and are still dropping marks, the problem is in their execution and only individual attention will locate it.

faqs.question: Which Dubai neighbourhoods hold most of the tuition centres?
faqs.answer: Al Quoz and Al Barsha are the two main belts, with long-established clusters in Karama, Oud Metha, Bur Dubai and parts of Deira. Premises follow affordable floorspace and passing trade. IB continuum schools, by contrast, have been built where new family housing went up, so their cohorts sit in Nad Al Sheba, Meydan, the Sustainable City, Dubai Investments Park, Mirdif and Al Jaddaf. Al Barsha is the one district where both maps genuinely overlap.

faqs.question: What does a monthly tuition package in Dubai usually include?
faqs.answer: Published figures read in October 2026 cluster at about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's wider monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. What is usually not stated is whether marking and written feedback happen outside the session, whether unused sessions roll over, and whether VAT is included.

faqs.question: How do we compare a centre's group rate with a one-to-one rate?
faqs.answer: Divide. A 60-minute class of six is ten minutes of individual attention at the group rate, plus a round trip of forty to fifty minutes out of an evening that only has about 150 usable minutes in it. That comparison is not always unfavourable to the centre: for first-pass content coverage the group hour is genuinely good value. For locating an unexplained mark loss it is the wrong instrument at any price, because the division of attention is the whole problem.

faqs.question: Does our child need separate tuition for each Diploma subject group?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Six subjects at one session a week each is six evenings and a student with no time left to do the work that was set. One or two subjects taught properly, with work set and actually done, moves more marks than six rushed hours. The usual honest shortlist is the Higher Level subject furthest from target plus whichever coursework deadline is nearest, and everything else waits until one of those is resolved.

faqs.question: Where do Biology Higher Level students lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: On data-based questions set in unfamiliar contexts, and on the Higher Level extension topics that arrive late in DP2. Recall is rarely the problem in Dubai cohorts: a student who can define a process in the abstract loses four marks applying it to a named organism in a graph they have not seen. The second recurring loss is the command term, where an answer describes a pattern that the question asked to have explained. Both show up on one marked script.

faqs.question: Is drop-in revision tuition worth it close to the May session?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether a diagnosis exists. Drop-in coverage eight weeks out, with no idea which component is costing marks, usually means re-teaching content the student already has. The same eight weeks spent on two identified components, with marked work at the start and the end of each block, is a different purchase. If you are starting late, spend the first session on a timed question and a written diagnosis rather than on content, however counter-intuitive that feels.

faqs.question: Can a tuition centre enter our child for IGCSE as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Only if it is a recognised examination centre for that board, which is a separate status from a teaching permit, and you should ask to see which boards it is recognised for. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and the published Pearson Edexcel calendar shows the whole shape of it: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, entries for it closed long before that, and results reach students the following January, as November 2025 results did on 22 January 2026. A UAE candidate with Cambridge sits June or November on the same pattern, with the closing date on the statement of entry. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six timetable zones and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk.

faqs.question: Why is this taught over live video rather than at a Dubai centre?
faqs.answer: Because we have no centre, by design, and because premises force a group. A room that must be paid for has to be filled, and a filled room cannot do diagnosis. Removing the premises is what makes one student per session affordable. It also removes a forty to fifty minute round trip from a usable evening of roughly 150 minutes. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai either; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: How do we check a Dubai tuition provider is permitted to operate?
faqs.answer: Ask which permission applies to what it is doing, and ask in writing. A provider with premises in Dubai should be able to name its KHDA Educational Services Permit and the address on it. An individual tutor should be able to confirm the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid two years. Nobody should quote you a fine amount for tutoring without a permit, because no fine schedule is published, and nobody should describe their tutors as approved by a regulator.

faqs.question: Does Language B tuition help with the Individual Oral?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the few places in the Diploma where a pair or a trio genuinely beats one-to-one, because another voice in the room creates the unpredictability the assessment depends on. Text-type conventions for the writing paper also teach well in a small group. What stays individual is feedback on a particular student's accuracy and register, since that is specific to the way one person speaks and writes.

faqs.question: What should a first IB tuition session in Dubai diagnose?
faqs.answer: Which marks went missing and why, before anything is taught. The student attempts one timed question unassisted while the tutor watches the working rather than waiting for the answer; the tutor marks it against the published scheme; you receive a written note naming secure topics, gaps, error categories and what the first three sessions would target. Content is available everywhere, often free. A specific reading of your child's own script is the part that is scarce.

faqs.question: What if nobody is free in the subject and level we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics in the early-evening Gulf Standard Time window are the tightest, along with Higher Level Computer Science and less common Language B options. We would rather leave a slot empty for a fortnight than put a Higher Level student with somebody who teaches the subject group but not the level. We will also say what is worth doing unsupervised in the meantime without consolidating the same errors.

dubai/ib-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Name the component and ask about group size
dubai/ib-tuition-near-me.closingBody: If you are comparing IB tuition near me in Dubai, two questions sort the results page faster than any price list. Ask how many students will be in the room, in that subject, at that level, on the evening you would attend. Then ask who reads your child's own working, and when. Send us the last marked script and the component it shows the loss in, book the free trial lesson, and read the written diagnosis afterwards. No card details are taken and the note is yours whether you continue or not.

intro.heading: What an IB tutor in Dubai should be able to prove
paragraphs: Most tutoring decisions in this city are made on one phone call and a feeling. A parent describes a problem, an agency describes a tutor, and six weeks later nobody can say whether anything actually changed. The alternative is not more enthusiasm. It is evidence: a marked paper with the lost marks circled, a dated list of the errors that keep recurring, a draft carrying examiner-language feedback, and a short written note after each session that a parent can read in ninety seconds. That record is the product. The lesson is how the record gets made.

IB Gram works as a matching platform rather than a tuition centre. There is no Dubai premises and no classroom. Lessons run over live video, one student with one tutor, on a shared whiteboard the student writes on while the tutor annotates. That distinction matters in Dubai specifically, because the thing that limits a family's choice of tutor here is rarely money. It is the drive. A Chemistry HL specialist living in Sharjah cannot reliably reach Arabian Ranches for a five o'clock session twice a week through a school term. Online, that constraint disappears and the shortlist gets better rather than closer.

The Diploma rewards different behaviour from the IGCSE years that precede it for most Dubai students. Content recall carries a student a long way at sixteen. At Diploma level the marks sit in command terms, in criterion wording, in the structure of a response rather than the facts inside it. A student who can explain a concept out loud and still scores a 4 is usually losing marks to form, not to knowledge. Diagnosing that gap takes a marked script, not a conversation, which is why the first session on every match is spent on work the student has already handed in.

Progress across a two-year programme is slow enough that it has to be measured or it feels like nothing is happening. Four things get logged weekly: the question types attempted, the marks available against the marks earned, the specific error class each lost mark belongs to, and the task set for the following week. Over one term that produces a line you can look at instead of an impression you have to trust. It also brings the uncomfortable conversation forward. If Paper 2 accuracy has not moved in six weeks, then the tutor, the subject or the session frequency is wrong, and a parent should hear that rather than be reassured.

This page is written for a parent whose child attends a Dubai school overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, sitting an IB programme alongside the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies that KHDA requires of every private school in the emirate whatever curriculum it is licensed for. Rates quoted here are market rates with the publisher named. Timetable guidance points at each board's own live pages rather than restating dates that get revised. Where something cannot be verified from a primary source, including any specific IB session or results date, the page says so and names who can confirm it.

dubai/ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Dubai runs the full IB continuum, and the three programmes need genuinely different things from a tutor. A Primary Years child needs reading fluency and number sense built patiently. A Middle Years student needs criterion wording decoded. A Diploma student needs papers marked and a core timeline held. Here is how each works in this emirate and what one-to-one support does inside it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP organises learning through transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than separate subject syllabuses, and it sets no external written examination. Assessment is continuous, teacher-designed and reported against learning outcomes the school writes itself. Tutoring at this stage is diagnostic and narrow: decoding and reading fluency, number bonds and place value, written sentence structure, and the habit of explaining a method out loud. The final year ends in the PYP Exhibition, a student-led inquiry that rewards research routine more than subject knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a large PYP cohort because several of the emirate's IB continuum schools run the programme from FS1 upward, including Dubai International Academy, GEMS World Academy Dubai and Uptown School. Parents here most often ask for primary support in the same term a child transfers in from a different curriculum, where the gap is usually written explanation rather than arithmetic. KHDA's mandatory Arabic requirement also starts in these years, and it surprises families arriving mid-primary.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks each subject against four published criteria, labelled A to D, each scored out of 8. The criterion totals convert to a 1-7 grade through boundaries the school applies. This is where most unexplained grade drops come from in Dubai: a student who knows the content writes an answer that never addresses criterion wording and loses the top band in that strand. MYP Year 5 adds the Personal Project, supervised in school, and some subjects sit externally marked eAssessment.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP to Grade 10 and then offer a choice of Diploma or a British route, so Grade 9 and 10 families here are often making a programme decision at the same time as fixing a grade. That changes what tutoring should do: the evidence a parent needs is not only the criterion score but whether the writing stamina and maths fluency will carry into HL. Ask the school which MYP subjects it enters for eAssessment before planning any revision block.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, graded 1-7, plus the core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Every subject carries internal assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB, and most carry two or three written papers. The Diploma total runs to 45 points, with a small number of points available from the Extended Essay and TOK combination. Award conditions on core components are set out by the school's DP coordinator.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma teaching in Dubai is concentrated in a smaller set of schools than the British-curriculum provision around it, which is why a parent in, say, Al Furjan may be driving a long way for a school place and then finds no Economics HL tutor within twenty minutes of home. The May session is the one Dubai schools sit. Confirm every published IB date with your DP coordinator or the IB's own assessment pages before you build a revision plan around it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs a smaller number of Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is a legitimate route rather than a consolation, and students on it still sit IB subject examinations in the Diploma courses they take. Tutoring works the same way as for the Diploma in those subjects, with the difference that the timetable has fewer written papers and more weight on the reflective project and the career study component.
programmes.countryNote: Only a handful of Dubai schools are authorised for the CP, so families here usually meet it as an option mid-Grade 11 rather than as a choice made at the start. If your child is moving onto a CP route, the most useful thing a tutor can do in the first fortnight is map which Diploma subject papers still apply and which assessment deadlines sit with the career-related provider instead of the school.

dubai/ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Dubai families request most, with the part of each that actually costs marks. The descriptions are deliberately narrow: a tutor who says they cover everything in a subject is describing a syllabus, not a plan. Read these as diagnostic starting points for a first session built around a script your child has already written.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency decides the HL grade more than any single topic. The marks that disappear quietly sit in proof, in complex numbers and in the calculus paper where a correct method gets no credit because the working is not shown in the order the mark scheme rewards. The exploration asks for genuine mathematics applied to something the student chose, and vague aims are the commonest cap on criterion A.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI trades proof for modelling, statistics and technology use. Students who moved across from AA often underestimate the written interpretation: a correct regression with no comment on validity scores badly. Calculator technique is examinable in practice, and students who learned a graphics calculator informally lose time they cannot afford. The exploration here rewards real data and a clear statistical question.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics punishes unit and significant-figure discipline harder than students expect, and the long-answer questions reward sequencing: define, state the relationship, substitute, evaluate. Fields, circuits and thermodynamics are where Dubai students most often report sudden drops. The internal assessment stands or falls on a measurable, controllable research question, which is the single most useful thing to fix in a first session.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most of the lost marks at HL, and the data-based questions reward reading the stem slowly rather than knowing more chemistry. Students who memorise reactions without the underlying electron behaviour cannot answer an unfamiliar mechanism. A tutor's first job is usually to rebuild bonding and periodicity properly before touching past papers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology looks like a memory subject and is marked like a precision subject. Command terms separate a 4 from a 6: outline, explain, evaluate and discuss each want a different shape of answer, and a student who writes everything they know about a topic scores in the middle every time. Statistical treatment in the investigation is where internally assessed marks are most often left on the table.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries more marks than students believe, and the evaluation sentence at the end of a long answer is frequently missing altogether. HL adds quantitative work that rewards arithmetic care. The internal assessment asks for commentaries on recent news articles, and the commonest failure is an article too old or too broad to support the required diagram and theory.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, techniques and theories have to be applied to the case rather than recited, and the pre-released case study at HL rewards structured preparation across months. Students lose marks by answering generically when the command term asks them to use the stimulus. Quantitative content, including ratio and investment appraisal work, is where a careless student concedes easy marks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The paper on unseen non-literary text rewards a method, and most students have never been taught one explicitly. The individual oral needs a global issue narrow enough to defend and two extracts that genuinely support it. HL adds an essay on a studied work. Vocabulary is rarely the problem for Dubai students; the structure of a comparative argument usually is.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper questions on data structures, algorithm tracing and system fundamentals need precise terminology, and students who code well often write loose prose answers that score poorly. The internally assessed solution requires evidence of a real client and a documented development cycle, and planning that properly in Grade 11 saves a crisis in Grade 12.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be used as evidence for an argument, not listed, and the research methods vocabulary is examined directly. Students regularly lose marks by describing a study accurately and never linking it to the question asked. The experimental study at SL and HL rewards a simple replicable design over an ambitious one, and ethical commentary is marked.

The recurring job here is curriculum-transition diagnosis rather than remediation: establishing what a student coming from an American or British system has actually covered against the IB subject guide.

regions.note: Raffles World Academy and the Jumeirah cluster of international schools sit here, with a mix of IB continuum and British provision on neighbouring streets. regions.note: Fast-growing communities where the nearest IB Diploma school is often a genuine drive away, so the school decision and the tutoring decision arrive together. Niche Diploma subjects such as Economics HL or Computer Science are rarely covered locally, and online delivery is what makes those matches possible at all.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and the central corridor
schoolClusters.note: The thickest concentration of IB provision in Dubai, which means a tutor here is usually working against three or four different internal assessment calendars at once. Knowing which school sets its IA deadline in October rather than January changes the whole autumn plan for a Grade 12 student.

schoolClusters.note: Schools serving Arabian Ranches, Emirates Hills, Dubai Hills and the Meadows. Diploma cohorts here are large enough that students often want help with the same paper in the same week, and we keep tutors on separate students rather than running anything resembling a class.

dubai/ib-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways families use IB Gram in Dubai, all delivered online one-to-one. They are not packages with different prices attached; they are different jobs, and most families move between them across a school year as the evidence changes what needs doing.

modes.title: Weekly subject session with a written record
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, and a short note after each lesson. This is the default and the one that produces a usable record, because it generates comparable data every seven days rather than a burst of activity before a deadline. Most Diploma families start with a single subject and add a second only once the first shows movement.

modes.title: Paper-marking block before mocks or finals
modes.description: A short intensive run where the student sits papers to time and the tutor marks them against the published assessment criteria, then teaches from the marking rather than from the syllabus. It is the most efficient use of money close to an exam series, because the diagnosis and the teaching come from the same artefact. It does not work well as a substitute for a term of teaching.
bullets: Papers sat under timed conditions at home, then marked in session

modes.title: Internal assessment and core supervision
modes.description: Structured support across an exploration, investigation, commentary, Extended Essay or TOK essay, run as a sequence of feedback conversations on drafts the student has produced. The tutor reads against the criteria, asks the questions the criteria ask, and records what feedback was given and when. Nothing is written for the student, and the record exists partly so the school can see that.

sections.heading: What a Dubai parent should be able to see after four IB sessions
paragraphs: After four one-to-one sessions you should hold four written notes, at least one marked script, a named error class that has come up more than once, and a stated decision about whether to continue. If what you have instead is a general sense that your child enjoys the lessons, the tuition is not being measured and you cannot tell whether it is working.

The reason to insist on this early is arithmetic. A weekly session across a Diploma year is roughly thirty-five hours of teaching. If the first month produces no diagnosis, a quarter of the first year's support has gone on finding out what the problem is. A marked script in the first session shortens that to one hour, because the lost marks tell the tutor what to teach before the student has to describe it.

The four-session review is deliberately a decision point rather than a progress report. Three outcomes are legitimate: continue as planned, change the frequency or the subject, or stop because the problem is not a tutoring problem. The third happens more often than agencies admit. Missed content from a school transfer, an undiagnosed reading difficulty or straightforward exhaustion in DP2 all look like a subject weakness and none of them is fixed by more hours of the same subject.

What a parent should ask at that review is narrow and answerable. Which error class cost the most marks across the four sessions? What has been done about it? What is the evidence that it is improving? If a tutor cannot answer those three questions with reference to specific pieces of work, the record does not exist.
bullets: Four dated session notes you have actually read
One or more marked scripts with lost marks identified by type
A named recurring error class, not a general weakness
A continue, change or stop decision put in writing

sections.heading: Reading a marked IB script: command terms and the marks they hide
paragraphs: The single most common reason a capable Dubai student scores a 4 or a 5 is that they answer the question they recognise instead of the question that was asked. Command terms are the instruction set of the IB, and they are not interchangeable. An answer that outlines when the paper said evaluate is not a weaker answer; it is an answer in the wrong category, and the mark scheme has nowhere to put it.

This is diagnosable from a script in minutes. A tutor reads the lost marks, sorts them by command term, and counts. A student who loses marks on explain and discuss but not on state or calculate has a writing problem with a precise shape, and it is fixable in a handful of sessions with the right drills. A student who loses marks evenly across every command term has a content problem instead, and the plan is completely different.

The table below sets out the command terms that cost Dubai IB students the most marks, what the examiner is actually marking in each, the mistake that recurs in school answers, and what a corrected response adds. It is written to be used with a script in front of you rather than read through.

None of this requires the tutor to have inside knowledge of marking. Every command term is published in the IB subject guides, which schools hold and can show you. What a tutor adds is the habit of sorting lost marks by category rather than by topic, which is what turns a disappointing paper into a plan.

table.caption: COMMAND TERMS AND WHERE THE MARKS GO
rows: A single correct item, no reasoning required
Writing a paragraph where one line scores
Nothing - it stops after the answer and saves time for later questions
An accurate account with the required level of detail
Explaining why, which earns no extra credit here
The specific features or steps, in sequence, with correct terminology
A causal chain with reasons attached to effects
Because and therefore doing real work: each claim linked to the next
Two separate descriptions with no comparative sentence
Explicit linking words and a shared basis of comparison in each point
A judgement supported by weighed evidence
A list of advantages and disadvantages with no conclusion
A stated judgement, the strongest counter-point, and why it does not overturn it
A reasoned proposal from given information
An answer from memory that ignores the stimulus
Direct reference to the data or stem, then the inference drawn from it

sections.heading: The weekly record, and what a parent is supposed to do with it
paragraphs: A session note that says the lesson went well is decoration. A useful note has four fields and fits on a phone screen: what was attempted, what it scored, which error class the lost marks belonged to, and what has been set for next week. Fields three and four are the ones that make the record cumulative, because an error class repeated across three weeks is a pattern and a task not completed twice is a different problem entirely.

Error classes need to be few enough to count. In practice six or seven cover almost everything at Diploma level: command-term mismatch, unshown or out-of-order working, unit and significant-figure slips, misread stimulus, missing evaluation, terminology imprecision, and timing. Sorting lost marks into those buckets week after week is dull and it is also the entire mechanism by which a grade moves, because it tells you which twenty minutes of teaching is worth more than the other forty.

For a parent the use of the record is simpler than it looks. You are not checking the mathematics. You are checking that the same error class is not still top of the list in week ten that was top of the list in week two. If it is, the teaching has not reached it, and that is a conversation to have with the tutor directly rather than an argument about effort to have with your child.

The record also matters at the other end of the year. When a school is setting predicted grades, a student who can show dated, marked evidence of improvement across a term is in a materially better position than one who can only report that they have been having lessons. The predicted grade still belongs to the school. The evidence is what the conversation runs on.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, mocks and the paper trail behind them
paragraphs: Predicted grades in Dubai IB schools are set by subject teachers from internal evidence, and the evidence varies more than parents realise. One school weights mocks heavily; another runs continuous assessment; a third leans on the most recent internally assessed component. Knowing which applies to your child's school changes what tuition should be aimed at, because improving the thing that is not being measured does not move the prediction.

The most useful question to ask a school is not what the prediction is but what it was calculated from. If the answer is a mock sat in November, then the mock is the lever and the autumn plan writes itself. If the answer is a rolling average of class assessments, then the lever is consistency across many small pieces of work, and an intensive block before one paper is close to useless.

A tutor's contribution here is to produce comparable evidence on the same terms as the school. Papers sat to time, marked against the published criteria, dated, and tracked. That is not a challenge to the school's judgement and it should never be presented as one. It is the material that lets a parent, a tutor and a subject teacher have a factual conversation rather than three different impressions.

The table sorts the evidence types a Dubai Diploma family will actually encounter, who produces each, what it genuinely predicts, and how often it is worth refreshing. The column that surprises most parents is the third one: several of these artefacts predict much less than the weight placed on them.

sections.heading: Internal assessment drafts: what feedback may do and what it may not
paragraphs: Every IB subject carries an internally assessed component, and it is the part of the Diploma where well-meaning help turns into malpractice fastest. The boundary is not a matter of taste. Work submitted for assessment has to be the student's own, and a tutor who rewrites a paragraph has crossed a line that puts the student's whole diploma at risk, not the tutor's reputation.

What legitimate support looks like in practice is narrow and genuinely useful. A tutor can explain what a criterion is asking for, in the criterion's own words. A tutor can read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is not yet met and why. A tutor can ask the questions the criteria ask, so the student finds the gap themselves. A tutor can teach the underlying content or statistics the investigation needs. A tutor can hold the student to a schedule.

What a tutor must not do is also short: no suggested sentences for insertion, no restructuring carried out on the student's behalf, no supplying of a research question the student then adopts as their own, and no editing that takes a draft from one band to another without the student doing the thinking. IB Gram tutors keep a dated log of feedback given, partly so a supervisor can see the shape of the support if they ever ask.

Families sometimes find this disappointing after talking to providers who promise more. It is worth being blunt: operations in this market sell finished internal assessments, and a student who submits one is exposed to an academic honesty investigation with consequences that reach beyond one subject grade. The useful version of this support is slower and it survives scrutiny.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks, measured: a progress ledger a parent can audit
paragraphs: A term is long enough for a plan and short enough to check. The ledger below is the shape a well-run twelve weeks takes for a Diploma student working on one subject, and the point of publishing it is that each row names an artefact. A parent who cannot find the artefact knows the week did not happen as described, without having to judge the teaching.

Weeks one and two are diagnostic and they feel slow. No new content is taught; marked work is sorted and the error classes get counted. Families in a hurry push to skip this and it is a false economy, because the alternative is teaching the syllabus from the start in the hope of hitting the gap by chance.

The middle weeks are where the work is, and they are dull by design: a narrow error class, a drill built from the student's own lost marks, a timed question, a re-mark. The ledger exists to stop that stretch drifting. By week eight there should be a measurable difference in one error class, and if there is not, week eight is when the plan changes rather than week twelve.

The last fortnight returns to whole papers under timed conditions, because technique that only works on single questions does not survive two hours of paper. The final artefact is a written list of what is still unsafe by topic, which is the thing a student should revise from after the sessions stop.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs in Dubai, and who published the number
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for this search publish no price at all, and two of the others quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The figures below are market rates in dirhams with the publisher named against each band. They are not an IB Gram price list, and nothing on this page should be read as a quote.

The bands are wide for a reason. A university student revising Maths SL with a Grade 10 pupil and a subject specialist marking Physics HL papers are both correctly described as tutors and the hourly rates sit a long way apart. What moves the number in Dubai, in rough order of weight: the level, whether the tutor marks to the published criteria, whether travel is involved, the session length, and how close the exam series is.

In-home visits carry the biggest premium in this market and the reason is mechanical rather than commercial. A tutor crossing Dubai in the late afternoon gives up a slot's worth of time to do it, and that time is priced into the hour whether it is itemised or not. Published market rates for in-home one-to-one sit well above the online bands for exactly that reason, and the quality of the match is also narrowed to whoever can physically get there.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one lessons online for UAE families. There are no in-home visits in the UAE at all, in Dubai or any other emirate, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. The first lesson is free for one student per family, with no card details required, which is deliberately the only price-shaped commitment on this page.

sections.heading: KHDA inspection bands and what a school report tells you about tutoring
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Inspection reports are published, and most Dubai parents have read their school's overall band without ever using it to make a decision about tuition. It is more useful than that, provided you read the subject-level detail rather than the headline.

An overall band is an average across phases, subjects and dozens of indicators. A school rated highly overall can have a weak Diploma cohort in one subject group, and a school in a middle band can have an exceptional maths department. The information that matters for a tutoring decision sits in the subject and phase tables inside the report, not on the cover.

Dubai's school market is also expanding fast enough to change the picture year to year. KHDA reported seven new private schools for the 2026-27 intake, four British curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places after six new schools opened the previous year and enrolment rose six per cent. New IB cohorts mean new Diploma teaching teams, and a first-year Diploma group is a reasonable place to want external marking as a second opinion.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the May session
paragraphs: The May session is the one Dubai IB schools sit, and the mistake families make is planning forwards from today rather than backwards from the deadlines. The deadlines that bite are rarely the examinations. They are the internal ones: the school's own draft dates for internally assessed work, the upload deadlines the school manages, and the point after which no new internal assessment work can realistically be started.

IB session and results dates are the one set of figures this page will not publish. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing here has been confirmed from the primary source, and a wrong date in a revision plan is worse than no date. Confirm every IB deadline with your school's Diploma coordinator or on the IB's published assessment pages before you build anything around it.

Where dates can be sourced, they illustrate the real point. Pearson Edexcel's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and entries for that series closed in the early autumn, well before the first paper was sat. Cambridge International runs the same two windows for a candidate sitting in the UAE, a June series and a November series, and its final entry deadline sits a similar distance ahead of the papers; the exact day is printed on the centre's statement of entry rather than anything worth restating here, because Cambridge revises it. An India-only series runs in the early part of the year and is not available to candidates sitting in Dubai, so a timetable found by search needs checking against the UAE series before a family plans revision around it. Both boards warn that timetables get revised, so the live official page is the only safe reference.
