sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB
paragraphs: Dubai private schools teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum they are licensed for, and KHDA's published guidance states these requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 where a school's year begins in April. Families arriving mid-programme are routinely surprised by this, and it is one of the most common reasons a strong student's reported grades look uneven.

The organisational detail matters for planning. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating plainly that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arab students are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language for Islamic Education and for moral, social and cultural studies.

There is also a content constraint that writers and tutors both need to respect. KHDA's guidance states that for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes.

What this means in practice for a Dubai family is that mandatory-subject support has to follow the school's own material and language stream rather than an imported programme, and that any tutor working in Arabic or Islamic Education should be matched to the stream the child is actually in. KHDA also requires that school teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential question worth asking your school directly.

sections.heading: When the evidence says stop, change or wait
paragraphs: The honest version of getting started includes the cases where tutoring is the wrong purchase. If a Grade 11 student is sleeping five hours a night and has three internally assessed components overdue, a weekly Physics session will not fix any of it, and selling one would be straightforwardly dishonest. The first conversation on every match is about what else is going on, because a tutoring plan built on a mis-stated problem wastes a term.

Availability is the second honest caveat. Coverage is deep in Diploma maths, the sciences, economics and English, and thinner in some group two languages, in a few of the arts and in less commonly taken options. When no suitable specialist is free at the time a family needs, we say so and give a realistic wait rather than filling the slot with someone who teaches the subject adjacent to it. A Chemistry teacher is not a Physics HL tutor, and the marked work makes that obvious within a fortnight.

The third case is timing. Starting six weeks before a final paper is not pointless, but what it buys is narrow: exam technique, a tighter error list and some confidence under timed conditions. It does not buy two years of missing content, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling hope. If a family comes to us late, we say what the six weeks can realistically do and let them decide.

What happens next is short. You send the subject, the level, the school and a recent piece of marked work. We come back with a named tutor and a slot in Gulf Standard Time, usually within two working days. The first lesson is free for one student per family with no card details taken, and it is spent on the marked work rather than on introductions. After the fourth session you get a written continue, change or stop recommendation, and you are free to act on any of the three.

process.title: Send the subject, level and a marked script
process.description: The single most useful thing a Dubai family can send first is a recent piece of marked work: a mock paper, a topic test, an internally assessed draft with teacher comments. It tells a tutor more in five minutes than a questionnaire does in a week, and it means the first session starts with teaching rather than diagnosis.

process.title: Get a named tutor and a Gulf Standard Time slot
process.description: We come back with a named subject specialist, their level and the papers they teach to, plus a proposed weekly slot. Dubai school runs make anything before four o'clock unrealistic for most families, so slots run from late afternoon into the evening. You confirm the tutor before anything is booked.

process.title: Use the free first lesson on the marked work
process.description: One free trial lesson per student, with no card details collected. It is spent on the script you sent: lost marks sorted by error class, one or two fixed live, and a written diagnosis afterwards. If the match is wrong, that is a useful outcome of a free hour rather than a problem to manage.

process.title: Read the weekly note, not the reassurance
process.description: Each session produces four fields: what was attempted, what it scored, which error class the lost marks belonged to, and the task set. Reading those takes under two minutes a week and it is the only reliable way to know whether the same weakness is still sitting at the top of the list a month later.

process.title: Take the four-session decision seriously
process.description: At session four you receive a written recommendation to continue, change or stop, with the evidence behind it. Changing the tutor, the subject or the frequency at that point is normal and costs nothing. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we would rather recommend it than carry a family through a term that is not working.

whyPoints.title: The record is the deliverable
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts, an error-class tally, a dated feedback log and a weekly four-field note. A parent can audit all of it in a few minutes a week without knowing the subject, because the questions it answers are whether the same weakness is still top of the list and what was done about it.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, named, not a pool
whyPoints.description: The same specialist stays with your child unless you ask for a change. Continuity is what makes the record cumulative: a tutor who marked September's paper can tell you whether February's mistakes are the same mistakes, and a rotating roster cannot answer that question at all.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery widens the shortlist
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, so the pool is not limited to whoever can drive to your community by five o'clock. For niche Diploma subjects in the newer southern communities that is the difference between a specialist and the nearest available generalist.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with their source
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure on this page names who published it and when. Market bands are presented as market bands, never as our quote, and the only commitment we make on price is the free first lesson with its condition stated in the same sentence.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty treated as a hard boundary
whyPoints.description: Internally assessed work gets feedback against the criteria and nothing else. No sentences supplied, no restructuring done for the student, and a dated log of what was said so a school supervisor can see the shape of the support if they ask for it.

faqs.question: What should I be able to see after my child's first four IB sessions in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Four dated session notes, at least one marked script with the lost marks identified by type, a named recurring error class, and a written recommendation to continue, change or stop. That is a deliberately low bar and most tutoring does not clear it. If after a month you have an impression rather than artefacts, the work is not being measured, and you have no way to tell whether the next three months will be different. Ask for the error-class tally specifically. It is the one document that shows whether the same weakness is still costing the most marks.

faqs.question: How do you work out which error is costing my child the most marks?
faqs.answer: By sorting lost marks on real scripts into a small number of categories and counting them. At Diploma level six or seven categories cover almost everything: command-term mismatch, working not shown in the order the mark scheme wants, unit and significant-figure slips, misread stimulus, missing evaluation, imprecise terminology, and running out of time. One paper gives a hint, three papers give a pattern. The point of counting rather than describing is that it tells the tutor which twenty minutes of a session is worth more than the other forty, and it gives you something to check in four weeks.

faqs.question: Can I read the session notes myself, or do they only go to the tutor?
faqs.answer: They go to you. A note that only the tutor reads is a private memo, not a record. Each one carries four fields, fits on a phone screen, and arrives within a day of the lesson. You are not expected to check the mathematics or the chemistry. You are checking two things: that the error class at the top of the list in week ten is not the same one that was there in week two, and that work set between sessions is being marked rather than merely assigned. If either looks wrong, raise it with the tutor directly.

faqs.question: My child's predicted grade dropped after mocks. What evidence should the school show us?
faqs.answer: Ask what the prediction was calculated from rather than arguing with the number. Schools in Dubai weight evidence differently: some lean heavily on one mock, others use a rolling average of class assessments, others weight the most recent internally assessed component. Once you know the basis, you know which lever matters. If it is the mock, the autumn plan is paper technique under timed conditions. If it is continuous assessment, an intensive block before one paper will not move it. The prediction belongs to the school; the evidence is what makes the conversation factual.

faqs.question: How many drafts of an IB Internal Assessment may a tutor comment on?
faqs.answer: Your school sets the rule on formal drafts and you should follow it exactly, because the limit sits in the school's own academic honesty policy. What a tutor can do within that rule is read work the student has written and say which criterion is not yet met and why, in the criterion's own language. What a tutor must never do is supply sentences, restructure on the student's behalf, or hand over a research question the student then adopts. We keep a dated log of feedback given so a supervisor can see the shape of the support if they ask.

faqs.question: What does a marked Paper 2 script actually get used for in a session?
faqs.answer: It becomes the lesson plan. The tutor reads the lost marks, sorts them by category, and teaches from the categories rather than from the syllabus. A student losing marks on explain and discuss questions but not on state or calculate has a writing problem with a precise shape, and it is fixable with drills built from their own answers. A student losing marks evenly across every question type has a content gap instead, and the plan is completely different. Both diagnoses take minutes from a script and weeks from conversation.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting IB tuition in Dubai halfway through DP2?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided everyone is honest about what it buys. A term and a half can fix exam technique, cut a recurring error class, build timing under pressure and tidy an internally assessed component that is behind. It cannot replace eighteen months of missing content, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling hope. If you come to us in the second year, we will say what the available weeks can realistically achieve, which subject gives the best return, and whether one subject done properly beats three done thinly.

faqs.question: How do we tell a plateau from a bad run of papers?
faqs.answer: By looking at the error classes rather than the scores. Scores bounce around for reasons that have nothing to do with learning: a harder paper, a bad night, an unfamiliar topic. The error-class tally is steadier. If the categories causing lost marks are shifting and shrinking while the raw scores stay flat, the work is landing and the grade usually follows. If the same category tops the list for six weeks, that is a genuine plateau, and the response is to change the teaching approach rather than to add more hours of the same.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow my child's school scheme of work or the IB subject guide?
faqs.answer: The school's sequence, with the subject guide as the standard. Teaching ahead of a Dubai school's own order confuses a student and makes the next class harder, so the tutor works to the order your child is actually being taught in. The criteria and command terms come from the published IB subject guide, which your school holds and can show you. Where the two appear to conflict, the tutor flags it in the session note rather than quietly choosing, because the person who should resolve it is the subject teacher.

faqs.question: What happens to the progress record if we change tutors?
faqs.answer: It travels. The marked scripts, the error-class tally and the session notes belong to the family, so a new tutor starts from the diagnosis rather than repeating it. That is the practical reason to keep the record in a consistent format from week one. Changing tutors is normal, usually after the four-session review, and it costs nothing. What it should never cost is the diagnostic work already done, which is exactly what gets lost when tuition is run on conversation alone.

faqs.question: How does a Dubai school's KHDA inspection band affect what tutoring we need?
faqs.answer: Less than the headline suggests and more than most parents use. An overall band averages across phases, subjects and many indicators, so a strongly rated school can still have a weak Diploma group in one subject area, and a middle-banded school can have an excellent maths department. The useful information sits in the subject and phase tables inside the published report. Read those, then ask the school how predicted grades are calculated and who is teaching the Diploma group this year. Both answers change a tutoring plan more than the cover page does.

faqs.question: Do you keep my child's marked work, and how do we have it deleted?
faqs.answer: Marked scripts and session notes are kept so the record stays cumulative, which is the whole mechanism this page describes. You can ask for everything held about your child to be deleted at any time and we will confirm when it is done. We ask for the subject, the level, the school and samples of marked work, and nothing beyond what the matching and the teaching need. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs this, and the privacy link on every page sets out the detail.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Maths AA HL and Physics HL evidence in the same week?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth testing rather than assuming. The overlap between the two at Higher Level is real in mechanics, in graph work and in algebraic fluency, so a genuinely dual-trained specialist can be more efficient than two separate matches. The test is the marking: ask for a marked question from each subject before committing. If the physics marking is noticeably thinner than the maths, you have a maths tutor who is comfortable with physics, which is a different purchase and should be priced and planned as one.

faqs.question: What does the free first IB lesson in Dubai include, and what is the condition?
faqs.answer: One free trial lesson per student, one student per family, with no card details collected and nothing to cancel afterwards. The condition is that single allocation. The lesson itself is a full-length one-to-one session with the named tutor you were matched with, spent on the marked work you sent rather than on introductions, and it produces the same written note every other session produces. If the match is wrong, you have found that out in a free hour, which is the point of running it before any payment.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education graded the same way as my child's IB subjects?
faqs.answer: No, and the difference catches out families arriving mid-programme. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and they follow Ministry of Education content rather than an IB subject guide. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in these subjects and sets the language of instruction for each stream. Any tutoring here has to follow the school's own material and the stream your child is in, so ask the school which stream that is before arranging support.

After four sessions you get a written continue, change or stop recommendation with the evidence behind it. Lessons are one-to-one over live video across every Dubai community, and if no suitable specialist is free when you need one, we will tell you that rather than fill the slot.

intro.heading: Five things decide what you pay, and only one of them is the tutor
paragraphs: Ask what an IB tutor costs in Dubai and the honest answer is a question back: which subject, at which level, starting when, for how long, and to fix what. Those five inputs move the final figure by a factor of five or more, and four of them are about your situation rather than about the tutor's seniority. A family that understands the five can usually get the same help for substantially less, mostly by changing when they buy rather than what they buy.

The market's published bands set the outer limits. The lowest advertised figures in this market are online and typically undergraduate-delivered: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted from AED 150 by Unitors for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB. Exam-level specialists run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 and beyond. The top advertised rate in the set is BartyED at AED 650. In-home visits form a separate band of roughly AED 180 to 500 once travel is included.

Those are other providers' published prices read in October 2026, named so you can check them. The spread is wide because the market is selling several different things under one word. What the numbers do not show is the variable that usually decides a family's total spend, which is hours rather than rate. Thirty hours at AED 200 costs more than ten hours at AED 450, and the thirty-hour plan is the one families drift into when nobody diagnosed the problem first.

That is why this page is organised around decisions rather than around a price list. Scarcity by subject, because a Computer Science HL request and a Maths AA SL request are not the same purchase in this emirate. Timing, because the same help bought in October and in March costs different amounts for reasons that have nothing to do with inflation. Session length and frequency, because a student who absorbs seventy minutes well does not benefit from a two-hour booking. And priority, because most families have a ceiling and the order you spend in matters more than the rate you pay.

IB Gram quotes per match rather than publishing a rate card, and we tell you which band a request sits in and why before anything is paid. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school week. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The practical effect on cost is that no part of the hour pays for a journey, and the tutor is selected for the component your child is losing marks on rather than for living within driving distance.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The band where cost questions get serious. Six subjects, externally marked papers, internally assessed components and a core, all landing inside two years. A DP2 request in March is the most expensive thing in this market because supply is tight and the remaining time is short, which limits what can be fixed and raises what families are willing to pay.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Cheaper per hour and cheaper in total, because the content is less specialised and one tutor can often cover two related subjects. The highest-value spend is criterion literacy: understanding what a criterion score means and which of the four is holding a grade down, which is usually two or three sessions of work rather than a term.

A short block aimed at that decision is better value than a term of general support, because the question is about fit for the next qualification as much as about current attainment.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The lowest cost per hour and the shortest useful session, often thirty to forty-five minutes. Spend here is most efficient when aimed at a named gap in reading fluency, number sense or research habits, rather than at general enrichment, which schools already provide and which does not need paying for twice.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's primary intake includes a steady flow of mid-year arrivals from British, Indian and American systems, so the usual request is to close a specific gap created by a move. Arabic as an additional language is the most requested primary subject, because Dubai private schools must teach Arabic whatever curriculum they are licensed for.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: The cheapest high-value hours available anywhere in a Diploma plan, provided they are bought early. A few hours spent testing whether a research question is answerable within the word limit prevents the much larger spend that follows a coursework crisis eighteen months later. Priced as a capped block rather than an open commitment.

Ask the school's coordinator for the dates first; buying hours against the wrong calendar is a common and entirely avoidable waste.

sections.heading: The five variables that set an IB tutor cost in Dubai
paragraphs: A quote is the product of five inputs, and a family can influence four of them. Subject and level set the band. Local scarcity of that specialism sets where in the band you land. The month you start sets availability, and availability behaves like price. Session length sets what you pay per useful minute. And the number of hours the problem needs sets the total, which is the figure that actually matters to a household budget.

The swings are large and uneven. Moving from a common SL subject to a scarce HL component can roughly double the band. Starting in November rather than March does not change a published rate but changes which tutors answer, which in practice is the difference between a specialist and whoever is left. Dropping a two-hour minimum to a seventy-minute session cuts a third off the invoice without cutting the teaching, because most Diploma students stop absorbing new technique before the ninety-minute mark.

The fifth variable, total hours, is the one nobody quotes and the one that dominates. A diagnosed problem addressed in eight focused hours costs less than an undiagnosed one addressed in thirty unfocused ones, even at twice the hourly rate. This is why we run a free diagnostic session rather than a sales call: an hours estimate attached to a named problem is the single most useful thing a parent can be given before spending, and it is also the thing that most often reduces what we are paid.

One variable you cannot influence: the permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years according to u.ae, so it adds nothing to any legitimate quote and should never appear as a line item. Anyone charging you for a tutor's licensing is charging for something that costs them nothing.

sections.heading: Scarcity by subject: why two Dubai families get different quotes
paragraphs: Two families can ask for the same thing in the same week and receive quotes a hundred dirhams apart, with no dishonesty involved. The reason is supply. Dubai has a large private school sector, 227 schools serving 387,441 students across 17 curricula in 2024-25, but International Baccalaureate students are a modest share of that total and the UK curriculum is by far the largest. So the pool of teachers who have taught a specific IB Higher Level course to examination in this city is smaller than the headline school count suggests.

That matters differently by subject. Maths AA SL has genuine depth: several tutors will be available in most weeks, and a quote near the bottom of the qualified band is reasonable. Chemistry HL between February and May has almost none, and a family looking then is bidding against every other DP2 family in the emirate. Computer Science HL is thin all year, which is why it is the request most likely to be matched from outside the UAE.

The practical use of this is to ask, before comparing quotes, where your request sits. If the answer is a plentiful subject at a common level, compare aggressively; the market is competitive and you should pay mid-band. If the answer is a scarce component in the peak window, the question changes from how little you can pay to whether anyone can cover it at all, and a disclosed fallback becomes worth more than a discount.

We publish our coverage position rather than concealing it, because the alternative wastes a fortnight of a family's time. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones at a Dubai-friendly hour, with no change to format or subject depth. Where we cannot cover it at all, we say that too.

sections.heading: The cost of waiting, priced out month by month
paragraphs: The most expensive decision in this market is not choosing an expensive tutor. It is waiting for a bad mock result before acting. Waiting raises the cost three times over: the problem has grown, the available time has shrunk so intensity must rise, and the specialists are already booked because every other family received their mock results in the same week.

Consider the same underlying problem, a DP student whose extended responses lose the top band, addressed at four different moments. In DP1 term two it is a technique fix: roughly eight hours over two months, at a mid-band online rate, with a free choice of tutor. In DP2 term one it is the same fix plus a term of accumulated habit: perhaps twelve hours, still at a reasonable rate. After January mocks it is twelve hours compressed into eight weeks, bought at the top of the band because supply has gone. Three weeks before final papers it is triage, and the honest plan covers two subjects rather than four.

None of that is a sales argument for buying earlier than you need to. It is an argument for diagnosing earlier than you need to, which is free. A single diagnostic session in DP1 tells you whether there is a technique problem at all, and most families who run one in DP1 buy fewer hours overall than families who wait, because they are fixing a small thing rather than a compound one.

The Dubai-specific wrinkle is the calendar. The school year runs from late August or early September to late June or early July, with winter and spring breaks, and Ramadan moves earlier each year and reshapes evening availability. Revision therefore happens in fewer usable weeks than a generic timeline suggests. Any plan built without the school's own assessment calendar in front of it will misjudge how much time is actually left.

sections.heading: Cost per useful hour: length, frequency and what a student can absorb
paragraphs: Families optimise the hourly rate and ignore the two things that decide how much of each hour is useful. The first is session length. Most Diploma students sustain about seventy minutes of genuinely demanding work, after which the session becomes revision of what has already been covered. A two-hour booking therefore often contains seventy minutes of teaching and fifty minutes of expensive company. Where a two-hour minimum exists it is usually there to justify a journey, which an online session does not have.

The second is frequency against independent practice. Tutoring works by setting a target, having the student practise it alone, and then checking whether it transferred. That cycle needs gaps in it. Two sessions a week in one subject leaves no room for independent practice, so the second session tends to repeat the first rather than build on it. The exception is a defined push: a mock-season timed-paper block, or catching up after illness or a move, where intensity is the point.

Put the two together and the efficient plan for most Diploma subjects is one session of sixty to ninety minutes a week, plus a short intense block at mock season. For a student with a genuine content deficit across a whole course, more is justified, but that is a different diagnosis and should be stated as one. A provider proposing three weekly sessions in a single subject without naming a content deficit is selling hours rather than solving a problem.

There is also a floor worth naming. Fortnightly sessions rarely work for exam-year subjects, because the target set in one session has gone cold by the next and the first twenty minutes are spent re-establishing where things were. If budget forces a reduction, a capped block of weekly sessions followed by a gap is usually more effective than the same hours spread thinly across a term.

sections.heading: If you can only buy ten hours, buy them in this order
paragraphs: Most families have a ceiling, and almost nobody is told how to spend against one. The ordering below is what we would advise a Dubai family with ten paid hours and a Diploma student, and it is deliberately front-loaded with the things that are cheap and change the most.

Hour zero is the free diagnostic session, which should happen before any of the ten are spent. Hours one and two go to the Extended Essay or internal assessment research question if either is still open, because a question that cannot be answered within the word limit caps several criteria at once and no later work recovers it. Hours three to six go to the single dominant error pattern in the student's marked work, usually command terms or absent working, because those transfer across every subject and every paper.

Hours seven and eight go to a timed-paper clinic in the weakest subject, where the student writes to time and then marks their own work against published criteria with the tutor challenging each decision. Hours nine and ten are held in reserve for the week before mocks or final papers, when a specific question has appeared and a general plan is useless. Spending them in advance is the most common way a budget gets wasted.

What not to buy with a ten-hour ceiling: general content revision, which the school already provides and which past papers cover for free; a second subject, because splitting ten hours across two subjects usually changes neither; and premium-band hours for a mid-band problem. A student losing marks to command terms does not need the top of the Dubai market, and anyone who tells you otherwise is quoting their availability rather than your need.

sections.heading: What the money cannot buy, at any rate in this market
paragraphs: No rate buys a grade. Nobody can promise one, and in the UAE a promise of that kind is a commercial representation about something entirely outside a provider's control: papers nobody has seen, boundaries published after marking, and what a seventeen-year-old does on a particular morning. Any provider offering a promised score, a promised improvement or a refund tied to a result is making a claim they cannot honour, and the published terms are usually where that unravels.

No rate buys influence over internal assessment moderation. Internal assessment is marked by the school and moderated by the IB, which compares the school's standard against its own using a sample and can adjust a whole cohort. A tutor cannot affect that, cannot predict it, and cannot request a results enquiry, which is a matter for the school's IB coordinator. Work that sits clearly inside a band is less exposed to adjustment, and that is the only lever anyone has.

No rate buys coursework. Everything submitted must be the student's own work, and a tutor's role is questioning, criterion-based feedback and method critique on material the student has already produced. At least one site competing for these searches openly sells completed internal assessments; a family that buys one is risking the candidate's entire Diploma for a handful of marks. We state the boundary in writing before a block starts so there is no ambiguity about what was bought.

And no rate buys exam-paper knowledge. Examiners mark completed scripts against a markscheme supplied for that session; they do not see future papers and cannot share markschemes. The legitimate version of that help, teaching a student to predict what a markscheme rewards from the command term and mark allocation, is available from any good specialist and does not carry a premium.

sections.heading: Free and low-cost moves that reduce the hours you need
paragraphs: Reducing paid hours is more effective than negotiating a rate, and most of the available reductions cost nothing. Start with the school. Dubai schools generally run subject clinics, revision sessions and coordinator meetings that families underuse, and the subject teacher who wrote the assessment is the best-informed person about why a mark was lost. Asking for ten minutes with them before buying ten hours of tutoring is both free and more targeted.

Then use official material properly. Past papers, subject guides, assessment criteria and command-term definitions are published by the boards and available through the school. We link official sources rather than redistributing them, because reproducing board material is a copyright problem and, for unreleased material, an integrity problem for the candidate. A student working through official past papers with a markscheme will cover content for free, and paid hours can then go to the things a markscheme cannot teach.

Peer study works for content and fails for technique, which is a useful distinction. Two students revising a syllabus together will cover ground efficiently. Two students marking each other's extended responses will reinforce each other's errors, because neither has calibrated judgement yet. So use study groups for recall and paid sessions for marking, and the same budget goes further.

The last move is organisational and it is free. Get your school's assessment calendar, write the internal deadlines and mock windows on it, and plan paid hours around those dates rather than evenly across the term. Hours spent in the fortnight before a deadline change the submitted work; the same hours spent two months earlier, with no deadline in sight, usually do not.

sections.heading: Scheduling, Ramadan and honest coverage in Dubai
paragraphs: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on a shared screen, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time. Most sessions sit between 16:30 and 20:30, after the school run and activities. Because no journey is involved, a session can be seventy minutes rather than a travel-justified two hours, which is a direct saving on the invoice rather than a compromise on teaching.

Ramadan reshapes the evening. School days shorten, energy in the late afternoon drops, and many families prefer a post-Iftar slot, which we arrange with notice. Planning for that in advance matters more than it sounds, because the weeks before the May session and Ramadan can overlap, and a revision plan built on a normal evening pattern will quietly lose a fortnight of its best hours.

On coverage, the position is uneven and we publish it. Common subjects at common levels match within a few days. Scarce components take one to two weeks, longer between February and May when the whole emirate wants the same specialists. Where no UAE-based tutor is free, the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones, at a Dubai-friendly hour, with no change to format or depth. Where we cannot cover a request, we say so rather than substituting a generalist and leaving you to discover it.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE: in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For cost purposes that is the main structural difference between us and the in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour published in this market. No part of our hour pays for a journey, and the tutor is chosen for the component your child is losing marks on rather than for proximity to your community.

process.description: Before payment, we say whether the request sits mid-band or at the specialist end, and whether that is because of difficulty or scarcity. If the reason is timing, we say so, because that is the one variable you can still change.

whyPoints.description: A diagnosed problem takes fewer hours than an undiagnosed one, and we would rather be paid for eight targeted hours than thirty vague ones. The free diagnostic session exists to make that argument concrete.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost per hour in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: Published figures in this market span roughly AED 33 to AED 650 an hour, which sounds unhelpful until you break it into bands. Budget online provision, typically undergraduate-delivered, is advertised from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik. Qualified subject tutors online are quoted from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB by Unitors. Exam-level specialists run around AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. The premium named end reaches AED 650 at BartyED. Those are other providers' published prices read in October 2026, not ours.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are most expensive to tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The expensive ones are scarce rather than hard. Chemistry at Higher Level between February and May is the tightest market in the emirate, because Diploma provision sits in a minority of Dubai schools and every DP2 cohort converges on the same eight weeks. Computer Science HL is thin all year. Maths AA HL, specifically Paper 3 investigation work, tightens from February. By contrast English A and Biology have reasonable supply at both levels, so a premium quote for either needs a specific justification. Ask where your request sits before comparing quotes, because supply explains most of the difference.

faqs.question: How many hours of IB tutoring will my child actually need?
faqs.answer: For a single diagnosed technique problem, usually six to ten hours: three or four sessions to teach and practise the fix, then two or three to check it transfers under timed conditions. For a genuine content deficit across a whole course, considerably more, and that should be stated as a different diagnosis rather than folded into the same plan. The number that matters is hours rather than rate, because thirty undiagnosed hours cost more than eight targeted ones even at half the price. Get an hours estimate attached to a named problem before committing to anything open-ended.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start tutoring in DP1 or to wait for the mock results?
faqs.answer: Starting earlier is cheaper, and by more than most families expect. The same underlying problem addressed in DP1 term two takes around eight hours at a mid-band rate with a free choice of tutor. Addressed after January mocks it takes twelve to sixteen hours compressed into eight weeks, bought at the top of the band because supply has already gone to families who received the same results in the same week. Waiting raises the cost three ways: the problem has grown, the available time has shrunk, and the specialists are booked. Diagnosing early is free and usually reduces the total.

faqs.question: Does a two-hour session cost less per hour than a one-hour session?
faqs.answer: Sometimes per hour, rarely per useful hour. Most Diploma students sustain about seventy minutes of genuinely demanding work, after which the session becomes revision of ground already covered. A two-hour booking therefore often contains seventy minutes of teaching and fifty minutes of expensive company. Two-hour minimums usually exist to make a tutor's journey worthwhile, which an online session does not have, so there is no reason to buy one. Match the session length to what your child can absorb and spend the difference on an extra week rather than an extra fifty minutes.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class better value than one-to-one for IB?
faqs.answer: For revising content several students share, yes: the cost per student is lower and structured coverage suits a group. For diagnosing and fixing one student's specific error it is poor value, because a group session cannot be built around which marks that student is losing. Families who use group classes as a substitute for diagnosis tend to buy more total hours, since the underlying problem persists through the coverage. The efficient combination is group or self-study for content and a small number of one-to-one hours for marking judgement and technique, which is where the marks actually move.

faqs.question: What can we do ourselves to reduce the number of paid hours?
faqs.answer: Four things, all free. Ask the subject teacher who marked the work why the marks went, because they are the best-informed person available and ten minutes with them is more targeted than ten paid hours. Use the school's own clinics and coordinator meetings, which most families underuse. Work through official past papers and published criteria, linked from the boards rather than redistributed. And plan any paid hours around the school's assessment calendar, since hours spent in the fortnight before a deadline change the submitted work while the same hours two months earlier often do not.

faqs.question: Does IB tutoring cost more than IGCSE tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, and the published bands reflect it: Unitors quotes IGCSE from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. The reason is supply rather than difficulty. The UK curriculum is the largest in Dubai by enrolment, so IGCSE-experienced teachers are plentiful, while Diploma provision sits in a minority of schools and specialist Higher Level teachers are correspondingly scarce. Within either qualification, the scarce component matters more than the label: a thinly covered HL subject costs more than a widely taught one regardless of which board sets it.

faqs.question: Can we buy tutoring just for the six weeks before final papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it can work if the plan is honest about what six weeks can change. Technique transfers in that window: command-term structure, working discipline in mathematics, converting partially credited questions into full marks. New content largely does not, so a plan that promises to cover an untaught HL topic in that period is selling hope. Expect to focus on two subjects rather than four and on near misses rather than topics never understood. Availability is the practical constraint, since that window is exactly when every family in the emirate is looking for the same specialists.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest thing to buy that actually changes a grade?
faqs.answer: Two or three hours spent on an internal assessment or Extended Essay research question before any writing has happened. A question too broad to control or impossible to answer within the word limit caps several criteria at once, and no amount of later polishing recovers it. Those hours are paid at a normal rate, happen early, and prevent the much larger spend that follows a coursework crisis in the final year. After that, the cheapest effective purchase is four hours on whichever error pattern dominates the student's marked work, because it transfers across every subject.

faqs.question: Why do some Dubai tutors charge AED 650 an hour?
faqs.answer: BartyED publishes that figure at the premium named end of the market, and the honest explanation is scarcity and reassurance rather than a different teaching method. It is defensible in a narrow case: a candidate already near the top of a subject, where the remaining marks are in judgement rather than knowledge, and where the tutor has specifically marked that component. It is not defensible for the far more common case of marks lost to command terms, absent working or a badly scoped coursework question. Those are mid-band problems with mid-band solutions, and paying double buys nothing extra.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram publish a fixed price list for Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is that the request determines the figure. A common subject at Standard Level and a scarce Higher Level component in April are different purchases, and a single advertised rate would either overcharge the first or fail to cover the second. What we do instead is tell you which band your request sits in and why before anything is paid, run a free trial lesson with no card details taken, and give an hours estimate attached to a named problem. Every market figure on this page is another provider's published rate, named and dated, not ours.

faqs.question: How does tutoring cost compare with resitting an IB subject?
faqs.answer: A retake costs more than money. There is an entry fee set through the school for the session, which your coordinator can quote precisely, but the larger costs are six additional months of study, a delayed university timetable and the effect on offers that were conditional. Set against that, a block of targeted hours in the term before final papers is usually the cheaper course of action, which is an argument for diagnosing early rather than for buying a large plan. Ask the school's IB coordinator about retake timing and entry arrangements before treating a resit as a fallback.

faqs.question: Will paying a higher rate improve my child's result?
faqs.answer: Only where the higher rate buys something the problem actually needs. If the marks are being lost to a repeatable technique error, a mid-band specialist who can mark accurately against published criteria fixes it, and a premium rate adds nothing. If the student is already near the top of a subject and the remaining marks are judgement calls in one specific component, specialist calibration in that component is worth paying for. Nobody at any rate can promise a grade, an improvement or a moderation outcome, and a provider offering one is making a claim about things entirely outside their control.

faqs.question: How quickly can you give us a cost estimate for Dubai?
faqs.answer: Usually the same day for the band, and after the free trial lesson for the hours. We can tell you immediately whether a request sits mid-band or at the specialist end, and whether that is because of difficulty or local scarcity, because that depends on the subject, level and component you name. The hours estimate needs the diagnostic session, since it depends on what is actually wrong. If no UAE-based specialist is free for a scarce component, we tell you that at the quoting stage rather than after you have committed, and explain where the match would come from instead.

dubai/ib-tutor-cost.closingHeading: Get the hours estimate before the hourly rate
dubai/ib-tutor-cost.closingBody: The most useful figure in any IB tutor cost conversation in Dubai is not the rate, it is the number of hours a named problem needs. Ask for that first, and ask which of the five variables is putting your quote where it is: subject, scarcity, timing, session length or hours. Four of the five are things you can still change. IB Gram runs a free diagnostic lesson with no card details taken, quotes per match with the band explained, and delivers one-to-one tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time with no travel inside the hour. Tell us the subject, the level and the component, and we will tell you what we think it will take.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-arabic-speaking-stude.tutorsIntro: The tutors matched for these pages work in Arabic A and Arabic B specifically, which is a different skill from teaching conversational Arabic. The distinction matters because the marks on both courses come from register, textual analysis and written form rather than from fluency.

intro.heading: The placement question comes before the tutoring question
paragraphs: An Arabic-speaking student in a Dubai IB school is in an unusual position. They are a first-language speaker of a subject the school is legally required to teach, sitting in a programme that offers that language at three different levels, at a school where the regulator sets rules about how the classes must be organised. Almost every problem that reaches a tutor on this page started as a placement decision rather than an academic one.

Start with the structure. In the Diploma, Arabic can appear as a Group 1 subject — Arabic A: Language and Literature, or Arabic A: Literature — or as a Group 2 subject in the form of Arabic B, or as Arabic ab initio for genuine beginners. A student fluent in spoken Arabic is not automatically an Arabic A student, because Arabic A is a literature and textual analysis course taught in Modern Standard Arabic, and spoken fluency in a dialect is a different competence. Conversely, placing a strong reader and writer in Arabic B wastes two years and a chance at the bilingual diploma.

The bilingual diploma is the specific prize that gets missed. A candidate who completes two Group 1 languages, or one Group 1 language plus a Group 3 or Group 4 subject studied and assessed in a second language, is awarded a bilingual diploma. For an Arabic-speaking student in Dubai this is genuinely achievable and genuinely valuable, and it is decided at options time in Grade 10, not in the final year. A tutor cannot retrofit it.

Then there is the layer most families only half understand: the mandatory subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes by group — for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

The language of instruction is specified too. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. It also requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and states that for the mandatory UAE subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited.

That last rule has a direct consequence for tutoring, and it is worth saying out loud. Support for the mandatory UAE subjects works from the student's own school material and the official curriculum, not from a separate scheme a tutor has written. Where this page describes support for Arabic A, Arabic B or Islamic Education, that is what it means. All IB Gram tuition in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is an India-only service.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-arabic-speaking-stude.programmesIntro: Arabic appears differently in each IB programme, and the decisions that matter are taken at different points. These notes concern the Arabic pathway specifically rather than the programme as a whole.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Arabic can sit in Group 1 as Language and Literature or Literature, or in Group 2 as Arabic B or ab initio. Group 1 assessment centres on textual analysis, a comparative essay, the Individual Oral and, in Literature, the HL essay.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the DP is where the bilingual diploma either happens or does not. An Arabic-speaking student taking Arabic A alongside English A qualifies on the two-Group-1 route; one taking a Group 3 or Group 4 subject assessed in Arabic qualifies on the other. Dubai schools vary in whether they timetable Arabic A at all, so this is a question to ask the school before Grade 11 rather than during it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four lettered criteria per subject, each scored 0-8 and converted to a 1-7 grade. Arabic sits in Language and Literature for first-language students or in Language Acquisition, which runs in phases rather than years. Grade 10 ends with the Personal Project.
programmes.countryNote: The phase placement in MYP Language Acquisition is the thing that quietly determines the DP route. A student parked in a low phase through Grades 6 to 10 arrives at options time without the written register for Arabic A, even if they speak the language at home every day. Dubai schools set phases internally, so a parent who thinks the placement is wrong should raise it in Grade 7 or 8, not Grade 10.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, built around units of inquiry, with no external examinations and assessment by portfolio plus the Grade 5 Exhibition. Languages are taught within the programme framework rather than as separate examined subjects.
programmes.countryNote: For an Arabic-speaking family in Dubai the PYP years are where reading and writing in Modern Standard Arabic is either built or not. Children who speak a dialect at home and study in English all day can reach Grade 6 fluent orally and well behind on script, vocabulary and formal register. KHDA requires separate first-language and additional-language Arabic streams, so check which one your child is actually in.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma subjects paired with a career-related study, plus personal and professional skills, a reflective project, service learning and a language development strand. The language development component is a defined part of the programme rather than an examined Group 2 subject.
programmes.countryNote: Rarely offered in Dubai, so a family interested in it has a short list of schools rather than a choice. Where it is available, the language development strand can be used for Arabic, but it does not carry the Group 1 weight that a bilingual diploma route needs. Check the IB's programme finder and then the school directly.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-arabic-speaking-stude.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones that matter to an Arabic-speaking student in a Dubai IB school, with the specific component where marks go missing. The Arabic entries come first because the placement question is the one this page exists to answer.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Studies literary and non-literary texts in Modern Standard Arabic. Assessment includes a guided analysis of an unseen text, a comparative essay on studied works, and the Individual Oral on a global issue. First-language speakers lose marks on analytical vocabulary and on structuring an argument about a text, not on comprehension.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Literature
subjects.description: Literary works only, with a guided literary analysis, a comparative essay, the Individual Oral and, at HL, an additional essay on a studied work. The heaviest reading load of any Arabic route and the clearest bilingual diploma path. Students underestimate the volume of classical and modern Arabic literature involved.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: A Group 2 language course for students with prior learning, assessed on productive and receptive skills against defined text types. The trap for a fluent speaker: an informal essay and a formal report are marked differently, and conversational strength does not carry a blog post, a letter or a speech written in the wrong register.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: For genuine beginners with little or no prior Arabic, built around themes and text types rather than literature. Not available to a first-language speaker, and a placement error in this direction is both a rules problem and a wasted subject slot.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The usual Group 1 partner for an Arabic A student and half of the two-Group-1 bilingual diploma route. Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, so advertisements, speeches and infographics are examinable alongside the Paper 2 comparative essay and the Individual Oral.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic and proof-led, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator at both levels. Where a student has been taught mathematics in English while thinking in Arabic, the recurring cost is not the mathematics but the extended written justification that command terms like 'justify' and 'hence show' demand.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling led with a graphical calculator assumed throughout. The interpretation questions carry heavy marks and are language-dense: a student is asked to comment on what a regression means in context, in writing, which is a composition task as much as a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Physical chemistry carries the load: enthalpy cycles, entropy and equilibrium constants. The internal assessment is a single scientific investigation marked against lettered criteria, and a bilingual student writing it in their second language often loses criterion marks on the evaluation section rather than the method.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty treatment separates IB Physics from most national syllabuses: propagating an error, drawing error bars, justifying stated precision. HL adds rotational dynamics, the quantum topic and more demanding field theory, with the written explanations as heavily weighted as the calculations.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Wide syllabus, precise command terms. 'Outline', 'explain', 'distinguish' and 'evaluate' set different scopes for the same knowledge, and students answering in a second language usually over-write for the low-scope terms. The internal assessment is one investigation against lettered criteria.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Arab students and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs, separate classes for the two groups, and that all teachers hold appropriate KHDA approval. Support works from the school's own official material.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed curriculum, with Arabic as the primary language of instruction for Arab students and the school's curriculum language for non-Arabs. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises a minimum lesson length of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject.

schoolClusters.note: The growth belt, where several of the 2026-27 places sit. Newer IB schools fill year groups unevenly and sometimes run Arabic A only when numbers allow, so the Group 1 question is worth asking in writing before a family commits.

sections.heading: What an Arabic-speaking IB student in Dubai is actually assessed on
paragraphs: A fluent Arabic speaker on Arabic A is assessed on textual analysis in Modern Standard Arabic, not on fluency. The components are a guided analysis of an unseen text, a comparative essay on studied works, the Individual Oral on a global issue explored through two texts, and at Higher Level an additional essay on a studied work. Nothing in that list rewards speaking Arabic well at home, which is why able students are routinely surprised by their first grade.

The gap is specific and it has a name: critical register. A student can read a passage of Naguib Mahfouz comfortably and still be unable to write four paragraphs about how its narrative perspective produces its effect, because the vocabulary of literary analysis in Modern Standard Arabic is a learned technical language. It is no more automatic for an Arabic speaker than the vocabulary of literary criticism in English is for an English speaker. It is, however, finite and teachable, which is the good news.

On Arabic B the assessment logic is different again. Productive and receptive skills are marked against defined text types, and the text type carries conventions that the examiner is specifically looking for. A formal report, a blog post, a speech and a letter to a newspaper are four different jobs. A fluent speaker who writes all four in the same voice loses marks that a less fluent student who matches each form will collect.

For the mandatory subjects the assessment is set by the school within the official curriculum, and KHDA specifies both language of instruction and class organisation. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab students, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

sections.heading: Arabic A or Arabic B: making the decision properly
paragraphs: This is the single most consequential academic decision an Arabic-speaking student in a Dubai IB school makes, and it is usually made on the strength of a conversation rather than on evidence. The useful test is not whether the student speaks Arabic well. It is whether they read extended literary prose in Modern Standard Arabic without strain, and whether they can write four hundred words of analytical argument in it.

Three signals point towards Arabic A. The student reads Arabic for pleasure or at least without effort. They have been in the KHDA first-language Arabic stream through the MYP years rather than the additional-language one. And their MYP Language and Literature criterion marks in Arabic have been in the upper bands rather than the middle. Where all three hold, Arabic A is the right place and Arabic B is a waste of a subject slot.

Three signals point the other way. The student speaks a dialect at home but has studied in English all day since the PYP, so the written register was never built. The MYP placement was in Language Acquisition rather than Language and Literature. And extended reading in Modern Standard Arabic is slow. Where those hold, Arabic B at Higher Level is usually a better outcome than Arabic A at Standard Level, and the reason is that Arabic B HL still demands genuine written competence while assessing it against text types the student can be taught in two years.

The decision interacts with the bilingual diploma, which is why it cannot be left late. It is also partly a timetable question: not every Dubai school runs Arabic A as a live option every year, and a family who assumes it is available can find at options evening in Grade 10 that it is not. Ask the school in writing, in Grade 9, which Arabic routes they will actually timetable.

sections.heading: The bilingual diploma: the thing most families find out about too late
paragraphs: A bilingual diploma is awarded to a candidate who completes two Group 1 languages, or one Group 1 language plus a Group 3 or Group 4 subject studied and assessed in a language other than their Group 1 language. For an Arabic-speaking student in Dubai, both routes are realistic, and the first is the straightforward one: Arabic A plus English A.

The reason it gets missed is structural rather than academic. Taking two Group 1 subjects uses a subject slot that would otherwise go to a Group 2 language, and the Diploma's six-subject frame means something has to give. Families looking at the subject grid for the first time in Grade 10 tend to optimise for university prerequisites, which is reasonable, and the bilingual diploma is not a prerequisite anywhere. It is simply an accurate and permanent statement about a student's capability in two languages, awarded by the IB, at no extra cost in exams.

The second route — a Group 3 or Group 4 subject assessed in a second language — is less common in Dubai because it requires the school to teach and assess, say, History or Biology in Arabic. Where a school does offer that, it is worth examining carefully: the subject content load is unchanged, the language load is real, and the student's own view of which language they think in matters more than their parents' preference.

A tutor's role here is honest and limited. Nobody can retrofit a bilingual diploma in the final year, because it depends on the subject grid chosen two years earlier. What a tutor can do is make Arabic A survivable for a student who has committed to it, which usually means building the critical register fast in DP1 rather than discovering in DP2 that the comparative essay is not going well.

sections.heading: Where bilingual students lose marks in subjects taught in English
paragraphs: A student who thinks in Arabic and is assessed in English does not lose marks where families expect. Comprehension is rarely the problem by the Diploma years. The losses cluster in extended written justification, in command-term scope, and in the parts of an internal assessment that require evaluative prose rather than data.

Command terms are the most fixable of the three. The IB uses instruction words with defined scopes: 'state' wants a sentence, 'outline' wants the shape of something, 'explain' wants a causal chain, 'evaluate' wants a judgement supported both ways. A bilingual student under time pressure tends to default to writing everything they know, which scores well on 'explain' and poorly on 'outline', and burns the time needed for the later questions. Mapping each command term to a target answer length and shape is a few sessions of work and it moves marks immediately.

The second cluster is the internal assessment evaluation. In the sciences, the method and data sections are procedural and bilingual students handle them well. The evaluation criterion asks for a discussion of limitations, sources of error and improvements, which is extended argumentative writing in a second language about the student's own work. It is consistently the lowest-scoring criterion for this cohort, and it is worth disproportionate attention.

The third is mathematics, counterintuitively. In Applications and Interpretation especially, the heavy marks sit on interpretation questions that ask what a result means in context — a composition task wrapped around a statistical one. In Analysis and Approaches, 'justify' and 'hence show that' demand written reasoning rather than a correct number. Both are language-dense and both reward exactly the kind of structured written practice that a bilingual student is least likely to be getting at school.

sections.heading: KHDA's mandatory subject rules, quoted rather than summarised
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, which for schools whose year begins in April meant April 2026. This is a federal principle applied at emirate level: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

On class organisation KHDA is explicit. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. For a parent, the practical use of that rule is as a question: which stream is my child in, and is it the right one? A dialect-fluent child placed in the non-Arab additional-language stream in primary will arrive at Grade 10 without the register for Arabic A.

On language of instruction, KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. It also requires that schools ensure all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a checkable credential point a parent is entitled to ask about.

On time, KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that the length of any mandatory subject lesson is at least 25 minutes. And on content, the use of any different or additional content for these subjects without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited — which is precisely why tutoring support for them works from the school's own material rather than from anything a tutor has written.

sections.heading: The exam calendar for an Arabic A or Arabic B candidate
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May session, and a Group 1 or Group 2 language candidate has an unusual calendar because a significant part of the grade is produced before the exams. The Individual Oral is recorded and assessed internally; the HL essay in Arabic A: Literature is written and submitted; and the studied works have to be finished in time for revision rather than being read during it.

That changes the planning order. For most subjects the final term is revision. For an Arabic A candidate the final term can still be carrying an internal component, and the single most common failure mode on this route is a student who has read the set works once, at the pace the class read them, and has no second reading in hand when the comparative essay arrives. Reading twice is the whole technique, and it cannot be compressed.

We do not publish a specific IB exam or results date on these pages. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date printed here would be second-hand, and a wrong date is worse than no date. Ask the school's Diploma coordinator for the entered session and the internal deadline calendar in writing, and verify against ibo.org.

For students also taking IGCSE subjects, including Arabic as a first or foreign language at IGCSE, the board calendars apply. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates — the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November final timetable having run from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong zone timetable.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on an Arabic A essay or an Extended Essay in Arabic
paragraphs: This boundary needs stating plainly on a language page, because a literature essay is the easiest piece of coursework in the Diploma to hand over and the hardest to defend afterwards. A tutor may teach, explain and give feedback. A tutor may not write.

What is allowed is substantial. A tutor may teach the critical vocabulary, model how an analysis of a passage is constructed, explain each assessment criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, discuss and challenge the student's thesis, suggest that an argument is unsupported, read the student's own draft and give written feedback against the criteria, and teach referencing conventions for Arabic-language sources, which students frequently get wrong.

What is not allowed is writing any part of it, dictating sentences to be transcribed, translating a student's Arabic draft into a polished English one or the reverse as though it were the student's own work, editing a draft into a finished state, or supplying a model essay to be adapted. For a bilingual student there is a specific trap here: having a tutor 'fix the Arabic' on a paragraph the student wrote is feedback if it is described and explained, and it is editing to completion if the tutor rewrites it. The line is whether the student makes the change.

The test to apply is whether the student could explain and defend every line of the work in an oral examination. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an IB malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student, who can be excluded, not on the seller. We also do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; we reference and link the official source.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency and what an Arabic A student should know early
paragraphs: If a student may apply to a UAE university, the Ministry of Education equivalency process converts a foreign school certificate into something a UAE institution can accept. It is worth understanding early because parts of it concern which subjects were taken, and by the final year that is settled.

For the British track the published requirements are specific: proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, plus passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3. Notably for this page, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That is a detail families with strong Arabic sometimes get wrong in the hopeful direction.

For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB we will not publish a points threshold, because we have not read one on moe.gov.ae and an unsourced figure on a page like this is a liability rather than a service. Ask the Ministry or the school's university counsellor and get the answer in writing.

Two cautions worth repeating. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry runs, not services IB Gram performs or can influence. And nothing about tutoring is required for equivalency, admission or progression — any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process they do not control.

sections.heading: Availability, permits and what we are not
paragraphs: Arabic A tutors are a genuinely specialist group, and no competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is itself informative. The honest position is that Arabic B and additional-language Arabic support is reasonably available, while Arabic A: Literature at Higher Level, taught by someone who has actually marked against those criteria, is a narrow pool. A specific evening hour on Gulf Standard Time in that subject can sometimes not be filled immediately, and when that is the case we say so rather than booking a generalist against a specialist syllabus.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider tutor base, including IB specialists in India, with sessions delivered identically by live video on Gulf Standard Time. What does not happen in either direction is a home visit in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service IB Gram offers only in India.

On permits, the position is clear and worth knowing before you hire anyone. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified.

One more thing to avoid specifically on a mandatory-subjects page: do not go looking for your child's own Arabic or Islamic Education teacher as a private tutor. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, is not KHDA approved, and operates no UAE office, centre or branch.
