process.title: Establish which Arabic route the student is actually on
process.description: Group 1 or Group 2, Literature or Language and Literature, and which KHDA stream they have been in since primary. This is five minutes of questions and it determines everything that follows, because support for Arabic A and support for Arabic B have almost nothing in common.

process.title: Test extended reading and analytical writing
process.description: A short diagnostic in the trial session: read a passage of Modern Standard Arabic prose and write a paragraph about how it achieves its effect. Fluency is assumed; what is being measured is critical register. The result usually surprises both the student and the parent.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: One session, no charge, with a tutor who teaches that specific route. By the end of it the tutor should be able to name the component where marks are being lost — guided analysis, comparative essay, text-type register, or the evaluation criterion on an internal assessment.

process.title: Set the slot against the real week
process.description: Dubai runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night. Mandatory subject lessons sit inside the school timetable, so support for them should not land on the same day. During Ramadan the slot moves after Iftar, agreed in advance.

process.title: Written work, marked against the criteria
process.description: Essays and tasks set between sessions and returned with written comments against the published criteria, so the student can see which criterion moved. For Arabic B that means one text type at a time; for Arabic A it means paragraph-level analysis before whole essays.

process.title: Review each term, and name the finish line
process.description: The plan says what it is for: a specific component, a specific criterion, a specific grade band. When that moves and holds, the right advice is usually to pause and return before the exam term rather than keeping a slot booked for two years.

whyPoints.title: Placement before tutoring
whyPoints.description: Most of the damage on this route is done at options time, not in lessons. We say plainly when a student is on the wrong Arabic course, when Arabic B HL is a better outcome than Arabic A SL, and when a bilingual diploma is still reachable — even where that means less tutoring, not more.

whyPoints.title: The KHDA rules quoted, not paraphrased
whyPoints.description: Separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for first-language Arabic and Islamic Education for Arabs, the 40-minute lesson unit, the 25-minute advised minimum. These are checkable requirements a parent can hold a school to, which is why they are quoted here.

whyPoints.title: Critical register is teachable; fluency is not the problem
whyPoints.description: An able Arabic speaker scoring 4s on Arabic A does not need more Arabic. They need the technical vocabulary of literary analysis in Modern Standard Arabic and a structure for an analytical paragraph. That is a finite body of work, and naming it is most of the fix.

whyPoints.title: Mandatory subjects worked from the school's own material
whyPoints.description: KHDA states that additional or different content for the mandatory UAE subjects requires prior Ministry of Education permission. So support for Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies uses the school's set material and the official curriculum, not a parallel scheme a tutor has invented.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line stated on the page
whyPoints.description: On a language course, 'fixing the Arabic' is feedback when the student makes the change and editing to completion when the tutor rewrites the paragraph. That distinction is written here rather than buried, because a literature essay is the easiest coursework in the Diploma to hand over.

whyPoints.title: Clear about availability and about what we are not
whyPoints.description: Arabic A at Higher Level is a narrow specialist pool and we say so before taking a booking. We offer no home visits in the UAE, hold no KHDA permit or regulator accreditation, and run no UAE office. Everything is delivered online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: Should a fluent Arabic speaker in Dubai take Arabic A or Arabic B?
faqs.answer: Test reading and analytical writing rather than conversation. Arabic A is a literature and textual analysis course in Modern Standard Arabic; the marks come from writing about how a text works, not from speaking Arabic well. Three signals point to Arabic A: the student reads extended Modern Standard Arabic prose without strain, has been in the KHDA first-language stream since primary, and has scored in the upper MYP criterion bands. Where a student speaks a dialect at home but studied in English all day, Arabic B at Higher Level is often a better result than Arabic A at Standard Level.

faqs.question: What is a bilingual diploma and can an Arabic-speaking student in Dubai still get one?
faqs.answer: It is awarded to a candidate who completes two Group 1 languages, or one Group 1 language plus a Group 3 or Group 4 subject studied and assessed in a second language. For an Arabic-speaking student the straightforward route is Arabic A plus English A. The catch is timing: it uses a subject slot, so it has to be chosen at Grade 10 options and cannot be retrofitted in the final year. It is not a university prerequisite anywhere, but it is a permanent, IB-awarded statement of capability in two languages at no additional exam cost.

faqs.question: Why is my child fluent in Arabic but only scoring a 4 on Arabic A?
faqs.answer: Because Arabic A does not assess fluency. The components are a guided analysis of an unseen text, a comparative essay on studied works, the Individual Oral, and at Higher Level an additional essay. All four require critical register: the technical vocabulary of literary analysis in Modern Standard Arabic and a structure for an analytical argument. That is a learned technical language, no more automatic for an Arabic speaker than literary criticism in English is for an English speaker. It is finite and teachable, and it is usually the whole of the gap between a 4 and a 6.

faqs.question: Can my child be moved into the first-language Arabic class if they are in the additional-language stream?
faqs.answer: That is a school decision, and it is worth raising early. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. A dialect-fluent child who was placed in the additional-language stream in primary will reach Grade 10 without the written register Arabic A needs. Raise the placement in Grade 7 or 8 rather than at options evening, and ask in writing which stream the child is recorded in.

faqs.question: Do you teach Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies, and how?
faqs.answer: Yes, worked from the student's own school material and the official curriculum. KHDA states that for the mandatory UAE subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so nothing parallel is introduced. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs, with the two groups taught separately. It also requires that school teachers of these subjects hold appropriate KHDA approval, which is a question a parent is entitled to ask the school.

faqs.question: Where do bilingual students lose the most marks in subjects taught in English?
faqs.answer: Three places, none of them comprehension. First, command-term scope: a student who writes everything they know scores well on 'explain' and poorly on 'outline', and loses the time needed for later questions. Second, the evaluation criterion on an internal assessment, which asks for extended argumentative prose about limitations and improvements in a second language and is consistently the lowest-scoring criterion for this cohort. Third, interpretation questions in mathematics, which ask what a result means in context and are short compositions wrapped around a calculation. All three respond quickly to targeted practice.

faqs.question: Can Arabic ab initio be taken by a student who speaks Arabic at home?
faqs.answer: No. Arabic ab initio is a Standard Level course for genuine beginners with little or no prior Arabic, and a first-language speaker is not eligible for it. Attempting that placement is both a rules problem and a wasted subject slot, since it occupies a Group 2 space that could carry a language the student does not already have. If the student's spoken Arabic is strong but their script and written register are weak, the honest options are Arabic B — often at Higher Level — or a serious programme of written work through MYP so that Arabic A becomes reachable by Grade 11.

faqs.question: How much reading does Arabic A: Literature actually involve?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect, and the volume is the main reason students come unstuck rather than the difficulty of any single work. The course studies literary works only, assessed through a guided literary analysis, a comparative essay, the Individual Oral and, at Higher Level, an additional essay on a studied work. The technique that makes it work is reading each set text twice: once with the class and once again independently, with notes. That second reading cannot be compressed into the revision term, which is why Arabic A planning has to start in DP1.

faqs.question: Does taking Arabic count towards the five subjects UAE equivalency requires?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth knowing before subject choices are made. The published British-track requirements are passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade — and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Families with strong Arabic sometimes assume the opposite. For the IB track we will not publish a points threshold we have not read on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Extended Essay written in Arabic?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach research methodology, discuss and challenge the research question, explain each assessment criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, read the student's own drafts and give written feedback against the criteria, and teach referencing conventions for Arabic-language sources, which students frequently get wrong. A tutor cannot write any part of it, dictate sentences, rewrite a paragraph, translate a draft as though it were the student's own work, or supply a model to adapt. The test is whether the student could defend every line in an oral examination.

faqs.question: Is 'fixing the Arabic' in my child's essay allowed or is it cheating?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on who makes the change. If the tutor identifies that a paragraph's register is wrong, explains why, shows what a correct register looks like in a different example, and the student rewrites it, that is feedback and it is legitimate. If the tutor rewrites the student's paragraph into correct Modern Standard Arabic, that is editing to completion and it is over the line. This distinction matters more on a language course than anywhere else in the Diploma, because the correction is so easy to make silently. The test remains whether the student could defend every line.

faqs.question: How many minutes a week must a Dubai school teach Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, advising that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes long. The specific weekly allocation is set in KHDA's mandatory subjects guidance and applies to all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirements due for implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. If you want the exact figure for your child's year group, ask the school for its KHDA mandatory subject timetable in writing.

faqs.question: Which exam series does a Dubai student sit if they take IGCSE Arabic?
faqs.answer: June or November with Cambridge International, and May/June or November with Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only, so it is not available to a UAE candidate and should not appear in any Dubai family's planning. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used, so work from the live official timetable for your school's zone. Pearson's November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

faqs.question: Are Arabic A tutors easy to find in Dubai at an evening slot?
faqs.answer: Arabic B and additional-language Arabic support is reasonably available. Arabic A: Literature at Higher Level, taught by someone who has worked against those specific criteria, is a narrow pool, and a particular evening hour on Gulf Standard Time sometimes cannot be filled immediately. When that happens we say so rather than booking a generalist Arabic speaker against a specialist literature syllabus. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider base including IB specialists in India, delivered identically by live video. No home visits happen in the UAE in any case.

faqs.question: Do you come to our home in Jumeirah or Al Khawaneej for Arabic lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time. For an Arabic A student this is usually an advantage rather than a compromise, because the binding constraint is finding someone who has taught and marked that specific course, not finding someone who can drive to your community by five. If physical presence in Dubai is your requirement, we are not the right provider and will say so.

faqs.question: My child speaks Arabic but writes it slowly. What does the first term of support look like?
faqs.answer: Paragraph-level work before whole essays, and script and register before literature. The first weeks are spent building the analytical vocabulary of Modern Standard Arabic and a reliable structure for a single analytical paragraph: claim, textual evidence, explanation of effect. Only once that holds do full comparative essays become useful, because an essay built from weak paragraphs cannot be marked usefully. Expect written work set between sessions and returned with comments against the published criteria, so the student can see which criterion actually moved rather than receiving a general grade.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-arabic-speaking-stude.closingHeading: Fix the placement first, then build the register
dubai/ib-tutor-for-arabic-speaking-stude.closingBody: Most of what goes wrong for an Arabic-speaking IB student in Dubai is decided before any tutoring starts: the KHDA stream they were put in at primary, the MYP phase they were parked in, and the Group 1 or Group 2 choice made at Grade 10 options. Those are worth checking now, in writing, with the school. Where the placement is right and the marks still sit below the ability, the gap is almost always critical register in Modern Standard Arabic, which is finite and teachable. Book a free trial lesson and the session will include a short reading and writing diagnostic. Sessions are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not send tutors to UAE homes.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-indian-students.tutorsIntro: The tutors matched here have taught both systems. That matters because the translation problem runs both ways: an Indian-schooled student arriving in the IB and an IB student aiming at an Indian or Gulf university are two different briefs, and the same tutor rarely handles both well without having lived in both.

intro.heading: Start with the bill, because nobody else will
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages measured in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in. One agency's own FAQ asks how much tutoring costs and then declines to answer. For an Indian family in Dubai that is more than an annoyance, because the budgeting instinct carried over from Chennai, Hyderabad or Delhi is calibrated to a market where a subject tutor costs a fraction of this one. The number has to be named before anything else is useful.

Here is the market, in AED, from published sources. A generalist or university-student online tutor sits at the bottom of the range: EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor working online is the working middle, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home visit adds a travel premium, which Bestimate puts at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500. A named IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200-450 and upward, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the examiner-positioned end. None of those are IB Gram's prices; they are what the market charges, cited so you can check them.

Converted to a monthly figure, which is what a family actually plans, Bestimate's Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages visible in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those bands are wide for a reason, and the width is where this page earns its place: the variables that decide where in the band you land are predictable, and several of them are specific to Indian families in Dubai.

The first is subject count. An Indian-curriculum transfer into IB Diploma usually needs two subjects supported, not one, because the gap pattern clusters in mathematics and the sciences at the same time. Two subjects at the mid-band rate is a different budget from one. The second is HL versus SL. The tutor pool for Maths AA HL and Chemistry HL is thinner than for the SL equivalents, and thin pools price higher everywhere, in every market, including this one.

The third variable is the one Indian families most often underestimate: the internal assessment. Each IB subject carries coursework marked inside the school, and process coaching on an IA, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is a different kind of work from teaching topics. It is front-loaded, it clusters around school deadlines rather than spreading evenly, and it tends to be bought in blocks. Bought as blocks it is predictable. Bought in a panic three weeks before a deadline it is not.

The fourth is Hindi. If your child is taking Hindi B or Hindi ab initio as their Group 2 language, the tutor pool for that is genuinely small in the UAE, and the honest answer is that availability at a specific evening hour on Gulf Standard Time cannot always be promised. All IB Gram tuition in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is an India-only service.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-indian-students.programmesIntro: Indian families in Dubai meet the IB at three different points, and the cost profile differs sharply between them. These notes are about what each programme costs a family in effort and money, not a general description of the programme.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four lettered criteria per subject, each scored 0-8 and converted to a 1-7 grade. There are no external exams in most MYP years. Grade 10 ends with the Personal Project. The assessment language is the obstacle for a student used to marks out of 100 for a correct answer, because an MYP criterion can award full marks for a wrong conclusion reasoned well.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest place for an Indian family in Dubai to intervene. MYP support is usually one subject, usually one session a week, at the lower end of the market band, and it fixes the criteria literacy problem before it compounds into a DP problem. Families who skip it and start tutoring in Grade 11 pay several times more for the same understanding, two years later.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the Creativity, Activity, Service strand. Each subject carries internal assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. UAE schools sit the May session. Subject grades run 1-7, with up to three bonus points from TOK and the Extended Essay, for a ceiling of 45.
programmes.countryNote: The expensive one, and the place Indian families in Dubai spend most. The driver is subject count: a transferring student commonly needs maths and one science supported simultaneously, and if an HL subject had to change because the Dubai school's block timetable differs, that subject is a standing start. Budget it separately rather than folding it into the same weekly hour.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, organised around units of inquiry. No external exams, no conventional grades, and assessment by portfolio plus the Grade 5 Exhibition. A child arriving from an Indian primary school often looks strong on arithmetic and computation and weak on explaining a method aloud or in writing.
programmes.countryNote: Rarely an academic spend for Indian families in Dubai. Where money goes at this stage it goes on Arabic, which is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and on written explanation. A non-Arab child joins the additional-language Arabic stream, which KHDA requires to be taught separately from the first-language classes.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma subjects paired with a career-related study, plus a personal and professional skills course, a reflective project, service learning and language development. Uncommon in the UAE but it exists, and for a student who cannot carry six Diploma subjects it is a landing place rather than a failure.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Dubai schools run it, so this is a short list rather than a choice, and the cost question becomes which two Diploma subjects are being carried. Check the IB's programme finder and then the school directly, since school websites in this market are frequently a year out of date.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-indian-students.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Indian families in Dubai most often pay for, with the specific reason the money goes there. Where a subject is listed, it is because the CBSE or ICSE preparation and the IB demand diverge in a way that costs marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The commonest single spend. A CBSE student arrives with more mechanical fluency than most IB classmates and loses marks on justification, because AA treats 'find', 'show that' and 'justify' as different instructions. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling led, with a graphical calculator assumed throughout. Students from a pure-maths background often find the content light and the technology unfamiliar, losing marks on calculator notation and on interpreting rather than computing a regression.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Physical chemistry is where the money goes: enthalpy cycles, entropy and equilibrium constants are standard IB and thinner in many Indian school backgrounds. The scientific investigation is a single piece of coursework marked against lettered criteria, unlike a practical record book.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty treatment is the differentiator. Indian-schooled students usually handle the mechanics comfortably and then lose marks propagating errors, drawing error bars and justifying the precision of a result. HL adds the quantum topic and harder field theory.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Breadth plus command-term discipline. The syllabus is wide and the instruction words are precise, so a student who writes everything they know for an 'outline' question scores below one who writes three lines. Recall-rewarding backgrounds make this worse, not better.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal assessment commentaries, each on a news article published inside a defined window, each applying a different syllabus unit. Popular with Indian families aiming at business degrees, and the commentary deadlines are the part that gets bought in a hurry.

subjects.name: Hindi B and Hindi ab initio
subjects.description: The Group 2 option many Indian families in Dubai choose, and the hardest to staff. Assessment is against defined text types and registers, so a fluent household speaker can still lose heavily on formal written register. Availability at a specific evening hour cannot always be promised.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, which is the surprise: advertisements, speeches and infographics are examinable. Students from literature-only English backgrounds are strong on Paper 2 and exposed on Paper 1 and the Individual Oral.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Approachable content, unforgiving assessment. HL requires a research project on a real organisation with supporting documents, and Paper 1 uses a pre-released case study that rewards early preparation. Often the subject a transferring student is moved into by timetable rather than choice.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a working solution for an identified client, documented through a development process. Students with competitive-programming backgrounds build well and document poorly, and the documentation is where most of the criteria marks sit.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Relevant to Indian families twice: as a Group 2 Diploma option and because Arabic is a KHDA-mandated subject in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum. A student with no prior Arabic starts in the additional-language stream.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together worth up to three bonus points. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent research piece with a supervisor and three formal reflection sessions. A tutor coaches the research process and gives feedback on the student's own drafts; the writing must be the student's.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-indian-students.regionsIntro: The practical cost of tutoring includes the hour it eats. These are the communities with the densest Indian-family populations in Dubai and what the commute does to an evening session.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Villa and townhouse living with a thick cluster of Indian and British curriculum schools nearby. Short runs mean a 4.30pm or 5pm weekday slot is usually realistic through term.

regions.name: Al Nahda and Al Qusais
regions.note: Dense apartment living near the Sharjah boundary, with many families commuting across the emirate line for work. The crossing at peak hours pushes the usable study window to 6.30pm or later on weekdays.

regions.name: Karama and Oud Metha
regions.note: Older central Dubai, close to several long-established Indian schools, so school runs are short. The constraint here is usually a shared study space at home rather than the commute.

regions.name: International City and Warsan
regions.note: Affordable apartment stock and long drives to most school clusters. Families here often prefer two weekend sessions over two weekday ones, because the weekday arithmetic rarely works.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Sports City
regions.note: A newer centre of gravity for Indian professional families, with schooling usually a community or two away. A fixed online slot avoids the parking and drop-off time that an in-home arrangement adds at both ends.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and The Gardens
regions.note: Apartment communities beside the Marina and Jebel Ali corridor, well used by families with children at schools along Sheikh Zayed Road. Expect an evening slot rather than a late-afternoon one.

regions.name: Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to several schools and universities, so commutes are short and the 5pm slot survives. A useful area for families wanting two sessions a week without losing two evenings to driving.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Al Barsha South
regions.note: Newer villa stock attracting Indian families moving out of apartments, with schooling often inside the community. One of the few Dubai areas where a 4pm weekday session is genuinely achievable.

schoolClusters.city: Central and eastern Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Where the long-established Indian-curriculum schools sit, several of which also run IB programmes. Families here frequently have one child on CBSE and one on IB in the same household, which is its own scheduling problem.

schoolClusters.city: Western and new Dubai
schoolClusters.note: The IB-heavy belt, where Indian families moving from a CBSE school to an IB one usually land. Several of these schools run the full PYP-MYP-DP continuum, which makes an internal transfer easier than a change of school.

sections.heading: What an IB tutor for Indian students in Dubai actually costs
paragraphs: A qualified online IB subject tutor in Dubai costs between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour at market rates, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Below that band you are buying a generalist; above it you are buying either a travel premium or a specialism. That is the whole answer, and the rest of this section is about which of those you need.

The cheap end is real and it has a real use. EdFlik's AED 45-65 and Tutopiya's AED 33-52 buy homework supervision and company, which for a Grade 7 MYP student who simply will not sit down is sometimes exactly the product. What it does not buy is a syllabus-accurate reading of why a Maths AA answer scored 3 out of 6, because that requires someone who has taught the course and marked against its criteria.

The travel premium is the band Indian families most often pay without deciding to. Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500. The gap between that and the online band is the commute, not the teaching. For a widely-taught subject the local pool is deep enough that you are only paying for convenience. For Maths AA HL, Chemistry HL or Hindi B in a specific community at a specific hour, the pool may be empty at any price.

The specialist band, AED 200-450 and upward with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650, is worth it for a narrow set of things: a Higher Level science in the final year, an internal assessment that is going badly, and a subject that had to be started from scratch after a timetable change. Outside those, it is usually money that would do more as a second subject at the mid-band rate.

sections.heading: The five things that move an Indian family's tuition bill
paragraphs: Bestimate's monthly bands run from AED 240 to over AED 2,000 for what is nominally the same product, a weekly one-hour session. That spread is not noise. Five variables explain almost all of it, and four of them are inside a family's control.

Subject count comes first and dominates everything else. A CBSE or ICSE transfer into the Diploma typically needs mathematics and one science supported in the same term, because the gap pattern hits both at once. Two subjects is two bills. Families who try to cover both inside one weekly hour get a worse result than families who pick one and do it properly, which is a cheaper mistake but still a mistake.

Level comes second: HL prices above SL because the pool of people who can teach Chemistry HL or Maths AA HL to the top of the syllabus is smaller. Timing comes third, and it works in both directions — the final two terms before the May session carry the specialist exam-year band, while the same support bought in DP1 sits in the mid-band and does more good. Internal assessment work comes fourth, and it is block-shaped rather than weekly, which makes it feel expensive when it is actually just compressed.

Fifth is availability, which is the variable families cannot control. Hindi B, Hindi ab initio and some Group 2 languages have genuinely thin UAE coverage, and a thin pool at a fixed hour prices higher in any market. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider base, including IB specialists in India, delivered identically over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

sections.heading: CBSE and ICSE to IB: where the marks go missing
paragraphs: This is the section that decides whether the money is well spent, because an Indian-schooled student entering the IB is almost never short of content. They are short of a set of habits, and the habits are worth naming precisely rather than describing as a general adjustment.

Justification is the big one. CBSE and ICSE reward a correct answer; the IB pays for the reasoning that produced it. In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, 'find', 'show that', 'justify' and 'hence deduce' are four different instructions with four different mark consequences, and a student who gives the right number without the working loses most of the marks. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which catches out anyone whose previous system allowed one in every paper.

In the sciences, the two gaps are uncertainty and coursework. Uncertainty treatment — propagating an error, drawing sensible error bars, justifying the precision of a stated result — is standard IB Physics and Chemistry and is thin in most Indian school preparation. The coursework gap is bigger: a CBSE practical record book and an IB scientific investigation marked against lettered criteria are not the same genre, and a student who has only produced the former has no feel for what 'personal engagement' is worth on a mark scheme.

In the humanities and English the gap is the opposite shape. Students who have learned to write a great deal are penalised for it, because the IB's command terms set a scope: 'outline' wants three lines and 'evaluate' wants a judgement. English A Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, so advertisements, speeches and infographics are examinable, which is a genuine surprise to a student from a literature-only background.

sections.heading: Hindi, Arabic and the Group 2 decision
paragraphs: Every Diploma student takes a Group 2 language, and for Indian families in Dubai this choice has cost consequences that nobody flags at the options evening. The three realistic routes are Hindi B, Hindi ab initio and Arabic ab initio, and they are not interchangeable.

Hindi B assumes prior learning and assesses productive and receptive skills against defined text types and registers. The trap for a household where Hindi is spoken daily is that fluency is not the thing being marked. A student who converses easily can still score poorly on writing a formal letter, a report or a blog post in the register the task demands, and on reading comprehension of unfamiliar written forms. Hindi ab initio is for genuine beginners, and placing a fluent speaker there is not permitted.

Arabic ab initio is the other common choice, and it carries a second benefit specific to Dubai. Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. A student already studying Arabic as an additional language in the mandatory stream has a running start. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

On availability, the honest position: Hindi B and Hindi ab initio tutors are scarcer in the UAE than any other subject an Indian family is likely to ask for. We will tell you if we cannot cover your preferred hour rather than booking a generalist against a specialist syllabus. This is the one place on this page where the limiting factor is supply and not budget.

sections.heading: Maths AA or AI, and what Indian and Gulf universities expect
paragraphs: This decision costs more money than any other single choice an Indian family makes in the Diploma, because getting it wrong means either a year of unnecessary struggle or a closed door at application time. The two courses are genuinely different subjects, not a harder and easier version of one.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented course. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, and the syllabus privileges deductive reasoning. Applications and Interpretation is statistics-led and modelling-led with a graphical calculator assumed throughout. For engineering, physics, mathematics and most quantitative economics degrees, AA — usually HL — is the expected route. For business, design, social sciences and many life-science paths, AI is appropriate and often the better fit.

The complication for Indian families in Dubai is that two admissions systems are in play. A student aiming at an Indian engineering route is usually also preparing for a separate entrance examination with its own syllabus, which runs alongside the Diploma rather than inside it. That is a second workload, and it is the main reason an Indian DP student in Dubai ends up needing two kinds of maths support at once. Families should decide early whether they are funding IB marks, entrance-exam preparation, or both, because the answer changes the tutor.

On specific university requirements, check the institution's own published entry criteria rather than any summary, including ours. Requirements change, they vary by faculty, and a page that printed them would be wrong within a year. The one thing worth stating plainly is that nothing about tutoring is required for admission anywhere, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a process they do not control.

sections.heading: Tuition cost in the context of a Dubai school fee
paragraphs: Tutoring is a line item next to a much larger one, and Indian families in Dubai are usually running the whole education budget in their heads at once. One useful anchor arrived in May 2026: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total.

That matters for planning because it makes the biggest number in the budget a known quantity for a year, and leaves tuition as the variable one. It also changes the arithmetic of a common decision: whether to move a child to a more expensive school or to keep the school and fund tuition. With fees held flat, the marginal cost of the school is predictable and the marginal cost of a tutor is the thing to model.

The second piece of context is market scale. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the Indian curriculum the second largest by enrolment behind the UK one. Seven new private schools arrive for 2026-27 — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. A family considering a move into an IB school has more options each year, not fewer.

Set against that, a mid-band tutoring budget of AED 600-1,200 a month for one subject, from Bestimate's published estimates, is a meaningful but not transformative share of most families' education spend. The planning question is not whether to spend it but where in the two years to put it, and the answer is almost always earlier than families choose.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, and the series your child will actually sit
paragraphs: Indian families carry a calendar instinct from a different system, and one specific error is common enough to be worth naming. Cambridge International's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. A family who plans a Dubai IGCSE year around a February or March exam window is planning around a series their child cannot enter.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, exams run in May/June and November. The published pattern shows why entry deadlines sit months ahead of the paper: the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January — November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June results come in August, with June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used.

For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session. We do not publish a specific IB exam or results date on these pages, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and any date we printed would be second-hand. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator for the entered session and the internal deadline calendar in writing, and verify against ibo.org.

Counted backwards, the planning sequence is the same whatever the board: confirm the session, get the internal deadlines in writing, work out which have passed, then place the tuition budget where it still changes something. The table below separates the dates the board controls from the ones the school controls, which is the distinction families most often miss.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor cannot cross for any fee
paragraphs: This belongs on a page about money because money is exactly how the line gets crossed. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. That is an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student, who can be excluded, not on the seller, who keeps the fee.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. They may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, challenge and narrow a research question, teach the methodology, read the student's own draft and give written feedback against the criteria, and teach referencing conventions. That is the help that actually moves a mark, and it is what the block pricing on this page refers to.

What a tutor may not do is write any part of the work, dictate sentences to be transcribed, supply a methodology or dataset as the student's own, edit a draft into a finished state, or hand over a model answer to be adapted. The practical test is whether the student could explain and defend every line of the work in an oral examination. If not, it is over the line regardless of how it was described when it was sold.

The same principle governs materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference and link the official source. If a provider offers a library of mark schemes as an inducement, that tells you how they are likely to handle the rest of it too.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you are paying legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: A cost question dressed as a compliance one, and the answer is clear enough to act on. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

Crucially for a family comparing quotes, the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and the application runs through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. A provider who builds a permit fee into a rate is inventing it.

There is a related restriction worth knowing if you are comparing an independent tutor against a platform. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. So an arrangement built around your child's own classroom teacher is not one to pursue. This is press-reported rather than read from the policy document, so verify against current ADEK guidance.

Finally, a tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold one, is not KHDA approved, and operates no UAE office, centre or branch. All UAE delivery is online.

process.title: Say which subject is actually losing marks
process.description: Not 'maths', but which paper, which topic and which question type. Send the last two marked assessments if you can. This is the step that decides whether one subject or two is the right spend, and it takes a parent ten minutes with a school report in hand.

process.title: A free trial lesson before any payment
process.description: One session, no charge, with the tutor we think fits the course, the level and the hour. By the end of it the tutor should be able to name the specific habit or topic costing marks. If the match is wrong you say so, and we match again before any money changes hands.

process.title: Agree the shape and the number
process.description: One subject or two, weekly slot or front-loaded block, and the quote for that exact arrangement rather than a headline rate. The plan says what will not be covered as well as what will, because an unbounded plan is how a tuition budget quietly doubles.

process.title: Fixed slot on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Set against your real commute, not the ideal one. Remember the Dubai week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night. During Ramadan the slot moves after Iftar, agreed in advance rather than renegotiated weekly.

process.title: Written work, marked, between sessions
process.description: Work set and returned with written comments against the mark scheme, so progress is visible in something other than a school grade three months later. For internal assessment blocks, feedback is against the criteria letter by letter, on the student's own drafts only.

process.title: Review termly and stop when it stops paying
process.description: At the end of each term the question is whether the slot is still earning its cost. When the gap is closed, the right advice is usually to pause and return for a block before mocks. We would rather tell you that than keep a slot booked for twenty-four months.

Tutors matched here have taught on both sides of that gap, which is why the first session produces a list rather than an impression.

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor for Indian students in Dubai charge per hour?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour at market rates, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Below that, EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, which buys supervision rather than syllabus diagnosis. Above it, named specialists run AED 200-450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits carry a travel premium of AED 180-500 and are not something IB Gram offers in the UAE. These are market figures with sources, not our price list; our own quote follows a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Why does a CBSE student entering IB Diploma usually need two subjects tutored rather than one?
faqs.answer: Because the gap arrives in two places at the same time. The mathematics gap is justification and non-calculator technique; the science gap is uncertainty treatment plus a coursework genre the student has never written. Both bite in the first term of DP1, and trying to cover both inside one weekly hour produces a worse result than picking one and doing it properly. The honest arithmetic is that two subjects costs roughly double. The alternative families often choose — one hour split across both — is cheaper and generally wasted, because neither subject gets enough continuity to shift.

faqs.question: Is Hindi B easier than Hindi ab initio for a child who speaks Hindi at home?
faqs.answer: Hindi ab initio is not an option for a fluent speaker, so the question does not arise that way. Hindi B assumes prior learning and assesses productive and receptive skills against defined text types and registers, which is where household fluency stops helping. A student who converses easily can still score poorly writing a formal letter, a report or a blog post in the demanded register, and on comprehension of unfamiliar written forms. Tutor availability for Hindi B in the UAE is the thinnest of any subject an Indian family is likely to request, so ask early rather than assuming a slot exists.

faqs.question: Should an Indian family in Dubai choose Maths AA or Maths AI?
faqs.answer: It depends on the destination, and it is the costliest choice to get wrong. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-led, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator at both levels, and it is the expected route for engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics — usually at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is statistics and modelling led with a graphical calculator assumed throughout, and suits business, design and many social-science paths. Check each university's own published entry criteria rather than any summary, including this one, because requirements vary by faculty and change.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our home in Mirdif or Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time. The cost consequence is worth seeing plainly: Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor. That gap buys the commute, not better teaching, and for a thin subject like Maths AA HL or Hindi B the local pool in your specific community may be empty at any price.

faqs.question: When in the two years of the Diploma is tutoring money best spent?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families choose. Bestimate's published estimates put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month, against AED 600-1,200 for the same weekly session bought in the mid-band. The final two terms are the most expensive hours in the programme and the least productive per hour, because the student is also sitting mocks, finishing coursework and applying to universities. The same budget placed in DP1, when a habit can still be retrained rather than patched, buys more marks. Keep a block in reserve for the weeks before mocks.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do on an IB Internal Assessment, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the subject content, explain each criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, challenge and narrow the research question, teach the methodology, read the student's own drafts and give written feedback against the criteria, and teach referencing. A tutor cannot write any part of it, dictate sentences for transcription, supply a dataset or methodology as the student's own, edit a draft to completion, or hand over a model to adapt. The test is whether the student could defend every line in an oral. One operator in this market sells completed IAs; that is a malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on your child.

faqs.question: Does our child need Arabic if they are on an IB programme in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. A non-Arab student joins the additional-language stream; KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA also requires that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval. Treat it as a long, low-intensity thread rather than a crisis.

faqs.question: Which exam series will a Dubai IGCSE student sit, and is February an option?
faqs.answer: No, February is not an option from Dubai. Cambridge International's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. This matters because families arriving from India sometimes plan a whole year around a February window their child cannot enter. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong zone timetable, so work from the live official timetable for your centre's zone.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a licence, and should that cost be in our quote?
faqs.answer: They need a permit and it costs nothing, so it should not be in your quote. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through a MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: How does a Dubai school fee compare with a year of tutoring?
faqs.answer: The fee is the larger and now the more predictable number. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. Against a flat fee, a mid-band tutoring budget of AED 600-1,200 a month for one subject, from Bestimate's published estimates, is meaningful but not transformative. It also reframes a common decision: with fees held, the question becomes whether to fund a tutor or move schools.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both IB maths and an Indian entrance exam syllabus?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it is usually two briefs and should be priced as such. The Diploma rewards justification, command-term discipline and non-calculator technique in Paper 1. An Indian engineering entrance syllabus rewards speed, pattern recognition and a different content map. A tutor strong at one is not automatically strong at the other, and compressing both into one weekly hour tends to shortchange the one with the nearer deadline. Decide which you are funding before booking. If both, expect two slots, and expect the entrance-exam preparation to sit outside the school's own calendar entirely.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for the subject and hour we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substituting. Coverage is not uniform: English, mathematics to IGCSE and the SL sciences are well supplied at most hours, while Maths AA HL, the HL sciences, HL Economics and Group 2 languages — Hindi above all — are thinner, and a specific evening slot sometimes cannot be filled immediately. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider base of IB and IGCSE specialists including tutors in India, delivered identically by live video on Gulf Standard Time. What never happens in either direction is a home visit in the UAE.

faqs.question: Is tutoring at the cheap end of the Dubai market ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a specific job. EdFlik's AED 45-65 and Tutopiya's AED 33-52 buy structure, supervision and company. For a Grade 7 MYP student who will not sit down without someone present, that is genuinely the right product and paying four times more would waste money. What the cheap band cannot do is explain why a Maths AA answer scored three out of six, because that requires someone who has taught the course and marked against its criteria. Match the band to the problem: supervision at the bottom, diagnosis in the middle, final-year HL depth at the top.

faqs.question: If our child later takes IGCSEs here, how many subjects will UAE equivalency need?
faqs.answer: Five, and the exclusions matter. The published British-track requirements are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. At least one page ranking in this market states six subjects are required, which is wrong. For the IB track we will not publish a points threshold we have not read on moe.gov.ae; ask the Ministry or your school's counsellor directly.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around a commute from Al Nahda or International City?
faqs.answer: Yes, but be realistic about the hour before booking. A family crossing the Sharjah boundary at peak times usually finds 6.30pm or later is the first slot that survives a term, and families in International City often prefer two weekend sessions to two weekday ones because the weekday arithmetic rarely works. In Mirdif, Karama or Silicon Oasis, where school runs are short, a 4.30pm or 5pm slot holds. Remember the Dubai week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night and a poor place for the heaviest session.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-indian-students.closingHeading: Get the number, then decide where it goes
dubai/ib-tutor-for-indian-students.closingBody: The market rate for a qualified online IB subject tutor in Dubai is AED 150-300 an hour, and the monthly bands published for this city run from AED 240 to over AED 2,000 for what looks like the same product. The difference is subject count, level, timing, internal assessment work and availability — and four of those five are yours to decide. Start with a free trial lesson, bring the last two marked assessments, and the session should end with a named topic rather than a general impression. Sessions are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to UAE homes, and if we cannot cover your subject at a workable hour we will say so.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.tutorsIntro: These are tutors who work regularly with students who joined an IB cohort late. They are used to reading a transcript from another country, finding what was never taught, and building the first six weeks around that list rather than around the next test.

intro.heading: What a new arrival is actually missing
paragraphs: A family relocating to Dubai usually gets the school place sorted before anything else. Dubai's private sector is the densest in the UAE: 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with 17 different curricula licensed, and 16,846 new places arriving with the seven schools opening for 2026-27. Four of those are UK curriculum and three are International Baccalaureate, according to KHDA's own announcement. A place is findable. What is harder is the thing nobody tells you at the enrolment interview: the IB does not run on a national syllabus, so what your child covered in Year 10 in Surrey, Grade 9 in New Jersey or Class X under CBSE in Chennai maps onto an IB course only partially.

The mismatch is specific and it is diagnosable. A student arriving from CBSE Class X into DP1 Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches has met calculus notation but not the IB's insistence on justifying every line with a command term. A student from an American high school has done statistics but may never have met a formal proof. A student from GCSE Combined Science walking into Chemistry HL has done moles and rates but not enthalpy cycles or spectroscopy, and has certainly never written a lab report against five lettered criteria. None of those students is behind in ability. Each is behind on a list, and a list can be worked through.

The second thing nobody mentions is the internal assessment clock. The IB Diploma is two years long and roughly a quarter of each subject grade is produced inside school, on deadlines the school sets rather than the IB. A student who joins in November of DP1 has already missed the lesson where the Maths IA exploration criteria were handed out. A student joining in DP2 may find the Extended Essay first reflection session happened before they arrived. These are not catastrophes but they are invisible until a deadline lands, and they are the single most common reason a new arrival's first report card is worse than their last one in their old country.

Then there is the practical matter of a new city. Sessions have to fit around a Dubai school run, which for a family in Arabian Ranches or Dubai Hills can mean a child is not home and settled until gone 4pm. Weekends run Saturday and Sunday, so Friday evening is a school night, which surprises families arriving from countries where it is not. During Ramadan the school day shortens and the useful study window moves after Iftar. All of this changes what a realistic tuition timetable looks like, and getting it wrong in the first term is how a family concludes that tutoring does not work for them.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one online tuition, live over video, to families anywhere in Dubai. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a newly arrived family that is often the better arrangement rather than the compromise, because the thing you need in your first term is not proximity. It is a tutor who has taught the exact course your child joined, and the pool of those people is not limited to whoever lives twenty minutes from your new villa.

This page is written for the first hundred days. It covers what transfers from your old system and what does not, how mid-year entry works in practice, what the market charges in AED, the exam calendar counted backwards from the session your child will actually sit, and what the UAE Ministry of Education will later want to see when your child applies to a university here.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.programmesIntro: New arrivals land in one of three IB programmes depending on age, and the entry problem is different in each. A Grade 6 arrival into MYP has time. A DP2 arrival in October has a term. The notes below are about entry, not about the programme in the abstract.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, organised around units of inquiry rather than subject textbooks. There are no external exams and no formal grades in the sense a transferring family will recognise. Assessment is a portfolio plus the Grade 5 PYP Exhibition, a substantial group inquiry presented to the school community. Numeracy and literacy are taught, but a child moving from a drill-heavy system can look strong on arithmetic and weak on explaining a method.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai a PYP arrival rarely needs academic rescue; the gap is usually in written explanation and in Arabic, which is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum under KHDA's requirements. A child arriving in Grade 4 with no Arabic sits alongside peers who have had it since FS2. KHDA requires separate Arabic classes for Arab and non-Arab students, so a non-Arab new arrival joins the additional-language stream rather than the first-language one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, and assessment against four lettered criteria per subject scored 0-8 each, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. The MYP teaches through global contexts and expects students to interrogate a question rather than reproduce an answer. Grade 10 ends in the Personal Project, an independent piece with a process journal and a report. Students arriving from exam-led systems usually find the criteria wording, not the content, is what costs them marks.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai runs more MYP cohorts than any other emirate, and many Dubai schools offer MYP to Grade 10 before students choose DP or move to A Level. A new arrival in Grade 9 or 10 therefore needs a view on that fork almost immediately, because MYP-to-DP and MYP-to-A-Level pull in different directions. Where a Dubai school runs MYP alongside IGCSE in the same year group, a transferring family should ask which track the place is actually in.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the Creativity, Activity, Service strand. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. UAE schools sit the May session. The grade is out of 7 per subject plus up to 3 bonus points from TOK and the Extended Essay, for a maximum of 45.
programmes.countryNote: A DP arrival in Dubai mid-course is the hardest transfer in the UAE market, because subject choices made at another school may not exist on the new school's timetable. A student who did Economics HL at a school in Singapore may find the Dubai school runs Business Management HL in that block instead. The honest answer is that one subject often has to change, and the practical work is covering a year of a new course while keeping five others moving.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The IB's fourth programme pairs at least two DP subjects with a career-related study, plus a personal and professional skills course, a reflective project, service learning and a language development strand. It is far less common than the Diploma in the UAE but it exists, and for a transferring student who cannot carry six DP subjects it is sometimes the sensible landing place rather than a downgrade.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Dubai schools run the CP, so a family who wants it has a short list rather than a choice. Where it is available it suits a student arriving late in Grade 11 from a vocational or applied track abroad, who would be set up to fail by a standing start in six DP subjects. Check the IB's own programme finder and then the school directly, because school websites in this market are often a year behind.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones new arrivals most often need unpicked, with the specific place the old syllabus and the IB one fail to line up. This is not a list of everything we cover; it is the list where a transfer gap is predictable.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The course most transfers get wrong. Students from CBSE or ICSE arrive with strong algebra and calculus mechanics but no habit of justification; students from American high schools arrive with the reverse. AA expects proof, and Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which catches out anyone whose previous system allowed one throughout.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling heavy, graphical calculator assumed throughout. A new arrival placed here from a pure-maths background often finds the content easy and the technology unfamiliar, losing marks on calculator notation and on interpreting a regression rather than computing one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The transfer gap is physical chemistry: enthalpy cycles, entropy and equilibrium constants are standard IB and often absent from a GCSE Combined Science background. The internal assessment is a single scientific investigation marked against lettered criteria, and students who have only written school lab reports have no feel for what 'personal engagement' means on a mark scheme.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty treatment separates IB Physics from most national syllabuses. Arrivals can handle the mechanics and struggle to propagate an error through a calculation or to draw a best-fit line with sensible error bars. HL adds rotational dynamics, the quantum topic and more demanding field theory.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the issue rather than difficulty. The IB syllabus is broad and the command terms are precise: 'outline', 'explain' and 'evaluate' earn different marks for the same knowledge. Students arriving from systems that reward full recall write too much and score less.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessment is a Paper 1 guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, a Paper 2 comparative essay, the Individual Oral on a global issue, and at HL an essay on a studied work. Students from literature-only backgrounds are unprepared for advertisements, speeches and infographics as examinable texts.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: The right placement for many new arrivals whose schooling was not in English, and a frequent misplacement in the other direction. English B assesses productive and receptive skills against defined text types; a strong conversational speaker can still lose heavily on register and on writing to a specified text type.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is three commentaries, each on a news article published within a defined window, each applying a different unit of the syllabus. New arrivals routinely discover that one or two commentaries were already submitted by the cohort, which is a scheduling problem before it is an academic one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Often the subject a transferring student is moved into because it is what the Dubai school runs in that block. The content is approachable; the assessment is not casual. HL requires a research project on a real organisation with primary or secondary supporting documents, and the case study for Paper 1 is pre-released.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio and Arabic B
subjects.description: Relevant twice over for a Dubai arrival: as a DP language option and because Arabic is a KHDA-mandated subject in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum. A student with no Arabic at all starts in the additional-language stream, which KHDA requires to be taught separately from the first-language classes.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by an exhibition of three objects with commentaries and a prescribed-title essay, together worth up to three bonus points with the Extended Essay. Mid-year arrivals often land after the exhibition has been done, and that has to be negotiated with the school's TOK coordinator rather than tutored around.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay in a chosen subject with a supervisor and three formal reflection sessions. A student joining in DP2 may have no topic, no supervisor and a submission date months away. A tutor can coach the research process and give feedback on the student's own drafts; the writing has to be theirs.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.regionsTitle: Where new arrivals in Dubai tend to land
dubai/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.regionsIntro: Relocating families cluster in a handful of communities, mostly because of where the schools and the villa stock are. Each has a different practical effect on when a weekday session can realistically start.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: A common first address for families with primary and secondary children because the school options are inside the community. Short school runs mean a 4pm session is genuinely possible on a weekday, which is unusual in Dubai.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Villa communities with internal schooling but a long run to the Al Khail Road corridor for anything else. Families here typically find 5pm the earliest workable weekday slot during term, earlier in the holidays.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Apartment living, often the first lease a relocating family signs before deciding where to settle. Schools are mostly a drive away, so Marina students frequently do their sessions later in the evening or at the weekend.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Older, closer to the coast, and surrounded by long-established British and IB schools. A short commute here means a new arrival can hold both a tuition slot and an after-school activity without one eating the other.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Strong among families arriving from South Asia, with a dense cluster of Indian and British curriculum schools nearby. Transfers here are frequently CBSE-to-IB or CBSE-to-IGCSE, which is the gap list this page is built around.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Tecom
regions.note: Central, mixed apartment and villa, and well supplied with schools in walking or very short driving distance. Useful for a family who wants to start tuition in their first fortnight before the longer-term address is settled.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Sports City
regions.note: Growing fast and popular with newer arrivals on a first contract. Schooling is often a community or two away, which makes a predictable online slot more valuable than a tutor who has to find parking.

regions.name: Downtown and Business Bay
regions.note: Fewer schools, more commuting. A Business Bay family with a child at a school in Al Barsha or Nad Al Sheba is realistically looking at a 6pm start on a school night, and a weekend double session in the run-up to exams.

schoolClusters.note: Longer-established schools serving Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim, Mirdif and the older residential belt. A new arrival offered a place here is usually joining an established cohort rather than a new year group, which makes the internal assessment calendar the first thing to ask about.

schoolClusters.city: Southern and western corridors
schoolClusters.note: The growth area, and where several of the new 2026-27 places sit. Newer schools fill year groups unevenly, so a Grade 9 place may exist where a Grade 11 one does not, and vice versa. Worth checking the published KHDA inspection record before committing.
