sections.heading: What a new expat student actually needs in the first hundred days
paragraphs: A new expat student in Dubai needs three things in order: an accurate gap list against the course they have joined, the internal assessment deadlines the school has already set, and a weekly slot that survives contact with the Dubai school run. Everything else is secondary. Most families instead start with a general tutor and a vague brief, which produces four weeks of pleasant revision of things the student already knew.

The gap list is the whole job. It is produced by putting the new school's scheme of work next to the student's old transcript and syllabus and marking what has not been taught. For a CBSE Class X student entering DP1 Chemistry that list typically includes enthalpy cycles, entropy, equilibrium calculations and the whole of the internal assessment methodology. For an American transfer into Maths AA SL it includes formal proof, non-calculator technique and the IB's command-term discipline. The list is rarely longer than a dozen items per subject, and a dozen items is a term's work alongside normal lessons.

The deadlines come second because they are invisible. The IB sets the final submission windows; the school sets everything before them, including first drafts, reflection sessions and the Personal Project checkpoints. A student who arrives in October of DP1 has missed at least one of those in most subjects. The fix is a conversation with the subject teacher and the Diploma coordinator in the first fortnight, not in the term when the deadline lands.

Third, the timetable. Dubai weekends are Saturday and Sunday, school ends at a time that depends on which community you live in, and the useful study window shifts after Iftar during Ramadan. A session booked at 4pm because that is what worked in London will be missed half the time from Arabian Ranches. Agree the slot against the actual commute, not the aspiration.
bullets: Week one: get the scheme of work for every subject in writing
Week two: ask the coordinator which internal deadlines have already passed
Week three: start on the two highest-weighted gaps, not the easiest ones
Week six: review the list and drop from two sessions a week to one

sections.heading: The curriculum transition map: what transfers and what does not
paragraphs: The single most useful document a relocating family can have is a subject-by-subject map of where their child actually is against where the IB course assumes they are. No school produces this, because no school teaches the system the child left. The table below covers the five transitions that account for most Dubai arrivals, with the real gap rather than a reassurance.

Read the gap column as a work list, not a verdict. In every one of these transitions the content deficit is finite and the habit deficit is the harder half. A CBSE student who has solved a thousand integrals is not short of mathematics; they are short of the IB's insistence that a solution shows its reasoning and that a question beginning 'justify' is answered differently from one beginning 'find'. That is retrainable in weeks, but only if someone names it.

The weeks-of-support column is an estimate from the pattern we see, not a promise. It assumes a weekly one-to-one session plus the student keeping up with class, and it assumes the student actually does the work set between sessions. A student doing nothing between sessions takes two or three times as long, which is the most predictable finding in tutoring and the one families are least keen to hear.

One structural point for DP arrivals specifically: if a subject has to change because the new school's block timetable does not offer the old one, treat that subject as a standing start and resource it accordingly. Trying to close a year of a new HL subject with the same weekly hour you give to the five continuing ones is the commonest planning error in a mid-course transfer.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs in Dubai, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure, because that is the one a relocating family is actually budgeting. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market numbers from a published source, not ours, and they are the right order of magnitude to plan a first year around.

Converted to an hourly rate, the Dubai market sorts into recognisable tiers. A university-student or generalist online tutor sits at the bottom: EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor working online is the middle band, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home visit carries a travel premium that Bestimate puts at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500. A named IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the examiner end.

What moves a new arrival's number is not the subject so much as the shape of the first term. Two sessions a week for six weeks to produce and start clearing a gap list costs more than a steady weekly slot, and then costs less, because the diagnostic block ends. Families who skip it usually spend the same money over a longer period discovering the gap list by failing assessments. The second multiplier is subject count: a DP student with a changed HL subject needs that subject resourced separately, not folded into the same hour.

Three of the six competitor pages measured in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. Publishing the AED bands with their sources is the honest version. IB Gram's own arrangement is a free trial lesson and a consultation first, so the quote you get reflects the actual subject, level and intensity rather than a headline rate.

sections.heading: Online versus a home tutor when you have just moved
paragraphs: This is the decision most relocating families make badly, because they make it on instinct. The instinct says a tutor in the room is better, especially for a child who has just lost their school, their friends and their bedroom. The instinct is not wrong about the child. It is wrong about the constraint, which in the first term is not presence but match.

A home tutor in Dubai is drawn from the people willing to drive to your community for the rate you are paying. For English or general maths that pool is deep. For Chemistry HL, Maths AA HL, Economics HL or Arabic ab initio, in your specific community, at the hour your child is actually home, it is thin and sometimes empty. The travel premium in the table above, AED 180-350 at Bestimate's figures, buys the commute rather than the specialism, and in a mid-course DP transfer the specialism is the whole point.

Online removes the geographic constraint entirely and leaves the scheduling one, which is the easier of the two to solve. It also handles something specific to new arrivals: relocating families travel. A term that includes two weeks back in the home country does not break a video schedule, whereas it reliably breaks a home-visit arrangement and often loses the slot.

IB Gram's position on this is fixed rather than preferential. We deliver UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. If what you want is a person at your dining table in Dubai Hills on a Tuesday, we are not the provider, and the table below is the honest comparison rather than a sales argument.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from the session your child will sit
paragraphs: A relocating family needs to know which session their child is entered for before anything else, because the whole plan hangs off it. UAE IB schools sit the May session. If your child is in DP2 on arrival, that is months away and the internal assessment deadlines are already the live constraint. If your child joined an IGCSE cohort instead, the boards matter: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and the February/March series is offered to India only, so do not plan around it from Dubai.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Pearson's published pattern gives a useful worked example of why entry deadlines sit months before an exam: the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January — November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June results go out in August; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used.

For IB dates specifically, we do not publish a session or results date on these pages. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date we printed would be second-hand. Ask the school's Diploma coordinator for the entered session and the internal deadline calendar in writing, and check ibo.org yourself. That is less satisfying than a date in a table and considerably more useful than a wrong one.

Counted backwards, the planning order for a new arrival is: confirm the session, get the internal deadlines, identify which ones have passed, then build the tuition plan around what is still movable. The table sets out the milestones that matter and who actually controls each one, which is the part families consistently get wrong — most of these dates are set by the school, not the board.

sections.heading: KHDA, your new school's inspection report, and what it actually tells you
paragraphs: In Dubai, private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Every private school is inspected and rated on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the reports are published. For a family choosing a school from abroad, these reports are the only independent evidence available, and they are worth more than any school tour.

Read them for the right thing. The headline band tells you about the school as a whole, which is an average across phases and subjects. A school rated Good overall can be Very Good in secondary English and Acceptable in secondary mathematics, and if your child is a DP maths student that detail matters more than the headline. The subject and phase tables inside the report are where the usable information is.

The other thing to read is the mandatory-subject provision. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. It also requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval.

A word on money in context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. For a relocating family building a first-year budget, that makes the school fee a known quantity and the tuition figure the variable one. IB Gram is not KHDA approved and does not claim to be — a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and we hold none.
bullets: Read the subject and phase tables, not just the overall band
Check Arabic and Islamic Education provision for the non-Arab stream if that applies

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not do with your child's work
paragraphs: This matters more for a new arrival than for anyone else, because a transferring student is under pressure, behind on an internal assessment, and being marketed to by providers who will offer to solve that for money. At least one operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an IB malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain the assessment criteria letter by letter with the marks attached, discuss and challenge a research question, teach the methodology, read the student's own draft and give written feedback against the criteria, and teach the referencing conventions. That is a lot of help, and it is the help that actually moves a mark.

A tutor may not write any part of the work, dictate sentences for the student to transcribe, supply a methodology or dataset as the student's own, edit a draft into a finished state, or hand over a model answer to be adapted. The test a school applies is whether the final work is the student's own, and the test a tutor should apply is whether the student could explain and defend every line of it in an oral. If not, it is over the line.

The same applies to materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link to the official source, because the official source is both correct and legally ours to point at. If a provider offers you a library of mark schemes, that tells you something about how they handle the rest of it.
bullets: Allowed: criteria explained by letter, feedback on the student's own drafts, methodology teaching
Not allowed: writing, co-writing, editing to completion, supplying a model to adapt
The test: could the student defend every line of it in an oral?
Official syllabus documents and past papers are linked, never reproduced or supplied

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the thing to sort out years before you need it
paragraphs: If there is any chance your child will apply to a university in the UAE, the Ministry of Education equivalency process is the paperwork that converts their foreign school certificate into something a UAE institution can accept. It is worth understanding on arrival rather than in the final term, because some of the requirements are about which subjects were taken, and by the final term that is already decided.

For the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must show proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3. Critically, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One page ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five excluding Arabic and Islamic education.

For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold we are willing to print, because we have not read one on moe.gov.ae and an unsourced number on a page like this is a liability rather than a service. Ask the Ministry or the school's university counsellor and get it in writing.

Two cautions. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry runs, not services IB Gram performs, and nothing about tutoring is required for them. And none of this is an argument for tuition — it is simply the administrative reality of schooling a child in the UAE on a foreign curriculum, and knowing it early prevents the subject-choice mistake that cannot be undone in Grade 12.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: A question most relocating families do not think to ask, and one of the few in this market with a clear legal answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and the application goes through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. If a provider tells you the permit costs money, they are wrong.

There is a separate restriction worth knowing, especially if you have moved to Abu Dhabi rather than Dubai. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. So 'your child's own teacher, privately' is not an arrangement to go looking for. This is press-reported rather than read from the policy document, so verify it against current ADEK guidance before relying on it.

Finally, a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. It needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold one and does not operate a UAE office, centre or branch, which is why this page describes online delivery and nothing else.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE calendar and when a new arrival can actually study
paragraphs: Scheduling is where tutoring plans die, and a family in their first UAE year does not yet have the instincts for it. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night and Sunday evening is the one before school, the reverse of what many arrivals are used to. Booking the family's heaviest session on a Friday because it was the quiet day in the old country is a mistake that takes a term to notice.

During Ramadan the school day shortens and the household rhythm changes substantially. For many families the genuinely productive study window moves to after Iftar, and a session at the pre-Ramadan time is either missed or attended by a child with nothing left. The practical answer is to agree in advance that the slot moves for the month, rather than renegotiating it weekly. The same applies to the Eid breaks, which are announced rather than fixed far ahead.

The academic year itself runs from late August or early September to late June or early July in most Dubai schools, with a long winter break in December and a spring break in March or April. New arrivals who land in January or February are joining with two terms gone, which is also when places are most likely to be free, which is why mid-year entry is so common here in the first place.

Build the plan around the quiet weeks. The two or three weeks after a long break, before assessments restart, are the best window a new arrival gets for closing a gap list, and families almost always use them for holiday instead. Using even one of them deliberately is worth more than a month of sessions crammed between homework and a mock.

sections.heading: What happens if no tutor is free for your child's subject
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is itself informative. The honest position is that availability is not uniform across subjects and levels. English, mathematics to IGCSE, and the SL sciences are well covered at most hours. Maths AA HL, Chemistry HL, Physics HL, Economics HL and the less common Group 2 languages are thinner, and a request for one of those at a specific evening hour sometimes cannot be filled immediately.

What we do in that case is say so. The sequence is: we tell you the subject is not currently covered at your preferred slot, we offer the slots that are available, and if neither works we say when we expect to be able to match rather than booking you with a generalist and hoping. A new arrival placed with a tutor who does not know the course loses the first month, which is the month that mattered.

Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, matching extends to our wider tutor base, which includes IB and IGCSE specialists in India. Those sessions run identically — live video, one-to-one, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time — and the subject expertise is the point rather than the location. What does not happen is a home visit, in either direction: the India-based team's home-visit service operates in India only.

For a relocating family the practical implication is to ask early. A DP2 student arriving in October who needs Chemistry HL should ask in their first week, not after the first internal deadline, because the specialist pool at 7pm Gulf Standard Time on a Tuesday is finite and it fills.

process.title: Tell us what your child has actually studied
process.description: Not the year group, the content. The old school's syllabus or scheme of work, the last two reports, and the subject list at the new Dubai school. Transcripts help; a photographed textbook contents page helps more. This is the raw material for the gap list and it takes a parent twenty minutes to gather.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: One session, no charge, with the tutor we think fits the course and the hour. The purpose is diagnostic as much as social: by the end of it the tutor should be able to name two or three things the student has not covered. If the match is wrong, you say so and we match again before any money changes hands.

process.title: The written gap list
process.description: After the trial and usually one further session, you get the list in writing: uncovered topics by subject, ranked by how much of the final grade they carry, with the internal assessment deadlines we know about flagged. This is the document to take into the meeting with your child's subject teachers.

process.title: Agree the shape of the first term
process.description: Usually a front-loaded block of two sessions a week for four to six weeks, then a step down to a single weekly slot. The slot is set against the real school run and the real commute, and the plan says explicitly what will not be covered, which is as useful as what will.

process.title: Weekly work, written feedback, a termly review
process.description: Work set between sessions and marked in writing, so progress is visible in something other than a mark. At the end of the term the gap list is revisited: items closed, items remaining, and an honest view on whether the weekly slot is still earning its place or should be paused.

process.title: Change or stop when it stops being useful
process.description: Tutoring for a new arrival should be a finite intervention, not a standing cost. When the gap list is clear and the student is keeping pace, the right advice is to stop and come back for the exam window. We would rather tell you that than keep a slot booked, and the plan should name the point at which that conversation happens.

whyPoints.title: The gap list is the product
whyPoints.description: Most tutoring for new arrivals is general revision of whatever came up that week. Ours starts from a written comparison of the old syllabus and the new scheme of work, which is the only way to find what was never taught. That document is useful even if you then do nothing with us.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the course, not to the postcode
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the Chemistry HL tutor is chosen because they teach Chemistry HL, not because they can reach Dubai Hills by five. For a mid-course Diploma transfer, which is the hardest version of this problem, that distinction decides whether the term works.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we are not
whyPoints.description: We do not offer home visits in the UAE, we are not KHDA approved, we hold no regulator accreditation and we have no UAE office. We say what the market charges with the source attached rather than publishing a rate card we would not honour. A relocating family has enough to verify already.

whyPoints.title: Sourced facts, not reassurance
whyPoints.description: Every regulatory and pricing figure on this page is attributable: u.ae for the permit and the regulators, KHDA for the mandatory subjects and the fee position, Pearson for the published series pattern, named competitors for their own rates. Where a figure is unverified, including every IB session date, we say so instead of printing it.

whyPoints.title: Built around the academic honesty line
whyPoints.description: The internal assessment is where a struggling new arrival is most likely to be sold something that gets them excluded. Our boundary is explicit: criteria explained, drafts read, feedback written, nothing authored. That is stated on the page rather than buried in terms.

whyPoints.title: A finite plan with an end in it
whyPoints.description: The first-term block is designed to stop. The weekly slot is reviewed termly against the gap list, and when the list is closed the recommendation is to pause until the exam window. Tutoring that never ends is a subscription, not an intervention.

faqs.question: We arrive in Dubai in November and our child is halfway through DP1. How bad is that?
faqs.answer: Manageable, but only if you act in the first fortnight. The academic gap is finite and usually a dozen topics per subject. The real problem is the internal assessment calendar: by November of DP1 most cohorts have had the IA criteria handed out and some have submitted a first draft or done an Extended Essay reflection session. Get the Diploma coordinator to put the internal deadline calendar in writing, find out which have already passed, and negotiate those directly with the school. Then build tuition around what is still movable. Families who treat the content gap as the whole problem discover the deadline gap three months later.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects does a student moving from CBSE usually find hardest in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not the ones families expect. A CBSE Class X student typically arrives strong on algebra, calculus mechanics and factual recall, so the content is rarely the barrier. What costs marks is justification: the IB expects a solution to show its reasoning, and treats 'find', 'justify', 'explain' and 'evaluate' as instructions with different mark consequences. Maths AA Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which surprises students allowed one throughout. In the sciences the internal assessment is the real gap, because a CBSE practical record is nothing like a scientific investigation marked against lettered criteria. Expect ten to sixteen weeks of retraining on habits rather than content.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help our child catch up on an Internal Assessment they joined too late to start?
faqs.answer: A tutor can do a great deal and cannot do the thing families most want. They can explain each assessment criterion letter by letter with the marks attached, help the student interrogate and narrow a research question, teach the methodology, read the student's own drafts and give written feedback against the criteria, and teach referencing. They cannot write any part of it, dictate sentences, supply a dataset or methodology, or edit a draft into a finished state. The test is whether the student could defend every line in an oral. At least one provider in this market sells completed IAs; that is an IB malpractice trigger and the consequence lands on your child.

faqs.question: How much should a relocating family budget per month for IB tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Plan in monthly terms, not hourly. Bestimate's published Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A new arrival's first term usually costs more than the steady state, because a front-loaded block of two sessions a week for four to six weeks is what produces and starts clearing the gap list. After that most families step down to one slot. Monthly packages advertised in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to our villa in Dubai Hills or Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one, live over video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. For a mid-course transfer this is usually the better arrangement rather than a compromise, because the binding constraint in your first term is finding someone who teaches the exact course your child joined, not finding someone who can reach your community by five o'clock. If you specifically want a tutor physically present in Dubai, we are not the right provider and will tell you so.

faqs.question: Our child has never studied Arabic. What happens when they start at a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed for, so your child will study it. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. A non-Arab new arrival therefore joins the additional-language stream rather than the first-language one. KHDA also requires that all teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval. Expect this to be a multi-year, low-intensity thread rather than a crisis.

faqs.question: Which exam session will our child actually sit after moving mid-year?
faqs.answer: Ask the school and get it in writing, because the plan depends on it entirely. UAE IB schools sit the May session. If your child joined an IGCSE cohort instead, Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates — the February/March series is offered to India only, so do not plan around it from Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong zone timetable, so use the live official timetable for your centre.

faqs.question: Is it a problem that one of our child's HL subjects is not offered at the new school?
faqs.answer: It is the hardest part of a mid-course Diploma transfer and it is common, because block timetables differ between schools. A student who did Economics HL elsewhere may find the Dubai school runs Business Management HL in that slot instead. The practical consequence is a standing start in a new HL subject while five others keep moving. The planning error families make is giving the new subject the same weekly hour as the continuing ones. It needs resourcing separately, and it is worth asking the school whether an alternative block arrangement exists before accepting the swap as fixed.

faqs.question: How do we read a KHDA inspection report when choosing a school from abroad?
faqs.answer: Read past the headline. KHDA inspects every Dubai private school annually and rates it on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the reports are public. The overall band is an average across phases and subjects, so a school rated Good can be Very Good in secondary English and Acceptable in secondary mathematics. If your child is a DP maths student, that line matters far more than the headline. Also check the mandatory-subject provision and the phase your child is actually entering, since a strong primary and a thin sixth form sit inside the same single rating.

faqs.question: Are private tutors in the UAE required to hold a permit, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: Yes to the permit and no to the cost. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through a MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: What should we gather before the first session so the time is not wasted?
faqs.answer: Four things, and a parent can collect them in twenty minutes. First, the old school's syllabus or scheme of work for each relevant subject — a photographed textbook contents page is often more useful than a transcript. Second, the last two school reports, for the comments rather than the grades. Third, the new Dubai school's subject list and, if you can get it, the scheme of work. Fourth, any internal assessment deadline the school has already mentioned. With those, the first session produces a real gap list. Without them, it produces a pleasant conversation and a general impression.

faqs.question: Does our child need five or six IGCSE subjects for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five, and the detail matters. The published requirements for the British track are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. At least one page ranking in this market states six subjects are required, which is wrong. For the IB track we will not publish a points threshold we have not read on moe.gov.ae — ask the Ministry or your school's counsellor directly.

faqs.question: How do sessions work during Ramadan and the UAE school holidays?
faqs.answer: The slot moves, and it is better to agree that in advance than renegotiate weekly. During Ramadan the school day shortens and for most families the genuinely productive study window moves to after Iftar, so a session kept at its pre-Ramadan time is either missed or attended by a child with nothing left. Eid breaks are announced rather than fixed far ahead. The long breaks are the opposite opportunity: the weeks after a December or spring break, before assessments restart, are the best gap-closing window a new arrival gets, and two-hour weekday sessions are only realistic then.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is available for the HL subject our child needs?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than booking a generalist. Coverage is not uniform: English, maths to IGCSE and the SL sciences are well supplied at most hours, while Maths AA HL, the HL sciences, HL Economics and less common Group 2 languages are thinner and a specific evening slot sometimes cannot be filled immediately. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, matching extends to our wider base of IB and IGCSE specialists including tutors in India, delivered identically by live video on Gulf Standard Time. What never happens is a home visit in the UAE. If your child is mid-course in an HL subject, ask in your first week.

faqs.question: Is tutoring something a new arrival should expect to need for the whole two years?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling a subscription. For most new arrivals the right shape is a front-loaded block of two sessions a week for four to six weeks to produce and start clearing the gap list, then a single weekly slot while the remaining items close, then a pause. Coming back for a focused block before mocks and before the exam window is usually better value than holding a slot for twenty-four months. The termly review should ask honestly whether the weekly session is still earning its place, and we would rather tell you to stop than keep it booked.

faqs.question: Can lessons fit around a Dubai school run, and what time is realistic?
faqs.answer: It depends on your community and it is worth being honest about before booking. A family inside Dubai Hills Estate with schooling in the community can genuinely hold a 4pm weekday slot. A family in Arabian Ranches with a run along the Al Khail corridor usually finds 5pm is the earliest that survives a term. Downtown or Business Bay with a school in Al Barsha realistically means 6pm, plus a weekend double session before exams. Remember the week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday-Sunday weekend, so Friday evening is a school night — booking the heaviest session there is a common first-year mistake.

dubai/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.closingHeading: Start with the gap list, not with a general tutor
dubai/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.closingBody: The first hundred days decide how a mid-year IB transfer in Dubai goes, and almost all of the damage comes from two invisible things: topics that were never taught in the old system, and internal assessment deadlines the school set before your child arrived. Both are findable in a fortnight if someone goes looking. Book a free trial lesson, bring the old syllabus and the last two reports, and the session will end with two or three named gaps rather than a general impression. Sessions are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not send tutors to UAE homes. If we cannot match your child's subject at a workable hour, we will say so.

intro.heading: Near me, in a city where the right specialist is rarely nearby
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near me in Dubai is a reasonable thing to type and a poor way to sort the answer. Distance made sense when a tutor had to arrive at a building: a 20-minute drive each way was the difference between a lesson that happened and one that got cancelled in March. Once the lesson runs over video, distance stops being a constraint and the thing it was quietly standing in for — availability — is better solved directly.

What a Dubai parent actually needs is narrower than a city. A student taking Chemistry at Higher Level needs someone who has taught that syllabus, knows that Paper 3 is the section where the data-analysis marks sit, and can mark a structured energetics question against the published scheme. There are far fewer people who fit that description than there are tutors in Dubai, and almost none of them live in your community. Sorting by proximity hides them.

Dubai makes this sharper than most cities because the school market is so segmented. The Dubai Media Office reported 227 private schools serving 387,441 pupils in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with the International Baccalaureate on 7% of enrolment against 37% on UK curricula. A neighbourhood with four schools inside a ten-minute drive may have only one running the Diploma, and a Higher Level cohort in a single subject there may number a dozen students.

There is a second reason the nearest qualified adult is the wrong default. The UAE regulates private tutoring by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Its code of conduct, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi school staff as reported by Gulf News, bar a teacher from tutoring students enrolled at their own school. The closest subject teacher is frequently the one person who may not take the work.

A plain word on how this is delivered. Sessions are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time so they fit between the school run and the point where concentration goes. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The trade is deliberate: you lose the person at the door and gain the person who teaches the component.

None of this makes proximity worthless. It decides when a session can start, because the school bus route and the evening traffic set the hour at which a student is home, fed and still able to absorb something. That is a real constraint and this page takes it seriously, district by district. What proximity does not decide is who should be teaching the component, and confusing the two is how a family ends up paying a specialist rate for a generalist hour.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Whether a school near you runs the full IB continuum or picks the Diploma up at 16 changes what a student arrives with. The notes below say what each programme assumes, and what that means for the kind of tutor a Dubai family should be looking for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three Higher Level subjects and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level is where specialist supply thins out: the content runs deeper, the extra papers are the ones that separate grades, and a tutor who is comfortable at Standard Level is not automatically comfortable above it. Match by level explicitly, in writing.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts sit the May session and apply to UK, North American and UAE universities in parallel. Several Dubai schools run the Diploma alongside A Level, so a Year 11 family is choosing routes rather than following one, and the useful tutor for that fortnight is someone who has taught both and can read a marked IGCSE paper against each.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-marked on A to D bands rather than by percentage, which trips up families arriving from a British or Indian system mid-stream. The tutoring need here is usually translation: what the band descriptor is asking for, and how a competent piece of work ends up in a 5-6 band. Subject knowledge matters less at this stage than fluency in the criteria.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP-to-DP transition is where the requests cluster, particularly in mathematics. Schools that run both place the personal project in Year 11, and a student whose Year 11 was spent on that project often enters DP1 with an algebra gap nobody noticed. A diagnostic in the first six weeks of DP1 is cheaper than a rescue in DP2.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, with no external examinations and no percentages. Parents searching for a tutor at this stage usually want reading fluency, number sense or English as an additional language, none of which need an IB specialist. What they do need is someone who will not import a British Year 5 scheme of work into an inquiry classroom and confuse the child.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools also deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies under KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab pupils and a prohibition on combining the two groups. A non-Arab child beginning Arabic as an additional language is the most common primary request in the emirate, and it is a language-teaching brief rather than an IB one.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. The Diploma courses inside it are examined exactly as they are in the full Diploma, so the tutoring brief is identical for those subjects and absent for the career-related units, which the provider assesses.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools license the Career-related Programme, so a proximity search returns almost nothing relevant and a family has no local peer group to compare with. The practical approach is to treat the Diploma courses as the tutorable part and ask the school's coordinator what evidence the reflective project criteria actually require.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: Below, the topic inside each subject that generates most of the requests we receive from Dubai families. Not the whole syllabus — the specific place where a cohort reliably stalls, which is also the place a weekly session earns its fee fastest.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and equilibrium at Standard Level; organic mechanisms and the data-analysis demands of Paper 3 at Higher Level. Requests spike in DP1 term two, when the internal investigation design lands at the same time as the first serious equilibrium questions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circular motion, then the written-explanation questions that ask for a reason rather than a number. Higher Level students who handle the mathematics comfortably often arrive needing help only with the prose half of the paper, which is a different lesson entirely.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus and proof at Higher Level; the step up from IGCSE algebra in the first term of DP1 at both levels. This is the single most requested subject and level combination across Dubai, and the one where early-evening availability is tightest.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical tests and the written conclusion that must follow them, plus documented calculator work. Students moving here from Analysis and Approaches mid-course often underestimate the modelling content and overestimate how much of it is arithmetic.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data-based questions on unfamiliar contexts, and the Higher Level extension topics that arrive late in DP2. Recall is rarely the problem in Dubai cohorts; applying a known process to a named organism in a graph is.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram-to-prose linkage, and the evaluation paragraph that must end in a judgement. Higher Level calculation questions are a separate brief and often need only two or three sessions once the formulae are secure.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Applying a tool to the stimulus rather than describing the tool. The marks a Dubai cohort usually leaves on the table sit in the application and evaluation strands of the case study, not in the content.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis and the global issue in the Individual Oral. Students fluent in English but schooled outside a literature tradition often need technique vocabulary before anything else, which is a short and very productive brief.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Text-type conventions for the writing paper and the structured conversation in the oral. The requests here come disproportionately from families whose child changed curriculum mid-secondary and landed in B rather than A.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-based Paper 1 and the Higher Level regional option essays. The constraint is almost always named detail: dates, figures, named actors. Sessions that build a usable case-study bank move marks faster than essay practice alone.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode precision and the Higher Level resource-management topics. Supply is thin across the whole region at Higher Level, so this is one to ask about early rather than in the term it becomes urgent.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Turning a topic into a knowledge question, and the exhibition's requirement to tie an object to a prompt. A single block of three or four sessions at the right moment usually does more here than a standing weekly slot.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: Proximity is not meaningless in Dubai — it decides when a session can start, not who should teach it. The notes below record what each district's commute does to an evening, which is the part of the map that still matters once the lesson is online.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: Large school population with a heavy CBSE presence and a smaller IB cohort, so a local search returns plenty of tutors and few Diploma specialists. Pupils are generally home by 3pm, making a 4pm start workable on weekdays.

regions.name: Motor City, Sports City and Dubai Studio City
regions.note: Several schools inside the ring but Diploma provision concentrated in two of them. The internal road network keeps the school run short, so 4.30pm sessions hold up even in term-time traffic.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Fast-growing catchments where many secondary pupils travel out to Barsha or Sustainable City schools. Return times drift to 4.45pm or later, which pushes a realistic weekday slot to 6pm.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and The Gardens
regions.note: Dense apartment stock with students spread across a dozen schools. The scheduling constraint here is a quiet room rather than the road, and a pair of headphones usually resolves it.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Sits next to the university cluster, which means plenty of undergraduate tutors advertising locally and few Higher Level subject specialists. Pupils at the nearby schools are generally home before 3.30pm.

regions.name: The Springs, The Meadows and The Lakes
regions.note: Villa communities feeding schools in Arabian Ranches and Emirates Hills. Secondary pupils are rarely home before 4.15pm, and sport on two evenings a week narrows the usable slots to three.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Short physical distances and a long single access road, so a 20-minute journey can become 40 at the wrong hour. Families here tend to prefer a fixed 6.30pm slot that the traffic cannot move.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Mizhar
regions.note: One full IB continuum school plus several large schools on other curricula, so households often run two systems at once. Early slots at 4pm are realistic, which matters for students carrying three Higher Levels.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Festival City, Al Garhoud and Deira
schoolClusters.note: Students we support in this cluster ask most often for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and for English A Paper 1 work. It is also the part of the city where a local search returns the fewest Diploma-specific results, because the schools on other curricula dominate the tutoring market here.

schoolClusters.city: The Sustainable City, Dubai Investments Park and Al Furjan
schoolClusters.note: A newer cluster with two full continuum schools, so Diploma students here have been criterion-marked for years and arrive with the vocabulary already in place. The requests skew towards Higher Level sciences, which is also where the supply across the region is thinnest.

schoolClusters.city: Al Quoz, Al Barsha and Dubai Science Park
schoolClusters.note: A mixed cluster where IB, British and Indian curricula sit within a few kilometres of each other. Families here frequently have two children on two systems, and the practical question is which child needs a specialist and which needs a generalist.

sections.heading: What a proximity search returns in a city of 227 private schools
paragraphs: A local search is a filter, and it is worth knowing what it filters on. It sorts by the business address a provider has published, by whether a listing claims to serve your community, and by advertising spend. None of those three correlate with whether anyone in the result teaches Higher Level Chemistry. The sort is working correctly; it is answering a different question from the one the family has.

The practical effect in Dubai is a results page dominated by generalists and tuition centres in the areas with the most centres, which are not necessarily the areas with the most Diploma students. Al Quoz and Al Barsha carry a disproportionate share of the city's tuition premises; Nad Al Sheba and the Sustainable City carry a disproportionate share of its continuum IB students. The map and the need do not line up.

Worth testing before you shortlist anyone: ask which level of which subject they teach this academic year, and which paper they would start on. A specialist answers in one sentence with a component in it. A generalist answers with a subject group. The question takes ten seconds and removes most of a local results page.
The table below sets out what a proximity search genuinely narrows and what it leaves entirely unaddressed, so you can see which of your decisions it is actually helping with.

One more thing a local result page hides. Tuition premises in Dubai cluster where commercial rent and footfall make sense, which is not where Diploma cohorts are largest, so the geography of the supply has very little to do with the geography of the need.

sections.heading: The twenty-minute radius, district by district
paragraphs: If a tutor has to travel, the radius they will realistically serve is about twenty minutes at the hour your child is free — which in Dubai is the hour when Sheikh Zayed Road, Al Khail Road and the Business Bay crossing are all at their worst. That radius is a different shape in every district, and in some of them it contains no Diploma schools at all.

Think of it as two numbers rather than one. The first is when your child is physically home and fed, which is set by the school bus route and nothing else. The second is the latest hour at which a 17-year-old absorbs new content, which most families put somewhere between 7.30pm and 8pm. The usable window between those two numbers is often ninety minutes, and a visiting tutor spends a third of it on the road.

The table below is the version of the map that still matters. It pairs each district with the school cluster it feeds and a session start that holds up in term time, drawn from what Dubai families actually book rather than from distances on a map.

Once the lesson is on video the first number is the only one that counts. The session starts when the student sits down, and the slot can be 4pm in Mirdif and 6.30pm on the Palm without anybody negotiating with the traffic.

Worth writing both numbers down before you ring anybody. A family that knows its child is home at 4.45pm and fading by 7.45pm has a three-hour window and a clear question to ask; a family that has not counted it will accept whatever slot is offered and wonder in March why the sessions stopped working.

sections.heading: Which Higher Level subjects Dubai is actually short of
paragraphs: Supply is uneven by subject and level, and no provider in this market publishes that. It is the most useful thing a family can know before booking, because it determines whether the right answer is to start next week or to accept a date three weeks out and plan around it. We would rather give a date than put a Higher Level student with someone meeting the syllabus for the first time.

The pattern is consistent. Standard Level humanities and both Standard Level maths routes are comfortably covered. Higher Level sciences are tighter, with Chemistry and Physics the tightest in the early-evening Gulf Standard Time window because the same hours are in demand across the Gulf. Computer Science and the less common Language B options at Higher Level are the thinnest of all, and those are worth asking about a term early rather than a week late.

The dates in the table are match times, meaning how long it typically takes to put a named specialist in front of a student for a trial, not a promise about a particular week. They move with the calendar: the fortnight after mock results and the eight weeks before the May session are the two points where everything tightens at once.

If the honest answer for your combination is a wait, you will get a wait and a date. What you will not get is a generalist described as a specialist, which is the standard failure mode of a marketplace that sorts by distance.

sections.heading: Where the marks go, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: A tutor matched by distance starts with a conversation about confidence. A tutor matched by component starts with a marked script and a known failure pattern. The patterns below are the ones that repeat across Dubai cohorts, grouped by the Diploma's own subject groups, and each has a different remedy with a different number of sessions attached to it.

Two of them are worth singling out because they are cheap to fix and expensive to ignore. The first is the command-term misread, which costs most in the essay-based subjects and almost nothing in mathematics. The second is unnamed detail in the humanities: a Geography or History answer that describes a general process scores in the bottom half of the band however well written it is, and the fix is a case-study bank rather than more essay practice.

The third pattern is the one families least expect. Strong students in Physics and both mathematics routes frequently lose marks not on the mathematics but on the prose — the question that asks for a reason instead of a value. That is a writing lesson inside a science subject, and a tutor who only sets more calculation questions will never touch it.
None of this is visible in a search result. It becomes visible in the first marked paper, which is why the trial lesson in our process starts with one.

The remedy column matters as much as the diagnosis. A command-term problem is four sessions of work; a missing case-study bank is closer to eight; dropped accuracy marks in mathematics can be largely cleared in two or three. Knowing which one you have is what stops a family paying for the wrong eight weeks.

sections.heading: What a session fixes that an evening of revision does not
paragraphs: A student revising alone practises what they can already do. It is not laziness; it is the only thing available, because the questions they get wrong produce no feedback and so no learning. Three hours of unsupervised past papers tends to consolidate the existing mark rather than move it, which is why a family can see real effort and no improvement and conclude the child is not trying.

A session breaks that loop in three ways. It picks the question the student would have avoided. It watches the working rather than the answer, which is where the diagnosis lives. And it marks against the published scheme, so the student sees the mark allocation instead of a tick or a cross. None of those three requires a tutor in the room, and all three require a tutor who knows the component.

The second thing a session does is set the next week's work precisely. Not "revise equilibrium" but four named questions, in an order, with the hard one third rather than last. Dubai students are generally busy rather than idle, and a vague instruction is what loses the week.

The third is pace. Left alone, a student will spend three weeks on the topic they find interesting and avoid the one that is costing marks. A session that opens with ten minutes on last week's weak topic makes avoidance impossible without anybody raising their voice.

There is a fourth gain, and it is the one students mention themselves. Somebody is expecting the work on Tuesday, which converts a vague intention into a fixed appointment. In a Dubai term with three internal deadlines in the same fortnight, that single external deadline is often what keeps a subject from being quietly dropped.

sections.heading: The nearest subject teacher may be the one person who cannot help
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. Under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, applied for through its app, website and e-services system.

The constraint that matters for a proximity search sits in the code of conduct attached to that permit, and in ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff as reported by Gulf News: a teacher may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on it. The direction of travel is clear either way.

So the most appealing result in a local search — your child's own subject teacher, who already knows the class and the deadlines — is frequently the one arrangement that should not be made. Asking a teacher to tutor your child privately puts their position at risk, not yours, and a professional will decline. It is better not to ask.

What a parent can verify is simpler than it sounds. Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, ask what their relationship to your child's school is, and ask the question in writing so the answer is in writing. Any provider that treats those as awkward questions has told you something useful.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges once the car is counted
paragraphs: Published AED figures in this market, read in October 2026, are set out below. They are other providers' rates rather than ours: IB Gram starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and a plan's cost depends on subject, level and how many sessions a week it genuinely needs. What the table adds to the usual price list is the travel column, because that is the part a near-me search is implicitly buying.

A visiting tutor's rate carries the journey inside it whether or not the invoice says so. Bestimate's Dubai figures for in-home one-to-one run AED 180-350, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is roughly the cost of a car in evening traffic, and it buys presence in the room rather than more teaching.

Monthly packages in this market sit at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Compare those on sessions and on minutes, not on the headline: eight shorter online sessions and four long in-home ones are different products, and the second spends a chunk of each visit settling in.

Ask three questions before agreeing any rate in Dubai. Does the figure include VAT. Does it include marking and written feedback outside the session. And what is the cancellation window, since a slot cancelled at 4pm for a school event is a cost somebody absorbs.

sections.heading: Why distance stops mattering once the lesson is on video
paragraphs: Stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Dubai, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Sessions on this page are one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing and a shared annotation surface so tutor and student work on the same script at the same moment. A scanned past paper can be marked up by both of them while they talk.

What that buys is the match. A Higher Level Physics student in Al Warqa is matched to a Higher Level Physics specialist rather than to the nearest available science teacher, and the search runs across the whole pool instead of a twenty-minute radius. For the subjects named earlier as tight, that is the difference between a specialist and a substitute.

It also buys back the minutes. A visiting tutor's hour contains the journey, the arrival, the settling and the departure; a video session contains the hour. Marking happens between sessions rather than in the first ten minutes, so an hour that costs less is also an hour with more teaching inside it.

The honest limitation is physical. Bench practical work and exhibition-based arts components happen at school and belong to the school. What a video session can do with them is the design, the data analysis and the write-up against the published criteria, which is where the majority of those components' marks actually sit.

For families moving between emirates or travelling in term time, the same property helps in a duller way: the slot survives the move. A student in a hotel in Abu Dhabi for a fortnight keeps the Tuesday session, which is not true of any arrangement that depends on somebody driving to a particular building.

sections.heading: Choosing by component instead of by community
paragraphs: The practical replacement for a proximity search is a four-line brief, and it takes a minute to write. Subject. Level. The paper or component causing trouble. The date of the next assessment that matters. Send that with one marked script and the shortlisting problem largely solves itself, because most tutors will self-select out of a brief that names a component.

Then ask the three questions a near-me search cannot answer. Who exactly will teach the sessions. Where marking happens and whether it sits inside the paid hour. And what the first six weeks would target, in component terms. A specialist answers all three quickly. Anyone who answers in generalities about confidence and rapport is describing a different service.

Use the trial lesson as a measurement rather than a meeting. Ours is free, takes no card details, and produces a written diagnosis you keep whether you continue or not: what the script showed, which topics are secure, what the first three sessions would do. Compare two of those diagnoses side by side and the decision is usually obvious.

If the answer for your combination is that nobody suitable is free, we say so and give a date. That is a worse answer than yes and a much better one than a generalist with a confident manner, which is what sorting by distance eventually produces.

Keep the brief when you have written it. Families who end up changing tutor once, for perfectly ordinary reasons, find that the same four lines plus an updated marked script restarts the process in a day rather than a fortnight, because the hard thinking was done the first time.

process.title: Write the four-line brief
process.description: Subject, level, the component causing trouble, and the date of the next assessment that counts. Four lines does more than a long conversation about how your child is finding school, because it lets us check real availability in that exact subject and level before anybody promises you anything.

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: A mock paper, a unit test, a returned draft with the teacher's comments. One marked page lets the specialist arrive at the trial with a hypothesis instead of an introduction, and it is the difference between a first session that diagnoses and one that gets acquainted.

process.title: Hear the honest availability
process.description: We tell you the match time for that subject and level and whether the slot you want exists in the Gulf evening window. If it is two weeks, you hear two weeks. Nobody is put in front of a Higher Level student on the basis that they teach the subject group.

process.title: Free trial, with a written diagnosis
process.description: Sixty minutes with the matched specialist, no charge and no card details. The student attempts a timed question, the tutor marks it against the published scheme, and you receive a note naming the secure topics, the gaps and what the first three sessions would target. Yours either way.

process.title: Fix the slot and the review date
process.description: Agree the weekly time around your real return commute rather than around a map, and set the week-six review in the same message. Sessions run live over video on Gulf Standard Time, and a session note reaches you within 24 hours of each one.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Chemistry means a Higher Level Chemistry teacher, named before you book. Because the lesson is online, that match is made across the whole pool rather than inside a twenty-minute drive of your community, which is where the specialists are not.

whyPoints.title: Availability told straight
whyPoints.description: We publish which subjects and levels are tight in the Gulf evening window and give a real match time. If the honest answer is a two-week wait for Higher Level Computer Science, that is the answer you get rather than a generalist with a confident manner.

whyPoints.title: The hour contains an hour
whyPoints.description: No journey, no settling, no arrival. Marking happens between sessions against the published scheme, so the paid time goes on teaching and diagnosis. That is a larger difference in useful minutes than most of the rate differences in this market.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the real commute
whyPoints.description: A 4pm slot works in Mirdif and does not work on the Palm, and we set the time from when your child is actually home rather than from a distance on a map. Slots can also move after school events without a travel cost attached to the change.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered in writing
whyPoints.description: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Ask us about permit status and the tutor's relationship to your child's school, and you get the answer in writing. We claim no regulator's approval for ourselves.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help that stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Feedback by criterion, delivered separately from the document, with the student's dated drafts untouched. IB Gram does not write, complete or edit Internal Assessments, Extended Essays or Theory of Knowledge essays, and says so on every page.

faqs.question: Does an IB tutor near me in Dubai mean a tutor in the same community?
faqs.answer: It usually means a provider whose published address or service-area claim sits near yours, which is not the same thing. Dubai has 227 private schools across 17 curricula, and a community with four schools inside a ten-minute drive may have only one running the Diploma. The person who teaches Higher Level Chemistry to a dozen students in your area is probably already teaching them. Sorting by distance returns generalists and tuition centres from the districts with the most premises, not the specialists for your subject.

faqs.question: How late can a tuition session realistically start in Mirdif on a school night?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most of Dubai, which is the useful part. Pupils in Mirdif and Al Mizhar are generally home by about 3.15pm, so a 4pm start is workable without touching the evening. Compare that with Dubai Marina or Jumeirah Village Circle, where a 4.45pm return pushes a sensible slot to 6pm. Set the time from when your child is actually home and fed, not from a distance on a map. On video the session begins when they sit down.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subjects are hardest to staff across Dubai?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics are consistently tight in the 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window, because the same hours are in demand across the whole Gulf. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the most requested combination overall. Computer Science at Higher Level and the less common Language B options are thinnest of all. If your child is taking any of those, ask about availability a term before it becomes urgent rather than in the week the mock result arrives.

faqs.question: Where do Dubai students most often lose marks in Chemistry Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Two places. Energetics and equilibrium produce the heaviest content losses, usually a dropped sign convention or an explanation that describes a shift without naming what drives it. The second is Paper 3, where the marks are for handling unfamiliar data and evaluating a method rather than for recall. Organic mechanisms lose marks on curly-arrow placement rather than on the chemistry. All three show up on a marked script within one session, which is why we ask for one before the trial.

faqs.question: What does a twenty-minute radius around Dubai Marina actually contain?
faqs.answer: At 5pm on a weekday, less than the map suggests. The Marina, JBR and Palm Jumeirah sit behind a small number of access roads, so a twenty-minute journey becomes forty at the wrong hour. The schools most Marina secondary pupils attend are in Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim rather than in the Marina itself. A tutor willing to travel into that radius at that hour is a short list, and it is not sorted by who teaches your child's subject.

faqs.question: Does Sheikh Zayed Road traffic change what time our lesson should start?
faqs.answer: It changes when your child is home, which is the only number that matters once the lesson is online. For households in Business Bay, Downtown and the Marina, the return commute lands between 4.30pm and 5pm in term time, so a 6pm or 6.30pm fixed slot is more reliable than an earlier one that keeps slipping. For a visiting tutor it changes much more, because the journey sits inside the hour you are paying for and inside the window your child can still concentrate in.

faqs.question: Is a nearby generalist better than a distant subject specialist?
faqs.answer: For homework supervision at 11 or 12, a competent generalist nearby is fine and cheaper. For a Higher Level Diploma subject it is not a close call. Higher Level content runs deeper than Standard Level, the extra papers are the ones that separate grades, and a tutor who has not taught that syllabus will be reading it alongside your child. Distance is irrelevant to a video lesson, so the only thing being traded away by choosing locally is subject depth.

faqs.question: Which Dubai areas have the most IB World Schools within one drive?
faqs.answer: Al Barsha and Barsha South hold the densest cluster in the emirate, followed by the newer catchments around Nad Al Sheba, Meydan and the Sustainable City, and the continuum schools serving Mirdif and Al Jaddaf. Deira, Al Qusais and Al Nahda have large school populations with proportionally fewer Diploma cohorts, which is exactly where a local tutor search returns the least relevant results. Check what your own school offers on KHDA's site rather than relying on a tutoring site's list.

faqs.question: What does a session fix in Physics Paper 2 that revision at home does not?
faqs.answer: Three things. It picks the question your child would have skipped, which is where the diagnosis lives. It watches the working rather than the answer, so a method mark lost to a missing line gets caught. And it marks against the published scheme, so the student sees where the marks actually sit on an extended-response question. Physics students in Dubai cohorts are usually strong numerically and thin on written explanation, and unsupervised past papers consolidate that imbalance rather than correcting it.

faqs.question: How soon can a Dubai family be matched with a Higher Level specialist?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the subject and the slot. Standard Level maths and humanities usually within a few days. Higher Level Chemistry or Physics in the 5pm to 7pm window is more often one to two weeks. Higher Level Computer Science can be two to three. We give you the real figure before you commit, and if it is a wait you get a date rather than a substitute. The two tightest points in the year are the fortnight after mock results and the eight weeks before the May session.

faqs.question: Do tutors drive to homes in Dubai, or is this taught over video?
faqs.answer: Over video, one-to-one, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Other providers in this market do travel, and their published rates reflect it at roughly AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for qualified online teaching. What you lose is somebody in the room. What you gain is a match made on subject and level rather than on a twenty-minute radius.

faqs.question: What does the market charge per hour for an IB tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published AED figures read in October 2026 run from about AED 45-150 an hour for a generalist or university student online, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 where a tutor travels to an address, AED 200-450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and AED 500-650 or more at the examiner-experienced end. Those are other providers' published rates, not ours. Ask whether VAT and marking are inside the figure, because both move the real cost per useful hour.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge worth a weekly session?
faqs.answer: Rarely weekly, often a block. The course asks students to turn topics into knowledge questions and to tie an object to a prompt in the exhibition, and both are skills that respond to three or four well-timed sessions rather than to a standing slot across two years. The right moments are when the exhibition prompts are issued and when the essay titles are released. A tutor may give criterion feedback on a draft; a tutor may not write or rewrite any part of it.

faqs.question: Our child studies Business Management Higher Level. What is the weak point?
faqs.answer: Application, almost always. Students learn the tools, draw them neatly, and then write an answer that never touches the stimulus material, which leaves the application and evaluation marks on the table. The quantitative questions lose marks on formula recall rather than on interpretation, which is a two-session fix. Higher Level students should also check how much of their grade sits in the internal assessment, because that is where an early, criterion-led conversation pays for itself several times over.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to know which school in Dubai our child attends?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the calendar rather than the status. Dubai schools set their own internal deadlines for coursework, their own mock windows and their own moderation timetable, and a tutor working to the wrong dates is useful in the wrong month. Hand over the school's assessment calendar at the first session. We name schools on this page as market context only, and we claim no affiliation with, or endorsement from, any of them.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody suitable is free in the week we want to start?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date. We would rather leave a slot empty than put a Higher Level student with somebody who teaches the subject group but not the level, because six weeks of that costs more than a fortnight of waiting. If the wait is long, we will say which component could usefully be worked on in the meantime and what your child can do unsupervised without consolidating the same errors.
