dubai/ib-tutor-near-me.closingBody: If you have been searching for an IB tutor near me in Dubai, the faster route is to stop sorting by distance and start naming the component. Send the subject, the level, the paper causing trouble, the date of the next assessment that counts, and one marked script. We will tell you the honest match time for that combination, put a named specialist in front of your child for a free trial lesson with no card details taken, and give you the written diagnosis afterwards whether or not you continue.

intro.heading: "Near me" is the wrong filter for an IB subject
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near me in Al Barari is a proximity search applied to a problem that proximity does not solve. Al Barari is a low-density villa district off Al Ain Road with roughly a few hundred homes and no school inside it. The chance that the right person for Chemistry Higher Level, or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, or History Higher Level with your child's prescribed subject, lives within a short drive of your gate is close to zero. That is not a failing of Al Barari. It is arithmetic, and it is equally true of Nad Al Sheba, Arabian Ranches, Mudon and Dubai Hills Estate.

This page therefore does something the competitors do not: it compares Al Barari with the communities immediately around it, honestly, and then shows that the comparison does not change the answer. Whether you live behind the Al Barari gates or in Arabian Ranches 3, the supply of IB Higher Level specialists within driving distance is thin, the afternoon drive across Dubai is the same drive, and the evening slot you need is after a commute that the school run has already eaten into.

What does change between these communities is the school ecosystem and the usable timetable. A child in Nad Al Sheba may be five minutes from their school; a child in Arabian Ranches 3 may be twenty-five. A Diploma student at an IB continuum school arrives with Middle Years criterion habits; one who came through IGCSE arrives with paper technique and content gaps in the Diploma syllabus. Those differences are real and they belong in a tutoring plan. Geography between neighbourhoods does not.

IB Gram delivers to all of these communities the same way: live, one-to-one, over video, at Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are an India-only service. That means the question of which villa community you live in stops mattering for supply, and the only remaining questions are which subject at which level, and which evening.

It is worth naming what the proximity instinct is actually protecting, because it is not irrational. Parents want someone accountable, someone who can be looked in the eye, and someone who will not vanish after two sessions. Those are the right concerns and distance is simply a poor proxy for them. The things that deliver them are a named tutor rather than a rota, a written record after each session, and a free first lesson in which you watch the teaching before any money moves. All three are easier to provide online than in a model where the tutor's willingness to drive to your gate is the binding constraint on who you can have at all.

The rest of this page is built to be used rather than read. There is a community comparison table, a tutor-supply table, the Dubai market rates in dirhams with their sources, the Higher and Standard Level weighting differences that decide how many sessions a subject actually needs, and the regulatory facts about tutor permits that very few parents in this emirate have been told.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barari.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes matter to families in this part of Dubailand, and the proximity question plays out differently in each. Here is what the search actually needs to deliver at each stage.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based, with no external examination and the Grade 5 Exhibition as its culmination. The useful tutoring target is not a grade but a baseline: reading fluency, number sense and written stamina that the Middle Years Programme will assume from the first week of Year 7.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Barari families this is the one age group where proximity genuinely matters, because a six-year-old often needs an adult in the room. Since IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, we will say plainly when an in-person arrangement is the better fit rather than selling you a screen.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade. Because marks accumulate through the year rather than resting on a final paper, a weak criterion identified in autumn is still inside the final grade in summer. MYP5 adds the Personal Project with its own process requirements.
programmes.countryNote: Al Barari and the Ranches communities are well served for Middle Years tutoring, and this is the level where a reasonably local tutor and an online specialist are genuinely interchangeable in supply terms. The choice at this stage is more about scheduling than about scarcity.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. A meaningful share of each subject grade is banked through the Internal Assessment before any exam is sat, which is why the month you start tutoring changes what tutoring can achieve.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the proximity search breaks down completely. Diploma provision near Al Barari is concentrated in a small number of schools, and Higher Level specialists for any one subject are scarce across the whole emirate, not just inside your community. Selecting by subject rather than by distance is the only approach that reliably finds one.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. The Diploma courses inside it are assessed exactly as they are in the full Diploma, Internal Assessment included, so subject tutoring is identical work.
programmes.countryNote: Offered at a small number of UAE schools. The question families usually need answered is what the Ministry of Education will recognise for a UAE university application, and that should be read on the Ministry's own pages rather than taken from any tutoring site.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barari.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Al Barari families ask for, with what the assessment rewards. Supply of genuine specialists narrows sharply as you move down this list, which is the practical case against searching by distance.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, calculus and proof, with complex numbers at Higher Level. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so students who rely on a graphing display lose marks they cannot see coming. The exploration is worth a fifth of the grade at both levels.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-led method. Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended problem-solving paper that is harder than the course's reputation. Interpretation is where marks go: correct calculator output with no explanation of its meaning earns little.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, fields and electricity with Higher Level extensions throughout. Explanation questions reward reasoning from a principle rather than describing a graph. The investigation needs a controllable variable chosen before any data exists.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure, reactivity, energetics and organic mechanisms. Multi-step calculations compound errors, so one early rounding mistake costs the whole question. Higher Level organic chemistry is the most common reason a Diploma student seeks help in this emirate.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term precision decides the grade. 'Outline', 'explain' and 'evaluate' carry different expectations, and students who write everything they know score below students who answer the verb. Data-based questions reward careful axis reading.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries on published articles, each tied to a different syllabus unit and word-limited. Diagram accuracy carries the explanation built on it. Higher Level adds quantitative content and a policy paper rewarding judgement over description.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis under timing in Paper 1, comparative essay in Paper 2, plus an internally assessed Individual Oral linking a global issue to two texts. Summarising instead of analysing is the standard loss.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-based Paper 1, thematic Paper 2 and a Higher Level regional option in Paper 3. The historical investigation requires formal source evaluation, where students describe content instead of assessing value and limitations.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frameworks applied to real organisations. The Higher Level research project needs a real business issue and evidence the student can actually gather. Describing a company instead of applying a tool is the usual failure.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems, computational thinking, and a programming solution documented through planning, design, development and evaluation. Tracing algorithms by hand is the skill students most often lack, having learned to run code rather than predict it.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Language A and Language B, plus mandated strands
subjects.description: Dubai schools must deliver Arabic alongside the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Tutoring splits the same way: literary and grammatical work on one side, script fluency and spoken confidence on the other.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, assessed on the quality of knowledge-question analysis rather than on content recall. Students struggle because there is nothing to revise; the support that helps is structured argument practice.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barari.regionsTitle: Al Barari against the communities next door
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barari.regionsIntro: These are the neighbourhoods a proximity search for an Al Barari address will return. Each has a different commute and school mix, and none has a meaningfully deeper pool of IB Higher Level specialists.

regions.name: Al Barari
regions.note: Villa plots off Al Ain Road, no school inside the gates, every pupil commuting out. Weekday sessions realistically begin at five. Low household density means almost no local tutor supply at any level.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: The immediate neighbour and the closest dense school provision, including schools running both British and IB routes. Shortest commute of the group, which is the one genuine scheduling advantage over Al Barari.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Mature community with its own primary school and an IB Diploma school nearby. Many pupils have attended one school throughout, so a sudden dip in results is usually a topic problem rather than a transition problem.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 3
regions.note: Newer and further out, with most secondary pupils travelling to Dubailand or Motor City. A high proportion are in their second school in three years, which makes syllabus-gap diagnosis the first task.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Dense provision including an IB continuum school within a short drive. Diploma students from here usually arrive with strong criterion habits and underestimate how differently the Diploma Internal Assessment is marked.

regions.name: Motor City
regions.note: Large British-curriculum cohort, so Diploma students here mostly came through IGCSE rather than the Middle Years Programme. The Maths route decision at Diploma entry is the recurring question.

regions.name: Mudon
regions.note: Villa community with schooling spread across the Dubailand periphery and shared transport that shifts arrival times day to day. A fixed online slot absorbs that variation better than a tutor waiting at a gate.

regions.name: Town Square
regions.note: Younger demographic, most pupils in primary or lower secondary. Middle Years criterion support and Arabic as an additional language are the two most requested streams, well ahead of Diploma work.

schoolClusters.city: Nad Al Sheba and Dubailand
schoolClusters.note: The nearest cluster to Al Barari and the one most pupils commute into. It mixes IB continuum schools with British-curriculum schools that run IGCSE before splitting into A Level or the Diploma, so neighbours can be on quite different routes.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills and the Ranches
schoolClusters.note: The closest dense IB Diploma provision, reachable from Al Barari in a single drive outside peak. Several schools here run the full continuum, which shapes how their Diploma students approach assessment.

sections.heading: What a proximity search returns for an Al Barari address
paragraphs: Type the phrase and you get three kinds of result. Agencies that serve all of Dubai and will quote you a rate that includes a drive to your gate. Marketplaces that list independent tutors by self-declared area, where 'Dubailand' can mean anywhere in a thirty-kilometre arc. And online platforms, including this one, that do not use distance as a filter at all. The first two look local and the third admits that it is not.

The honest position is that for most IB subjects the third category is the one that can actually produce a specialist, and the reason is household arithmetic. Al Barari is a small, low-density community. The number of residents within it who teach Chemistry Higher Level to examination standard, have current syllabus knowledge, and have an unused Tuesday evening is realistically zero. Expand the radius to Nad Al Sheba and the Ranches and the number stays very small, because a specialist in one Higher Level subject is a narrow thing and there are not many of them in the whole emirate.

What a local tutor can genuinely provide is a younger child's supervised homework hour, general Middle Years subject support, and the presence of an adult in the room for a pupil who needs one. Those are real services and distance matters for them. We do not offer them in the UAE, because we make no home visits here, so if that is what your child needs this page should send you elsewhere rather than talk you into a screen.

For Diploma subject work the ranking changes completely. The variables that predict whether tutoring works are whether the tutor knows the specification, whether they can read a mark scheme, and whether they turn up every week. Distance predicts none of those and actively reduces the pool you choose from.

sections.heading: Al Barari compared with the communities around it
paragraphs: Here is the comparison a proximity search implies but never shows you. These communities sit within a short drive of each other in the Dubailand belt, they share schools and roads, and they differ in ways that matter for scheduling rather than for supply. Read the right-hand column of the table: the answer to the tutoring question is the same in every row, which is the point of putting them side by side.

The differences that do matter are commute length and school route. A Nad Al Sheba pupil can be home by half past three; an Arabian Ranches 3 pupil on a shared bus may not be settled until half past four. That is a full hour of difference in when a session can start, and over a term it decides whether a weekday slot is sustainable or whether the family should be looking at a weekend morning. School route matters because a Diploma student from an IB continuum school and one from a British-curriculum school need different first six sessions even in the same subject.

What does not differ is specialist supply. No community in this belt has a deeper bench of Higher Level subject teachers than any other, because the constraint is the total number of such people in Dubai rather than how they are distributed. Nor does the cost difference go the way families expect: an in-home tutor charges more to reach the further communities, so the premium rises with distance from the centre while the quality of the available pool does not.

Use the table to decide your slot and your diagnosis, not your provider. Whichever of these gates you live behind, the shortlist worth having is the list of people who teach your child's subject at your child's level.

sections.heading: The tutor-pool arithmetic, subject by subject
paragraphs: This is the table that explains why 'near me' fails. It is not a claim about Al Barari being poorly served; it is a claim about how narrow a Higher Level specialism is. A person who teaches Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, knows where Paper 1 marks disappear without a calculator, and has marked the exploration against its criteria is not interchangeable with a good general maths teacher, and there are far fewer of them.

Now apply a distance filter. You are asking that person to live within driving range of a specific villa community and to have a free slot in a narrow evening window on a specific day. Each filter multiplies the scarcity. Remove the distance filter and you remove the one constraint that has nothing to do with teaching quality. That is the entire argument for online delivery in this market, stated as arithmetic rather than as a benefit.

The practical consequence shows up in what families actually get. An in-home search in a villa community usually ends with a capable generalist teaching a Higher Level science, which produces reasonable homework support and very little movement on paper technique. An online search ends with someone who has taught the specification, which is why the diagnostic session so often relocates the problem on the first attempt.

One caveat belongs here for balance. Online delivery adds its own requirement: a quiet room, a reliable connection and a student who will engage with a screen for an hour. For Diploma-age students that is rarely an obstacle. For a distractible Year 5 it can be, and in that case the honest answer is in-person tuition from a provider who offers it, which is not us in this country.

sections.heading: What it costs, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages open their pricing with the premium tier so that everything below it looks reasonable. This one starts at the bottom, because for a lot of families the cheapest workable option is the right one and nobody tells them it exists.

At the bottom of the Dubai market sit online tutors charging from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Those figures are theirs, published by them, read in October 2026. For supervised homework, Middle Years consolidation and keeping a Year 8 on top of weekly work, that tier is genuinely adequate and a family spending four times as much for the same job is wasting money. Monthly, at one session a week, that is roughly AED 240 to AED 600.

The middle band, roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour online, is where qualified subject teachers sit. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is the right band for Standard Level Diploma subjects and strong Middle Years work, and for most families it is where the money should go. Above it, AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond buys specification-level knowledge: TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's table reaches AED 450 and above for IB and IGCSE specialists. That premium is worth paying for Higher Level subjects and Internal Assessment coaching, and is usually wasted on a Year 7.

In-home visits run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with monthly packages seen at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions against around AED 799 for eight online sessions. The premium there is the drive, which for a community off Al Ain Road is a real cost. IB Gram publishes no hourly rate on this page, because the right figure depends on subject, level and weeks remaining; what we publish is the market, so any quote can be checked, and a free first lesson so you judge the tutor rather than the number.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, and what it does to session count
paragraphs: Parents in these communities routinely ask how many sessions a subject needs, and the answer depends far more on level than on the child. Higher Level is not Standard Level with harder questions. It adds syllabus content, it adds assessment components in several subjects, and in the sciences and mathematics it extends the depth of every topic rather than appending a few at the end.

The practical implication is that a Higher Level subject consumes roughly half again as much tutoring time as the Standard Level version of the same subject to reach the same relative position. A Standard Level student who is behind can often be brought level in a term of weekly sessions. A Higher Level student with the same gap is usually looking at a term of weekly sessions plus a holiday block, because there is more ground and the questions require sustained multi-step reasoning rather than recall.

This matters when a family is choosing where to spend. Three Higher Level subjects all tutored weekly is more evening than most Diploma students have, and it produces a student too tired to do the set work, which is where most of the gain actually comes from. The usual sensible allocation is one Higher Level subject at two sessions a week, or two Higher Level subjects at one each, with the third managed through school support and set work.

The table gives the structural comparison. Treat it as a guide to how the levels differ in kind rather than as a component list for a specific subject, because each subject's weightings are set in its own current guide and those are revised periodically. Your child's teacher or Diploma coordinator can confirm the exact figures for the course being sat.

sections.heading: The regulator, the school report and the mandatory subjects
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Inspection runs annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. If you are comparing communities because you are also comparing schools, the inspection report is the document to read, and the part worth reading is the subject and phase commentary rather than the headline band.

The scale of the market is worth knowing when you weigh a proximity search. Dubai had 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. Seven new private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places. So the IB cohort in Dubai is a minority of a very large market, which is exactly why Higher Level specialists are thin on the ground in any single community.

The other thing to understand about your child's timetable is that it carries more than the Diploma. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies and prohibits combined classes, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Mandatory-subject time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit.

One caution. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and nobody in this market should claim such a thing without showing a permit number. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. We name KHDA because it governs your child's school and publishes a report you should read.

sections.heading: Permits: the question to ask whoever you hire
paragraphs: A proximity search surfaces a lot of independent tutors, and most Dubai parents have never been told that private tutoring here is permit-regulated. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 regarding the introduction of private tuition work permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. MoHRE's own service page is titled 'Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee, and gives a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system. So if a tutor tells you the permit is costly or optional, both halves of that are wrong.

No fine amount appears here, and you should distrust any page that prints one. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and the figure circulating online could not be verified. Publishing an unverifiable penalty to frighten parents into booking is a tactic, not information.

There is one more question worth asking, especially if your family straddles emirates. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to pupils enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK document if it affects your decision. Either way, 'your child's own teacher, privately' is an arrangement to avoid rather than to seek out.

sections.heading: Coursework boundaries, stated before you ask
paragraphs: This search result includes operations that sell completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is not tutoring, and the consequence of submitting bought work falls on the student rather than the seller. Because parents in Dubai are often approached by such providers through the same channels as legitimate ones, it is worth setting out the line before anyone asks.

A tutor may teach the content a piece of coursework rests on, explain what each criterion rewards and what its descriptors actually mean, discuss whether a research question will generate usable data, read the student's own draft and give feedback, and teach referencing properly. That is the same range a supervising teacher works within, and it is where almost all of the available improvement lies.

A tutor may not write any part of the work: not a paragraph, not a method, not a conclusion, not a rewritten section. A tutor may not hand over a topic to be adopted wholesale, edit a draft into something the student did not produce, or supply data the student did not collect. The test we apply and state to the student is that any sentence in the submission must be theirs. Where a draft needs changing, the tutor says what is wrong and the student makes the change.

There is a self-interested argument for the same position, which is worth knowing because it is more persuasive to a sixteen-year-old than the ethical one. The criteria that carry the most accessible marks reward engagement, exploration and reflection, and work a student did not do reads exactly like work a student did not do. The students who score well chose a question they could investigate, early, and then did the weeks of small steps. That is the thing a tutor is actually for.

process.title: Drop the distance filter
process.description: Tell us the subject, the level and the evenings that genuinely work, and leave out where you live beyond the time zone. Al Barari, Nad Al Sheba and the Ranches produce the same shortlist once proximity stops being a criterion, and that shortlist is larger and more specialised than any of them could supply locally.

process.title: A diagnostic that produces evidence
process.description: Before teaching begins, the tutor works through a past paper or recent school tasks with your child under timing where it helps, then reports where marks were lost by type: content, method, units, command term or timing. This regularly contradicts both your theory and your child's, which is the point of doing it first.

process.title: Meet the tutor on a free first lesson
process.description: One full lesson, no charge, with the person who would teach every session afterwards. Judge whether they know the course and its mark scheme, whether they found the real gap, and whether the work they set was clear enough to attempt alone. If any answer is no, say so and we will match again.

process.title: Pick the slot the commute allows
process.description: For Al Barari the realistic weekday start is five o'clock or later, and for the further Ranches phases it is later still. Where a weekday evening is genuinely overloaded we will suggest a weekend morning instead, because a tired session is a wasted one. Ramadan weeks shorten rather than skip.

process.title: Session notes the same evening
process.description: A short written note after each lesson: what was covered, what was wrong, what is set, what next. You read it that night rather than waiting for a school report, and it doubles as the record showing that any assessed work is your child's own and the tutor's role was feedback.

process.title: Review at every real checkpoint
process.description: Each report, mock and marked paper is a point at which the plan is tested against evidence rather than renewed by habit. Sometimes the right call is to stop in one subject and move the hour elsewhere, and we will say so. A weekly session with no current target has become a routine rather than a plan.

whyPoints.title: Selection by subject, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: Because delivery is online, the shortlist is everyone who teaches that subject at that level rather than everyone within reach of an Al Barari gate on a Tuesday. For Higher Level sciences, Maths AA and minority Paper 3 options, that is the difference between a specialist and a capable generalist.

whyPoints.title: An honest account of what proximity buys
whyPoints.description: This page says plainly where a local in-person tutor is the better answer: early primary, and pupils who need an adult in the room. We do not offer that in the UAE, so in those cases the useful thing we can do is tell you to look elsewhere rather than sell you a screen.

whyPoints.title: One named tutor, every week
whyPoints.description: The same person teaches every session, so nobody spends the first ten minutes rediscovering where your child is. For Internal Assessment work this is a requirement rather than a preference, since an investigation develops across weeks and cannot be usefully commented on by someone who missed the last one.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: The dirham bands here are competitors' own published figures with the month they were read, and they start at the cheapest tier rather than the premium one. Any quote you receive, ours included, can be judged against something real, which three of the six pages ranking for these searches make impossible.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain criteria, test viability and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They write no part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, and they say so to your child. In a market where completed coursework is openly sold, that boundary protects the candidate.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we do not do
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE. No special-educational-needs assessment. No guaranteed grades or predicted scores. No claim of approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because we hold none.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB tutor living near Al Barari?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not for a Higher Level subject. Al Barari is a small, low-density villa community with no school inside it, so the chance that a current Chemistry Higher Level or Maths Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist lives within a short drive and has a free evening slot is close to zero. The same is true of Nad Al Sheba, Mudon and the Arabian Ranches phases, because the constraint is how few such specialists exist in the emirate rather than how they are distributed between communities. Selecting by subject instead of distance is what finds one.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send anyone to an Al Barari address?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE session is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run only in India and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. The benefit you get in exchange is the removal of the distance filter from the shortlist, which for Higher Level subjects usually matters more than the room. Where a child genuinely needs an adult physically present, this page will tell you so rather than talking you into a format that will not work for them.

faqs.question: How does Al Barari compare with Nad Al Sheba for getting a tutor?
faqs.answer: For specialist supply, they are the same: neither community has a meaningful pool of IB Higher Level subject teachers, because the shortage is emirate-wide. What differs is the commute. A Nad Al Sheba pupil is often home by half past three and can start a session at half past four; an Al Barari pupil commuting out of the community is realistically starting at five. Over a term that hour decides whether a weekday evening slot is sustainable or whether a weekend morning is the better arrangement for your household.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to get IB help in this area?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai start at roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for online budget and university-student tutors, which works out at around AED 240 to AED 600 a month at one session a week. For homework supervision and Middle Years consolidation that tier is genuinely adequate, and paying four times as much for the same job wastes money. The qualified subject tutor band, roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, is the right level for Standard Level Diploma work. Those are published market figures read in October 2026, not our prices.

faqs.question: Why do Higher Level subjects need more sessions than Standard Level ones?
faqs.answer: Because Higher Level is not Standard Level with harder questions. It adds syllabus content, extends the depth of most topics rather than appending a few, and in the sciences and mathematics adds an entire additional paper with its own technique. A Standard Level student who is behind can often be brought level in a term of weekly sessions; a Higher Level student with the same gap usually needs that term plus a holiday block. Budget roughly half again the time, and do not try to tutor three Higher Level subjects weekly at once.

faqs.question: Should we book a weekday evening or a weekend morning?
faqs.answer: In villa communities with long commutes, weekend mornings are underused and often better. A Diploma student on a Saturday morning is rested; the same student at half past six on a Wednesday has done a drive, a full school day and two hours of homework first. Weekend slots also allow a longer session or two subjects back to back, and specialist availability is frequently better. If your child's week is already overloaded, moving the session rather than shortening it is usually the fix that works.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor start after we enquire from Al Barari?
faqs.answer: For Middle Years subjects and common Standard Level Diploma courses, usually within a few days, because supply is broad once distance is not a filter. For Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, or a specific Paper 3 option, it can take longer and we will tell you so rather than booking a generalist into the slot. If the subject cannot be covered at a Gulf Standard Time-compatible hour at all, we say that too. Nothing is confirmed until you have had the free first lesson.

faqs.question: Do independent tutors in Dubai need a permit, and should I check?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of pages quoting amounts. Ask to see the permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance, and ask any agency the same question.

faqs.question: What does the KHDA inspection band actually tell me when comparing schools?
faqs.answer: Less than parents assume. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the band is a summary of a long document. The useful content sits in the subject and phase commentary, which often names the precise weakness a parent has been sensing without evidence. A report saying secondary mathematics attainment is below expectation while everything else is strong tells you more about your child's problem than the overall rating does. Read the current report for any school you are weighing up.

faqs.question: Why does my child have Arabic lessons at an IB school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the emirate requires it regardless of the licensed curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies and prohibits combined classes, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Practically, that means the school day carries load beyond the six Diploma subjects, and Arabic is one of the most requested tutoring streams in Dubai, split along the same first-language and additional-language line.

faqs.question: May an Al Barari tutor comment on an Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is exactly the right use of a tutor. Feedback on the student's own draft, explanation of what each criterion rewards, discussion of whether a research question will produce usable data, and teaching of referencing conventions are all legitimate and are what a supervising teacher does. What a tutor cannot do is write any part of the work, supply a topic wholesale, edit a draft into something the student did not produce, or provide data the student did not collect. Our tutors state that boundary to the student directly.

faqs.question: Is the free first lesson genuinely free, and what should I look for?
faqs.answer: One full lesson, no payment and no card required. Judge it on three things rather than on rapport. Did the tutor show real knowledge of the specific course and level, including how marks are awarded? Did they locate the actual gap rather than accepting your child's account of it? Was the work set afterwards clear enough to attempt without help? If any answer is no, tell us and we match again. That hour settles the single most important variable in tutoring before any money changes hands.

faqs.question: How many tutored subjects can a Diploma student realistically manage?
faqs.answer: One subject at two sessions a week, or two subjects at one session each, is the sustainable maximum for most Diploma students in term time. Three tutored subjects produces a student too tired to do the set work, and the set work is where most of the gain comes from. If three subjects genuinely need attention, the usual answer is to sequence them across terms and holidays rather than run them all at once. We will say so rather than take the larger booking, because an exhausted student does not improve.

faqs.question: What happens at the end of a block of sessions?
faqs.answer: The plan is reviewed against the evidence available: the latest report, a mock result, or a marked past paper. Sometimes the right outcome is to stop, because the subject is secure and the hour is better spent elsewhere, and we will tell you when that is the case. Sometimes it is to move to a different subject with the same tutor or a new one. What we will not do is roll a weekly session forward indefinitely with no current target, because at that point it has become a habit rather than a plan.

faqs.question: Are there IB schools inside Al Barari itself?
faqs.answer: No school sits inside the Al Barari community. Pupils commute out, most often to the Nad Al Sheba and Dubailand belt or west towards Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills Estate, where IB Diploma provision is concentrated in a small number of schools. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment, and seven new schools including three IB schools open for 2026-27. Named schools on this page are ecosystem context; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

Specialist supply is thin in all of them, the commute decides your slot rather than your provider, and the variables that predict whether tutoring works are whether the tutor knows the course, can read a mark scheme and turns up every week. So send us the subject, the level and the evenings that work, book a free first lesson with the named specialist who would continue, and judge them on whether they found the real gap in an hour. dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barsha.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach named Diploma courses at Higher and Standard Level to students at Al Barsha schools. Matching runs on course, level and the deadline in front of the student, which means a Chemistry Higher Level tutor is assigned to a Chemistry Higher Level problem rather than to whoever is geographically convenient.

intro.heading: A proximity search, answered with a calendar
paragraphs: A near-me search is a map query. The phone answers it with a radius, and the radius is drawn around your home in Al Barsha 1, 2, 3 or South. For a dentist that is the correct filter. For an IB Diploma subject at Higher Level it is close to useless, and it is worth being precise about why. The Diploma is six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, drawn from a menu that includes two mathematics routes, two English routes and a long list of group three and group four options. A student needing Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level with Paper 3 in front of them is not looking for a maths tutor. They are looking for one of a modest number of people in the region who teach that specific paper well.

Draw a five-kilometre circle around Al Barsha 2 and you have filtered that already small group down to whoever happens to live inside it and be free at 17:00 on a Tuesday. The circle does not improve the teaching. It only reduces the choice. Meanwhile the thing that genuinely determines whether the next three months produce a grade change is sitting on a sheet of paper the school sent home in September, and almost nobody reads it as the planning document it is.

That sheet is the Diploma calendar. It carries the internal deadline for every piece of internal assessment, the mock window, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay dates, and the Extended Essay milestones. All of those are set by the school rather than by the IB, because the school has to mark, moderate and upload before the external deadlines fall. Work backwards from them and the picture of what tutoring should be doing in any given fortnight becomes obvious. Work forwards from a vague sense that a child needs help and you buy twelve months of weekly sessions that cover whatever the student happened to be confused about that week.

This page is organised as that calendar. It walks the two-year Diploma from the start of DP1 to the final fortnight, naming what each stretch has to produce and where the recoverable marks sit in each one. It covers the subject-choice decisions in DP1 that quietly determine the ceiling, the January mock and the high-return eight weeks after it, the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay load that runs underneath everything else, and the point in the year where a subject option is still changeable and the point after which it is not.

A note on delivery, stated early so there is no ambiguity. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we arrange only in India. Every lesson described on this page is one tutor and one student over live video, at a time agreed with the family. Where the in-home market is mentioned, it is being priced and compared, not offered. The relevant Dubai market band for an in-home one-to-one visit is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, and a section below looks at exactly what the difference between that and an online specialist rate is actually buying.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barsha.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes matter to Al Barsha families, and each has its own clock. The notes below are about timing rather than content: when the decisions fall, and when it becomes too late to change them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight against a published strand descriptor. A student can know the content and sit at a five because the criterion being assessed is inquiry or communication rather than knowledge. The Personal Project in the final year is a substantial piece of independent work with its own supervision and reporting requirements, and it tends to collide with everything else in the spring term.
programmes.countryNote: In the Al Barsha cluster the MYP runs at Dubai International Academy Al Barsha and GEMS World Academy Dubai, and the handover into the Diploma is where most tuition enquiries originate. The critical timing point is that Diploma subject choices are made in the final MYP year, on the strength of criterion grades that measure something different from what a Diploma paper measures.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject and is produced over weeks rather than hours. Final grades run to seven per subject with up to three bonus points available from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix, making 45 the maximum.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools register for the May session, which makes the preceding autumn and winter the loaded part of the calendar: internal assessment deadlines, mocks and the Extended Essay final draft all land in that window. The November session exists mainly as a resit route. An Al Barsha family planning tuition should treat September to February as the expensive months and March onwards as consolidation.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, service learning and a language development strand. It carries a lighter academic load than the full Diploma and suits a student who is strong in a narrow area. Tutoring concentrates on the Diploma courses taken and on the reflective project's research method rather than across six subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools license the Career-related Programme, so an Al Barsha family considering it is generally looking outside the immediate district. Where a student is on it, the tutoring requirement and the cost are both materially lower than for a full Diploma, which is worth knowing before assuming the two are priced alike.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barsha.subjectsIntro: The courses below are the ones Al Barsha Diploma students most often need help with, and the notes name the component where the clock runs out rather than the content list, which is in the school's subject guide.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The calculator-free paper is where the term's work shows or does not. At Higher Level, Paper 3 is a two-part investigation worth roughly a fifth of the grade, and students typically meet their first full one in a mock. The exploration has to be scoped before the end of DP1 to be written without panic in DP2.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, which students mistake for easier. Modelling questions require choosing a function family and justifying the choice, and statistics questions require stating the conclusion in the right terms. The exploration tends to arrive data-rich and analysis-poor because the data was collected before the question was settled.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The investigation is the piece that needs calendar discipline: a research question agreed in DP1, data collected before the winter break of DP2, and the evaluation written with time left. Content-wise, organic mechanisms and energetics carry the losses, usually for notation reasons rather than conceptual ones.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circuits are the reliable collapse points, and the cause is unit tracking and sign conventions rather than concept. Paper 2 extended responses reward a labelled diagram drawn before any algebra. Higher Level adds depth that compounds any weakness carried out of the Middle Years Programme.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume makes it look like a memory subject and command terms make it one about precision. Outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each demand a different answer shape, and writing everything known on a four-mark question scores two. Data-based questions on Paper 2 are the most recoverable component in the subject.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral needs a global issue and two extracts, one from each of two works, and must be rehearsed rather than improvised. Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis where the common failure is describing content instead of analysing construction. Both are coachable; neither improves by reading more.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal assessment commentaries, each under 800 words, each tied to a different syllabus unit, each needing a news article that actually illustrates something assessable. Students pick articles first and discover the mismatch later. Diagrams drawn early and referred to in the prose carry marks that argument alone cannot recover.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application separates grades: students name a framework and then do not apply it to the case in front of them. The Higher Level extended case study is released in advance, which rewards preparation and punishes students who meet it for the first time in the examination hall.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The developed solution and its documentation form the internal assessment, and the documentation is where marks go: the criteria reward a defensible design record rather than working code alone. Pseudocode and trace tables are under-practised and directly tested.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The exhibition requires three objects and a 950-word commentary tied to published prompts; the essay is 1,600 words on a prescribed title. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words assessed across five criteria, with the research question doing most of the work. Together they contribute up to three points, and both run underneath every other deadline.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barsha.regionsIntro: The near-me radius lands differently depending on which part of Al Barsha you are in. The notes below say what each community does to an evening, because that is the only part of the geography that actually affects tutoring once the car is removed.

regions.name: Al Barsha 1
regions.note: Red Line Metro at Mall of the Emirates, the densest school cluster in the district, and the shortest pickup times. The earliest realistic weekday start here is around 16:15.

regions.name: Al Barsha 2

regions.name: Al Barsha 3

regions.name: Al Barsha South

regions.name: Al Sufouh

regions.name: Al Quoz

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh IB schools
schoolClusters.note: The Diploma cohort in this part of Dubai is spread across a handful of schools rather than concentrated in one, which is precisely why a proximity search produces thin results for a specific Higher Level course. schoolClusters.city: British and American schools in the same radius
schoolClusters.note: Several schools in the Al Barsha radius run no Diploma at all, which matters for a near-me search because it means the local population of IB-experienced teachers is smaller than the local population of teachers. sections.heading: What a near-me search returns in Al Barsha, and why the radius is the wrong filter
paragraphs: Run the search and look at what comes back. A proximity query returns tuition centres with Al Barsha addresses, agency landing pages listing every district in Dubai, individual tutors advertising a drive radius, and marketplaces sorting profiles by distance. None of those result sets is sorted by the thing a Diploma student needs, which is whether the person teaches the exact course at the exact level. Distance is being used as a proxy for availability, and availability is being used as a proxy for suitability, and by the time you have made both substitutions you are choosing a Higher Level Chemistry tutor on the basis of where they parked.

The arithmetic of the Diploma makes this worse than it sounds. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, from a menu with two mathematics routes, two English routes, five group three subjects commonly offered and five or six group four options. The number of distinct subject-and-level combinations a Dubai school produces across a cohort is large, and the number of students in any one of them at a single Al Barsha school can be in single figures. The teaching population that matches a given combination is correspondingly small, and it is not distributed by neighbourhood.

What the radius does buy is a physical presence, and there is a real case for that in some situations. A younger student who cannot be left alone with a screen, or a student whose difficulty is organisational rather than academic, genuinely benefits from an adult in the room. The Dubai in-home market serves that need and prices it at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE at all, so if that is the requirement, the right answer is a local in-home tutor rather than us.

For a DP1 or DP2 student working towards a May session, the trade almost always runs the other way. Removing the radius widens the pool to everyone who teaches the course, recovers the twenty to thirty minutes an arriving tutor spends on the journey and the doorstep, removes traffic as a cancellation cause, and takes the drive out of the hourly rate. What replaces the radius as a filter is the calendar, and the rest of this page uses it.

sections.heading: The two-year Diploma clock, term by term
paragraphs: The Dubai academic year opens in late August or early September, breaks in mid-December, resumes in January and closes in late June or early July. Laid across two Diploma years that gives six terms, and each one has a job that is different enough from the others that tutoring bought for the wrong term is largely wasted money. The common failure is buying DP2 tutoring in DP1 style, which means weekly content coverage in a year where the marks are being decided by coursework and paper technique.

DP1 term one is the adjustment term. A student arriving from the Middle Years Programme or from IGCSE meets the pace difference in the first fortnight, and the gap is nearly always in the same places: algebraic fluency for both mathematics routes, quantitative handling in the sciences, and the volume of independent reading in group one and group three subjects. Tutoring in this term is cheap in the sense that it is preventative, and it is the term families most often skip.

DP1 terms two and three carry the decisions. Subject and level changes are still possible in most Al Barsha schools during term two, and become progressively harder after that. The internal assessment topic in most subjects can and should be scoped before the summer break, and the Extended Essay subject and research question are usually settled in term three. A student who reaches the summer with a viable research question and an exploration topic that has survived a conversation with the teacher has removed most of the pressure from the following November.

DP2 is three terms with no slack in them. Term one is internal assessment submission and the Extended Essay final draft. Term two opens with mocks and contains the single highest-return eight-week window in the programme. Term three is papers, and new content stops being worth teaching about six weeks out. Any tutoring plan for a DP2 student should be placeable on this grid, and if it cannot be placed, it is not pointed at anything.

sections.heading: DP1 is the year that decides the grade without producing one
paragraphs: No external marks are awarded in DP1 and almost every lever that matters is pulled in it. That is the uncomfortable shape of the first Diploma year, and it is why an Al Barsha family that waits for a bad DP2 report before acting is acting a year late. Three decisions in DP1 set the ceiling: which subjects, which levels, and whether the internal assessment is scoped early or late.

The level decision is the biggest and the least evidenced. Students choose three Higher Level subjects in the final Middle Years Programme year or at the end of Year 11, on the strength of criterion grades or IGCSE results that measure something different from what a Diploma paper measures. A student with a grade 7 at IGCSE Chemistry has demonstrated that they can handle IGCSE Chemistry; Higher Level Chemistry asks for quantitative work at a different density. Most Al Barsha schools allow a level change during DP1 term two, and the window closes after that. Two or three sessions plus a marked Higher Level past paper produces real evidence to take into that conversation.

The second lever is subject-choice repair. A student who has taken Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches because it is thought to be the more prestigious route, and who is drowning in the calculator-free paper, may be better served by Applications and Interpretation, particularly where the intended degree does not require Analysis and Approaches. That conversation has to happen in DP1 and it requires somebody who knows which UAE and overseas university programmes actually specify which route. Guessing at it is expensive in both directions.

The third is coursework scoping, which is the cheapest high-value thing available in the whole Diploma. A chemistry investigation whose data cannot be collected, a mathematical exploration whose mathematics sits below the level of the course, an Extended Essay question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words: all three are visible to a specialist in a twenty-minute conversation and all three are catastrophic if discovered in November of DP2. Scoping them before the DP1 summer break costs a handful of sessions and removes a term of pressure.

sections.heading: The January mock, and the eight weeks that follow it
paragraphs: Al Barsha schools run Diploma mocks in January or February, and the script that comes back is the most useful document a parent receives in two years. It is also the one most consistently misread. A mock grade of four is not a diagnosis; it is a summary statistic that conceals the diagnosis. The diagnosis is in the distribution: which paper, which question numbers, which command terms, which topics, and whether the losses came from not knowing, not finishing or not answering the question asked.

Those three causes need completely different responses and they are distinguishable from the script. A student who lost marks on the last two questions of every paper has a timing problem, and timing is fixed with timed practice rather than content teaching. A student who lost marks scattered across one topic has a content gap, and that is six to eight sessions of teaching. A student who wrote accurate material that did not answer the command term has a technique problem, which is the fastest of the three to fix and the one most often mistaken for a content gap.

The eight weeks after the mock are the highest-return period in the Diploma for a simple reason: the student now knows the format, the content is mostly covered, and there is still enough time for correction to bed in. Earlier in the year there is no diagnostic information; later there is no time. An eight-week block pointed at a named error log, with timed papers from week four and a second timed paper at the end to confirm movement, does more than twelve months of undirected weekly sessions and costs a fraction of it.

What should not happen in that window is new content at pace. By January a DP2 student has seen most of the syllabus, and the marginal value of covering an unfamiliar Higher Level option topic for the first time is low compared with converting partially-known material into marks. The exception is a genuine hole, where a topic was taught during an absence or in a term with a staffing gap, and that shows up clearly in the mock distribution. Everything else is technique.

sections.heading: What the hourly rate inside a five-kilometre radius is actually paying for
paragraphs: A near-me search tends to produce in-home quotes, so it is worth isolating what the difference in price between those and an online specialist consists of. The Dubai in-home one-to-one band is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's rate table putting it at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors are quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards.

Line those up and the in-home premium over a comparable online specialist is somewhere between AED 50 and AED 150 an hour. That is the travel. It buys a car journey, a parking search, and the fifteen minutes of settling that follows an arrival. Over a weekly session for a nine-month school year, the midpoint of that premium is in the region of AED 3,500 to 4,000, which is real money for a service that produces no teaching. It is a legitimate purchase if a physical presence is what the student needs. It is worth knowing that is what the line item is.

At the other end of the market, budget online tutoring runs from AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour put that band at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month against AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-market tutor and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upwards for an exam-year specialist. The premium tier of named or examiner-led tutors reaches AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Three cautions on all of it. These are other providers' published rates read in October 2026 and any of them can change; they are not IB Gram's price list, and we quote ours on request rather than printing a figure that will be stale. A rate tells you nothing about diagnosis quality, which is the actual variable. And beware the examiner premium specifically: unless current examiner status can be evidenced, the word is a marketing term, and examiner status in any case gives no access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, running underneath everything
paragraphs: The core runs on its own clock and collides with every other deadline, which is why it is the part of the Diploma most often left until it is a crisis. Theory of Knowledge requires an exhibition of three objects with a 950-word commentary linking each to a prompt from the published list, and an essay of 1,600 words on one of the prescribed titles. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words in a subject of the student's choosing, assessed across five criteria, with a supervisor assigned by the school. Between them they contribute up to three points through the published matrix, which in practice is the difference between a 34 and a 37.

The scheduling problem is that both are produced in the same months as internal assessment. An Al Barsha DP2 student in October is typically carrying a chemistry investigation, a mathematical exploration, three economics commentaries, a Theory of Knowledge essay draft and an Extended Essay final draft, alongside six taught courses and the KHDA mandatory subjects. Nothing in that list is optional and nothing in it can be done in an evening. The students who come through it comfortably are the ones who scoped the Extended Essay question in DP1 term three and did the bulk of the writing in the summer.

On what a tutor may do here, the boundary needs stating rather than implying. A tutor may teach the subject content the essay rests on, discuss whether a research question is answerable in the word count, explain what each criterion asks for, show the student how to evaluate a source, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite paragraphs into better English, supply data or hand over a model to adapt. The work is submitted as the student's own and a breach is a malpractice finding against the student. There is an open market in completed Internal Assessments in this region, advertised at four-figure AED prices; it is an academic-integrity breach and we will not go near it.

What remains is still the difference between a three-point bonus and a zero. Most Extended Essay underperformance is structural rather than linguistic: a question too broad to answer, sources that do not support the argument, a reflection section written in an hour, a conclusion that restates the introduction. A specialist reading a student's draft identifies all four in one pass, and the student fixes them. That is a legitimate, useful and entirely permissible piece of work.

sections.heading: Where the local tutor pool genuinely runs out
paragraphs: Availability transparency is the gap nobody in this market fills, so here it is plainly. There are Diploma courses where the supply of competent tutors in the UAE is thin enough that a proximity search will return nothing useful, and a provider that does not say so simply sends a generalist. The pattern is consistent: group four options at Higher Level, the less commonly taken group three subjects, Higher Level mathematics Paper 3 specifically, and languages other than English and Arabic.

The reason is cohort arithmetic rather than anything mysterious. A Dubai school might run one Higher Level group in a minority subject every other year. The teachers who have taught it are correspondingly few, and most of them are employed full-time in schools and constrained by permit conditions about which students they may tutor. Abu Dhabi's ADEK ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct similarly bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, which removes the most obvious local candidates from the pool for exactly the students who need them.

Our answer to a gap is to name it. If no specialist in a course is free at the hour an Al Barsha family needs, one of three things is true and you will be told which: another slot works with the right person, there is a date when they free up, or the right person is based outside the UAE and teaches the same course over the same live video at the same Gulf Standard Time hour. That last option is the one most providers conceal, sometimes behind a non-UAE phone number on a UAE page. We would rather state it, because a family that knows where the tutor is sitting can make a decision.

The alternative, which is the industry default, is to put a mathematics teacher in front of a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 problem and let the family work it out in six weeks. That costs more than the honest answer, because the six weeks are not recoverable.

sections.heading: KHDA, the inspection bands, and what they tell a Diploma parent
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a report grading the school on a six-band scale. Every Al Barsha school has one and it is free to read, and it contains more usable information about the teaching your child actually receives than any open day.

The context helps. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK-curriculum schools the largest group by enrolment at 37 per cent, Indian curriculum at 26 per cent, American at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. That last figure explains a lot about a near-me search: the IB is a minority curriculum in Dubai by enrolment, so the local density of IB-experienced teachers is lower than the local density of teachers generally. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK-curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

Reading the report usefully means ignoring the overall band and going to the subject-level judgements, which are broken out. An Outstanding school can have a thin Higher Level Physics department and a Good school can have an exceptional mathematics one, and the band averages those out. Read the attainment and progress judgements by subject, read the commentary on teaching for effective learning, and read the stated areas for improvement. If the same subject appears in that list across three consecutive years, that is structural and your child is not the problem.

A boundary on all of this: IB Gram holds no KHDA, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership, and no individual tutor acquires one by tutoring. The KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument for training institutes with physical premises in Dubai, requiring initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. We hold none of it and do not claim it, and a page that claims its tutors are approved by KHDA should be asked for the permit number.

sections.heading: Booking from Al Barsha: the trial, the plan and the limits
paragraphs: The sequence is short and starts with paper rather than conversation. Send the subject, the level, the school and the deadline, and either a marked mock script or recent internal assessment feedback. That is enough to identify a specialist in the exact course. A trial lesson at no cost follows, at a time that fits the school run from your part of Al Barsha, and afterwards you get a written view of what the next eight weeks should do. Nothing is paid before the trial and nothing is committed after it.

The test to apply during the trial is specific. A good specialist will name the component where marks are going before you tell them, and will say what they would do about it in weeks rather than in adjectives. A tutor who spends the hour establishing rapport and asking what the student finds difficult has produced no diagnosis, and you will be paying for the diagnosis in week four instead. Ask for the error log and the topic sequence in writing before anything is paid.

Scheduling in this district runs to a pattern worth stating. The first workable weekday slot is around 16:15 from Al Barsha 1, 16:30 from Al Barsha 2 and closer to 17:00 from Al Barsha 3 and Al Barsha South where a second school run is in play. Arabic and Islamic Education periods are fixed and homework has not shrunk to accommodate tutoring. Ramadan moves families to post-Iftar sessions and the shortened school day opens a late-morning window. The July and August break is the single most underused stretch in the Diploma: a DP1 student can scope and largely write an internal assessment in it, which removes the heaviest pressure from DP2 term one.

On the enquiry form, because it collects data about a minor: year group, subject, level, school and a parent contact is what we need. Not a photograph, not a full report card, not identity documents. Anything sent for diagnostic purposes is used for that and nothing else, and you can ask for it to be deleted at any time. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the governing framework and the privacy link on this page sets out retention periods and the deletion route.

process.description: A mock, an internal assessment submission or the May papers. A subject and a level with no date produces open-ended weekly lessons, which is the most expensive way to buy tutoring and the least likely to move a grade. The date decides the sequence and the intensity.

process.title: Send the script, not the summary
process.description: A marked mock paper or internal assessment feedback tells a specialist in five minutes what a half-hour conversation cannot. Where nothing marked exists, the tutor sets a short diagnostic inside the trial lesson and builds the plan from that instead.
