process.description: A no-cost lesson with the tutor who would actually teach it, at a time that fits the school run from your part of Al Barsha. Judge it on whether they identified the losing component before you described it, and on whether they can say what eight weeks would change.

process.title: Get the plan in writing against the school calendar
process.description: Which week handles which topic, when timed papers start, what the student does between sessions. If the sequence cannot be laid against the deadline sheet the school sent in September, it is not pointed at anything and should not be bought.

process.title: Confirm movement at week four and week eight
process.description: The error log either shortens or it does not. At week four the right response to no movement is a change of diagnosis or of tutor, not more hours. At week eight a second timed paper settles whether the block worked, which is a question worth answering before buying another.

whyPoints.title: Course and level, not proximity
whyPoints.description: A student with Higher Level Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 in front of them is matched to somebody who teaches that paper, rather than to the best available adult inside a five-kilometre circle. The circle reduces the choice without improving anything.

whyPoints.title: Plans anchored to your school's own calendar
whyPoints.description: Every engagement is placed against the internal deadline sheet, the mock window and the point at which new content stops being worth teaching. That makes the plan auditable at week four, which an indefinite weekly arrangement never is.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: The student writes their own internal assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge work. We teach the content, question the method and comment on their drafts. Nothing is written, rewritten or supplied by the tutor, and the student is told so in the first session.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before you book
whyPoints.description: Where the right specialist is outside the UAE, you are told that before the trial rather than after. Several providers in this market conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking contact route; a family that knows where the tutor sits can make its own decision.

whyPoints.title: Market rates with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider that published it and dated to October 2026. Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family pays in.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Dubai week as it runs
whyPoints.description: Session starts after the school run clears, Arabic and Islamic Education treated as fixed periods, post-Iftar and late-morning slots during Ramadan, and the July window used for coursework rather than sold as revision.

faqs.question: Why does searching for an IB tutor near me in Al Barsha return so few real specialists?
faqs.answer: Because the search filters by distance and the Diploma is a highly subdivided qualification. Six subjects at two levels, two mathematics routes, two English routes and a long list of group three and four options produce a large number of distinct course-and-level combinations, and the teaching population for any one of them is small and not distributed by neighbourhood. Drawing a five-kilometre circle around your villa does not improve the pool; it only cuts it down. The IB is also a minority curriculum in Dubai at around 7 per cent of private enrolment, so local density of IB-experienced teachers is lower than it looks.

faqs.question: Does it matter at all whether the tutor is physically in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For scheduling, yes: Gulf Standard Time has to be the tutor's working hours, not a late-night slot for them. For teaching, no. What matters is whether they teach the course at the level your child sits it, and can read a mark scheme accurately. We will always tell you where a tutor is based before you book, because several providers in this market hide non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking contact route, and a family that knows can decide for itself. What we will not do is use distance as a substitute for subject match.

faqs.question: What should a DP1 student at an Al Barsha school have finished by the winter break?
faqs.answer: No unaddressed gap in algebra or in quantitative science work, because both compound for the next eighteen months. Any Higher Level or Standard Level change should be decided or at least evidenced, since most schools close that window during DP1 term two. And the mathematics route question, Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation, should be settled on the basis of performance on a calculator-free paper rather than on which course sounds more demanding. Internal assessment topics can wait until term three, but they should be scoped before the summer rather than in DP2 September.

faqs.question: How should I read a January mock result rather than just the grade?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the script. Then split the lost marks into three groups: marks lost on the final questions of every paper, which is a timing problem; marks clustered in one or two topics, which is a content gap; and marks lost on accurate material that did not answer the command term, which is technique. The three need different responses and different numbers of sessions, and only the second is fixed by teaching more content. Most students at a five are losing marks they already know how to earn, which is why the eight weeks after a mock are so productive.

faqs.question: What does the travel premium in a Dubai tutoring rate actually buy?
faqs.answer: A car journey and the fifteen minutes of settling that follows an arrival. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 200 to 450 for an online specialist, so the premium is somewhere between AED 50 and AED 150 an hour, with Bestimate putting in-home at AED 180 to 350. Across a weekly session for a school year that is in the region of AED 3,500 to 4,000 for transport. It is a reasonable purchase if a physical presence is what the child needs. It produces no teaching, and these are other providers' figures read in October 2026.

faqs.question: When do Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay deadlines land in a Dubai school year?
faqs.answer: Both run underneath everything else and collide with internal assessment in DP2 term one. The Extended Essay subject and research question are usually settled in DP1 term three, with the final draft due in the autumn of DP2. The Theory of Knowledge exhibition, three objects with a 950-word commentary, and the 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title typically sit in the same window. Exact dates are school-set, so they are on the calendar your school issued in September. The two together carry up to three points through the published matrix.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in this market?
faqs.answer: Group four options at Higher Level, the less commonly taken group three subjects, Higher Level mathematics Paper 3 specifically, and languages other than English and Arabic. The cause is cohort arithmetic: a Dubai school may run a minority Higher Level group once every two years, so few teachers have taught it. Permit conditions narrow it further, since the MoHRE code of conduct and ADEK's ethics rules both bar tutoring students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Where we cannot cover something, we say so rather than substituting a generalist.

faqs.question: What do the KHDA inspection bands mean in practice for a Diploma parent?
faqs.answer: KHDA inspects annually and grades on six bands from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the band is an average that conceals departmental variation. An Outstanding school can run a thin Higher Level Physics department; a Good school can have an exceptional mathematics one. Go to the subject-level attainment and progress judgements, the commentary on teaching for effective learning, and the stated areas for improvement. If the same subject appears in that last list for three years running, it is structural. All of this is published and free to read before you choose Higher Level subjects.

faqs.question: Can a Standard Level student move up to Higher Level during DP1?
faqs.answer: In most Al Barsha schools, yes, during term one and sometimes into term two, after which it becomes impractical because the Higher Level content taught in the interim has to be caught up. The decision should rest on evidence rather than ambition: two or three sessions on genuine Higher Level material followed by a timed Higher Level past paper marked to the scheme produces something a head of department will engage with. The reverse move, down from Higher to Standard, stays available longer but costs a Higher Level slot that may be required for a degree route.

faqs.question: How much free time does an Al Barsha Diploma student realistically have in a week?
faqs.answer: Less than the timetable suggests. Six Diploma courses, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service sit alongside the KHDA mandatory subjects, which are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises a minimum of 25 minutes per lesson, and schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Those periods are real and they are not optional, so an evening tutoring slot competes with homework that has not shrunk.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to look at my child's Extended Essay draft at all?
faqs.answer: Yes. A tutor may teach the subject content the essay rests on, discuss whether the research question can be answered in 4,000 words, explain what each of the five criteria asks for, show the student how to evaluate a source, and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite paragraphs into better prose, supply data or provide a model to adapt. The essay is submitted as the student's own work and a breach is a malpractice finding against them. School-assigned supervision remains the school's responsibility.

faqs.question: My child is predicted a four in a subject a university offer requires. What now?
faqs.answer: Get the mock script and find out which of the three causes applies, because the answer changes the plan entirely. A timing problem at a four is often worth two grades and takes four to six sessions. A content gap in one topic is six to eight. A prediction based on evenly spread weakness across the whole syllabus is a harder conversation and the honest answer may be that the offer needs a backup. Also check whether the prediction is from mock performance or from coursework, because internal assessment marks are already banked and cannot be improved after submission.

faqs.question: Should we tutor the weakest subject or the one closest to a grade boundary?
faqs.answer: Usually the one closest to a boundary, which is counter-intuitive and almost always right. A student two marks below a boundary in one subject and twenty below in another will gain a point faster in the first, and the total is what the university offer is written against. The exception is where the weak subject is a required one for a specific degree, in which case it has to be fixed regardless of efficiency. The mock script tells you where the boundaries sit relative to the marks, which is why the script matters more than the grade.

faqs.question: Do you work with the school or around it?
faqs.answer: With it, as far as the school permits. Tutoring follows your child's own scheme of work and their internal deadline sheet rather than running a parallel syllabus, because a student carrying two different sequences in one subject is being made to do more work for less. Where a school is happy to share the mock script and the internal assessment feedback, that material shapes the plan. Where it is not, we work from what you can send. We do not contact a school directly without a parent asking us to.

faqs.question: What is the no-cost trial lesson actually testing?
faqs.answer: Whether the tutor can diagnose. A full one-to-one lesson with the specialist who would teach the course, working from whatever marked material you send or from a short diagnostic set in the session. Afterwards you get a written view of what eight weeks should cover. The thing to judge is whether they named the component where marks are going before you told them, and whether they described the fix in weeks rather than in adjectives. No payment is taken beforehand and nothing is committed afterwards, so the only cost is the hour.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barsha.closingBody: Proximity is the one variable in Diploma tutoring that does not affect the teaching. Send the subject, the level, the school and the date the work is pointed at, with a marked mock script if there is one, and we will put a specialist in that exact course on a no-cost trial at a time that fits an Al Barsha school run. You will get a written plan laid against your school's own deadline sheet, including an honest account of what the available weeks cannot do. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. Nothing is paid before the trial and nothing is committed after it.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barsha-sout.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach individual IB Diploma subjects at Standard and Higher Level, matched by subject group rather than by programme. Each works to that subject's published command terms and internal assessment criteria. All sessions run online in Gulf Standard Time, so an Al Barsha South evening slot is a real one.

intro.heading: The Diploma is not a subject, and that is the whole problem
paragraphs: Parents in Al Barsha South searching for IB support usually begin with the programme rather than the subject, which is understandable and is the first thing worth undoing. The Diploma is six subjects chosen across six groups, each taken at Standard or Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. Each of those subjects has its own syllabus, its own paper structure, its own internal assessment and its own published command terms. There is no such thing as an IB tutor in the sense a parent initially means.

The arithmetic of the qualification explains why the subject matters so much. Each of the six subjects is graded from one to seven, giving a maximum of forty-two points. Up to three further points come from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay grades, which are awarded from A to E. Forty-five is therefore the maximum, twenty-four is the minimum for the award of the Diploma subject to further conditions, and a failing grade in Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay is itself a condition that can prevent the award. So a student's problem is almost always located in one or two specific places rather than spread across the programme.

That location is what a family should identify before buying anything. A student at twenty-nine points who wants thirty-four is usually losing them in two subjects and one core component, and the work needed in each is different. Higher Level chemistry failing on extended response is a technique problem. Mathematics failing on the exploration is a coursework problem. Theory of Knowledge failing on the essay is an argument-structure problem. One weekly session labelled IB tutoring addresses none of them precisely.

There is a second thing almost no student has had explained to them, and it runs across every subject in the programme. The IB publishes command terms, and they are examinable. State, define and list ask for recall. Describe, outline and summarise ask for an account. Explain, analyse, evaluate, discuss, compare and contrast and justify ask for reasoning, and each one specifies a different kind of reasoning. A student who answers an evaluate question with a description has written something accurate that cannot reach the upper markbands, and that happens across history, biology, economics and English simultaneously.

IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as one-to-one online tuition over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. For a subject-led page the relevance is direct: matching a student to somebody who has taught Higher Level economics, or supervised a historical investigation, or marked a Theory of Knowledge essay, is a search across the whole market rather than across the few square kilometres a car can cover in Al Barsha South at half past six.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barsha-sout.programmesIntro: The three bands below are what an Al Barsha South family is actually choosing between or moving through, described by what each assesses rather than by how hard it is.

programmes.name: The Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard, with Higher Level carrying 240 guided teaching hours and Standard Level 150. Each subject is graded one to seven and carries an internal assessment component completed during the course. Alongside sit Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service, the first two of which together contribute up to three points.
programmes.countryNote: Al Barsha South Diploma sets are small, which affects which subjects and levels actually run in a given year. A school may offer a subject on paper and not run it if the cohort is too small, and a Higher Level option may be delivered partly outside the main timetable. Both are questions for the Diploma coordinator rather than inferences from a prospectus.

programmes.name: The Career-related Programme
programmes.description: An alternative IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills component. It is a different qualification with a different structure, and support for a student on it is not the same purchase as support for a Diploma candidate, even where the subject courses overlap.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubai schools offer this alongside the Diploma. If your child is on it, saying so at the outset prevents a tutor planning against Diploma requirements that do not apply, particularly around the reflective project, which replaces the Extended Essay rather than sitting beside it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme into the Diploma
programmes.description: The IB's preceding programme, assessed against four criteria per subject group rather than by papers. Students arriving at the Diploma from MYP generally bring investigation and reflection skills from the criteria and less procedural drilling than classmates arriving from IGCSE, which makes their first-term gaps almost the mirror image.
programmes.countryNote: Al Barsha South contains an IB continuum school in Dwight School Dubai, so the MYP-to-Diploma route is a genuine local pathway here rather than a theoretical one. A tutor supporting a Year 12 student in this district should establish which feeder route they came through before planning the first term.

programmes.name: IGCSE into the Diploma
programmes.description: The commonest entry route in Dubai, where the UK curriculum accounts for 37 per cent of private enrolment against 7 per cent for the International Baccalaureate. IGCSE builds procedural fluency and single-step recall; the Diploma asks for extended independent work, command-term precision and multi-step reasoning. The gap shows in the first term and in the first internal assessment.
programmes.countryNote: British-pathway schools in Al Barsha and Al Sufouh supply a steady flow of IGCSE students into Diploma sets in this part of Dubai. Four or five bridging sessions in the summer before Year 12, aimed at command terms and extended writing, removes most of the first-term difficulty and almost nobody buys them.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-barsha-sout.subjectsIntro: These are the six groups with the subjects most requested by Al Barsha South families, and what each actually assesses. The internal assessment form is named in each case, because that is the component families most often need help with.

subjects.name: Group 1: Language A, Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessed by written papers plus an individual oral, with an additional essay at Higher Level. Marks are lost in the oral when a student describes a text rather than analysing how it constructs meaning through a global issue, and in the papers when a comparative question receives two separate accounts instead of a comparison.

subjects.name: Group 2: Language B and ab initio
subjects.description: Reading, writing and listening papers plus an individual oral. Students are placed by prior experience rather than by year, and the oral is the component least rehearsed because it cannot easily be practised alone. Text-type conventions carry marks that are straightforward to secure and routinely ignored.

subjects.name: Group 3: History
subjects.description: Source-based and essay papers, with a historical investigation as the internal assessment. The essay command terms do the damage: discuss, evaluate and to what extent each demand a judgement, and a chronological narrative cannot reach the upper markbands however accurate it is. Source reliability work is a trainable, repeatable skill.

subjects.name: Group 3: Economics
subjects.description: Papers combining explanation, diagrams and, at Higher Level, quantitative work, with a portfolio of commentaries as the internal assessment. Diagram accuracy with correctly labelled axes is reliable marks. Evaluation is where strong students cap out, because a judgement is required rather than a list of consequences.

subjects.name: Group 3: Business Management and Psychology
subjects.description: Both carry substantial internal assessment and both reward structured evaluation over recall. Psychology marks go to studies described without their relevance to the argument; business management marks go to tools applied without a conclusion. Each has its own command-term set and its own assessment criteria.

subjects.name: Group 4: Biology, Chemistry and Physics
subjects.description: Papers with multiple-choice, data-analysis and extended-response sections, plus a scientific investigation worth twenty per cent assessed on four criteria of research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth six marks. The data-analysis section is the most neglected and the most trainable part of all three subjects.

subjects.name: Group 5: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Two papers at Standard Level and three at Higher, plus an exploration worth twenty per cent assessed on five criteria for twenty marks in total. Standard Level Paper 1 is sat without technology, which exposes students who learned every method on a screen. Higher Level Paper 3 carries twenty per cent and fails students structurally rather than mathematically.

subjects.name: Group 5: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route with technology assumed throughout, reaching graph theory and voronoi diagrams at Higher Level, and the same twenty per cent exploration. Marks go to calculator output presented without interpretation, and to results stated without saying what they mean in the question's context.

subjects.name: Group 6: Visual Arts, Theatre and Music
subjects.description: Heavily coursework-weighted, with process documentation assessed alongside the work itself. Students who produce strong outcomes and thin process evidence lose marks they have already earned in practice. Deadlines here are school-managed and tend to collide with science and mathematics internal assessments.

subjects.name: The core: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay, service
subjects.description: Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition; the Extended Essay is an independent research piece with a school-appointed supervisor. Both are graded A to E and together contribute up to three points. Creativity, activity and service carries no points and is a completion requirement.

sections.heading: How 45 points is actually built
paragraphs: Before any subject is discussed, the structure of the score is worth laying out, because it tells a family where their child's missing points are. Six subjects each graded one to seven gives a maximum of forty-two. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are each graded A to E, and their combination contributes up to three further points, which is where forty-five comes from. Twenty-four points is the minimum for the award of the Diploma, subject to further conditions, and a failing grade in Theory of Knowledge or in the Extended Essay is itself one of those conditions.

The practical consequence is that points are lumpy rather than smooth. Moving from a five to a six in one subject is one point. Moving the core combination from one point to three is two points, and it comes from two pieces of written work rather than from a two-year course. For a student close to a threshold, those two pieces of writing are frequently the cheapest points available in the whole programme, and they are also the ones most often left to the school alone.

Inside each subject, the points are built from a paper structure plus an internal assessment. The internal assessment is completed during the course, marked by the school and moderated by the IB, and in the sciences and mathematics it carries twenty per cent of the subject grade. That means a fifth of each of those subject grades is decided before any examination is sat, on work that has a school deadline rather than an examination date.

The table below sets out where the points sit. The reason to read it before choosing a tutor is that it turns a vague ambition into a short list. A student who wants three more points has to name where they are coming from, and in almost every case the answer is one subject's extended response, one internal assessment, and the core. Those are three different purchases.

sections.heading: Command terms, which are published and examinable
paragraphs: This is the single highest-leverage piece of teaching available across the Diploma, and most students reach Year 13 without having received it. The IB publishes command terms for each subject, grouped by the kind of thinking they demand, and examiners apply them literally. A question is not asking the student to write about a topic; it is asking for a specific operation on it.

The lowest tier asks for recall: state, define, list, identify, label. These want a short, exact answer, and students lose time writing paragraphs where a line was wanted. The middle tier asks for an account: describe, outline, summarise, annotate. These want content organised but not argued. The upper tier asks for reasoning: explain, analyse, evaluate, discuss, compare and contrast, justify, examine, to what extent. These want a mechanism, a breakdown, a judgement or a comparison, and each is a different operation.

The failure is consistent and it is not a knowledge failure. A student asked to evaluate who describes has written something true that cannot reach the upper markbands. A student asked to compare and contrast who writes two separate accounts has supplied the material for a comparison and not made one. A student asked to explain who states a relationship without giving the mechanism has stopped one step short. In each case the content is correct and the marks are not available.

Because command terms run across every subject, fixing the habit pays several times. A student taking history, biology and economics who learns to recognise what evaluate demands improves in three subjects from the same work. That makes a command-term block one of the few genuinely cross-subject purchases in Diploma tutoring, and at a mid-market rate of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, three or four sessions is AED 450 to AED 1,200 for an effect that is not confined to one subject.

sections.heading: Internal assessment, subject by subject
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internal assessment completed during the course, marked by the school and moderated by the IB, and its deadline is set by the school rather than published anywhere a parent can search. Because the forms differ so much between subjects, a family needs to know what their child's actually is before asking anyone for help with it.

In the sciences it is a scientific investigation worth twenty per cent of the subject grade, assessed on four criteria of research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth six marks for twenty-four in total. In mathematics it is an exploration, also worth twenty per cent, assessed on five criteria for twenty marks, with criterion E on use of mathematics carrying six of them. In history it is a historical investigation. In economics it is a portfolio of commentaries. In Language A there is an individual oral, with a further essay at Higher Level. In the arts the coursework weighting is heavier still.

Two patterns run across all of them and both are worth knowing. The first is that the criterion asking the student to judge their own work, under whatever name, is where marks are most consistently left behind. Evaluation in the sciences, reflection in the mathematics exploration, the evaluative strand in a historical investigation: students write them as apology or as summary rather than as analysis, and the shift is a change of approach rather than new knowledge. The second is that scope decides the ceiling before any work is done, which is why the earliest session on any internal assessment is the most valuable one.

The boundary is identical across every subject and should be stated to the student before work begins. A tutor may discuss candidate topics and say which will not work, question whether a method or an argument holds, ask what the evidence actually supports, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, draft, complete or produce any assessed work, and should not edit it until the voice is no longer the student's. Where a school requires an authenticity declaration, the candidate signs it. One operator in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; buying that places a malpractice exposure on the student rather than on the seller.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level: what the extra hours buy
paragraphs: A Diploma candidate normally takes three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard, and the difference is substantial rather than cosmetic. Higher Level carries 240 guided teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, which is roughly sixty per cent more contact time, and that time goes into additional content, deeper treatment and in some subjects an additional assessment component.

The additional components matter for tutoring because they are where generalist help runs out. Mathematics at Higher Level adds Paper 3, one hour and twenty per cent of the grade, built from two extended problem-solving questions that develop an unfamiliar idea in stages. Language A at Higher Level adds an essay. The sciences extend several themes or units rather than adding separate options. History extends with additional in-depth study. Each of those is a specific piece of teaching, and a tutor comfortable with the shared core may not have taught any of them.

This is also where a level mismatch becomes expensive. A student struggling at Higher Level may have a content problem, a technique problem, or a level problem, and the three have different answers. Where a level change is still possible, which is usually early in Year 12, the honest intervention is a diagnostic session rather than a term of support, because a student coping comfortably at Standard Level is in a better position than one drowning at Higher. Where the level is fixed, the plan has to work within it.

The table below compares the two on the dimensions that change what a family should buy. The practical instruction it leads to is simple: when asking for help, say the level as well as the subject, and ask whether the tutor has taught the Higher Level additional components specifically. Those two sentences remove most of the mismatch risk in Diploma tutoring.

sections.heading: The core, and the points most families ignore
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are graded A to E and together contribute up to three points, which is the difference between thirty-one and thirty-four. For a student near a university threshold that is often the cheapest movement available in the whole Diploma, because it comes from two pieces of writing rather than from two years of a subject. Despite that, the core is the part of the programme families most reliably leave entirely to the school.

Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an essay on a prescribed title and by an exhibition. The essay rewards a sustained argument about knowledge questions with developed counter-positions, and the characteristic failure is a tour of opinions that never commits. Students who are strong essay writers in other subjects often struggle here because the subject matter is unfamiliar and because the essay must be about knowledge rather than about the examples it uses.

The Extended Essay is independent research with a school-appointed supervisor, its own criteria and a word limit. The characteristic failures are a research question too broad to answer within the limit, and a reflective element treated as an afterthought. Scope again decides the ceiling, which is why a conversation before the research begins is worth more than weeks of help afterwards. A student writing an Extended Essay in a subject they also take at Higher Level is carrying two independent pieces of work in that subject at once.

The boundary applies with particular force here, because both pieces are extended writing and the temptation is greatest. A tutor may discuss a prescribed title, interrogate an argument's structure, ask whether a counter-position has been fairly represented, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, draft or complete a Theory of Knowledge essay, an exhibition commentary or an Extended Essay, and must not replace the school-appointed supervisor. The candidate signs the authenticity declaration.

sections.heading: Past-paper work in the Diploma, which is not IGCSE past-paper work
paragraphs: Families arriving from an IGCSE route apply IGCSE habits to Diploma revision and get less from them than they expect. The two qualifications reward different practice, and the difference is worth stating because it changes how a tutoring hour should be spent.

IGCSE past-paper work is largely about coverage and recall under time pressure: a candidate meets many short items, and fluency plus accuracy carries most of the marks. Diploma papers contain extended-response work where the same content can score well or badly depending on how it is argued, and where command terms determine what counts as an answer. Doing more papers therefore helps less than doing fewer papers properly, with somebody reading what the student actually wrote.

The useful regime has three parts. First, whole papers under timed conditions once content coverage is reasonable, because the timing problem in Diploma papers is usually caused by over-writing early extended responses. Second, marking by somebody other than the student, against the published expectations, with the losses categorised by behaviour rather than by topic: described instead of evaluated, mechanism missing, comparison not made, judgement absent, units dropped. Third, a return to an early paper some weeks later to test whether the fix held, which is the only honest evidence available.

Two further points specific to this programme. Internal assessment work is not past-paper work and should not be squeezed into the same sessions; it has its own criteria and its own school deadline, and mixing them means neither gets done. And no past paper, mark scheme, subject guide or grade-boundary table should be supplied to you as a download by a tutoring provider: those belong to the IB, and should be referenced and linked at source. If a provider offers a bundle as a selling point, the right question is where it came from.

sections.heading: What runs locally, and what to verify before paying
paragraphs: Al Barsha South has genuine IB provision, including an IB continuum school in Dwight School Dubai, with further Diploma provision in the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh clusters and inland at Emirates Hills. What a family cannot assume is which subjects and levels actually run in a given year, because Diploma sets in this part of Dubai are small. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 with the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent of enrolment, against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum, so a Diploma set is smaller than a British-curriculum set almost everywhere.

Three questions to the Diploma coordinator settle most of it. Which subjects and levels are confirmed as running for your child's cohort. How any Higher Level additional content is delivered, since in small sets it is often taught outside the main timetable and a tutoring slot must sit outside that rather than compete with it. And when the internal assessment deadlines fall for each subject, since those are school-set and published nowhere a parent can search. All three are free.

Then the standard verification, which applies to any provider. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

And the claims. IB Gram holds no accreditation from the IB, from Cambridge, from Pearson, from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, and claims none; regulators are named on these pages to explain what they govern. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry, and that is a numbered document. Nobody should be described as an IB examiner unless current examiner status can be evidenced, and examiner status should never be presented as access to marking or boundaries. No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because none has been verified from the IB's own published source; confirm every date with your coordinator.

sections.heading: Why a subject-led search is not a local search
paragraphs: Everything above leads to one practical conclusion about the phrase this page is written for. A search for an IB tutor near me in Al Barsha South is a search for proximity, and proximity is the wrong filter once the question has been narrowed to a subject and a level. The right filter is whether this person has taught Higher Level economics, or supervised a historical investigation, or marked a Theory of Knowledge essay against the published descriptors.

The scarcity is structural rather than accidental. The Diploma is a small programme in this emirate, and inside it each subject at each level is a smaller population again. The number of people within a twenty-minute drive of Al Barsha South at half past six who have taught Higher Level Language A and marked the additional essay is not a number worth relying on. Restricting the search geographically does not sample the specialist population evenly; it samples whoever among them happens to live nearby and happens to be free.

IB Gram's delivery position is therefore not a workaround. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one online tuition over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. What that buys an Al Barsha South family is a match on the subject and the level, an evening slot that does not depend on anybody's drive, and a session that survives the twenty to forty minute peak journeys this district generates.

It also suits the work. Reading a student's extended response against the published markbands needs both documents visible at once, annotation that can be undone, and a record afterwards. A shared screen holds the question, the student's own answer and the criteria together, and the session can be recorded so an argument structure is available again in revision week. For an internal assessment draft or a Theory of Knowledge essay, that is a better working surface than a kitchen table, and for a two-year programme it is the format that holds.

faqs.answer: They are published instructions that examiners apply literally, and they specify the operation a question wants. State, define and list ask for a short exact answer. Describe and outline ask for an organised account. Explain wants a mechanism, analyse wants a breakdown, compare and contrast wants one integrated comparison, and evaluate, discuss and to what extent want a supported judgement. faqs.answer: Because students write the judging criterion as apology or as summary rather than as analysis. dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-furjan.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors an Al Furjan family is matched with for Diploma and Middle Years work. What you are paying for is the match on the component your child is assessed on, which is the only variable in this market that reliably changes a grade.

intro.heading: What the word 'near' is costing you
paragraphs: Al Furjan is a villa and townhouse community between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Yalayis Road, with Discovery Gardens to the north and Dubai Investments Park to the south. It is residential rather than academic. The IB Diploma specialists in Dubai cluster around the schools that run the programme, and in this corner of the city those schools are thinner on the ground than they are in Al Barsha, Al Khail or Jumeirah. So the pool of people who will drive here for a 17:00 lesson is genuinely small.

That scarcity has a price, and the market publishes it. Visiting one-to-one tutors in Dubai charge roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel priced in, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is the drive. It is not a quality premium, and in a community like this one it frequently buys the opposite of quality, because the nearest available tutor is being chosen over the right one.

The second cost is harder to see on an invoice. When the pool is small, a Chemistry Higher Level student gets taught by whoever is free, and that is often someone comfortable to Standard Level but not past it. The lessons look fine. The Internal Assessment criteria never get read properly, the Paper 2 extended responses never get marked against a real mark scheme, and a term goes by. That is a far more expensive mistake than an extra AED 150 an hour.

IB Gram runs every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. We say that in the first screen of every page because a family who needs someone physically present should stop reading here rather than find out after a phone call.

What this page does is price the alternatives properly. It covers what the Dubai market charges by provider model, what a two-year Diploma support plan actually totals, where families in this corridor waste money most reliably, how group classes compare on the arithmetic rather than the brochure, and what a free trial should tell you before you commit a fee. Every figure carries its source and the month it was read.

One figure to hold onto before the detail. The MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge. If a tutor adds a licensing or permit cost to your monthly invoice, they are billing you for something with no price, and that tells you more about the arrangement than any rate card. The permit is granted for two years and the ministry lists a two-working-day turnaround, so there is no administrative burden being recovered either. Ask the question once, before the first invoice, and the answer will tell you how carefully the rest of the arrangement has been put together.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-furjan.programmesIntro: Cost behaves differently at each IB stage, because the thing being paid for changes. These are the three programmes Al Furjan families buy support for, and what the money is actually for in each.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units, continuous teacher assessment and no external exam. What a parent buys at this stage is early diagnosis: reading fluency, number fact recall, written structure and the ability to explain a method aloud. Short sessions work better than long ones and twice-weekly beats once-weekly at the same total cost, because retention at this age depends on frequency rather than duration.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Furjan this is the cheapest stage to buy and the one most often skipped. Primary children on Dubai Investments Park routes are home by 15:30, so a forty-minute session at 15:50 costs less than an hour and achieves more. Families with two primary children often run consecutive slots, which keeps the evening to one block and one device rather than two separate disruptions.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criteria A to D in every subject group, each marked on an eight-point scale and converted to a 1-7 grade. The money here buys a criteria diagnosis, because the commonest reason a capable student sits at a 4 is that nobody has shown them what the criterion actually rewards. One session reading a marked task against the strand descriptors frequently finds in forty minutes what a term of general support missed.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years students in Al Furjan are home between 15:40 and 16:30 depending on the route, so a 17:00 slot is the usual fit. This is the stage where spending early is measurably cheaper than spending late: a weekly session in MYP 4 costs a fraction of a Diploma 2 rescue block, and it decides whether Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is realistic in two years' time.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal Assessments carry roughly 20 to 30 per cent of each subject grade. This is where spending concentrates and where it is most often mistimed: money spent in the autumn term of Diploma 2 protects internal marks, while money spent in the spring can only chase exam technique on marks already banked.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Al Furjan travel furthest, usually to the Al Barsha or Al Khail corridor, so they are home late and book 18:00 or 19:00 slots. Two-year planning matters more than hourly rate here: a weekly session across both Diploma years at a mid-market rate costs less in total than one intensive term at specialist rates, and it protects the Internal Assessment marks that an intensive term cannot touch.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, CAS
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is 4,000 words of supervised independent research and the Theory of Knowledge assessment is an exhibition commentary plus an essay from prescribed titles; together they carry the bonus points. Support here is bought in short blocks rather than weekly sessions, typically four to six, and the highest-value session is the earliest one, where the research question gets interrogated before months of work rest on it.
programmes.countryNote: The core is where Al Furjan families most often overpay, by buying help late and at premium rates to rescue a research question that was unanswerable from the start. A single early session on the question costs one hour; rebuilding an essay in the final term costs several and still scores lower. Tutors give feedback on the student's own drafts and never write any part of the submission.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-furjan.subjectsIntro: Price varies by subject in this market because scarcity does. These are the subjects Al Furjan families ask for most, with a note on what makes each one expensive or cheap to support well.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested subject in this corridor, so the easiest to match and the most competitively priced. Higher Level adds Paper 3, worth 20 per cent, where sustained reasoning rather than question recognition earns marks. Money is wasted here on general maths tutors who cannot mark Paper 3 style work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and calculator-led methods. Cheaper to support than Analysis and Approaches because the content is narrower, but the route choice itself has a cost: some engineering courses will not accept it, which is a Diploma 1 decision with a price tag years later.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: One of the scarcer Higher Level specialisms in this part of Dubai, which makes it one of the more expensive to staff in-home and one of the strongest arguments for online matching. Energetics sign conventions, organic mechanisms and the Scientific Investigation are where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty propagation and graph gradient interpretation cost more marks across a cohort than any single topic, and both are fixable in a handful of sessions. That makes Physics unusually good value to support, provided the tutor teaches the current theme structure rather than an older syllabus.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Punishes imprecise language more than weak content: a student who writes that a value increases without naming the mechanism scores nothing. Statistical treatment of data, standard deviation and error bars are reliably under-taught and reliably examined, which makes them cheap marks to recover.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three Internal Assessment commentaries on published news articles plus diagram-led extended response. The commonest waste is paying for content revision when the problem is article choice: a commentary built on an article with no clear economic concept cannot score well however good the writing.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers where command-term discipline decides the grade, and a Higher Level research project needing a real organisation and primary data. The project is where families overspend late, because arranging access to an organisation takes longer than writing about it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the Individual Oral and, at Higher Level, a 1,200 to 1,500 word essay. Marked essay practice is what moves this subject, and it is time-intensive to deliver, so it is priced at the upper end of the mid-market band.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Scarce at Diploma level in the Dubai market, so harder to match and slower to arrange than any science. Dubai private schools must teach Arabic to all pupils under KHDA rules, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and support works from the school's own prescribed material.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word exhibition commentary on three objects and a 1,600-word essay from prescribed titles. Bought in short blocks. The highest-value hour is the first one, spent choosing objects and a title that can actually carry a knowledge argument rather than an opinion.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of supervised independent research. Essays that fail are nearly always answering a question too broad for the word count, and that is diagnosable in one session. Paying for a rescue in the final term is the single most expensive pattern in Diploma support.

subjects.name: Visual Arts and Design Technology
subjects.description: Both are portfolio and process subjects, marked on documented development rather than finished polish. Support is bought in blocks around deadlines. Students who make impressive work without recording iterations score below students who document modest work properly.

modes.description: One sixty-minute session a week in a fixed slot, from September. Spread across a Diploma year this is the lowest total-cost option that actually changes outcomes, because it protects Internal Assessment marks rather than chasing exam technique afterwards. It is also the pattern that makes the hourly rate least important, since fewer hours are needed overall.

sections.heading: The Dubai market priced by provider model, not by adjective
paragraphs: Comparing tutoring quotes is hard because providers describe themselves rather than their model. The useful comparison is structural: an agency with a managed roster, an international marketplace, a freelance tutor found through a community group, a tuition centre running group classes, and an online one-to-one service each have a different cost base and a different failure mode. The rate follows the model, not the quality of the teaching.

At the budget end, published online rates run from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, generally with university-student tutors. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to 300, and Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate's Dubai table, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the examiner end.

Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. That is why the figures above carry a provider name and a reading date of October 2026. A rate without a source is not information, and in this market the absence of a source is usually deliberate.

None of these is an IB Gram rate card. We do not publish one on a landing page, because a price without a subject, a level, a slot and a number of weeks attached is a number that misleads. What we do publish is the free trial: one lesson, no payment, after which there is something concrete to price.

sections.heading: A two-year Diploma support budget, written out in full
paragraphs: Hourly rates hide the only number that matters to a household, which is the total. So here is the arithmetic for a Diploma student from Al Furjan, using the published mid-market online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour. One weekly session in one subject across a thirty-six week school year is thirty-six hours, or roughly AED 5,400 to 10,800 a year. Across both Diploma years in one subject, that is AED 10,800 to 21,600.

Most families do not buy one subject for two years. The common pattern in this corridor is a weekly session in the hardest Higher Level subject through Diploma 1, two subjects through Diploma 2, and a short block on the Extended Essay or an Internal Assessment. That totals somewhere between sixty and a hundred hours over two years, and at mid-market rates it lands between AED 9,000 and AED 30,000 depending on rate and intensity.

Compare that with the alternative pattern, which is doing nothing until the spring of Diploma 2 and then buying an intensive block at specialist rates. Twenty hours in six weeks at AED 300 to 450 is AED 6,000 to 9,000 for a package that cannot touch Internal Assessment marks, because those are already submitted. The spend is lower and the ceiling is lower with it. That is the single most important cost fact on this page.

Context helps as well. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. A family planning tutoring is therefore working against a stable fee base this year, which makes a planned weekly commitment easier to carry than an unplanned emergency one.

sections.heading: Where families in this corridor waste tutoring money
paragraphs: The first and largest waste is paying a specialist rate for homework supervision. A tutor at AED 250 an hour sitting beside a student who is working steadily through set questions is an expensive invigilator. If what the household needs is someone to make sure the work happens, that is a different and much cheaper service, and conflating the two is how a monthly invoice doubles without a grade moving.

The second is session length chosen for the invoice rather than the child. Ninety-minute sessions are common because they feel substantial, but a Middle Years student concentrating hard for fifty minutes is doing nothing useful for the last forty. Two forty-five minute sessions at the same total cost retain more and let the tutor check set work. Families buy the long session because it looks like better value per booking.

The third is timing, and it is the one unique to the Diploma. Internal Assessments carry roughly 20 to 30 per cent of each subject grade and are submitted months before the exams. Money spent after those submissions cannot reach those marks. A family spending nothing until March is buying from a smaller menu at a higher price, and the Al Furjan pattern of discovering this in Diploma 2 is common enough to be predictable.

The fourth is the proximity premium itself, which brings this page back to its first point. Paying AED 150 extra an hour for a tutor who can reach the villa districts by 17:00 is paying for a drive. In a community with a small local pool of Diploma specialists, that premium frequently buys a less well-matched tutor than the same money spent online. Convenience is a real benefit; it is simply not an academic one.

sections.heading: Group classes against one-to-one, on arithmetic rather than brochure
paragraphs: Group classes are genuinely cheaper per hour and sometimes the right purchase. A tuition centre running a Diploma Standard Level group of six can price well below any one-to-one rate, and for a student who is broadly on track and wants structured revision alongside peers, that is a sensible use of money. The question is what gets lost, and the answer is diagnosis.

In a group, the pace is set by the group and the content is set in advance. A student whose Paper 2 marks are falling because of command-term errors in extended response will sit through a syllabus review that does not address it. One-to-one, that is the whole of the first session. The cheaper per-hour option is more expensive per grade moved when the problem is specific rather than general.

The honest split looks like this. Group classes suit broad revision, motivation and structure. One-to-one suits a diagnosed gap, Internal Assessment work, Higher Level depth and any case where the student's errors have a pattern nobody has named yet. Many families in this corridor use both: a group revision course in the holidays and a weekly one-to-one session on the one subject that is not moving.

A note on small-group pricing in the market. Small groups of two to four are sometimes offered at a lower per-student rate than one-to-one, and that is a real saving when the two students are at the same level in the same subject with the same gaps. When they are not, one of the two is paying to watch the other get taught.

sections.heading: The permit question that changes what is on your invoice
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the terms are worth knowing precisely because they affect what a tutor can legitimately charge you for. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The ministry's own service page for it is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. So there is no permit fee to pass on to a parent, in any amount, in any form.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so this page quotes no amount; a figure circulating online could not be verified against a ministry source. For a parent the useful action is a single question asked before the first invoice: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit?

There is one related rule that closes off an arrangement many families consider. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Hiring your child's own class teacher privately is the one option the rules specifically exclude.

sections.heading: What a free trial lesson should tell you before any money moves
paragraphs: A trial lesson that functions as a sales call is worth nothing, and most of this market treats it as one. A trial worth taking does three things: it puts your child's own marked work on the screen, it produces a specific statement about where the marks went, and it gives you a plan with a number of sessions attached. If you finish the call without those three, the tutor has not been tested.

The test question is narrow. Hand over a marked Paper 2 or a returned Internal Assessment draft and ask the tutor what pattern connects the lost marks. A specialist answers at the level of the component: the extended responses are describing rather than evaluating, or the uncertainty treatment is missing throughout, or the criterion D reflection strand is unaddressed. A generalist answers at the level of the topic, which sounds reasonable and tells you nothing.

The second thing to check is honesty about scope. A tutor who says that eight weeks is enough for exam technique but cannot recover submitted internal marks is telling you the truth. A tutor who implies that everything is recoverable in any timeframe is selling. In a market where some providers sell completed Internal Assessments outright, a frank statement of limits is a useful signal about everything else.

IB Gram runs the trial free and takes no payment for it, with no obligation afterwards. If the match is wrong, say so and we will try one more tutor or stop. The families in Al Furjan who get the most from this treat the trial as an interview with a prepared question, which takes ten minutes to think about and saves a term.

sections.heading: What the money cannot buy: coursework, and why that protects you
paragraphs: There is a part of this market where money buys something a family should not purchase. At least one UAE provider advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. The transaction looks like a shortcut and is in fact a transfer of risk: the IB treats submitted work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the exposure falls on the student and their Diploma, not on the seller's revenue.

What a tutor can legitimately be paid for is wider than parents often assume. A tutor can read the assessment criteria with the student and explain what each strand rewards, interrogate a research question or hypothesis until it is answerable, teach the statistical or practical technique the work requires, model how a published study structures its analysis, and give written feedback on the student's own draft against each criterion. That is teaching, and most of the recoverable marks sit there.

What a tutor cannot be paid for is writing, rewriting, drafting, outlining for the student to complete, or supplying content that then appears in a submission. IB Gram tutors state that boundary at the first session of any Internal Assessment or Extended Essay block and give their feedback in writing, so that a school asking what support was received gets an answer that holds up to scrutiny.

The same rule covers materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We cite and link the official sources and work from what the school has issued. That is a copyright matter for published material and a malpractice exposure for anything unreleased, and neither is worth risking to save a download.

sections.heading: Availability, and the price of asking in January
paragraphs: Scarcity moves price in tutoring as in anything else, and the Dubai calendar makes scarcity predictable. In September, specialists in most Diploma subjects have space and a family in Al Furjan can have a choice of tutor and slot. In January and February, when every Diploma 2 household in the city is looking for the same Higher Level subjects in the same evening window, the choice narrows to whoever is free and the rate reflects it.

Subject matters too. Mathematics and the three sciences at Middle Years and Standard Level are usually matched within a few days. Arabic B, Design Technology, Music and the smaller Higher Level options take longer at any time of year, and in the peak weeks they may not be available at all. That is a real limit and this page states it rather than implying a bottomless roster.

When the specialist for your subject and slot is not free, you get one of three answers: a different time with the right tutor, a short wait with a date attached, or a straight recommendation to look elsewhere. We do not place a tutor one level below the one your child sits and let the family discover the difference over a term. In Higher Level subjects it becomes obvious in about two sessions anyway.

The practical consequence for budgeting is simple. Booking early costs less for the same outcome, because you are buying from a wider pool in a quieter month and spreading the hours across a year instead of compressing them into six weeks. Nothing on this page saves a family more money than that single decision about timing.
