process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the budget shape
process.description: Not just Chemistry, but Chemistry Higher Level, Diploma 2, Internal Assessment due in February, and whether you are looking at a weekly session or a defined block. Knowing the budget shape lets us say honestly whether what you want is achievable in those hours rather than discovering it in month three.

process.title: We match a specialist and name them
process.description: You are told who the tutor is and which components they have taught before any session is booked. For an Al Furjan family the match is made on availability in UAE evening hours rather than on who lives nearby, which is the whole point of delivering online.

process.title: Free trial with marked work on the screen
process.description: Bring a marked paper or a returned draft and ask what pattern connects the lost marks. Forty to sixty minutes is enough to judge the answer. No payment is taken, and if the match is wrong you say so and we try once more or stop. That is the cheapest hour in this process.

process.title: Agree the pattern and the number of sessions
process.description: Weekly through a term, or a defined block of four to six attached to one deadline. The total is agreed in advance either way, so the commitment is a known number rather than a rolling monthly charge that nobody reviews until the term ends.

process.title: Written session notes you can audit
process.description: A short note after every lesson naming what was covered, what was set and what to practise. Over a term it is the record of what the money bought, and for internal work it is the evidence that the support given was teaching and feedback rather than anything else.

process.title: Review against the deadline calendar
process.description: Every few weeks we check progress against the school's internal deadlines rather than against hours delivered. Before a mock window that usually means two shorter sessions a week; afterwards it goes back to one. Hours follow the calendar instead of accumulating by habit.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries a source
whyPoints.description: Each AED rate on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Three of the most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote US dollars, which is not what a Dubai family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium in the rate
whyPoints.description: Nobody drives to Al Furjan, so nobody prices a drive into your invoice. What that removes is the AED 100 to 200 an hour gap between the published online and in-home bands, and what it adds is a tutor chosen from everyone free in UAE evening hours.

whyPoints.title: A known total, not a rolling charge
whyPoints.description: Sessions are agreed as a weekly slot for a term or a defined block with an end date. You know the number before it starts. Open-ended monthly arrangements are how tutoring spend grows without anyone deciding that it should.

whyPoints.title: The free trial is genuinely free
whyPoints.description: One lesson with your child's own work on screen, no payment taken, no obligation afterwards. If the match is wrong, say so. The condition is stated here rather than discovered later, because free with conditions attached is the oldest trick in this market.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what spending late cannot buy
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessments carry roughly 20 to 30 per cent of a subject grade and are submitted before the exams. Money spent afterwards cannot reach those marks. A provider who tells you otherwise is selling, and that is worth knowing before you choose one.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated before any payment
whyPoints.description: No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is India-only. There is no IB Gram office in the UAE. If no specialist is free for your subject and slot, we say so rather than substituting one and hoping.

faqs.question: In Al Furjan, how much more does a tutor who comes to the villa cost?
faqs.answer: Roughly AED 100 to 200 an hour more, and the gap is travel rather than teaching. Published Dubai rates put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. From Al Furjan the drive from the Al Barsha and Jumeirah tutor clusters is long in evening traffic, which pushes quotes to the upper end. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Is there any IB tutor actually based in Al Furjan itself?
faqs.answer: Al Furjan is residential rather than academic, and Dubai's IB Diploma specialists cluster near the schools that run the programme, which in this corner of the city are fewer than in Al Barsha, Al Khail or Jumeirah. So the genuinely local pool for a specific Higher Level subject is small. That matters more than it sounds: choosing from a small pool means taking the available tutor rather than the right one. Online delivery replaces the map with a calendar, which is a much larger space to choose from.

faqs.question: What does a full two-year IB Diploma support plan cost from this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Using the published mid-market online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, one weekly session in one subject across a thirty-six week year is about AED 5,400 to 10,800. The common pattern here, one subject through Diploma 1, two through Diploma 2 and a short core block, runs sixty to a hundred hours over two years, landing somewhere between AED 9,000 and AED 30,000. A spring-only intensive of twenty hours at specialist rates costs AED 6,000 to 9,000 and cannot reach submitted internal marks.

faqs.question: Which is the single biggest waste of money in Dubai tutoring?
faqs.answer: Paying a specialist rate for homework supervision. A tutor at AED 250 an hour sitting beside a student working steadily through set questions is an expensive invigilator, and the grade does not move because nothing is being taught. If the household needs someone to make sure work happens, that is a cheaper and different service. The second biggest is buying ninety-minute sessions for a child who concentrates for fifty; two forty-five minute sessions at the same weekly cost retain more and let the tutor check set work.

faqs.question: Do group revision courses make sense alongside one-to-one for an Al Furjan student?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and many families here use both. Group courses price well below any one-to-one rate and give structure, pace and peer motivation, which suits broad revision for a student who is roughly on track. What they cannot do is diagnose: a student losing Paper 2 marks to command-term errors will sit through a syllabus review that never addresses it. The sensible split is a group course in the holidays plus a weekly one-to-one session on the one subject that is not moving.

faqs.question: Can a tutor charge me for their UAE licence or permit?
faqs.answer: No, because it has no price. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time. If a permit or licensing line appears on your invoice, you are being charged for an item with no cost, which is worth asking about directly.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time of year to book an IB tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: September, and the saving is both in rate and in choice. Early in the year specialists in most Diploma subjects have space, so an Al Furjan family can choose the tutor and the slot. By January and February every Diploma 2 household in the city is after the same Higher Level subjects in the same evening window, and the choice narrows to whoever is free. Booking early also spreads the hours across a year instead of compressing them into six weeks, which lowers the total spend for a better result.

faqs.question: Why can money spent in March not fix an IB grade?
faqs.answer: Because a large part of the grade has already been submitted. Internal Assessments carry roughly 20 to 30 per cent of each subject grade and are completed and uploaded months before the papers are sat, along with the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. Tutoring bought after those deadlines can only work on exam technique for the remaining marks. That is useful and often worth doing, but it is a smaller ceiling, and any provider implying otherwise is selling rather than advising.

faqs.question: What should I bring to a trial lesson to judge whether a tutor is worth the rate?
faqs.answer: A marked paper or a returned Internal Assessment draft, and one question: what pattern connects the lost marks? A specialist answers at component level, naming extended responses that describe rather than evaluate, or missing uncertainty treatment throughout, or an unaddressed reflection strand. A generalist answers at topic level, which sounds reasonable and tells you nothing. Also listen for honesty about scope: a tutor who says eight weeks can fix technique but not submitted internal marks is telling you the truth.

faqs.question: Are small-group sessions of two or three students better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: They are when the students genuinely match: same subject, same level, same gaps. Then the lower per-student rate is a real saving and the shared practice helps. They are poor value when the levels or the weaknesses differ, because one student spends the hour watching the other get taught at a rate that is only slightly below one-to-one. Before agreeing to a pairing, ask what the other student's current grade and specific difficulty are. If the answer is vague, decline it.

faqs.question: Does the AED rate I am quoted in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, in writing, before the first invoice. We do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees on this page because doing so would need a Federal Tax Authority citation we are not going to paraphrase from memory. What a parent can reasonably require from any provider is a clear statement of whether the quoted figure is the amount payable or the amount before tax, and a tax registration number if one is held. A provider who will not put that in writing has told you something useful.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects cost the most to support properly in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The scarce ones rather than the hard ones. Arabic B at Diploma level, Design Technology, Music and the smaller Higher Level options are harder to staff anywhere in the city, so they are slower to match and priced at the upper end. Chemistry Higher Level is scarcer in this corridor than Mathematics, which is why online matching matters more for it. Mathematics and the three sciences at Standard Level are the most competitively priced, simply because supply is widest.

faqs.question: Can both of my children share one session to halve the cost?
faqs.answer: Not usefully, unless they are in the same subject at the same level with the same gaps, which siblings rarely are. A Year 8 Middle Years student and a Diploma 2 student need different specialists and different content, and a shared hour shortchanges both. What does work is consecutive slots with separate tutors, which keeps the evening to one block and one device. It is an evening-management saving rather than a financial one, and we would not pretend otherwise.

faqs.question: Why do so many Dubai tutoring sites refuse to publish a price?
faqs.answer: Because a quote is easier to defend in a conversation than on a page. Of the most visible competitor pages in this market, three publish no AED figure at all and two quote in US dollars, a currency Dubai families do not transact in. One even asks the price question in its own list of frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it. This page takes the other approach and publishes the market bands with the provider and the reading date attached, while keeping our own quote to a conversation after the free trial.

faqs.question: What exactly cannot be bought, however much a family is willing to pay?
faqs.answer: A completed Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project. At least one UAE provider advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; the risk in that transaction sits entirely with the student, because the IB treats submitted work that is not the student's own as malpractice. IB Gram tutors teach technique, question a research question, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not write, rewrite or supply submitted content, and that boundary is stated at the first session.

faqs.question: Is a tutor at AED 650 an hour ever worth it for a student in this corridor?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and almost never before the final two terms. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the examiner-experienced end of the Dubai market. That depth has a use: a Higher Level student already scoring well who needs component-level marking insight to move the last few marks. For a student with a diagnosed content or method gap, the same money buys three times as many hours at the published AED 150 to 300 mid-market band, and hours are what closes a gap. We also do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence of current status.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-furjan.closingHeading: Price the alternatives before you pay for proximity
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-furjan.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB tutor near me in Al Furjan, the figures on this page should let you judge any quote you receive. Published Dubai in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included; a qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300. The gap is a drive, not a grade. Tell us the subject, the level and the earliest time your child is realistically at the desk, and we will match a specialist in that component and run a free trial with your child's own marked work on screen. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and nothing is paid until you have judged the match yourself.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-garhoud.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here are matched by IB subject and level. We quote after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a flat hourly figure, because a term of Mathematics SL and a final year of Chemistry HL are different commitments and should not carry the same number.

intro.heading: The money question nobody in this search answers
paragraphs: Three of the six pages currently ranking for Dubai IB tutoring queries publish no price at all. One of them has an FAQ that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. The two that do publish a figure quote United States dollars, which is not the currency an Al Garhoud household transacts in. So the first useful thing this page can do is put the dirham numbers on the screen, with the name of whoever published each one, and let a parent work out what a fair quote looks like.

The second useful thing is to separate price from cost. An hour at AED 60 that produces completed homework and no change in a predicted grade is more expensive than an hour at AED 250 that identifies why a student loses four marks on every data-analysis question. Families in Garhoud, where households tend to be settled and budget-conscious rather than extravagant, usually arrive at this conclusion the slow way: two terms of cheap tutoring, no movement, then a specialist. The point of publishing the bands is to let you skip the first two terms.

The third is scale. The IB Diploma is a two-year commitment in six subjects. A family who books weekly tutoring in two subjects from the start of Year 12 to the examination session is committing to roughly seventy weeks of sessions, and that is a real number that should be written down before the first one is booked. Most families do not need that. Most need one subject for one term, then a different subject the following year, plus a short block around the internal assessments. Knowing the shape of the full commitment is what lets you buy the part of it that matters.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. This matters on a cost page more than anywhere else, because the in-home premium is the single largest avoidable line in a Dubai tutoring budget. Compare two advertised packages and the arithmetic is plain: online blocks appear at roughly AED 799 a month for eight sessions, while in-home monthly packages of four two-hour sessions appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Same contact hours, roughly double the money, and the difference is a car crossing Al Garhoud Bridge.

What follows is a budget, not a brochure. There is a provider-model comparison that compares models rather than naming competitors unfairly. There is a two-year Diploma cost table. There is a list of the six ways money gets wasted, which is the section most worth reading twice. There is the cost of tutoring set against Dubai school fees and the KHDA fee freeze. And there is a plain account of what you are entitled to ask before paying anybody, including whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition permit, which is free and therefore has no excuse for being absent.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-garhoud.programmesIntro: Cost varies by programme more than families expect, because what is being bought changes. A PYP hour buys skills practice, an MYP hour buys criterion literacy, and a Diploma hour buys mark-scheme diagnosis, which is the scarcest and therefore the dearest of the three.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led with no examinations and no subject marks. Tutoring requests here are almost always reading fluency, number facts or written output, and they respond to short frequent sessions rather than long ones. This is the one band where a budget-tier tutor can be genuinely good value, because the skill being taught is not assessment-specific.
programmes.countryNote: Primary-age children from Al Garhoud attend schools spread across Oud Metha, Festival City and Al Qusais rather than one local school. Three thirty-minute sessions a week at the budget band often costs less than one specialist hour and does more for a seven-year-old's reading.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each marked against four criteria out of 8 for a total of 32, converted to a 1-7 grade. The Personal Project falls in MYP 5. The money here is best spent on one criterion at a time, because a criterion can be moved in six to eight weeks whereas a subject grade cannot.
programmes.countryNote: The mid-band of the Dubai market, around AED 150 to 300 an hour, is usually the right band for MYP work, provided the tutor has actually marked against MYP descriptors. Paying specialist rates for MYP content teaching is rarely necessary; paying budget rates for criterion work rarely achieves anything.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and CAS. Most assessment is external and concentrated in one session. HL carries extra content, extra teaching hours and in several subjects an extra paper, so an HL hour is harder to supply and priced accordingly.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the Dubai specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above becomes justified, and where the premium band above AED 500 starts appearing. A Garhoud family should expect to pay mid-band for SL support and specialist band for HL sciences, mathematics and the Group 3 subjects where local supply is thinnest.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-garhoud.subjectsIntro: Not every IB subject costs the same to support, because supply differs. These are the subjects Garhoud families ask about, with a note on what the hour is being spent on in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic and proof-heavy, with HL adding substantial content and a further paper. HL hours go on multi-step reasoning and on the exploration; SL hours go on method marks and calculator technique. HL supply is thinner than SL, which is visible in the rate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics-led with heavier technology use. Cheaper to support than Analysis and Approaches at the same level simply because more tutors can teach it credibly. The route decision should still be made against named university requirements rather than cost.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The hour is spent on application rather than recall: interpreting unfamiliar data, handling energetics and equilibrium, and narrowing an internal assessment question until it generates usable quantitative data. HL requests sit firmly in the specialist band.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity first, fields and quantum later. Most of the money goes on written explanation quality, because students who can calculate often cannot connect cause to effect in the order a mark scheme rewards.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty. Sessions are best spent on command-term discipline and data-based questions, both of which are cheap to teach and expensive to leave untaught. A mid-band tutor is often sufficient at SL.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram precision is the mark scheme, and the internal assessment commentaries need real news articles applied to named theory. Local supply in Dubai is thinner than for the sciences, so quotes run higher for the same level of experience.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frameworks applied to real organisations, with HL adding further content. The hour is spent teaching judgement rather than content, because the marks sit in the evaluation. Research access for the internal assessment needs planning early.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis of literary and non-literary texts, an individual oral, and a written component. A repeatable analytical paragraph structure is the cheapest high-return intervention in the Diploma, and it does not require a premium-band tutor.

subjects.name: History and Psychology
subjects.description: Essay structure, source evaluation and a word-limited internal investigation. These are the hardest Diploma subjects to staff in Dubai, which means longer waits and firmer rates. Budget accordingly if your child takes either at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Supervised in school, assessed externally. Paid support here is process coaching: question design, research method, referencing, timeline discipline. It is usually a short block rather than a weekly commitment, and anyone offering to produce the work should be refused.

regions.note: Villas and compounds around the golf club and the airport road, with Al Mawakeb School Al Garhoud inside the area. Short internal journeys, but any tutor coming from the Jumeirah or Marina side is pricing in a long drive.

regions.name: Oud Metha and Al Jaddaf

regions.note: Dense eastern school district with a large supply of tuition centres and group classes, which is where the lowest advertised group rates in this part of Dubai tend to come from.

regions.note: Older districts with difficult parking, where in-home visits take longer than the map suggests. Online uptake here has been faster than in the newer villa communities for exactly that reason.

sections.heading: The dirham bands, and who published each one
paragraphs: Here is the market, in dirhams, with sources. At the budget end Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both online and generally delivered by generalists or university students. The qualified-subject-tutor band online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table giving the 200 to 450 plus range. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 for named or examiner-level tutors.

In-home visiting rates cut across those bands because they carry travel. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 for a weekly one-hour session at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Advertised packages show the same shape: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those are market figures read in October 2026 and attributed to the publisher in each case. They are not IB Gram's prices and should not be read as ours. We quote after a free trial lesson, one per subject before any payment, against a written plan, because the honest price for a term of Mathematics SL is not the honest price for a final year of Chemistry HL and a single advertised hourly rate hides that difference rather than resolving it.

Use the table as a screening tool. A quote materially above the specialist band should come with a specific justification — a named level, a demonstrable specialism, a scarce subject. A quote materially below the qualified band for Higher Level work should prompt a question about what exactly is being supplied.

sections.heading: A two-year Diploma support budget, written out
paragraphs: Nobody in this market writes the full number down, so here it is. Treat the table below as a planning model using the published bands above, not as a quote. The purpose is to let a Garhoud family see which lines are large and which are small, and therefore where to spend and where to decline.

Two observations fall out of it immediately. First, the weekly-session lines dominate everything else, which means the decision that controls your total spend is how many subjects you support weekly and for how long — not the hourly rate you negotiate. Dropping from two weekly subjects to one halves the largest line in the budget. Second, the internal assessment and Extended Essay blocks are small, high-leverage lines: a handful of sessions at the right moment, early, is cheap and prevents the expensive rescue work later.

Set against this, Dubai school fees are the larger number in any case. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion out of AED 2.5 billion in total. That freeze is the right anchor for a conversation about tutoring: the school fee is fixed for the year, so the discretionary education line in a Garhoud household budget is the tutoring one, and it is worth planning rather than drifting into.

Examination entry costs are deliberately left blank in the table. Entry fees are set and collected by the school as a registration centre and vary; private-candidate arrangements vary more. Ask your school's examinations officer for the actual figure rather than taking one from any website.

sections.heading: Six ways Garhoud families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: This is the section worth reading twice, because every item on it is something we see monthly and every one is avoidable without spending more. None of them are about choosing the wrong provider. They are about buying the wrong thing.

The first is buying hours before a diagnosis. A family books ten sessions, the tutor spends the first three working out what is wrong, and the diagnosis is paid for at teaching rates. A short diagnostic block first costs less and tells you whether the ten sessions are needed at all. The second is paying specialist rates for homework supervision. If what a student needs is somebody sitting with them while they work, the budget band at AED 33 to 65 does that perfectly and a specialist at AED 300 is being wasted on it. The third is the reverse error: paying budget rates for Higher Level paper technique, which requires mark-scheme literacy that the budget band generally does not have.

The fourth is the in-home premium paid out of habit. Roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour, every session, for proximity that does not affect how well a subject is taught. The fifth is three subjects at once, where a student's week cannot absorb three sessions plus school plus coursework, so all three are half-attended and none of them moves. The sixth is late internal assessment help, which is the most expensive mistake available: four sessions in the term the assessment is set costs a fraction of the rescue work required when a research question that could never have scored well is discovered six weeks before submission.

A seventh, less common but worth naming: paying for a tutor who will not be named until after payment. If an agency cannot tell you who will teach your child and what level they have taught, you are buying an option rather than a service.

sections.heading: Provider models compared on the things that cost you money
paragraphs: Every provider in this market compares itself to an unnamed set of other platforms, which tells a parent nothing. A more useful comparison is between models, because the model determines the cost structure and the cost structure determines what you can and cannot expect.

An agency carries overhead and a vetting process, prices in the mid to specialist band, and usually offers a replacement if a match fails. An international marketplace is cheaper because it does no matching, which transfers the vetting work and the risk to you. A freelance independent tutor is often the best value per hour and the least resilient: no replacement, no cover for illness, and no recourse if the fit is wrong. A tuition centre group class is the genuine low-cost option and is frequently dismissed unfairly, since a small group at a fraction of one-to-one rates is better value than a cheap one-to-one hour with a generalist. School-run support is usually free and under-used.

On the lines in the table, two columns matter most and are almost never published. The first is whether the provider can confirm the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge for two years and therefore has no excuse for being absent. The second is what happens when a match fails: a replacement at no extra cost, a refund, or nothing. Ask both questions before paying and the answers will separate providers more sharply than the hourly rate does.
IB Gram's own row is in the table for honesty: online only, mid to specialist band, free trial first, replacement if the fit is wrong, and no UAE in-home service at all.

sections.heading: What a cheap hour buys and what an expensive one buys
paragraphs: The difference is not enthusiasm or qualifications on paper. It is whether the tutor can look at a marked script and say, in mark-scheme language, exactly which behaviour cost the marks. That single capability is what separates the AED 60 hour from the AED 300 hour, and it is testable in ten minutes without understanding the subject yourself.

Ask any candidate to mark one page of your child's most recent written work out loud, saying what each annotation is worth and why. A specialist does this comfortably, names command terms, and finishes by telling you the one behaviour to change. A generalist corrects spelling, says the work looks good, and suggests more practice. The second person may be perfectly pleasant and genuinely helpful for homework supervision. They cannot move a Higher Level grade, and paying them specialist rates to try is the error the previous section describes.

There is also a middle case worth naming. A strong graduate who has read the syllabus carefully can teach Standard Level content well and is good value in the AED 150 to 300 band. What they generally cannot do is supervise an internal assessment or diagnose why a student plateaus at a 5, because both require having marked against the criteria. For those two jobs, buy the specialist hour and buy fewer of them.

The practical rule we would give a Garhoud parent: match the band to the job rather than to the subject. Homework supervision at the budget band, Standard Level content at the mid band, Higher Level diagnosis and internal assessment work at the specialist band, and nothing at all at the premium band unless a specific scarcity justifies it.

sections.heading: HL and SL: where the extra hours and the extra money actually go
paragraphs: Higher Level is not Standard Level taught faster. It is a longer syllabus with additional content, more teaching hours, and in several subjects an extra examination paper, and that is why an HL hour is both scarcer and dearer. A family budgeting for Diploma support should know which of their child's three HL subjects is likely to need paid help, because supporting all three weekly is the most expensive plan available and almost never the right one.

The decision usually resolves itself on two tests. First, which HL subject does the student need for their intended university course, and therefore which grade actually carries consequences. Second, which HL subject shows the largest gap between current attainment and the required grade. Spend on the intersection of those two and leave the third alone unless it is failing.

Internal assessment weighting is the other budget lever. Every Diploma subject carries internally assessed coursework, and the weighting means a few well-spent sessions early can protect a meaningful share of the final grade. This is the cheapest high-value purchase in the whole Diploma and the one most often left until it is expensive. Book it in the term the assessment is set, not the term it is due.

The table sets out the comparison families actually need: not a content list, but where the hours go and what that implies for the budget. One further point of arithmetic is worth making. Because Higher Level carries materially more timetabled teaching at school, a gap in an HL subject is usually a gap in depth rather than coverage, and depth gaps take longer to close than missing topics do. That is the real reason an HL plan runs for a term rather than a fortnight, and why a family should budget in terms rather than in hours.

sections.heading: Paying for internal assessment and Extended Essay support legitimately
paragraphs: At least one site competing for this search sells completed Internal Assessments outright. It is worth understanding the economics of that transaction from the buyer's side: the fee is paid once, the malpractice risk sits permanently with the student, and the possible outcome is the loss of the Diploma. The seller carries none of it. No price makes that a good purchase.

Legitimate paid support is narrower and considerably cheaper, because it is a handful of sessions rather than a produced document. A tutor may teach the content the assessment rests on, help narrow a research question until it is answerable with available data, explain the assessment criteria and mark a completed draft against them, teach referencing, challenge a method, and enforce a timeline. For the Extended Essay the most valuable thing a paid hour buys is scheduling discipline, because most Extended Essays fail on timeline rather than ability.

A tutor may not write, draft or edit any part of the submission to completion, supply data the student did not collect, or dictate sentences for transcription. The test is whether the student can explain, unprompted, why each sentence and each decision is in the work. If a provider offers more than this, the extra is not a service you are buying; it is a risk you are being sold.

For budgeting purposes: four sessions per internal assessment, booked in the term the task is set, and four to six sessions of Extended Essay process coaching spread across the year. Those are small lines that prevent large ones.

sections.heading: What you are entitled to ask before any payment
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work rather than informal work, and the permit is free, so there is nothing awkward about asking. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount quoted online is unverified. Separately, an operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, which is a different authorisation entirely. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, operates no premises in the UAE, and is not approved or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any provider claiming such approval should be asked for the permit or centre number.

Two more questions are worth asking before money changes hands. Who, by name, will teach my child, and what level have they taught? And what happens if the match does not work — replacement, refund, or nothing? A provider who will not answer the first is selling an option. A provider with no answer to the second has transferred all the risk to you while charging agency rates.

On data, one practical point: lead forms for tutoring collect personal information about a minor. Ask what is collected, why, and how to have it deleted, and expect a privacy policy to be reachable from the page. That is a reasonable question in any market and a specifically reasonable one under UAE personal data protection law.

process.description: Tell us the budget and the subject together. A family with AED 1,000 a month to spend on IB support should be advised differently from one with AED 4,000, and the advice is not simply fewer sessions. Sometimes the right answer at a lower budget is a group option or a shorter, better-aimed block.

faqs.question: What should an IB tutor cost per hour for a family in Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: Judge it by band rather than by a single number. Published Dubai figures read in October 2026: budget online generalists AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; qualified subject tutors online AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270; premium named tutors up to AED 650. Anything well above the specialist band needs a specific justification, and anything below the qualified band for Higher Level work needs a question about what is actually being supplied.

faqs.question: Is in-home tuition worth the extra AED 100 an hour?
faqs.answer: Only if a screen genuinely will not work for your child. The premium is roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour and it buys proximity, not teaching. The arithmetic is visible in advertised packages: about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is the same contact time for roughly double the money. For a young child who cannot settle on screen, or a home with no quiet corner, that premium is defensible. Paid out of habit, it is the largest avoidable line in a Dubai tutoring budget.

faqs.question: What does two years of IB Diploma support actually add up to?
faqs.answer: Using the published bands, one subject supported weekly across both years is roughly 70 sessions, which at AED 150 to 450 an hour comes to somewhere between AED 10,500 and AED 31,500. Two subjects in the final year lands in a similar range. The lines that dominate are the weekly ones, so the decision that controls your total is how many subjects you support and for how long, not the rate you negotiate. Most families actually need one subject for one term at a time, plus a short internal assessment block.

faqs.question: Where do Dubai families most often waste money on tutoring?
faqs.answer: Six places. Buying hours before a diagnosis, so the diagnosis is billed at teaching rates. Paying specialist rates for homework supervision. Paying budget rates for Higher Level paper technique. The in-home travel premium paid from habit. Three subjects at once, all half-attended. And internal assessment help bought a term too late, which turns a four-session job into a rescue. None of these are about choosing a bad provider; they are about buying the wrong thing from a reasonable one.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class better value than a cheap one-to-one hour?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and it is dismissed too quickly. A small group at a fraction of one-to-one rates with a tutor who knows the syllabus generally beats a one-to-one hour with a generalist at the budget band, because the quality of the teaching matters more than the ratio once the group is small. Group classes are concentrated in the Al Qusais and Al Nahda belt near Al Garhoud. What a group cannot do is diagnose one student's specific mark-losing behaviour, which is what a specialist one-to-one hour is for.

faqs.question: How do I tell a specialist from a generalist without knowing the subject?
faqs.answer: Ask them to mark one page of your child's most recent written work aloud, saying what each annotation is worth and why. A specialist uses mark-scheme language, names command terms, and ends by identifying one behaviour to change. A generalist corrects spelling, says it looks good and suggests more practice. You do not need subject knowledge to hear the difference. Run the test during a free trial rather than over the phone, where anybody can sound convincing.

faqs.question: Should I pay for all three Higher Level subjects?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Supporting three Higher Level subjects weekly is the most expensive plan available and a student's week cannot absorb it alongside school, coursework and CAS. Choose on two tests: which Higher Level subject does the intended university course actually require, and which shows the largest gap between current and required attainment. Spend on the intersection. Leave the third unless it is failing, and review at the next mock rather than committing for the year.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest moment to buy internal assessment help?
faqs.answer: The term the task is set, not the term it is due. Four sessions early — narrowing the research question until the available data can answer it, reading the criteria, planning the method — costs a fraction of the rescue work needed when a question that could never score well is discovered six weeks before submission. It is the smallest high-leverage line in a Diploma budget and the one most often left until it has become the largest.

faqs.question: Can I ask a Dubai tutor to show me their MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Because it costs nothing, there is no innocent reason for a working tutor not to hold one. MoHRE lists the service as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing with a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school fee freeze change what I should budget for tutoring?
faqs.answer: It makes the planning easier. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. With the school fee fixed for the year, tutoring becomes the discretionary education line in a household budget, which is an argument for planning it as a figure rather than letting it accumulate session by session. Write down the term total before booking the first hour.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish one hourly rate like other providers?
faqs.answer: Because a single figure would either overcharge a Standard Level term or undercharge a final-year Higher Level plan, and in both cases it hides the information a parent needs. We publish the market bands instead, with sources, so you can screen any quote including ours, and we give our own number after a free trial lesson against a written plan. If you want a comparison figure before talking to anybody, the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 is the honest one to budget against.

faqs.question: Who carries the cost if the match has to be changed?
faqs.answer: Ask that question of every provider before paying, because the answers differ enormously. An agency usually offers a replacement. A marketplace generally offers nothing, because it did no matching. A freelance tutor cannot cover their own illness. With us the match is replaced and we tell you whether we think the mismatch was personality, level or subject, since the three need different replacements. Fit problems normally show within two or three sessions, so raise it early rather than waiting for a report.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start tutoring in the first year or the final year?
faqs.answer: Cheaper overall to start earlier and buy less. A term of support in the first Diploma year, aimed at one weak paper technique, costs a fraction of a final-year rescue across two subjects, and it protects the internal assessment work that happens in between. The expensive pattern is doing nothing for eighteen months and then buying intensively for six, which is also the pattern least likely to work, because examination technique needs repeated practice over a term to become automatic.

faqs.question: Do you charge more for Higher Level than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Effectively yes, because supply differs. Higher Level carries additional content, more timetabled hours and in several subjects an extra paper, and fewer tutors can teach it credibly — particularly in the sciences and the Group 3 subjects, where Dubai supply is thinnest. The Dubai specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above reflects that scarcity rather than a decision by any provider. For Standard Level content teaching, the mid band of AED 150 to 300 is usually the right place to be shopping.

faqs.question: What should I refuse to pay for?
faqs.answer: Any offer to write, complete or produce an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or coursework. At least one operation competing for this search sells finished internal assessments; under IB rules that is malpractice and the consequence falls on your child, not the seller. Also refuse to pay before the tutor is named with the level they have taught, refuse any promise about a grade or a score, and treat a self-published star rating with no countable reviews behind it as a reason to look elsewhere.

faqs.question: How much notice do I need to give to stop?
faqs.answer: Ask before you start, and prefer a provider whose plan has built-in exit points. Ours are tied to the next marked assessment, so a family can stop at a review with nothing outstanding. The pattern to avoid is a long prepaid block with no review structure, because it converts a teaching relationship into a sunk cost and makes it harder to recognise that something is not working. A term is a sensible unit to commit to; a year is not.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-garhoud.closingBody: The useful order is budget, then diagnosis, then hours. Tell us the subject, the level and what you are willing to spend in a term, and you will get either a plan that fits it or an honest statement that the money would be better spent elsewhere — including on a group class or on your school's own support sessions. The first lesson is free, one per subject, taken before any payment, and the quote comes after it rather than before. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with no travel premium because nobody is travelling.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-habtoor-cit.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects for students in Al Habtoor City and the Jumeirah coast. Each one teaches a named subject at a named level rather than general study skills, and each session is scheduled against your child's own school assessment calendar.

intro.heading: Why the calendar, not the postcode, decides what help is worth buying
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near me in Al Habtoor City is really two questions wearing one coat. The first is practical: who can teach my child this week. The second is the one parents ask only after a disappointing report, which is whether there is still time for teaching to change the grade. The second question has a numerical answer, and that answer is what should decide how you spend money. A student in the first term of DP1 has roughly eighteen months of teachable time, four internal assessment cycles and two mock windows ahead. A student in February of DP2 has weeks, one mock window behind them, and an internal assessment already uploaded. The same tutor, the same subject and the same hourly rate buy two completely different things.

Al Habtoor City itself is a cluster of three residential towers, Noora, Amna and Meera, plus hotels and the theatre, sitting on the Dubai Water Canal where Sheikh Zayed Road meets Al Safa. It is a short drive to Jumeirah, Al Wasl and Business Bay, and a longer one to Al Barsha and Al Sufouh where much of Dubai's IB capacity actually sits. Families here are typically spread across four or five schools rather than concentrated in one, which matters more than it sounds: four schools means four different internal deadline calendars, four mock timetables and four sets of report-card conventions. A tutor who works to your child's school calendar is doing something a tutor who works to a generic syllabus plan is not.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video. There is no home-visit service here; home visits are offered only in India. That is not an apology, it is the mechanism that makes the calendar argument work. A Diploma student who needs Chemistry HL help in the eight weeks before mocks needs a Chemistry HL teacher, not the nearest available graduate. Removing the drive from the equation widens the pool from whoever can reach Al Habtoor City by half past four to anyone who can teach the subject at the right level in the right time zone, and it gives back the twenty to forty minutes of travel each way that an in-home arrangement quietly bills for.

What follows is ordered the way a Diploma year actually runs. The exam session comes first, then the registration and upload deadlines that sit months in front of it, then the internal assessment chain, then the mock windows, then the ordinary weekly teaching that fills the gaps. Market rates are published with their sources so you can see what the figures are and are not. The schools around the canal are named as context for which subjects and programmes local students are sitting, with no suggestion of any relationship between those schools and IB Gram.

One caution before the detail. IB session and results dates are published by the International Baccalaureate and by your child's school, and this page deliberately does not restate them as fixed numbers, because a date printed once and left alone becomes wrong without anybody touching it. Where a date matters, the page names the series by its month and tells you which office publishes the authoritative version. Cambridge and Pearson dates are quoted from the boards' own timetable pages, which is why those carry a citation and the IB ones do not.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-habtoor-cit.programmesIntro: Students in Al Habtoor City sit across the full IB continuum, and the programme a child is in changes what tutoring can realistically achieve in a term. Each entry below gives the programme, the ages it covers, and what the calendar looks like inside it for a Dubai family.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment worth between twenty and thirty per cent of the final grade, marked by the school and moderated by the IB. Final grades run from 1 to 7 per subject, with up to three bonus points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination, for a ceiling of 45.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools almost all enter candidates for the May session, which means DP2 runs from an August start to an April finish with no slack in it. For an Al Habtoor City family that compresses everything: internal assessment drafts land in DP2 term one, mocks sit in the new year, and the window where teaching can still move a grade closes earlier than most parents expect. November entry exists and a small number of Dubai students use it after a resit decision.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, lettered A to D, with task-specific descriptors rather than percentage marks. Reports arrive as criterion levels out of 8 and an overall grade out of 7, which is why parents find them harder to read than a percentage. MYP 5 ends with the Personal Project and, in some schools, eAssessment in a selection of subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai IB schools run MYP to Year 11 while the British-curriculum schools a few minutes away run IGCSE over the same two years. Families who move between the two mid-stream are the most common MYP tutoring request in this part of the city, because the assessment language changes completely even when the content overlaps.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, concluding with the Year 6 Exhibition. Assessment is formative and descriptive, so there is no grade to improve in the usual sense. Tutoring at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the English language load that a child arriving mid-year carries.
programmes.countryNote: PYP requests from the Jumeirah coast cluster around two moments: a mid-year arrival from a non-English school system, and the Year 6 to Year 7 transition where a child moves from inquiry-led primary work into the eight subject groups of MYP with eight separate teachers.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning requirement and language development. Offered by a limited number of UAE schools. Students take the same Diploma course assessments for their chosen subjects, so subject tutoring works exactly as it does for a Diploma candidate.
programmes.countryNote: Few schools near Al Habtoor City offer the Career-related Programme, so most families encountering it have either moved from abroad or chosen it deliberately for a vocational pathway. The reflective project supervision boundary is the same as the Extended Essay one: feedback on the student's own drafts, nothing more.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-habtoor-cit.subjectsIntro: Requests from the Al Habtoor City and Al Safa side of the canal concentrate in the sciences, mathematics and the two economics and business courses, which is what a cohort aiming at engineering, medicine and business degrees looks like. Each subject below is listed with the levels taught and the specific place marks tend to go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus, statistics and probability, assessed across two papers at SL and three at HL. Marks leak at HL in the proof questions and in the Paper 3 extended investigation, where students who can execute a technique still cannot structure an argument about it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-heavy, modelling-led and calculator-dependent throughout, including Paper 1. The common failure is treating the graphing calculator as the answer rather than the tool, so working is thin and method marks are lost even when the final number is right.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Reorganised around structure and reactivity rather than the old topic list. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most lost marks, and the data-based questions in Paper 2 punish students who have never been taught to read an uncertainty.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, waves, fields, nuclear physics and the HL extension material. The reliable weak point is not the physics but the algebra underneath it: rearranging before substituting, carrying units, and knowing when a graph gradient is the quantity asked for.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. The command terms do the damage here. A question that says outline wants three lines and a question that says evaluate wants a judgement, and students who write the same paragraph for both lose half the marks available.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and the internal assessment portfolio of three commentaries on published news articles. Diagram accuracy is the cheapest mark in the subject and the most frequently thrown away, usually by unlabelled axes or a shift drawn in the wrong direction.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business organisation, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with a research project at HL and a written commentary at SL. Students lose marks by describing a tool instead of applying it to the case material in front of them.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided textual analysis of unseen non-literary texts, Paper 2 comparative essay, plus the individual oral and, at HL, the essay. The unseen paper is where preparation shows: students who have analysed fifty text types handle an unfamiliar one, and students who have revised quotations do not.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive skills across five prescribed themes. The productive paper rewards register control, so a student who writes a blog in the style of an essay loses marks for conceptual understanding even when the grammar is clean.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition of three objects with commentaries and the prescribed-title essay of 1,600 words. Both are assessed against published criteria, and the essay fails most often because the student argues about the topic rather than about how knowledge in that area is produced and justified.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a chosen subject with a supervisor, assessed on focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation and engagement. The research question is where most of the final grade is decided, long before any writing happens.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in every Dubai private school alongside the licensed international curriculum. KHDA sets the weekly instructional time and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, so a child's Arabic stream depends on their registered category rather than their actual fluency.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-habtoor-cit.regionsIntro: Al Habtoor City sits at a junction, which is the practical reason an online schedule works better here than a travelling one. The areas below are the ones families in these towers move between for school, and the notes are about the parts that affect when a lesson can start.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: Immediately inland across Al Safa Park. Jumeirah College and Horizon English School sit here, so an Al Habtoor City child may be a five-minute drive from school and still arrive home after half past three.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: The strip between Al Safa and Jumeirah, with Al Wasl Road carrying much of the school-run traffic. Afternoon congestion here is the reason a four o'clock in-home slot is often really a quarter to five.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: Home to Jumeira Baccalaureate School, one of the IB continuum schools closest to the canal. Families here are frequently the ones comparing MYP against the IGCSE their neighbours' children sit.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2
regions.note: Low-rise villa streets with a mix of British and IB school allegiances. The practical note is parking and school-gate timing rather than distance, since nothing here is far from anything.

regions.name: Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Stretches towards Umm Suqeim and the JESS Jumeirah campus. Primary-age tutoring requests from this strip outnumber Diploma ones, which is the reverse of the pattern inside Al Habtoor City itself.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Raffles World Academy and Kings' School Dubai draw students from here. A canal-side family choosing between the two is choosing between an IB continuum and a British route, which changes the tutoring question entirely.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Across the water and two minutes away by road, with a high-rise population and the same spread-across-many-schools pattern as Al Habtoor City. Evening slots after seven are more common here than elsewhere.

regions.name: Al Manara
regions.note: Quiet inland villas between Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim, closer to the Al Barsha IB cluster. Families moving from Al Habtoor City to Al Manara usually keep the school and inherit a longer run.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira
regions.note: A newer coastal development with young families and a primary-weighted tutoring demand. PYP and early MYP requests dominate, and the sessions that work are the ones immediately after school rather than late evening.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: A single access road, which is the clearest illustration on this coast of why travelling tuition prices in uncertainty. A lesson over video starts at the time it says it starts.

schoolClusters.city: The canal and Jumeirah coast
schoolClusters.note: The schools nearest Al Habtoor City split between British-curriculum routes running IGCSE at sixteen and IB continuum schools running MYP over the same years. That split is why two neighbours in the same tower can be preparing for completely different assessments in the same week.

schoolClusters.city: Mohammed Bin Rashid City and Al Jaddaf
schoolClusters.note: A short run across the canal and the fastest-growing IB and British cluster near the city centre. Several Al Habtoor City families send children here rather than west into Al Barsha, which shortens the afternoon run and shifts the realistic lesson slot earlier.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
schoolClusters.note: Where much of Dubai's IB Diploma capacity actually sits, fifteen to twenty-five minutes west depending on the hour. Families who choose a school here accept a long run, which is precisely the cohort for whom an online evening slot removes a problem rather than creating one.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-habtoor-cit.modesIntro: Three ways of working, chosen by how much calendar is left rather than by preference. A DP1 student in term one and a DP2 student six weeks from mocks should not be buying the same arrangement.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, built on the school's assessment dates
modes.description: A fixed slot each week in one subject at one level, planned backwards from your child's own school deadlines rather than from a generic syllabus order. The tutor works from the topics the class is covering, the internal assessment stage the student is at, and the next piece of assessed work on the school calendar.
bullets: Same tutor, same slot, in Gulf Standard Time
Session plan written against the school's own deadline list
Short written note after each lesson naming what was covered and what to practise
Topic sequence adjusted when the school's order differs from the textbook's

modes.title: An eight-week block before a mock or exam window
modes.description: An intensive course with a defined end date, usually two sessions a week, targeted at the specific papers coming up. The content is past-paper work and mark-scheme discipline rather than new teaching, because eight weeks is not long enough to learn a syllabus and is long enough to stop losing marks you already know how to win.
bullets: Diagnostic on a full past paper in week one, marked against the real mark scheme
Two sessions a week, one on content gaps and one on timed questions
A written list of the topics not worth attempting, which is often the most useful page
A final week on exam logistics, timing splits and question order

modes.title: Internal assessment and core supervision
modes.description: Scheduled feedback sessions across the internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge cycle. The tutor reads the student's own drafts against the published criteria, explains which criterion is costing marks, and asks the questions that make the student revise it. The writing is not done for them at any stage.
bullets: Research-question and topic-viability conversation before any drafting begins
Criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own draft
Method and data-handling coaching for science and mathematics explorations
Nothing is written, edited to completion or supplied on the student's behalf

sections.heading: What "near me" is really asking, and the honest answer
paragraphs: The search phrase assumes distance is the constraint. For most subjects at most levels in Dubai it is not. The constraint is how many people can teach that subject at that level, and in a city of 227 private schools running seventeen curricula, the specialists for any single Diploma course at Higher Level are a small and scattered group. Narrowing that group to the people who can reach Al Habtoor City by half past four on a Tuesday does not improve your odds. It makes them considerably worse.

Work it through with a real example. Suppose your child is taking Chemistry at Higher Level and is losing marks consistently on energetics and equilibrium. The useful question is not who lives nearby. It is who has taught the current Chemistry course, knows how the data-based questions in Paper 2 are marked, and can tell within one session whether the problem is the chemistry, the mathematics underneath it, or the way the student reads the question. A geography graduate who tutors general science and lives in Business Bay cannot answer that. A chemistry teacher in another time zone, teaching over video at seven in the evening Gulf Standard Time, can.

So the honest answer to the search is this: there is no IB Gram tutor who will arrive at an Al Habtoor City address, and the service is not sold on that basis anywhere in the UAE. Home visits exist only in India. What replaces proximity is a wider pool and a fixed start time. Nobody is sitting in traffic on Al Wasl Road at your expense, nobody shortens the lesson because the previous one overran across town, and the tutor is chosen for the subject rather than for the postcode.

The one thing proximity genuinely buys is a person in the room with a reluctant eleven-year-old. That is a real advantage and it is worth saying out loud rather than arguing around. For a Diploma student working on an internal assessment or a mock paper, it is not the advantage that matters, and it costs between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour in the Dubai in-home market according to the rate comparisons published by Bestimate and by the home-tutor agencies operating here.

sections.heading: The Diploma counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Almost every Dubai IB school enters candidates for the May session, and almost every parent discovers the shape of that year too late. The useful exercise is to run it in reverse. Start at the exam window, step back to the internal upload deadlines, step back again to the school's own draft deadlines, and then look at how many ordinary teaching weeks are actually left between now and the first of those. That number, not the hourly rate, is what tells you whether to buy weekly teaching or an eight-week block.

The table below is a planning skeleton rather than a date list. Specific IB session and results dates are published by the International Baccalaureate and confirmed by your school's Diploma coordinator, and this page deliberately does not reprint them, because a date typed once and left alone becomes wrong on its own. What the table does give you is the order of events and who controls each one, which is the part schools assume you already know.

Two things fall out of reading it backwards. The first is that the internal assessment deadlines, not the exams, are what create the crunch, because they land in the middle of DP2 teaching and they are set by the school rather than by the IB. The second is that the window in which additional teaching can still change a subject grade closes around the mock results, which in a Dubai school typically means the new year. After that point, tutoring is still worth buying, but what it buys is mark recovery on papers the student can nearly do, not new content.

For a sibling studying Cambridge IGCSE alongside a Diploma student, the calendar is different and the dates are published. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series exists in India only, and a UAE family planning around it has planned around the wrong country. Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable, so the version to work from is the one the school's exams officer issues.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can and cannot change
paragraphs: The most common message IB Gram receives from a Dubai parent is a version of the same sentence: the mocks were bad, the exams are close, what can be done. The answer depends almost entirely on which of three situations the student is in, and a tutor who does not establish that in the first session is going to waste your money politely.

The first situation is a student who understands the material and loses marks on execution. Timing, question reading, working shown, units, significant figures, the command term ignored. This is the best case and eight weeks of disciplined past-paper work against the real mark scheme can move it substantially, because every one of those losses is a procedure rather than a gap. The method is unglamorous: attempt under time, mark against the published scheme, catalogue the loss by type, drill the type, repeat. Students are often surprised by how many marks they were giving away on things they already knew.

The second situation is a student with real content gaps in two or three topics while the rest is sound. Eight weeks is enough for this if the triage is honest. You pick the topics by marks available per hour of teaching, not by what the student finds most frightening, and you accept that some topics will be left. Writing down the list of topics that are not worth attempting is frequently the single most useful thing a tutor produces in that block, and it is the thing an anxious student will resist hardest.

The third situation is a student who has not learned the syllabus. Here eight weeks cannot deliver a transformation and anybody who says otherwise is selling. What it can deliver is a defensible partial: secure the foundation topics that recur across papers, build a workable approach to the structured questions, and protect the internal assessment marks that are already banked. It is also the moment to have the November resit conversation, and to have it early enough that it is a decision rather than a reaction. No tutor can promise a grade, and a promise of one is the clearest signal to stop reading.
bullets: Week one is a full timed past paper, marked against the published mark scheme, not a chat
Losses get catalogued by type, so drills target the pattern rather than the paper
Topic triage is by marks per teaching hour, which means some topics are deliberately dropped

sections.heading: The internal deadline chain: assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
paragraphs: The Diploma's internal components are where Dubai families lose the most time, partly because the deadlines belong to the school rather than to the IB and partly because the rules about who may help are genuinely strict. Each subject's internal assessment is worth a fifth to nearly a third of the final grade, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together carry up to three bonus points, and all of them are assessed against criteria that are published and that most students have never actually read.

That last point is where tutoring earns its fee. A student who has read the criteria for their own internal assessment, in order, and has mapped their draft against them, writes a different second draft from a student who has been told it needs more analysis. The criteria are lettered and each carries a stated maximum, so the conversation becomes arithmetic: this criterion is capped at six, your draft supports three, here is what the descriptor for five and six actually asks for. That is teaching, and it is permitted. Producing the content is not.

The boundary matters enough to state plainly. A tutor must not write the internal assessment, draft the Extended Essay or produce a Theory of Knowledge essay, in whole or in part. Under IB academic honesty rules that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the tutor. One of the sites ranking for these searches in Dubai sells completed internal assessments outright. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring; it is a different and far riskier transaction, and it is the reason this page states the limit rather than leaving it implied.

What a tutor may legitimately do is extensive, and parents are often relieved to hear how much of it there is. Pressure-test a research question before weeks are spent on it. Explain why a dataset will not support the claim being made. Teach the statistics the exploration needs. Mark a draft against the criteria and explain the gap. Ask the student the questions that make the weakness visible to them. Rehearse the oral or the viva. All of that is teaching the student to do their own work better, which is what the criteria are measuring in the first place.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs around Sheikh Zayed Road
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number that decides whether an arrangement survives past March. Bestimate's Dubai rate work puts weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are the published shapes of the market; none of them is an IB Gram price.

Translated to the hour, the Dubai bands are reasonably consistent across sources. A university-student or budget online tutor runs AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, is quoted at AED 180 to 500. An IB or A-Level specialist is AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. A premium named or examiner-badged tutor reaches AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650. All of those figures were read from the providers' own pages in October 2026.

The gap worth staring at is the one between the online specialist band and the in-home band. A chunk of the in-home premium is not teaching. It is travel, and in this part of Dubai it is unpredictable travel, which is why in-home agencies tend to sell two-hour blocks rather than one-hour ones. There is no reliable way to buy forty minutes of a tutor's driving time back, and a two-hour block for a fourteen-year-old on a Wednesday is frequently ninety minutes of teaching and thirty of fatigue.

Three places the money genuinely goes to waste, in order of how often they appear. Buying group classes for a Higher Level subject where the whole point is the individual diagnosis. Buying hours in a subject the student is already passing because it is the one they enjoy, while the actual problem sits untouched. And buying a long package before a trial lesson has established whether the tutor can teach that specific course. For reference against school costs, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package reported at AED 1.5 billion.
