sections.heading: Term dates, Ramadan and the weeks that quietly disappear
paragraphs: A Dubai academic year looks longer on paper than it is in practice, and families planning a tutoring block from a calendar rather than from experience consistently overestimate how many weeks they have. Three things remove time: the winter and spring breaks, the shortened Ramadan school day, and the two to three weeks either side of mocks when the school's own revision programme fills every afternoon. Plan an eight-week block across a period containing two of those and it is a five-week block with an eight-week invoice.

Ramadan deserves specific thought rather than a line. School days shorten, which sounds like it creates time and generally does not, because the day ends earlier and the evening restructures around iftar and family. For many families the workable slot moves to after iftar, which in practice means later evening sessions. For others the honest answer is to pause and come back, and a tutor who offers that rather than quietly billing through a month of poor attention is behaving correctly. Fasting students in an exam year need a schedule built around when they can actually concentrate, not around the slot that was convenient in November.

The other predictable loss is the school's own revision timetable. Dubai schools run extensive internal revision in the weeks before mocks and again before the final session, often in after-school slots. That is good teaching and it is already paid for in the fees. Stacking a tutoring block on top of it produces a child doing the same past paper twice with two different people and no time to practise alone, which is the one activity that actually consolidates. The sensible move is to coordinate: ask the school for its revision calendar, then put tutoring in the gaps.

The practical scheduling rule for Al Habtoor City specifically is that the earliest reliable slot is around half past four for a child at a Jumeirah or Al Safa school, and closer to five for a child travelling from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh. Because lessons run over video, that slot holds regardless of what Sheikh Zayed Road is doing, and a late-evening slot is possible for an older student without anybody driving home at nine o'clock.

sections.heading: The schools either side of the canal, and what a KHDA report actually tells you
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is described by the UAE government's own portal as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band for each school: Outstanding, Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak and Very Weak. Those words are the single most quoted and least understood pieces of information in Dubai school conversations.

What a band is, and is not, is worth being precise about. It is a judgement about the school as a whole across teaching, learning outcomes, student personal development, leadership and provision for students with additional needs. It is not a prediction for your child's Chemistry Higher Level grade, and it is not a subject-level verdict. A school in a strong band can have a weak year in one subject because a specialist left in August, and a school in a middling band can have an outstanding mathematics department. The report is a starting point for questions, not an answer.

The useful thing to do with a KHDA report is to read the subject and assessment sections rather than the headline, and then ask the school three direct questions: how many students took this subject at Higher Level last year, who teaches it this year, and what the internal deadline calendar looks like. Those three answers tell you more about the risk to your child's grade than the band does. Dubai's market is also growing quickly, with the 2026-27 intake adding seven new private schools, four British-curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent.

One more regulatory fact that surprises IB families. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed to teach, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that no mandatory lesson run shorter than 25 minutes. For a Diploma student these subjects sit outside the six IB courses and still occupy timetable space, which is part of why DP2 feels as tight as it does.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, the tutor permit, and the two questions to ask before you pay
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity with a permit attached. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is the MoHRE service called Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Two consequences follow for a parent in Al Habtoor City. The first is that anyone offering private lessons in the UAE without that permit is operating outside the rules, and the government portal states that individuals doing so are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any specific figure quoted at you is somebody's guess. The second consequence is more immediate: the permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. An offer of your child's own class teacher, privately, is not the inside track it sounds like.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again. It requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific permit issued to a specific entity at a specific address. IB Gram does not hold one, does not operate a UAE centre or office, and does not describe itself using any regulator's name. Any provider that calls itself regulator-approved in a search result is making a claim you can and should ask them to evidence with a permit number.

Which leaves the two questions worth asking before any money moves. First: which syllabus, by name and code, and which level, have you taught, and for how many cohorts? A specialist answers immediately and in detail. A generalist answers with reassurance. Second: show me how you would mark this, handing over one page of your child's actual work. The response to that single request separates somebody who knows the mark scheme from somebody who knows the subject, and the difference between those two is most of what you are paying for.

process.title: Tell us where the calendar sits
process.description: The first message should say the school, the year group, the subjects and levels, and the next dated thing on the horizon, whether that is a mock window, an internal assessment deadline or the written papers. That last detail is what decides whether weekly teaching or a defined block is the right purchase.

process.title: Match on the course, not the postcode
process.description: A tutor is proposed who has taught that named course at that level, with the cohorts they have taught stated. If no specialist is free for that subject and level, you are told so rather than offered a near-enough alternative, and told roughly when one is expected to come free.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the terms stated
process.description: One lesson at no cost, no card details collected and no obligation to continue. It is a real teaching session, not a sales call, and it is where you find out whether the tutor can diagnose from your child's own work. Bring one marked past paper or one internal assessment draft to it.

process.title: A plan written backwards from the deadlines
process.description: After the trial the tutor sets out the session sequence against your child's school dates: what is covered when, which topics are being deliberately left, and what the student practises alone between lessons. The deliberately-left list is part of the plan rather than an omission from it.

process.title: Weekly notes and an honest mid-point review
process.description: A short note after each session naming what was covered and what to practise. At the block's mid-point there is a direct conversation about whether the arrangement is working, including the version of that conversation where the answer is that a different tutor or a different subject is the better use of the money.

whyPoints.title: The pool is the subject, not the drive time
whyPoints.description: Matching on who can teach the named course at the named level rather than on who can reach Al Habtoor City by half past four changes which tutors are available to you. For a Higher Level science or a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches student, that difference is the whole decision.

whyPoints.title: Rates on the page, with their sources
whyPoints.description: Three of the six best-ranking Dubai tutoring pages publish no price at all and the two that do quote in US dollars. The AED bands on this page are attributed to the providers that published them and dated to when they were read, so you can check them yourself rather than take them on trust.

whyPoints.title: The assessed work stays the student's
whyPoints.description: Feedback against published criteria, method coaching and draft critique, with nothing written or supplied on the student's behalf at any stage. One site ranking for these searches sells finished internal assessments; under IB rules the consequence of that lands on the student, which is why the limit is stated here rather than implied.

whyPoints.title: A start time that holds
whyPoints.description: A video lesson starts when it says it starts, whatever Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Wasl Road are doing at the time. Nothing is shortened because the previous session overran across the city, and nobody is billing you for the drive from Al Barsha to the canal.

whyPoints.title: Dates named by month, not by year
whyPoints.description: Exam series are named by their month, because a page that prints a specific future date becomes wrong on its own. Cambridge and Pearson dates come from the boards' own timetable pages with the source given; IB session dates are left to the International Baccalaureate and your school's coordinator, who are the authorities on them.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated plainly
whyPoints.description: If no tutor is free for a particular course at a particular level, you are told that and told when one is expected, rather than matched with the nearest available subject. The commonest version of this is a specific Higher Level science in the weeks immediately before the May session, when demand concentrates.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor based inside Al Habtoor City itself?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram, and that is worth being direct about. All UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video; home visits are a service offered only in India. Al Habtoor City is three residential towers on the Dubai Water Canal, and the chance that a specialist in your child's exact Diploma course at the exact level happens to live in them is small. Working over video widens the pool from whoever can drive here by half past four to anyone who can teach that course in Gulf Standard Time, which for a Higher Level science is the difference between a specialist and a generalist.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the May session is it too late to start IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: There is no cliff, but what you are buying changes. More than six months out, weekly teaching can still cover content gaps properly. Inside about eight weeks, new content is largely off the table and the work becomes timed past papers, mark-scheme discipline and triage of which topics to abandon. Even four weeks out there is value in protecting marks the student can nearly win and in tightening exam technique. What nobody can honestly offer at any distance is a grade, so treat a promised score as a reason to stop the conversation.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 at a Jumeirah school. Should we wait until DP2 to get help?
faqs.answer: Usually not, because DP1 is where the cheap wins are. Subject and level choices are confirmed early, the Extended Essay research question is set, Theory of Knowledge begins, and the habits that cost marks in DP2 are formed. An hour a week in DP1 on the subject your child is least secure in costs less and achieves more than the same hour in the term before the exams, when the calendar leaves no room to teach anything new. The exception is a student already coping well, where waiting and watching the first full report is reasonable.

faqs.question: Which exam series do Cambridge IGCSE students in Dubai actually sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge International runs an IGCSE and O Level June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered in India only, so a Dubai family planning around it is planning around another country's calendar. Cambridge also allocates each exam centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable, so always work from the timetable your school's exams officer issues.

faqs.question: What does an internal assessment actually count for in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Roughly a fifth to nearly a third of the final grade in each subject, depending on the course, which makes it the largest single piece of assessment most students will ever submit without an invigilator in the room. It is marked by the school against published criteria and then moderated by the IB. The practical implication is that the criteria are the specification: a student who has read them in order and mapped their own draft against each lettered criterion writes a materially different second draft from one who was told to add more analysis.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Extended Essay without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. Permitted support includes pressure-testing the research question before weeks are spent on it, discussing whether sources and data can support the claim, explaining the assessment criteria, giving feedback on the student's own draft, and preparing for the reflection sessions with the school supervisor. What is not permitted is drafting any section, rewriting prose to completion, or selecting and summarising sources on the student's behalf. The work has to be the student's own, and under IB academic honesty rules the consequence of a breach falls on the student.

faqs.question: What do private tutors around Al Safa and the canal charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 run roughly as follows. Budget online tutors, often university students, AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits including travel AED 180 to 500. IB and IGCSE specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650. Those are market figures, not IB Gram's.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tuition in Dubai more expensive than the same tutor online?
faqs.answer: Because a large part of the in-home premium is travel rather than teaching. A tutor crossing from Al Barsha to the canal in afternoon traffic spends forty minutes or more each way, and that time is priced into the rate whether or not it appears as a line item. It is also why in-home providers tend to sell two-hour blocks: one hour does not justify the journey. Market quotes of AED 180 to 500 an hour for in-home visits sit against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online, and the gap is mostly the car.

faqs.question: Does the KHDA inspection band tell me whether my child will do well in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: No, and it is not designed to. KHDA inspects each Dubai private school annually and publishes a whole-school band from Outstanding down to Very Weak, covering teaching, outcomes, personal development, leadership and inclusion. It is not a subject-level judgement. A school in a strong band can have a difficult year in one Higher Level subject because a specialist left, and a school in a middling band can have a strong mathematics department. Read the subject sections of the report, then ask the school who teaches the course this year and how many sat it last year.

faqs.question: Do Diploma students in Dubai still have to take Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because expectations and the language of instruction differ. KHDA calculates the time on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Diploma student these sit outside the six IB subjects and still occupy timetable space, which is part of why DP2 feels so compressed.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with an Al Habtoor City family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include school and government employees, private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The route is the MoHRE service Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing. The UAE government portal states that individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but publishes no fine schedule, so any quoted amount is unverified.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher tutor them privately in the evenings?
faqs.answer: Treat this as a problem rather than a shortcut. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with teachers tutoring outside school hours required to hold the MoHRE permit. The arrangement also creates an obvious conflict where the same person teaches, tutors and marks. Verify the current policy with the school before any money changes hands.

faqs.question: How should we plan tutoring around Ramadan and the school holidays?
faqs.answer: Count the weeks you actually have rather than the weeks on the calendar. The winter and spring breaks, the shortened Ramadan school day and the two or three weeks the school fills with its own pre-mock revision together remove a surprising amount of an eight-week block. During Ramadan the workable slot often moves to after iftar, and for a fasting student in an exam year the schedule should follow concentration rather than convenience. Pausing and resuming is a legitimate answer, and a tutor who offers it instead of billing through a weak month is behaving properly.

faqs.question: What should I bring to the first session to make it useful?
faqs.answer: One marked past paper or one internal assessment draft, with the teacher's comments still on it, plus the school's deadline calendar for the term. Those two documents let a tutor diagnose in a single session rather than spending three on orientation. The marked work shows where marks are actually going, which is almost never where the student thinks. The deadline calendar shows what the next dated obligation is, which decides whether the sensible purchase is weekly teaching or a defined block with an end date.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for a specific Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You are told, and told when one is expected to be free, rather than offered a near-enough match. The commonest instance is a specific Higher Level science in the weeks before the May session, when demand across the region concentrates on the same small group of specialists. A general science tutor for a Higher Level Chemistry candidate eight weeks from the papers is a poor use of money, and saying so is more useful than filling the slot. Where a wait is likely, the honest alternatives are a shorter block later or a different subject first.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring really as effective as having someone in the room?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student and the task, and the honest split is by age and by work type. For a Diploma student working on a past paper, an internal assessment draft or a worked problem, a shared screen with annotation is at least as good as paper on a table, and the recording of the session is an advantage paper does not offer. For a reluctant younger child, a person physically present genuinely helps. All UAE delivery here is online, so if your need is the second kind it is fair to say the arrangement may not suit.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-habtoor-cit.closingHeading: Work out how many weeks are left, then decide what to buy
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-habtoor-cit.closingBody: Before contacting anybody, do one piece of arithmetic. Find the next dated obligation on your child's school calendar, whether that is an internal assessment deadline, a mock window or the written papers, and count the teaching weeks between now and it, subtracting the holidays and the school's own revision programme. If the answer is more than twenty weeks, weekly teaching in the weakest subject is the efficient purchase. If it is under ten, a defined block aimed at specific papers is. Bring that number and one marked piece of work to a free trial lesson, with no card details taken, and a tutor who has taught the course will tell you in an hour whether your money is better spent on teaching, on technique, or on a November entry conversation.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-jaddaf.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering the IB Diploma for families in Al Jaddaf: matched to one subject at one level, with internal assessment criteria experience, and quoted after a free trial rather than from a rate card.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a two-year purchase, so cost it that way
paragraphs: Most families in Al Jaddaf buy IB tutoring reactively. A grade slips in the first term of Year 12, support is bought weekly for that subject, and nobody asks what the next twenty-two months will cost or where in those months the money does most work. By the spring of Year 13 the household has often spent several times the figure it imagined, because the expensive hours were bought at the point of maximum panic rather than the point of maximum return.

The structure of the Diploma makes the spending pattern predictable, which means it can be planned. Six subjects, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, deliver forty-two of the forty-five points at a maximum of seven each. The remaining three come from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together. Every subject carries an internally assessed component with its own published criteria. And predicted grades, which university offers rest on, are produced by the school from the school's own evidence partway through the second year.

That last fact is where most of the wasted money sits. A plan that peaks in the spring of Year 13, ahead of the external session, arrives after the predictions have already been made. A plan that peaks earlier, around the school's internal assessments and the Extended Essay deadline, does the same work for the same money and also affects the offers. Nobody explains this at a parents' evening and it changes the whole shape of a budget.

On prices, the published market bands are the right frame because they are per subject and per month. Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Hourly figures behind them: budget online tutoring from AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik, qualified online at AED 150 to AED 300 with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED at AED 650. All of those belong to the providers named and were read in October 2026.

In-home visiting rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Al Jaddaf or anywhere else in the UAE; tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visiting is a service we operate only in India. On a page about cost that limit is worth stating up front, because removing travel removes a premium and also removes the constraint that your specialist must live within a drive of Dubai Healthcare City.

What follows costs the two years stage by stage, ranks subjects by how expensive they are to support and why, identifies where a single Diploma point is cheapest to gain, and sets out the scheduling and timing decisions that change the total without changing the hourly rate.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-jaddaf.programmesIntro: An Al Jaddaf family buying IB support is at one of four stages, and the cost per useful outcome differs sharply between them. These are the stages we cover.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 12
programmes.description: Six subjects begin, Theory of Knowledge starts, and the Extended Essay question is chosen towards the end of the year. Content arrives fast and timed-paper technique is usually the weakest thing a student brings from the Middle Years Programme or IGCSE. The internally assessed components are introduced here and started in most subjects.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest year to buy effectively and the year families most often skip. A short diagnostic block costing a handful of hours identifies whether the problem is content, timing or written method, and fixing timing or method in Year 12 is a fraction of the cost of fixing it in Year 13 with predictions pending. Al Jaddaf's short commutes make an early weekday slot realistic, which raises the usable fraction of each paid hour.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 13 before predictions
programmes.description: Internal assessments are completed and moderated, the Extended Essay is finished, Theory of Knowledge is submitted, and the school assembles the evidence from which predicted grades are produced. University applications depend on those predictions.
programmes.countryNote: The highest-return window in the whole Diploma and the one most families under-buy. Money spent here affects both the final grade and the offers, because the same work feeds the school's evidence base. Specialist rates of AED 200 to AED 450 and above are more defensible in this window than in the final term, where the predictions have already been issued and only the examination remains.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 13 final term
programmes.description: Content is complete and the work is timed-paper technique, past papers marked against published schemes, and Paper 3 practice at Higher Level in mathematics. Nothing internally assessed remains to influence, so the whole return is on examination performance.
programmes.countryNote: This is the most expensive window in the market because demand across Dubai peaks simultaneously, and it is where the specialist pool thins fastest. Booking the slot earlier costs the same and secures a better match, which is the one free improvement available. UAE schools sit the main May session; no IB date is published here, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and your school coordinator holds the calendar.

programmes.name: The core: EE, TOK and CAS
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent research essay. Theory of Knowledge is an essay on a prescribed title limited to 1,600 words plus an exhibition of three objects with a commentary limited to 950 words. Creativity, Activity, Service is not graded but is required for the Diploma to be awarded.
programmes.countryNote: Three points sit here, and they are the cheapest three points on the board to protect. Two hours spent narrowing an Extended Essay research question in Year 12 does more than twenty hours of editing in Year 13. A tutor may question a research question, explain a criterion and comment on the student's own draft; a tutor may not produce the essay, restructure it or supply the argument.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-jaddaf.subjectsIntro: Subjects differ in how expensive they are to support, and the reasons are structural rather than arbitrary. These are the ones Al Jaddaf families buy most, with the cost driver named.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: The most expensive subject to support in this market, because the specialist pool is thinnest and Paper 3 plus the Exploration together carry forty per cent of the grade. Paper 3 cannot be revised by topic, so it needs calendar room rather than extra hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Cheaper to support than Analysis and Approaches at the same level, because the pool of tutors comfortable with modelling and statistics is wider. The Exploration carries the same twenty per cent and the same five criteria, so the core cost is unchanged.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Expensive at Higher Level and moderate at Standard. The internally assessed investigation needs uncertainty analysis taught properly, which is a narrow skill, and most lost marks are in evaluation rather than in physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Similar cost profile to Physics. Organic chemistry and energetics drive most requests, and the investigation is marked on exploration, analysis, evaluation and communication, so a thin evaluation section costs more than a modest experiment does.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The cheapest of the three sciences to support, because the content is wide rather than technically narrow and the budget tier can genuinely help with recall discipline. The investigation and data-based questions are where a specialist earns the difference.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Moderate cost with a high-return component: the portfolio of commentaries on published articles. Students lose marks by summarising an article rather than analysing it with a correctly drawn and labelled diagram, which is a few sessions of work rather than a term.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Inexpensive to support relative to the sciences. Marks come from application to a real organisation, so the teachable skill is anchoring theory to the named firm in the stem, and the Higher Level research project needs scope control more than content.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Moderate cost and often under-bought. Paper 1 guided analysis and the individual oral both reward analysing how choices create effect rather than describing content, and that shift is teachable in a short block.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The cheapest point on the board to protect. One session taking a prescribed title apart clause by clause prevents the commonest failure, which is answering an adjacent question well. Essay limit 1,600 words, exhibition commentary 950.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Cheap if bought early and expensive if bought late. A research question too broad to answer in 4,000 words is the dominant failure, and it is visible and fixable at the question stage months before the word count becomes the problem.

sections.heading: A two-year Diploma support plan, costed stage by stage
paragraphs: Here is the plan a family in Al Jaddaf can actually budget, built from the published market bands rather than from invented figures. The principle is that spending should be uneven and front-loaded relative to the school's internal calendar, not relative to the external session. The expensive window is the final term and it is also the window with the lowest marginal return, because by then the internally assessed components are closed and the predictions are issued.

The first stage is a short diagnostic block in Year 12, four to six sessions, at the qualified tier rather than the specialist one. Its purpose is to establish whether the problem is content, timing or written method. That answer is worth more than the sessions cost, because it determines everything afterwards, and the three answers have different and non-interchangeable solutions. Families who skip this stage buy a year of weekly support aimed at whichever cause felt most likely.

The second stage runs through the first half of Year 13, around the internal assessments and the core deadlines. This is where specialist rates are defensible, because the work simultaneously affects the final grade and the evidence from which predicted grades are produced. It is also where most families under-buy, having spent their budget on routine weekly support in Year 12 that addressed a cause nobody had identified.

The third stage is the final term, and the honest advice is to buy less of it than instinct suggests and to book it earlier than feels necessary. Content is complete; the work is timed papers and command terms. The slot booked in the autumn costs the same as the slot booked in panic and comes with a better match, because the specialist pool in Dubai thins sharply when every school's cohort reaches the same point at once.

sections.heading: Where a Diploma point is cheapest to gain
paragraphs: Forty-five points, and they are not equally priced. Some are expensive because the specialist pool is thin and the component is technically demanding. Others are cheap because a single session on a misunderstanding fixes something that was costing marks across a whole component. A family working to a budget should buy the cheap points first, and almost nobody does, because the cheap ones are not where the anxiety is.

The cheapest are in the core. Three points sit on the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination, and both components fail in predictable ways. The Extended Essay fails on question scope, visible months in advance. The Theory of Knowledge essay fails by answering an adjacent question rather than the prescribed title as written. One or two sessions on each, early, protect three points for the price of a few hours at the qualified tier. No subject offers that ratio.

The next cheapest are command terms and evaluation technique, and they are cheap because they transfer. The IB's command terms are published and tiered: state, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, discuss. A student who describes when asked to evaluate has written something true and unmarkable, and the same error is costing marks in every subject simultaneously. One session on the glossary with three past questions improves six subjects at once. Evaluation sections in the sciences behave the same way.

The expensive points are concentrated in Higher Level mathematics and the Higher Level sciences, where Paper 3 and technically demanding internal assessments meet a thin specialist pool. Those are worth paying specialist rates for. The mistake is paying specialist rates across six subjects while the three cheapest points on the board go unprotected, which is the single most common budgeting error we see from Al Jaddaf families.

sections.heading: The timing trap: predicted grades come before the exams
paragraphs: This is the structural fact that costs Al Jaddaf families the most money and is explained the least. Predicted grades are produced by the school, from the school's own evidence, partway through Year 13. University offers rest on them. The external examination happens afterwards. So a tutoring plan designed to peak just before the external session has, by definition, arrived after the decision that determines where the student can apply.

The consequence is that the school's internal assessments are not practice. They are the evidence base. A December paper treated as a mock by the student and by the family is being treated as data by the school. That reframing changes when support is worth buying: earlier, around internal assessments and core deadlines, rather than later around revision. It is the same money spent for two outcomes instead of one.

It also changes what to ask the school for. Request the internal assessment calendar, the internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, and the school's own policy on how predicted grades are formed. Those three documents are free, they exist, and they let a family place spending where it does double duty. Without them, a plan is built from the external session date, which is the wrong anchor.

One honest qualification. We publish no IB session or results dates anywhere on this page. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and an unverified exam date is something a family would plan a term and a budget around. UAE schools sit the main May session. Your school's IB coordinator holds the authoritative calendar, including the internal deadlines that matter more to a tutoring plan than the external ones.

sections.heading: Why "near me" costs more than it saves in Al Jaddaf
paragraphs: Searching for a tutor near me in Al Jaddaf is a request for convenience, and in this market convenience is priced. Published in-home one-to-one rates run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online. A meaningful share of that difference is a tutor's time on the roads around Dubai Healthcare City and the Creek crossings in the late afternoon.

There is a second cost that does not appear on an invoice. A visiting tutor's diary is built around geography, because they can only serve families whose homes cluster. That means your match is constrained by their route before it is constrained by your child's subject and level. For a Standard Level subject in a mainstream group that constraint is tolerable. For Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or for a Higher Level science with a technically demanding internal assessment, it is the binding constraint, and it is invisible at the point of hiring.

The third is replacement speed, which matters most exactly when money is tightest. If a visiting arrangement ends mid-term, a local replacement takes weeks because the pool is bounded by the same geography. In the first half of Year 13, with internal assessments live and predictions pending, a three-week gap is more expensive than any difference in hourly rate. An online match can be replaced inside the same week.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Al Jaddaf or anywhere else in the UAE, and home visiting is a service we operate only in India. There are real cases where a visiting tutor is the right purchase, mostly involving younger or easily distracted students who need an adult present. A Year 12 or Year 13 Diploma candidate working on an internal assessment is not one of them, and for that student the premium buys logistics rather than learning.

sections.heading: Spending that does not work, named
paragraphs: Buying support in all six subjects simultaneously is the most expensive mistake available, and it is usually a response to a report with several middling grades. The Diploma's weaknesses are frequently shared rather than subject-specific: command terms, timed-paper pace, written method for an unknown marker, thin evaluation. Fixing a shared weakness once moves several subjects, and six parallel arrangements cost six times as much to achieve the same thing less well.

Buying hours before a diagnostic is the second. A student sitting at a five in three subjects may have a content gap, a timing problem or a method problem, and the three have nothing in common except the symptom. A tutor without a marked timed paper in front of them will spend the first month finding out, and the family pays for that month. One diagnostic paper marked against the published scheme costs one session and removes the guessing.

Buying the premium tier for routine work is the third. BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour and specialist bands run from AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Those rates are defensible for Higher Level mathematics Paper 3, for a scarce subject, or for a technically demanding internal assessment. They are not defensible for Standard Level content review, where a qualified tutor at AED 150 to AED 300 does the identical job, and the difference across a year is substantial.

Buying the final term heavily is the fourth, and the hardest to resist. It feels like the decisive moment and it is the window with the lowest marginal return, because the internal components are closed and the predictions are issued. The useful version of final-term spending is a slot booked in the autumn and used in the spring: same price, better match, and no scramble when the whole Dubai market reaches the same point in the same fortnight.

sections.heading: Al Jaddaf scheduling, and the usable fraction of a paid hour
paragraphs: If the rate is fixed, the real unit price is the rate divided by the fraction of the hour that works, and that fraction falls as the evening goes on. Al Jaddaf is well placed on this measure. The district is compact, sits beside Dubai Healthcare City Phase 2, and is minutes from the Creek crossings, so a student at Swiss International Scientific School Dubai or at a Festival City school is frequently home in time for a 16:30 start. That is earlier than most Dubai neighbourhoods manage and it is worth real money across a two-year plan.

The subjects most sensitive to this are mathematics and the sciences, because holding several steps of a derivation or an uncertainty calculation in working memory degrades faster with fatigue than reading and annotating a text does. For those subjects we will recommend a shorter earlier session over a longer later one, which is less revenue and better value. For English and the individuals and societies group a later slot costs less.

For Al Jaddaf families whose children attend schools further out, in Nad Al Sheba or beyond Al Khail Road, the geographic advantage reverses into a constraint. Those students arrive home when their Al Jaddaf-schooled neighbours are already working. The answer is a weekend morning, which is the cheapest hour in real terms and also widens the choice of specialist, because the weekday window from 17:00 to 19:00 Gulf Standard Time is the busiest in the UAE tutoring day.

One more scheduling lever with a financial effect. During Ramadan the UAE school day shortens and household routines shift, and the sessions that work are usually either earlier in the day or after Iftar. Agreeing that shift in advance rather than cancelling three weeks of a paid arrangement is a straightforward saving, and it is the kind of thing a tutoring plan should state before the term it applies to.

sections.heading: Claims to discount before you compare prices
paragraphs: Part of what is quoted in this market is a claim rather than a capability, and claims are free to make. Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. An inspection rating judges a school and does not transfer to a tutor. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises and staff that we do not hold.

Discount self-asserted ratings too. Competitors in this market publish star ratings and review counts that contradict each other on the same page, and one shows a figure in its structured data that differs from the one visible to a reader. Fabricated review markup breaches Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, is a consumer-protection exposure. A rating with no countable, attributable, dated reviews behind it should be treated as decoration when comparing prices.

Discount examiner claims that cannot be evidenced. Describing tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners, where current examiner status cannot be shown, is a claim rather than a credential, and using examiner status to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content is worse than useless. Similarly, any statistic quoted without a sample size, a date and a method is not a number you can price.

Finally, the permit, which is the one claim you can check and which is free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service with no fee and a stated two working days. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is unverified. A provider citing permit costs to justify a rate is citing a cost that does not exist.

sections.heading: Getting started on a plan rather than an hour
paragraphs: Send four things: the subject and level you are worried about, which internally assessed component is in progress, the school's internal deadline for it, and two evening windows that genuinely work from Al Jaddaf after the school run. We match a subject specialist and run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep. One trial per student, nothing charged beforehand, no card details needed to book it.

The tutor then writes a short note naming what they found and what they would do first. Judge the arrangement on that note rather than on the lesson, because a note that identifies content, timing or written method as the cause is the thing that makes the next two years affordable. A general note means nobody has diagnosed anything, and hours bought against a general note are hours spent finding out.

If no specialist is free in your window we say so, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing whoever is available. Scarcity concentrates in Higher Level mathematics and sciences and in the weeks when internal deadlines cluster across Dubai schools. Booking that window early costs the same and gets a better match, and in a two-year plan it is the single largest free improvement available.

Two limits stated plainly. Nobody can promise a grade or a point total, and this page does not. And nothing here implies that tutoring is required for the Diploma to be awarded, for university admission or for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency; those are institutional and regulatory processes with their own published rules, and the authority rather than a tutoring provider is where to verify them.

process.title: Ask the school for three free documents
process.description: The internal assessment calendar, the internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, and the school's policy on how predicted grades are formed. All three exist, all three are free, and together they tell you where spending does double duty.

process.title: Buy a diagnostic before buying hours
process.description: One timed paper on the exact subject and level, marked against the published scheme. It answers whether the problem is content, timing or written method, and those three have non-interchangeable solutions. Without it, the first month of any arrangement is paid exploration.

process.title: Protect the three core points first
process.description: An Extended Essay question answerable in 4,000 words, and a Theory of Knowledge prescribed title read as written. Two to three sessions and one to two sessions respectively, early, at the qualified tier. No subject on the board offers that ratio of points to hours.

process.title: Spend heaviest before the predictions
process.description: The first half of Year 13, around internal assessments and core deadlines, is where specialist rates are defensible, because the same work moves the final grade and the evidence from which predicted grades are produced. Most families under-buy here and over-buy later.

process.title: Book the final-term slot in the autumn
process.description: The price is identical and the match is better, because the specialist pool thins sharply when every Dubai cohort reaches the same point in the same fortnight. This is the only free improvement available in the whole process, and it requires a decision rather than money.

process.title: Review against a specific mark, then stop
process.description: At the school's next internal assessment, ask whether the targeted weakness moved and what evidence shows it. If nobody can point to a mark, the block ends rather than renewing. That discipline prevents most of the money wasted across a two-year Diploma.

whyPoints.title: We cost the two years, not the hour
whyPoints.description: The Diploma is a twenty-two-month purchase with a predictable spending pattern, and the expensive window has the lowest marginal return. Setting that out in advance is more useful to an Al Jaddaf family than any hourly rate, and it is the thing nobody in this market publishes.

whyPoints.title: We name where not to spend
whyPoints.description: Six parallel subject arrangements for one shared weakness. Premium rates for Standard Level content review. Heavy final-term buying after the predictions are issued. Saying so costs us revenue and is the only way the recommendations we do make carry weight.

whyPoints.title: The cheap points get protected first
whyPoints.description: Three core points sit on two documents that fail in predictable ways, and a handful of qualified-tier hours protects them. Command terms transfer across all six subjects from one session. Those are bought before any specialist rate is considered.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium, and no route constraint
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates run AED 180 to AED 500 per hour, partly to recover a tutor's time on the Creek-side roads. IB Gram makes no UAE home visits, so the premium does not exist and your match is not constrained by a visiting tutor's geography.

whyPoints.title: Figures that name their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED number here belongs to the provider that published it and carries the month it was read. Three of the strongest pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, a currency Dubai families do not transact in.

faqs.question: What does two years of IB tutoring actually cost a family in Al Jaddaf?
faqs.answer: Counted per subject per month against published bands: roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle band, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, on Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session. The total depends far more on how many subjects and which months than on the hourly rate. A plan spending unevenly, heaviest in the first half of Year 13, costs less and achieves more than a flat weekly arrangement across both years.

faqs.question: Why does spending before predicted grades matter more than spending before exams?
faqs.answer: Because predicted grades are produced by the school from the school's own evidence partway through Year 13, and university offers rest on them. The external examination comes afterwards. A plan peaking just before the session has arrived after the decision that determines where a student can apply. Money spent around internal assessments and core deadlines does double duty: it moves the final grade and the evidence base at the same time. Ask the school for its predicted-grade policy; it is free.

faqs.question: Which Diploma points are cheapest to protect with tutoring?
faqs.answer: The three core points, by a wide margin. The Extended Essay fails predictably on question scope, which is visible months in advance and fixable in two or three conversations. The Theory of Knowledge essay fails by answering an adjacent question rather than the prescribed title as written, which one session prevents. After those, command terms: the published glossary is tiered, a student describing when asked to evaluate is losing marks in all six subjects, and one session with three past questions fixes it everywhere.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are most expensive to get help with in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Higher Level mathematics, particularly Analysis and Approaches, and the Higher Level sciences. Two reasons compound. The specialist pool is thinnest there, so the rate reflects scarcity, and the components are technically demanding: Paper 3 plus the Exploration together carry forty per cent of an HL maths grade and Paper 3 cannot be revised by topic. Biology is usually the cheapest science to support because the content is wide rather than technically narrow, and Business Management is cheaper still.

faqs.question: Is it worth buying support in all six subjects at once?
faqs.answer: Almost never, and it is the most expensive mistake available. Several middling grades usually reflect a shared weakness rather than six subject gaps: command terms, timed-paper pace, written method for an unknown marker, or thin evaluation sections. Fixing a shared weakness once moves several subjects. Six parallel arrangements cost six times as much to achieve the same thing less well, and they also exhaust a student's evening capacity, which reduces what each session achieves.

faqs.question: Does a visiting tutor in Al Jaddaf cost much more than an online one?
faqs.answer: On published figures, yes: in-home one-to-one rates run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online. Part of the gap is a tutor's time on the roads around Dubai Healthcare City and the Creek crossings at the school-run hour. IB Gram does not visit UAE addresses at all; tuition for UAE families is one-to-one online on Gulf Standard Time, and home visiting is an India-only service.

faqs.question: How early should I book a tutor for the final term before the exams?
faqs.answer: In the autumn, even though the sessions will not be used until the spring. The price is the same and the match is better, because every Dubai cohort reaches the revision window in the same fortnight and the specialist pool thins sharply. This is the only free improvement available in a two-year plan: it costs a decision rather than money. Families who wait until the pressure is visible pay the same rate for whoever remains available, which is not the same purchase.

faqs.question: Is the premium tier at AED 650 an hour ever worth it?
faqs.answer: In narrow cases. BartyED publishes AED 650 and specialist bands run from AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Those rates are defensible for Higher Level mathematics Paper 3, for a scarce subject combination, or for a technically demanding internal assessment where experience of what moves marks quickly has real value. They are not defensible for Standard Level content review, where a qualified tutor at AED 150 to AED 300 does the identical job, and across a year the difference is substantial.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's IB school for before spending anything?
faqs.answer: Three documents, all free and all held by the school. The internal assessment calendar, showing when each subject's component is due. The internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. And the school's policy on how predicted grades are formed. Together they tell you which months matter, which is the information that makes an uneven spending plan possible. Without them, a family anchors its plan to the external session date, which is the wrong anchor.

faqs.question: Why does this page not list the IB exam or results dates?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified from the IB itself, whose website blocks automated checking. No IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and an unverified date is something a family would plan both a term of revision and a budget around. UAE schools sit the main May session. Your school's IB coordinator holds the authoritative calendar, and the internal deadlines they also hold matter more to a tutoring plan than the external dates do.

faqs.question: Does Al Jaddaf's location make tutoring cheaper in practice?
faqs.answer: In real terms, yes, and the mechanism is session timing rather than price. The district is compact and minutes from the Creek crossings, so a student at a school inside Al Jaddaf or across in Dubai Festival City is often home for a 16:30 start. The real unit price of an hour is the rate divided by the usable fraction of it, and that fraction falls as the evening goes on. Mathematics and the sciences lose more to fatigue than reading subjects do, so an earlier slot is worth money.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary we state before starting. A tutor may help narrow a research question so it can be answered in 4,000 words, explain what a criterion rewards, ask questions that expose a weak argument, and comment on the student's own draft. A tutor may not produce the essay, restructure it to a standard, or supply the argument. The school supervisor remains the supervisor. Providers in this market sell completed assessments outright, and the malpractice consequence falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Should I trust a tutoring company's star rating when comparing cost?
faqs.answer: Only where the reviews are countable, attributable and dated. Competitors in this market publish ratings that contradict each other on the same page, and one shows a figure in its structured data that differs from what a reader sees. Fabricated review markup breaches Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, is a consumer-protection exposure. Treat an unevidenced rating as decoration. The same applies to any statistic quoted without a sample size, a date and a method behind it.

faqs.question: Does the UAE tutoring permit add cost that explains a higher rate?
faqs.answer: No. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A provider citing permit costs to justify a rate is citing a cost that does not exist. No fine schedule is published, so any quoted fine is unverified.

faqs.question: How do I know when to stop paying for tutoring?
faqs.answer: At the school's next internal assessment, ask whether the targeted weakness moved and what evidence shows it. If the tutor can name the weakness and point to a mark that shifted, continue while there is more to gain. If the answer is improved confidence with no measurable change, the block ends rather than renewing, because hours bought against an undiagnosed problem do not become effective with repetition. One timed paper marked to the published scheme, before and after, is the cheapest evaluation available.

intro.heading: The Diploma does not fail on knowledge, it fails on hours
paragraphs: Ask a Year 13 student in Al Khail Gate what went wrong in a subject and the honest answer is usually arithmetic rather than comprehension. Six subjects each setting work, three core components with their own deadlines, CAS requiring documented activity, the Arabic and Islamic Education lessons Dubai schools must deliver, and an hour or more a day in a bus along the Al Khail corridor. The hours do not add up, and the subject that loses is whichever one had no deadline that week.

That is why a near-me search is the wrong first move. The constraint on a Diploma student in this community is not the absence of a tutor within driving distance; it is that the available study hours are already committed and badly allocated. A tutor who adds one more fixed appointment to a saturated week without changing anything else has made the problem marginally worse at a cost.

The productive first step is a genuine audit of the week. Not the timetable the school publishes, which shows lessons, but the hours that actually remain after the commute, the mandatory subjects, CAS, sport, prayer, family commitments and sleep. Most Diploma students in Dubai have between eight and fifteen usable study hours a week outside school, which is considerably fewer than the twenty-five their revision plan assumes, and the plan therefore fails in week three every single time.

The second step is to know which weeks are impossible before they arrive. Diploma deadlines cluster, and the worst cluster in the programme sits in the autumn of Year 13, when internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay final submission in many schools, mock preparation and university application deadlines all land inside ten weeks. A family that maps those ten weeks in September has options. A family that meets them in November has none.

The third is predicted grades, which almost nobody plans for and which decide which offers a student can even hold. Predictions are produced by teachers from the evidence in front of them, principally mock performance and completed internal assessment, at a point in the autumn of Year 13. Work done after the prediction is submitted improves the final grade and not the offer, which means the timing of improvement matters as much as its size.

So this page is about the week and the term. What a realistic Diploma week contains, where the autumn crunch sits, how predictions are formed, what mocks mean, and how to buy eight weeks of support that lands at the point where it changes something. The near-me question gets answered too, with the published rates, but it is the least important question on the list. Everything in it can be done by a family in one evening with a pen and the school portal, before a single dirham changes hands, and that evening is worth more than the first month of sessions.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-khail-gate.programmesIntro: The weekly load differs by stage, so it is worth being specific about which year a family is planning.

programmes.name: Diploma year one
programmes.description: Six subjects begin together, the core starts, and the workload rises sharply from IGCSE or MYP. The year's real output is decisions: levels confirmed, the Extended Essay question set, internal assessment topics chosen, and a sustainable weekly routine established or not established.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students carry Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the Diploma because KHDA requires them of every private school regardless of curriculum. That makes a Dubai Diploma week fuller than the programme outline suggests and makes the routine question more urgent here than in most countries.

programmes.name: Diploma year two
programmes.description: The year of collisions. Internal assessments complete, the Extended Essay is submitted in most schools, mocks sit in the winter, predicted grades are produced, university applications close, and the paper phase occupies the final term. Nothing new is added; everything outstanding arrives at once.
programmes.countryNote: University application deadlines are set overseas and ignore the Dubai school calendar entirely, so the autumn crunch is structural rather than a local scheduling failure. Families who know the dates in September can move drafts forward by agreement; those who do not meet all of it simultaneously.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The feeder programme, assessed on four criteria per subject rather than papers. Students arriving from MYP have documented process habits and little practice writing to a clock, which shows in Diploma term one as a timing problem rather than a knowledge one.
programmes.countryNote: In the Dubailand belt most schools run IGCSE rather than MYP, so a Diploma cohort here typically mixes both entry routes. The two profiles need different first-term support, and naming which one a student has saves a term of generic help.

programmes.name: IGCSE as the entry route
programmes.description: The commonest feeder in Dubai. Strong examination technique, weaker independent research habits, and a tier dependency: Core or Foundation entries omit content that Higher Level Diploma courses assume as prior knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE in the June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with its November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-khail-gate.subjectsIntro: These subjects are described by the weekly demand they place on a student rather than by syllabus content, because weekly demand is what a Diploma plan has to budget for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The highest steady weekly demand of any Diploma subject, because fluency decays without practice. Twenty minutes four times a week beats two hours on a Sunday, and students who treat it as a revision subject rather than a practice subject fall behind invisibly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Lower algebraic maintenance demand but heavier on tool fluency and statistical interpretation, which means shorter but more frequent work with the permitted calculator rather than long written sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Lumpy demand: steady low-level content work punctuated by the investigation, which consumes whole weekends if left late. Scheduling the investigation's data collection away from a mock fortnight is worth more than any study technique.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Demands maintained algebra more than memorised content, so it competes directly with mathematics for the same kind of weekly slot. Students taking both Higher Level often under-budget for this overlap.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The largest content volume in most students' timetables, which makes it the subject most often postponed. Little and often works; a single long session a week does not, because retention is the whole problem.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Commentary deadlines arrive three times across the course and each one swallows a weekend. The articles should be collected gradually rather than hunted the week before, which is a five-minute weekly habit that saves several hours.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Reading has to happen outside the timetable, which means it competes with everything else and usually loses. Setting a fixed reading slot that is not negotiable is more useful than any essay-writing advice.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Low weekly demand and two hard deadlines, which is precisely the profile of work that gets forgotten. The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay both reward early title selection and almost nothing else done late.

subjects.name: CAS
subjects.description: A completion requirement with real weekly time cost and documented evidence. Students who leave the reflections uncompleted create an administrative crisis in Year 13 for work they have genuinely already done, which is the most avoidable problem in the programme.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-khail-gate.regionsIntro: Al Khail Gate students commute in several directions, and the direction determines how many usable evening hours a week actually exist. These notes describe that rather than listing amenities.

regions.name: Al Khail Gate
regions.note: Dense apartment living beside the Al Khail Road interchange with no Diploma school nearby. The usable weekday evening starts whenever the bus arrives, which varies by school rather than by address.

regions.name: Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: The closest school cluster, slow at peak but short. Students here keep one or two more usable weekday hours a week than those travelling further, which is enough to matter over a term.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Shorter run than Al Barsha South, which makes it a common move within the belt. The commute cost is almost entirely interchange traffic rather than distance.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Arabian Ranches 2

sections.heading: What a near-me search can and cannot get you
paragraphs: A proximity search for Diploma support in Al Khail Gate returns a short list, and the shortness has a cause worth understanding. International Baccalaureate students are a minority of Dubai's private-school population, around seven per cent against thirty-seven per cent on UK curricula, and Diploma teaching experience is concentrated among people who work in the handful of schools that offer it. The chance that the person who best understands Economics Higher Level commentary marking lives a few minutes from this community is low, and it is low in every community.

What proximity can genuinely offer is presence and reliability of a particular kind: somebody at the table, a parent in earshot, and a student who cannot quietly not log in. For a household where the real problem is that nothing happens without supervision, that is worth paying for, and the published Dubai in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included is the benchmark for what it costs.

What proximity cannot offer is selection. A Diploma subject at a named level is a narrow specialism, and in a programme where the margin between a 5 and a 6 often lies in knowing how a particular component is marked, the pool matters more than the postcode. Nor can it offer flexibility: a tutor crossing the Al Khail interchange at five in the afternoon can usually hold one window per evening, and in the autumn of Year 13 the useful session is frequently the one that has to move.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Khail Gate or anywhere else in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time. The reframe this page recommends is to stop searching by distance and start by auditing the week, because that is where the recoverable loss actually sits.

sections.heading: The Diploma week audited honestly
paragraphs: Start with the hours that are not negotiable. School, including the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons KHDA requires of all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. The commute, which for students travelling from Al Khail Gate towards Al Barsha South or Nad Al Sheba in term-time traffic is substantial in both directions. Sleep, at a quantity a seventeen-year-old actually needs rather than the quantity they claim to manage on.

Then subtract the semi-fixed commitments. CAS activity, which is a completion requirement and a real weekly time cost. Sport or music, often several hours and frequently the thing a family is most reluctant to cut, usually correctly. Prayer times, family obligations, and the weekend day that is genuinely not available. What remains in most cases is eight to fifteen usable study hours a week, and the number is worth calculating rather than estimating because the estimate is always generous.

Against that, count what the six subjects and the core are asking for. Mathematics needs frequent short practice because fluency decays. English needs reading time that competes with everything. Biology needs little and often because retention is the issue. Each internal assessment needs a block of hours at some point. Theory of Knowledge needs almost nothing weekly and two hard deadlines. Put those demands against eight to fifteen hours and the overcommitment becomes visible immediately.

The audit is useful because it changes the conversation from effort to allocation. A student working fifteen hard hours a week badly allocated will be beaten by one working twelve well allocated, and telling the first student to work harder is both unkind and ineffective. The output of the audit should be a written weekly pattern with named slots for named subjects, and an explicit decision about what is not going to be done.

sections.heading: The autumn of Year 13: ten weeks that decide the offers
paragraphs: The hardest stretch of the Diploma is not the examination term. It is the autumn of Year 13, when several things that were scheduled independently arrive together. Internal assessment deadlines fall across the autumn in most schools. The Extended Essay reaches final submission. Mock preparation begins. University applications close, on deadlines set overseas that take no account of the Dubai school calendar. And predicted grades are produced in the middle of it.

Those pressures interact badly. A student spending a weekend on a personal statement is not writing the chemistry investigation due on Monday. A student finishing an internal assessment at two in the morning is not performing in a mock the following week. And because predictions are formed from mock performance and completed coursework, a bad autumn produces predictions that limit which offers can be held, regardless of how strong the final results turn out to be.

The response is sequencing, and it has to happen in September. Put every deadline on one page: each internal assessment, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge dates, the mock window, and every application deadline for every country being applied to. The collisions become visible immediately, and most schools will agree to move a draft deadline forward by a fortnight if asked in September with a reason. Almost none will move one in November.

The second part of the response is to protect the mock window specifically. Mocks are not just practice; they are the primary evidence for predicted grades. Treating them as a dress rehearsal that can be sacrificed to a coursework deadline is the single most expensive trade a Year 13 student makes, because the coursework can be finished a week late with a small penalty and the prediction cannot be revisited.

sections.heading: Predicted grades: how they are formed and what actually moves them
paragraphs: Predicted grades decide which university offers a student can hold, and most families understand them vaguely. They are produced by subject teachers from the evidence available at the time: mock performance, completed or near-complete internal assessment, classwork and timed assessments across the course. They are professional judgements, not guesses, and they are submitted at a point in the autumn of Year 13 after which they are difficult to change.

The practical consequence is a timing asymmetry that students rarely grasp. Improvement before the prediction is formed changes which offers are available. Identical improvement afterwards changes the final grade and nothing about the offer. A student who finds another level of performance in February has earned a better result and not a better place, which is a real outcome and a frustrating one.

What moves a prediction is evidence a teacher can point to, which means timed work rather than effort. A student who revises conscientiously and scores the same in two mocks has given a teacher nothing to revise a prediction with. A student who sits a mock better than their previous timed work, with a completed internal assessment at a good standard, has given them two concrete reasons. That is why a block of support timed at the mock rather than after it is worth disproportionately more.

Two honest caveats. Teachers are usually accurate, and a prediction that feels low is often a fair reading of the evidence, in which case the useful response is to produce better evidence rather than to dispute the judgement. And nobody, tutor or teacher, can promise a grade or a prediction; a provider implying otherwise is making a claim it cannot support.
