sections.heading: The eight-week block as the unit of planning
paragraphs: Open-ended weekly tutoring is the default in this market and it has a structural flaw: nobody ever evaluates it, because continuing requires no decision while stopping does. Families end up eighteen months into an arrangement they would not have chosen deliberately, and the review that never happened is the reason the complaint about tutoring not working is so common.

An eight-week block fixes that with a date. It starts, it has one named target expressed in marks or in a deadline met, and it ends. At the end, the family and the tutor compare the evidence with the target and decide to renew with a new target or to stop. That conversation is occasionally awkward and always more useful than drifting, and it is the single easiest change a household can make to how it buys support.

Eight weeks is also the natural length for Diploma work. It is long enough to change a technique and see it in a timed assessment, long enough to take an internal assessment from design to a solid draft, and short enough to be scheduled around a known collision. It is not long enough to close a two-year content gap, and a provider should say so at the start rather than at the review.

The scheduling matters as much as the length. A block aimed at a mock should end a week before the mock, not during it. A block aimed at an internal assessment should end at the draft deadline, not the final one. A block aimed at paper technique belongs in the final term. Lining the end of the block up with the thing it is meant to affect is what makes the same eight hours produce a different result.

sections.heading: CAS, co-curricular commitments and the hours nobody counts
paragraphs: CAS is a Diploma requirement rather than a graded component, and it is where families most often misread the cost. It requires sustained activity across both years with documented reflection, and while the activity itself is usually something the student would do anyway, the documentation is not. Students who leave reflections uncompleted create an administrative emergency in Year 13 over work they genuinely did, which is the most avoidable crisis in the programme and a surprisingly common one.

The fix is a weekly habit measured in minutes. A short reflection written at the time, while the detail is fresh, is both better evidence and faster to produce than a reconstruction months later. Twenty minutes a fortnight across two years is a fraction of the time a Year 13 panic costs, and it removes a whole category of stress from the autumn crunch.

Co-curricular commitments are different and should usually be protected rather than cut. A student who drops the sport they love to study more frequently studies worse, not better, and in this community the sports facilities around Dubai Sports City and the Ranches mean many students have serious commitments. The honest conversation is about which commitment to reduce in a specific heavy fortnight, not about abandoning the thing that keeps a seventeen-year-old functional.

What should be cut, where something has to be, is usually the least examined: time spent reorganising notes, making revision resources, and rereading material already understood. Those feel like work and produce little. Trading two hours of note-beautification for one hour of timed paper practice is the most reliable efficiency available in a saturated week.

sections.heading: What a term of Diploma support costs at published Dubai rates
paragraphs: Budget by block rather than by hour, because a block is what gets bought. Eight one-hour sessions is the unit. At published Dubai market rates that puts a block somewhere between a few hundred and a few thousand dirhams depending on the band, and the band should be chosen on how specific the need is rather than on what feels appropriate.

The published figures: Tutopiya advertises online tutoring from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists around AED 270, Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED charges AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one is published at AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Monthly packages in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. All of those are the providers' own published figures rather than ours.

The useful rule for a Diploma family is that the specialist band is worth paying for when the need is component-specific, and is not worth paying for general content help. If a student needs the HL extension topics in physics taught, a competent graduate can do it. If a student needs to know why an Economics commentary scored in the middle band, that requires somebody who marks against that criterion regularly, and the band reflects it.

Context worth having: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a household already carrying Dubai fees, a flat year is the practical window in which two or three planned blocks across a Diploma year becomes a decision rather than an improvisation.

sections.heading: Honesty boundaries, claims and the exam calendar
paragraphs: Most Diploma assessed work is written at home, which makes the academic-honesty line a weekly practical question. A tutor can teach the subject, question a methodology, explain a published criterion, ask what evidence supports a claim and give feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor cannot write any part of it, do the analysis for it, edit it to completion or supply a model for submission. Operations advertising completed Internal Assessments for sale exist in the Gulf market, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

On what we claim: IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no UAE office, centre or branch. Individual tutoring in the UAE is regulated by the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, which a parent may reasonably ask any individual tutor about. We publish no statistics about our own outcomes, because we cannot produce the underlying data.

On dates: we do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no IB session date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family plans around has to be right. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session; confirm the window and results dates with the school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org.

Where dates can be stated, they come from the boards themselves. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE centres, with the February/March series offered to India only, and allocates centres to one of six administrative zones each with its own timetable. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

faqs.question: How many study hours a week does a Dubai Diploma student really have?
faqs.answer: Usually eight to fifteen outside school, which is far fewer than most revision plans assume. The subtractions are school including the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons KHDA requires of all Dubai private schools, the commute, sleep at the quantity a seventeen-year-old actually needs, CAS activity and documentation, and co-curricular commitments. Counting the real number rather than estimating it is worth doing on paper, because the estimate is always generous and a plan built on twenty-five hours collapses in week three.

faqs.question: Why is the autumn of Year 13 harder than the exam term?
faqs.answer: Because several independently scheduled pressures arrive together. Internal assessment deadlines fall across the autumn, the Extended Essay reaches final submission in most schools, mock preparation begins, predicted grades are formed, and university application deadlines set overseas close without regard to the Dubai calendar. Each is manageable alone; together they are not. Mapping all of them onto one page in September makes the collisions visible, and most schools will move a draft deadline forward if asked then rather than in November.

faqs.question: How are IB predicted grades decided?
faqs.answer: By subject teachers, from the evidence available in the autumn of Year 13: mock performance, completed or near-complete internal assessment, classwork and timed assessments across the course. They are professional judgements rather than guesses, and they are difficult to change once submitted. The important consequence is a timing asymmetry: improvement before the prediction changes which offers a student can hold, while identical improvement afterwards changes only the final grade. Nobody, tutor or teacher, can promise a particular prediction.

faqs.question: Should we protect the mocks or the coursework deadline when they clash?
faqs.answer: The mocks, almost always. Coursework handed in a week late usually carries a small internal penalty and can still be good work. A mock sat badly because a student was awake at two in the morning finishing an investigation feeds directly into predicted grades, and a prediction cannot be revisited. That trade is the most expensive one a Year 13 student makes, and it is avoidable by asking in September for a draft deadline to be moved rather than discovering the clash in the week it happens.

faqs.question: Does it matter that a Diploma tutor is not based in Al Khail Gate?
faqs.answer: For selection, no; for supervision, sometimes. International Baccalaureate students are around seven per cent of Dubai's private-school population, and Diploma teaching experience concentrates among those working in the few schools offering it, so a local search returns a short list in any community. What proximity genuinely buys is a person at the table, which matters for a student who will not work unsupervised. What it cannot buy is a specialist in the specific component that is losing marks, or a session that can move during the autumn crunch.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send someone to our home in the Dubailand belt?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Khail Gate, Motor City, Arabian Ranches or anywhere else in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time. The published Dubai in-home band is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 online, and that is the benchmark if in-home is what your household needs.

faqs.question: Is an eight-week block better than ongoing weekly tutoring?
faqs.answer: Usually, because it gets reviewed. An open arrangement is never evaluated, since continuing requires no decision while stopping does, and families end up eighteen months into something they would not have chosen deliberately. A block with one named target and an expiry date forces a comparison against evidence. Eight weeks is also the natural Diploma length: long enough to change a technique and see it in a timed assessment, short enough to be scheduled around a known collision week.

faqs.question: How should the block be timed relative to a mock?
faqs.answer: It should end about a week before the mock, not during it or after it. A block that finishes in the mock week leaves no room to consolidate, and one that starts after the mock has missed the evidence window that feeds predicted grades. The same logic applies to coursework: a block aimed at an internal assessment should end at the draft deadline rather than the final one, so there is time to act on the feedback the draft generates.

faqs.question: What does CAS actually cost in time?
faqs.answer: The activity is usually something the student would do anyway; the documentation is not. CAS requires sustained activity across both years with reflections, and students who leave the reflections uncompleted create an administrative emergency in Year 13 over work they genuinely did. Twenty minutes a fortnight written at the time, while the detail is fresh, is both better evidence and much faster than a reconstruction months later, and it removes a whole category of stress from the autumn.

faqs.question: Should my son drop football to study more for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Students who drop the thing that keeps them functioning tend to study worse rather than more, and in this part of Dubai, with the facilities around Dubai Sports City and the Ranches, many students have serious commitments that are genuinely good for them. The more productive cut is the least examined work: reorganising notes, building revision resources and rereading material already understood. Trading two hours of that for one timed paper is the most reliable efficiency available in a full week.

faqs.question: What does a term of IB tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Think in eight-session blocks. At published rates that is roughly AED 264 to 520 at the budget end, where Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400 for a qualified online tutor, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; and roughly AED 1,600 to 3,600 or more at specialist rates, where Bestimate's band is AED 200 to 450 and above and TutorChase lists around AED 270. The specialist band is worth paying for component-specific marking knowledge, not for general content help.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my daughter finish an internal assessment that is overdue?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help her finish it; a tutor cannot finish it for her. That means teaching the subject content she needs, questioning whether the methodology supports her conclusions, explaining what each published criterion rewards, asking what evidence backs a claim, and giving feedback on what she has written. It does not mean writing sections, doing the analysis, editing to completion or supplying a model. Providers selling completed Internal Assessments exist in this market, and the malpractice consequence lands on the student.

faqs.question: When does my child actually sit the IB exams?
faqs.answer: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and we deliberately publish no specific examination or results dates here. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family plans around has to be right. Confirm the window and the results date with the school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge qualifications sat alongside, UAE centres sit the June and November series and must use the correct zone timetable.

faqs.question: My child understands the subject but the marks stay flat. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Most often one of three things, and all are diagnosable from timed work. Command terms: an answer written at the wrong level, explaining where the question said evaluate, is capped regardless of knowledge. Allocation: minutes spent evenly across questions worth different marks, so the heavily weighted questions are rushed. Or component blindness: effort going into a component carrying a small published share while a heavily weighted paper goes unpractised. None of those is fixed by more revision, which is usually what gets tried first.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free at the only time we can manage?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than filling the slot with whoever is available. Diploma specialisms are narrow and demand across the city peaks in the same weeks, so a particular subject at a particular level at a particular hour does occasionally come up empty. The honest options are a different time, a different tutor with a handover of the component plan, or a wait with a date attached. A mismatched tutor in a Diploma subject costs a term, and in Year 13 there is no spare term.

intro.heading: What families around here actually pay, and what they get for it
paragraphs: Nobody searching for a tutor near Al Khawaneej is only asking about geography. Underneath the search there are three money questions. Is this going to cost two hundred dirhams an hour or six hundred. Is the cheap option a bargain or a waste. And how do I tell, before paying for three months, whether this particular hour is worth it. Those are reasonable questions and this market answers them badly: of six competitor pages examined for this project, three publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family pays in.

So here is the position, published. Dubai tutoring rates span from around AED 33 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for premium named teaching, and almost every point in that range is occupied by somebody. The span is not a quality ladder with a single rung for each price. It is several different products: company while homework gets done, a qualified teacher who knows the course, a specialist who can diagnose a component, and a scarce named individual booked for a final stretch. A family that buys the wrong product at the right price has still wasted the money.

The second thing worth saying early is that the commonest waste in this catchment is not overpaying per hour. It is buying hours the week cannot absorb. An Al Khawaneej Diploma student travels out of the community to school, arrives home late and has perhaps ninety usable minutes on a weekday evening. A family that commits to three weekly sessions has bought something that will be attended twice and then quietly abandoned, and the money is gone whether the sessions happened or not.

The third is about what the in-home premium actually purchases. Published in-home rates run above online rates for teaching of comparable quality, and the market's own monthly packages make the gap explicit. The difference is a drive to the eastern edge of Dubai and back. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For UAE families the teaching happens one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which puts the whole of the fee into the teaching rather than into travel.

What follows is the detail: the bands read from cheapest upwards, what each one is genuinely capable of, the five specific ways money leaks away in this catchment, tutoring costs set against the school fees they sit beside, the extras to ask about before paying, and the evidence to demand at four sessions before committing to a term. Read it even if you decide against us; the arithmetic works the same either way.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-khawaneej.programmesIntro: The price question has a different answer for each IB programme, because the scarcity of specialists differs. These are the three as Al Khawaneej families meet them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus three core elements. This is where the market's highest prices sit, because Higher Level specialists in the scarcer subjects are genuinely few and the stakes are university entry. It is also where the budget bands are least useful, since the gains come from component-level diagnosis rather than from company while working.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate programmes held seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, and Dubai's latest intake added three new International Baccalaureate schools among seven new private schools creating 16,846 places. Supply is rising faster than the specialist tutoring pool is.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed by summative tasks against four criteria rather than by terminal papers. Prices sit lower than Diploma rates because the specialist scarcity is less acute, and the budget and mid bands are more genuinely useful here, particularly for habit-building rather than content rescue.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary years with no terminal assessment. Support here is about numeracy, reading fluency and written explanation, and it is the one stage where the budget band represents honest value, because what a young child often needs is structured attention rather than subject expertise.
programmes.countryNote: Primary provision sits closer to home in this part of Dubai than secondary provision, including a Dubai Schools campus at Al Khawaneej, so younger children finish earlier and are less tired. dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-khawaneej.subjectsIntro: Prices vary by subject more than most families expect, and the reason is supply. These are the Diploma subjects Al Khawaneej families ask about, with a note on where each sits in the market.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested Diploma subject in this catchment and therefore one of the better supplied. Higher Level still commands the specialist band, because the calculus and proof content thins the pool of people who can teach it confidently.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Better supplied than Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level, with rates nearer the qualified-tutor band. The statistics and modelling content is taught competently by a wider range of teachers, which shows up in the price.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Among the scarcest at Higher Level, with a typical school running one or two qualified staff. Expect the specialist band, and expect availability rather than price to be the binding constraint in some weeks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Similar scarcity to Physics at Higher Level. The qualified band can cover Standard Level content well; the specialist band is what buys component-level diagnosis on calculation and organic reasoning.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Better supplied than the other two sciences. Much of the work is recall discipline and command-term precision, which a strong qualified tutor delivers effectively without specialist pricing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Moderately supplied. Evaluation marks are the differentiator and they need a tutor who argues well in writing, which is a skill worth paying the qualified or specialist band for rather than the budget one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Reasonably supplied, with the internal assessment the main reason families seek help. Coaching on process and criteria is where the value sits; drafting support is not something any band should be buying.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Well supplied overall but variable in quality, because the subject looks approachable and is not. Oral assessment preparation is the most under-bought part of it and the cheapest to fix early.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Thinly supplied, because few tutors teach it as their own subject. Where a family needs it, expect to pay for scarcity rather than for difficulty, and expect the work to be about argument structure.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Supervision sits with the school; external coaching covers scoping, planning and feedback on the student's own drafts. Short and early is far better value than long and late, and no band should be paying for writing.

sections.heading: The dirham bands, read from the cheapest upwards
paragraphs: Reading a rate card from the top down makes everything look expensive. Reading it from the bottom up makes the question clearer, which is what each additional hundred dirhams actually buys. At the bottom sit Tutopiya, publishing online tuition from around AED 33 to 52 an hour, and EdFlik, from around AED 45 to 65. Both lean on university students, many of them studying out at Academic City. For a Middle Years student who needs structure and company while working, that is honest value and nobody should apologise for buying it.

The next step up is the largest in effect and not the largest in price. Unitors publishes from AED 150 an hour for IGCSE tuition and from AED 200 for IB, and TutorChase quotes around AED 270. What that step buys is somebody who knows the course and can mark a script against the scheme. The difference between being told an answer is wrong and being told which criterion the answer failed is the difference between an hour that feels useful and an hour that moves a mark.

Above that, Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home visits at roughly AED 180 to 350, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named teaching. Monthly packages in circulation run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Every figure here is provider-published and was read in October 2026; none of them is an IB Gram price, and for our own arrangement the starting point is a free trial lesson and a consultation.

sections.heading: The five places the money actually leaks
paragraphs: Overpaying per hour is not the main way families in this catchment lose money on tutoring. There are five specific leaks, and all of them are avoidable with a decision taken before any payment rather than after three months of drift. Each one is worth more than the difference between two adjacent price bands.

The first is buying hours the week cannot absorb. Three weekly sessions for a student with a ninety-minute usable weekday window is a purchase of something that will be attended twice. The second is paying for travel rather than teaching, which the market itself prices at roughly double for the same quantity of hours. The third is a group class sold in language that sounds individual: ask for the ratio in writing, because a class of eight at a per-head rate is not one-to-one tuition however it is described. The fourth is starting too late, where the same money buys triage instead of repair. The fifth, and the most common, is buying teaching before buying a diagnosis, so that the first eight sessions address the wrong problem.

The fifth leak deserves emphasis because it is the cheapest to plug. A parent reports a subject; a marked script and one hour frequently show something narrower, such as algebra inside physics, or an inability to start a question unaided, or marks lost to command terms across every subject. Four to six sessions bought explicitly as an investigation, with a written list at the end, costs less than a month of weekly teaching aimed at the wrong target. Almost nobody buys it, and almost everybody should.

sections.heading: Tutoring set against the fees it sits beside
paragraphs: A tutoring figure quoted alone is hard to judge. Quoted next to the school fees a family already pays, it becomes a proportion, and proportions are easier to decide about. This is context no competitor page in the fees cluster provides, and it is the single most useful framing available to a parent weighing a decision in Dubai.

There is a specific reason this year's arithmetic is more favourable than usual. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a household that had budgeted an annual fee rise and did not get one, there is room in the education line that was not there last year. Dubai's private sector taught 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, so this is not a marginal policy.

The table puts the numbers side by side. The point of it is not to argue that tutoring is cheap; it is to make the comparison that families make in their heads explicit, and to show that the sensible question is not whether to spend but what the spending is for. One subject taught well by a specialist for a term is a different purchase from four subjects covered thinly for a year, and the second is usually the more expensive of the two.

sections.heading: What each band is genuinely capable of for a Diploma student
paragraphs: Price bands are products, and matching the product to the problem is where value is won or lost. The budget band buys attention and structure. For a student who can do the work but does not start it, that is exactly the right purchase, and paying four times as much would buy nothing extra. For a Higher Level candidate losing marks to a specific component, it buys an hour of encouragement.

The qualified band buys course knowledge and the ability to mark against a scheme. This is the right purchase for most Diploma students most of the time, and the band most often skipped by families who jump from the cheapest option straight to a specialist in a panic. A qualified tutor who knows the course will find a command-term problem or a rearrangement problem in one session, which is most of what a family actually needs.

The specialist band buys diagnosis at the component level and the ability to triage under time pressure. That is worth paying for in two situations: a scarce Higher Level subject where the content genuinely requires it, and the weeks before a session when the right three fixes have to be found quickly. The premium named band buys scarcity, and it makes sense as a short block rather than a course. Buying it for two years is buying a scarce commodity you do not need every week. Matching the band to the problem, rather than to the anxiety, is most of what good value looks like here.

Qualified band: course knowledge and mark-scheme literacy, the common need

sections.heading: The extras to ask about before anything is paid
paragraphs: A quoted hourly rate is not the price. Four questions asked before payment prevent most of the disputes families report in this market, and all four should be answerable in writing without hesitation.

Is the figure per hour or per session, and how long is a session? A sixty-minute hour and a forty-five minute session at the same price differ by a quarter. What is the cancellation and rescheduling policy, including how much notice is required and what happens when a child is unwell or a bus is late? For a family with a long school run this is not a technicality; it determines whether the arrangement survives a difficult term. Does the quoted figure include value added tax, and if tax treatment is uncertain, is the figure quoted as inclusive or exclusive? A provider should be able to state what their own price includes without reference to anybody's interpretation of the law.

And what happens if the match is wrong? A provider who treats a tutor change as a complaint has the wrong model; it should be a routine request, handled in a week, because a mismatch identified early costs nothing and a mismatch tolerated for a term costs the term. One further point: the private tuition work permit in the UAE is issued free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, so any line item described as a licensing or registration fee deserves a direct question about what it actually covers.
bullets: Per hour or per session, and how many minutes is a session
Cancellation terms, notice required, and what a late bus means
Whether tax is included in the quoted figure
How a tutor change is handled, and how quickly

sections.heading: The evidence to demand at four sessions
paragraphs: Value in tutoring is not measurable at session one and it is measurable at session four, which is why four sessions is the right unit to buy and judge. What should exist by then is a marked piece of work showing movement on the specific thing that was targeted. Not a happier child, although that often happens too. A marked script with fewer marks lost to the named cause.

If the agreed target was command terms, there should be fewer explain questions answered descriptively. If it was unit discipline in physics, there should be fewer bare numbers. If it was mole conversions, there should be a calculation question set up correctly without prompting. The reason to agree the target in writing at session one is precisely so that this check is possible later, and the reason most families cannot perform it is that no target was ever named.

When the evidence is not there, the correct response is to change the method or the tutor, not to add hours. Adding hours to an arrangement that has not produced movement is the single most expensive decision available in this market, and it is the one providers are least likely to discourage. A provider who tells you to pause and reconsider at session four is worth more than one who tells you to double up, and that is a reasonable thing to say out loud on a page like this one. Say it to any provider you are considering and listen carefully to the answer.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we will tell you before you pay
paragraphs: Begin with a short consultation about the actual problem rather than the subject, and send two things: the most recent marked piece of work with the teacher's comments intact, and the measured time your child is genuinely able to work on a weekday. The second matters as much as the first, because a slot outside the real window is money spent on sessions nobody attends.

Then a free trial lesson, one-to-one over live video, before any commitment. Use it as a diagnostic: ask the tutor to work through the marked script and name where the marks went and what the first block will target. If the answer is specific, book four sessions and judge them on evidence. If the hour was spent describing an approach, you have learned something useful about the provider rather than about your child.

Two disclosures before money changes hands. There is no IB Gram rate card published on this page, because the honest answer depends on the subject, the level and the scarcity, and a figure invented for a page is worse than no figure; the consultation and the trial are where that conversation belongs. And specialist coverage has limits: in some weeks no UAE-based specialist in a scarce Higher Level subject holds an evening slot that fits an Al Khawaneej timetable. Where that is the case you will be told, and offered a specialist based elsewhere teaching over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time, rather than a general tutor presented as a specialist.

process.title: Count the hours before pricing anything
process.description: Usable weekday evenings, minus homework, gives the number of tutored hours the week can genuinely absorb. For most Al Khawaneej Diploma students that number is one. Buying three is the commonest and largest waste in this market, and it happens before any rate is negotiated.

process.title: Buy a diagnosis first
process.description: Four to six sessions bought explicitly as an investigation, ending in a written list of loss causes and a recommendation that includes stopping. It costs less than a month of weekly teaching aimed at the wrong target, and almost nobody buys it.

process.title: Agree the target in writing
process.description: Name the specific thing the block is meant to change: command terms, unit discipline, mole conversions, question starting. Without a named target at session one, there is no way to judge value at session four, which is how arrangements drift for a term.

process.title: Ask the four extras questions
process.description: Per hour or per session and how many minutes. Cancellation and rescheduling terms. Whether tax is included. How a tutor change is handled and how fast. All four should be answerable in writing without hesitation before any payment.

process.title: Judge at four sessions on a marked script
process.description: Fewer marks lost to the named cause, on paper. If the evidence is absent, change the method or the tutor rather than adding hours, which is the most expensive response available and the one least likely to be discouraged.

whyPoints.title: The waste named, not just the rates
whyPoints.description: Five specific leaks are set out, each worth more than the gap between two adjacent price bands. The largest of them, buying hours the week cannot absorb, happens before any rate is agreed and is therefore invisible on a rate card.

whyPoints.description: Tutoring is set beside the Dubai fees it shares a budget with, including KHDA's confirmation of no fee increase for 2026-27. No competitor page in the fees cluster provides that context, and it is the comparison families make in their heads anyway.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis sold as diagnosis
whyPoints.description: A short investigative block with a written list at the end, and a recommendation that may be to stop. Providers rarely offer this because it can end in no sale, which is precisely why it is the best first purchase a family can make.

whyPoints.title: No fee for travel
whyPoints.description: Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the whole of the fee goes into teaching. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed before payment
whyPoints.description: Where no UAE-based specialist in a scarce Higher Level subject can fit your week, you are told and offered a specialist elsewhere on Gulf Standard Time. No competitor page reviewed for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost per hour for a family in Al Khawaneej?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai span runs from around AED 33 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for premium named teaching. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; Unitors publishes from AED 200 an hour for IB tuition; TutorChase quotes around AED 270; Bestimate's rate table puts specialist tuition at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above; BartyED publishes AED 650. These are provider figures read in October 2026 rather than IB Gram prices, and the bands are different products rather than one product at several prices.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest tutoring band ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a specific problem. A student who can do the work but will not start it needs structure and attention, and the budget band of roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour supplies exactly that. Paying four times as much buys nothing extra in that situation. Where the budget band fails is a Higher Level candidate losing marks to a particular component, because the gains there require somebody who can mark a script against the scheme and name the criterion that failed, which is a different skill from having passed the course recently.

faqs.question: Where do families in this area waste the most tutoring money?
faqs.answer: Buying hours the week cannot absorb. An Al Khawaneej Diploma student travels out of the community to school and has roughly ninety usable minutes on a weekday evening, so a three-session weekly commitment will be attended twice before it quietly lapses, and the money is gone either way. The second largest leak is paying for travel instead of teaching, which the market itself prices at roughly double for the same number of hours. Both decisions are made before any rate is negotiated.

faqs.question: How much should we budget per month rather than per hour?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Published packages run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Monthly figures are the ones worth planning with, because they expose immediately whether a proposed arrangement fits beside the school fees already being paid.

faqs.question: Does the no-fee-increase announcement affect tutoring decisions?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, and usefully. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A household that had budgeted an annual fee rise and did not get one has room in the education line that was not there previously. That makes it a better year than most to spend deliberately on one subject taught well rather than thinly across several.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a group class is being sold as individual tuition?
faqs.answer: Ask for the student-to-tutor ratio in writing, before paying. A class of eight at an attractive per-head rate is not one-to-one tuition however the advertising is worded, and the distinction matters because diagnosis is what individual tuition buys. In a group, your child's particular reason for a wrong answer will not be found. Group teaching has an honest use, which is covering content efficiently before a test. It is not a substitute for finding out why one student keeps losing the same marks.

faqs.question: What questions should I ask before paying a tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: Four. Is the figure per hour or per session, and how long is a session. What are the cancellation and rescheduling terms, including what happens when a child is unwell or a school bus is late. Does the quoted price include tax, stated as inclusive or exclusive. And how is a tutor change handled, and how quickly. All four should be answerable in writing without hesitation. Note also that the UAE private tuition permit is issued free of charge, so any licensing line item deserves a direct question.

faqs.question: How soon should I expect to see value for the money spent?
faqs.answer: By the fourth session there should be a marked piece of work showing fewer marks lost to the specific cause that was targeted. That is why the target has to be named in writing at session one: without it, no judgement is possible later and the arrangement drifts for a term on goodwill. A happier child is welcome but is not the evidence. If the marked work has not moved, the right response is changing the method or the tutor, not adding hours.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying premium rates for a named or examiner-led tutor?
faqs.answer: As a short block, sometimes. The premium band, published at AED 500 to 650 and above, buys scarcity rather than a different kind of teaching, and scarcity is worth paying for in the weeks before a session when the right three fixes must be identified quickly. Buying it as a two-year arrangement is paying for a scarce commodity you do not need weekly. Be cautious of examiner claims generally: current examiner status is difficult to evidence and should never be used to imply access to marking or boundaries.

faqs.question: Why does the price differ between IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Supply. Higher Level Physics, Chemistry and Theory of Knowledge are taught by few people in any one school, so the pool of tutors who can teach them confidently is small and the price reflects scarcity rather than difficulty. Mathematics at Standard Level and Biology are better supplied and sit nearer the qualified band. The practical consequence is that for scarce subjects availability, not price, is often the binding constraint, and that is worth knowing before a search starts.

faqs.question: Can we start cheap and move up if it is not working?
faqs.answer: You can, and many families do, but the sequence costs more than it looks. Three months at the budget band that does not move a Higher Level grade is three months of a two-year course spent, and the replacement purchase is then made under time pressure at specialist rates. The cheaper route is a short diagnostic block first, at the qualified band, which identifies what the problem actually is and therefore which band the problem needs. That decision costs less than a month of misdirected teaching.

faqs.question: What does the in-home premium actually buy in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Presence in the room and an hour of a tutor's driving. Published in-home rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour sit above the AED 150 to 300 published for qualified tutors teaching online, and the monthly packages make the gap explicit: eight hours priced at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against around AED 799. What the premium does not buy is a wider choice of teacher, since the pool narrows to those willing to drive to the eastern edge of the city on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Should an Al Khawaneej family commit to a term or to four sessions?
faqs.answer: Four, with a named target and an agreed review. Four is long enough for a diagnosis to turn into visible movement on a marked script and short enough that a wrong choice costs little. Term-long commitments made at the outset remove exactly the decision point that protects a family's money, which is the moment at session four where the evidence either exists or does not. A provider comfortable with a four-session commitment is telling you something reassuring.

faqs.answer: Not on this page, and the reason is that an honest figure depends on the subject, the level and how scarce the specialist is, so a single number invented for a web page would be less useful than no number. intro.heading: The honest answer to 'is anyone near me any good at this'
paragraphs: A parent typing 'IB tutor near me' in Al Mamzar is usually not asking about geography at all. They are asking a harder question: is there anybody within reach who genuinely knows this syllabus - the right subject, at the right level, with a working grasp of how the internal assessment is marked? Most pages answering this search reply with a reassurance. This one tries to reply with the actual position, including the parts that are unflattering.

Start with where IB is taught. International Baccalaureate programmes account for about 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, against 37 per cent for UK curriculum and 26 per cent for Indian. That 7 per cent is not spread evenly across the city. It concentrates in Emirates Hills, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim and the New Dubai belt, with the nearest provision to Al Mamzar sitting across in Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City, and in Mirdif. Deira, Al Qusais and Al Nahda are predominantly Indian-curriculum and Ministry-curriculum districts.

Tutor supply follows school supply, with a lag and a concentration. Someone who teaches Diploma Biology at Higher Level builds a practice around the schools that run it, and those schools are mostly a long drive from Al Mamzar. So the honest answer to 'is anyone near me' is: fewer people than in Al Barsha, and fewer again once you specify a level and a weak area. That is a statement about this neighbourhood's geography rather than about its families, and it is the reason this page exists in this form.

The second honest point is about what 'knows the syllabus' means, because it is where most tutoring money in this market is wasted. A tutor who studied a subject at university knows the content. A tutor who knows the Diploma syllabus knows which content is on it, what each paper weights, which command terms appear, how the internal assessment criteria are worded, and where a particular cohort reliably loses marks. The gap between those two is invisible in a credential list and obvious within ten minutes of a trial lesson.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Mamzar or anywhere else in the UAE; a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason that matters most here is not convenience - it is that removing the travel requirement means the match can be made on subject and level rather than on who is willing to cross the city at 4.30pm. Below, we set out what is well covered, what is thin, how long a match usually takes, and what we do when the answer is that nobody suitable is available.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-mamzar.programmesIntro: An IB family in Al Mamzar may be in any of three programmes, and the supply position differs for each. These are the stages and what coverage actually looks like at each one.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with transdisciplinary themes rather than subject syllabuses and no external examination. Support here is rarely subject tutoring. The useful work is on literacy, numeracy fluency and the research and presentation habits the programme assumes, and a generalist primary teacher is usually a better match than a subject specialist.
programmes.countryNote: Because the Primary Years Programme has no published subject syllabus, parents cannot look up what their child is supposed to know, which produces a particular kind of anxiety. The practical move is to ask the class teacher which specific skill is below expectation, then address that - not to buy generic maths tutoring against a worry.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria each scored zero to eight, converted to a one-to-seven grade. Coverage here is middling: tutors who understand criterion-referenced assessment are less common than subject tutors, and the two are not the same thing. A tutor who cannot read a criteria descriptor will teach content while the criterion stays low.
programmes.countryNote: The Middle Years Programme's criterion scores are diagnostic if read properly, and for a family in this neighbourhood that is useful because it narrows what needs buying. A high knowing-and-understanding score with a low processing-and-evaluating score in sciences is a data-handling gap, not a science gap, and it needs a specific kind of tutor.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups at Higher or Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. This is where supply gets genuinely uneven. Mathematics, the sciences, economics and English are reasonably covered; several Group 2 languages, music, and specific Higher Level options are thin. Sat in the May session UAE schools use, with a November session also available.
programmes.countryNote: The two nearest schools to Al Mamzar offering Diploma programmes sit in Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City, with further provision in Mirdif. That commute is why an Al Mamzar Diploma family is often the only one in their building, and why asking neighbours for a tutor recommendation produces nothing useful here.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme and the core components
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme is offered by a small number of schools, and coverage for its specific components is the thinnest in the whole set. The Diploma core - Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, CAS - is separately scarce, because supervising an Extended Essay well is a different skill from teaching the subject it sits in.
programmes.countryNote: Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay support is the request we most often have to be careful about, because the line between coaching and producing work is narrowest there. What a tutor can do is interrogate a research question, explain the assessment criteria and comment on the student's own draft. What nobody may do is write it.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-mamzar.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Al Mamzar families ask about, with the component that usually decides the grade named and an honest note where local coverage is thin.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, which is where the course is really tested. Higher Level Paper 3 carries 20 per cent and is the component students have practised least. Coverage is reasonable at Standard Level and thinner at Higher.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with calculator access throughout. The Higher Level statistics content - hypothesis testing, regression, graph theory - is demanding and the hardest part of this course to find a specialist for.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume and the data-based questions decide the grade. The commonest Diploma science request in this catchment, driven by health-science ambitions, and reasonably well covered.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole-based calculations drain marks across every paper; organic is taught last and revised least. Higher Level organic specialists are genuinely scarce across the city, not just near Al Mamzar.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circuits are the reliable mark drains, and the data-analysis section of Paper 1 rewards uncertainty work that is rarely taught systematically. Higher Level coverage is thin.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the command terms decide more marks than the economics does. Higher Level carries quantitative content that catches out students who chose it to avoid mathematics. Coverage is good.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The quantitative tools - ratio analysis, investment appraisal, break-even - are where strong written candidates lose marks. Popular in this part of the city, where many parents work in trade and logistics.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper on unseen non-literary texts are where marks move. Students who read widely still lose marks for not shaping an argument to the question asked.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Taken by many students in this catchment whose home language is not English. The individual oral and the writing task need timed practice rather than vocabulary work, and coverage is good.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic A first-language provision is more in demand in this neighbourhood than the city average, and local supply for it is genuinely strong - this is the one subject where a nearby tutor is often the better option.

subjects.name: Psychology and Global Politics
subjects.description: Both reward command-term discipline and the use of specific studies or cases rather than general argument. Coverage is moderate, and thinner for the Higher Level extensions.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
subjects.description: Separately scarce, because supervising an Extended Essay is a different skill from teaching its subject. Support is on question viability, criteria and feedback on the student's own draft - never on producing the work.

sections.heading: Where IB actually sits in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: The first half of the question - who is near me - has a factual answer. International Baccalaureate programmes account for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, in a sector of 227 private schools and 387,441 students teaching seventeen different curricula. UK curriculum is 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26 and US 14. Those shares vary enormously by district, and Al Mamzar sits in one of the districts where the Indian-curriculum share is well above the city average and IB provision is sparse.

No IB school sits in Al Mamzar itself. The nearest substantial international-curriculum cluster is in Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City, which includes Diploma provision, and there is further IB continuum provision east in Mirdif. Everything else is a longer run - Emirates Hills, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim and the New Dubai belt carry most of the city's IB schools and most of its IB-experienced teachers.

That geography has a consequence families here discover socially before they discover it commercially. An Al Mamzar Diploma family is often the only one in their building, and sometimes the only one on their street. The ordinary way parents find tutors - asking the person whose child is in the same class - does not work when nobody nearby is in the same programme. What replaces it is usually a search, which is how most readers arrive at this page.

The useful conclusion is not that the neighbourhood is badly served in general. It is well served for CBSE subjects, for Arabic as a first language, and for Ministry-curriculum support, because that is where the local demand sits and supply follows demand. It is thinly served for Diploma subjects, and the gap widens sharply at Higher Level and in the core components. The table sets that out by district so the position is checkable rather than asserted.

sections.heading: Subject by subject: what is covered, what is thin, and what we do about it
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit. Every one of them implies that any subject at any level can be matched immediately, which is not true of any provider including us. Publishing the real position is more useful, and it is also the single question worth asking every provider you speak to before paying anything.

Coverage is good for the subjects most students take: Biology, Economics, Business Management, English A and English B, and mathematics at Standard Level. It is moderate for Psychology, Global Politics and Standard Level sciences. It is thin for Higher Level physics and chemistry, for Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, for several Group 2 languages, for music and visual arts, and for the core components - Extended Essay supervision in particular, because that is a different skill from teaching the subject.

Match times follow the same pattern. A well-covered subject at Standard Level is usually matched within a few days. A thin Higher Level requirement can take a week or two, and sometimes cannot be matched at the hour a family wants. When that happens there are three honest answers rather than one: how long a match realistically takes, whether a closely related specialist could cover part of the need, and whether the school's own department or a different approach is the better route for now.

The fourth answer, which we also give, is that tutoring is sometimes the wrong purchase. A Diploma student failing across four subjects usually has an organisation or workload problem rather than four subject problems, and buying four tutors makes it worse by removing the independent study time. Saying that costs us a sale and saves a family several thousand dirhams, which is the trade this page is making.

sections.heading: Three tests for whether a tutor actually knows the syllabus
paragraphs: The second half of the question - does anyone near me know this syllabus - cannot be answered from a credential list, and a parent does not need to be a subject expert to test it. Three questions in a trial lesson will separate a tutor who knows the content from one who knows the course, and the difference between those two is where most tutoring money in this market goes to waste.

The first test is weightings. Ask what each paper is worth and what the internal assessment contributes. A tutor who teaches the Diploma knows that the internal assessment carries a fifth of the grade in most subjects, that Higher Level mathematics has a Paper 3 carrying 20 per cent, and roughly how the written papers split. A tutor who hesitates here has taught the subject somewhere else and is working out the Diploma as they go.

The second test is the assessment criteria. Ask them to name the criteria for the internal assessment in your child's subject and say what each is worth. In the sciences the scientific investigation is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria; in mathematics the exploration is marked out of twenty across five. Someone who works on internal assessments regularly can describe these without notes, and someone who cannot should not be charging a specialist rate for internal assessment support.

The third test is diagnostic. Hand over a marked paper and ask what the pattern of lost marks indicates. A tutor who knows the course will distinguish content gaps from unwritten method, from misread command terms, from running out of time - and will say which of those the next six weeks should target. A tutor who responds by proposing to go through the whole syllabus has told you they cannot diagnose, which makes the sessions a lottery regardless of how well they explain.

sections.heading: Why a general tutor cannot cover a six-subject Diploma
paragraphs: Families in this neighbourhood sometimes hope for one tutor who can support a Diploma student generally, and it is worth explaining why that does not exist rather than simply declining. The Diploma is six subjects drawn from different groups, at two levels, plus three core components, and each has its own assessment structure. The breadth is the point of the programme and it is also what makes general coverage impossible.

Consider what a single tutor would need. For the sciences, the scientific investigation criteria and the uncertainty treatment the data-based questions test. For mathematics, two separate courses with different papers and a different exploration mark scheme. For English A, the individual oral and the analysis of unseen non-literary text. For a Group 3 subject, command-term discipline and case specificity. For Theory of Knowledge, a form of argument that appears nowhere else in the programme. No individual holds that set.

What one person can usefully cover across a Diploma is the layer underneath the subjects: workload planning, how to read an assessment criterion, how to plan backwards from an internal deadline, how to revise against weightings rather than evenly. That is genuinely valuable and frequently the right purchase for a student who is drowning rather than failing, and it is also considerably cheaper than four subject tutors.

The practical rule we apply is this. One or two subjects failing means subject tutors, matched by subject and level. Four or more subjects failing means the problem is workload, organisation or wellbeing, and subject tutoring will make it worse by consuming the hours in which independent work has to happen. Diagnosing which of those two situations a family is in takes one honest conversation, and it is the conversation most providers skip.

sections.heading: What scarcity does to the price, and what a parent should pay for
paragraphs: Scarcity shows up in the rate, and this market makes that visible if you read the published figures in order. Budget online tutoring starts at roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour with Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik, which generally means a university student. A qualified subject tutor online is published from around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB work is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at around AED 270, and examiner-led sessions at around AED 650 with BartyED.

That ladder is a scarcity ladder rather than a quality ladder, and the implication is practical: pay for narrowness only when the need is narrow. A Standard Level biology student working through a unit does not need the top of the ladder. A Higher Level chemistry student eight weeks from the papers who is losing marks specifically on organic mechanisms does, because the number of people who can diagnose and fix that is small.

In-home one-to-one sits separately, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and advertised packages run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. For Al Mamzar the travel component is larger than average, because the tutors teaching these syllabuses mostly live nearer the schools that teach them. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so that band is the market's rather than a choice we are declining to make.

We publish no rate card on this page, because a figure quoted without knowing the subject, the level and the frequency is a number rather than information. The trial lesson and the consultation are free. For budgeting context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: The internal assessment line, and why it protects your child
paragraphs: Internal assessments carry a fifth of the grade in most Diploma subjects, and together with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay they are the part of the programme where the honesty question is sharpest. The boundary is clear and worth stating before any deadline pressure arrives. A tutor may teach content, explain what each criterion rewards, interrogate a research question, model a technique on different material, and give feedback on a draft the student has written.

A tutor may not produce the work. The research, the data, the argument and the words have to be the student's own, and the school authenticates that. If the authentication is untrue the sanction falls on the candidate rather than on whoever helped, which is the asymmetry worth understanding. One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price; that transaction puts the entire risk on a seventeen-year-old while the seller keeps the money.

This is also where unverifiable credentials do the most damage. We do not describe tutors as IB examiners for individuals whose current status cannot be evidenced, and no examiner claim should be read as implying access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. A provider using examiner status to suggest inside knowledge of an internal assessment is making a claim that should fail a parent's basic scepticism test.

Materials follow the same principle. We reference IB subject guides, past papers and mark schemes, cite them, and point to the official source. We do not reproduce them or supply them as downloads, because they are the board's copyright and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. We also publish no IB session or results dates, because ibo.org blocks automated access and nothing in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself - the May session is the one UAE schools sit, and exact dates come from the school's Diploma coordinator.

sections.heading: The permit question, and why so few parents ask it
paragraphs: There is one thing about a tutor that a parent in Al Mamzar can verify in a single question, and almost nobody asks it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system, and it lists no fees. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published anywhere official, so a figure quoted to you as the penalty - including figures that circulate in parent groups - should be treated as unverified.

Anyone telling you private tutoring in Dubai is unregulated, or that a permit is optional, is wrong, and that is a useful signal about the rest of what they say. So is the opposite error: a provider claiming KHDA approval as a tutoring service is describing something specific. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. A platform without premises does not hold one, and should not imply it.

There is a related point about who teaches. Abu Dhabi's ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct barring the same arrangement. Those are press-reported positions and should be verified against the current policy document, but the principle travels across the UAE: engaging your child's own classroom teacher privately is the arrangement most likely to put that teacher in breach.

sections.heading: KHDA, SPEA and the regulator map that matters on this border
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The regulator map for the rest of the country is worth knowing here specifically, because Al Mamzar sits minutes from the Sharjah boundary and some families in this neighbourhood have children at schools under a different authority.

In Abu Dhabi, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. In Sharjah, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education, and in Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge does the same. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map for UAE private schools, and ADEK in particular is named by none of the competitor pages researched in this market.

The Sharjah distinction is more than administrative. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum and fee approval, not merely inspection, sits with the emirate regulator. A family in Al Mamzar with a child at a Sharjah school is therefore dealing with a different approval framework from their neighbour whose child is at a Dubai school five minutes away.

Within Dubai, the mandatory UAE subjects apply regardless of curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Separate classes are required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; instructional time is calculated against a forty-minute lesson unit; and for the mandatory subjects, additional or different content needs prior permission from the Ministry of Education, which limits what any tutor may legitimately offer in them.
