process.title: Name the subject and the level together
process.description: Higher or Standard, alongside the subject. Those two words determine whether we have someone suitable and how long a match takes, and a request that omits the level will come back with a question rather than a tutor.

process.title: Ask us about coverage before anything else
process.description: We will tell you whether the subject and level you need is well covered, thin, or unavailable at your preferred hour, and roughly how long a match takes. Ask every provider you speak to the same question; the answers are informative.

process.title: Send a marked script
process.description: A marked paper lets us distinguish content gaps from unwritten method, misread command terms and running out of time. Those four need different work, and a predicted grade distinguishes none of them.

process.title: Run the three tests in the free trial
process.description: Ask the tutor what each paper is worth, ask them to name the internal assessment criteria and marks, and hand them the marked script to interpret. Ten minutes of that tells you more than any credential list.

process.title: Choose the slot by arrival reliability
process.description: The commute from Al Garhoud, Mirdif or across the creek varies by twenty-five minutes at 3pm. We will usually recommend the evening slot that depends on no road at all, unless the student travels by metro.

process.title: Expect us to say no sometimes
process.description: If four subjects are failing, if an internal assessment deadline is four days away, or if no suitable specialist exists for a thin requirement, we will say so. That is the point of publishing a coverage position rather than implying unlimited supply.

whyPoints.title: The coverage question answered in public
whyPoints.description: We publish which subjects and levels are well covered, which are thin and what the fallback is. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which makes it the most useful question you can ask any provider.

whyPoints.title: Matched by subject and level
whyPoints.description: Higher and Standard Level diverge in content, papers and depth. A booking names both, because a tutor comfortable at one level is not automatically useful at the other and the difference shows within a fortnight.

whyPoints.title: Three tests you can run yourself
whyPoints.description: Paper weightings, internal assessment criteria, and interpreting a marked script. A parent does not need subject expertise to tell a tutor who knows the content from one who knows the course.

whyPoints.title: The pool is national, not local
whyPoints.description: IB provision concentrates away from Deira, and tutor supply follows it. Video delivery gives this neighbourhood the same pool as Al Barsha, which is a larger relative gain than it would be anywhere else in the city.

whyPoints.title: Honest about when tutoring is the wrong purchase
whyPoints.description: Four failing subjects is a workload problem, not four subject problems, and buying four tutors removes the hours independent work needs. We say that even though it costs us the sale.

whyPoints.title: No unverifiable credentials
whyPoints.description: We do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence, do not claim regulator approval we do not hold, and do not publish ratings that are not backed by countable reviews.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB tutor near Al Mamzar who knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: Fewer than in Al Barsha, and the honest reason is geography. IB programmes are about 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment and they concentrate in Emirates Hills, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim and the New Dubai belt. The nearest provision to Al Mamzar is in Al Garhoud, Dubai Festival City and Mirdif. Tutor supply follows school supply, so a local search here produces a thin result for Diploma subjects. It produces a strong result for CBSE subjects and Arabic as a first language.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a tutor knows the Diploma or just the subject?
faqs.answer: Three questions in a trial lesson will tell you, and you do not need subject expertise to ask them. First, what is each paper worth and what does the internal assessment contribute? Second, name the internal assessment criteria for this subject and the marks for each. Third, here is a marked script - what does the pattern of lost marks indicate? A tutor who knows the course answers all three without notes. One who proposes going through the whole syllabus has told you they cannot diagnose.

faqs.question: Which schools near Al Mamzar actually offer IB programmes?
faqs.answer: Not any in the neighbourhood itself. The nearest provision sits in Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City, which is under twenty minutes outside peak traffic, with further IB continuum provision east in Mirdif. Everything else is a longer run towards Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim. Check each school's current programme authorisation on KHDA's own site rather than relying on reputation, because authorisation and the post-16 offer both change between intakes.

faqs.question: Can you tell me before I pay whether you have someone for Higher Level physics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we think you should ask every provider that. Higher Level physics coverage is thinner than Biology or Economics, particularly for the fields theme, and a specific hour can take a week or two to match. If we cannot cover it we will say so and give you three alternatives: how long a match realistically takes, whether a Standard Level specialist can cover the shared content meanwhile, and whether the school's own department is the better route. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit.

faqs.question: Do you visit homes in Al Mamzar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Mamzar, in Dubai, or anywhere else in the UAE - a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In-home tutoring exists in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and that travel is longer to Al Mamzar than to most districts because IB-experienced tutors cluster nearer the schools that teach these programmes.

faqs.question: My son is failing four Diploma subjects. Should we hire four tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not, and this is the recommendation we most often give against our own interest. Four failing subjects is usually a workload, organisation or wellbeing problem rather than four separate subject problems, and four weekly tutors consume the hours in which independent work has to happen. The better first purchase is one person working on the layer underneath: planning backwards from internal deadlines, reading assessment criteria, revising against weightings. Then address one subject properly once the student has time to absorb it.

faqs.question: Why does nobody seem to cover Extended Essay supervision well?
faqs.answer: Because supervising an Extended Essay is a different skill from teaching the subject it sits in, and far fewer people have it. The work is about question viability, scope, methodology and the assessment criteria rather than about content. The school supervisor is the primary route and should stay so. What an outside tutor can usefully add is interrogating whether the research question is answerable within the word limit and the resources available, and giving feedback on a draft the student has written - never producing text.

faqs.question: Is a university-student tutor at AED 50 an hour ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth saying so. Published rates at that level - roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour across this market - usually mean a university student, and for working through routine exercises, building arithmetic fluency, or supervised practice on content already taught, that can be entirely adequate. It is the wrong choice for diagnosing why a Higher Level grade has fallen, for internal assessment criteria work, or for judging whether an exploration topic can generate level-appropriate mathematics.

faqs.question: Does the Sharjah border affect our options if our school is across it?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two ways. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than KHDA, and SPEA approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum approval, not just inspection, sits with the emirate. Practically, border traffic makes an afternoon tutoring appointment unrealistic from Al Mamzar, which means an evening online session is effectively the only workable option rather than merely the preferable one.

faqs.question: How quickly can a match be made for a Standard Level subject?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days for the well-covered subjects - Biology, Economics, Business Management, English A and B, and mathematics at Standard Level. Thinner requirements take longer: Higher Level physics or chemistry, Applications and Interpretation Higher Level statistics, or a Group 2 language other than English or Arabic can take a week or two, and occasionally cannot be matched at a specific hour. We tell you which category you are in when you ask, rather than after you have paid.

faqs.question: What should a Primary Years Programme parent in this area actually buy?
faqs.answer: Rarely subject tutoring. The Primary Years Programme is inquiry-led with transdisciplinary themes and no published subject syllabus, which is why parents cannot look up what a child is meant to know and why anxiety fills the gap. The useful step is asking the class teacher which specific skill is below expectation - decoding, number fluency, written organisation, research habits - and addressing that. A generalist primary teacher is usually a better match than a subject specialist at this stage.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an internal assessment that is due in four days?
faqs.answer: Honestly, not much, and we will say so rather than taking the booking. Most internal assessment marks are decided at the design and planning stage - whether the question is answerable, whether the data can support analysis, whether reflection was written as the work progressed. Four days out, what remains is proofreading the student's own work for clarity against the criteria, which is legitimate and limited. Anything beyond that crosses into producing assessed work, and the risk of that falls entirely on the candidate.

faqs.question: Everyone advertising near here says 'examiner-led' - should that move my decision?
faqs.answer: We do not make that claim, and we would be cautious about any provider that does. Current examiner status cannot be verified by a parent, and examiner experience should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. Several pages ranking in this market lean on examiner language and on self-published star ratings - one shows two different ratings and review counts on the same page. What we do state is the subject, the level and the coverage position, all of which you can test in a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Which IB session do Dubai schools sit, and where do the dates come from?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session, with a November session also available. We publish no IB examination or results dates on these pages, because ibo.org blocks automated access and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. The school's Diploma coordinator holds the current dates, including the internal deadlines for internal assessments and the Extended Essay - and those internal deadlines, rather than the IB's own, are what actually govern your child's term.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-mamzar.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB tutor near me in Al Mamzar, the most useful question is not who is closest. It is whether a provider can tell you, before you pay, that they have someone for your child's subject at your child's level and at an hour that works - and what they will do if they do not. Ask us that. Then send the subject, the level and a marked script, and test the match in a free trial using the three questions on this page. We do not visit homes in the UAE, and we would rather explain the supply position in this neighbourhood than imply it does not exist.

intro.heading: There are tutors near Al Manara. Are any of them IB teachers?
paragraphs: Most pages answering this query assume the local supply is zero and sell you distance as the problem. In Al Manara that would be dishonest. The neighbourhood sits inland along Al Wasl Road and Umm Suqeim Street, with the coastal Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah campuses on one side and the dense Al Barsha and Al Quoz cluster on the other. There are teachers living within fifteen minutes in both directions, and many of them tutor privately. A proximity search from an Al Manara villa returns real people with real classroom experience.

The question that actually matters is which curriculum those people teach. Dubai's private-school market, as reported by the Dubai Media Office for 2024-25, enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum taking 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. That distribution shapes the tutor pool exactly as you would expect. For every teacher near Al Manara who has marked an IB internal assessment, there are several who have taught IGCSE and A Level for years and have never seen a Diploma criterion descriptor.

Those teachers are not weak. Many are excellent, and for a Year 10 student sitting Cambridge 0620 they are precisely the right hire. But the Diploma is structurally different from A Level in ways that cannot be picked up on the job without cost to somebody's child. Grades are 1-7 rather than A*-E and the mapping between them is not intuitive. Every subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth of the grade, marked against published criteria identified by letter, each with its own mark allocation. Command terms are specified and carry mark-scheme consequences. There is a core - Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, Creativity Activity Service - with no A Level equivalent at all.

A teacher who does not know those things will teach your child the chemistry correctly and still miss the marks, because the marks are not purely in the chemistry. That is the honest content of the question "is there an IB tutor near me in Al Manara". The answer is: there is a tutor pool near you, it is mostly a British-curriculum pool, and the way to find a Diploma teacher inside or outside it is to test rather than to measure the distance.

This page gives you the tests. It sets out what changes between A Level and the Diploma, names the internal assessment criteria by letter so you can hear whether a tutor recognises them, explains what a 1-7 grade and a predicted total actually mean, and maps the twenty-minute radius around Al Manara so you can see for yourself what is in it. It also gives the Dubai market rates in AED with the source that published each one, which is the part a parent can verify independently.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for an Al Manara family are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That is what makes it possible to match a household with a Diploma specialist rather than with the best British-curriculum teacher inside a driving radius.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-manara.programmesIntro: An Al Manara IB enquiry needs placing in the continuum before anything useful can be said, because the four programmes assess so differently that advice about one is actively misleading about another.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Subject grades run 1-7 and the diploma total runs to 45 including up to three bonus points from the core. Each subject carries an internally assessed component - an exploration, an investigation, a portfolio, an oral - marked against criteria identified by letter with published mark allocations.
programmes.countryNote: This is the overwhelming majority of Al Manara Diploma enquiries, and the usual trigger is a Year 12 October or November report. A student who moved up from IGCSE at a nearby British-curriculum school meets Higher Level, finds that recall no longer earns marks, and the family starts searching. That is a specific and fixable problem, and it needs a teacher who has marked the course.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria labelled A to D and scored 0-8 against published band descriptors. No external examination for most students, though MYP Year 5 candidates may sit eAssessment for the MYP certificate. The criterion structure is the first place IB students meet assessment of process rather than only of answers.
programmes.countryNote: Relevant to an Al Manara family in two situations: a child already at a continuum school in the Al Barsha cluster, and a child at a British-curriculum school whose parents are weighing a move into an IB school for sixth form. In the second case the MYP is what the new cohort will have had and your child will not, which is worth planning for.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external assessment and reporting against conceptual understanding and learner-profile attributes. What it builds, and what later IB assessment relies on, is the habit of explaining and justifying rather than producing a correct answer and stopping.
programmes.countryNote: Al Manara has primary provision in both directions and families often move between British-curriculum and IB primaries without expecting any adjustment. The adjustment is real but small, and it is about being asked why rather than about content being ahead or behind.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma courses taken alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and language development. Offered by a small number of UAE schools. Where a CP student takes DP courses, those courses are assessed exactly as a Diploma student's are, with the same papers and the same internal assessment.
programmes.countryNote: Worth distinguishing clearly because a CP certificate is not the Diploma, and the two are frequently conflated in conversations about sixth-form options in Dubai. If a UAE federal university is in view, check the Ministry of Education equivalency position directly with the authority before committing to a pathway.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-manara.subjectsIntro: Al Manara Diploma enquiries arrive as a subject and a level. For each one, the internally assessed component and the place the marks actually go - the two things a British-curriculum tutor is least likely to know.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is the internal assessment: a 12 to 20 page piece of independent mathematics marked against criteria including presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. HL adds Paper 3, a sustained problem-solving pair of questions that cannot be topic-spotted.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same exploration structure, different mathematics: modelling, statistics and a graphical display calculator assumed throughout. Students lose marks reporting a regression coefficient without interpreting it in context, and choosing a statistical test the data does not support. HL adds matrices and graph theory.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a scientific investigation marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Uncertainty propagation is where strong candidates lose a whole criterion. On the papers, circular motion and fields at SL and quantum and nuclear at HL are the recurring difficulty.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same investigation structure as Physics, assessed on the same criteria. On the papers, organic mechanisms and energetics separate grades, with HL adding entropy, equilibrium calculations and harder spectroscopy. Marks go on state symbols, significant figures and explanations that describe instead of explaining.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A volume subject that marks terminology tightly - near-miss vocabulary earns nothing where the scheme wants a precise mechanism. The investigation needs a biologically meaningful variable, and students frequently choose one that produces data too noisy to analyse, which costs them in data analysis and evaluation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a portfolio of commentaries on published news articles, each linked to a specific syllabus concept. Students lose time and marks by choosing an article that does not actually illustrate the concept. On the papers, a correctly labelled and shifted diagram with the new equilibrium marked earns what prose cannot.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based - Ansoff, SWOT, break-even, ratio analysis, investment appraisal - with responses capped when a tool is applied without reference to the named organisation. HL adds the business research project, where the real difficulty is scoping a question answerable from evidence the student can actually obtain.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided textual analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the Individual Oral, and at HL the HL Essay. The Individual Oral requires a global issue evidenced from two extracts in a fixed time, and the usual failure is choosing an issue too broad to evidence at all.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language-acquisition course that strong speakers underestimate. Register, text type and audience carry the marks rather than vocabulary breadth, and the writing task is assessed against a specified text type - an email written as an essay loses a criterion before the content is read.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation is the internal assessment, with a strict word limit and a structure that includes an evaluation of sources. Students lose marks by writing a narrative rather than an argument, and by evaluating sources generically instead of by origin, purpose and content.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by the exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, and contributing to the bonus points on the diploma total. Students lose marks writing about the world rather than about knowledge. Support is argument structure and question discipline; the essay must be the student's own work and is reviewed, never drafted.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent 4,000-word research essay in a subject, with a school supervisor and an assessed reflection process. The dominant failure is a research question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words. A tutor's legitimate role is coaching the question, the method and the reading - never producing text.

sections.heading: Why an A Level teacher is not automatically an IB teacher
paragraphs: Start with what the two qualifications share, because it is substantial. The physics is the same physics. A teacher who can explain electromagnetic induction to a Year 13 A Level student can explain it to a Diploma student, and a good mathematician is a good mathematician on either syllabus. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling specialism rather than describing it. The content overlap is why the nearby British-curriculum pool around Al Manara is genuinely useful for some kinds of Diploma help, particularly straightforward content gaps in the first year.

What differs is everything around the content. Grades run 1-7 per subject against A*-E, and the mapping is not a simple translation - a 6 is not an A and treating it as one leads to bad decisions about predicted grades and university offers. Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth of the grade, marked against criteria identified by letter with published mark allocations, and completed months before the papers. A Level coursework, where it exists at all, works differently and carries different weight.

Then there is the core, which has no A Level counterpart. Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words of independent research with an assessed reflection process and a school supervisor. Together they contribute bonus points to the diploma total. A tutor who has never supervised either will give generally sensible essay advice that misses what the criteria reward, which is a particular and expensive kind of near-miss.

Finally, command terms. The IB publishes them and mark schemes act on them: evaluate asks for something distinct from discuss, which asks for something distinct from explain, and a response that answers the wrong one is capped regardless of quality. An experienced IB marker knows this instinctively. A new one learns it at the cost of a student's practice papers. sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, named by letter
paragraphs: This is the single best test of whether somebody has actually taught the Diploma, and it takes thirty seconds. Ask a prospective tutor to name the internal assessment criteria in their subject and say what each is worth. Across the entire competitor corpus researched for this market, not one page names a single IB criterion. A teacher who has marked the course will answer immediately; a teacher who has not will talk about quality in general terms.

The structures are specific. In the sciences, the investigation is assessed across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each with its own mark allocation, and the uncertainty treatment sits inside data analysis where it quietly costs strong students a band. In mathematics, the exploration is assessed across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics - and personal engagement is the one students and generalist tutors both neglect, because it rewards something that is not mathematical skill.

In economics the internal assessment is a portfolio of commentaries, each tied to a published article and a specific syllabus concept, with word limits and a diagram expectation. In history it is a historical investigation with a strict structure including source evaluation. In the languages it is oral work assessed against criteria covering language, message and interaction. These are not interchangeable, and advice generalised across them is worth very little.

Two practical notes for an Al Manara parent. Always get the criteria from the school or from the subject guide rather than from a tutor's summary, including this page's - the IB revises them between cycles and schools hold the current version. And note the one-way door: internal assessment marks are banked before the papers, so a weak internal assessment cannot be recovered in the exam hall. That is the arithmetic that makes early support cheaper than late support.

sections.heading: What a 1-7 grade and a predicted total actually mean
paragraphs: Parents who went through A Levels or a national system read IB numbers wrongly, and expensive decisions follow. A subject grade of 4 is a pass in that subject and is a long way from a 6. The diploma total runs to 45: six subjects at up to 7 each gives 42, with up to three further points available from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. There are also requirements around minimum grades and totals for the diploma to be awarded at all, which the school will confirm for your child's specific profile.

The predicted grade is the number that does the work in university applications, and it is the school's judgement rather than a measurement. It is built from mock performance, internal assessment marks where available and teacher assessment, which means it is influenced by exactly the things tutoring can affect - and also that a tutor who reports progress only against their own internal tests is reporting on something no university will ever see. Progress should be measured against the school's own marking.

Where this becomes a live decision for Al Manara families is the Higher Level drop. Three Higher Levels is a heavy load and a student visibly struggling in one of them will sometimes be better served by moving to Standard Level, which the school may permit within a window. The arithmetic of that decision needs somebody who can read a mock script and say whether the Higher Level grade is recoverable in the time available. It is not a decision to take on the basis of a single disappointing report.

One caution, which is also a promise this page keeps. No specific grade outcome is predictable and nobody should promise one to you. What can honestly be said is which component is costing marks, roughly how much work the recovery needs, and whether the timeline allows it. A provider who answers a question about grades with a number rather than with a diagnosis is telling you something about how they work.

sections.heading: Mapping the twenty-minute radius for yourself
paragraphs: Rather than asserting that local supply is inadequate, here is the radius so you can judge. Within roughly twenty minutes of Al Manara in normal traffic you have the Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah coastal cluster seaward, Al Safa and the Al Wasl corridor to the north-east, and Al Barsha and Al Quoz inland across Sheikh Zayed Road. That is a lot of schools, and a lot of teachers. It is also a radius whose curriculum profile is weighted heavily towards the UK curriculum, which at 37% of Dubai private-school enrolment is the emirate's largest single track.

The IB capacity in that radius is concentrated inland. The IB World Schools in the Al Barsha and Al Quoz direction are where Diploma teaching experience sits, and they are the furthest part of the radius from an Al Manara villa in afternoon traffic. That is the geography problem in one sentence: the nearest teachers are the least likely to know the Diploma, and the ones most likely to know it are the hardest to get to at 4.30pm.

Note also that the radius is changing. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 with enrolment up 6%. New IB capacity in the inland corridors will eventually widen the local Diploma teaching pool. It does not help a Year 12 student with a mock in five weeks.

Which is the argument for taking the radius off the search entirely. Over live video the relevant distance is a time zone, not a drive, and the pool becomes every Diploma specialist working on Gulf Standard Time. sections.heading: Maths AA or AI, and which doors each keeps open
paragraphs: This decision costs more than any tutoring purchase and it is frequently made badly, often on the basis that one route is easier. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof route, with an HL Paper 3 extended investigation. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route, with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout and HL content including matrices and graph theory. They are different courses, not tiers of the same one.

The practical consequence is admissions. Competitive engineering, mathematics, physics and many economics programmes expect the Analysis route, typically at Higher Level, and a student who took Applications may find courses closed that nobody mentioned when the choice was made in Year 11. Conversely a student headed for business, design, medicine in some systems, or the social sciences may be better served by Applications, where the statistics content is genuinely more relevant and the grade more achievable.

The honest advice for an Al Manara family is to check requirements with the specific universities in view rather than relying on general guidance, including this page's. UAE institutions, UK universities and US admissions all treat the two routes differently, and requirements change between cycles. Published entry requirements on the university's own admissions pages are the only source worth acting on.

Where a tutor genuinely helps is in the diagnosis before the choice: whether a student's current algebraic fluency makes Analysis HL a realistic proposition, or whether it would consume the time their other five subjects need. That is a judgement from evidence - a marked paper, a piece of algebra done under time pressure - rather than an opinion. Get it made in Year 11, because changing route in Year 12 is possible at some schools and painful at all of them.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line, and why it protects your child
paragraphs: Every internally assessed Diploma component must be the student's own work, and a malpractice finding can cost the diploma rather than a grade. For an Al Manara parent buying support that makes this a safety question rather than an ethics seminar, and the line is worth establishing before any money changes hands.

Legitimate support is extensive. A tutor can explain a criterion descriptor in plain language and say what separates one band from the next. They can interrogate a research question until the student can state and defend it in a sentence. They can teach the statistical test the data needs, or the uncertainty propagation a physics investigation requires. They can mark a practice paper, explain why a fluent response landed mid-band, and set another. They can read a draft the student wrote and respond with questions and comments.

Illegitimate support is anything that generates content the student did not produce. Writing a section. Rewriting a paragraph to demonstrate the right register. Supplying a dataset or a research question the student adopts without understanding. Editing to completion. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which is not a shortcut but a malpractice case handed to an IB coordinator with the student's name on it.

The test a parent can apply without IB knowledge: could your child explain every decision in the document, unprompted, to a supervisor who asks why? If the method, the question and the conclusions are all defensible in their own words, the support was teaching. If any part would need looking up, it was not. Ask any tutor to state their boundary in the first conversation, and treat vagueness as the answer it is.
bullets: Explaining criteria, teaching method, marking practice work: legitimate and valuable
Questions and comments on a draft the student wrote: legitimate
Writing, rewriting or completing any part of a submission: malpractice

sections.heading: How to verify a tutor is permitted, in two questions
paragraphs: A proximity search performs no checks at all, so here are the two that matter and how to make them. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as unreliable.

Because the permit is free and MoHRE states a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system, there is no practical reason for a working private tutor to lack one. The eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Asking to see it is a normal question that a permitted tutor expects.

The second check concerns who the tutor already teaches. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported and should be verified against the current policy document, but the direction is clear enough to act on: decline the arrangement where your child's own classroom teacher is paid privately, however helpfully it is offered.

Finally, be clear about what no provider can claim. KHDA regulates and inspects Dubai private schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes operating premises in the emirate; it does not rate or approve individual tutors, so no tutor holds a KHDA approval and the phrase is not a credential. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no premises in the UAE and claims no regulator or board accreditation of any kind.

sections.heading: What a useful first fortnight looks like
paragraphs: Concrete beats reassuring, so here is the shape of two weeks well spent for an Al Manara Diploma student. The first session is diagnostic and nothing is taught until the problem is named: the marked paper or the internal assessment feedback is read together, the criterion or the command term that cost the marks is identified, and the honest size of the gap is stated. If a tutor proposes a plan in the first conversation without seeing marked work, that plan is guesswork.

The second and third sessions attack the named thing on the student's own next piece of work rather than on a generic exercise. For a science investigation that means building the uncertainty treatment into the data the student actually collected. For a maths exploration it means making the personal engagement criterion visible in a piece the student cares about. For a Paper 2 extended response it means rewriting one answer to the command term, properly, once.

The fourth session closes the loop against the school's own marking, because that is the only measure that counts. The new mark on the same component either moved or it did not. If it moved, the plan continues; if it did not, the diagnosis was wrong and it gets revised rather than repeated louder. A provider reporting progress only against their own internal assessments is reporting on themselves.

After that, the decision is genuinely open and should be presented that way. Some students need a second component addressed. Some need nothing further this term. Some have a foundations problem that will take two terms and should be told so plainly rather than sold a package. The free trial lesson means the first of those four sessions costs nothing, and the diagnosis happens before any block is agreed.

faqs.question: Are there actually any IB tutors near Al Manara, or is the pool all British curriculum?
faqs.answer: There is a genuine local pool, which makes Al Manara different from parts of Dubai with no schools inside their boundary. The pool's curriculum profile is the issue. Dubai's private-school enrolment in 2024-25 ran UK 37%, Indian 26%, US 14% and IB 7% across 227 schools, and tutor supply mirrors that. Most teachers within fifteen minutes of Al Manara have taught IGCSE and A Level; a smaller number have marked a Diploma internal assessment. The way to find the second group is to test for IB experience rather than to filter by distance, which is what matching by subject and level does.

faqs.question: Can an A Level teacher tutor my child's IB Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: For content gaps in the first Diploma year, often yes - the physics is the same physics and a strong teacher is a strong teacher. For everything structural, be careful. Grades run 1-7 rather than A*-E and do not map simply. Every IB subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth of the grade, marked against criteria published by letter. Command terms are specified and mark schemes act on them. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay have no A Level counterpart at all. A teacher learning those on the job learns them at the cost of your child's practice papers.

faqs.question: What question separates a real Diploma teacher from a confident generalist?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the internal assessment criteria in their subject and say what each one is worth. In the sciences the investigation is assessed across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. In mathematics the exploration is assessed across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. A teacher who has marked the course answers in seconds. One who has not will talk about quality in general terms. Across the sixty-odd competitor pages researched for this market, not one names a single IB criterion, which tells you how rare the knowledge is.

faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. For an Al Manara family lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the marked paper, the internal assessment draft and the criteria document are all visible to both sides. That is the mechanism rather than a limitation. A tutor who drives cannot specialise, because nobody fills a week with Chemistry HL students living within twenty minutes of their own villa, so removing the drive is what reaches the specialist.

faqs.question: Why is the IB teaching capacity near Al Manara concentrated inland?
faqs.answer: Because that is where the IB World Schools are. Within Al Manara's twenty-minute radius the coastal cluster towards Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah is predominantly UK curriculum, while the inland cluster across Sheikh Zayed Road towards Al Barsha and Al Quoz holds most of the area's Diploma provision. The awkward consequence is geographic: the nearest teachers are the least likely to know the IB, and the ones most likely to know it are the hardest to reach in afternoon traffic. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools, which will widen the pool over time.

faqs.question: How should I read my child's IB predicted grades?
faqs.answer: As the school's judgement rather than a measurement, and in the right scale. Subject grades run 1-7, the diploma total runs to 45 with up to three bonus points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay combined, and a 6 is not an A. Predictions are built from mock performance, internal assessment marks where available and teacher assessment, which means they respond to exactly what tutoring can affect. It also means progress should be measured against the school's own marking, not against a tutor's internal tests, because no university will ever see those.

faqs.question: Is it worth moving a Higher Level subject down to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is a decision for evidence rather than for a single disappointing report. Three Higher Levels is a heavy load, and a student visibly drowning in one may do better across all six subjects after a move, where the school permits one within its window. What the decision needs is somebody who can read a marked script and say whether the Higher Level grade is recoverable in the time left, separating fixable content gaps from fluency problems. Raise it with the IB coordinator early; the window for a change closes well before the exam session.

faqs.question: Which IB maths route should a student aiming at engineering take?
faqs.answer: Generally Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, but verify against the specific universities in view rather than any general guidance including this page's. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof route with an HL Paper 3 extended investigation. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout. Competitive engineering, mathematics and physics programmes usually expect Analysis, and a student who took Applications may find courses closed that nobody mentioned in Year 11. Published admissions pages are the only source worth acting on.

faqs.question: Why can a weak internal assessment not be fixed in the exam hall?
faqs.answer: Because it is already marked and banked. Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth of the grade, completed and submitted months before the written papers. Whatever band it lands in travels with the student into the session, and no amount of strong paper performance retrieves the marks lost there. That arithmetic is why support early in the first Diploma year is cheaper than support in the spring of the exam year - and why the single most valuable intervention available is often at the point where an internal assessment topic is chosen.

They may not write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph to demonstrate the right register, supply data or a research question, or edit to completion. faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and states a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without it face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since the permit costs nothing, not having one is a choice.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher at a nearby school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: It is the one arrangement to decline. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document, but the direction is unambiguous. It is also worth saying that the arrangement is usually offered kindly rather than cynically - which makes it harder to refuse and no less inadvisable.

faqs.question: Why does this page give no IB exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified. ibo.org returns an error to automated fetching, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and publishing an unverified exam date to a parent who will plan around it is worse than publishing none. UAE candidates sit the May session, which is stated because it is the pattern rather than a date. Confirm every specific IB date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. Cambridge and Pearson dates are sourced from the boards and appear elsewhere on this site with their framing intact.

faqs.question: What should a first fortnight of Diploma support actually deliver?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis, then work on it, then a measurement. The first session reads the marked paper or internal assessment feedback and names the criterion or command term costing marks - nothing is taught before the problem has a name. Sessions two and three attack that named thing on the student's own next piece of work rather than a generic exercise. Session four compares the school's new mark on the same component. If a tutor proposes a plan before seeing any marked work, that plan is guesswork, and if progress is reported only against their own tests, they are reporting on themselves.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-manara.closingHeading: Test for IB experience, not for proximity
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-manara.closingBody: If you came here searching for an IB tutor near me in Al Manara, the useful shift is from a map to a test. There are capable tutors within fifteen minutes of your villa in both directions, and most of them know the UK curriculum rather than the Diploma. Send the subject, the level and the last marked piece of work, and ask whoever you speak to - here or anywhere - to name the internal assessment criteria in that subject and what each is worth. You will get a named tutor with the IB subjects and levels they have taught, the reasoning behind the match, and a free trial lesson before any block is agreed. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.
